images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; crowns, antlers, wings and heads stay well inside the central band; no title, no lettering. Night of the coronation above the giwa roofs of Seorabeol, a vast starry sky torn by splashed-ink cloud. Low angle from the palace yard stones. INTERACTION: the wingless white heavenly horse Chunma has come down out of the sky and lowers its long arched neck to her; Queen Sunduk, in her gold Silla tree-and-antler crown with jade comma pendants (the real Silla gold crown — upright tree-shaped prongs and antler prongs, not a fantasy orb or crescent), coral-red and white royal silk, reaches up and lays her open palm flat on its forehead, her chin lifted, a small fierce smile; its forelock falls across her fingers and its breath stirs her veil-pendants. Its hind legs still trail in curling cloud streamers above the roofline. CHUNMA HAS NO WINGS: a wingless white heavenly horse, bare white back and shoulders, nothing feathered anywhere; it rides the air on curling cloud-and-flame streamers trailing from its legs. One warm torch key (#E8552B) from the lower left catches her crown, cheek and the horse’s muzzle; the rest is indigo night and ink. Dark eaves in the near foreground. STYLE: HEEWON STYLE, more painterly, with hints of Korean ink painting — Korean webtoon figures (clean ink linework, simplified expressive faces matching the attached portrait, watercolor-washed) inside a hand-painted world of watercolor and oil with traditional sumukhwa ink: splashed-ink storm clouds, bold dry calligraphic brush strokes in manes, fur, feathers, robes and grass, ink bleeding into wet wash, small ink splatters and drips near the frame edges, patches of bare rice paper where the edges dissolve; oil glazes only deepen the darks, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. Movie-poster key art: bold iconic silhouette, the two subjects large and close, one dramatic low angle, one bright break of light behind them, big dark masses, few hues plus one accent, film-poster drama but NO text, NO title, NO credits, NO logo, NO seal stamp. Not photoreal, not 3D. No glow aura, no halo, no emissive outline — the accent colour is real light. One of each named person. No watermark. CANON — QUEEN SUNDUK — FACE and garments from attached /ch_sunduk.png (face only; invent a new pose). Hair ornament matches attached /bn_sunduk.png when the head is visible. Look: Pale oval face, dark calm eyes; black hair in a full coiled updo; when crowned, the gold Silla tree-and-antler crown hung with jade gogok. Dress: Crimson court robe with gold phoenix brocade, blue embroidered cape-collar, a red ribbon bow at the chest. Demeanor: Composed, faint smile, wit in the eyes; looks up at the sky (Cheomseongdae). Never weepy, never cowed. #E8552B as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: Tang empress costume; fantasy tiara in place of the Silla gold crown. | CHUNMA (천마, hyukgose's heavenly horse, guardian of Silla) — attached board /obj_chunma.png: WINGLESS white heavenly horse in the Cheonmachong saddle-flap style: long arched neck, streaming white mane and tail, legs flung out in a flying gallop. It has NO WINGS — no feathers, no bird wings, nothing growing from the shoulders. It rides the sky on curling cloud-and-flame streamers trailing from its legs and chest, as on the painted birch-bark flap. Divine render: numinous through scale and atmosphere, never a glow outline. Kneels and cries beside the purple egg at Najeong, sees men approach, neighs and rises into the sky. | PLACE Surabol (서라벌 (경주)) — attached board /pl_eastern_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Seorabeol palace: Silla giwa halls, packed-earth yards, timber verandas. | HORSE ANATOMY is a centrepiece: the whole horse body reads clearly and beautifully — arched neck, deep chest, sloping shoulder, round haunch, clean long legs in a correct gait, every muscle modelled by the one hard key with a bright edge along the topline and deep shadow under the belly; the horse is never cropped into a blob, never hidden behind dust, never stiff like a toy; mane and tail as flowing painted strokes; the coat colour exactly as the board. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS are a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST room (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt) painted in that same wash-and-glaze: a warm umber-to-black ground, walls, timber, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft with soft sfumato falloff — the webtoon figures are set INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. ONE DEVICE: the father-and-son pyramid as the only upright shape against the vast sky. The only warm light: a squat granite stone lantern (seokdeung) beside them, raking across both. The city a dark band of giwa roofs with tiny lamp points. No glass lanterns. Faces drawn, matching the attached portraits. No text. Look: Slim and elegant; shoulder-length loose black hair parted in the middle; thin moustache and goatee stubble; amused eyes, small knowing smile. Dress: Magenta-crimson silk po with a charcoal sash, dark layered collar. Silk even on campaign. Demeanor: Diplomat and strategist: talks with his hands, smiles while calculating, never shouts; half-lidded watchful eyes. #D8258C as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Look: Square jaw, goatee and moustache, confident grin; arms folded when he is pleased with himself. Dress: As king: crimson robe with gold dragon embroidery, blue shoulder pieces, gold Silla crown. Earlier: prince/hwarang stage portraits. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. blocks.ko: 즉위식 아침

blocks.html: Somebody says it in the corridor, not quite quietly enough. Behind the screen, Princess Dukman is being dressed for a crown. She is thirty-seven, and by noon she will be Queen Sunduk. The maid with the sash stops breathing.
blocks.ko: 누군가 복도에서 그 말을 한다. 충분히 작은 목소리는 아니다. 병풍 뒤에서는 덕만공주가 왕관을 쓰려고 옷을 입는 중이다. 서른일곱. 정오면 선덕여왕이 된다. 띠를 매던 시녀가 숨을 멈춘다.

blocks.html: The old king is dead, and in Silla only Sacred Bone may wear the crown. The Sacred Bone men have run out. What is left is women: Dukman, her older sister, and a cousin named Seungman who is very glad it isn’t her.
blocks.ko: 선왕이 승하했다. 신라에서 왕관은 성골만 쓸 수 있다. 그런데 성골 사내가 바닥났다. 남은 건 여자들이다. 덕만, 그 언니, 그리고 그게 제가 아니라서 몹시 다행인 사촌 승만.

blocks.hanja: 骨品
blocks.html: Bone, as in the bone you were born with. Sacred Bone may wear the crown. True Bone may run the country. Everyone else may count the robes.
blocks.ko: 뼈. 타고난 그 뼈다. 성골은 왕관을 쓸 수 있다. 진골은 나라를 굴릴 수 있다. 나머지는 옷 색깔을 셀 수 있다.

blocks.html: Which of the three it will be is settled the night before, in a pavilion off the pond, by six men and a brazier. By morning the palace has a name, and the name has to be dressed.
blocks.ko: 셋 중 누가 될지는 전날 밤, 연못가 작은 정자에서 여섯 사내와 화로 하나가 정한다. 아침이 되자 궁에는 이름이 하나 생기고, 그 이름에 옷을 입혀야 한다.

en: Ridiculous. Yes.
Name me the man, my lord. The Sacred Bone one. I’ll wait.
lines: 그럼 그 사내 이름을 대 보게. 성골 사내 말일세. 기다리겠네.

blocks.html: The corridor suddenly remembers it has somewhere else to be.
blocks.ko: 복도가 갑자기 다른 볼일이 생각난 모양이다.

en: Tie it tight. If I’m going to be ridiculous, I won’t be late as well.
lines: 단단히 매거라. 우스운 건 그렇다 쳐도, 늦기까지 할 순 없지.

blocks.html: One man stays at the door, where a guard would stand if the guard were the most famous swordsman in Silla. Kim Yushin is thirty-seven. He runs the Hwarang yard: horse, bow, gyuku, the place boys learn whether they matter. People call him the Sword of Silla. He is also, everyone notices, very fond of the princess.
blocks.ko: 문 옆에 한 사내만 남는다. 호위가 설 자리다. 그 호위가 신라에서 가장 이름난 검객이라는 것만 빼면. 김유신, 서른일곱. 화랑의 연무장을 맡고 있다. 말, 활, 격구. 소년들은 거기서 제가 중요한 사람인지 배운다. 사람들은 그를 신라의 도검이라 부른다. 그리고 다들 눈치챘듯, 공주를 유난히 아낀다.

blocks.caption: Thirty-seven. Gaya blood, Silla rank, and the yard is his.
blocks.ko: 서른일곱. 가야의 피, 신라의 품계, 그리고 마당은 그의 것.

en: You heard him.
I put on this confident face, but honestly — me, a king…
I’ll do it no matter what. I just don’t know if I can.
lines: 난 이렇게 당당한 척은 하지만, 솔직히… 내가 왕이라니.
무슨 일이 있어도 할 걸세. 다만 해낼 수 있을지를 모르겠어.
이 세상에서, 항상 공주님 편인 한 명이라도 있으면 좋지 않겠습니까?
en: Whether you do it well or badly —
that is what “no matter what” means.
In all this world, wouldn’t it be good to have one person always on your side, Princess?
Hwarang Kim Yushin.
I will serve you to the end.

blocks.html: She laughs. Nobody else will hear her do that today. Then the bells start.
blocks.ko: 그녀가 웃는다. 오늘 다른 누구도 듣지 못할 웃음이다. 그리고 종이 울리기 시작한다.

blocks.label: The Palace Road
blocks.ko: 궁궐 길

blocks.html: Across the palace, Yushin’s little sister is late. Munhee is getting her hair done at the gate, because her husband has already saddled the horses.
blocks.ko: 궁 건너편에서는 유신의 누이가 늦고 있다. 문희는 대문 앞에서 머리를 매만지는 중이다. 남편이 벌써 말에 안장을 얹었기 때문이다.

blocks.caption: Twenty-six, sharp-tongued, and married to the wrong man on purpose.
blocks.ko: 스물여섯, 입이 매섭고, 일부러 엉뚱한 남자에게 시집간 여자.

lines: 귀족 여인에게 영 어울리지 않는구나… 얘야, 더 나은 걸 못 찾겠니?
en: Totally unfit for a Noble woman… Come on, boy, can’t you find something better?

blocks.html: Her husband Chunchu is twenty-nine, and already the most cunning man in Samhan. Only the quiet rooms know it yet.
blocks.ko: 남편 춘추는 스물아홉, 벌써 삼한에서 가장 교활한 사내다. 아직은 조용한 방들만 그걸 안다.

blocks.caption: Spring and autumn. Also the name of the oldest chronicle Confucius ever edited. He means to be in the next one.
blocks.ko: 봄과 가을. 공자가 엮은 가장 오래된 역사책의 이름이기도 하다. 그는 다음 역사책에 들어갈 작정이다.

blocks.html: Gotaso sits in front of him on the same horse. Bupmin, six, has his own, and will not share the saddle.
blocks.ko: 고타소는 아버지와 같은 말 안장 앞자리에 앉는다. 여섯 살 법민은 제 말이 있고, 안장을 나눠 타지 않는다.

blocks.caption: Chunchu’s daughter. Whatever it is, she wants it faster.
blocks.ko: 춘추의 딸. 무엇이든 더 빨리 가길 원한다.

en: Faster.
Father. Faster.
You'll bite your tongue.
Then you'll talk less, which — wait, that's the joke? Fine. Hold on.
lines: 그러면 말이 줄지 — 잠깐, 그게 농담이냐? 그래. 잡아.

en: I'm not racing.
I'm following. That's different.
That's a lawyer's horse, son.
Look at you. I'm going to tell your mother you invented a new kind of slow.
lines: 봐봐. 어머니한테 네가 느린 걸 새로 발명했다고 이를 거야.

blocks.html: The road climbs past the hill where adults invent countries. Bupmin reins in and looks down at the city, where the slaves are already sweeping the coronation road.
blocks.ko: 길은 어른들이 나라를 만드는 언덕을 지나 오른다. 법민이 고삐를 당기고 아래 도성을 내려다본다. 노비들이 벌써 즉위식 길을 쓸고 있다.

blocks.caption: Six years old, and already drafting laws for the people with no bones.
blocks.ko: 여섯 살. 벌써 뼈 없는 사람들을 위한 법을 짜고 있다.

en: When I’m king everyone has to listen to me.
Even the bone people.
…And the ones with no bone. Those most, there’s more of them.
lines: 나 임금 되면 다들 내 말 들어야 돼.
…뼈 없는 사람들도. 그 사람들이 더 많으니까 더 들어야 돼.

en: Listen to him.
He gets the sentences from you. The volume is his own.
lines: 저 아이 말 좀 들어 봐요.
문장은 당신한테서 가져가는데, 목청은 지 거예요.

en: …Keep that.
I may need to borrow it back when I am braver.
lines: 내가 더 용감해지면 다시 빌릴지도 모르니.

blocks.html: Chunchu looks up the hill. He made a country up there once, with Yushin, when he was nine and the stars were still negotiable. Neither of them tells it the same way twice.
blocks.ko: 춘추가 언덕 위를 올려다본다. 거기서 한번 나라를 만든 적이 있다. 유신과 함께, 아홉 살이었고 별도 아직 흥정이 되던 시절이었다. 둘 다 그 이야기를 할 때마다 조금씩 다르게 한다.

blocks.html: Two boys on a hill above Surabol, lying on their backs, arguing about the sky.
blocks.ko: 서라벌이 내려다보이는 언덕. 두 소년이 드러누워 하늘을 두고 다투고 있다.

en: Brother. That star, in the east.
That one’s the brightest, isn’t it?

lines: 그건 별이 아니라 행성이다, 이 녀석아.
en: That is a planet, not a star, you idiot.

lines: 그럼 더 좋지요. 별들 사이에 섞여 있으면서 별이 아니잖습니까.
en: Even better. It sits among the stars without being one of them.
Just like you.

lines: 고려도, 백제도, 신라도 없이. 그냥… 사람들만.
그리고 그 위에, 모두를 위한 임금 하나.
en: Brother. Let us make Samhan one country.
No Goguryeo, no Baekje, no Silla. Just… people.
And over them, one king for all of them.
“A king for all.”
…You be that. I will stand beside you.
That is a promise, then.

blocks.html: Then the bells change, and the whole family is late for a coronation.
blocks.ko: 그때 종소리가 바뀌고, 온 집안이 즉위식에 늦는다.

blocks.label: The Throne Hall
blocks.ko: 정전

blocks.html: In the hall the sleeves are the census. Purple at the front for True Bone, then scarlet, blue and yellow, down to the doors. You can read a man before he speaks.
blocks.ko: 전각에서는 소매가 호적이다. 앞줄은 진골의 자주색, 그 뒤로 붉은색, 푸른색, 노란색이 문까지 이어진다. 입을 열기 전에 사람을 읽는다.

blocks.html: Past the yellow there is no colour at all. The men holding the canopy poles wear undyed hemp. Nobody counts them.
blocks.ko: 노란색 너머엔 아무 색도 없다. 일산 장대를 든 사내들은 물들이지 않은 삼베를 입었다. 아무도 그들을 세지 않는다.

en: Slaves, Princess. They aren’t in the count.

lines: …사람을 사람 수에 넣지 않는 나라가, 어떻게 천 년을 가겠는가.
en: …A country that does not count people as people. How is that meant to last a thousand years?

blocks.html: Then she walks the length of the hall alone. Two hundred sleeves bow, some of them late.
blocks.ko: 그러고 그녀는 홀로 전각 끝까지 걷는다. 소매 이백 개가 고개를 숙인다. 몇은 늦게.

blocks.html: The crown is carried by the oldest man on the Council. She knows the voice. This morning it said “ridiculous” in her corridor.
blocks.ko: 왕관은 화백의 가장 늙은 사내가 받쳐 든다. 그녀는 그 목소리를 안다. 오늘 아침 그녀의 복도에서 “웃기지도 않는군” 하던 목소리다.

en: Still ridiculous, my lord?
…Entirely, Majesty.
Hold still. It’s heavier than it looks.
So am I.

blocks.html: He sets it on her head. It fits. Nobody mentions it.
blocks.ko: 그가 왕관을 그녀 머리에 얹는다. 꼭 맞는다. 아무도 그 말을 하지 않는다.

blocks.html: And so she becomes the first Queen of Silla. They will call her Queen Sunduk, the Blue Moon of the Divine Country.
blocks.ko: 그렇게 그녀는 신라의 첫 여왕이 된다. 사람들은 그녀를 선덕여왕, 신국의 푸른 달이라 부를 것이다.

blocks.hanja: 德曼性寬仁明敏。
blocks.html: Deokman was generous and humane by nature, clear-sighted and quick.
blocks.ko: 덕만은 성품이 너그럽고 어질며, 총명하고 민첩하였다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 5, Silla Annals — Queen Seondeok, accession notice

blocks.hanja: 聖骨男盡 故女王立
blocks.ko: 성골의 사내가 다하였으므로, 여왕이 섰다.
blocks.html: The sacred-bone males were exhausted, and therefore a queen was set up.
blocks.source: Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) bk. 1, Royal Chronology (王曆) — Queen Seondeok

blocks.label: The Yard
blocks.ko: 마당

blocks.html: The capital’s daughters follow the Sword of Silla around the yard. He does not look at them. He looks only at the Queen.
blocks.ko: 도읍의 딸들이 마당에서 신라의 도검을 따라다닌다. 그는 그들을 보지 않는다. 여왕만 본다.

en: The marshal walked past.
I know. Don’t look.
…I’m looking.
The most popular man in Silla, and he will not even turn his head.
If he smiled once the colonnade would fall over.
lines: 신라에서 제일 인기 있는 남자인데, 고개도 안 돌리네요.
한 번만 웃으면 회랑이 쓰러질 거예요.

blocks.html: Then the yard-coat is open down the spine, and she sees the width of his back — muscle the court is not supposed to want — and the Queen’s face goes vermilion before she can pretend it is the sun.
blocks.ko: 그러다 연무장 도포가 등줄기를 따라 열리고, 그녀는 그 등의 너비를 본다 — 조정이 원해서는 안 되는 근육 — 여왕의 얼굴이, 햇볕 탓으로 돌리기도 전에 주홍으로 오른다.

blocks.html: The Queen has forgotten to look away.
blocks.ko: 여왕은 눈을 돌리는 걸 잊었다.

en: Are you feeling alright, your majesty?
Hm? (startled)
Look at me.
Not the door. (smiles)

blocks.html: For a moment neither of them says anything. Then she straightens, and she is the Queen again.
blocks.ko: 잠시, 둘 다 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 이윽고 그녀는 등을 펴고, 다시 여왕이 된다.

en: …Once.
Once what.
Call me by name, not by title. / Today, since it is the last day for it.
…Yushin-ah.

blocks.html: Nobody in the yard hears it. She will not say it again until a night of small rain, years from now. He will still hear it on the day he dies.
blocks.ko: 마당의 누구도 듣지 못한다. 그녀는 여러 해 뒤, 가랑비 내리는 어느 밤까지 다시는 그 이름을 부르지 않는다. 그는 죽는 날에도 그 소리를 들을 것이다.

lines: 나는 새벽까지 앉아 있는 회의를 얻었고.
en: Lord Yushin.
My sister married for love and got a son out of it.
I got a council that sat until dawn.
…Your Majesty.
So from now on — «Your Majesty». Nothing else.
…That is what I have.

blocks.label: The Pledge
blocks.ko: 화랑의 맹세

blocks.html: Then the young knights kneel and pledge themselves to the throne. In front kneels the yard’s Second Blade, a cool young man who has never once waited his turn. You’ll meet him properly last night.
blocks.ko: 젊은 화랑들이 무릎 꿇고 왕좌에 충성을 맹세한다. 맨 앞에는 연무장의 제이검이 있다. 한 번도 제 차례를 기다린 적 없는 서늘한 젊은이다. 그와는 어젯밤에 제대로 인사하게 될 것이다.

lines: 혁거세 성조의 빛에 걸고, 신라의 젊은 화랑들은 여왕 폐하께 영원한 충성을 맹세합니다!
en: By Hyukgosé’s light, we, the young Hwarang knights of Silla, pledge eternal allegiance to the Queen!

blocks.html: At the end of the ceremony, everyone chants for their new queen.
blocks.ko: 의식이 끝나고, 모두가 새 여왕을 연호한다.

blocks.html: May the heavenly White Horse bless this queen… Long live the Queen! Long live the Hwarang spirit! Long live Silla!
blocks.ko: 하늘의 백마여 이 여왕을 축복하소서… 여왕 폐하 만세! 화랑의 얼 만세! 신라 만세!

blocks.label: The Envoys
blocks.ko: 사신들

blocks.html: Silla sends envoys to tell the neighbours. The neighbours have opinions.
blocks.ko: 신라는 이웃 나라들에 사신을 보내 새 여왕을 알린다. 이웃들은 할 말이 많다.

blocks.caption: Baekje’s old king. He has buried a great many Silla plans and keeps the shovel handy.
blocks.ko: 백제의 늙은 임금. 신라의 계획을 수없이 묻었고, 삽은 늘 손 닿는 데 둔다.

lines: 그 진평이 늙은이가 드디어 죽었다고… 흥! 잘됐군. 그런데 딸을 앉혔다고, 어…?
en: So that old brat Jinpyung is finally dead… Bah! Good riddance. And they have seated a daughter, eh…?

blocks.html: In Pyongyang a tired king laughs into his wine and bets on how long her council lasts. Across the eastern sea, a king with an empress for an aunt calls it a trend.
blocks.ko: 평양에서는 지친 임금이 술잔에 대고 웃으며, 그 회의가 얼마나 갈지 내기를 건다. 동쪽 바다 건너에서는 여제를 숙모로 둔 왕이 새 유행이라 부른다.

blocks.caption: The emperor of Tang. The largest empire under heaven, run by a man who has never lost a war.
blocks.ko: 당의 황제. 하늘 아래 가장 큰 제국을, 한 번도 전쟁에 져 본 적 없는 사내가 다스린다.

blocks.hanja: 龍鳳之姿，天日之表，年將二十，必能濟世安民矣。
blocks.html: “The bearing of a dragon and a phoenix, the face of heaven’s sun. Before he is twenty he will rescue the age and give the people peace.”
blocks.ko: “용과 봉황의 자태요, 하늘의 해와 같은 얼굴이다. 스무 살이 되기 전에 반드시 세상을 건지고 백성을 편안케 하리라.”
blocks.source: Jiu Tangshu (舊唐書) bk. 2, Annals of Taizong — a physiognomist on the boy Li Shimin

lines: 여자 임금이라… 동이 오랑캐들이 또 시작이로구나.
꽃이나 보내 주어라. 그 여인에게 어울리는 것으로.
en: A woman king… those Samhan barbarians are at it again, aren’t they?
Send her flowers. Something that suits her.
zh: 女主……東夷又在胡鬧了，是不是？武！備袞龍袍。
zhLatn: Nǚzhǔ… Dōngyí yòu zài húnào le, shì bu shì? Wǔ! Bèi gǔnlóngpáo.

blocks.label: The Peonies
blocks.ko: 모란 그림

blocks.html: He sends her a gift: a painting of peonies in three colours, and a packet of their seeds.
blocks.ko: 그는 선물을 보낸다. 세 가지 빛깔의 모란을 그린 그림 한 폭과, 그 씨앗 한 봉지.

en: …There are no butterflies on these flowers.
Lovely work. Tang brushwork, three colours of— Majesty?
lines: 훌륭한 솜씨입니다. 당나라 붓놀림에, 세 가지 빛깔의— 폐하?
…그리고 황제께서는, 내게 지아비가 없는 걸 알아채셨다고 내가 알아주기를 바라시는 게지.
en: It means no scent.
…And the Second Emperor would like me to know he has noticed I have no husband.
…I’d have hung it in the hall.
Somebody remind me never to play go with Her Majesty.
lines: 폐하와는 바둑을 두지 말라고, 누가 좀 일러 주십시오.

blocks.html: She has the seeds planted anyway. When they bloom, they have no scent. The court decides she is a sage. She knows she simply reads people.

blocks.name: Sunduk
blocks.ko: 선덕

blocks.html: Six men who hate the word “woman” crowned one anyway. One of them carried the crown. How? Go back one night, to a brazier…!
blocks.ko: “여자”라는 말을 질색하는 사내 여섯이, 끝내 여자를 왕으로 세웠다. 그중 하나는 왕관까지 받쳐 들었다. 어떻게? 하룻밤 전, 화로 하나 앞으로 돌아가 보자…!

images.alt: The Coronation of Napoleon as a vast Neoclassical canvas: young Bidam raising the Silla gold crown over Dukman kneeling before him, True Bone elders watching
images.prompt: A parody of Jacques-Louis David’s THE CORONATION OF NAPOLEON, painted exactly like the real enormous canvas: Neoclassical oil, smooth glazing, warm gold and crimson palette, old varnish, a packed ceremonial hall with a crowd of dignitaries in tiers. Same central action: a standing man on the dais raising a crown in both hands above a woman kneeling before him with hands folded, her long train spread behind her, onlookers crowding both sides. The man is young BIDAM (attached white-robed portrait: face and white horse-embroidered robe over plum hanbok); he lifts a SILLA GOLD CROWN with tree-shaped uprights and dangling jade over PRINCESS DUKMAN (attached portrait: face and garments, hair ornament matching the attached binyeo ref) in vermilion #E8552B silk. The hall is a Silla palace of red timber pillars and lattice; the crowd are True Bone nobles in court silk, several looking sour. PARODY RULES: always a hand-made PAINTING, never photoreal. Reproduce the original work’s composition, poses and signature look so it reads instantly as that exact work, with our characters swapped in. If the original is a painting, mural, print or scroll, match its medium, surface and brushwork. If the original is a photograph, film poster, album cover, anime frame or statue, PAINT it: a painterly illustration of that image with visible brushstrokes, simplified forms and anime-adjacent faces, NOT a photo, NOT photoreal skin or pores, NOT a 3D render, NOT a CGI statue. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portraits, recognizable but restyled into the medium; never the portrait’s standing clasped-hands stance. Character hex lives only as real color inside the work (pigment, cloth, light), never a glow aura, halo, emissive skin or neon outline. If a sword is visible it is the ring-pommel 환두대도 (small ring pommel at the heel of the fist, short grip, long straight blade, handle:blade 1:3), never a katana, never a tsuba. No readable text, no title, no credits, no legible inscriptions or signatures (red seal stamps only as blank red squares), no logos, no watermark.

images.prompt: Minimal iconic 2:1 still composed like a symbolic old-master history painting — the BRILLIANT, STRANGE FATHER AND THE CLEVER SON. FAR WIDE, high angle over a night river: still black water fills most of the canvas, a line of pale flat stepping stones runs as one diagonal from the lower-left corner toward the upper-right. Small in the lower-left nine-year-old Chunchu (small magenta jeogori, no headband) stands on the first stone holding up a Korean paper lantern; far along the stones, tiny, his father Yongsu walks away toward the far bank, his back turned. ONE DEVICE: the diagonal of stones and the widening gap between the boy’s lantern and the father’s back; the lantern’s gold reflection stretches across the water toward him. Far bank a black band with tiny lights. Faces drawn, matching the attached portraits. No text. CANON — KIM YONGSU. #6a7cb0 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | KIM CHUNCHU — FACE and garments from attached /ch_chunchu_hwarang.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Slim and elegant; shoulder-length loose black hair parted in the middle; thin moustache and goatee stubble; amused eyes, small knowing smile. Dress: Magenta-crimson silk po with a charcoal sash, dark layered collar. Silk even on campaign. Now: Young hwarang (stage portrait): beardless, eager. Demeanor: Diplomat and strategist: talks with his hands, smiles while calculating, never shouts; half-lidded watchful eyes. #D8258C as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: front-line armored warrior pose; shouting battle face; katana. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: One night earlier. Six nobles, one brazier, and nobody stands up until they all agree.
blocks.ko: 하룻밤 전. 귀족 여섯, 화로 하나. 뜻이 모두 같아질 때까지 아무도 일어서지 않는다.

blocks.label: The Night Before
blocks.ko: 전날 밤

blocks.hanja: 和白
blocks.html: Hwabaek. It means “speaking in harmony,” which is the polite way of saying nobody goes home. It is older than the bone ranks, older than the Buddha in Silla, and it still picks the kings.
blocks.ko: 화백. ‘어울려 말한다’는 뜻이다. 아무도 집에 못 간다는 말을 점잖게 한 것이다. 골품보다 오래됐고, 신라에 부처가 오기보다 오래됐고, 지금도 임금을 고른다.

blocks.html: Night in a small pavilion off the pond. Someone lights the small brazier. The flame is red first.
blocks.ko: 연못가 작은 정자다. 누가 화로에 불을 붙인다. 불꽃은 먼저 붉다.

blocks.html: It runs hotter. The flame turns blue. Only then may the session start.
blocks.ko: 불이 더 뜨거워진다. 불꽃이 푸르게 바뀐다. 그제야 회의가 시작된다.

blocks.html: Each sleeve has a cup of tea and a wooden piece on a personal mat. They vote by setting the piece on either side of the cup.
blocks.ko: 소매마다 차 한 잔과 개인 자리보 위의 나무패가 있다. 잔의 좌우에 패를 놓는 것이 표다.

blocks.html: The Council decides by unanimity. One voice against is enough to stop a name. That is why it takes all night.
blocks.ko: 화백은 만장일치로 정한다. 반대 하나면 이름이 멈춘다. 그래서 밤이 샌다.

blocks.title: Harmony Council · 화백회의
blocks.caption: Six seats, one motion. Initial vote, deliberation, final vote: all six, or the name dies in the room.
blocks.ko: 자리 여섯, 안건 하나. 초투표, 숙고, 최종 투표. 여섯 모두가 아니면 그 이름은 방에서 죽는다.

blocks.html: Six seats. Yushin has none. He has a wall, and he is leaning on it, because the Marshal was invited to answer questions, not to ask them.
blocks.ko: 자리는 여섯. 유신의 자리는 없다. 벽이 있고, 그는 거기 기대어 있다. 대장군은 물음에 답하라고 부른 것이지, 물으라고 부른 게 아니다.

blocks.html: The first count is three to three. A hung jury in silk.
blocks.ko: 초투표는 셋 대 셋. 비단 옷 입은 배심이 갈렸다.

blocks.html: Three pieces go to the yes side of the cup. Three go to the no side.
blocks.ko: 패 셋은 잔의 찬성 쪽, 셋은 반대 쪽.

blocks.title: Initial vote · 초투표 3:3
blocks.caption: Three sleeves for Dukman, three against a woman on the throne. Deliberation is the only door.
blocks.ko: 덕만을 드는 소매 셋, 여왕을 막는 소매 셋. 숙고만이 문이다.

blocks.html: Then the names start. Somebody always tries a man first.
blocks.ko: 이제 이름들이 오간다. 누군가는 꼭 남자 이름부터 꺼낸다.

en: Prince Chunchu, then. His mother is royal.
lines: 그럼 춘추 공은 어떻소. 어머니가 성골이오.

en: And his father isn’t. Chunmyung’s boy is a Noble, Murim. By your own rule.
lines: 아버지는 아니잖소. 천명 공주의 아들은 진골이오, 무림 공. 공의 규칙대로라면.

blocks.html: Chunchu is not in the room. He was nine when he learned why.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 그 방에 없다. 왜 없는지는 아홉 살 때 배웠다.

blocks.html: Chunchu is nine. His father wakes him past midnight, which is normal, and walks him to the stream below the palace, which isn't. Kim Yongsu is the son of a king the Council threw out. The capital has a word for him that it only says after he leaves. He talks to the dark. He laughs a beat late. He adds a granary ledger faster than the clerk can read it.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 아홉 살이다. 자정 넘어 아버지가 그를 깨우는 건 흔한 일이고, 궁 아래 개울로 데려가는 건 흔치 않다. 김용수는 화백이 끌어내린 왕의 아들이다. 도성엔 그가 방을 나간 뒤에만 쓰는 말이 있다. 그는 어둠에 대고 말한다. 한 박자 늦게 웃는다. 곳간 장부는 서기가 읽는 것보다 빨리 머릿속으로 더한다.

blocks.html: Tonight he is laying flat stones across the water by lamplight, one at a time, as if someone on the far bank were waiting for the bridge to be finished before dawn.
blocks.ko: 오늘 밤 그는 등불 아래서 납작한 돌을 하나씩 물 위에 놓고 있다. 건너편 기슭의 누군가가 새벽 전에 다리가 끝나기를 기다리고 있기라도 한 것처럼.

lines: ……아니, 찾지 마. 쳐다보는 거 싫어해. 나처럼.
en: Shh. They’re working.
…No, don’t look for them. They hate being looked at. Like me.
Father… who is?

lines: 네 할아버지가 그 큰 자리에 네 해 앉았다. 세 번 세고 나서, 방이 도로 가져갔지.
그 방은 자길 즐겁게 해 주는 사람을 먹어.
그러니까— 그 방엔 들어가지 마. 다른 데 앉아. 다리 위에 앉든가.
en: Your grandfather sat in the big chair four years. Three counts, and the room took it back.
That room eats the men who amuse it.
So— stay out of that room. Sit anywhere else. Sit on the bridge.
…If not in the room, where does a person sit?
(laughs, a beat late)
Wherever the room has to come to you.

blocks.html: By morning there is a bridge of flat stones across the stream that nobody in the palace remembers ordering. The servants say goblins. Chunchu, who carried the lamp, says nothing at all, and finds he is good at it.
blocks.ko: 아침이 되자 개울 위에 납작한 돌다리가 놓여 있다. 궁에서 그걸 시킨 기억이 있는 사람은 없다. 하인들은 도깨비라고 한다. 등불을 들었던 춘추는 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 그리고 자기가 그걸 잘한다는 걸 안다.

blocks.html: Tonight Chunchu is sitting on the rail of the little bridge over the pond. Every man who leaves the pavilion will have to pass him.
blocks.ko: 오늘 밤, 춘추는 연못 위 작은 다리 난간에 앉아 있다. 정자를 나서는 사내는 누구든 그 앞을 지나야 한다.

en: The Kim of Gaya, then. The Marshal’s blood is royal.
lines: 그럼 가야 김씨는. 대장군의 피는 왕족이오.

en: Royal in a country that no longer exists.
If we start counting kingdoms that no longer exist, half this room is royal.
lines: 없어진 나라까지 세기 시작하면, 이 방 절반이 왕족이오.

blocks.html: By the wall, Yushin does not move. He has heard it before. He will hear it again.
blocks.ko: 벽 앞의 유신은 꿈쩍하지 않는다. 전에도 들은 말이다. 또 듣게 될 말이다.

blocks.caption: Yushin’s old yardmate. Blunt, folksy, and the only man on the Council who has killed a tiger.
blocks.ko: 유신의 연무장 동기. 투박하고 구수하고, 화백에서 호랑이를 잡아 본 유일한 사내.

en: Three left, and all of them in skirts.
Well. Somebody say something new, or we’re here till the frost.
lines: 남은 피는 셋, 셋 다 치마요.
자. 누가 새 말 좀 하시오. 아니면 서리 올 때까지 여기 있을 거요.

blocks.html: The newest member of the Council — a Hwarang barely seated among them — stands up.
blocks.ko: 회의의 가장 새로운 일원 — 겨우 자리를 얻은 젊은 화랑 하나가 일어선다.

blocks.caption: The youngest sleeve in the room. He has never once waited his turn.
blocks.ko: 방에서 가장 어린 소매. 한 번도 제 차례를 기다린 적이 없다.

lines: 어른들께서 오늘 밤 한 마디만 마흔 번 하셨습니다. «여자».
저는 덕만공주를 어릴 적부터 뵈어 왔습니다.
이 방 어느 분도, 그분이 답하지 못할 물음을 던져 보신 적이 없습니다.
법화경에서는 용녀가, 비구들이 반대하기도 전에 성불합니다. 저도 읽었고, 어르신들도 읽으셨지요.
성골이 셋뿐이라면, 저는 그 셋 중 가장 총명한 분을 택하겠습니다.
en: My lords have said one word forty times tonight. “Woman.”
I have known Princess Dukman since I was a boy.
Not one of you has ever put a question to her that she could not answer.
In the Lotus Sutra a dragon girl becomes a Buddha faster than the monks can object. I’ve read it. So have you, my lords.
If only three of the Sacred Bone remain, then I choose the cleverest of the three.

lines: …총명하다는 걸로 왕을 고르면, 내일은 누구 말을 듣소.
en: …If cleverness picks a king, whose cleverness do we hear tomorrow.
Bone is the measure. Bone does not change.

lines: 바닥난 뼈로 나라를 버티는 게, 총명한 여왕보다 더 위험하지 않소.
en: The bone has run out.
Holding a country on empty bone is more dangerous than a clever woman.

blocks.html: Murim looks at the brazier for a long time. Then he moves his piece without a word, the way a man pays a debt he has decided not to argue about. Four to two.
blocks.ko: 무림은 한참 화로를 본다. 그러고는 말없이 패를 옮긴다. 따지지 않기로 한 빚을 갚는 사람처럼. 넷 대 둘.

lines: 한 밤의 연설로 삼백 년을 뒤집기엔, 이 방이 너무 오래됐소.
en: I still… cannot raise my hand.
This room is too old to be turned by one night’s speech.

lines: 답이 왔소. 이 방의 절반은 질문도 안 던져 보고 여자라는 단어만 반복했소.
숙고가 그래서 있는 거요. 초투표를 뒤집으라고.
en: I have put questions to her.
They were answered. Half this room never asked — they only repeated the word woman.
That is what deliberation is for. To overturn the first count.
Alchun. You’ve wrestled worse than a woman.
lines: 알천. 자네는 여자보다 무서운 것과도 붙어 봤잖나.

en: I have taken a tiger.
A tiger has no sex. It has teeth.
…I raise it.

blocks.html: Then a great tiger burst in among the seats. The lords leapt up. Lord Alchun barely moved. He went on talking and laughing, caught the tiger by the tail, dashed it to the ground and killed it. Such was Alchun's strength that he took the head of the mat. Yet all the lords bowed to Yushin's authority.
blocks.ko: 그때 큰 호랑이가 자리 한가운데로 뛰어들었다. 여러 공이 놀라 일어났으나 알천공은 조금도 움직이지 않았다. 태연히 웃으며 이야기하다가 호랑이 꼬리를 잡아 땅에 메쳐 죽였다. 알천공의 완력이 이와 같아 윗자리에 앉았다. 그러나 여러 공은 모두 유신의 위엄에 복종하였다.
blocks.hanja: 時有大虎走入座間。諸公驚起。而閼川公略不移動。談笑自若。捉虎尾撲於地而殺之。閼川公膂力如此。處於席首。然諸公皆服庾信之威。
blocks.source: Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) bk. 1, Marvels (紀異) — the lords' council on Namsan's Ujiam rock

blocks.html: Five to one. Every face in the pavilion turns to the oldest sleeve in it. One voice against is still enough.
blocks.ko: 다섯 대 하나. 정자 안의 모든 얼굴이 가장 늙은 소매에게로 돌아간다. 반대 하나면 여전히 충분하다.

blocks.html: Suljong’s hand is on his piece. It stays there. The brazier, which was blue, is going red again.
blocks.ko: 술종의 손이 패 위에 있다. 그대로 있다. 푸르던 화롯불이 다시 붉어지고 있다.

en: You want me to say she can do it. I don’t know that.
Nobody in this room knows that.
lines: 그분이 해낼 수 있다고 말하라는 거요. 나는 그걸 모르오.

en: No, my lord. Nobody does.
A raft isn’t ashamed of the river. You don’t have to believe in her. Just move the piece to the other side of the cup.
Then call it ridiculous all the way home. Nobody counts the grumbling. They count the pieces.
lines: 뗏목은 강을 부끄러워하지 않습니다. 그분을 믿으실 필요는 없습니다. 패만 잔 건너편으로 옮기십시오.
그리고 댁에 가시는 내내 우습다고 하십시오. 투덜거림은 아무도 세지 않습니다. 세는 건 패입니다.

en: …Ridiculous.

blocks.html: He moves the piece. All six sit on the yes side. He will say the word again in the morning, in a corridor, not quite quietly enough.
blocks.ko: 그가 패를 옮긴다. 여섯이 모두 찬성 쪽에 앉는다. 아침에 그는 그 말을 한 번 더 한다. 어느 복도에서, 충분히 작지 않은 목소리로.

blocks.title: Final vote · 최종 투표 6:0
blocks.caption: Deliberation turns the hung room. Six sleeves. The gate opens.
blocks.ko: 숙고가 미결을 뒤집는다. 소매 여섯. 문이 열린다.

en: …That boy Bidam has no fear in him at all.

blocks.html: Across the floor, Yushin catches the Second Blade's eye. He and Bidam have been trading wins since they were boys in the yard. The count stands at one hundred and eight apiece. Neither lets the other stay ahead for long.
blocks.ko: 마루 건너, 유신이 제이검과 눈을 맞춘다. 그와 비담은 연무장 소년 시절부터 승패를 주고받아 왔다. 수는 백팔 대 백팔. 어느 쪽도 상대를 오래 앞서 두지 않는다.

en: Well stood.
Tomorrow on the yard, the hundred-and-ninth is mine.
Ha. Listen to him.
You still owe me a jar from the hundred-and-eighth. Pay that first.
Today is the country’s business. Tomorrow you can lose to me again.
lines: 하. 이 사람 말하는 것 좀 보게.
백여덟째 판 술 한 동이부터 갚아.
오늘은 나라 일이고. 내일 또 지게 해 주지.

blocks.label: Dawn
blocks.ko: 새벽

blocks.html: The brazier is out by the time Alchun carries the six pieces to the princess’s door. He carries them in his fist, because nobody told him there was a box.
blocks.ko: 알천이 여섯 개의 패를 공주의 문 앞까지 들고 갈 무렵, 화로는 꺼져 있다. 그는 패를 주먹에 쥐고 간다. 담는 함이 있다는 걸 아무도 일러 주지 않았으니까.

en: All six?
All six, Princess. Took till the fire went out.
There’ll be talk. The old men are already at it. “There hasn’t been a real king since the Cloud King.”
lines: 여섯 다요, 공주님. 불 꺼질 때까지 걸렸소.
말이 많을 거요. 늙은이들은 벌써 그러고 있소. “구름왕 이후로 임금다운 임금이 없었다”고.

en: My great-grandfather. They say that at every crowning.
…Four stones on four mountains, and a yard full of boys. And now me.
lines: ……네 산에 비석 넷, 사내아이로 가득한 마당. 그리고 이제 나.

en: We all came out of that yard. Every man who voted tonight.
lines: 우리 다 그 마당에서 나왔소. 오늘 밤 패를 놓은 사내들 전부.

en: Then find me someone who remembers him. Not the stones. The man.
If I’m going to be measured against him, I’d like to see the ruler.
lines: 그럼 그분을 기억하는 사람을 찾아 줘. 비석 말고, 사람으로.
그분한테 재어질 거라면, 그 자부터 봐야겠어.

blocks.html: Every man who voted that night grew up in her great-grandfather’s yard. Who was the Cloud King? Ask anyone in Surabol…!
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 패를 놓은 사내들은 모두 그녀의 증조부가 만든 마당에서 컸다. 구름왕은 누구였나? 서라벌 아무에게나 물어보라…!

logline.en: Ask anyone in Surabol about the Cloud King and they’ll tell you about his stones. Ask anyone in Sabi and they’ll change the subject.
logline.ko: 서라벌 사람에게 구름왕을 물으면 그의 비석 이야기를 할 것이다. 사비 사람에게 물으면 말을 돌릴 것이다.

images.alt: Jinheung the Crescent Moon as a monumental commander under a silver crescent halo, Hwarang bowing in a circle
images.prompt: Anime-painterly crescent-halo blocking, cool monochrome, flat night field, no clouds.

images.alt: A crescent moon floating in vast Silla blue sky above mountain silhouettes - symbol of destiny
images.prompt: Iconic minimal composition: A single crescent moon in brilliant white against vast midnight blue negative space (Silla blue #3E79E4)

images.alt: A golden crown floating in Silla blue space, illuminated by crescent moon - destiny awaits
images.prompt: Cinematic legend: A young king's crown floating alone in vast Silla blue negative space, illuminated by a crescent moon

blocks.html: Ask anyone in Surabol about the Cloud King and they'll tell you about his stones. Ask anyone in Sabi and they'll change the subject. You'll find out why. Not yet.
blocks.ko: 서라벌 사람에게 구름왕을 물으면 그의 비석 이야기를 할 것이다. 사비 사람에게 물으면 말을 돌릴 것이다. 왜인지는 알게 된다. 아직은 아니다.

blocks.caption: The Cloud King’s shade, and where it fell.
blocks.ko: 구름왕의 그늘, 그리고 그 그늘이 드리운 곳.

blocks.label: Coronation Night
blocks.ko: 즉위식 밤

blocks.html: On her first night as queen, Sunduk does not sleep. Alchun has found her a man who remembers. He is seventy-one, the last boy left from the Cloud King’s yard, and he arrives in a litter, complaining about the stairs.
blocks.ko: 여왕이 된 첫날 밤, 선덕은 잠들지 않는다. 알천이 기억하는 사람을 찾아 왔다. 일흔하나, 구름왕의 마당에서 남은 마지막 소년이다. 그는 가마를 타고 와서 계단 불평부터 한다.

blocks.speaker: The Old Hwarang
en: Majesty. You wanted the Cloud King.
Everyone loses to him, you know. He’s dead. The dead stop making mistakes.
lines: 다들 그분한테 집니다. 돌아가셨으니까요. 죽은 사람은 더 실수를 안 하거든요.

en: Then tell me his mistakes. I’ve heard the rest all day.
lines: 그럼 그분 실수를 말해 주게. 나머지는 하루 종일 들었네.

blocks.html: He was seven when they put the crown on him. It was too big, and nobody mentioned it. By the end, Silla had a river, a coastline and Gaya. He got there by being the best ally in Samhan, right up until the afternoon he wasn't.
blocks.ko: 왕관을 쓸 때 그는 일곱 살이었다. 왕관은 너무 컸고, 아무도 그 말을 하지 않았다. 마지막엔 신라가 강 하나, 해안 하나, 그리고 가야를 쥐고 있었다. 그는 삼한에서 가장 믿을 만한 동맹이라서 거기까지 갔다. 믿을 수 없게 된 그 오후까지는.

blocks.caption: The Cloud King. Wherever he rides, the border rides after him.
blocks.ko: 구름의 왕. 그가 말을 달리면 국경이 뒤따라 달린다.

blocks.html: He put up stones wherever he stopped — four of them, on mountains, at the edges of what he had taken — and the stones do not boast. They say who came, and when, and that the land is now inside the border. They are property deeds.
blocks.ko: 그는 멈추는 곳마다 비를 세웠다. 넷을. 산 위에, 제가 취한 것의 가장자리에. 그 비들은 뽐내지 않는다. 누가 언제 왔는지, 그리고 이 땅이 이제 국경 안이라는 것을 적었을 뿐이다. 등기 문서다.

blocks.speaker: The Old Hwarang
en: There’s no boasting on those stones at all. I’ve read them. I climbed two mountains to do it.
Boasting is for men who are worried about losing it.
lines: 그 비석들엔 자랑이 하나도 없습니다. 제가 읽어 봤지요. 그거 읽자고 산을 둘이나 올랐습니다.
자랑은 뺏길 걱정을 하는 사람이나 하는 겁니다.

blocks.html: On the twenty-first day of the eighth month, in the first year of Taechang, the Great King Jinheung toured the lands in his keeping, and had this cut into stone. … And so the borders were carried out on every side, and people and land were won far and wide. Neighbouring countries swore good faith, and envoys of peace came and went.
blocks.ko: 태창 원년 무자년 8월 21일 계미일, 진흥태왕이 다스리는 땅을 순수하고 돌에 새겨 기록한다. …… 이로써 사방으로 경계를 넓혀 백성과 땅을 널리 얻었고, 이웃 나라는 신의를 맹세하였으며 화친의 사신이 오갔다.
blocks.hanja: 太昌元年歲次戊子八月卄一日癸未，眞興太王巡狩管境，刊石銘記也。……因斯四方託境，廣獲民土，隣國誓信，和使交通。
blocks.source: Jinheung Stele (眞興王巡狩碑), Maunnyeong stone (磨雲嶺碑), front face (568)

blocks.html: Late in his reign he invents the Hwarang. Take the noblest boys and put them in one yard. Make them ride, sing and rank each other until the ranking feels like fate. Nearly every man who matters later comes out of that yard.
blocks.ko: 말년에 그는 화랑을 만든다. 가장 귀한 집 소년들을 한 마당에 모은다. 말 타고 노래하고 서로 순위를 매기게 한다. 순위가 운명처럼 느껴질 때까지. 훗날 중요해지는 사내는 거의 다 그 마당에서 나온다.

blocks.hanja: 花郞
blocks.html: “Flower youths.” Noble sons in powder and silk, taught to ride, to sing, and to die, in about that order. The name is a joke. The enemy stopped laughing at it in the second generation.
blocks.ko: ‘꽃 같은 사내’. 분 바르고 비단 입은 귀족 자제들이 말 타기, 노래, 죽는 법을 대략 그 순서로 배운다. 이름은 농담이다. 적들은 두 번째 기수쯤에서 웃기를 그만뒀다.

blocks.html: Every man who voted for her last night came out of that yard. So did the old man in the litter, in its first years, when it was still mostly bruises.
blocks.ko: 어젯밤 그녀에게 패를 놓은 사내들은 모두 그 마당에서 나왔다. 가마 속 늙은이도 그랬다. 처음 몇 해, 아직 거의 멍뿐이던 시절에.

blocks.html: Near the end he shaved his head. The king of the four mountain stones put on a monk's robe and took a new name: Dharma Cloud. His queen went into a nunnery beside him. The court kept calling him Majesty. He kept answering to the other thing.
blocks.ko: 말년에 그는 머리를 깎았다. 네 산에 비석을 세운 왕이 승복을 입고 새 이름을 받았다. 법운. 법의 구름. 왕비도 그 곁 절로 들어갔다. 조정은 계속 전하라 불렀다. 그는 계속 다른 이름에 대답했다.

en: Why the robe? He had everything.

blocks.speaker: The Old Hwarang
en: I asked him that. I was fifteen and stupid. Same question, worse manners.
lines: 저도 여쭸습니다. 열다섯에, 멍청했지요. 같은 질문인데, 버릇은 더 없었고요.

blocks.html: A boy is losing in the yard when a bald monk leans on the fence and laughs at him. Everyone else is kneeling. The boy is too busy losing to notice.
blocks.ko: 한 소년이 연무장에서 지고 있을 때, 까까머리 중 하나가 울타리에 기대 그를 보고 웃는다. 다른 이들은 다 무릎을 꿇고 있다. 소년은 지느라 바빠서 그걸 못 본다.

en: You drop your shoulder before you swing. He knows what you’ll do before you do.
lines: 휘두르기 전에 어깨가 먼저 떨어지는구나. 네가 뭘 할지 저놈이 너보다 먼저 안다.

blocks.speaker: The Boy
en: Who asked you, monk?
Nobody. That’s the nice thing about this robe.
lines: 아무도. 이 옷의 좋은 점이 그거다.

blocks.html: Then the boy sees the kneeling yard, and the face under the shaved head, and goes down in the dust so fast he bruises a knee.
blocks.ko: 그제야 소년은 무릎 꿇은 마당을 보고, 깎은 머리 아래 얼굴을 본다. 얼마나 빨리 엎드렸는지 무릎이 멍든다.

blocks.speaker: The Boy
en: Majesty— why— the robe, Majesty, why?
lines: 전하— 어찌— 그 옷은, 전하, 어찌하여?

en: They put a crown on me at seven. It was too big. I grew into it.
Then I filled it. A river. A coast. A kingdom.
Everything I won, I won from a friend first.
…The robe is lighter. Get up. Fix your shoulder.
lines: 일곱 살에 왕관을 씌우더구나. 너무 컸지. 자라서 맞췄다.
그다음엔 채웠다. 강 하나. 바닷가 하나. 나라 하나.
얻은 건 전부, 먼저 벗한테서 얻은 것이다.
……이 옷이 더 가볍다. 일어나라. 어깨나 고쳐라.

en: From a friend. Which friend?

blocks.speaker: The Old Hwarang
en: He never said. He died that same year.
Ask in Sabi, Majesty. They’ll change the subject. That’s how you know.
lines: 사비에 가서 물어보십시오, 폐하. 말을 돌릴 겁니다. 그걸로 아는 거지요.

blocks.speaker: The Old Hwarang
en: We called him the Cloud King, after the name he took at the end.
A cloud has no border, you see. It goes where it likes, and for an afternoon the ground underneath is its ground.
A cloud never asks whose field it’s raining on.
lines: 우리는 그분을 구름왕이라 불렀지요. 마지막에 받은 그 이름 따라서.
구름엔 경계가 없거든요. 가고 싶은 데로 가고, 한나절은 그 아래 땅이 다 제 땅입니다.
구름은 누구 밭에 비를 뿌리는지 묻지 않습니다.

blocks.html: The queen sits with that a long time. Her great-grandfather marked the edges of what he took. She has nothing to take, and a council that counts her every step.
blocks.ko: 여왕은 오래 그 말을 곱씹는다. 증조부는 제가 취한 것의 가장자리에 표시를 했다. 그녀에게는 취할 것이 없고, 걸음마다 세는 회의가 있다.

en: He put his stones at the edges.
…I’ll put one in the middle, and point it at the sky. Nobody can say I took that from a friend.
lines: ……나는 한가운데 세우겠네. 하늘을 향해서. 그건 벗한테서 뺏었다고 아무도 못 하겠지.

blocks.html: Within a year there is a stone tower in the middle of Surabol for reading the stars. It boasts about nothing. It just looks up.
blocks.ko: 한 해가 안 돼 서라벌 한복판에 별을 읽는 돌탑이 선다. 아무것도 뽐내지 않는다. 그저 올려다볼 뿐이다.

blocks.html: The rain fell on Baekje’s field, and Baekje kept the grudge. In five days, it names the prince who will inherit it…!
blocks.ko: 그 비는 백제의 밭에 내렸고, 백제는 원한을 간직했다. 닷새 뒤, 백제는 그 원한을 물려받을 왕자를 세운다…!

logline.en: Thirty-two is late to be named crown prince. By then the clans have had years to decide which of his sons they own.
logline.ko: 서른둘은 태자가 되기엔 늦은 나이다. 그 사이 가문들은 그의 아들 중 누구를 가질지 정할 시간이 넉넉했다.

Below him, sinking, the limp boy in white with the rope on his ankle and the dark mass of willow branches dragging them down. ONE device: the rope as a hard diagonal line from corner to corner. A shaft of moonlight from above catches the knife steel, bubbles and Euija's straining face in amber #e08a2e bounce off the silt. Ink-black water, painted bubbles, manga speed lines in the water. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM).
