Interior night, the Eastern Hall of the Yeon mountain fortress (attached pl_yeon_fortress board: stone, dark timber, one red munru; snow visible through an open lattice door behind). LOW THREE-QUARTER ANGLE at floor level beside an iron brazier set on the stone floor, its coals the practical key raking up from below. ONE DEVICE: the two hands meeting in the exact centre of the frame over the brazier glow — an old spotted hand pressing a small square bronze seal on a crimson cord into a big young palm. Yeon Taejo, about seventy, white topknot and long white beard, fur-trimmed charcoal robe, sits upright on a low dais, leaning forward over his staff, face unsmiling, eyes tired and watchful. Yeon Gesomun, thirty, massive, black close beard, kneels on one knee in charcoal robe with red edging (no armor, no helm), head lowered, jaw tight, receiving the seal as if it were heavier than it is. Brazier light #8f3a2e crimson on the old man's beard and the seal's edge; blue snow-light spill from the door behind as the cool counter. Sharp out-of-focus brazier rim in the foreground, the pair razor sharp in the midground, the snowy door dissolving into bokeh. Their shadows climb the angled timber wall. Old-master tenebrist canvas, crushed blacks, no clutter. No text. No watermark. CANON — YEON TAEJO — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_taejo.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Gesomun's father and an old man in every still: snow-white hair in a tight topknot tied with dark red cord, long white beard and moustache, the same heavy straight Yeon brows and hard jaw as his sons, deep lines around tired, watchful eyes; shoulders once massive, now slightly stooped. Dress: Retired High Commander's court dress, not armor: long charcoal-black silk robe crossed left over right with deep crimson #8f3a2e edging at collar, cuffs and hem, crimson sash, short dark fur-trimmed overcoat over the shoulders, black boots. Demeanor: Quiet, unsmiling, economical; says half of what he thinks. Reads reports more than once. The only man Gesomun lowers his voice for. Carry: A plain wooden walking staff in the right hand. He no longer wears a sword. #8f3a2e as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: armor or a helm; dark hair or a black beard; a young or vigorous body; shouting; a sword at the hip. | YEON GESOMUN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_gesomun.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Massive, broad-chested; black hair in a tight topknot tied with red cord; thick black beard trimmed close to the jaw, heavy brows, glaring eyes. Dress: Dark charcoal robe and trousers under red-edged armor, a red cape falling off the shoulders. Headwear: the jougwan (see HEADWEAR). Demeanor: Arrogant, theatrical, loud; looks down at people (worm's-eye suits him). Laughs while fighting. #d0362f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: gold-plated armor; beardless face (except a flashback to youth). | HEADWEAR: JOUGWAN (조우관, feather cap) — copy the SHAPE from the attached hat boards and ignore their Korean labels, museum photos, paper-craft gems and dragon medallion: a small black lacquered gauze cap (변형모, a peaked or square-topped crown no bigger than the topknot it covers) set high on the crown of the head over a small knot of gathered hair (any loose hair the portrait shows still falls beneath it); a thin black band round the head with a small square opening at the front; black cords tied under the chin; two long barred pheasant tail feathers (tan with umber bars), or a spray of bird plumes, rising straight up or sweeping back from either side of the cap, much taller than the cap itself. It replaces any other hat or cap on the portrait; headbands and ribbons stay. Real lacquer and feathers lit by the scene key, never a glow. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Goguryeo: attached /ref_hanbok_goguryeo.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. images.alt: Yeon Gesomun on the north wall of Pyongyang, the grown Gulgul a step behind him
images.prompt: Night, deep winter, the north wall of Pyongyang: over-the-shoulder from just behind the grown Gulgul, who stands one step behind Yeon Gesomun at the parapet; both in fur mantles over armor, breath steaming; below, the Taedong river frozen white runs as a long pale diagonal. One brazier on the wall walk is the key, lighting Yeon’s profile and beard. ONE device: the frozen river’s diagonal. Gulgul is a grown man here (thin moustache, short chin beard, weathered). HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). images.alt: Gesomun on the north wall of Pyongyang, arms flung wide
Xue Rengui in white armour in the Andong Protectorate yard, a real Tang compound on Goguryeo ground
images.prompt: Cinematic historical still, 16:9, of a REAL Tang protectorate courtyard: rammed-earth walls, a white banner, timber halls. Xue Rengui in pale armour stands small in the yard. A thin red of old Goguryeo hills on the horizon. Painterly cinema, iconic but geographically real. Flat sky, no clouds. No text, no watermark.

blocks.html: Everyone in the north has a story about the Eternal General. None of them are bedtime stories.
blocks.ko: 북쪽 사람이라면 누구나 영원의 대장군 이야기를 하나씩 안다. 자장가로 들려줄 만한 건 하나도 없다.

blocks.html: This one starts in the snow, two winters after Silla crowned its queen. A young man is caught on the border and dragged to Commander Yeon, who is twenty-nine and holds the east in his father’s name.
blocks.ko: 이 이야기는 눈 속에서 시작한다. 신라가 여왕을 세우고 두 번째 겨울이다. 국경에서 붙잡힌 청년 하나가 연 장군에게 끌려온다. 스물아홉, 아버지의 이름으로 동쪽을 쥔 사내다.

blocks.caption: Twenty-nine. He holds the eastern border in his father’s name, and nobody here calls him a son.
blocks.ko: 스물아홉. 아버지의 이름으로 동쪽 국경을 쥐고 있고, 여기서 그를 아들이라 부르는 이는 없다.

en: Do you know what happens to traitors, young man...?
They say you… leaked our secrets to the enemy.

blocks.speaker: Prisoner
en: I have… no name.
Good. Then nobody will miss it.

blocks.html: It is over quickly, and it is not clean. Nobody in the yard looks away, because looking away is also a report.
blocks.ko: 금방 끝났고, 깔끔하지 않았다. 마당에 선 누구도 눈을 돌리지 않는다. 눈을 돌리는 것 또한 보고가 되니까.

blocks.html: The guards talk about him the way men talk about weather. “He’s a monster, you know. He’s made the Eastern Commandery the safest in the kingdom. The barbarians run if they hear his name.”
blocks.ko: 경비병들은 날씨 얘기하듯 그를 입에 올린다. “저 사람 괴물이야, 알지? 동부 도호부를 나라에서 제일 안전한 데로 만들어 놨잖아. 오랑캐들은 이름만 들어도 도망간다니까.”

blocks.html: Gaesomun*, also called Gaegeum. His surname was Yeon. He claimed he had been born in water, to awe the crowd. He was imposing to look at, and bold and free in spirit.
blocks.ko: 개소문*은 개금이라고도 한다. 성은 연씨이다. 스스로 물속에서 태어났다고 말하여 무리를 현혹하였다. 풍채가 웅장하고 위엄 있었으며, 기개가 호방하였다.
blocks.hanja: 蓋蘇文，或云蓋金。姓淵氏。自云生水中，以惑衆。儀表雄偉，意氣豪逸。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 49, Biographies — Yeon Gaesomun

notes.html: The Korean annals spell him Gaesomun. This book says Gesomun. One man, five swords.
notes.ko: 기록의 개소문이 곧 이 책의 연개소문이다. 영어 표기만 다르다.

blocks.html: The outpost is also a building site. Three summers ago, the Tang flattened Goguryeo’s pile of enemy bones. It is the same emperor who sent Silla’s new queen flowers with no scent. Goguryeo got the message. Now it builds a wall. A thousand li of it. When Yeon isn’t killing anybody, he walks it with a plumb line and kicks the crooked stones.
blocks.ko: 초소는 공사장이기도 하다. 세 해 전 여름, 당이 고구려의 적군 뼈 무덤을 밀어 버렸다. 신라의 새 여왕에게 향 없는 꽃을 보낸 바로 그 황제다. 고구려는 알아들었다. 그래서 지금 성을 쌓는다. 천 리나. 연은 누굴 죽이지 않을 때면 다림줄을 들고 그 성을 걸으며 삐뚤어진 돌을 걷어찬다.

blocks.label: The Burned Village
blocks.ko: 불탄 마을

blocks.html: A month before the summons, in a Mohe village the Eastern Command has finished with, there is a boy who will not move out of the doorway of a house that no longer has a roof. Snow is settling on the ash. He has a shaved crown and two braids, and he holds a stick the way he has seen men hold spears. Yeon gets down off the red bay and walks up until the stick touches his chest.
blocks.ko: 소집령이 오기 한 달 전, 동부대가 일을 마치고 떠난 말갈 마을에, 지붕이 없어진 집 문간에서 비키지 않는 사내아이가 하나 있다. 재 위로 눈이 내려앉는다. 정수리를 밀고 머리를 두 갈래로 땋은 아이가, 어른들이 창 잡는 걸 본 대로 막대기를 쥐고 서 있다. 연은 붉은 밤색 말에서 내려, 막대기 끝이 가슴에 닿을 때까지 걸어온다.

en: Move.

blocks.caption: A Mohe boy Yeon pulled out of the snow. He has followed him ever since.
blocks.ko: 연이 눈 속에서 끌어낸 말갈 소년. 그 뒤로 줄곧 그를 따른다.

en: Do you understand me.

blocks.html: He does not. Yeon looks at him for what his officers later agree was an unreasonable length of time. Then he laughs, the slap of a laugh they will learn to dread, and pulls off his gloves.
blocks.ko: 알아듣지 못한다. 연은 부하들이 뒷날 지나치게 길었다고 입을 모으는 시간 동안 아이를 본다. 그러다 웃는다. 부하들이 두려워하게 될, 뺨을 치는 듯한 웃음이다. 그러고는 장갑을 벗는다.

lines: 이놈 봐라. 다 타 버린 집을 지키고 섰네.
en: Look at this one. Guarding a house that’s already burned.
Good. This is what Goguryeo looks like.
Get on. The second horse.

blocks.html: He hands the gloves down. They do not fit. The boy gets on the second horse anyway, the stick still in his fist.
blocks.ko: 장갑을 내려 준다. 맞지 않는다. 아이는 그래도 막대기를 쥔 채 두 번째 말에 오른다.

blocks.caption: An old Yeon friend. The one man at the outpost who asks the commander questions.
blocks.ko: 연의 오랜 벗. 초소에서 장군에게 질문을 하는 단 한 사람.

en: …You are taking him?

lines: 저 아이가 크면 어디에 서 있을 것 같으냐.
en: Where do you think that boy is standing when he is grown.
…Opposite us, I should think.
That is why I am taking him.

blocks.html: He gives him the name Gulgul, which is not a Goguryeo name and is not a Mohe one either, and raises him in Pyongyang alongside his own sons — one step behind them at every meal.
blocks.ko: 그는 아이에게 걸걸이라는 이름을 준다. 고구려 이름도 아니고 말갈 이름도 아니다. 그리고 평양에서 제 아들들과 함께 기른다. 끼니마다 아들들보다 한 걸음 뒤에서.

blocks.label: The North Wall
blocks.ko: 북쪽 성벽

blocks.html: Years later, on the north wall of Pyongyang in a winter worse than this one, Yeon stands with the grown boy a step behind him and the river frozen white below. He says the thing he says every winter, to anyone in earshot, as if the cold might forget it otherwise.
blocks.ko: 여러 해 뒤, 이번보다 더 혹독한 겨울, 평양 북쪽 성벽 위에 연이 서 있다. 다 큰 아이가 한 걸음 뒤에 있고, 아래로는 강이 하얗게 얼어 있다. 연은 겨울마다, 듣는 사람만 있으면 누구에게나 하는 말을 한다. 추위가 잊어버리기라도 할 것처럼.

en: Cold?
…No, sir.

lines: 우리 임금 한 분이 여기서 돌아가셨다. 백제 화살이었지. 그래도 성은 버텼다.
기억해라. 왕은 죽고, 조정은 지치고, 성은 무너져도—
en: Liar. I’m cold too.
A king of ours died up here once. Baekje arrow. The wall held anyway.
Remember it. Kings die, courts get tired, walls come down—
Goguryeo never dies.

blocks.html: Gulgul grows up quiet. Years from now, Yeon will send him north to guard the marches and give him a surname to take along. Dae. Big, as big as the country.
blocks.ko: 걸걸은 조용히 자란다. 훗날 연은 그를 북쪽 변경으로 보내며 성 하나를 붙여 준다. 대. 나라만큼 크라는 뜻이다.

blocks.label: The Summons
blocks.ko: 소집령

blocks.html: Back in that first winter, the summons comes. The summons isn't addressed to him. It's addressed to his father, who still holds the Eastern seal. Yeon Taejo sat in the capital's big chair for twelve years. Now he is too old to ride that far. The son has done the work for years. The seal is still the old man's.
blocks.ko: 다시 그 첫 겨울. 소집령이 온다. 소집령은 그에게 온 게 아니다. 아직 동부의 인장을 쥔 아버지에게 왔다. 연태조는 도성의 큰 자리에 열두 해를 앉아 있었다. 이제는 거기까지 말을 탈 수 없을 만큼 늙었다. 일은 몇 해째 아들이 해 왔다. 인장은 아직 노인의 것이다.

blocks.caption: The old Eastern Commander. He sat in the big chair long enough to know what it costs.
blocks.ko: 늙은 동부 대가. 큰 자리에 오래 앉아 봐서, 그 값을 안다.

lines: 인장 가져가라. 올해는 네가 내 자리에 앉는다.
en: Take the seal. You sit in my place this year.
…And say half of what you think.

lines: 제가요? 평양엔 제가 왜 가야 합니까?
어차피 쓸데없는 소리나 하려고 주둥이 벌리는 데인데...
en: Me? Why do I have to go to Pyongyang?
It’s a place where mouths open only to say useless things…

lines: 안다. 내가 열두 해를 앉아 있었다.
지금은 네 숙부가 그 자리를 맡고 있다. 너한테 다정하게 굴 거다. 그게 더 나쁘다.
en: I know. I sat in it for twelve years.
Your uncle chairs it now. He’ll be kind to you. That’s worse.
Half, son. Half.

blocks.html: He promised his father half. He has never said half of anything. Next stop: Pyongyang, and a room full of men counting grain…!

INTERIORS are a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST room (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt) painted in that same wash-and-glaze: a warm umber-to-black ground, walls, timber, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft with soft sfumato falloff — the webtoon figures are set INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Half, his father said. Yeon manages it until the second pot of tea.
blocks.ko: 반만, 아버지는 그렇게 말했다. 연은 두 번째 차 주전자까지는 그럭저럭 해낸다.

blocks.html: He rides in at the red two-tier gate, in his father’s place. Pyongyang already knows the sound of those hooves.
blocks.ko: 그는 아버지 대신 붉은 이중 문루로 들어간다. 평양은 이미 그 발굽 소리를 안다.

blocks.html: Goguryeo works like this. Five commanders argue at the High Summit. The High Commander holds the first sword. The king has the last word.
blocks.ko: 고구려는 이렇게 돌아간다. 제가회의에서 대가 다섯이 다툰다. 막리지가 첫 칼을 쥔다. 마지막 말은 왕이 한다.

blocks.hanja: 諸加會議
blocks.html: The meeting of the ka. A ka was a tribal chief, back when Goguryeo was five roofs in one valley. The roofs became commands, the chiefs became generals, and the meeting kept its old name, the way old men keep their nicknames.
blocks.ko: 가(加)들의 모임. 가는 고구려가 한 골짜기의 지붕 다섯이던 시절의 부족장이다. 지붕은 군단이 되고, 족장은 장군이 됐지만, 모임은 옛 이름을 그대로 썼다. 노인들이 어릴 적 별명을 버리지 않듯이.

blocks.html: The chamber is already loud when Yeon arrives — not with strategy, with arithmetic. Every banner wants a larger share of the same winter grain.
blocks.ko: 연이 들어올 때 전각은 이미 시끄럽다 — 전략이 아니라 셈으로. 깃발마다 같은 겨울 군량의 더 큰 몫을 원한다.

blocks.html: Five swords sit at this table, a crow stamped in every ring. Nobody draws at the Summit. Everybody comes armed anyway. The South’s grip is worn smooth by Yushin’s passes. The North’s edge is nicked from the Mohe frost. The West oils his scabbard with Liao timber, so he smells faintly of a forest.
blocks.ko: 이 상에는 칼이 다섯 자루 놓인다. 고리마다 삼족오가 찍혀 있다. 제가회의에서 칼을 뽑는 자는 없다. 그래도 다들 차고 온다. 남부의 칼은 유신의 고개에서 손잡이가 닳아 매끈하다. 북부의 칼날엔 말갈 서리에 이 빠진 자국이 있다. 서부는 칼집에 요하 목재 기름을 먹여, 희미하게 숲 냄새가 난다.

blocks.html: The clerk who only keeps the minutes wears one too, because the rules say so. Ink on the grip, none on the edge. By the High Commander’s teacup lies the first sword, a small stone haetae carved under its crow. Yeon left his own at the gate. Junior seats do. He looks at theirs a little too long.
blocks.ko: 회의록만 적는 서기도 규칙이라 한 자루 찬다. 손잡이엔 먹이 묻었고, 날엔 아무것도 없다. 막리지의 찻잔 옆에는 첫 칼이 누워 있다. 삼족오 아래 작은 돌 해태가 새겨져 있다. 연은 제 칼을 대문에 맡겼다. 말석은 원래 그렇다. 그는 남의 칼을 조금 오래 본다.

en: Enough.
I did not call five commands to Pyongyang to divide a granary.
I will be the “King for All” — Samhan under one roof. Silla and Baekje first.
lines: 곳간이나 나누자고 오부를 평양에 부른 것이 아니다.
짐이 “삼한왕검”이 되리라 — 삼한을 한 지붕 아래로. 신라와 백제부터.

blocks.html: He is not the first man this year to want to be king for all. He is the first to want it on a budget.
blocks.ko: 올해 ‘모두를 위한 임금’이 되겠다는 사내가 그가 처음은 아니다. 예산 안에서 되겠다는 사내로는 처음이다.

en: Then the Southern Command takes the next levy.
Yushin’s banners have been testing the passes. If His Majesty wants Samhan, give me men — not speeches.
lines: 유신의 깃발이 고개를 두드리고 있습니다. 폐하께서 삼한을 원하시면 병력을 주십시오 — 연설이 아니라.

blocks.html: The north wants horses. The west wants timber and iron. Both want them from Central, and both say so twice.
blocks.ko: 북부는 말을 원한다. 서부는 목재와 쇠를 원한다. 둘 다 중부에서 받아 내고 싶어 하고, 둘 다 그 말을 두 번씩 한다.

blocks.caption: The High Commander. He chairs the room like a feast and counts it like a granary.
blocks.ko: 막리지. 잔치처럼 회의를 주재하고, 곳간처럼 셈한다.

en: (mild, as if chairing a feast)
Each front believes it is the only front. That is why we meet.
Eastern Command has kept the marches quiet. Let us not reward noise over results.
lines: 전선마다 자기만 전선이라 믿지. 그래서 모이는 것이오.
동부대는 변방을 조용히 지켜 왔소. 성과보다 목소리를 상 주지 맙시다.

en: Quiet?
I have been killing tribes so this room can argue about who gets the horses.
Meanwhile the Second Emperor is not a tribute account. He is a man who murders brothers for a throne and then invents a reason.
lines: 이 방이 말 배분을 놓고 다투라고 내가 오랑캐를 베어 온 줄 아시오.
그사이 당 황제는 조공 장부가 아니오. 왕좌를 위해 형제를 죽이고 나서 이유를 발명하는 사내요.

en: Commander Yeon. Watch your tongue about foreign kings.
We have bought decades with gold. We will buy more — and spend the peace on Samhan.
lines: 연 장군. 외국 임금 혀를 조심하게.
금으로 수십 년을 샀고, 더 살 것이다 — 그 평화로 삼한을 사겠다는 뜻이야.

en: You cannot buy a man who has already decided the price of your head.
I have watched how courts die. They starve the wall that is screaming, and fatten the wall that—
lines: 제 목값을 이미 정한 사내는 살 수 없소.
조정이 죽는 꼴을 봤소. 비명 지르는 성벽은 굶기고, 아첨하는 성벽은—

en: Enough, Commander. We heard you the first time. The whole hall heard you the first time.
lines: 그만하게, 연 장군. 처음에 다 들었네. 온 전각이 처음에 다 들었어.

en: Easy for the East to lecture. You fight people without cities.
I fight Kim Yushin. Send me the next levy or stop talking about Samhan.
lines: 동부가 훈계하긴 쉽지. 당신들은 성 없는 놈들과 싸우니까.
나는 김유신과 싸운다. 다음 징발을 주든지, 삼한 이야기는 그만두시오.

blocks.html: Yeon’s hands are flat on the table. The nails have gone white. This is the face of a man who has already fought the war the room refuses to schedule.
blocks.ko: 연의 손이 상 위에 납작하다. 손톱이 하얘졌다. 방이 일정에 넣기를 거부하는 전쟁을, 이미 싸워 본 사내의 얼굴이다.

en: Listen to yourselves.
Horses. Timber. Bodies. A crown-word.
When the Second Emperor comes he will not ask which of you was most polite in committee.
lines: 당신들 말하는 꼴 좀 들어 보시오.
황제가 오면, 이 중 누가 회의에서 제일 공손했는지는 묻지 않을 거요.

blocks.html: The Southern Commander is up before the sentence is finished. The smooth grip turns once in his palm. Then the blade is out, resting a finger’s width under Yeon’s jaw.
blocks.ko: 말이 끝나기도 전에 남부 대가가 일어선다. 닳은 손잡이가 손바닥에서 한 번 돈다. 그리고 칼날이 나와, 연의 턱 밑 한 마디 거리에 멈춘다.

en: Polite?
Say it again. Say “polite” to the South.
…Nice edge. You keep it sharp.
Pity about the arm holding it.
Commander Son.
Not in my hall.

blocks.html: The blade does not move. The High Commander does not stand. He reaches over and sets two fingers on the flat of it, the way you’d steady a cup about to spill.
blocks.ko: 칼은 움직이지 않는다. 막리지는 일어서지 않는다. 손을 뻗어 칼등에 손가락 두 개를 얹는다. 넘치려는 잔을 붙잡듯이.

en: Daeha. Put it away.
If this room ever cuts my nephew, it will do it properly. In writing.
lines: 이 방이 언젠가 내 조카를 벤다면, 제대로 할 걸세. 글로.

blocks.html: It goes back in on the second try. Yeon touches his throat, looks at his fingers, and finds nothing on them. He watches that scabbard for the rest of the afternoon.
blocks.ko: 칼은 두 번 만에 칼집에 들어간다. 연은 목을 한 번 만지고, 손가락을 보고, 아무것도 묻지 않은 걸 확인한다. 그날 오후 내내 그는 그 칼집을 본다.

en: If you keep defying the king, Commander Yeon…
we may have to name you a traitor.
(to Yeon, almost kindly — which is worse)
Nephew. Sit down. The Summit does not run on prophecies.
lines: 조카. 앉게. 제가회의는 예언으로 돌지 않네.

en: Then keep your Summit.
Keep your tribute. Keep your Samhan dream carved into a budget fight.
When the Second Emperor’s drums reach the Liao, remember who tried to spoil the feast.
lines: 조공도, 예산 싸움으로 깎아 낸 삼한의 꿈도.
황제의 북이 요하에 닿거든 — 잔치를 망치려 한 자가 누구였는지 기억하시오.

blocks.html: He walks out before it ends. Outside, the corridor is very long and very cold. Behind him the chamber returns to numbers — as if he had never brought an emperor into the room.
blocks.ko: 그는 회의가 끝나기 전에 나와 버린다. 밖으로 나서니 복도가 몹시 길고 몹시 차다. 등 뒤에서 전각은 다시 숫자로 돌아간다 — 그가 황제를 방에 들여온 적도 없었다는 듯이.

en: Heaven above… help this foolish country…!

blocks.html: The Tang keep notes on this room. Theirs are less polite.
blocks.ko: 당은 이 방에 대해 기록을 남긴다. 그쪽 기록은 덜 점잖다.

blocks.html: Their highest office is called Daedaero, the High Commander. It ranks with our first grade, and its holder oversees all the business of the state. It changes hands every three years, though a man who does the job well is not held to the term. On the day of handover, if the parties will not submit to each other, they all call out their troops and fight, and the winner takes the post. Their king simply shuts the palace gates and guards himself. He cannot stop it.
blocks.ko: 그 벼슬 가운데 큰 것은 대대로라 부르니, 1품에 견주며 나랏일을 모두 맡는다. 3년마다 한 번 바뀌되, 직책을 잘 해내는 자는 햇수에 구애받지 않는다. 교대하는 날 서로 복종하지 않으면 모두 군사를 거느리고 서로 공격하여, 이긴 자가 그 자리를 차지한다. 그 왕은 다만 궁궐 문을 닫고 스스로를 지킬 뿐, 이를 막지 못한다.
blocks.hanja: 其官大者號大對盧，比一品，總知國事，三年一代，若稱職者，不拘年限。交替之日，或不相祗服，皆勒兵相攻，勝者爲之。其王但閉宮自守，不能制禦。
blocks.source: Jiu Tangshu (舊唐書) bk. 199上, Eastern Barbarians — Goguryeo

blocks.label: The Palace Yard
blocks.ko: 궁 마당

blocks.html: In the yard the Eastern banners answer him anyway — a roar that has nothing to do with the Summit’s minutes.
blocks.ko: 마당의 동부 깃발들은 그래도 그를 받아 준다 — 제가회의 회의록과는 상관없는 함성으로.

en: Look at that — see how Pyongyang loves you.
Of course. The people have never once abandoned me.
It is the politicians…!
lines: 당연하지. 백성은 날 버린 적이 없어.

en: So. That was half?
That was a quarter. You should’ve heard what I didn’t say.
lines: 그게 사분의 일이다. 안 한 말을 들었어야 해.

en: His Majesty wants Samhan under one roof.
The Summit wants the roof itemised.
…Get the horses. I would rather sleep in a tent tonight.
lines: 폐하께서는 삼한을 한 지붕 아래 두고 싶어 하시지.
제가회의는 그 지붕을 항목별로 적고 싶어 하고.
…말 준비해라. 오늘 밤은 천막에서 자는 게 낫겠다.

en: Gold to the Tang for quiet. Grain counted twice. A king who’d rather pay than ride.
There was a time Goguryeo didn’t pay anybody, Dosuryu. Other kings paid us. Silla came begging on its knees, and we rode south and saved it.
Now look at us.
lines: 조용하게 해 달라고 당에 금을 바치고. 곡식은 두 번 세고. 말 타느니 돈 내겠다는 임금이고.
고구려가 아무한테도 바치지 않던 때가 있었어, 도수류. 다른 임금들이 우리한테 바쳤지. 신라가 무릎 꿇고 빌러 왔고, 우리가 남으로 내려가 구해 줬다.

en: That was two hundred years ago.
Then we’re two hundred years late. Get the horses.
lines: 그럼 이백 년 늦은 거지. 말 가져와.

blocks.html: That night, in the tent, a rider finds him. His wife’s time has come, and it has gone badly before.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤, 천막에서 전령이 그를 찾는다. 아내의 해산이 시작됐다. 전에도 잘 안 된 적이 있다.

blocks.label: Birth of Namseng
blocks.ko: 남생의 탄생

blocks.html: He reaches the house after midnight. One lamp, one midwife, and the mother. On the wall hangs a painting of Samsin, the birth goddess, prayed at so often that the paint has gone pale where the hands touch it.
blocks.ko: 그가 집에 닿는 건 자정이 지나서다. 등불 하나, 산파 하나, 그리고 어머니. 벽에는 아이를 점지하는 여신, 삼신의 그림이 걸려 있다. 하도 빌어서 손이 닿는 자리마다 물감이 바랬다.

en: Samsin…
This child alone — please.
…This time — please.

blocks.html: The painting does not stay paint. Samsin steps from the frame the way steam steps from a kettle, and lays a hand where mortal hands have failed.
blocks.ko: 그림은 그림으로 남지 않는다. 삼신이 주전자에서 김이 오르듯 액자에서 내려와, 사람의 손이 닿지 못한 곳에 손을 얹는다.

blocks.caption: The birth goddess. She does not knock.
blocks.ko: 아이를 점지하는 여신. 문을 두드리지 않는다.

en: Do not weep.
I will open the breath.
The name — that is yours to give.

blocks.html: So the first heir arrives under Samsin's hand, the year of the Summit. They call him Namseng. Nobody wanted a poem in the name. It's the sound the room makes when the baby breathes.
blocks.ko: 그렇게 삼신의 손 아래, 제가회의가 열린 해에 맏아들이 온다. 남생. 사내가 났다는 뜻이다. 이름에 시를 넣고 싶은 사람은 없었다. 아기가 숨을 쉴 때 방이 내는 소리, 그게 이름이다.

en: Namseng.
…Heavier than it sounds.
This country. You will have to keep it.

blocks.html: He holds the boy up to the lamp and tells him the only bedtime story he knows: the one about the king who rode south and never counted grain.
blocks.ko: 그는 아이를 등불 쪽으로 들어 올리고, 제가 아는 유일한 옛날이야기를 들려준다. 남으로 말을 달렸고 곡식 따위는 세지 않았던 임금 이야기다.

blocks.html: Once, Silla begged Goguryeo for an army, and Goguryeo came. To meet the king who answered, we go back two centuries…!
blocks.ko: 한때 신라가 고구려에 군대를 빌었고, 고구려는 왔다. 그 부름에 답한 임금을 만나려면 이백 년을 거슬러 가야 한다…!

logline.en: His stele lists sixty-four fortresses. It does not list the nerve it took.
logline.ko: 그의 비석에는 성 예순네 곳이 적혀 있다. 그만한 배짱은 적혀 있지 않다.

blocks.html: Silla is drowning. An army from across the sea is inside its walls, and its king has one move left.
blocks.ko: 신라가 가라앉고 있다. 바다 건너 온 군대가 도성 안에 있고, 신라 왕에게 남은 수는 하나뿐이다.

blocks.caption: Goguryeo’s widest king. The stele ran out of room before he ran out of fortresses.
blocks.ko: 고구려에서 가장 넓은 임금. 성이 바닥나기 전에 비석 자리가 먼저 바닥났다.

blocks.hanja: 生而雄偉，有倜儻之志。
blocks.html: He was born big and imposing, with a will that would not be bridled.
blocks.ko: 태어나면서부터 체격이 크고 웅장하였으며, 얽매이지 않는 뜻을 품었다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 18, Goguryeo Annals — King Gwanggaeto, accession notice

blocks.caption: Watch the red run south. One reign did that.
blocks.ko: 붉은빛이 남쪽으로 번지는 걸 보라. 한 사람의 치세가 한 일이다.

blocks.label: The Burning Capital
blocks.ko: 불타는 도성

blocks.html: The Silla king stands on his own wall and counts the sea-raiders’ fires. They sit on the north road, on the south road, and under the west wall. There are more every night. Below, in the hall, his court is arguing about pride.
blocks.ko: 신라 왕은 제 성벽 위에 서서 바다 도적들의 불을 센다. 북쪽 길에도, 남쪽 길에도, 서쪽 성벽 밑에도 있다. 밤마다 늘어난다. 아래 전각에서는 조정이 체면을 두고 다툰다.

blocks.speaker: A Silla Elder
en: If we ask the north, they will come. And then they will stay.

blocks.speaker: The Silla King
en: And if we don’t ask, the Wa stay. Which guest would you rather feed?
lines: 안 청하면 왜가 눌러앉지. 어느 손님을 먹이고 싶은가?

blocks.speaker: A Silla Elder
en: Majesty, the letter will have to say… they’ll want a word. A low word.
lines: 전하, 서신에는… 그쪽이 바라는 말이 있을 겁니다. 낮은 말이요.

blocks.speaker: The Silla King
en: I know the word. Bring the brush.
I’ll write it myself, so nobody else has to.
lines: 내가 직접 쓰마. 다른 누가 쓰지 않아도 되게.

blocks.label: The Plea
blocks.ko: 청원

blocks.html: His envoy rides north for nine days and kneels in the tent of a Goguryeo king who is twenty-six and has never lost.
blocks.ko: 그의 사신은 아흐레를 북으로 달려, 스물여섯에 한 번도 져 본 적 없는 고구려 임금의 막사에 무릎 꿇는다.

blocks.speaker: Silla’s Envoy
en: The Wa are inside our walls, Great King. My king writes in his own hand.
“Silla is your servant. Save your servant.”
lines: 왜가 우리 성 안에 들어와 있습니다, 대왕. 저희 임금께서 친필로 쓰셨습니다.

en: Servant. He wrote that word himself?
lines: 종이라. 그 글자를 제 손으로 썼단 말이냐?

blocks.speaker: Silla’s Envoy
en: …In his own hand.
Then they’ll come. Fifty thousand of them.
Tell him one thing more, so he hears it from me first. Servants don’t decide when the master’s horsemen go home.
lines: 하나 더 전해라. 나한테서 먼저 듣게. 주인의 기병이 언제 돌아갈지는 종이 정하는 게 아니다.

blocks.html: The Silla king reads the answer twice. The first half saves his kingdom. The second half he does not read aloud.
blocks.ko: 신라 왕은 답장을 두 번 읽는다. 앞의 반이 그의 나라를 구한다. 뒤의 반은 소리 내어 읽지 않는다.

blocks.label: The Horsemen
blocks.ko: 기병

blocks.html: The horsemen come down out of the north like weather.
blocks.ko: 기병들이 날씨처럼 북에서 내려온다.

blocks.speaker: A Silla Lookout
en: Majesty— the north road. That dust isn’t Wa.
lines: 전하— 북쪽 길입니다. 저 먼지는 왜가 아닙니다.

blocks.speaker: The Silla King
en: No. That’s my letter.

blocks.html: From his wall he watches the raiders’ fires go out one by one. Then he watches the red banners come through his own gate, and keep coming.
blocks.ko: 그는 성벽 위에서 도적들의 불이 하나씩 꺼지는 것을 본다. 그다음엔 붉은 깃발들이 제 성문으로 들어오는 것을 본다. 들어오고, 또 들어온다.

blocks.speaker: A Silla Elder
en: They’re still coming in, Majesty.

blocks.speaker: The Silla King
en: I wrote the word. Let them in.

blocks.html: A red sun. The three-legged crow rides south on his banners. The stele will list sixty-four fortresses. It will not list the nerve it took.
blocks.ko: 붉은 해. 세발까마귀가 그의 깃발에 실려 남으로 간다. 비석은 성 예순넷을 적을 것이다. 거기 든 배짱은 적지 않는다.

blocks.html: The horsemen ride at the raiders’ backs, southwest over the big river and into Gaya country. At the last fortress the gate opens before the ladders are even up.
blocks.ko: 기병들은 도적들의 등 뒤를 몰아 남서쪽으로, 큰 강을 건너 가야 땅까지 내려간다. 마지막 성은 사다리를 대기도 전에 문을 연다.

blocks.speaker: A Goguryeo Rider
en: That’s it? I didn’t even get off my horse.

blocks.html: Silla had asked. That’s the part everyone forgets. Then the horsemen ride back to the Silla capital, and don’t leave for fifty years.
blocks.ko: 신라가 청했다. 다들 잊는 대목이다. 그리고 기병들은 신라 도성으로 돌아와, 오십 년 동안 떠나지 않는다.

blocks.html: Silla’s crown princes go north as hostages. The first one is twelve. Silla’s court takes Goguryeo titles. Silla’s army takes Goguryeo orders. It lasts two generations. Silla does not forget it.
blocks.ko: 신라의 태자들이 볼모로 북으로 간다. 첫 번째는 열두 살이다. 신라의 조정이 고구려의 관작을 받는다. 신라의 군대가 고구려의 명을 받는다. 두 세대가 그렇게 흐른다. 신라는 그것을 잊지 않는다.

blocks.html: He goes with a pony and a tutor. At the border he asks how long. Nobody answers him, which is how he finds out.
blocks.ko: 소년은 조랑말 한 필과 스승 하나를 데리고 간다. 국경에서 그는 얼마나 오래냐고 묻는다. 아무도 대답하지 않는다. 그렇게 그는 알게 된다.

blocks.speaker: The Silla Court
en: They did save us.
So why are they still here?

blocks.html: His stele, naturally, remembers it more kindly.
blocks.ko: 그의 비석은 물론 그 일을 더 너그럽게 기억한다.

blocks.hanja: 庶寧其業 國富民殷 五穀豊熟
blocks.ko: 서민이 그 업에 편안하고, 나라는 부유하며 백성은 은성하고, 오곡이 풍성히 익었다.
blocks.html: The common people were at peace in their work; the country was rich and the people abundant; the five grains ripened in plenty.
blocks.source: Gwanggaeto Stele (廣開土王碑), south face, ll. 3–4 (414 CE); Best, “The Kwanggaeto Stele,” p. 147

blocks.html: Two hundred and forty years later a Silla prince will stand in front of a foreign emperor and ask for an army, and every single person in Surabol will know exactly what that costs, because it has been done to them before.
blocks.ko: 이백사십 년 뒤 한 신라의 왕자가 외국 황제 앞에 서서 군대를 청한다. 그리고 서라벌의 모든 사람이 그 값을 정확히 안다. 전에 이미 당해 봤기 때문이다.

blocks.html: The prince who will beg has a son. Bupmin is fifteen now, and his uncle has one question: which rule will you break first…?
blocks.ko: 언젠가 빌러 갈 그 왕자에게는 아들이 있다. 법민이 열다섯이 되었고, 외숙에게는 질문이 하나 있다. 어느 계율을 제일 먼저 어기겠느냐…?

toneNote: A K-drama heart beats inside a season of alliances — vows, longing, and clan hands moving behind every throne.
title: The Five Principles

logline.en: Fifteen is old enough for the headband, and too young to invent a country alone.
logline.ko: 열다섯은 머리띠를 매기엔 충분하고, 혼자 나라를 만들어 내기엔 이른 나이다.
