The master is YUSHIN (attached portrait: face, marshal blue #2A5FB8 robe), stern but softening; the crying boy is young BUPMIN (attached portrait: face) in a Hwarang headband; the pupils are teenage Hwarang cadets in headbands with a few scrolls and a practice bow on the floor. PARODY RULES: always a hand-made PAINTING, never photoreal. Reproduce the original work’s composition, poses and signature look so it reads instantly as that exact work, with our characters swapped in. If the original is a painting, mural, print or scroll, match its medium, surface and brushwork. If the original is a photograph, film poster, album cover, anime frame or statue, PAINT it: a painterly illustration of that image with visible brushstrokes, simplified forms and anime-adjacent faces, NOT a photo, NOT photoreal skin or pores, NOT a 3D render, NOT a CGI statue. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portraits, recognizable but restyled into the medium; never the portrait’s standing clasped-hands stance. Character hex lives only as real color inside the work (pigment, cloth, light), never a glow aura, halo, emissive skin or neon outline. If a sword is visible it is the ring-pommel 환두대도 (small ring pommel at the heel of the fist, short grip, long straight blade, handle:blade 1:3), never a katana, never a tsuba. No readable text, no title, no credits, no legible inscriptions or signatures (red seal stamps only as blank red squares), no logos, no watermark.

images.at: Then make it true at fifteen
images.alt: In torchlight Yushin stands over seventeen-year-old Bupmin and lifts the kneeling boy’s chin with the tip of a long wooden practice staff
images.prompt: Minimal iconic 2:1 still composed like a symbolic old-master history painting — the STRONG, DISCIPLINED UNCLE AND THE APPRENTICE NEPHEW. INTIMATE CLOSE-UP, low angle from the dirt: seventeen-year-old Bupmin on his knees, face and shoulders large in the lower-right, sweat and dust on his cheek, head tipped back, eyes burning up at his teacher. Yushin stands over him in the upper-left holding a long plain wooden practice staff at full arm’s length; its blunt tip rests under the boy’s chin. Yushin looks down, stern, almost proud. ONE DEVICE: the long staff diagonal from the standing mentor to the kneeling student’s chin. A torch below-right lights Bupmin’s face hot gold; Yushin falls into cold shadow. Background pure black with ember bokeh. Wood only. Faces drawn, matching the attached portraits. No text. CANON — KIM YUSHIN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_kim_yushin.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Tall, broad-shouldered, long black hair in a high topknot-ponytail with trailing Silla-blue cloth tails; level hard brows, deep-set eyes. Dress: Silla-blue po and trousers, plum-violet sash knotted at the waist, white inner collar, dark wrapped forearms. Off duty: plain blue po, no jewelry. Now: Marshal: full black beard and moustache; a blue ribbon in the topknot instead of the headband. Demeanor: Confucian: he STANDS — never sits in lotus. Weighs, counts, frowns at sums; tight jaw, rare dry half-smile. Grief shows as stillness, not tears. The most feared warrior in all of Samhan: a line goes quiet when the tall Silla helm and the white horse appear. Massive, deliberate, terrifying at a walk; by Hwangsan (65) heavier and slower than Gyebek but still the man armies are built around. #2A5FB8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: sitting in lotus or holding prayer beads; katana, tsuba or curved blade (ignore the sword drawn on his portrait); two swords at once; blue glow aura. | BUPMIN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_bupmin_hwarang.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Square jaw, goatee and moustache, confident grin; arms folded when he is pleased with himself. Dress: As king: crimson robe with gold dragon embroidery, blue shoulder pieces, gold Silla crown. Earlier: prince/hwarang stage portraits. Demeanor: Cocky, warm, practical; his father's charm with his uncle's spine. #C41E3A as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: katana; Tang dragon robe in place of Silla court dress. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.alt: Bupmin in armour, shouting in the yard
Bupmin in red, running through the night yard
Bupmin grinning, holding a scroll up
Four hwarang spar in the sandy yard, seen from above
images.at: crowd the fence of the yard

blocks.label: Flowering Youth
blocks.ko: 화랑의 꽃

blocks.html: Fifteen is old enough for the headband. It is not old enough to invent a country, though Bupmin keeps trying.
blocks.ko: 열다섯이면 머리띠를 맬 나이다. 나라를 발명할 나이는 아니다. 법민은 그래도 자꾸 해 본다.

blocks.html: The Hwarang train under the Marshal: horse, bow, verse, and above all gyuku, a horse-ball game a lazier age will call polo.
blocks.ko: 화랑은 장군 밑에서 배운다. 말, 활, 노래, 그리고 무엇보다 격구. 훗날 게으른 시대가 폴로라 부를, 말 위의 공놀이다.

blocks.html: His father is in the Council chamber, collecting votes. His uncle keeps the yard, and the yard is where Bupmin lives now.
blocks.ko: 아버지는 화백 회의실에서 표를 모으고 있다. 연무장은 외숙이 지킨다. 법민은 이제 그 연무장에서 산다.

blocks.title: Yard as state · 화랑
blocks.caption: Class 51 still sits together — Bidam, Yushin, Alchun.
blocks.ko: 51기는 아직도 같이 앉는다 — 비담, 유신, 알천.

blocks.html: Yushin does not soften the yard because the boy is royal. He softens nothing. The new boys sleep six to a hall and learn each other's snores before each other's ranks. They trade rumours about the Marshal like relics. He sleeps in his armour. He bathes in a haunted lake. He can hear a lie drop a shoulder at fifty paces.
blocks.ko: 유신은 소년이 왕손이라고 연무장을 무르게 두지 않는다. 무엇 하나 무르게 두지 않는다. 새로 온 소년들은 한 방에 여섯씩 자며, 서로의 골품보다 코 고는 소리를 먼저 익힌다. 장군 소문은 성물처럼 오간다. 갑옷을 입은 채 잔다더라. 귀신 나오는 호수에서 목욕한다더라. 오십 보 밖에서도 거짓말에 어깨 처지는 소리를 듣는다더라.

blocks.html: Girls crowd the fence of the yard the way other towns crowd a market — not for the ball, for the Hwarang. They pretend they came for the verse.
blocks.ko: 소녀들이 연무장 울타리에 모인다. 다른 고을이 장터에 몰리듯 — 공 때문이 아니라, 화랑 때문에. 노래 들으러 왔다고 한다.

lines: 저 채, 가야 쇠심 박은 거냐?
아니 — 월성 측백이지. 작년 시즌 거.
en: That club — Gaya ironwood core?
No — the Moon Palace cypress. Last season’s.
…Last season? And he brought it out?

lines: 진골은 지난 시즌 채를 안 든다.
en: A True Bone does not play last season’s shaft.
Is that law?
Worse.

blocks.label: The Turn
blocks.ko: 굽이

blocks.html: The practice road runs east along the river and bends hard at a split pine. That bend is where boys find out who they are. Gotaso is not supposed to ride it. Gotaso rides it.
blocks.ko: 연습로는 강을 따라 동쪽으로 뻗다가 갈라진 소나무에서 확 꺾인다. 사내애들은 그 굽이에서 자기가 누군지 알게 된다. 고타소는 거기서 달리면 안 된다. 고타소는 달린다.

lines: 지는 사람이 한 달 동안 채 함 들기.
en: Bupmin. To the pine and back.
Loser carries the other one’s club box for a month.
You’re not allowed on the practice road.
…Fine. One month.
Gotaso. Off the road.

lines: 한 번만요, 외숙. 얘가 하자고 했어요.
en: One run, Uncle. He asked me.
I did not—
…One run.

blocks.html: They go off the line together. On the straight he is ahead. At the split pine the horse leans, the ground tilts, and his hands decide for him. He pulls up. Gotaso doesn’t. She takes the bend flat out, one stirrup empty, and comes back laughing with pine needles in her hair.
blocks.ko: 둘이 함께 출발선을 박차고 나간다. 직선에서는 그가 앞선다. 갈라진 소나무에서 말이 기울고, 땅이 기울고, 그의 손이 먼저 정해 버린다. 그는 고삐를 당긴다. 고타소는 안 당긴다. 등자 하나가 빈 채로 굽이를 그대로 돌아 나오더니, 머리에 솔잎을 꽂고 깔깔 웃으며 돌아온다.

blocks.html: The girls at the fence cheer for her, which is worse than laughing. Yushin has watched from the pine the whole time. He does not cheer for anybody.
blocks.ko: 울타리의 아가씨들이 그녀에게 환호한다. 웃음보다 더 아프다. 유신은 처음부터 소나무 곁에서 보고 있었다. 그는 누구에게도 환호하지 않는다.

en: Club box. A month.
Carry it where the girls can see.
Again.
A king for all who cannot hold a saddle is a poem, not a country.
lines: 안장도 못 잡는 모두를 위한 임금은 시이지, 나라가 아니다.

en: Uncle—
Father said it on the hill. I only said it louder. I was six.
lines: 아버지가 언덕에서 하신 말이에요. 저는 더 크게 말했을 뿐이고요. 여섯 살 때.

en: Then make it true at fifteen.
The Hwarang do not train for your father’s cleverness. They train for the hour the cleverness runs out.
lines: 화랑은 네 아비의 꾀를 위해 닦는 게 아니다. 꾀가 바닥날 시각을 위해 닦는다.

en: West of here is Baekje.
Learn a landscape before it learns your name.
lines: 땅이 자네 이름을 익히기 전에, 자네가 먼저 그 땅을 익히게.

blocks.label: Under the Eaves
blocks.ko: 처마 밑

blocks.html: At dusk he gathers the flower youth under the eaves and speaks the Five Principles, the way other houses recite ancestors. A monk wrote them for boys who would never be monks. Loyalty to the king comes first, so nobody can say they missed it. Duty to your father is easy, until the king and your father want different things. The boys elbow each other at no retreat. They go quiet at no needless killing. Boys skip that one. Old soldiers don’t. Each of them is privately certain the Marshal is looking at him. He is looking at all of them.
blocks.ko: 해 질 녘 그는 처마 아래 꽃다운 소년들을 모으고, 다른 집이 조상을 외듯 세속오계를 왼다. 중이 될 리 없는 아이들을 위해 중 하나가 지은 계율이다. 임금에 대한 충성이 맨 앞이다. 못 들었다는 소리는 못 하게. 부모에 대한 효는 쉽다. 임금과 아버지가 서로 다른 걸 원하기 전까지는. 소년들은 임전무퇴에서 서로 팔꿈치를 찌른다. 살생유택에서는 조용해진다. 아이들은 그 계율을 건너뛴다. 늙은 군인들은 안 그런다. 저마다 장군이 바로 자기를 보고 있다고 남몰래 확신한다. 장군은 그들 모두를 보고 있다.

en: Loyalty to the sovereign.
Filial duty to parents.
Trust among friends.
No retreat in battle.
No needless killing.
Bupmin — which one will you break first?
lines: 법민아 — 너는 무엇을 제일 먼저 어길 것 같으냐.

en: …No retreat.
I always pull up first. At the pine, today. Every time she rides too fast.
I’d rather know it now than find out on a field.
lines: 저는 늘 먼저 고삐를 당겨요. 오늘도 소나무에서요. 누님이 너무 빨리 달릴 때마다요.
들판에서 알게 되느니, 지금 아는 게 나아요.

blocks.html: Nobody laughs. A few boys look down at their sandals. Every one of them has a pine of his own.
blocks.ko: 아무도 웃지 않는다. 몇몇이 제 짚신을 내려다본다. 다들 저만의 소나무가 하나씩 있다.

en: Good. Most boys lie.
Then see the country the way a Hwarang sees a field: who holds, who falters, who dies for a vow he meant.
Tomorrow you ride the pine again. Beside her.
lines: 그럼 화랑이 들판을 보듯 나라를 보게. 누가 버티고, 누가 흔들리고, 누가 진심으로 한 맹세에 죽는지.
내일 다시 소나무까지 달리게. 누님 옆에서.

blocks.html: Gotaso has been listening from the fence, where she is not supposed to be either.
blocks.ko: 고타소는 울타리에서 듣고 있었다. 거기 있으면 안 되는 건 그녀도 마찬가지다.

en: You pulled up because of me?
No. Because of me.
…Tomorrow, then. Don’t you dare let me win.

blocks.html: She means it. She always means it. That is the trouble with Gotaso, and also the best thing about her.
blocks.ko: 진심이다. 그녀는 언제나 진심이다. 고타소의 문제가 바로 그거고, 고타소의 제일 좋은 점도 그거다.

blocks.html: The yard has two names it still whispers. Tonight the Marshal says them out loud…!
blocks.ko: 연무장이 아직도 목소리를 낮추는 이름이 둘 있다. 오늘 밤, 장군이 그 이름을 소리 내어 말한다…!

logline.en: Every yard has its ghosts. This one has two, and they have never missed roll call.
logline.ko: 연무장마다 귀신이 있다. 이곳엔 둘이다. 점호에 빠진 적이 한 번도 없다.

images.alt: Tiny Sadaham on a vast empty Gaya road — ice-blue accent, monumental emptiness
images.prompt: Minimal iconic 16:9 poster. Sadaham, God of the Hwarang, fifteen, taking Great Gaya. ONE geometric device: a long empty ROAD as a pale wedge receding to a hard horizon; tiny silky Hwarang figure in the lower third, standing, not kneeling. Face matches the attached Sadaham portrait only as a tiny likeness. Ice-blue #6fa8ff as the single accent on silk. REAL empty country road, natural dusk sky. Monumental emptiness. No army catalog. No crescent halo. No text. No watermark. Graphic color-blocking, anime-painterly, monumental.

images.at: asked to ride against Great Gaya
images.alt: Fifteen-year-old Sadaham kneels on the stone floor of Jinheung’s hall at night, head up, asking to ride
images.prompt: Worm’s-eye from the stone floor of King Jinheung’s timber hall at night, an oil lamp set on the floor in the sharp foreground. Sadaham, fifteen, kneels mid-bow but with his head already up, chin out, refusing to look down, in his Hwarang coat; the lamp rakes up across his jaw and the ice-blue of his collar. Behind and above him, out of focus on the dais, King Jinheung leans forward on one fist, half amused, half doubtful, red robe catching the same lamp. Pillars recede at an angle; Sadaham’s shadow climbs the floor toward the dais. CANON — SADAHAM — FACE and garments from attached /ch_sadaham.png (face only; invent a new pose). Demeanor: Hwarang taken Gaya at fifteen; ice-blue #6fa8ff cloth on campaign; dies young of grief. #6fa8ff as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | KING JINHEUNG — FACE and garments from attached /ch_jinheung.png (face only; invent a new pose). #2f6fd4 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.alt: By one candle, Sadaham sits at Mugwan’s sickbed holding his wrist, counting the pulse

Sadaham, sixteen, sits hunched beside him with two fingers pressed on Mugwan’s wrist, counting the pulse, jaw tight, refusing to cry. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.label: The First Class
blocks.ko: 제일기

blocks.html: Every yard has its ghosts. This one has two, and they have never missed roll call.
blocks.ko: 연무장마다 귀신이 있다. 이곳엔 둘이다. 점호에 빠진 적이 한 번도 없다.

blocks.html: The lamps go up under the eaves. Nobody sends the boys to bed. They decide this is an honour, and they are right, though not for the reason they think.
blocks.ko: 처마 아래 등이 걸린다. 아무도 소년들을 재우러 보내지 않는다. 소년들은 이를 영광으로 여긴다. 맞는 말이다. 다만 그들이 생각하는 이유는 아니다.

blocks.html: The Marshal does not let trust among friends stay a pretty line. He tells the new boys of the first class — the two names the yard still lowers its voice for.
blocks.ko: 장군은 교우이신을 예쁜 문장으로 두지 않는다. 새로 온 소년들에게 제일기를 말한다 — 연무장이 아직도 목소리를 낮추는 두 이름.

en: Before your fathers were born, the first class had two.
Sadaham. Mugwan. They swore to die together. Then, the year Great Gaya fell, one of them kept the swear without asking the other.
lines: 너희 아비가 태어나기 전에, 제일기에 둘이 있었다.
사다함. 무관랑. 함께 죽기로 맹세했다. 그러고 대가야가 떨어진 해, 한 쪽이 상대에게 묻지 않고 맹세를 지켰다.

en: Which one, Uncle?
Which one kept it?
Sit down and you’ll find out.
Is this the one about the haunted lake?
blocks.speaker: A new boy

en: No. That one’s about me.

blocks.html: Back then the yard was new, and so was the idea. The king wanted boys who would ride ahead of the army and not ask why. The first year, he got a lot of them. Two of them got each other.
blocks.ko: 그때는 연무장도 새것이었고, 그 생각도 새것이었다. 왕은 군대보다 앞서 달리면서 이유를 묻지 않을 소년들을 원했다. 첫해에 그런 소년은 많이 왔다. 그중 둘은 서로를 얻었다.

blocks.html: Sadaham is thirteen and talks like a dare. Mugwan is thirteen too, and says less than his horse. The hall has one gap, so they share it. They argue for a month about who snores.
blocks.ko: 사다함은 열셋이고, 말마다 내기를 건다. 무관랑도 열셋인데, 자기가 타는 말보다도 말수가 적다. 방에 빈자리가 하나뿐이라 둘은 한 방에 든다. 누가 코를 고는지 한 달을 다툰다.

blocks.caption: The first class’s brightest boy. He makes promises the way other boys throw stones.
blocks.ko: 제일기에서 가장 빛나던 소년. 다른 아이들이 돌을 던지듯 약속을 던진다.

en: You snore.
Don’t argue. The whole hall heard you.

blocks.caption: Sadaham’s best friend in the First Class. The two of them made a promise boys should not make.
blocks.ko: 제일기에서 사다함의 단짝. 둘은 사내아이들이 해서는 안 되는 약속을 했다.

en: That was you.
…Then prove it. Stay up and listen.

blocks.html: Mugwan stays up. It is the first of a great many nights he will stay up for Sadaham, and the only one either of them will find funny.
blocks.ko: 무관랑은 안 자고 듣는다. 앞으로 사다함 때문에 지새울 수많은 밤 가운데 첫날이고, 둘 다 웃을 수 있는 건 그날 밤뿐이다.

blocks.html: Their first spring, the yard sends them down to the river for stones. Mugwan turns one over and goes very still. Somebody has cut writing into it.
blocks.ko: 첫봄, 연무장은 둘을 냇가로 보내 돌을 날라 오게 한다. 무관랑이 돌 하나를 뒤집더니 꼼짝도 않는다. 누군가 거기에 글을 새겨 두었다.

en: Come here.
Read this.
You read it. You’re the one who studies.

blocks.hanja: 壬申年六月十六日二人幷誓記天前誓今自三年以後忠道執持過失无誓若此事失天大罪淂誓若國不安大舐世可容行誓之又別先辛未年七月卄二日大誓詩尙書礼傳倫淂誓三年
blocks.html: Year imsin, sixth month, sixteenth day. The two of us swear together and write it down. We swear before Heaven: from today, for three years, we will hold fast to the way of loyalty and commit no fault. If we break this, we swear it is a great sin against Heaven. If the country is not at peace and the world falls into great disorder*, we swear we will go and do it. And apart from this: before, on the twenty-second day of the seventh month of the year sinmi, we swore a great oath, to master in turn the Odes, the Documents, the Rites and the Tradition† within three years.
blocks.ko: 임신년 6월 16일, 두 사람이 함께 맹세하여 적는다. 하늘 앞에 맹세한다. 지금부터 3년 동안 충도를 굳게 지니고 허물이 없기를 맹세한다. 이 일을 어기면 하늘에 큰 죄를 짓는 것이라 맹세한다. 만약 나라가 편안하지 않고 세상이 크게 어지러워지면*, 나아가 행할 것을 맹세한다. 또 따로, 앞서 신미년 7월 22일에 크게 맹세하였으니, 시경·상서·예기·전†을 차례로 3년 안에 익히기로 맹세하였다.
blocks.source: Imsin Oath Stone (壬申誓記石), Silla, year imsin (552 or 612); found 1934 at Seokjang-dong, Gyeongju; Gyeongju National Museum, Treasure No. 1411

back.html: Face down in the river mud. That is how two boys found it, and how they put it back.
back.ko: 냇가 진흙에 엎어진 채. 두 소년이 찾았을 때도, 도로 놓았을 때도.

notes.html: The stone’s character here is worn. The database prints 舐; nearly every editor reads it as 亂, “disorder”.
notes.ko: 이 자리의 글자는 닳아 있다. 판독문은 舐로 적지만, 거의 모든 연구자가 亂(어지러울 란)으로 읽는다.

notes.html: The Tradition (傳) is usually taken as the Zuo commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals.

blocks.html: No names. Two boys, before the yard even had a name, promised Heaven three years of books, and a war if the country wanted one. What became of them, the stone doesn’t say. Stones rarely do.
blocks.ko: 이름은 없다. 연무장에 이름이 붙기도 전의 두 소년이, 책으로 3년, 나라가 원하면 전쟁을 하늘에 약속했다. 그 둘이 어떻게 됐는지 돌은 말하지 않는다. 돌은 원래 말이 없다.

en: Three years?
That’s all they had in them? Give me your knife.
That’s not ours. Put it back.
lines: 그거 우리 거 아니야. 도로 놔.

en: Not that one. We get our own.
lines: 그거 말고. 우리 건 따로 만들 거야.

blocks.html: He finds a smaller stone, flat and grey, and scratches at it until the light goes. His characters are terrible. He leaves out the books entirely. What’s left fits in a closed hand.
blocks.ko: 사다함은 더 작은 돌을 찾는다. 납작하고 잿빛이다. 해가 질 때까지 긁어 댄다. 글씨는 엉망이다. 책 얘기는 아예 뺀다. 남은 것은 주먹 하나에 다 들어간다.

en: Read it.
…“Two of us. One dies, the other follows.”
That’s it?
What else is there?

blocks.html: Mugwan takes the knife. Under the bad characters he cuts one more, small and neat: friend. Then he puts the old stone back exactly where they found it, face down, as if they had never been there.
blocks.ko: 무관랑이 칼을 받아 든다. 엉망인 글씨 아래에 한 글자를 작고 반듯하게 더 새긴다. 벗. 그러고는 옛 돌을 찾았던 자리에 그대로, 엎어서 도로 놓는다. 둘이 거기 온 적도 없다는 듯이.

blocks.html: A museum in Gyeongju keeps the first stone now. Nobody has ever found the second. Good.
blocks.ko: 첫 번째 돌은 지금 경주의 박물관에 있다. 두 번째 돌은 아무도 찾지 못했다. 다행이다.

en: So who snored?
blocks.speaker: A new boy

en: Both. That is not the story.

blocks.html: Two summers on, Great Gaya stops paying. The king calls the war in his hall, and the hall fills up with men old enough to have opinions.
blocks.ko: 두 해 뒤 여름, 대가야가 공물을 끊는다. 왕은 전당에서 전쟁을 정하고, 전당은 할 말이 있을 만한 나이의 사내들로 가득 찬다.

blocks.html: A hill kingdom that has just stopped saying yes.
blocks.ko: 막 “예”라고 하기를 그만둔 산골 왕국.

blocks.html: Sadaham was fifteen when he asked to ride against Great Gaya. He asked on his knees, in front of everyone. It is the only way a boy can ask a king for anything and not be sent outside.
blocks.ko: 사다함은 열다섯에 대가야를 치겠다고 청했다. 무릎을 꿇고, 모두가 보는 앞에서. 소년이 왕에게 무언가를 청하면서 쫓겨나지 않는 방법은 그것뿐이다.

en: Go home. Grow a beard.
War is not a yard. Nobody hands the ball back.
lines: 전쟁은 연무장이 아니다. 공을 돌려주는 놈이 없어.

en: Then I’ll ask again tomorrow.

blocks.html: He does. And the day after. The old general leading the campaign once took an island by frightening it with wooden lions. He tells the king it will be quicker to bring the boy than to keep hearing him.
blocks.ko: 청한다. 그다음 날도. 원정을 맡은 늙은 장군은 예전에 나무 사자로 겁을 줘서 섬 하나를 통째로 받아 낸 사람이다. 그가 왕에게 아뢴다. 저 아이를 데려가는 편이 저 아이 말을 계속 듣는 것보다 빠르겠다고.

en: Fine. Take him.
If he dies, it was his idea. Write that down.
lines: 죽으면 제 생각이었던 거다. 적어 둬라.

en: You’re going.
We’re going.
I told them you’re my second. Don’t make me a liar.
lines: 네가 내 부장이라고 했어. 나 거짓말쟁이 만들지 마.

en: You didn’t ask me.
I’m asking now.
…Well?
…I’ll get the horses.
And the battle? Uncle, what happened at the gate?
lines: 그래서 싸움은요? 외숙부, 성문에서 어떻게 됐어요?

en: Any old man in the market will give you the gate. He’ll get it wrong, but he’ll give it to you.
I am telling you about the rice.
lines: 시장 노인 아무나 붙잡아라. 성문 얘기는 해 줄 거다. 틀리게 하겠지만, 해는 줄 거다.

blocks.html: Ninth month. Gaya rebelled. The king ordered Isabu to punish it, with Sadaham as his second. Sadaham rode ahead with five thousand horse, went in through the Jeondan Gate and planted a white banner. The people in the city were terrified and did not know what to do. When Isabu brought up his troops, they surrendered all at once.
blocks.ko: 9월, 가야가 배반하니 왕이 이사부에게 명하여 치게 하고, 사다함을 부장으로 삼았다. 사다함이 기병 5천을 거느리고 앞서 달려 전단문으로 들어가 흰 깃발을 세우니, 성안 사람들이 두려워 어찌할 바를 몰랐다. 이사부가 군사를 이끌고 다다르자 한꺼번에 모두 항복하였다.
blocks.hanja: 九月，加耶叛，王命異斯夫討之，斯多含副之。斯多含領五千騎先馳，入栴檀門，立白旗，城中恐懼，不知所爲。異斯夫引兵臨之，一時盡降。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 4, Silla Annals — King Jinheung, yr. 23 (562)

blocks.html: Silla is a petty villain of the western barbarians. It defies Heaven and knows no decency. It has betrayed our kindness and destroyed our miyake. It poisons our people and butchers our districts.
blocks.ko: 신라는 서쪽 오랑캐의 보잘것없는 무리로, 하늘을 거스르고 무도하다. 우리의 은혜를 저버리고 우리의 관가를 깨뜨렸으며, 우리 백성을 해치고 우리 군현을 짓밟았다.
blocks.hanja: 新羅西羌小醜，逆天無狀，違我恩義，破我官家，毒害我黎民，誅殘我郡縣。
blocks.source: Nihon Shoki (日本書紀) bk. 19, Emperor Kinmei — yr. 23 (562), 6th month

blocks.html: Afterward the king pays him the way kings pay: in people. Three hundred Gaya captives, roped in a line, his to keep. Sadaham walks down the line once. Then he starts cutting rope.
blocks.ko: 싸움이 끝나자 왕은 왕들이 늘 하는 방식으로 값을 치른다. 사람으로. 줄줄이 묶인 가야 포로 삼백, 그의 몫이다. 사다함은 줄을 따라 한 번 걸어 내려간다. 그러고는 밧줄을 끊기 시작한다.

en: The court will say you’re showing off.
lines: 조정에선 네가 잘난 척한다고 할 거다.

en: Then the court can have them back.
Help me with this knot.

blocks.html: The land they give him instead is a strip of stones by the Alcheon that nobody wanted. The chronicle calls this virtue. Mugwan calls it typical, and holds the knot.
blocks.ko: 대신 받은 땅은 알천 가의, 아무도 원하지 않던 돌밭이다. 기록은 이를 덕이라 한다. 무관랑은 늘 그렇다고 하고, 매듭을 잡아 준다.

en: My father would have found a use for three hundred people.
lines: 아버지셨으면 삼백 명을 어디 쓸 데를 찾으셨을 거예요.

en: Your father would have found a use for three hundred and one.
lines: 네 아비라면 삼백한 명 쓸 데를 찾았을 거다.

blocks.html: That winter Mugwan catches a cough he cannot put down. Sadaham sits by the mat and counts his breathing, the way they used to count snores.
blocks.ko: 그 겨울, 무관랑은 내려놓을 수 없는 기침을 얻는다. 사다함은 자리 옆에 앉아 숨소리를 센다. 예전에 코 고는 소리를 세던 것처럼.

blocks.html: The little grey stone sits on the sill. Neither of them looks at it. Both of them know exactly where it is.
blocks.ko: 작은 잿빛 돌이 창턱에 놓여 있다. 둘 다 그쪽을 보지 않는다. 둘 다 그게 어디 있는지 정확히 안다.

en: Go eat. You smell like a sickroom.
lines: 가서 밥 먹어. 너한테 병자 냄새 나.

en: You remember what we swore.
We were thirteen. We also swore to marry the same girl.
If you die first, I will not eat.
So don’t.
lines: 네가 먼저 죽으면 나는 안 먹는다.

en: If I die first— you already know.
lines: 내가 먼저 죽으면 — 너는 이미 알지.

en: Then neither of us is allowed to be late.
lines: 그럼 우리 둘 다 늦으면 안 된다.

blocks.html: Mugwan pushes the stone across the mat with two fingers. It is the last thing he does on purpose.
blocks.ko: 무관랑이 두 손가락으로 돌을 자리 너머로 밀어 준다. 그가 마음먹고 한 마지막 일이다.

blocks.html: Mugwan died of illness not long after the campaign. He did it quietly, the way he did everything, before dawn, so as not to wake anyone.
blocks.ko: 무관랑은 전역이 끝난 지 얼마 되지 않아 병으로 죽었다. 무엇이든 그렇게 했듯 조용히, 새벽이 오기 전에, 아무도 깨우지 않으려는 듯이.

blocks.html: Sadaham did not take food for seven days. The cooks left bowls by his door. The order sent its oldest men to argue with him. He thanked them, and did not eat.
blocks.ko: 사다함은 이레 동안 음식을 들지 않았다. 부엌에선 문 앞에 그릇을 두었다. 화랑은 가장 나이 든 이들을 보내 그를 설득했다. 그는 고맙다고 하고, 먹지 않았다.

blocks.html: He keeps the stone in his fist. At night he holds it up to the lamp, as if the bad characters might have changed.
blocks.ko: 그는 돌을 주먹에 쥐고 지낸다. 밤이면 등잔에 비춰 본다. 엉망인 글씨가 바뀌기라도 했을 것처럼.

en: …It’s quiet in here. Nobody snoring.

blocks.html: On the seventh night the bowl by the door is still full. He lies down on Mugwan’s side of the mat.
blocks.ko: 이레째 밤에도 문 앞의 그릇은 그대로다. 그는 자리의 무관랑 쪽에 눕는다.

en: …Wait up.
I’m not late.

blocks.html: He was seventeen. The order buried two headbands beside him, and one small stone with terrible handwriting. It kept the story, because a Hwarang who outlives his vow is only a boy with a nice coat.
blocks.ko: 열일곱이었다. 화랑은 그 곁에 머리띠 둘과, 글씨가 엉망인 작은 돌 하나를 묻었다. 그리고 이야기를 남겼다. 맹세보다 오래 사는 화랑은, 옷만 좋은 소년에 불과하므로.

blocks.html: The lamp under the eaves has burned down a finger’s width. Nobody has moved. One boy is pretending he has something in his eye, and the others are kind enough to look at the lamp.
blocks.ko: 처마 아래 등잔 기름이 손가락 한 마디만큼 줄었다. 아무도 움직이지 않았다. 한 소년은 눈에 뭐가 들어간 척하고, 나머지는 친절하게도 등잔만 본다.

en: That is friends. Not a song.
If your vow is lighter than a meal, do not wear the headband.
lines: 맹세가 밥보다 가벼우면 머리띠를 매지 마라.

en: Uncle.
Who would you stop eating for?

blocks.html: Yushin looks at the boy for a long moment. You can probably name her. He doesn’t.
blocks.ko: 유신은 한참 동안 소년을 본다. 당신은 아마 그 이름을 댈 수 있을 것이다. 그는 대지 않는다.

en: …Go to bed. Gyuku at dawn.

blocks.html: When his sister rides too fast, Bupmin always pulls up first. Gotaso never pulls up. Not for horses. Not for anyone…!
blocks.ko: 누나가 너무 빨리 달리면 법민은 늘 먼저 고삐를 당긴다. 고타소는 당기지 않는다. 말 앞에서도, 누구 앞에서도…!

logline.ko: 어린 여자애는 하고 싶은 건 결국 하고 만다.

blocks.html: A young girl is going to do what she’s going to do.
blocks.ko: 어린 여자애는 하고 싶은 건 결국 하고 만다.

blocks.html: Two springs ago she proved it, and her father has not slept properly since.
blocks.ko: 두 해 전 봄에 그 애가 그걸 증명했다. 그 뒤로 아버지는 잠을 제대로 자 본 적이 없다.

blocks.label: Two Springs Earlier
blocks.ko: 두 해 전 봄

blocks.html: Gotaso is fourteen. She goes out to the lantern market with two maids and does not come back with any. The maids are found first, by the river, in the morning.
blocks.ko: 고타소는 열네 살이다. 시녀 둘을 데리고 등 시장에 나갔다가, 아무도 없이 돌아오지 못한다. 시녀들이 먼저 발견된다. 강가에서, 아침에.

en: Husband.
…Husband.

blocks.html: Chunchu says nothing. This is the part the household remembers afterwards and none of them can describe properly: he does not shout, he does not ask a second question, he simply stops being the man who talks.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 뒷날 집안 사람들이 모두 기억하되 아무도 제대로 옮기지 못하는 대목이 이것이다. 소리치지 않고, 두 번 묻지 않고, 그저 말하는 사람이기를 그만둔다.

en: Chunchu. Sit down.
I already have men out.
…Chunchu.
How many horses do we have.

blocks.html: It is the only sentence he speaks for two days. Yushin will try to tell it later as a joke and will stop halfway through, every time.
blocks.ko: 이틀 동안 그가 입 밖에 낸 문장은 그것 하나다. 유신은 뒷날 그 이야기를 우스개로 꺼냈다가, 매번 중간에서 그만둔다.

blocks.html: They were not bandits, in the sense that bandits want money. No word came and nothing was asked for, which is worse, and Chunchu understood what it meant before anyone in the room said it aloud.
blocks.ko: 돈을 원한다는 뜻에서의 도적은 아니었다. 기별도 없고 요구도 없었다. 그편이 더 나쁘고, 춘추는 방 안의 누가 소리 내어 말하기 전에 그 뜻을 알아들었다.

blocks.label: The Ford
blocks.ko: 여울

blocks.html: They find the road on the second night. What Chunchu does at the ford is in no record, because the two men who could have written it down were at the ford.
blocks.ko: 이틀째 밤에 길을 찾는다. 여울에서 춘추가 한 일은 어느 기록에도 없다. 그것을 적을 수 있었을 두 사람이 그 여울에 있었기 때문이다.

en: Enough.
Chunchu. Enough.
…The child is watching.

blocks.html: He stops. He wipes his hands on the grass, carefully, both sides, the way a man does before he picks up something clean.
blocks.ko: 그는 멈춘다. 풀에 손을 닦는다. 양손을, 조심스럽게 — 깨끗한 것을 들어 올리기 전에 사내가 하는 방식으로.

en: …Gotaso.
Father… there is something on your coat.
So there is.
I will change it later.

blocks.html: He carries her the whole way home. It is nineteen li. He does not let anyone take a turn and he does not put her down to eat.
blocks.ko: 그는 돌아오는 길 내내 아이를 업는다. 십구 리다. 아무에게도 넘기지 않고, 밥을 먹으려고 내려놓지도 않는다.

en: …Put her down.
Your arms will come off.
A little longer.

lines: 자네가 그렇게 조용해지는 건 처음 봤네.
en: I have never seen you go quiet like that.
…Brother.
I have two sons and one daughter.
One daughter.

blocks.label: The Gyuku Match
blocks.ko: 격구 시합

blocks.html: Before anyone says the word wedding, there is a spring match. Gotaso attends with two new guards, and her father watches her instead of the ball.
blocks.ko: 누가 혼인이라는 말을 꺼내기도 전에, 봄 격구가 있다. 고타소는 새 호위 둘을 달고 나오고, 아버지는 공 대신 딸을 본다.

blocks.html: At a spring gyuku match the Hwarang ride for the Queen. The stands smell of horse and expensive varnish. Servants carry club-boxes the way other households carry ancestral tablets. Gotaso is sixteen now, and only meant to watch.
blocks.ko: 봄 격구에서 화랑들이 여왕 앞에서 달린다. 관중석에서는 말 냄새와 비싼 니스 냄새가 난다. 시종들은 다른 집이 신주를 모시듯 채 함을 모신다. 고타소는 이제 열여섯이고, 보기만 하러 왔다.

lines: 저 나이 화랑이 저런 걸 들고 나오면… 집안이 보여.
en: Look at that club box.
A Hwarang that young carrying that… you can see the household.
I am not looking at the club.
Only the man.

blocks.html: Pumsuk takes the ball on the off-side — a showy, illegal-looking, completely legal cut — and for half a breath too long catches her eye instead of the goal. His premium gyuku club flashes once in the sun: presentation-silk still on the headcover, five coloured rings on the shaft, vulgar as Surabol sport gets.
blocks.ko: 품석이 오프사이드에서 공을 받는다 — 허세 같고 반칙 같아 보이지만 완전히 합법인 컷 — 그리고 반 호흡만큼 너무 길게, 골이 아니라 그의 눈을 붙잡는다. 프리미엄 격구채가 햇살에 한 번 번쩍인다. 헤드커버엔 아직 진열용 비단, 자루엔 오방색 고리 다섯. 서라벌 경기가 천박해지는 지점이다.

blocks.caption: Kim Pumsuk. Rich, handsome, and legal by about an inch.
blocks.ko: 김품석. 돈 많고, 잘생겼고, 딱 한 뼘 차이로 반칙이 아니다.

en: …Who is that.
Mother.
Mother. I asked who that is.
Hwarang Kim Pumsuk. / Don’t stare.
I already did.
And he looked back. He did, he did.

lines: 저 이제 다른 사람은 안 볼 거예요.
en: I am never going to look at anyone else.
For the rest of my life.
…Sixteen years old, using the word “life.”
Sixteen is exactly when you are allowed to use it.
Later you get too embarrassed.

blocks.html: She looks at him the way a person looks at weather they have decided to live in — not bargaining, not counting rooms. Just the face.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 그를, 살기로 한 날씨를 보듯 본다 — 흥정하지 않고, 방을 세지 않고. 그저 그 얼굴.

lines: 자네 딸은 다른 걸 보고 있고.
en: You are watching your daughter, Chunchu.
Your daughter is watching something else.
…I see it, Majesty.
I am choosing not to.

blocks.label: The Flowering Trees
blocks.ko: 꽃나무 아래

blocks.html: They meet again under the flowering trees behind the training ground — not by accident the second time, and not the third.
blocks.ko: 수련장 뒤 꽃나무 아래에서 다시 만난다. 두 번째는 우연이 아니고, 세 번째도 아니다.

blocks.html: Under the flowering trees they forget to be a princess and a Hwarang.
blocks.ko: 꽃나무 아래에서 그들은 공주와 화랑이기를 잊는다.

en: I shouldn’t… see Your Highness here.
Then why do you come every day.
I come every day.
Yesterday I came twice.

lines: 경기 때 아버님께서 저를 보셨습니다. 쏘아야 할지도 모르는 말을 보듯이.
그래도 왔습니다. 오면 안 되는 줄 알면서.
en: …I don’t know.
Your father looked at me at the match. The way a man looks at a horse he may have to shoot.
I came anyway. Knowing I shouldn’t.

lines: 아버지는 요즘 다들 그렇게 봐요. 그 나루 일 뒤로.
다른 사람들은 다 안 왔어요. 당신은 두 번 왔고요.
en: He looks at everyone like that now. Since the ford.
The others stopped coming. You came twice.

lines: 경기 때 그 컷 말입니다. 심판들이 다투던.
아씨 보시라고 한 겁니다. 평생 반칙을 무릅써 본 적이 없습니다.
en: That cut at the match. The one the umpires argued over.
It was for you. I have never risked a foul in my life.
…I would risk it again.

lines: 그럼 왜… 아직 제 손목을 놓지 않으세요.
en: And I’m not supposed to… touch your hand either?
Then why… won’t you let go of my wrist.
You mustn’t.
…And yet you’re holding it.
And… I cannot take it back.

blocks.label: The Palace Steps
blocks.ko: 궁궐 계단

blocks.html: Rain finds them once on the palace steps. Neither of them moves to go inside.
blocks.ko: 비는 궁 섬돌에서 한 번 그들을 붙잡는다. 둘 다 안으로 들어갈 생각을 하지 않는다.

en: You’re soaked.
…Why are you smiling.
Ah. / Is it my hair… on your sleeve?

lines: 공주님 머리카락이… 제 소매에 붙어 있어서요.
en: Your hair is… caught on my sleeve.
I should free it.
My hand won’t move.
Neither will my feet.

lines: 저는 이 소매 옆에 평생 서 있을 수도 있어요.
en: Then leave it.
Leave it there.
The sleeve. The hair.
I could stand beside this sleeve for the rest of my life.
No — closer.
My lady.
If this goes on… I will come apart.
Here. On the steps.
So will I.
So I settled all of it last night.
Four children. I have named them.
I am telling my parents today.
…Four?
You don’t want them?
…I want to know the names.

blocks.html: Four children, already named. Now the boy has to ask her father. And her father wants a vow…!
blocks.ko: 아이 넷, 이름까지 다 지어 두었다. 이제 그 사내가 아버지께 청할 차례다. 그리고 아버지는 맹세를 원한다…!

logline.en: Pumsuk asks for the girl. Chunchu asks for something else.
logline.ko: 품석은 딸을 청한다. 춘추는 다른 것을 청한다.
