blocks.hanja: 於羅瑕
blocks.html: What Baekje’s lords call their king. The farmers have their own word for him. The king has heard it, and prefers this one.
blocks.ko: 백제의 귀족들이 임금을 부르는 말. 농사꾼들은 따로 부르는 말이 있다. 임금도 그 말을 들어 봤고, 이쪽을 더 좋아한다.

blocks.caption: The boy with the borrowed name, grown. He still cannot say a thing he does not believe.
blocks.ko: 이름을 빌린 아이가 자랐다. 아직도 믿지 않는 말은 입에 올리지 못한다.

en: …Your Majesty. That is not a dragon.

lines: 아니지. / 그런데 저기 서 있는 사람들한테 가서 그렇게 말해 봐라. / 누가 이기나.
en: No, it isn’t. / Now go and say so to those people standing there. / See who wins.
Wins what.
It is paper and sticks. I can see the string.
I will go and tell them. You said to.

lines: 가라는 말이 아니야. 누가 이기나 보라는 거지.
en: They cannot see the string.
I did not say go. I said see who wins.
That is the same order.
I will not call it a dragon anywhere.

lines: 한 시각만 여기 서 있어라. 입은 다물고.
너는 그걸 못 하지. 그래서 내가 너를 옆에 두는 거다.
en: Stand here for one hour. Mouth shut.
You cannot do the other thing. That is why I keep you beside me.

lines: 폐하. 그 용, 저희도 봤습니다. / …폐하 곁에서도요.
en: Your Majesty. We saw the dragon too. / …From beside you.
…You two know better.

lines: 알지요. / 그래도 폐하께서 만드신 것 중에… 제일 오래 남는 건 용이 아니고요.
en: We do. / But of all Your Majesty has made… the thing that lasts longest isn’t a dragon.
…What did you say.

lines: 기적이요, 폐하. / 밤에만 가까이 두는 기적.
en: Miracles, Your Majesty. / The kind you keep close only at night.

blocks.html: His father had done it first, and better. Before he was king, King Mu paid the children of Sabi to sing a song he had written himself. By the third month the song was older than anyone could remember, and what it said about him had become a thing everybody had always known.
blocks.ko: 아버지가 먼저 했고, 더 잘했다. 왕이 되기 전 무왕은 제가 지은 노래를 사비의 아이들에게 삯을 주고 부르게 했다. 석 달이 지나자 그 노래는 아무도 기억하지 못할 만큼 오래된 것이 되었고, 그 노래가 그에 대해 말하는 바는 모두가 처음부터 알고 있던 사실이 되었다.

blocks.html: Nobody had to pay the children again. Euija filed that away.
blocks.ko: 아이들에게 다시 삯을 준 사람은 없다. 줄 필요가 없었다. 의자는 그것을 마음에 새겨 두었다.

lines: 서른째 어라하는 노래로 나라를 사셨지. 군대도 없이, 돈도 거의 없이.
그때 내가 열둘이었지. 그 뒤로 그만큼 감탄한 적이 없다.
en: The thirtieth Eraha bought a country with a song. No army, almost no money.
I was twelve. Nothing since has impressed me that much.

blocks.html: So the reign begins with small wonders. All of them arranged. None of them expensive.
blocks.ko: 그리하여 치세는 작은 기적으로 시작된다. 전부 꾸민 것이고, 어느 것도 비싸지 않다.

blocks.html: The white deer is the cheapest one. You take a young doe, you keep it out of the sun for a season, and you let it out on the hunting ground on a day the ministers are watching.
blocks.ko: 흰 사슴이 가장 싸다. 어린 암사슴 한 마리를 한 철 동안 볕에 내놓지 않다가, 재상들이 보고 있는 날에 사냥터에 풀면 된다.

blocks.html: The stone at the Rock of Politics sweats before a good decision. It sweats because somebody rubs it with brine the night before, and the somebody is always the same man.
blocks.ko: 정사암의 바위는 좋은 결정이 나기 전에 땀을 흘린다. 전날 밤 누군가 소금물로 문질러 두기 때문이고, 그 누군가는 늘 같은 사람이다.

blocks.html: Rice comes up on ground where nothing was planted. Something was planted. It was planted at night.
blocks.ko: 아무것도 심지 않은 땅에서 벼가 올라온다. 무언가 심겼다. 밤에 심겼다.

blocks.caption: The minister who asks the question the king hoped nobody would.
blocks.ko: 임금이 아무도 묻지 않기를 바란 질문을 묻는 신하.

en: Your Majesty. What happens when the people work it out?

lines: 알아채지 못한다. / 사람은 자기가 믿고 싶은 것의 증거는 절대 검사하지 않아.
en: They won’t. / Nobody inspects the evidence for a thing they already want to believe.

blocks.label: The Morning After
blocks.ko: 이튿날 아침

blocks.html: He walks the riverbank the morning after the dragon as if the mist itself had appointed him. Children point. A grandmother weeps. A clerk from the Board of Rites drops his brush and does not pick it up, because picking it up would mean deciding whether to write what he saw or what he was told.
blocks.ko: 용을 만든 다음 날 아침, 그는 안개 자체가 임명한 사람처럼 강둑을 걷는다. 아이들이 가리킨다. 할멈이 운다. 예조의 서리가 붓을 떨어뜨리고도 집지 않는다. 집는 순간 — 본 것을 쓸지, 들은 것을 쓸지 — 결정해야 하니까.

lines: 군대는 국경을 옮기는 데 한 달이 걸리지.
이야기는 하룻밤에 옮기고, 그 특권을 고맙다 하지.
en: Look at them.
An army takes a month to move a border.
A story moves it overnight, and thanks you for the privilege.
Your Majesty is… enjoying this.

lines: 잘하는 일은 즐겨야지. 안 그러면 심통이 나서 못하게 되거든.
en: I am good at it.
A man should enjoy what he is good at. Otherwise he does it badly, out of spite.

blocks.label: The Rock
blocks.ko: 정사암

blocks.html: At the Rock of Politics he arrives last, lets the ministers wait, rests two fingers on the sweating stone as if taking a pulse, and smiles the small smile of a physician who already wrote the prescription.
blocks.ko: 정사암에는 가장 늦게 도착해 대신들을 기다리게 한 뒤, 땀 흘리는 바위에 손가락 둘을 올려 맥박을 짚듯 하고, 처방을 이미 써 둔 의원처럼 작게 웃는다.

lines: 바위의 취향이 이리 좋다니, 우리 모두 행운이오.
en: The rock agrees.
How fortunate for all of us that the rock has such good taste.
The rock did not agree.
It is brine. I can smell it.
I am not going to nod at a wet rock.

lines: 대신들은 바위를 듣고 있소. 그대를 듣는 게 아니야.
고개는 끄덕이지 마시오. 침묵은 저들이 마음대로 읽거든. 그대 입은 못 읽고.
en: The ministers are listening to the rock. Not to you.
Do not nod. Silence they can misread. Your mouth they cannot.

lines: 그걸 진짜라고 믿는 자는, 이미 내 배역이고.
en: Gods are props. Spirits are lighting.
And any man who believes it is already in my cast.

blocks.html: This is entirely correct, and it is the sentence that kills him, nineteen years later, word for word.
blocks.ko: 완전히 옳은 말이고, 십구 년 뒤 그를 죽이는 문장이며, 한 글자도 다르지 않다.

en: …Your Majesty.

lines: 다만 통하지 않는다는 소리는 하지 마시오.
en: Sungchung. Hate the method. You have my permission.
Only do not stand there telling me it does not work.
Tonight?
One miracle, or two?

lines: 나라는 용을 보고. 너희는 임금을 보고.
en: Two.
I am in a generous mood.
The country can watch the dragon. You can watch the king.

blocks.html: This is the Righteous and Merciful at full height: before the wine years. He wrote the sky this morning. He walks under it and does not look up.
blocks.ko: 전성기의 인자군왕이 이렇다. 술의 시절 이전이다. 오늘 아침 하늘을 써 넣었다. 올려다보지 않고 그 아래를 걷는다.

blocks.label: The King’s Chamber
blocks.ko: 침전

blocks.html: Two court maids attend him — close enough that the air between them feels arranged. He is proud of the number the way a man is proud of a hunger he has not yet failed to satisfy.
blocks.ko: 궁녀 둘이 그를 모신다 — 그 사이 공기가 이미 정해진 것처럼 가깝게. 그는 그 수효를 자랑스러워한다. 아직 실패해 보지 않은 허기를 자랑하는 사내의 방식으로.

en: …Don’t both be greedy.
I am… looking at a map.

lines: 지도보다… 저희 목이 더 가까이 있지 않습니까.
en: The greed is Your Majesty’s.
You look at us… as if you already know.
Our throats… are closer than the map.

lines: …나는 지금 신라 국경 얘기를 하고 있었다.
en: …I was talking about the Silla border.

lines: 국경 얘기 하실 때 목소리가 제일 좋으세요.
en: Yes, Your Majesty.
Your voice is at its best when you talk about borders.
So we keep asking.
…Leave.
Shall we?
Your Majesty has not let go.

lines: 천록의 나라, 부처님의 나라 — 두 이름을 따뜻이 두어라. 하나는 장사치의 것, 하나는 스님의 것.
en: Righteous and merciful — so he was named.
Land of the Heavenly Deer, Land of the Lord Buddha — keep both names warm. One is for merchants. One is for monks.

blocks.label: The Princes
blocks.ko: 왕자들

blocks.html: Gyebek is twenty-one, and seated far down the table. No market calls him Hundred-Victories. Not yet. He is passed over every season, because nobody knows what clan he comes from, and he won’t make one up.
blocks.ko: 계백은 스물하나, 상 끝자락에 앉아 있다. 아직 어느 장터도 그를 백승이라 부르지 않는다. 아직은. 철마다 승진에서 밀린다. 어느 가문 출신인지 아무도 모르고, 그는 지어낼 생각이 없다.

blocks.html: At the coronation feast the princes sit by age, and the table has to be lengthened twice. Yung sits nearest the king, with a Satek cup-bearer at his elbow. Behind every brother's chair stands a clan tutor, like a second shadow. At the far end, servants pour for boys who don't have names worth carving yet.
blocks.ko: 즉위 잔치에서 왕자들은 나이순으로 앉고, 상을 두 번이나 늘려야 한다. 왕 바로 옆엔 융, 그 곁엔 사택의 술 시중. 형제들 의자 뒤마다 가문의 스승이 두 번째 그림자처럼 서 있다. 저 끝에선 아직 새길 만한 이름도 없는 아이들에게 시종들이 술을 따른다.

lines: 저 상 좀 봐라! 서른 번째 어라하께선 나라를 하나 남기셨지. 나는 아들로 나라를 하나 더 만들었다.
세어 봐라, 성충. 어서. 나는 서른 넘어가면 헷갈려.
en: Look at that table! The thirtieth Eraha left me a country. I made a second one out of sons.
Count them, Sungchung. Go on. I lose track after thirty.

lines: 마흔하나입니다, 전하. 올봄에 난 둘까지 치면.
…그리고 언젠가는 저마다 자리가 하나씩 필요할 겁니다. 자리는 정해져 있는데, 그…
en: Forty-one, Majesty. If the two born this spring are counted.
…And each of them will need a chair, one day. There are only so many chairs, and—

lines: 그럼 자리를 더 만들지. 아니면 몇 개 비우든가.
en: Then we’ll build more chairs. Or empty some.
Pung! Where’s Pung?

blocks.html: Prince Pung stands. He is seventeen. He is the quiet one, the one with the good handwriting, and he already knows what is coming because his mother told him the night before, crying into his collar.
blocks.ko: 풍 왕자가 일어선다. 열일곱 살이다. 말수 적고 글씨 잘 쓰는 아들. 무슨 말이 나올지 그는 이미 안다. 어젯밤 어머니가 그의 옷깃에 얼굴을 묻고 울면서 말해 주었으니까.

blocks.caption: The quiet prince with the good handwriting. He is about to learn what a hostage is for.
blocks.ko: 글씨 잘 쓰는 조용한 왕자. 볼모가 무엇에 쓰이는지 곧 배운다.

lines: 바다 건너 섬나라 임금이 백제 왕자를 제 조정에 두고 싶어 한다. 우리 둘이 얼마나 가까운지 세상에 보이고 싶은 게지. 네가 가거라.
그쪽 시를 배우고, 그쪽 술을 마셔라. 내가 전쟁까지 치러야 할 여자랑은 혼인하지 말고.
en: The island king across the sea wants a prince of Baekje at his court, to show the world how close we are. You’re going.
Learn their poems. Drink their wine. Don’t marry anyone I’ll have to go to war over.
As Your Majesty commands.
…For how long?

lines: 하! 그런 얼굴 하지 마라. 칭찬이다. 다시 찾을 생각 없는 왕자를 보내는 놈은 없어.
en: Until I need you.
Ha! Don’t look like that. It’s a compliment. Nobody sends a prince he doesn’t mean to want back.

blocks.html: One day Baekje will send for him after all. Nobody at the feast would have believed it, Pung least of all.
blocks.ko: 언젠가 백제는 결국 그를 부르러 사람을 보낸다. 잔치에 있던 누구도 믿지 않았을 것이다. 풍 자신이 가장.

blocks.html: Euija can fake a dragon. He can’t fake a fortress. For that he needs a general who does exactly what he says…!
blocks.ko: 의자는 용을 지어낼 수 있다. 성은 지어낼 수 없다. 그러려면 말한 대로만 하는 장수가 하나 필요하다…!

logline.en: There was only one man Euija knew he could trust to deliver.
logline.ko: 의자가 믿고 맡길 수 있는 사람은 단 한 명뿐이었다.

images.alt: Worm’s-eye: crowned Euija mid-cut on his own forearm — hard red blood-line, empty Sabi hall
images.at: Your Majesty. Does that mean you will not use me, or tha
images.prompt: Minimal iconic 16:9 still. WORM’S-EYE dutch: crowned King Euija mid-cut on his own forearm before an empty REAL Sabi court hall — timber from attached palace. FACE from attached portrait — fierce will, NEW kinetic body. ONE device: a hard red #C30000 blood-line on pale silk forearm as the only accent plane. Crushed blacks, empty hall. No army. No court crowd dump. No text. No watermark. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock: anamorphic movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain. A CAMERA in a real Korean place — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D archviz, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow, rim-aura, or god-ray envelope around people — light is a plane or a hard key. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portrait — NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: dutch, crane, worm’s-eye, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key + long shadows — not even daylight wash. ICONIC MINIMAL: ONE architectural device a lens can see; empty negative space; tiny figures or lower-third; the world stays in the shot. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex is lighting / a plane / one accent — NEVER recolor portrait garments gold. Real Korean architecture: grey giwa, timber, packed earth. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: movie frame in a real place, not a graphic poster; iconic one-device layout, empty frame, lower-third; high contrast chiaroscuro, not even wash; 2D animated cel-painterly, no photoreal; cinematography: dutch, wide, bokeh, mise-en-scène. Never: halo / bloom / glow around figures; graphic split-screen or black-triangle overlay; photoreal live-action or 3D archviz; busy extras crowding an iconic frame; copy-pasted reference as a fashion plate; flat even-daylight postcard wide.

images.alt: King Euija shoves the good cushion across the floor to General Yunchung, who has not yet decided to sit
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still, interior at night = old-master tenebrist canvas. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. The king’s winter chamber in the Sabi palace: dark timber pillars, plank floor, a low lacquered table, one bronze brazier. Low two-shot across the floor, worm’s-eye from beside the brazier set on the planks: King Euija leaning forward on one knee with a grin, shoving a thick embroidered silk cushion across the boards with one hand; General Yunchung standing stiff in his lamellar on the other side of the frame, helm tucked under one arm, looking down at the cushion as if it were a trap. The brazier between them is the one warm key, raking up across the king’s crimson silk and the grey plates; their shadows climb the pillars at an angle. Device: the cushion sliding across the empty floor between them. CANON — KING EUIJA — FACE and garments from attached /ch_king_euija.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Broad, bearded king; black hair in a topknot with a yellow-gold headband whose tails trail; heavy brows, cynical eyes. Dress: Crimson robe with a dark charcoal collar and gold trim; a steel lamellar pauldron peeking at one shoulder. Crown: Baekje king, as the attached crown (ignore its studio backdrop and logo): a tall rounded black silk cap (오라관) with a plain black band at the brow, and a pair of tall openwork gold flame-and-leaf ornaments (금제관식) pinned to either side of the cap, rising above it like twin flames — thin gold blades fanning upward with leaf buds and curls; the king’s red robe and wide-sleeved layers as the Baekje king on the costume chart. Demeanor: Licensed wit: drinks, smirks, slumps on the throne, speaks in polished aphorisms. Fatalist. #e08a2e as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: heroic battle pose; smiling innocence. | YUNCHUNG — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yunchung.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Hard-bitten Baekje frontier general in his forties: full black beard, heavy scowling brows, a band of red war-paint smeared across both eyes, long black hair falling from under a dented round steel helm with a cracked crown and a short red-black plume knob. Dress: Grey steel lamellar with red-edged shoulder guards over an ochre-yellow robe, a broad red sash with a round bronze boss, red-and-black striped bracers; a ring-pommel sword in a red-lacquered scabbard. Demeanor: Plain speech is also a weapon: says the ugly thing without a cushion under it, and does exactly what he says he will. #c9932a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | PLACE Sabi (사비 (부여)) — attached board /pl_sabi_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Sabi palace on the Baengma river bluffs; Baekje giwa halls and pavilions. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Baekje: attached /ref_hanbok_baekje_gaya.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: There was only one man Euija knew he could trust to deliver.
blocks.ko: 의자가 믿고 맡길 수 있는 사람은 단 한 명뿐이었다.

blocks.html: That winter Euija sends for Yunchung, and nobody from the eight houses is told. Yunchung is a general from a family too small to keep a clan tutor. He has held the Silla frontier for eleven years by doing exactly what he says he will do, which the Assembly finds tiring.
blocks.ko: 그해 겨울 의자는 윤충을 부르고, 여덟 가문 누구에게도 알리지 않는다. 윤충은 가문 스승을 둘 만큼 크지 않은 집안의 장수다. 그는 열한 해 동안 신라 국경을 지켰다. 하겠다고 한 일을 꼭 그대로 해서인데, 대신회의는 그게 피곤하다.

blocks.caption: A frontier general from a family too small to count. That is the point.
blocks.ko: 셈에도 안 들 만큼 작은 집안의 변방 장수. 바로 그게 요점이다.

lines: 앉게, 장군. 아니, 그 좋은 방석. 내 마음 바뀌기 전에 깔고 앉아.
en: Sit, General. No, the good cushion. Take it before I change my mind.
Tell me. Who rules Baekje?
Your Majesty does.
On paper.
Ha! And off paper?

lines: 문서 밖에서는 바위가 다스립니다. 그리고 그 바위에 소금물 바르는 자들이요.
여덟 가문이 좌평을 고르고, 좌평이 대신들을 고르고, 대신들이 제게 군량을 늦게 보냅니다. 제 군사들 녹은 그쪽이 주니, 군사들도 압니다.
en: Off paper, the Rock does. And whoever rubs the brine on it.
The eight houses pick the Premier, the Premier picks the ministers, and the ministers send me the grain late. They pay my men. My men know it.

lines: 그래. 왕이 안에서 피 안 보고 바위한테서 나라를 도로 찾으려면 어찌해야 하나?
en: So. How does a king get his country back off the Rock without a war at home?

lines: 성을 하나 빼앗은 왕은 그 성을 빼앗은 군사들을 갖습니다. 가문들은 승리를 두고 표결할 수 없습니다. 잔치에 얼굴이나 내밀 수 있지요.
en: With a war abroad, Majesty.
A king who wins a fortress owns the men who took it. The clans can’t vote on a victory. They can only show up to the feast.

lines: 거 참 말 한번 시원하게 하네.
나는 험한 말을 방석도 안 깔고 하는 사람이 좋아. 제가 내 방석에 앉아 있어도 말이야.
en: Plainly put.
I like a man who says the ugly thing without a cushion under it. Even when he’s sitting on mine.

blocks.html: It is the first time in the reign that Euija says what he has decided before the Assembly hears it. By spring the Assembly will hear it anyway, in the form of a question he has already answered.
blocks.ko: 의자가 대신회의보다 먼저 제 결정을 입 밖에 낸 것은 이 치세에서 처음이다. 봄이면 대신회의도 결국 듣게 된다. 그가 이미 답을 정해 둔 질문의 모양으로.

blocks.label: The Assembly
blocks.ko: 정사암 회의

blocks.html: By spring the Assembly is fighting about harbours, as it always is. Gyebek sits through three sessions. He understands every number and none of the smiles.
blocks.ko: 봄이 되자 정사암 회의는 늘 그렇듯 항구 문제로 싸운다. 계백은 세 번의 회의를 끝까지 앉아 있는다. 숫자는 다 알아듣고, 웃음은 하나도 못 알아듣는다.

en: Enough.
You can count berths when the frontier is settled.
Until then, the Eraha counts fortresses.

blocks.html: Euija has already decided. Now the clans have to believe it was their idea.
blocks.ko: 의자는 이미 정했다. 이제 가문들이 그게 제 생각이었다고 믿게만 하면 된다.

blocks.caption: A young Satek with good manners and a quick eye for an opening.
blocks.ko: 예의 바르고, 빈틈을 빨리 보는 젊은 사택.

en: As Your Majesty well knows,
the will of the Rock is the will of Heaven.
The eight houses decide it together.

lines: 하늘…? 아, 그 안 보이는 위원회.
en: Heaven…? Ah — the invisible committee.
Restore the reign of the thirteenth Eraha…!
The thirteenth Eraha…! Ten thousand years!

lines: 우리가 왜 백제 사람이고 고구려나 신라 사람이 아니냐? 생긴 건 똑같은데.
백제 땅 어디를 가도 시조는 다 안다.
en: Do you know what a country is?
A country is a territory governed by a single story.
Why are we Baekje people, and not Goguryeo or Silla people? We look exactly the same.
Anywhere in Baekje, everyone knows the founders.
Speak of King Onjo — that is Baekje.
So the king makes the story.
Let us make an interesting one…!
Goguryeo is too large to move.
Silla is too old to surprise anybody.

lines: 지금 신라왕은 군대를 통솔하지 못하는 여인이며,
그 나라 안에서도 민심이 확실치 않은 것으로 압니다.
이 틈을 타 신라 변방의 성을 치신다면, 대업을 이루시기 어렵지 않을 것입니다.
en: The present king of Silla is a woman who cannot command an army,
and even within her country, the people’s hearts are unsettled.
Seize this opening, take a border fortress, and the great work will be within reach.

lines: 폐하. 왕자님들께 이런 나라를 물려주실 셈입니까?
en: Your Majesty — is this the country you mean to hand the princes?

blocks.html: Gyebek steps forward. Nobody asked him to.
blocks.ko: 계백이 앞으로 나선다. 아무도 시키지 않았다.

lines: 닭 잡는 데 소 잡는 칼을 쓰겠느냐?
en: No, Gyebek… not you.
Why use an ox-cleaver to kill a chicken?

lines: 폐하. 그건 저를 쓰지 않겠다는 뜻입니까, 아끼겠다는 뜻입니까?
en: Your Majesty. Does that mean you will not use me, or that you are saving me?
…It means I am saving you.

lines: 그러면 그렇게 말씀해 주십시오. 저는 비유를 못 알아듣습니다.
en: Then say that. I do not follow figures of speech.

blocks.html: The Assembly finds him rude, which misses the point by a courtyard’s width. All he wants — every single time — is the sentence handed over with nothing folded inside it, and nobody at that court has spoken that way in their lives.
blocks.ko: 회의는 그를 무례하다 여기지만, 그것은 마당 하나쯤 빗나간 판단이다. 그가 바라는 것은 매번 하나뿐이다 — 안에 아무것도 접혀 있지 않은 문장을 그대로 건네받는 것. 그런데 그 조정의 누구도 평생 그렇게 말해 본 적이 없다.

en: A border fortress…
That too is good.
I have one in mind.

lines: 사실… 이 나라 사람들에게는 새 이야기가 필요하다.
en: In truth… the people of this country need a new story.
They have lived in the old one long enough.

lines: 삼한에서 우리가 제일 컸던 때가 있다.
열셋째. 군대를 이끌고 평양 한복판까지 들어갔지.
그 뒤로 백제는 한 조각이 되었다. 이름은 남고, 몸집은 빠지고.
그런데 하늘이, 늘 그렇듯 친절하게, 표식을 보내더군. 우리를 구할 새 임금이라고.
en: There was a time we were the greatest power in Samhan.
The thirteenth. He led armies into the heart of Pyongyang.
Then came the Severing.
After that, Baekje was a fraction. The name stayed. The size did not.
And then heaven, helpful as always, sent signs. A new king, meant to save us.
The thirty-first. Great King Euija.

blocks.caption: The thirteenth’s Baekje, and what is left of it.
blocks.ko: 열세 번째 어라하의 백제, 그리고 남은 것.

en: What is the Severing.
You said you do not follow figures of speech.
This is not one. It is the Severing.
Today we only have to tell it.
Baekje… is in crisis!
Then we make the crisis.
We take back the Silla frontier.

blocks.caption: Daeya. The last wall between Baekje and the Silla capital.
blocks.ko: 대야성. 백제와 신라 도성 사이의 마지막 성벽.

blocks.html: You’ve been to Daeya. You waved a cart into it.
blocks.ko: 대야에는 당신도 가 봤다. 수레 한 대를 손 흔들어 들여보냈다.

en: Then Silla’s finished at Daeya. Plain and simple.

lines: 하! 그럼 가서 끝장을 보게, 장군. 군사 만이야.
en: Ha! Then go and finish it, General. Ten thousand men.
Bring me back the fortress. And a story to go with it.
Daeya by autumn, Majesty.

blocks.html: The hall empties. Gyebek does not.
blocks.ko: 회의장이 빈다. 계백은 남는다.

lines: 비유가 아니라 하셨습니다. 그럼 사실입니다. 저는 그 사실을 모릅니다.
왜 진군하느냐고 병사들이 물을 것입니다. 사실로 답하고 싶습니다.
en: Majesty. The Severing.
You said it is not a figure of speech. Then it is a fact. I do not know it.
Men will ask me why we march. I want to answer with a fact.

lines: 하! 전쟁을 하면서 장부까지 달라는 놈은 처음 보는구나.
사비 아무 할미한테나 물어보거라. 나보다 잘 이야기한다. 나는 용을 보태서 탈이지.
en: Ha! A man who wants his war with the ledger attached.
Ask any grandmother in Sabi. They tell it better than I do. I add dragons.

blocks.html: “What is the Severing?” Gyebek asked. Any grandmother in Sabi could tell him. We’ll go back a hundred years and see for ourselves…!
blocks.ko: “斷이 뭡니까.” 계백이 물었다. 사비의 할머니라면 누구나 말해 줄 수 있다. 우리는 백 년을 거슬러 가서 직접 보자…!

logline.en: The sad thing about betrayal… is that it never comes from your enemies.
logline.ko: 배신이 슬픈 건… 그게 절대 적에게서 오지 않는다는 거다.

ONE device: the cone as a vertical splitting the torchlight. Stone fortress bokeh. Crushed black, one torch key. No text. No watermark.

images.alt: Night ink handscroll: almost all black wash, a thin pale road, a tiny cluster of fifty riders stopped on it, and a slanted line of red torches climbing the bank toward them
images.prompt: A Korean night ink-wash handscroll, wide horizontal, the paper soaked almost entirely in layered black and charcoal ink wash, a few dry-brush reeds. ICONIC MINIMAL LAYOUT: the only light areas are a thin pale strip of road running across the lower third and a faint grey ridge line near the top. ONE device: a single slanted diagonal line of small torch flames climbing the dark embankment from the lower right toward the road, each flame a dab of red #C30000, the only colour on the page. On the road, left of centre, a tiny tight cluster of about fifty ink riders reined in, horses rearing, a single small royal parasol among them; nobody’s face readable. Heavy empty darkness everywhere else, dread, stillness. One blank red seal square. PARODY RULES: always a hand-made PAINTING, never photoreal. Reproduce the original work’s composition, poses and signature look so it reads instantly as that exact work, with our characters swapped in. If the original is a painting, mural, print or scroll, match its medium, surface and brushwork. If the original is a photograph, film poster, album cover, anime frame or statue, PAINT it: a painterly illustration of that image with visible brushstrokes, simplified forms and anime-adjacent faces, NOT a photo, NOT photoreal skin or pores, NOT a 3D render, NOT a CGI statue. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portraits, recognizable but restyled into the medium; never the portrait’s standing clasped-hands stance. Character hex lives only as real color inside the work (pigment, cloth, light), never a glow aura, halo, emissive skin or neon outline. If a sword is visible it is the ring-pommel 환두대도 (small ring pommel at the heel of the fist, short grip, long straight blade, handle:blade 1:3), never a katana, never a tsuba. No readable text, no title, no credits, no legible inscriptions or signatures (red seal stamps only as blank red squares), no logos, no watermark.

blocks.html: The sad thing about betrayal… is that it never comes from your enemies.
blocks.ko: 배신이 슬픈 건… 그게 절대 적에게서 오지 않는다는 거다.

blocks.html: Gyebek finds the chestnut seller at the west gate of Sabi. She is not his grandmother. She is everybody’s, and she has waited her whole life for a soldier to ask.
blocks.ko: 계백은 사비 서문에서 군밤 파는 할미를 찾아낸다. 그의 할미는 아니다. 사비 모두의 할미다. 그리고 군인 하나가 이걸 물어 주기를 평생 기다려 왔다.

lines: 전하께서 아무 할머니나 이야기해 줄 수 있다 하셨습니다.
en: What is the Severing.
His Majesty said any grandmother could tell it.

blocks.speaker: A Sabi grandmother
lines: 아무 할미나? 흥. 앉아 봐. 밤 하나 먹고. 진군하기엔 너무 말랐어.
강에서 시작해. 그리고 친구. 이런 얘긴 늘 친구로 시작하지.
en: Any grandmother? Hmph. Sit, then. Eat a chestnut. You’re too thin to march.
It starts with a river, and a friend. They always start with a friend.
How long ago.

blocks.speaker: A Sabi grandmother
lines: 백 년. 소식이 왔을 때 우리 할미의 할미가 이 문에서 밤을 팔았지.
온 성안이 눈 온 것처럼 조용해졌대. 그날 하루 종일 아무도 아무것도 안 샀대.
en: A hundred years. My grandmother’s grandmother sold chestnuts at this gate when the news came.
She said the whole city went quiet, like snow. Nobody bought a thing all day.

blocks.hanja: 斷
blocks.html: For a hundred and twenty years Baekje and Silla kept one rule: when Goguryeo comes south, we stand together. Baekje calls the day that rule broke the Severing. Silla doesn’t call it anything. Winners rarely name things.
blocks.ko: 백이십 년 동안 백제와 신라에게는 규칙이 하나 있었다. 고구려가 내려오면 함께 막는다. 백제는 그 규칙이 깨진 날을 단(斷)이라 부른다. 신라는 아무 이름도 붙이지 않는다. 이긴 쪽은 좀처럼 이름을 붙이지 않는다.

blocks.caption: Two kings took the river together. One of them kept it.
blocks.ko: 두 임금이 강을 함께 되찾았다. 한 사람이 그것을 가졌다.

blocks.html: Two kings take a river back together: Seong of Baekje and the Cloud King of Silla. For a while their banners fly side by side. Then the Cloud King turns his army on Baekje’s half. He takes the river mouth and fills it with men who won’t ask what the alliance meant.
blocks.ko: 두 임금이 함께 강을 되찾는다. 백제의 성왕과 신라의 구름왕. 한동안 두 나라 깃발은 나란히 나부낀다. 그러다 구름왕이 백제 몫으로 군대를 돌린다. 하류를 빼앗고, 동맹이 무엇이었는지 묻지 않을 사람들로 그곳을 채운다.

blocks.html: King Seong feels the cut in the marrow. He calls in everyone who still owes him: the last Gaya houses, a boatload of soldiers from the islands. Then he marches east, on the fortress that opens Silla’s throat.
blocks.ko: 성왕은 그 칼날을 골수로 느낀다. 아직 그에게 빚진 이들을 모두 불러 모은다. 가야의 남은 집안들, 섬나라에서 건너온 군사들. 그리고 동쪽으로, 신라의 목을 여는 성으로 진군한다.

blocks.caption: Baekje’s king. He has lost a river, and he means to get it back.
blocks.ko: 백제의 임금. 강 하나를 잃었고, 되찾을 작정이다.

blocks.html: Every road into Silla’s valley squeezes through here.
blocks.ko: 신라 골짜기로 드는 길은 모두 여기서 좁아진다.

en: How many.

blocks.speaker: A Sabi grandmother
lines: 다. 빚진 집은 다 아들을 보냈어. 그 행렬이 이 문 지나가는 데 아침나절이 다 걸렸대.
en: All of them. Every house that owed him sent its sons. The column took a whole morning to pass this gate.

blocks.html: For months the fight goes Baekje’s way. The garrison keeps trying its gate and keeps getting shoved back inside. The crown prince holds the forward camp below the wall, half-starved; his men are boiling their saddle leather.
blocks.ko: 몇 달 동안 싸움은 백제 쪽으로 기운다. 수비군은 자꾸 성문을 나서고, 자꾸 도로 밀려 들어간다. 태자는 성벽 아래 앞 진영에서 굶주리며 버틴다. 군사들은 안장 가죽을 삶아 먹는다.

blocks.speaker: A Sabi grandmother
lines: 이기고 있었다니까. 그해 내내 사비는 이기고 있었어.
우리 할미의 할미가 밤을 두 배로 팔았대. 수레 지나갈 때 다들 뭐 따뜻한 거 하나씩 쥐고 흔들고 싶어 했거든.
en: Winning, see. All that year Sabi was winning.
My grandmother’s grandmother sold twice the chestnuts. Everybody wanted something warm in their hand to wave at the carts.

blocks.html: Nobody in the forward camp is watching the north road. Down it comes a second Silla army, out of the new lands on the river. Part of it leaves the road, goes into the hills, and swings south and then west, around behind the prince.
blocks.ko: 앞 진영에서 북쪽 길을 보는 사람은 아무도 없다. 그 길로 신라군이 하나 더 내려온다. 강가에 새로 얻은 땅에서. 그중 일부가 길을 벗어나 산으로 들어가더니, 남쪽으로, 다시 서쪽으로 돌아 태자의 등 뒤로 간다.

en: Behind him.

blocks.speaker: A Sabi grandmother
lines: 등 뒤로. 태자는 내내 성벽만 보고 있었지. 지금 네가 나 보듯이.
en: Behind him. And the prince was looking at the wall the whole time. The way you’re looking at me.

blocks.label: The Night Road
blocks.ko: 밤길

blocks.html: One night King Seong rides out from the west with fifty horse to steady his son. Silla’s ambush is waiting. The road to the prince is a ditch that was not there at dusk. Fifty horse stop, because the torches coming up the bank are the wrong color.
blocks.ko: 어느 밤, 성왕이 아들을 다독이러 기병 쉰을 이끌고 서쪽에서 달려온다. 신라의 복병이 기다린다. 태자에게 가는 길은, 해 질 녘에는 없던 도랑이다. 보기 오십이 멈춘다. 둑으로 올라오는 횃불이 틀린 색이어서.

blocks.html: On the ridge, the Cloud King’s hand drops. That is the signal. He has already said the rest, low, to the only man the rank will allow to finish it.
blocks.ko: 능선 위에서 구름왕의 손이 떨어진다. 그것이 신호다. 나머지는 이미 낮게, 골품이 끝을 허락할 단 한 사람에게 말해 두었다.

lines: 종이 베는 거야. 뒷사람이 입에서 못 잊게.
en: You. A slave.
He is a lord with a name.
A slave does the cutting. So later mouths cannot forget it.

blocks.html: A man in a Gaya cone helm is already down in the cut. He wears Silla's commission over it. His cone cuts the night ridge. He does not draw. He watches.
blocks.ko: 가야의 고깔 투구를 쓴 사내가 이미 패인 길 아래에 있다. 그 위에 신라의 임명을 걸쳤다. 그의 고깔이 밤 능선을 가른다. 그는 칼을 뽑지 않는다. 본다.

en: Gaya…?
A prince of Geumgwan — on this road, tonight, why.
Military governor of Sinju.
Sit.

blocks.html: They sit him on a camp stool. Out of the cone’s shadow a man kneels twice, the way you kneel to a king, and asks.
blocks.ko: 그를 호상 위에 앉힌다. 고깔의 그림자에서 한 사내가 두 번 무릎을 꿇는다. 임금에게 꿇듯. 그리고 청한다.

blocks.caption: A slave in the Silla camp. Remember the name; the annals almost didn’t.
blocks.ko: 신라 진영의 노비. 이름을 기억해 두라. 사서는 하마터면 잊을 뻔했다.

en: …I’m asking.
Let me take the head.

lines: 종의 손이— 안 돼. 왕의 머리는 종의 손을 안 받아.
en: What.
A slave’s hand— no. A king’s head does not take a slave’s hand.
If you broke the oath.
Even a king… takes it. I was told.

blocks.html: Which oath, and whose, nobody on the ridge asks.
blocks.ko: 어느 맹세를, 누가 깼는지. 능선 위에서 그걸 묻는 사람은 없다.

en: Dodo.
Every time I think of it…
It went into the marrow.
I cannot live on in disgrace.

blocks.html: He looks up. The breath that leaves him is not another sentence. He unfastens his own knife, gives it to the kneeling man, and puts his neck out.
blocks.ko: 그가 올려다본다. 빠져나가는 숨은 다음 문장이 아니다. 제 칼을 풀어 꿇은 사내의 손에 주고, 목을 내민다.

blocks.html: The ditch takes the head. Dodo does the work the rank will not put on a prince’s hands. The record almost forgets the slave.
blocks.ko: 도랑이 목을 가져간다. 도도가, 골품이 왕자의 손에 올리지 않을 일을 한다. 기록은 노비를 거의 잊는다.

blocks.html: By dawn the news is at the fortress. Thirty thousand men hear it at once. Silla comes down the north road and up out of the ditch together, and the ring around the wall comes apart. The prince gets out west, behind the island archers.
blocks.ko: 새벽이 되자 소식이 성에 닿는다. 삼만이 한꺼번에 듣는다. 신라가 북쪽 길로 내려오고 도랑에서 올라와 한꺼번에 덮치자, 성을 두른 고리가 풀린다. 태자는 섬나라 궁수들 뒤에 숨어 서쪽으로 빠져나간다.

blocks.html: The chestnuts have gone cold. Gyebek has not eaten his.
blocks.ko: 군밤이 식었다. 계백은 제 몫을 먹지 않았다.

en: How many came home.

blocks.speaker: A Sabi grandmother
lines: 태자. 섬사람 몇. 말은 묻지도 마.
en: The prince. A few islanders. Don’t ask me about the horses.

blocks.speaker: A Sabi grandmother
lines: 그게 斷이야. 신라는 그 해골을 계단 밑에 두고 아침마다 밟고 다녀.
en: That’s the Severing. Silla keeps his skull under a staircase and walks on it every morning.
So. Now you know why you march.

lines: 맹세를 깬 건 신라입니다. 종은 성왕이 깼다고 했습니다.
en: That is a fact. Thank you.
Silla broke the oath. The slave said Seong did.
I will remember which.

blocks.speaker: A Sabi grandmother
lines: 어느 쪽인지 기억해. 다들 그 걸상만 기억하더라.
en: Remember which. Most people only remember the stool.

blocks.html: A hundred years on, Baekje has not forgiven the cloud that emptied itself over its side of the river. The grandmothers tell it with chestnuts. Euija tells it with dragons. Either way, ten thousand men are about to march on it.
blocks.ko: 백 년이 지나도 백제는 강 건너 제 쪽에 비를 다 쏟아 버린 그 구름을 용서하지 않았다. 할미들은 군밤을 까며 이야기하고, 의자는 용을 띄워 이야기한다. 어느 쪽이든, 이제 만 명이 그 이야기를 들고 진군한다.

blocks.html: Ten thousand Baekje men march on Daeya. Its grain clerk is called Gumil. Remember that name…!
blocks.ko: 백제군 만 명이 대야성으로 향한다. 그 성의 곳간지기 이름은 검일. 기억해 두라…!

toneNote: The year everything hardens: coup-thriller nights, a tragedy played sincerely, and steam-cavern respites between them.
title: Iron Will

logline.en: In Silla, bone decides how high a man can climb. Gumil has climbed exactly that high.
logline.ko: 신라에서는 뼈가 사내가 오를 수 있는 높이를 정한다. 검일은 딱 그만큼 올랐다.

blocks.html: Gumil counts rice for a living. None of it has ever been his.
blocks.ko: 검일은 쌀을 세어 먹고산다. 그중 제 것이었던 쌀은 한 톨도 없다.

blocks.label: DAEYA FORTRESS
blocks.ko: 대야성

blocks.html: The last wall between Baekje and the capital, and the granary behind it.
blocks.ko: 백제와 서라벌 사이의 마지막 성벽, 그리고 그 뒤의 곳간.

blocks.html: The granary at Daeya can feed the garrison through a winter siege. Gumil knows the exact number of sacks. He counted them. Every tally he writes goes up the stair to a young man in a purple sleeve, who seals it without reading it.
blocks.ko: 대야성 곳간은 겨울 농성 한 철을 버틸 만큼의 쌀을 품고 있다. 검일은 그 가마니 수를 정확히 안다. 그가 셌으니까. 그가 쓰는 장부는 전부 계단 위, 자줏빛 소매의 젊은이에게 올라간다. 그 젊은이는 읽지도 않고 도장을 찍는다.

blocks.caption: A yellow-sleeve officer. He does the work, and the purple sleeve signs it.
blocks.ko: 누런 소매의 관리. 일은 그가 하고, 서명은 자줏빛 소매가 한다.

blocks.html: In Silla the sleeve tells you everything. Purple is True Bone, the old royal blood. Yellow is a man who will die at the rank he was born to. Nobody has to explain it twice. You can see it from across a yard.
blocks.ko: 신라에서는 소매가 모든 걸 말해 준다. 자주는 진골, 오래된 왕의 피다. 누런 소매는 태어난 그 자리에서 죽을 사람이다. 두 번 설명할 필요도 없다. 마당 건너편에서도 보인다.

blocks.label: The Stair
blocks.ko: 계단

blocks.html: This morning Gumil climbs the stair with the harvest tally and one more sheet under it. The second sheet is his. Four years of border pay, owed and never paid, added up to the last measure.
blocks.ko: 오늘 아침 검일은 추수 장부와, 그 밑에 한 장을 더 끼워 계단을 오른다. 그 한 장은 제 것이다. 사 년 치 변방 녹봉, 받을 것인데 한 번도 못 받은 것을 마지막 한 되까지 더한 것.

blocks.html: Pumsuk is twenty-four. He has held the fortress for a year, because his blood is right and his wife’s father is Chunchu. He is not a bad man. He is just a man who has never had to read the second sheet.
blocks.ko: 품석은 스물넷이다. 피가 맞고 장인이 춘추라서, 이 성을 맡은 지 한 해가 되었다. 나쁜 사람은 아니다. 그저 두 번째 장을 읽을 일이 한 번도 없었던 사람이다.

en: The harvest count. Good.
And this?

lines: 제 녹봉입니다요, 성주님. 사 년 치.
서라벌에선 쌀을 보낸답니다. 서라벌하고 저 사이 어디선가 누가 다 먹어 치우고요.
en: My pay, Commander. Four years of it.
The capital sends the rice. Somewhere between the capital and me, it gets eaten.

lines: 그건— 그래선 안 되는 일이오. 서라벌에 서신을 쓰겠소.
잔치가 끝나면. 이번 주엔 모든 게 잔치 뒤요.
en: Four years…
I— that should not happen. I will write to Surabol.
After the feast. Everything is after the feast this week.

blocks.html: He seals the harvest count. He hands the second sheet back, unsealed, with a kind smile. He does not ask Gumil’s name. In a year he has never needed it.
blocks.ko: 추수 장부에 도장을 찍는다. 두 번째 장은 도장 없이, 다정한 웃음과 함께 돌려준다. 검일의 이름은 묻지 않는다. 한 해 동안 그럴 일이 없었다.

blocks.label: The Granary
blocks.ko: 곳간

blocks.html: Down in the granary Mochuk is waiting. He is yellow too: same rank, same pay, same four years. He reads Gumil’s face before Gumil sits.
blocks.ko: 곳간 아래에서 모척이 기다리고 있다. 그도 누런 소매다. 같은 품계, 같은 녹봉, 같은 사 년. 검일이 앉기도 전에 얼굴부터 읽는다.

en: After the feast?

lines: 아니, 이런 귀에 피도 안 마른 놈을 국경에 놓는 게 말이 되나?
en: After the feast.
Putting a boy this green in charge of the border — does that make any sense?

lines: 저쪽은 말이 된다고 생각하지. 그게 문제야.
en: Keep your voice down.
It makes sense to them. That’s the whole trouble.

lines: 아, 여기가 무슨 나란지 까먹었나? 우린 결국 흙만도 못한 것들이여~
진골이라고 하면 하늘이 알아서 쫙 열리는 그런 나라라구~~
en: Ah, forgotten what country this is? To them we’re not even dirt~
Say “True Bone” and the heavens part on their own~~

lines: 아니~~ 난 또 왜 이런 망할 나라에서 태어나서 이런 고생을 하고 있네!!
en: Why was I even born in this wretched country, to suffer like this!!

blocks.html: Silla uses men by bone rank. If you are not of the right lineage, then however great your talent and however outstanding your deeds, you cannot rise past it.
blocks.ko: 신라는 사람을 쓸 때 골품을 따지니, 그 족속이 아니면 비록 큰 재주와 뛰어난 공이 있어도 넘어설 수 없다.
blocks.hanja: 新羅用人論骨品，苟非其族，雖有鴻才傑功，不能踰越。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 47, Biographies — Seol Gyedu (621)

lines: 자네 마누라도 똑같은 소리 하더만. 더 예쁘게.
en: Your wife says the same thing. Prettier.

lines: 잔치에 입을 새 저고리가 갖고 싶대. 비단으로. 초록으로. 그러마 했어.
en: My wife says a lot of things.
She wants a new jeogori for the feast. Silk. Green. I said yes.
…With what, I didn’t say.

blocks.label: Home
blocks.ko: 집

blocks.html: Maehwa is the poorest woman in Daeya and the one every eye in it finds first. She is thirty-one. She stopped pretending not to know what happens to a room when she walks into it a long time ago, and the fortress has never forgiven her for it.
blocks.ko: 매화는 대야에서 가장 가난한 여자이고, 성 안의 모든 눈이 가장 먼저 찾는 여자다. 서른하나. 자기가 들어서면 방이 어떻게 되는지 모르는 척하기를 그만둔 지 오래고, 이 성은 그것을 한 번도 용서한 적이 없다.

blocks.caption: Maehwa. Plum blossom: the flower that does not wait for spring.
blocks.ko: 매화. 봄을 기다리지 않는 꽃.

lines: 이 성에 있는 사내들 말이야. 다 똑같은 냄새가 나. / 흙이랑 술이랑… 그리고 자꾸만 곁눈질하는 냄새.
en: The men in this fortress. They all smell the same. / Dirt, drink… and looking when they think I won’t notice.
Cover yourself when you go out.

lines: 옷을 사 주시든가요. / 있는 거라곤 몸에 안 맞는 것뿐인데.
en: Buy me clothes, then. / Everything I own refuses to fit.
…You know what I am paid.

lines: 알죠. / 그래서 사람들이 다 보는 겁니다.
en: I do. / Which is why everyone looks.

lines: 오늘 달라고 했어. 사 년 치.
en: I asked today. For the four years.
And?
He smiled at me.
Did he.
What colour was the smile?
…Purple.

lines: 그럼 헌 초록 입고 가지 뭐.
en: Then I’ll wear the old green.
Let them all see what you’re paid.

blocks.label: The Well-Post
blocks.ko: 우물 기둥

blocks.html: By noon the yard splits. Porters, smiths and the grain boys find work at the well-post. Maehwa crosses alone, in the green jeogori washed too many times and one red sash. They do not come closer. She does not invite them.
blocks.ko: 한낮이 되면 마당이 갈라진다. 짐꾼, 대장장이, 곳간 아이들이 우물 기둥 곁에서 일거리를 찾는다. 매화가 혼자 마당을 건넌다. 너무 여러 번 빤 초록 저고리에 붉은 띠 하나. 사내들은 가까이 오지 않는다. 그녀도 부르지 않는다.

en: Look at that hem…
No — the waist. The waist.
That's Gumil's wife.
I know. That's why it's worse—

blocks.html: She hears every unfinished sentence. Bored chin, and the men keep looking anyway. Dirt under the nails, the same sour drink on every breath. She is tired of being their festival. She walks as if the yard were built around her anyway.
blocks.ko: 끝나지 않은 문장을 하나도 빠짐없이 듣는다. 지루한 턱. 사내들은 그래도 본다. 손톱 밑의 흙, 숨마다 같은 시큼한 술. 그들의 구경거리 노릇도 지겹다. 그래도 마당이 자기를 둘러 지어진 것처럼 걷는다.

en: That is a road.
Do not stand in it.

blocks.html: One of them forgets to close his mouth. She turns just enough. The hem stays a breath too long, and she lets him have that second like a coin she can afford to drop. Then the silk falls back.
blocks.ko: 한 놈이 입 다무는 걸 잊는다. 그녀는 딱 그만큼만 돈다. 치맛자락이 한 숨쯤 오래 머문다. 떨어뜨려도 아깝지 않은 동전처럼 그 한순간을 그에게 준다. 그리고 비단이 다시 내려온다.

en: Just now—
I saw. I saw.
…She didn't even say anything.

blocks.html: She leaves them wrecked on the packed earth and almost smiles. Up on the stair, a purple sleeve has stopped in the middle of a sentence. The yard is about the curve she takes with her.
blocks.ko: 흙마당에 그들을 무너뜨려 놓고, 그녀는 거의 웃는다. 계단 위에서 자줏빛 소매 하나가 말을 하다 멈춘다. 마당은 그녀가 데리고 가는 곡선의 것이다.

blocks.html: Over the western hills, King Euija reads Silla’s border the way he reads everything: patiently, and only once. Daeya is young at the top and hollow underneath. He sends Yunchung east with ten thousand men.
blocks.ko: 서쪽 산 너머에서 의자왕은 신라의 국경을, 모든 것을 읽듯이 읽는다. 참을성 있게, 그리고 단 한 번만. 대야성은 윗자리가 어리고 그 밑이 비어 있다. 그는 윤충에게 군사 만 명을 주어 동쪽으로 보낸다.

lines: 뒤의 이천은 하루 늦게 따라오시오. 누가 묻거든 짐이라고 하시오.
en: Three weeks to the river, if the roads behave.
The last two thousand keep a day behind us. If anyone asks, they are the baggage.

blocks.html: Surabol’s dreams don’t change. Its famous sword is far from here this week, in a warm cave in the hills, being told by three women who should not exist to watch a door in the north. That is another night’s story. Nobody tells Daeya anything.
blocks.ko: 서라벌의 꿈자리는 그대로다. 그 유명한 칼은 이번 주 여기서 멀리, 산속 따뜻한 동굴에 있다. 있어선 안 될 세 여인이 그에게 북쪽의 문을 조심하라 이른다. 그건 다른 밤의 이야기다. 대야에는 아무도 아무 말도 해 주지 않는다.

blocks.label: The Night Before
blocks.ko: 전날 밤

blocks.html: The night before the feast, the room is only a lamp and the two of them. The old green jeogori hangs on its peg, mended at the seam for tomorrow. They still know how to find each other. They will not know how tomorrow.
blocks.ko: 잔치 전날 밤, 방에는 등잔 하나와 두 사람뿐이다. 헌 초록 저고리가 내일을 위해 솔기를 기운 채 못에 걸려 있다. 그들은 아직 서로를 찾을 줄 안다. 내일은 모를 것이다.

en: Tomorrow they all look.
Today… only today.
Keep your hand on my waist.
It does not have to be a True Bone hand.
I know.
I know.
…Leave tomorrow for tomorrow.

lines: 사 년 치 받아 낼 거야. 진짜로.
en: I’ll get the four years. I will.
You’ll have silk by the first frost.
Liar.
…Say it again anyway.

blocks.html: They stop talking. The lamp is too small for manners. The red sash comes off the way it always does in this room, one impatient pull, and the old silk follows it onto the boards. Thirty-one, and she still puts him where she wants him.
blocks.ko: 말이 멎는다. 예의를 차리기엔 등잔이 너무 작다. 붉은 띠는 이 방에서 늘 그렇듯 성급하게 한 번에 풀리고, 헌 비단이 그 뒤를 따라 마루에 떨어진다. 서른하나. 그녀는 아직도 그를 원하는 자리에 둔다.

en: Tomorrow can wait.
Tonight you stay under me.
Don’t use a name. / Just… stay.

blocks.html: She knows his body the way a person knows a door they have opened every winter. He says her name at the end, not a rank. They sleep facing the same wall. In the morning the silk goes back on as if the night had been ordinary. It never is.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 그의 몸을 겨울마다 열어 온 문처럼 안다. 끝에 그는 품계가 아니라 그녀 이름을 부른다. 둘은 같은 벽을 보고 잠든다. 아침이면 비단은 아무 일 없던 밤처럼 다시 입혀진다. 그런 밤은 없다.

blocks.label: The Feast
blocks.ko: 잔치

blocks.html: The harvest feast fills the long hall. Purple at the top table, yellow at the back, families on the floor between. Lady Gotaso sits beside her husband for the first cup and goes up at the first drum. She is seventeen, and wine makes her sleepy.
blocks.ko: 추수 잔치가 긴 전각을 채운다. 윗상엔 자주, 뒷줄엔 누런 소매, 그 사이 바닥엔 식구들. 고타소 아씨는 첫 잔까지 남편 곁에 앉았다가 첫 북소리에 올라간다. 열일곱이고, 술을 마시면 졸리다.

blocks.html: At the feast the wine finds Pumsuk first. Clean ice-blue silk, a cup he is not tasting. Then the lamp-line is hers. Maehwa walks the cheap hanging lamps like she built them, in the old green and the red sash tied by habit. Every head at the top table turns. His turns last, and stays.
blocks.ko: 잔치에서 술은 품석을 먼저 찾는다. 깨끗한 연하늘 비단, 맛보지 않는 잔. 그다음 등잔 줄은 그녀의 것이다. 매화는 싸구려 걸이 등잔 사이를 제가 지은 것처럼 걷는다. 헌 초록 저고리에 버릇처럼 맨 붉은 띠. 윗상의 고개가 모두 돌아간다. 그의 고개가 맨 마지막에 돌아가고, 거기 머문다.

blocks.html: The feast is not a private room. It is every man in Daeya and the families they brought. Bowls stop. Necks turn. The wives watch her, not the food, and the watching is already a fight. The families are still eating. She is already working.
blocks.ko: 잔치는 밀실이 아니다. 대야의 사내들과 데려온 식구들이다. 그릇이 멈춘다. 고개가 돈다. 아내들은 밥이 아니라 그녀를 보고, 그 눈이 이미 싸움이다. 식구들은 아직 먹고 있다. 그녀는 이미 일하고 있다.

blocks.html: She takes a plum from a tray and eats it slowly, because a plum is cheaper than silk. She has practised this. At the back of the hall, among the yellow sleeves, Gumil watches the purple sleeve watch his wife.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 쟁반에서 자두 하나를 집어 천천히 먹는다. 자두가 비단보다 싸니까. 연습한 것이다. 전각 뒤편, 누런 소매들 사이에서 검일은 자줏빛 소매가 제 아내를 보는 것을 본다.

blocks.html: Pumsuk talks to his cup. It does not help. The training is a joke tonight. Nine years of Hwarang drill, and nobody taught him what to do with his eyes.
blocks.ko: 품석은 잔에 대고 말한다. 소용없다. 오늘 밤 수련은 농담이다. 아홉 해의 화랑 수련 동안 누구도 눈 둘 곳은 가르쳐 주지 않았다.

blocks.html: Then he does something he has not done in a year. He sends for the grain clerk.
blocks.ko: 그러다 그는 한 해 동안 한 번도 안 하던 일을 한다. 곳간지기를 부른다.

en: You. The— grain tallies. You are…
I am sorry. Your name.
Gumil, Commander.
Four years.
Gumil. Yes.
That woman. In the green. Who is she?

blocks.html: Gumil has waited four years for the purple sleeve to learn his name. It has taken a plum.
blocks.ko: 자줏빛 소매가 제 이름을 알게 되기까지 검일은 사 년을 기다렸다. 자두 하나면 되는 일이었다.

en: My wife, Commander.

blocks.html: Pumsuk goes very red. He looks into his cup. Then he does the worst kind thing a man in his chair can do.
blocks.ko: 품석의 얼굴이 아주 붉어진다. 잔 속을 내려다본다. 그리고 그 자리에 앉은 사내가 베풀 수 있는 가장 고약한 친절을 베푼다.

lines: 자네 녹봉 말이오. 사 년 치.
내일 그 장을 가져오시오. 내가 직접 도장을 찍겠소.
그리고— 오늘 밤. 백제가 길에 올랐소. 날이 밝기 전에 곳간 가마니를 전부 세어 놓으시오. 제대로 셀 사람은 자네뿐이오.
en: Your pay. The four years.
Bring the sheet to me tomorrow. I will seal it myself.
And— tonight. Baekje is on the road. Every sack in the stores counted by dawn. You are the only one who can do it right.

blocks.html: It may be an honest order. Baekje really is on the road. Gumil will spend the rest of his life deciding which it was.
blocks.ko: 정직한 명령일 수도 있다. 백제는 정말 길에 올랐다. 검일은 그게 어느 쪽이었는지 남은 평생 따지게 될 것이다.

en: …By dawn, Commander.

blocks.html: On his way out he passes Maehwa. He does not tell her to cover herself. She does not ask where he is going. She saw him on the stair, and she can count too.
blocks.ko: 나가는 길에 매화를 지난다. 가리라는 말은 하지 않는다. 그녀도 어디 가느냐고 묻지 않는다. 계단 앞의 그를 봤고, 그녀도 셀 줄은 안다.

lines: 자두요— 아, 잔 말고 입이에요, 성주님.
en: The plum— ah, it’s the mouth, Commander, not the cup.
Your lady went up early.
Twenty-four, and still sitting here.

blocks.html: He does the correct thing. He stands. He bows to a feast that has not asked him to leave. He goes up past Gotaso’s pink door to a cold pallet of his own. It does not take him.
blocks.ko: 그는 옳은 일을 한다. 일어선다. 아무도 나가라 하지 않은 잔치에 절한다. 고타소의 분홍 방문을 지나 제 차가운 침상으로 올라간다. 잠은 그를 받아 주지 않는다.

blocks.html: One husband counting sacks till dawn. One cold pallet. One feast still lit down the hall. How long can a True Bone lie still…?
blocks.ko: 새벽까지 가마니를 세는 남편 하나. 차가운 잠자리 하나. 복도 끝엔 아직 불 밝힌 잔치. 진골은 얼마나 오래 누워 버틸 수 있을까…?

logline.en: A man is measured by his self-control.
logline.ko: 사내의 그릇은 자제력으로 잰다.

blocks.html: A man is measured by his self-control.
blocks.ko: 사내의 그릇은 자제력으로 잰다.

blocks.label: HE TRIES TO SLEEP
blocks.ko: 자려고 한다

blocks.html: One dying lamp on dark timber. He lies in ice-blue with his eyes open. He tries to sleep and the hall comes with him: her hip, her mouth, the plum. A True Bone should be able to close his eyes. He is twenty-four. He knows exactly why he can’t.
blocks.ko: 검은 마루 위에 꺼져 가는 등잔 하나. 그는 연하늘 비단 차림으로 눈을 뜨고 누워 있다. 자려 하면 전각이 따라 들어온다. 그녀의 허리, 그녀의 입, 그 자두. 진골이라면 눈쯤은 감을 수 있어야 한다. 그는 스물넷이다. 왜 못 감는지 너무 잘 안다.

blocks.html: She arrives in the gold behind his lids, plum first. The look-back in the dark, over a shoulder in mended green. He sits up. Palm on the ice-blue, as if he could press the night flat.
blocks.ko: 감은 눈꺼풀 뒤 금빛 속으로 그녀가 온다. 자두부터. 어둠 속에서 돌아보는 눈길, 기운 초록 어깨 너머로. 그는 일어나 앉는다. 연하늘 비단 위에 손바닥. 밤을 눌러 펼 수 있기라도 한 것처럼.

blocks.html: On his way down he passes Gotaso’s door. A pink ribbon hangs on the post where her maid tied it. He turns his shoulder so his sleeve won’t brush it. That is the whole of his self-control tonight, and he is proud of it for four steps.
blocks.ko: 내려가는 길에 고타소의 방문을 지난다. 시녀가 묶어 둔 분홍 댕기가 기둥에 걸려 있다. 소매가 스치지 않게 어깨를 돌린다. 오늘 밤 그의 절제는 그게 전부다. 그리고 그는 네 걸음 동안 그게 자랑스럽다.

blocks.label: Back at the Feast
blocks.ko: 다시 잔칫자리

blocks.html: He goes back. The families have thinned. The screen is cheaper in this hour. She is still there. She sits as if she knew he would fail the pallet.
blocks.ko: 돌아간다. 식구들은 줄어 있다. 이 시각의 병풍은 더 싸다. 그녀는 아직 있다. 침상에서 실패할 줄 알았다는 듯이 앉는다.

lines: 앉아. 아니 거기 말고, 여기. 무릎 붙이게.
en: Here— ah, don’t bother with the wind.
Sit. Not there, here. Closer. Your knee can touch.

blocks.html: She drops beside him before he has stood. She sits like the chair was always hers. Jeogori already a little open — not court, not accident. The smirk shows teeth. His mouth is already open and he has not used it yet.
blocks.ko: 그가 일어서기도 전에 옆에 앉는다. 자리는 원래 자기 것이었다는 듯이 앉는다. 저고리가 이미 조금 열려 있다 — 궁도 아니고, 실수도 아니다. 이빨이 보이는 미소. 그의 입은 이미 열려 있고, 아직 말을 안 했다.

lines: 잠깐. 입이 먼저 열렸소. 그건 안 하려고 했는데.
en: Your husband—
Wait. My mouth opened first. I was not going to say that.

lines: 손— 여기. 매듭에. 벌써 다 해졌어요.
en: Stores. Till dawn. Your order, Commander.
Hand— here. On the knot. It’s already tearing.
You didn’t do that. Not yet.

blocks.html: She puts his clean True Bone hand on the frayed red knot herself — not the waist, the chest, where the cheap sash is already tearing. His palm finds the worn knot. More skin than a minute ago. She does not look at the hand. She looks at his face, to see the exact second it stops being a general’s face.
blocks.ko: 진골의 깨끗한 손을 헐거운 붉은 매듭 위에 제 손으로 올려 둔다 — 허리가 아니라 가슴, 싼 끈이 이미 찢어지는 곳. 손바닥이 낡은 매듭을 찾는다. 일 분 전보다 살이 더 보인다. 손은 안 본다. 얼굴을 본다. 장군 얼굴이 끝나는 그 초를 보려고.

lines: 다리가. 다리가 거역합니다. 미안하오. 훈련이— 오늘 밤 훈련은 농담이오.
en: I should move—
My legs. My legs will not obey. Forgive me. The training is— the training is a joke tonight.

lines: 입 보는 거. 열일곱. 열일곱이야, 내가 세었어.
진골 아씨면 눈 내렸을 텐데. 나는 그거 안 배웠거든.
en: You were counting. Not the cup.
My mouth. Seventeen. Seventeen, I counted.
A True Bone lady would have looked down. I never learned that part.

blocks.html: She says seventeen with her tongue still on her tooth. Jeogori looser. The dirtied green falls another finger-width. She counts his looks out loud. A True Bone lady would have looked down. Maehwa never learned that, and she is using the gap.
blocks.ko: 열일곱을 이빨에 혀를 붙인 채로 말한다. 저고리가 더 헐겁다. 때 묻은 초록이 손가락 하나만큼 더 내린다. 그가 본 횟수를 소리 내어 센다. 진골 아씨라면 눈을 내렸을 것이다. 매화는 그걸 배운 적이 없고, 그 빈칸을 쓴다.

blocks.html: She leans him into the post. His ice-blue has come open at the chest, clean silk, stupidly clean next to her mended green. Her mouth finds the tendon. She does not move back.
blocks.ko: 그녀가 그를 기둥에 기대 세운다. 연하늘 비단이 가슴께에서 벌어져 있다. 깨끗한 비단. 그녀의 기운 초록 옆에서 바보처럼 깨끗하다. 그녀의 입이 그의 목 힘줄을 찾는다. 물러서지 않는다.

en: Wait— I’ll make a sound.
I was trying not to. I am.

lines: 소리는 내 입에 넣어. 병풍이 다 들을 필요는 없잖아. 아니, 들어도 돼. 나는 상관없어.
en: I’m not waiting. Sorry. I’m not.
Put the sound in my mouth. The screen doesn’t have to hear. Or it can. I don’t care.

blocks.html: Then she does the modest thing she never uses. Jeogori closed. Back to him. One step toward the dark. I should go, she says, like a joke that wants to be caught. His hand is already in the air.
blocks.ko: 한 번도 안 쓰던 정숙함을 한다. 저고리를 여민다. 등을 보인다. 어둠 쪽으로 한 걸음. 이만 갈게, 라고 한다. 잡히고 싶은 농담처럼. 그의 손은 이미 허공에 있다.

lines: 이만 갈게— 아니 가라는 게 아니라.
잡히면 남는 거고. 장군은 잔치에 남아. 남아도 되고.
en: I’m going— I don’t mean go.
If you catch me I stay. You stay with the feast. Or don’t.

blocks.html: He is already on the floor. She has sat back down as if the leaving were a game. Bare foot. Cheap hem hiked just enough. His clean blue sleeve on her ankle. He does not remember kneeling.
blocks.ko: 이미 바닥에 있다. 그녀는 가는 척이 장난이었다는 듯이 다시 앉는다. 맨발. 싼 자락이 조금 걷혀 있다. 깨끗한 푸른 소매가 발목에. 무릎 꿇은 줄은 모른다.

lines: 남아. — 남아 줘. 무릎이 먼저 왔소. 나는 아직—
en: Don’t go.
Stay. — Stay. My knees got here first. I am still—

blocks.html: She looks down at him, a little pleased. She does not start with her hands. She takes a plum from the tray. She puts the plum in her mouth so he has to watch. Thirty-one. She has never rushed a man who was already lost.
blocks.ko: 그녀가 그를 내려다본다. 조금 흐뭇하게. 손부터 쓰지 않는다. 쟁반에서 자두를 집는다. 그가 볼 수밖에 없게 자두를 입에 문다. 서른하나. 이미 넘어온 사내를 서두른 적은 한 번도 없다.

en: I have a wife upstairs.
I know. Gotaso. The pink ribbon.
Did you walk past it on the way down?
A man is measured by it.
…I turned my shoulder.

lines: 그래도 우리 그이가 평생 가져 볼 것보다는 많네.
en: Half of a True Bone.
Still more than mine will ever be.

blocks.html: The mouth goes first. He holds her like he is afraid the hall will take her back. Wine on her tongue, and a hunger ten years older than his. The feast keeps talking on the other side of the cheap screen.
blocks.ko: 입이 먼저 간다. 그는 전각이 그녀를 도로 데려갈까 겁내는 사람처럼 그녀를 붙든다. 혀끝의 술, 그리고 그보다 십 년은 묵은 허기. 싸구려 병풍 저편에서 잔치는 계속 떠든다.

blocks.html: As little silk as the lamp allows. She means to teach him, and keeps the teacher-voice for three breaths. Then the voice thins. He is not gentle, and she does not ask him to be. She meant to laugh. The laugh becomes a scream, and the feast behind the screen goes quiet to listen. The lamp keeps dying and he does not stop.
blocks.ko: 등잔이 허락하는 만큼만 비단이 남는다. 그녀는 가르칠 생각이었고, 세 숨 동안은 선생 목소리를 지킨다. 그러다 목소리가 가늘어진다. 그는 부드럽지 않고, 그녀도 그러라고 하지 않는다. 웃을 생각이었다. 웃음이 비명이 되고, 병풍 뒤 잔치가 귀를 기울이느라 조용해진다. 등잔은 자꾸 꺼져 가고 그는 멈추지 않는다.

en: Don’t— don’t you dare stop—
I hate you. I hate you—
Don’t go back to him.
Not tonight—

blocks.html: When the lamp dies they are both still on the worn pine. She cannot sit up yet. She does not try. The feast on the other side of the screen has gone very quiet.
blocks.ko: 등잔이 꺼질 때 둘은 아직 낡은 소나무 마루 위에 있다. 그녀는 아직 일어나 앉지 못한다. 애쓰지도 않는다. 병풍 저편 잔치는 아주 조용해졌다.

blocks.html: He stands. He looks once, the way a man looks at someone he has already lost. He never asked her name. He leaves the feast without a word, back into the rank that will pretend this timber never happened. She stays on the floor.
blocks.ko: 그가 일어선다. 이미 잃은 사람을 보듯 한 번 본다. 끝내 이름은 묻지 않았다. 그는 말 한마디 없이 잔치를 떠난다. 이 마루가 없었던 일인 척해 줄 품계 속으로. 그녀는 바닥에 남는다.

blocks.label: Dawn
blocks.ko: 새벽

blocks.html: By dawn the whole fortress has a version. The well-post has three.
blocks.ko: 새벽이 되자 성 안 사람마다 제 이야기가 하나씩 있다. 우물가에는 셋이 있다.

lines: 뺏은 거야. 진골이잖아. 적을 땐 그렇게 적는 거야.
en: The commander took Gumil’s wife.
Took? I heard she—
Took. He’s True Bone. That’s how it gets written.
Took.
…Is that what happened.

blocks.html: Before this, the commander Pumsuk had seen that the wife of his staff officer, the saji Gumil, was beautiful, and took her. Gumil resented it.
blocks.ko: 이에 앞서 도독 품석이 막객인 사지 검일의 아내가 아름다운 것을 보고 빼앗으니, 검일이 이를 원망하였다.
blocks.hanja: 先是，都督品釋，見幕客舍知黔日之妻有色，奪之，黔日恨之。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 47, Biographies — Jukjuk

blocks.html: Morning comes. So does her husband, back from the stores. He wants the whole story. Every word of it…!
blocks.ko: 아침이 온다. 곳간에서 남편도 돌아온다. 그는 전부 듣고 싶어 한다. 한 마디도 빼지 말고…!

logline.en: Gumil doesn’t ask his wife if she’s hurt. He asks for the story.
logline.ko: 검일은 아내에게 다쳤느냐고 묻지 않는다. 이야기를 하라고 한다.

Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

Daeya’s gate with the red seam
images.at: Yunchung’s ten thousand are under the wall

images.at: Yunchung’s ten thousand are under the wall

Do not invent a different gate. Crushed storm light, one red seam of light in the door crack as the only accent. Two tiny spear-guards. Webtoon-painterly, high contrast, real Korean architecture. No army. No text, no watermark, no halo.

images.at: Yunchung’s ten thousand are under the wall

Between them one thin cinnabar stroke runs top to bottom, the omen, with bristles and a dry tail. A tiny guard is two ink flicks at the bottom of the seam. The red is only that seam. No building, no text, no seal.

images.at: Yunchung’s ten thousand are under the wall
