Between them one thin vertical seam of cinnabar red only. At the base, two tiny spear-guard marks. No roof, no bricks, no seal, no red stamp, no signature, no calligraphy, no characters anywhere in the image.

blocks.html: Gumil comes home at dawn with every sack in Daeya counted. He sits down to count one more thing.
blocks.ko: 검일은 대야의 가마니를 하나도 빠짐없이 세고 새벽에 집에 온다. 그리고 앉아서 하나를 더 센다.

blocks.label: THE NEXT MORNING
blocks.ko: 다음날 아침

blocks.html: Grey in the door-slit. Gumil comes back from the stores and finds his wife where the True Bone left her, the old green still open, last night still on the boards. He does not ask if she is hurt. He asks for the story.
blocks.ko: 문틈이 잿빛이다. 검일은 곳간에서 돌아와, 진골이 두고 간 그 자리에서 아내를 찾는다. 헌 초록 저고리는 아직 벌어져 있고, 간밤은 아직 마루 위에 있다. 다쳤느냐고 묻지 않는다. 이야기를 하라고 한다.

en: From the start.
All of it.
Don’t leave any out.
The lamp-line.
Sit. The plum.
After that… the floor.
After that.
The name.
How many times.

blocks.html: She tells it. The walk. The knot. The scream the screen did not hide. He makes her say the leaving last. She tells him she said the wife’s name, and the boy stayed anyway.
blocks.ko: 그녀가 말한다. 걸음. 매듭. 병풍이 가려 주지 못한 비명. 그는 떠나는 대목을 맨 마지막에 말하게 한다. 그녀는 아내의 이름을 입에 올렸는데도 그 애가 그대로 있더라고 말한다.

en: He didn’t speak.
He just left.
I… stayed on the floor.
Half a True Bone.
More than mine.
You said that too. Did you.

lines: 당신 부하들도. 이 성벽도. 이 나라도.
en: I did.
Because everyone in this fortress is trash.
Your men. These walls. This country.
…Right.
But you are here too.
You are trash as well.

blocks.html: They stand in the door-slit of morning and do not touch. What is left is the count of what she said, and a marriage that has finished speaking.
blocks.ko: 둘은 아침 문틈에 서서 서로 닿지 않는다. 남은 것은 그녀가 한 말의 셈, 그리고 할 말을 다 해 버린 혼인이다.

blocks.html: By noon she has a bundle and the old green on her back. She leaves by the south gate on her own feet. Nobody else in Daeya will.
blocks.ko: 한낮이 되자 그녀는 보따리 하나에 헌 초록을 걸치고 있다. 남문으로, 제 발로 나간다. 대야에서 그렇게 나가는 사람은 그녀 하나뿐일 것이다.

en: Where.
Somewhere nobody knows my husband.

blocks.html: That is the last thing they ever say to each other.
blocks.ko: 두 사람이 서로에게 한 마지막 말이다.

blocks.label: The Roof
blocks.ko: 지붕

blocks.html: Three weeks later, Yunchung’s ten thousand are under the wall. The river covers three sides of the hill, so they all camp on the fourth, the north. From the granary roof you can count their cookfires. Gumil does.
blocks.ko: 세 주 뒤, 윤충의 만 명이 성벽 아래에 와 있다. 강이 언덕 세 면을 막고 있으니, 모두 남은 한 면, 북쪽에 진을 친다. 곳간 지붕에 오르면 그들의 밥 짓는 불을 셀 수 있다. 검일은 센다.

en: How many?

lines: 곳간이 타 버리면 어떨까? 겨울 한 철이. 통째로.
en: Enough.
What if the stores burned? The whole winter. Gone.

lines: 그럼 성벽이고 뭐고 소용없지. 굶으면서 성벽 지키는 놈은 없어.
en: Then the walls don’t matter. Nobody holds a wall hungry.
…You’ve thought about it.

lines: 저쪽 장수가 사람을 보냈어. 약속은 지키는 놈이래.
불이 나면 곳간 문을 열어. 그쪽이 성벽을 먹고. 우린 걸어 나가.
en: Their general sent a man. Keeps his word, they say.
Open the granary gate when the fire starts. He takes the wall. We walk out.
We?
You’re yellow too.

blocks.label: The Granary Gate
blocks.ko: 곳간 문

blocks.html: The fire starts where Gumil starts it. Gumil puts the torch to the stores he counted, sack by sack, in the order he wrote them down.
blocks.ko: 불은 검일이 붙인 데서 시작된다. 검일은 제가 센 곳간에 횃불을 댄다. 장부에 적은 순서대로, 한 가마니씩.

blocks.html: Mochuk lifts the bar. The leaf swings. The approach road fills with Baekje men who have walked round the hill in the dark, along the river. He does not look at the men coming in. He looks at the man who asked him to.
blocks.ko: 모척이 빗장을 든다. 문이 열린다. 어둠 속에 강을 따라 언덕을 돌아온 백제군으로 진입로가 찬다. 들어오는 사람들을 보지 않는다. 열어 달라 한 사람을 본다.

blocks.html: Gumil puts his shoulder to the other leaf and opens the granary gate to Yunchung. It is not for Baekje. It is not for money.
blocks.ko: 검일이 다른 쪽 문짝에 어깨를 대고, 윤충에게 곳간 문을 열어 준다. 백제를 위해서가 아니다. 돈 때문도 아니다.

lines: 동쪽 곳간 줄이 통째로 타고 있네—
en: The whole east row is going up, man—
Why are you doing this. Truly.
Because everyone in this fortress is trash.

blocks.html: He is quoting her. He will keep quoting her for the eighteen years he has left, until a king he wronged finds him.
blocks.ko: 아내의 말을 옮기는 것이다. 남은 십팔 년 동안 그는 계속 그 말을 옮길 것이다. 그가 저버린 왕이 그를 찾아낼 때까지.

blocks.label: The Wall
blocks.ko: 성벽

blocks.html: From the granary roof Gumil watches the rest. Smoke. Shouting. A purple sleeve on the wall, asking the dark for terms.
blocks.ko: 곳간 지붕에서 검일은 나머지를 지켜본다. 연기. 고함. 성벽 위의 자줏빛 소매 하나가 어둠에 대고 조건을 묻는다.

en: If you swear to spare us all, I will surrender.

lines: 만일 그렇게 한다면 공과 나에게 모두 좋은 일이 될 것이요. 저 밝은 해를 두고 맹세하리다.
en: If you do, it will go well for both you and me. I swear it on that bright sun.

blocks.html: Beside him a yellow-sleeve officer named Jukjuk says what yellow sleeves never say upstairs.
blocks.ko: 그 곁에서 죽죽이라는 누런 소매 하나가, 누런 소매들이 윗자리에선 절대 하지 않는 말을 한다.

lines: 성주님. 백제는 손바닥 뒤집듯 말을 바꾸는 나라입니다.
저 달콤한 말은 미끼입니다. 성문을 열지 마십시오.
en: Commander. Baekje turns its word over like a hand.
That sweet talk is bait. Don’t open the gate.
…My wife is inside.

blocks.html: The north gate opens. The garrison files out first, shields down, onto the road toward the Baekje camp. Out of the west come the men Yunchung kept a day behind. The oath lasts until the last Silla shield is down.
blocks.ko: 북문이 열린다. 수비군이 먼저, 방패를 내린 채 백제 진영 쪽 길로 줄지어 나간다. 서쪽에서, 윤충이 하루 뒤에 두었던 군사들이 몰려온다. 맹세는 마지막 신라 방패가 내려질 때까지만 간다.

blocks.html: Then the killing starts. Yunchung turns his horse so the sun is behind him. On the roof, Gumil is not glad. He had thought he would be.
blocks.ko: 그다음엔 살육이 시작된다. 윤충은 해가 등 뒤로 가도록 말머리를 돌린다. 지붕 위의 검일은 기쁘지 않다. 기쁠 줄 알았다.

blocks.label: The Inner Room
blocks.ko: 안채

blocks.html: In the inner room Gotaso understands before anyone says the word. Her pink ribbon is crooked on the post. She tied it again herself at dawn, badly, and knew why. She is seventeen, and the forever she promised at the wedding has run out of road.
blocks.ko: 안방에서 고타소는 누가 말하기도 전에 안다. 기둥의 분홍 댕기가 삐뚤다. 새벽에 제 손으로 다시 묶었다. 서툴게. 그리고 왜 그래야 했는지 알았다. 열일곱. 혼례 날 약속한 영원은 갈 길이 다했다.

en: Husband…
If you are going to do it — look at me.

blocks.html: Pumsuk looks at her, the way she asked. Then he does what a True Bone does when there is no road left. First her, then himself. He looks at her the whole time.
blocks.ko: 품석은 그녀가 청한 대로 그녀를 본다. 그리고 길이 끊긴 진골이 하는 일을 한다. 그녀를 먼저, 그다음 저 자신을. 그동안 내내 그녀를 본다.

blocks.html: A man who was not in the fortress is suddenly in the fortress, ledger under one arm, crow-dark robe, standing the polite distance of a messenger. The underworld’s. Whose king is Yumla.
blocks.ko: 성에 없던 사내가 갑자기 성 안에 있다. 한쪽 팔에 명부, 까마귀빛 도포, 사신처럼 한 걸음 물러선 거리. 저승에서 온 것이다. 임금은 염라다.

blocks.html: It keeps a ledger, and it is never late.
blocks.ko: 명부를 쥐고 있고, 늦는 법이 없다.

blocks.html: Kangrim reads her name aloud three times before he asks anything. Gotaso. Gotaso. Gotaso. It is the underworld’s way of making sure the ledger has opened the right door.
blocks.ko: 강림은 무엇을 묻기 전에 그녀의 이름을 세 번 크게 부른다. 고타소. 고타소. 고타소. 명부가 올바른 문을 열었는지 확인하는 저승의 방식이다.

blocks.caption: The underworld’s fetch. He asks one question at the door, and he waits for the answer.
blocks.ko: 저승차사. 문 앞에서 질문 하나를 묻고, 대답을 기다린다.

en: Lady Gotaso.
One question, then we walk.
When you chose forever — did you choose the man, or the vow?
lines: 영원을 고르실 때 — 그 사람을 고르신 겁니까, 맹세를 고르신 겁니까?

en: Who… are you?
I don’t know your face. I don’t know your house.
Are you Baekje? Are you—
Neither. I collect.
You do not need to know me. Almost nobody does, until they do.
The question stands.
lines: 둘 다 아닙니다. 저는 거둬 갑니다.
저를 아실 필요 없습니다. 알기 전까지는 거의 아무도 모릅니다.

en: …Both.
Is that allowed?
…When he came for me there was something on his coat. He said he would change it later.
lines: …저를 데리러 왔을 때, 그이 옷에 뭐가 묻어 있었어요. 이따 갈아입겠다고 했고.

en: Honest. Rare.
Come. Nobody where we are going will ask you to swear anything.
lines: 갑시다. 우리가 갈 곳에서는 아무도 낭자께 맹세를 시키지 않습니다.

blocks.html: She goes with him surprised to the last — not by dying, but by discovering there was a door she had never been told about.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 끝까지 놀라며 그와 함께 간다 — 죽는 것 때문이 아니라, 아무도 알려 주지 않은 문이 있었다는 발견 때문에.

blocks.html: He reads the husband’s name three times next. Pumsuk. Pumsuk. Pumsuk. A second door in the same fortress.
blocks.ko: 이어 남편의 이름을 세 번 부른다. 품석. 품석. 품석. 같은 성 안의 두 번째 문.

en: Hwarang Pumsuk.
…No. Not for you.
…Ask me.
I wanted the love and the oath to be one thing.
They were not. Ask me.

blocks.html: Kangrim does not ask him. You may decide whether that is mercy. A year ago Pumsuk rode into Daeya beside her cart, at the wheel, never ahead. Tonight he walks behind her into the dark.
blocks.ko: 강림은 그에게 묻지 않는다. 그게 자비인지는 당신이 정하시라. 한 해 전 품석은 그녀의 수레 곁에서, 바퀴 옆에서, 한 번도 앞서지 않고 대야에 들어왔다. 오늘 밤 그는 그녀 뒤를 따라 어둠 속으로 걸어간다.

blocks.label: The Last Gate
blocks.ko: 마지막 문

blocks.html: Jukjuk gathers the men who are left and shuts the inner gate behind them.
blocks.ko: 죽죽이 남은 군사를 모아 안쪽 성문을 닫아건다.

en: Sir— surrender while they’re still offering!

lines: 아버지께서 대나무를 따라 내 이름을 지으셨소.
추운 철에도 시들지 말라고. 부러질지언정 굽히지는 말라고.
죽음이 두려워 항복해서 살 수야 있겠소?
en: My father named me for the bamboo.
So I would not wither in the cold season. So I might be broken but never bent.
How should I fear death, and live by surrendering?

blocks.html: They come up the hill from the north gate, the way the garrison went down. He holds the inner gate until sundown. Then he is broken, exactly as promised, and not bent.
blocks.ko: 그들은 수비군이 내려간 그 길로, 북문에서 언덕을 올라온다. 그는 해 질 녘까지 안쪽 문을 지킨다. 그리고 약속대로 부러진다. 굽지 않고.

blocks.html: In the morning a thousand of Daeya’s people walk west on one long rope. Gumil walks beside the rope, not on it.
blocks.ko: 아침이 되자 대야 사람 천 명이 긴 밧줄 하나에 묶여 서쪽으로 걷는다. 검일은 그 밧줄 곁에서 걷는다. 묶이지 않은 채.

blocks.speaker: A Daeya captive
lines: 검일이? …검일아! 말 좀 해 줘. 나 안다고 말 좀—
en: Gumil? …Gumil! Tell them. Tell them you know me—

blocks.html: Gumil does not turn his head.
blocks.ko: 검일은 고개를 돌리지 않는다.

blocks.label: The Moon Palace
blocks.ko: 월성

lines: 대야성이 함락되고... 품석 화랑, 고타소 양은 염라대왕 앞으로 가셨다 합니다...!
en: Daeya has fallen… They say Hwarang Pumsuk and Lady Gotaso have gone before Yumla…!
…What was it that girl said at her wedding.
“We will be happy forever.”

blocks.html: Chunchu does not shout. He asks, very calmly, for the names of everyone who was inside the fortress. Then, more calmly still, for the name of the man who opened the gate.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 소리치지 않는다. 아주 차분하게, 그 성 안에 있던 사람들의 이름을 모두 적어 오라 이른다. 그리고 더 차분하게, 성문을 연 자의 이름을.

blocks.caption: One summer. Daeya was the door, and the capital sits right behind it.
blocks.ko: 한 여름. 대야성은 문이었고, 도성은 바로 그 뒤에 있다.

lines: 자네 딸을 지키겠다고 맹세한 건 품석이었네.
en: Chunchu.
It was Pumsuk who swore to protect your daughter.
Not you.
Brother.
I am the one who made him swear it.

blocks.label: The Empty Hall
blocks.ko: 빈 대전

blocks.html: That night his mother finds him in the empty audience hall, sitting on the floor below the dais the way he used to sit there when he was small enough to be overlooked. Princess Chunmyung is sixty-two. She gave up a throne to marry his father and has never once brought it up. She lowers herself down beside him slowly, one hand on his shoulder for the knees, and does not ask how he is.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 어머니는 텅 빈 정전에서 그를 찾아낸다. 어좌 단 아래 바닥에 앉아 있다. 눈에 띄지 않을 만큼 작았을 때 거기 앉곤 하던 그대로. 천명 공주는 예순둘이다. 그의 아버지와 혼인하려고 왕위를 내려놓았고, 그 얘기를 꺼낸 적은 한 번도 없다. 그녀는 무릎 때문에 아들 어깨에 한 손을 짚고 천천히 그 옆에 앉는다. 괜찮으냐고 묻지 않는다.

lines: 바둑에선 돌 하나 잃으면, 그게 얼마짜리 집이었는지 세요.
en: Mother.
In go, when you lose a stone, you count the territory it cost.
This one… I can’t find the edge of it.

lines: 아홉 살 때부터 세고 있잖니. 네 아버지가 가르쳤고, 난 내버려 뒀지.
……머리 대. 오늘 밤만. 이 방에선 아직 내가 너보다 크다.
en: Then stop counting.
You’ve been counting since you were nine. Your father taught you, and I let him.
…Put your head down. Just tonight. In this hall I’m still bigger than you.

blocks.html: He does. The most cunning man in Samhan sleeps an hour with his head on his mother’s knee, and in the morning he asks the Queen for a road north.
blocks.ko: 그는 그렇게 한다. 삼한에서 가장 교활한 사내가 어머니 무릎을 베고 한 시진을 잔다. 그리고 아침에 여왕께 북으로 가는 길을 청한다.

blocks.label: The Moon Palace Gate
blocks.ko: 월성 문

blocks.html: In Surabol Bupmin waits at the gate the way a boy waits for a sister who promised forever. Munhee does not send him inside. She lets him see the empty road. Some educations are cruel on purpose.
blocks.ko: 서라벌에서 법민은 영원히를 약속한 누나를 기다리듯 문 앞에서 기다린다. 문희는 그를 들여보내지 않는다. 빈 길을 보게 둔다. 어떤 교육은 일부러 잔인하다.

en: Look at the road. Don’t look away.
You said you would be king for everyone.
Everyone includes the ones who do not come back.
…I will make a country where sisters come home.
Good. Start by surviving your father.
lines: 좋아. 일단 아버지 옆에서 살아남는 것부터.

blocks.html: In Pyongyang, Yeon has spent all summer bowing. Now he is throwing a party, and everyone important is invited…!

images.alt: Cellini’s Perseus in the banquet hall: Yeon on an overturned table, a commander’s ring-pommel sword raised high, his own crow blade lowered
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. POSE: Cellini’s Perseus. Worm’s-eye from the wet floor of the Pyongyang banquet hall at night: Yeon Gesomun stands on an overturned lacquer banquet table, weight on one leg, head bowed as he looks down, right arm raising a captured commander’s ring-pommel sword high overhead, his own crow-ring sword hanging low in his left hand. At his feet the edge of a slumped commander’s silk sleeve and a spilled wine cup, no gore. One fallen oil lamp on the floor below him is the only key, raking up his red-wing lamellar and both blades; smoke drifts; the hall’s pillars dissolve into black. Encased in darkness: at least 80% of the frame is near-black umber void, the figures pulled out of it by one hard raking key. Old-master tenebrist canvas (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour oil brushwork, glazed umber-black darks, impasto on the brightest highlight, canvas grain; silk brushed in loaded strokes; only faces and hands keep clean webtoon ink line. The steel glistens: the key runs down every blade as one long white-hot streak with a tiny star-glint on the edge. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — YEON GESOMUN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_gesomun.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Massive, broad-chested; black hair in a tight topknot tied with red cord; thick black beard trimmed close to the jaw, heavy brows, glaring eyes. Dress: Dark charcoal robe and trousers under red-edged armor, a red cape falling off the shoulders. Demeanor: Arrogant, theatrical, loud; looks down at people (worm's-eye suits him). Laughs while fighting. Armor: Goguryeo kit: steel lamellar with red-edged plates and RED WING shoulder-flaps, peaked helm with plume — red cloth, never gold plate. Battle armor: plates are METALLIC GRAY STEEL lamellar copied from the attached lamellar ref, cloth peeking at collar, sleeves, skirt, sash and plume-cord in the wearer's color only. Ignore labels and watermarks on armor refs. Not Japanese kabuto, not fantasy plate, not a gold-painted suit. Sword: High Commander Blade — Ring-pommel High Commander Blade — haetae carved beneath the crow stamp; the 막리지검 of the Summit’s first chair. Pommel motif crow inside the small ring (name only; do not attach the pommel ECU). Carry: FIVE crow-ring swords (身佩五刀): four crossed in a fan on his back with the hilts rising above his shoulders, plus one at the hip. Fighting: DUAL-WIELDS: a crow-ring sword in EACH hand, both forward one-hand grips, ring pommels at the heel of each fist. Wide aggressive stance, arms flung apart, scissoring cross-cuts and windmill slashes; lose one blade and he pulls another off his back. Each blade straight sw_bidam anatomy, 1:3. #d0362f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: one sword in a fight; gold-plated armor; beardless face (except a flashback to youth). | DAMUL (다물, gesomun's horse) — attached board /obj_damul_gaema.png: The biggest horse on any field: a red-bay Goguryeo war stallion, coat a deep BROWN-RED like oxblood lacquer (browner and darker than Hadong, redder and larger than Bisamun), a thick BLACK mane and BLACK tail, black lower legs, heavy arched neck — match the board. In battle it wears Goguryeo 개마 (gaema) barding as in the Anak Tomb No. 3 mural: steel lamellar skirts over the body and neck, a steel chamfron on the face, red cords and a red plume; the black mane falls over the steel. Named for 다물 (多勿), the old Goguryeo word for winning back the lost land; charges into water and spears without being asked, bites other horses. | HORSE ANATOMY is a centrepiece: the whole horse body reads clearly and beautifully — arched neck, deep chest, sloping shoulder, round haunch, clean long legs in a correct gait, every muscle modelled by the one hard key with a bright edge along the topline and deep shadow under the belly; the horse is never cropped into a blob, never hidden behind dust, never stiff like a toy; mane and tail as flowing painted strokes; the coat colour exactly as the board. | Kingdom banners: copy field colour and emblem from the attached flag_*.png ref onto period silk war-banners — tall poles behind each side, long streamers, small pennants on spear-tips and saddle-backs. Painted silk, wind-whipped, torn and smoke-stained in battle; never a flat modern flag graphic. Each side's banner colour is the clearest colour on its half of the frame, so the kingdom reads at a glance. Goguryeo banners: red silk with the black three-legged crow inside a studded black sun-ring. Attached flag /flag_goguryeo.png. | SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.alt: A red rider before the fortress at night
Yeon Gesomun on a galloping horse at full stretch, turned backward in the saddle drawing a bow in the famous Parthian shot, red wing shoulder-flaps streaming; a…
images.prompt: 16:9 still in the style of a Goguryeo tomb mural like the Muyongchong hunting scene: flat mineral pigments on cracked ochre-cream plaster, bold black outlines, stylised wavy mountain bands in red, white and black, no perspective. Yeon Gesomun on a galloping horse at full stretch, turned backward in the saddle drawing a bow in the famous Parthian shot, red wing shoulder-flaps #d0362f streaming; a stylised tiger and deer flee across the wavy mountain bands; a painted sun disc with a three-legged crow in one corner. FACE matches the attached Yeon Gesomun portrait, drawn in the mural's simplified line. Aged plaster texture, chips and cracks, faded earth colours. Not photoreal, not 3D. No text, no hanja, no watermark. No halo or glow aura.

images.alt: One horse-shaped ink mass standing, not running, all four legs planted, bristles in the mane.
images.prompt: Original sumi on white paper. No pasted general. Story: Gesomun's promise, the horse held still. One horse-shaped ink mass standing, not running, all four legs planted, bristles in the mane. A small cinnabar bleed on the shoulder. Empty white around it. No text, no seal.

blocks.html: Everyone in Pyongyang agrees that a man who bows all summer has learned his place.
blocks.ko: 여름 내내 고개를 숙인 사내라면 제 분수를 배운 것이다. 평양에서는 다들 그렇게 생각한다.

blocks.html: Yeon's father dies in the spring, in his own bed in the east. The seal should pass to the son. The Summit takes the whole summer to admit it. When it finally does, Yeon decides to host a banquet. The king is in attendance.
blocks.ko: 봄에 연의 아버지가 동쪽 제 집 자리에서 숨을 거둔다. 인장은 아들에게 가야 마땅하다. 제가회의는 그걸 인정하는 데 여름 한 철을 다 쓴다. 마침내 인정하자, 연은 연회를 열기로 한다. 왕도 자리한다.

blocks.html: All summer he has bowed. He went to every seat at the Summit one at a time and asked for his father’s seal like a younger son asking for an inheritance. Among themselves they have already agreed that he will have it for one winter, out on the border forts, and not come back.
blocks.ko: 여름 내내 그는 고개를 숙였다. 제가회의의 자리를 하나하나 찾아가, 막내아들이 유산을 청하듯 아버지의 인장을 청했다. 그들끼리는 이미 정해 두었다. 인장은 주되, 한 겨울만. 변경의 성 쌓는 데로 보내고, 돌아오지 못하게.

blocks.label: The Banquet
blocks.ko: 연회

blocks.html: October cold sits under the eaves. The lamps are already lit when the Five Commanderies take their seats — wine first, then meat, then the old joke that Pyongyang never runs out of either. Each commander wears a ring-pommel sword at his hip, the three-legged crow stamped in the ring. The hall smells of sesame oil and autumn horse-sweat brought in on Eastern boots.
blocks.ko: 시월의 냉기가 처마 아래 앉아 있다. 오부가 자리에 들 때 등불은 이미 켜져 있다 — 술 먼저, 고기 다음, 그리고 평양엔 둘 다 마르지 않는다는 낡은 농담. 욕살마다 허리에 환두대도를 찼고, 고리에는 삼족오가 찍혀 있다. 전각에서는 참기름 냄새와, 동부의 군화가 들여온 가을 말땀 냄새가 난다.

lines: 아, 그 명망 높은 개소문도 이제 고개 숙일 줄을 아는구나…
en: Ah — so even the renowned Gesomun has learned to bow…
Your father would have liked to see it.
Good — everyone is here.
We settle the succession today.
Gesomun! So you kneel at last!
Ah—

lines: 제가... 이제 신의 운명은 신이 책임지려 합니다...!
en: I… will take responsibility for my own fate from now on…!
May Your Majesty live ten thousand years….!

blocks.html: Every door in the hall closes at once, from the outside.
blocks.ko: 전각의 문이 바깥에서 한꺼번에 닫힌다.

blocks.html: The side doors were never for servants. When they open again, Yeon’s soldiers come through every one of them. Tables overturn. Wine becomes a darker color before anyone names it. Yeon does not shout orders. He walks the length of the room the way a man walks a border he has already decided to keep, and he takes each commander’s blade himself.
blocks.ko: 옆문은 원래 하인을 위한 것이 아니었다. 다시 열릴 때, 그 문마다 연의 군사들이 들이닥친다. 상이 뒤집힌다. 술이, 누가 이름 붙이기 전에, 더 어두운 색이 된다. 연은 명령을 외치지 않는다. 이미 지키기로 한 국경을 걷듯 전각을 가로지르며, 장수들의 칼은 제 손으로 거둔다.

blocks.html: First the Southern Commander. He wanted the next levy for Yushin’s passes, and called Eastern fighting easy work.
blocks.ko: 먼저 남부 욕살. 유신의 고개를 막겠다며 다음 징발을 달라 했고, 동부의 싸움은 쉬운 일이라 하던 자.

en: Yeon…!
Samhan… the Samhan His Majesty named—

lines: 지난번엔 이게 내 턱 밑에 있었지.
연설 말고 병력을 달라 했지. 병력은 내가 가져가오.
en: Son Daeha.
Last time, this was under my chin.
You asked for men, not speeches. I am taking the men.

blocks.html: He draws the Southern ring-pommel from a belt that no longer needs it. The grip is still smooth. One crow. One weight on the spine to come.
blocks.ko: 더 이상 필요하지 않은 허리띠에서 남부의 환두를 뽑는다. 손잡이는 여전히 매끈하다. 삼족오 하나. 앞으로 등에 올릴 무게 하나.

blocks.html: Then the Northern Commander. He would not freeze another winter while the capital counted his remounts twice.
blocks.ko: 다음은 북부 욕살. 중앙이 보충 말을 두 번 세는 동안 또 한 겨울을 얼고 싶지는 않다던 자.

en: The horses… still in… the warehouses…
blocks.art: In his own blood, still counting.

en: Go Ul.
…The three villages. I remember them.

blocks.html: The Northern crow joins the first, frost-nicks and all. Outside, a horse screams in the yard and then does not.
blocks.ko: 서리에 이 빠진 북부의 삼족오가 첫 번째에 더해진다. 바깥 마당에서 말이 울다 만다.

blocks.html: The Western Commander had warned that this would gift the Tang a road. He dies looking west, as if the road might still be argued shut.
blocks.ko: 서부 욕살은 이러다 당에게 길을 선물하게 된다고 경고했었다. 그는 서쪽을 보며 죽는다. 그 길을 아직 말로 닫을 수 있다는 듯이.

en: The Liao…
The Emperor’s drums…
You were right about the road.

blocks.html: Three crows. The third still smells of Liao timber. The hall’s lamps lean as if listening.
blocks.ko: 삼족오 셋. 세 번째에선 아직 요하 목재 냄새가 난다. 전각의 등불이 듣는 것처럼 기운다.

blocks.html: Lee Gaesa carries no banner. He is the Summit’s clerk, and he wrote its verdict on Yeon: one winter on the border, and do not come back. Tonight he has wine in his mouth, and then nothing.
blocks.ko: 이가사는 깃발을 든 적이 없다. 대대로 회의의 서기이고, 연에게 내린 판결을 제 손으로 적었다. 국경에서 겨울 한 철, 그리고 돌아오지 말 것. 오늘 밤 그의 입에는 술이 있고, 그다음엔 아무것도 없다.

en: Traitor…!
That day… I…

lines: 그대는 내게 겨울 한 철을 적어 주었소.
en: Lee Gaesa.
You wrote me one winter.
I am giving you one night.

blocks.html: Four. Ink on the grip, and now something on the edge. The verdict becomes metal he can wear.
blocks.ko: 넷. 손잡이엔 먹, 이제 날에도 무언가. 그에게 내린 판결이, 멜 수 있는 쇠가 된다.

blocks.html: Last of the banners: his uncle. The soft voice that told a nephew to sit down, because the Summit does not run on prophecies.
blocks.ko: 깃발의 마지막은 숙부다. 제가회의는 예언으로 돌아가지 않는다며 조카에게 앉으라 하던, 그 부드러운 목소리.

en: Nephew…
Traitor… a feast… like this…
blocks.art: Almost kindly, which hurts more.

en: Uncle.
You told me to sit down.
You called me traitor for standing.
A Yeon takes this one from a Yeon.

blocks.html: Five ring-pommels. Five crows. The first sword comes off the High Commander’s belt last, stone haetae and all. Yeon wipes none of them clean.
blocks.ko: 환두 다섯. 삼족오 다섯. 첫 칼이 막리지의 허리에서 마지막으로 풀린다. 돌 해태째. 연은 하나도 닦지 않는다.

blocks.html: He finally approaches King Youngryu for the final blow. The crown has slid. The Samhan dream is still in the king’s mouth, too late to be a budget.
blocks.ko: 마침내 영류왕 앞에 선다 — 마지막 일격. 면류관이 비뚤어져 있다. 삼한의 꿈은 아직 왕의 입에 남아, 예산이 되기엔 너무 늦다.

en: Gesomun…
With gold… decades…
The King for All…

lines: 금으로 될 일이 아니었습니다. 당 황제는 이미 폐하의 목값을 매겨 두었으니.
en: Your Majesty.
The gold was never going to be enough. The Tang emperor had already priced your head.
May You live ten thousand years.

blocks.html: Yeon places each of the Five Blades onto his own back.
blocks.ko: 연은 다섯 자루의 칼을 모두 제 등에 짊어진다.

blocks.html: He wore five swords on his body, and no one around him dared look up at him. Every time he mounted or dismounted, he made nobles and generals lie on the ground and stepped on them.
blocks.ko: 몸에 칼 다섯 자루를 차니, 좌우가 감히 우러러보지 못하였다. 말에 오르내릴 때마다 늘 귀인과 무장을 땅에 엎드리게 하고 그를 밟았다.
blocks.hanja: 身佩五刀，左右莫敢仰視。每上下馬，常令貴人、武將伏地而履之。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 49, Biographies — Yeon Gaesomun
blocks.claim: He wore five swords, and stood on men to mount.
blocks.claimKo: 그는 칼 다섯 자루를 찼고, 사람을 밟고 말에 올랐다.

blocks.html: He was imposing and handsome, with a fine beard, and his cap and robes were all trimmed in gold. He wore five swords, and no one around him dared look up. He made nobles lie on the ground and stepped on them to mount his horse.
blocks.ko: 생김새가 우람하고 빼어났으며 수염이 아름다웠고, 관과 옷을 모두 금으로 꾸몄다. 칼 다섯 자루를 차니 좌우가 감히 우러러보지 못하였다. 귀인을 땅에 엎드리게 하고 그를 밟고 말에 올랐다.
blocks.hanja: 貌魁秀，美須髯，冠服皆飾以金，佩五刀，左右莫敢仰視。使貴人伏諸地，踐以升馬。
blocks.source: Xin Tangshu (新唐書) bk. 220, Eastern Barbarians — Goguryeo

blocks.html: He steps into the doorway with the blades on his back. Red-wing chalgap fills the door.
blocks.ko: 그가 칼들을 등에 진 채 문간에 선다. 붉은 날개 찰갑이 문을 가득 채운다.
blocks.art: Worm’s-eye from the hall floor: Yeon in the doorway, steel lamellar and red-wing shoulder cloth filling the frame.

lines: 고구려의 충신들은 이 연개소문의 말을 들으시오!
서쪽에서는 황제가 나라를 하나씩 도륙하며 이리로 오고 있소!
그동안 무능한 임금과 썩은 신하들은 눈을 감고, 이 나라를 망국의 길로 끌고 갔소!!
오늘은 신라와 동쪽, 내일은 백제, 그다음은 당이오!
en: Loyal men of Goguryeo — hear the words of Yeon Gesomun!
In the south, Baekje and Silla covet us,
and in the west the Second Emperor comes this way, butchering nation after nation!
And all the while an incompetent king and rotten ministers shut their eyes to the world and lead this country down the road to ruin!!
Silla and the East, then Baekje the next day, then the Tang!

lines: 그러면 백성은 어찌 되오? 우리는 갈 데가 없소!
이 땅에서 살고 이 땅에서 죽고, 저들이 올 때마다 피 흘리는 건 우리요!
세상은 우리를 미쳤다 할 것이오! 그렇겠지 — 제 운명을 제 손으로 쥐는 일은 언제나 세상 눈에 미친 짓이었으니!
en: But what of the people? We have nowhere else to go!
We live on this land, we die on it, and we are the ones who bleed every time they come!
The world will call us mad! Of course — to take your own fate in your own hands has always looked like madness to the world!

lines: 우리를 구하러 오는 자는 없소!! 오직 우리가, 우리 손으로 해야 하오!!
en: No one is coming to save us!! Only we can do it — with our own hands!!

blocks.html: In the aftermath, Yeon enthrones the king’s nephew as King Bojang and creates a new position for himself, as the Supreme Commander.
blocks.ko: 연은 왕의 조카를 보장왕으로 세우고, 스스로를 위한 새 자리를 만든다 — 대막리지.

en: You there… what is your name?
M-my name? My surname is Go—
You there… what is your name?

blocks.caption: The old king’s nephew. He has been given a crown and very little to do with it.
blocks.ko: 옛 임금의 조카. 왕관은 받았는데, 그걸로 할 일은 별로 받지 못했다.

blocks.caption: A chair he built himself, above every other chair in the room.
blocks.ko: 스스로 짠 자리. 방 안의 모든 자리 위에 있다.

blocks.html: He makes one more appointment before the blood is dry. Dosuryu — an old friend of the Yeon house, one of the few men who has ever told him no and lived — is named Grand Herald, a post that did not exist until the banquet needed a voice that was not the throne’s.
blocks.ko: 피가 마르기 전에 임명 하나를 더 한다. 도수류 — 연씨 집안의 오랜 벗, 그에게 아니라고 말하고도 살아남은 몇 안 되는 사람 — 을 대대로에 앉힌다. 연회가 왕좌가 아닌 목소리를 필요로 하기 전까지는 없던 자리이다.

lines: 내가 네 아버지 살아 계실 때부터 네 뒷덜미를 잡던 사람인데.
en: Grand Herald…
I have had you by the scruff since your father was alive.
And now you want that mouth to read the country aloud?
If you will not, who will.
That Bojang… I only need the name.
The one who speaks to the people is you.

lines: 다만 — 네가 내 말을 들을 때만이야.
안 들으면 나는 전령이지, 친구가 아니야.
en: Very well.
Only — for as long as you still listen to me.
If you stop, I am a herald, not a friend.

blocks.html: Yeon listens. Not always. Often enough that the court learns which door to fear besides his.
blocks.ko: 연은 듣는다. 늘은 아니다. 그래도 조정이, 그를 빼고도 두려워할 문이 하나 더 있다는 걸 배울 만큼은.

blocks.label: The Temples
blocks.ko: 절집

blocks.html: After the blood dries, Yeon looks at the temples. They are rich, and they pray for whoever is winning. He has an idea about that, which can wait. One young monk named Shinsung learns how to wait too.
blocks.ko: 피가 마른 뒤 연은 절들을 본다. 부자이고, 누가 이기든 이기는 쪽을 위해 비는 절들이다. 거기에 대해 그는 생각이 하나 있다. 그건 기다려도 된다. 신성이라는 젊은 스님도 기다리는 법을 배운다.

en: Pray quieter.
Or pray to something that does not own half the capital.
lines: 아니면 수도 절반을 소유하지 않은 것한테 기도해.

blocks.caption: A monk of Pyongyang. Very quiet, and very well connected.
blocks.ko: 평양의 승려. 아주 조용하고, 아는 사람이 아주 많다.

en: Amitabha.
blocks.art: Bows.

blocks.html: What has the most strength? Forbearance is the strongest. One who forbears bears no grudge, and is sure to be honoured among men.
blocks.ko: 무엇이 가장 힘이 센가? 참는 것이 가장 굳세다. 참는 이는 원한을 품지 않으니, 반드시 사람들의 존경을 받는다.
blocks.hanja: 何者多力？忍辱最健，忍者無怨，必為人尊。
blocks.source: Sutra of Forty-two Sections (四十二章經), attr. Kāśyapa Mātaṅga & Zhu Falan · T17n0784, p. 722c

blocks.label: AFTER THE KNIVES
blocks.ko: 칼이 마른 뒤

blocks.html: In the markets the news arrives the way all bad news arrives — ahead of the official word, behind the smell of smoke. Grain sellers count on their fingers. Children stop racing. Someone says banquet and means blood.
blocks.ko: 저잣거리에 소식이 닿는 법은, 나쁜 소식이 늘 닿는 법과 같다 — 공식 말보다 먼저, 연기 냄새보다 늦게. 곡식 장수가 손가락을 접는다. 아이들이 달리기를 멈춘다. 누군가 연회라 말하고 피를 뜻한다.

blocks.speaker: Vendor
en: The king… they say he’s dead.
The commanders too. More than a hundred.

blocks.speaker: Wall sentry
lines: 어떤 이들은 영원의 대장군이 우리를 살렸다고 해.
조정에서 먼저 칼을 갈았대. 다음은 우리였을 거고. 평민들은… 연보다 그 이름을 먼저 불러.
en: Some say the Eternal General saved us.
The court was sharpening first. We were next. Commoners… we say that name before we say Yeon.

lines: 그 칼… 다섯 자루를 등에 맸다더라.
en: Those blades… they say he strapped five of them to his back.
The commanders’ swords. On his own spine.
By Haemosu’s light… incredible…
No — terrifying. Incredible, and terrifying.

blocks.speaker: Quiet man
lines: 그래도… 연회장에서 베는 게 나라를 구하는 거냐.
en: Still… is butchering a banquet the same as saving a country.
blocks.art: Low.

blocks.speaker: Wall sentry
en: Don’t say that on the wall.

blocks.html: On the barracks steps the same argument runs until the drum tells them to stop arguing and start marching.
blocks.ko: 병영 층계에서도 같은 논쟁이 돌다가, 북이 다투지 말고 행진하라 이른다.

blocks.html: The capital learns a new etiquette. Officials swear loyalty to the Supreme Commander’s door, not the nephew-king’s smile. Envoys who ask for an audience are told the kingdom is closed for inventory: of grain, of blades, of who belongs inside the walls.
blocks.ko: 도읍이 새 예법을 배운다. 관리들은 조카왕의 미소가 아니라 대막리지의 문에 충성을 맹세한다. 알현을 청하는 사신은 나라가 재고 조사 중이라는 말을 듣고 돌아간다. 곡식과, 칼과, 성 안에 남을 자격의.

blocks.label: The Yeon House
blocks.ko: 연씨 집

blocks.html: At night the house is quieter than the city. Yeon’s wife has kept three boys from the sound of cheering that is not quite cheer. She waits until the lamps are few enough that even a Supreme Commander looks like a husband.
blocks.ko: 밤이 되면 집은 도읍보다 고요하다. 연씨부인은 환호가 아닌 환호 소리로부터 아들 셋을 막아 두었다. 등불이 적어져 대막리지조차 남편처럼 보일 때까지 기다린다.

lines: 바깥에서 우리 겨레를 어떻게 부를지… 생각만 해도—
en: What will Tang say…
Silla too. Baekje.
Massacre. Traitor.
How those outside will name our people… even thinking of it—

lines: 들어… 저들이 우리에 대해 뭐라 하든, 상관없어.
들리냐? 전혀. 제로. 한 톨도 아니야.
en: Listen… it doesn’t matter what they’ll say about us.
Do you hear me? It doesn’t matter at all — zero. Not even one bit.

lines: 저들 조상이 이 흙을 위해 죽어 줬나?
우리가 피 흘릴 차례가 오면, 저들이 여기 서 있어 주나?
en: Did their ancestors die for this dirt?
Will they be standing here when it is our turn to bleed?

lines: 그러니 바깥에서 우리 겨레를, 우리 사는 법을 뭐라 하든 —
네 인생 단 일 초도 거기 쓰지 마. 제발.
en: So whatever they say out there about our people, our way of living —
not one second of your life. Please.
Look at me. Promise me.

lines: 다만 — 아이들이 자라면, 당신은 그 말도 해 줘요.
en: …I promise.
Only — when the boys are grown, tell them that too.

blocks.html: He nods. Outside, the drums keep time for a kingdom learning to live with its doors shut.
blocks.ko: 그는 끄덕인다. 바깥에서는, 문을 닫고 사는 법을 배우는 나라의 북이 박자를 맞춘다.

blocks.html: A kingdom with its doors shut, and a man with five swords on his back. Naturally, Chunchu wants to go and knock…!
blocks.ko: 문을 걸어 잠근 나라, 그리고 칼 다섯 자루를 등에 멘 사내. 그러니 당연히, 춘추는 그 문을 두드리러 가겠다고 한다…!

logline.en: To save Silla, Chunchu has to walk into Pyongyang and ask the most dangerous man in Samhan for a favour.
logline.ko: 신라를 살리려면, 춘추는 평양으로 걸어 들어가 삼한에서 가장 위험한 사내에게 부탁을 해야 한다.

images.alt: Caravaggio’s Ecce Homo: Chunchu presented between two attendants, bleeding hand lifted, face perfectly composed
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. POSE: Caravaggio’s Ecce Homo. Tight three-figure frame in a dark Pyongyang palace corridor at night: Chunchu stands between two attendants who grip his arms, his left hand lifted a little before him, red and dripping, his face calm and almost amused. Dosuryu leans in from the right edge in profile, hand on his sword hilt, the ring-pommel catching the light. One torch off frame left rakes hard across Chunchu’s face, the blood and Dosuryu’s blade; a guard’s spear tip glints in the black behind. Encased in darkness: at least 80% of the frame is near-black umber void, the figures pulled out of it by one hard raking key. Old-master tenebrist canvas (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour oil brushwork, glazed umber-black darks, impasto on the brightest highlight, canvas grain; silk brushed in loaded strokes; only faces and hands keep clean webtoon ink line. The steel glistens: the key runs down every blade as one long white-hot streak with a tiny star-glint on the edge. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — KIM CHUNCHU — FACE and garments from attached /ch_chunchu.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Slim and elegant; shoulder-length loose black hair parted in the middle; thin moustache and goatee stubble; amused eyes, small knowing smile. Dress: Magenta-crimson silk po with a charcoal sash, dark layered collar. Silk even on campaign. Demeanor: Diplomat and strategist: talks with his hands, smiles while calculating, never shouts; half-lidded watchful eyes. #D8258C as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: front-line armored warrior pose; shouting battle face; katana. | DOSURYU — FACE and garments from attached /ch_dosuryu.png (face only; invent a new pose). #c98578 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

en: What…! The King of Goryeo, murdered by his own subject?

lines: 허 참… 난 우리나라가 먼저 망하는 줄 알았더니, 고려가 먼저 가는구먼. 그래, 그 신하는 또 누군가?
en: Well I never… I thought our country would fall first, and Goryeo goes ahead of us. So who is this subject?

lines: 영원의 대장군이라 부릅니다 — 연, 혹은 개소문. 평민들은 조정이 못 들을 때 평양의 붉은 해라고 하지요.
en: They call him the Eternal General — Yeon, or Gesomun. Commoners say Red Sun of Pyongyang when they think courts cannot hear.
“Yeon Gesomun”…

lines: 그런 자에게 자네가 부탁을 하러 가겠다고?
en: A man who kills his own king at a banquet.
And you want to go and ask him for a favour.

lines: 그런 자라야 아직 "예"라고 할 수 있습니다, 폐하.
다른 이들은 다 회의에 물어야 하니까요.
en: A man like that is the only kind who can still say yes, Majesty.
Everyone else has to ask a council.
And what will it cost?
Only me. I’m cheap.

lines: 자네가 하는 일 중에 싼 건 없네, 춘추.
…가게. 내가 더 좋은 질문을 떠올리기 전에.
en: Nothing you do is cheap, Chunchu.
…Go. Before I think of a better question.

blocks.html: The Queen lets him go. Nobody offers to go instead.
blocks.ko: 여왕이 그를 보낸다. 대신 가겠다는 사람은 없다.

lines: 공이 가서 돌아오지 않는다면, 내 흰 말의 말발굽이 반드시 고려 왕정을 짓밟을 것이오.
en: If you go and do not return, my white horse will trample Goryeo underfoot without fail.

lines: 60일 이내면 돌아올 것인데 이때에도 돌아오지 않는다면 다시 볼 기약이 없을 것입니다.
en: I will return within sixty days. If I have not returned by then, there will be no promise of meeting again.

blocks.label: The West Gate
blocks.ko: 서문

blocks.html: He leaves by the west gate of the Moon Palace on Hadong, a lean red bay he named for summer and winter, because a diplomat’s horse, he says, has to stand in both. Yushin walks beside the bridle as far as the gate and no farther, which for Yushin is a speech.
blocks.ko: 그는 하동을 타고 월성 서문으로 떠난다. 여름과 겨울에서 이름을 딴 마른 적갈색 말. 사신의 말은 둘 다 견뎌야 한다고, 그는 말한다. 유신은 굴레 옆을 걸어 문까지만 따라오고 그 이상은 오지 않는다. 유신에게 그건 연설이다.

blocks.caption: Sixty days there and back, through a country that has just killed its own king. He packs light.
blocks.ko: 가고 오는 데 육십 일. 방금 제 왕을 죽인 나라를 지나는 길이다. 짐은 가볍게 꾸린다.

en: Sixty days.
He knows the way back. Even if you forget.
You’re saying he’s smarter than me.
…Hear that, Hadong? Yushin trusts you.
It’s you I don’t trust.

blocks.label: Pyongyang
blocks.ko: 평양

blocks.html: Pyongyang lets him in through the red gate and keeps him waiting on the stair. When someone finally comes down, it is Dosuryu, the Grand Herald.
blocks.ko: 평양은 붉은 문루로 그를 들이고, 층계에서 기다리게 한다. 마침내 누가 내려오는데, 대대로 도수류다.

en: Your Excellency…

blocks.html: Chunchu requests to see the king.
blocks.ko: 춘추가 왕의 알현을 청한다.

blocks.html: King Bojang makes his request — though the word his is doing generous work, and everyone in the room knows for whom.
blocks.ko: 보장왕이 요구를 내놓는다 — 그의라는 말이 꽤 후하게 쓰인 셈이고, 방 안의 모두가 그것이 실은 누구의 요구인지 안다.

blocks.html: The price is simple. Give back the passes Silla took.
blocks.ko: 값은 간단하다. 신라가 가져간 고개들을 돌려 달라는 것이다.

en: Oi, Silla — why the long face?
And call it Goguryeo.
Not Goryeo. I am not tired enough to shorten my own country.
lines: 고려가 아니라. 내 나라를 줄일 만큼 지치지 않았다.

en: Goguryeo, then — if the chronicles insist.
Most men I meet have already shortened it.
lines: 제가 만난 대부분은 이미 줄여 부릅니다.
이 땅의 위기를 기회 삼아 영토를 내놓으라 하실 수 있습니까?
저는 신하이니 어쩔 수 없지요. 처분만 기다리겠습니다. 그럼, 이만…
en: You would take this land’s crisis as your chance, and demand territory?
As a subject I have no say, so I await your judgement. And now — I take my leave…

lines: 남의 집에 들어와 값을 거절하고도 눈을 피하지 않는구나.
신라엔 자존심이 없나? 아니면 자네만 없나?
en: You come into another man’s house, refuse his price, and still look me in the eye.
Has Silla no pride left? Or is it only you?

lines: 저는 제가 어디로 가는지만 압니다. 이 방에는 그 앞을 막아설 만큼 큰 것이 없습니다.
en: I know no such thing as pride.
Pride is a decoration for men who can afford to lose.
I know where I am going. There is nothing in this room large enough to stand in the way.

blocks.html: Outside the door, two Goguryeo soldiers have been listening the way soldiers listen — professionally, and for sport.
blocks.ko: 문 밖에서는 고구려 병사 둘이, 병사들이 듣는 방식으로 — 직업적으로, 그리고 심심풀이로 — 듣고 있다.

lines: …대막리지 면전에 대고 그러고도, 눈 한 번을 안 깜빡여.
en: Did you hear him?
…Said it to the Mangniji’s face. Didn’t blink once.

lines: 신라 놈들은 염라대왕 앞에 폼 나게 끌려가고 싶을 때 저런 소리를 하지.
en: Silla men talk like that when they want to walk into Yumla’s court stylishly.

lines: 말린 생선 하나 걸지. 무릎으로 기어 나올걸.
en: Bet you a dried fish he crawls out on his knees.
Bet you two he cries.

blocks.html: The door opens. Chunchu is escorted out between two attendants. His left hand is a red glove. Blood runs off the wrist and dots the stone like a trail someone meant to follow.
blocks.ko: 문이 열린다. 춘추가 시종 둘 사이에 호송되어 나온다. 왼손이 붉은 장갑이다. 피가 손목에서 흘러 돌바닥에 점점이 찍힌다. 누가 따라오라고 남긴 자국처럼.

en: …Ah?

lines: 왜 피야. 성왕의 활에 맹세코, 왜 이렇게 피가 많아.
en: Why is there blood. By the Holy King’s bow, why is there so much blood.
Did—— did the Mangniji cut him?
Move. Prison.

lines: 옥? 저승사자 코앞까지 갔다 온 놈이 얼굴은 그대로인데.
en: Prison? The man brushed past the death escort and he still has that face on.

blocks.label: The Cell
blocks.ko: 옥

blocks.html: They put him in a cell with a window. That is meant to be a courtesy. The courtesy does not include a physician.
blocks.ko: 그들은 창이 있는 방에 그를 가둔다. 나름의 예우라고 한다. 그 예우에는 의원은 포함되지 않는다.

en: (…Good. He looked. He will remember looking.)
blocks.art: Thought balloon.

blocks.html: What the guards do not know — what nobody in the corridor knows — is whose blade opened the hand. That answer waits in another man’s memory, for another meeting.
blocks.ko: 병사들이 모르는 것 — 복도의 그 누구도 모르는 것 — 은 누구의 칼이 그 손을 열었느냐다. 그 답은 다른 사람의 기억 속에, 다른 만남을 위해 기다려 둔다.

blocks.html: Chunchu has no physician, but he has a sleeve, and sewn into it is what a Silla envoy carries when he expects to be robbed. Somehow it reaches Seon Dohae, the king’s favourite, without passing through any door the Mangniji is watching.
blocks.ko: 춘추에게 의원은 없지만 소매는 있다. 그 안에는 털릴 각오를 한 신라 사신이 챙기는 것이 꿰매져 있다. 그것은 어찌어찌 막리지가 지키는 어느 문도 지나지 않고 왕의 총신 선도해에게 닿는다.

blocks.html: Chunchu secretly gave three hundred measures of blue cloth to the king’s favourite, Seon Dohae.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 푸른 베 삼백 보를 왕의 총신 선도해에게 몰래 주었다.
blocks.hanja: 春秋以靑布三百步 密贈王之寵臣先道解
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biographies — Kim Yushin; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 2 (Chunchu in Goguryeo, 642)

blocks.html: Seon Dohae arrives with a jar of wine and no guards, which is either courage or an arrangement. He pours two cups, drinks both when Chunchu does not reach for his, and starts talking about the sea.
blocks.ko: 선도해는 술 한 단지를 들고 호위도 없이 온다. 배짱이거나, 이미 말이 된 일이거나. 그는 두 잔을 따르고, 춘추가 손을 뻗지 않자 두 잔을 다 마신 뒤, 바다 이야기를 꺼낸다.

lines: 손이 그래서야 잔을 들겠소. 내가 마셔 드리지.
……그런데 공, 거북이와 토끼 이야기 들어 보셨소?
en: Can’t hold a cup with a hand like that. I’ll drink it for you.
…Tell me, my lord. Ever heard the one about the turtle and the rabbit?

lines: ……들어 봤어도, 공의 입으로 다시 듣고 싶군요.
en: …Even if I had, I’d like to hear it from you.

lines: 동해 용왕의 딸이 가슴앓이를 했다지. 의원이 그러는 거요, 토끼 간이면 낫는다고.
바다에 토끼가 있나. 그래서 거북이가 뭍에 올라가 토끼한테 말을 걸어.
“저 바다 한가운데 섬이 있는데, 물 맑고 열매 많고, 매도 수리도 못 오는 데다. 가자, 내 등에 타라.”
en: The Dragon King of the Eastern Sea had a daughter with a sick heart. The physician said a rabbit’s liver would cure her.
No rabbits in the sea. So the turtle climbs up on land and strikes up a conversation with a rabbit.
“Out in the middle of the sea there’s an island. Clear water, fruit everywhere, no hawks, no eagles. Come on. Get on my back.”
And the rabbit got on.

lines: 탔지. 성왕께서 강 건너실 때도 거북이 등을 밟으셨으니, 거북이는 대개 믿을 만하거든. 대개는.
두어 리쯤 가서 거북이가 고개를 돌리고 실토를 해. 사실은 네 간이 필요하다고.
en: Got right on. The Holy King ran across a river on turtles’ backs, so turtles are generally trustworthy. Generally.
Two or three li out, the turtle turns his head and confesses. Actually, we need your liver.
And do you know what the rabbit said?

lines: “아이고, 나는 신령의 자손이라 오장을 꺼내 씻어 둘 수 있거든. 마침 요새 속이 답답해서 간을 꺼내 바위 밑에 말려 두고 왔지 뭐냐. 돌아가서 가져오자.”
거북이가 믿고 돌아갔지. 뭍에 닿자마자 토끼는 풀숲으로 쏙.
“멍청하긴. 간 없이 사는 놈이 어디 있냐.”
en: “Oh dear. I’m descended from spirits, I can take out my insides and wash them. My chest’s been tight lately, so I left my liver drying under a rock. Let’s go back and fetch it.”
The turtle believed him and turned around. The moment they touched the shore, the rabbit was into the grass.
“Idiot. Who lives without a liver?”

blocks.html: Seon Dohae refills his own cup and looks at nothing in particular. Chunchu looks at his ruined hand for a long time, then laughs once, quietly, the way a man laughs when a lock he has been picking turns over.
blocks.ko: 선도해는 제 잔을 다시 채우고 아무 데도 아닌 곳을 본다. 춘추는 망가진 손을 오래 내려다보다가, 한 번 조용히 웃는다. 붙들고 있던 자물쇠가 돌아갈 때 사람이 웃는 식으로.

en: …Could I trouble you for paper?
The left one’s in no state, so I’ll use the right.

blocks.html: The letter goes to the king, not the Mangniji. The passes were Goguryeo's to begin with, it says, and once Chunchu is home he will ask his sovereign to give them back. He signs with a flourish. He has no intention of doing any such thing. His drinking partner, finishing the jar, has no intention of mentioning it.
blocks.ko: 편지는 막리지가 아니라 왕에게 간다. 그 고개들은 본래 고구려 땅이니, 돌아가면 제 임금께 돌려드리라 청하겠다고 적혀 있다. 춘추는 멋들어지게 서명한다. 그럴 생각은 털끝만큼도 없다. 술단지를 비우던 술친구도 그 말을 꺼낼 생각이 털끝만큼도 없다.

blocks.label: Surabol
blocks.ko: 서라벌

blocks.html: On the sixtieth day Yushin starts counting out men. He does not ask the Queen first.
blocks.ko: 예순째 되는 날, 유신은 병사를 헤아리기 시작한다. 여왕께 먼저 여쭙지 않는다.

blocks.label: The Mangniji’s Desk
blocks.ko: 막리지의 책상

blocks.html: In Pyongyang, Dosuryu brings Yeon two pieces of paper on the same morning. One is the envoy’s letter to the king. The other is a scout’s report from the border.
blocks.ko: 평양에서 도수류가 같은 날 아침 연에게 종이 두 장을 가져온다. 하나는 사신이 왕에게 쓴 편지다. 다른 하나는 국경에서 온 척후의 보고다.

lines: 편지엔 저놈이 제 여왕한테 고개를 돌려 달라 청하겠다고 써 있어.
이건 신라 군사 만이 국경에 진을 쳤다는 거고. 맨 앞에 흰 말이 있대.
en: The letter says he’ll ask his queen to give back the passes.
He won’t, of course.
This one says ten thousand Silla men are camped at the border. With a white horse at the front.
…What? The Sword of the Divine Country is coming?
…Let him go.
Sir?

lines: 그런데 진짜… 삼한에서 가장 교활한 자라는 이 춘추가 뭐길래, 신라의 도검이 직접 온다는 거냐?
en: Did you not hear me? Release Chunchu.
But truly… who is this Chunchu — the most cunning man in Samhan — that the Sword of Silla comes for him himself?

lines: 신라의 검이 누군데 영원의 대장군이 이렇게 펄쩍 뛰어?
en: Who is this Sword of Silla, that the Eternal General jumps like this?
Don’t tell me… you’re afraid?

lines: 형님, 아무리 죽을 각오를 한 자라도, 호랑이는 함부로 건드리는 게 아니오.
우리도 언젠가 유신을 대적할 날이 오겠지…
하지만 춘추 따위로 그럴 건 아니오.
en: Old man— even a man ready to die does not poke a tiger for no reason.
The day will come when we face Yushin…
but not over something like Chunchu.

lines: 저놈이 서명했소. 언젠가 내 앞에서 소리 내 읽게 할 거요.
en: Keep the letter.
He signed it. One day I’ll make him read it back to me.
That’s the win.

blocks.label: The Border Camp
blocks.ko: 국경 진영

blocks.html: On the Silla side of the border, in a camp that should not exist, Yushin has brought the horse. Hadong is tied at the front of the lines with an empty saddle, the way some armies carry an empty chair. When Chunchu comes down the last hill on foot, thinner, the left hand bound against his chest, the horse sees him before the men do.
blocks.ko: 국경 이쪽, 있어서는 안 될 진영에 유신은 그 말을 데려와 있다. 하동은 빈 안장을 얹은 채 대열 맨 앞에 매여 있다. 어떤 군대가 빈 의자를 메고 다니듯이. 춘추가 마지막 언덕을 걸어 내려올 때, 더 마르고, 왼손을 가슴에 동여맨 채, 사람들보다 말이 먼저 그를 알아본다.

lines: 너 살쪘다. 유신이가 나보다 잘 먹였네.
en: …Hadong.
You got fat. Yushin fed you better than they fed me.
Hand.
…Give it here. The right one.

blocks.html: Chunchu cannot close the left hand on a rein, so Yushin ties both reins around his right wrist himself, in a knot he learned in the drill yard for men who have been shot. He says nothing about the hand, and Chunchu says nothing about the camp.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 왼손으로 고삐를 쥘 수 없다. 그래서 유신이 두 고삐를 그의 오른 손목에 직접 묶는다. 화살 맞은 사람을 위해 연병장에서 배운 매듭으로. 그는 손에 대해 아무 말도 하지 않고, 춘추도 진영에 대해 아무 말도 하지 않는다.

lines: 자네 진이 선 그날 아침에 내 방 문이 열렸네. 까닭도 없이.
en: They opened my door the morning your camp appeared. No reason given.
Perhaps he heard I was coming.
(…A more fearsome man than I expected. Both of them.)

blocks.caption: One envoy coming south, ten thousand Silla men coming north, and a border between them that has gone very polite.
blocks.ko: 남쪽으로 오는 사신 하나, 북쪽으로 가는 신라군 만 명. 그 사이의 국경은 갑자기 몹시 예의 바르다.

blocks.html: One envoy left Pyongyang bleeding. Whose blade was it? Now the King of Baekje walks in on purpose, laughing…!
blocks.ko: 사신 하나가 피를 흘리며 평양을 떠났다. 누구의 칼이었을까? 이번엔 백제의 왕이 제 발로 걸어 들어온다. 웃으면서…!

logline.en: Two new strongmen, one table. Yeon is surprised the King of Baekje came himself.
logline.ko: 새로 힘을 쥔 두 사내, 탁자 하나. 연은 백제 왕이 몸소 왔다는 게 놀랍다.

images.alt: Dutch: disguised Euija at Pyongyang seongmun — gate shadow-wedge hiding a royal face
images.prompt: Minimal iconic 16:9 still. DUTCH at a REAL Pyongyang seongmun — red two-tier munru, timber doors with iron bosses from attached fortress/city place refs. King Euija in commoner disguise mid-stride asking at the gate — FACE AND garments from attached Euija portrait but stripped to dusty travel silk / cloak, NEW body leaning into the gatekeeper’s shadow, not fashion-plate clone. ONE device: a hard shadow-wedge of the gate leaf hiding a royal face. Euija hex as a thin warm rim only. Natural dusk sky, crushed blacks, long shadows. No army. No readable plaques. No text. No watermark. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock: anamorphic movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain. A CAMERA in a real Korean place — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D archviz, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow, rim-aura, or god-ray envelope around people — light is a plane or a hard key. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portrait — NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: dutch, crane, worm’s-eye, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key + long shadows — not even daylight wash. ICONIC MINIMAL: ONE architectural device a lens can see; empty negative space; tiny figures or lower-third; the world stays in the shot. Dress: Dark charcoal robe and trousers under red-edged armor, a red cape falling off the shoulders. Demeanor: Arrogant, theatrical, loud; looks down at people (worm's-eye suits him). NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft.
