blocks.html: King Euija hears how Goguryeo’s king died, and feels the one thing a king should never admit to. Envy.
blocks.ko: 의자왕은 고구려 왕이 어떻게 죽었는지 듣고, 왕이라면 절대 인정해선 안 될 감정을 느낀다. 부러움.

blocks.label: Sabi
blocks.ko: 사비

en: What…! The King of Goryeo, murdered by his own subject?
This is an opportunity…

lines: 회의 하나를 통째로, 저녁 한 끼에.
내가 그랬다간 사택 놈들이 나를 국에 넣어 끓이겠지.
en: A whole Summit, in one dinner.
If I tried that, the Satek would serve me in the soup.
Gyebek. We’re going north.
How many days.
As long as it takes. Forever, if he’s charming.
Forever is not a number, Majesty.
I will pack for twenty.

blocks.html: Other kings would write for troops. Euija rides north himself, with three men, one of them Gyebek counting the days. The man at the door does not give his name.
blocks.ko: 다른 왕이라면 군사를 청하는 편지를 쓸 것이다. 의자는 직접 북으로 간다. 데려가는 것은 셋, 그중 하나는 날짜를 세는 계백이다. 문 앞의 사내는 이름을 대지 않는다.

blocks.label: Pyongyang
blocks.ko: 평양

en: Have you come to see the king?
No… I have come to see the one with real power.
He does not grant an audience to just anyone.
Tell him who I am, and he will come at once.

blocks.html: Yeon is surprised that the new King of Baekje has come personally.
blocks.ko: 백제의 새 임금이 몸소 왔다는 사실에 연도 놀란다.

lines: 벽은 왕과 귀족세력을 싹 다 갈아엎어버렸다지요? 그거 하나만은 조금 부럽네...
en: I hear you ploughed under the king and the whole noble faction? That one thing, I rather envy…
Could you not do the same on your side?

lines: 나는 폭군 소리 듣고 그다음 날 죽을 거요, 참.
en: Look here — I am the king myself.
General Gesomun—
I would be called a tyrant and killed the next day, ah.

lines: 그대들이 저 바깥 성벽에서 우리 임금을 죽였소. 이 방에서도 보이는 저기서.
en: Your people killed a king of ours on that wall out there. You can see it from this room.

lines: 그럼 한성은? 우리 임금 목을 그쪽 성벽에 걸어 놓고 한 철 농사라 하지 않았소.
en: And Hansung? You put our king’s head on your own wall and called it a season’s work.

blocks.html: Once, a Goguryeo king came south and took Baekje’s old capital. The Baekje king tried to run. They caught him and killed him at the foot of a mountain. Baekje has not forgotten. Goguryeo has not apologised.
blocks.ko: 한때 고구려 왕이 남으로 내려와 백제의 옛 도읍을 빼앗았다. 백제 왕은 달아나려 했다. 그들은 그를 붙잡아 산 아래에서 죽였다. 백제는 잊지 않았다. 고구려는 사과하지 않았다.

lines: 게다가… 이 방에 있는 둘 중, 실제로 고려왕을 시해해 본 자는 하나뿐이고. 나는 아니외다.
en: Besides… of the two men in this room, only one has actually murdered a king of Goryeo. It was not me.

blocks.html: Yeon puts the blade on the table between them. Not pointed at anything. Just there.
blocks.ko: 연이 칼을 둘 사이의 상 위에 올려놓는다. 겨눈 것도 아니다. 그냥 거기에 놓아둔다.

blocks.html: Behind the king, Gyebek’s hand is already on his own hilt. Nobody saw it get there.
blocks.ko: 왕의 등 뒤에서 계백의 손은 이미 제 칼자루에 가 있다. 언제 갔는지 본 사람이 없다.

lines: 내가 지금 이 칼로 그대를 베지 말아야 할 이유를, 하나만 대 보시오…!
en: Give me one reason I should not cut you down with this blade where you stand…!
Four steps.
Three.

lines: 네 걸음이오. 몸을 뒤로 빼고 있소.
en: Four. You are leaning back.
Pfft—hahahahahaha!!

lines: 개소문 자네… 군사는 통솔할 줄 알아도, 정치는 딱 봐도 초보구려. 정치가 뭔지 아나?
정치는 연금술이야. 내가 이미 하고 싶은 일에다, 명분을 만들어 붙이는 연금술.
지금 이웃 나라 백성들 사이에 자네를 우러르는 자가 얼마나 되는지 아나?
연개소문 — 탐관오리를 싹 갈아엎고 새 시대를 열 사내.
그런데… 여기서 백제왕을 죽이면, 그 나라들에 죄다 소문이 나겠지.
자네는 임금 죽이기를 즐기는 미친놈이 되는 거야. 그것뿐이고.
en: Gesomun… you may know how to command an army, but in politics you are plainly a novice. Do you know what politics is?
Politics is alchemy. The alchemy of manufacturing a justification for what I already want to do.
Do you know how many people in the surrounding countries admire you right now?
Yeon Gesomun — the man who ploughed under the corrupt officials and will bring a new age.
But… kill the King of Baekje now, and word reaches every one of those countries.
You become a madman who enjoys killing kings. Nothing else.

lines: 고구려는 태양신의 피를 이은 성스러운 임금이 세운 나라요.
성왕. 해모수의 아들. 하늘에서 내려온 줄기요.
en: This land is not just dirt.
Goguryeo is the land of the holy king, descended from the sun god.
The Holy King. Son of Haemosu. A line that came down from heaven.

lines: 잠깐… 잠깐만. 지금 한 나라의 대막리지가 —
다 큰 사내가, 나라를 이끄는 사내가 —
en: Pfft—!!
Hahahahaha!!
Wait… wait. The Supreme Commander of a country —
a grown man, a man who leads a kingdom —
still believes in spirits and sun chariots?

lines: 그는 하늘에서 내려왔다. 활로 나라를 열었다.
en: Do not laugh.
He came down from heaven. He opened a kingdom with a bow.
That blood is the bone of these people.

lines: 아, 물론. 활 잘 쏘는 사내는 하나 있었겠지.
나머지는 백성 줄 세우려고 지은 이야기고.
농부를 무릎 꿇리는 데는, 칼보다 태양신이 싸게 먹히거든.
en: Oh, certainly. There was probably a man who shot well.
The rest is a story for keeping people in line.
To make a farmer kneel, a sun god is cheaper than a sword.

lines: 나는 들에서 자랐소. 들에서 들은 건 — 거짓이 아니오.
en: …So that is what your palace teaches.
I grew up in the marches. What the marches tell — is not a lie.

blocks.html: Yeon asks for the same thing he asked Chunchu for. He has only ever had one price.
blocks.ko: 연은 춘추에게 요구했던 것과 똑같은 것을 요구한다. 그의 값은 언제나 하나뿐이었다.

lines: 죽령 이북 땅은 본래 고구려의 것이었다. 돌려주면 구원병을 보내 주겠다.
en: The land north of the pass was Goguryeo’s. Return it, and I will send relief troops.

lines: 도대체 무슨 배짱으로 저 앞에 나선 건지…!
en: What nerve, to come before him like that…!

lines: 이보게, 나는 한 나라의 왕일세. 왕은 사람이 아니야.
죽을 자리까지 다 정해 두고 왔고, 바깥에도 미리 일러 두었네.
나를 죽여 봐야, 더 젊고 더 성난 백제왕이 하나 앉을 뿐이지.
en: Listen — I am the king of a country. A king is not a man.
I made my arrangements even for death, and gave warning abroad beforehand.
Kill me and all you get is a newer, angrier King of Baekje on the throne.
Not a man, you say…

lines: 신라에는 «노비는 사람 수에 넣지 않는다»는 말이 있다더군.
우습지 않소? 맨 아래도 사람이 아니고, 맨 위도 사람이 아니야.
사람인 것들은 전부 그 사이에 끼어 있고.
en: They have a saying in Silla — that slaves are not counted as people.
Funny, is it not? The bottom is not a person, and the top is not a person either.
Everyone who gets to be a person is wedged in between.

lines: 신라에는 바닷길이 없어. 당이든 천축이든 서역이든, 나가려면 이 항구 하나뿐이야.
en: Look at this map.
Silla has no trade route at all — for Tang, for Tianzhu, for the western regions, there is only this one harbour.
Danghang Fortress would be the right target.

blocks.caption: One harbour. Silla’s only door to the Tang.
blocks.ko: 항구 하나. 신라가 당으로 나가는 단 하나의 문.

en: We have our own mouth — the White River under Sabi.
Clan berths stacked like teeth. Cut Danghang Fortress and Silla starves for partners; keep our river and we eat either way.
lines: 우리에겐 우리 하구가 있다 — 사비 아래 백강.
가문 선석이 이빨처럼 겹쳐 있지. 당항성을 끊으면 신라는 짝이 굶고, 우리 강만 지키면 우리는 어느 쪽이든 먹는다.

en: You sound like a harbour clerk.
Good. Kings who forget docks start wars they cannot feed.
lines: 좋다. 부두를 잊는 임금은, 먹일 수 없는 전쟁을 시작한다.

en: Do you know a “Kim Chunchu” of Silla?
Kim Chunchu? First I have heard of him… royalty? Why?

lines: 그냥… 궁금해서. 자네를 그리 좋아하는 것 같지가 않더군.
자네를 없애 달라고, 두 손 모아 빌더구먼.
en: Just… curious. He does not seem to care for you much.
He spoke of being rid of you, hands folded in prayer.

lines: 춘추라… 누군지는 몰라도, 그렇게 쌓아 두는 자는 만만치 않지.
허나 남에게 무릎 꿇는 자는 두렵지 않소이다.
en: Chunchu… whoever he is, a man who stores things up like that is no easy sort.
But I do not fear a man who kneels to others.

blocks.html: For a moment Yeon’s eyes go somewhere else — to a door, to a hand, to a stare that did not ask to be liked.
blocks.ko: 잠깐, 연의 눈이 다른 곳으로 간다 — 문과, 손과, 호감을 바라지 않던 눈빛으로.

blocks.html: After the territory talk the room had gone quiet in the wrong way. Yeon had asked if the man had no pride. The answer had been worse than no.
blocks.ko: 영토 이야기가 끝난 뒤 방은 잘못된 방식으로 조용해졌다. 연이 자존심이 없느냐고 물었다. 대답은 없다는 것보다 나빴다.

en: I know no such thing as pride.
I know only my goal.

blocks.html: Then Chunchu had reached to his own belt, drawn a short blade, and driven it through his own left hand — clean, deliberate, eyes never leaving Yeon’s face — and held the wound up like a seal.
blocks.ko: 그때 춘추는 제 허리에서 짧은 칼을 빼어, 제 왼손을 스스로 찔렀다 — 말쑥하고 고의적으로, 눈은 한 번도 연의 얼굴에서 떼지 않은 채 — 그리고 그 상처를 도장처럼 들어 올렸다.

lines: 제가 저를 얼마까지 쓸 수 있는지, 이것입니다.
자존심을 묻지 마십시오. 무엇을 망가뜨릴 각오인지 물으십시오.
en: This is how much of myself I will spend.
Do not ask me for pride. Ask me what I am willing to ruin.

blocks.html: Yeon remembers the stare more than the blood. Hot, dry, almost joyful. The stare of a man who had decided the room would believe him, and had paid in advance.
blocks.ko: 연은 피보다 그 눈빛을 더 오래 기억한다. 뜨겁고, 건조하고, 거의 기쁘기까지 한. 방이 자기를 믿게 되리라 결정한 사람의 눈빛. 값을 먼저 치른 사람의 눈빛.

lines: 제 손을 제 칼로 뚫어서 내 귀를 열더군.
그런 눈을 한 사람을 하나 더 만났소.
en: That Chunchu…
He put steel through his own hand to make me listen.
I have met one other man with eyes like that.
Oh?

lines: 둘 중 누가 더 무서운지는 아직 모르겠소.
en: You.
I do not yet know which of you frightens me more.
Flattery. Keep going.
It was not flattery.

lines: 그럼 다른 하나는? 저쪽 칼 말이오. 김유신.
en: And the other one? Their sword. Kim Yushin.

blocks.html: Yeon’s cup stops an inch from his mouth. Just for a breath. Then he drinks.
blocks.ko: 연의 잔이 입 앞 한 치에서 멈춘다. 딱 한 숨. 그리고 마신다.

en: Ha! Did you see that, Gyebek? His cup stopped.
I don’t flinch.
It stopped, Majesty.

lines: 올 때는 셋이더니, 갈 때는 다섯이구려.
en: You came with three. You’re leaving with five.
…Did Your Majesty come as an envoy, or to do some shopping?
blocks.art: Dusk in the guest-house yard: Gesomun looks over Euija’s retinue, two more faces than came with him.

lines: 나는 사람을 모으는 재주가 있소. 공은 사람을 줄이는 재주가 있고.
en: I have a gift for gathering people. You have a gift for reducing them.

lines: 평양에 남아라. 탈 만한 말 한 필 주지.
en: You. The one who counts steps.
Stay in Pyongyang. I’ll give you a horse worth riding.
I gave my word.

lines: 관두시오. 저놈은 그 말을 딱 한 번만 하오.
en: Don’t bother. He only ever says it once.

blocks.html: In the morning he rides south with all five. Nobody raises the subject of the extra two. He carries a map of Danghang Fortress in his head, and Yeon’s warning about Chunchu folded away like a knife he intends to use later.
blocks.ko: 아침에 그는 다섯을 모두 거느리고 남으로 떠난다. 늘어난 둘에 대해서는 아무도 입을 열지 않는다. 머릿속에는 당항성 지도가 있고, 춘추를 조심하라던 개소문의 말은 나중에 쓸 칼처럼 접어 품에 넣어 두었다.

blocks.html: On the road home, Euija is still laughing.
blocks.ko: 돌아오는 길에도 의자는 계속 웃는다.

en: His cup stopped! Find out why.
Yes, Majesty.

blocks.html: He does not wait for the answer. By the first frost, forty-odd Silla fortresses are flying Baekje yellow. He takes them in one autumn, and he laughs the whole way.
blocks.ko: 그는 답을 기다리지 않는다. 첫서리가 내릴 무렵, 신라 성 마흔 남짓에 백제의 누런 깃발이 걸린다. 한 가을에 다 거두고, 내내 웃는다.

blocks.html: In the sixteenth year Euija raised troops, attacked more than forty Silla cities and sent men to hold them. He made peace and friendship with Goguryeo, and plotted to take Danghang Fortress and cut off Silla's road to court.
blocks.ko: 16년, 의자가 군사를 일으켜 신라의 40여 성을 치고 또 군사를 보내 지키게 하였다. 고구려와 화친하여 우호를 맺고, 당항성을 빼앗아 신라가 조정에 들어오는 길을 끊으려 꾀하였다.
blocks.hanja: 十六年，義慈興兵伐新羅四十餘城，又發兵以守之，與高麗和親通好，謀欲取党項城以絕新羅入朝之路。
blocks.source: Jiu Tangshu (舊唐書) bk. 199上, Eastern Barbarians — Baekje, Zhenguan 16 (642)

blocks.html: Why does the Eternal General flinch at one Silla name? Go back to a ditch, a white horse, and an unknown captain…!
blocks.ko: 영원의 대장군은 왜 신라의 이름 하나에 움찔하는가? 참호 하나, 흰 말 한 마리, 이름 없는 대장 하나에게로 거슬러 가 보자…!

logline.en: Kim Yushin — a name that strikes fear in all of Samhan. Maybe this is why.
logline.ko: 김유신. 삼한 어디서든 두려움을 부르는 이름. 아마 이래서일 것이다.

images.alt: Over his father's armored shoulder, young Yushin kneels with his helmet in hand, the white horse steaming behind him and Nangbi Fortress in smoke
images.prompt: 16:9 over-the-shoulder still from behind Seohyun's armored shoulder (sharp foreground, steel lamellar and blue cloth). Midground: young beardless Yushin kneeling on one knee in churned earth, helmet held in his hand, head up, eyes fierce, crescent-moon headband. Behind him the white war horse, still nameless, steaming. Background: Nangbi Fortress walls on a hill in smoke, melting into bokeh. Storm light with one hard break, #2A5FB8 on his blue cloth. CANON — KIM YUSHIN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_kim_yushin_hwarang.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Tall, broad-shouldered, long black hair in a high topknot-ponytail with trailing Silla-blue cloth tails; level hard brows, deep-set eyes. Dress: Silla-blue po and trousers, plum-violet sash knotted at the waist, white inner collar, dark wrapped forearms. Off duty: plain blue po, no jewelry. Now: Hwarang years (stage portrait): BEARDLESS, Silla-blue headband with a gold crescent moon, its tails trailing. Demeanor: Confucian: he STANDS — never sits in lotus. Weighs, counts, frowns at sums; tight jaw, rare dry half-smile. Grief shows as stillness, not tears. Armor: Silla kit: steel lamellar cuirass and skirt, tall pointed jonghyeongju helm with a short plume. Battle armor: plates are METALLIC GRAY STEEL lamellar copied from the attached lamellar ref, cloth peeking at collar, sleeves, skirt, sash and plume-cord in the wearer's color only. Ignore labels and watermarks on armor refs. Not Japanese kabuto, not fantasy plate, not a gold-painted suit. Sword: Fish sword — Ring-pommel fish sword — Gaya fish on the pommel, Silla blue in the fuller. Pommel motif fish inside the small ring (name only; do not attach the pommel ECU). Carry: One fish-ring sword at the left hip. Never two blades. Fighting: Orthodox FORWARD one-hand grip, ring at the heel of the fist; square upright stance, short economical straight cuts and thrusts — the drill-yard form he teaches. Mounted, he cuts down from the saddle on the off side. #2A5FB8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: sitting in lotus or holding prayer beads; katana, tsuba or curved blade (ignore the sword drawn on his portrait); two swords at once; blue glow aura. | HANGYUL (한결, yushin's horse) — attached board /obj_hangyul.png: Pure white war horse, long flowing white mane, powerful galloping build — match the board. Eighteen years under Yushin since Nangbi; puts his nose into Yushin's chest and waits. | KIM SEOHYEON — FACE and garments from attached /ch_kim_seohyun.png (face only; invent a new pose). Demeanor: Yushin's father; Gaya blood, Silla duty, quiet. Armor: Silla kit: steel lamellar cuirass and skirt, tall pointed jonghyeongju helm with a short plume. Battle armor: plates are METALLIC GRAY STEEL lamellar copied from the attached lamellar ref, cloth peeking at collar, sleeves, skirt, sash and plume-cord in the wearer's color only. Ignore labels and watermarks on armor refs. Not Japanese kabuto, not fantasy plate, not a gold-painted suit. Sword: Fish sword — Ring-pommel fish sword — Gaya fish on the pommel, Silla blue in the fuller. Pommel motif fish inside the small ring (name only; do not attach the pommel ECU). #3E8EF0 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a hand-painted ANIME film frame composed like a Romanticist master painting. FIGURES are anime: clean ink linework, simplified anime faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is watercolor and oil: skies, dust, ground and light are visibly hand-painted — wet-in-wet blooms, pigment granulation, soft bleeding edges, dry-brush dust, rich oil glazes in the darks, faint paper grain; edges of the frame dissolve into wash. LAYOUT is Romanticism (Delacroix, Géricault, Friedrich, Goya, Turner): heroic diagonal or pyramid composition, small figures against a sublime storm sky or vast field, extreme foreshortening (worm’s-eye from the dirt or straight down from above), one break in the clouds or one shaft as the key. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength (Caravaggio, Rembrandt, night-interior cinema): an extreme value range — inky blacks right beside small near-white highlights, almost no middle grey; 70–80% of the frame in deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo and black); ONE hard directional key (a lamp, a single cloud-break, a low sun shaft, firelight) carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock: anamorphic movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain. A CAMERA in a real Korean place — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D archviz, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portrait — NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: dutch, crane, worm’s-eye, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key + long shadows — not even daylight wash. ICONIC MINIMAL: ONE architectural device a lens can see; empty negative space; tiny figures or lower-third; the world stays in the shot. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor portrait garments gold. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Not a katana, not a tsuba, not a short jian, not a ball pommel. Real Korean architecture: grey giwa, timber, packed earth. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: movie frame in a real place, not a graphic poster; iconic one-device layout, empty frame, lower-third; high contrast chiaroscuro, not even wash; 2D animated cel-painterly, no photoreal; cinematography: dutch, wide, bokeh, mise-en-scène. Never: halo / bloom / glow aura / emissive skin around figures; graphic split-screen or black-triangle overlay; photoreal live-action or 3D archviz; busy extras crowding an iconic frame; copy-pasted reference as a fashion plate; flat even-daylight postcard wide; katana / tsuba / random sabre length instead of sw_bidam 환두대도.

images.at: takes the trench in one jump
images.alt: From inside the trench, the white horse flies overhead with Yushin low on its neck, soldiers staring up
images.prompt: 9:16 extreme worm's-eye from inside a muddy trench. Overhead, the white war horse flies across the trench in one leap, belly and tucked hooves filling the upper frame against a storm sky with one break; young beardless Yushin low over its neck, sword in a one-handed forward grip. At the frame edges, crouched Silla soldiers' silhouettes and spear shafts, faces turned up, mouths open. Mud spray in dry-brush. blocks.html: Kim Yushin — a name that strikes fear in all of Samhan. Maybe this is why.
blocks.ko: 김유신. 삼한 어디서든 두려움을 부르는 이름. 아마 이래서일 것이다.

blocks.html: Autumn. Silla’s army is breaking against a Goguryeo line that didn’t bother to stay behind its wall. It came down the hill and formed up behind a row of pits, and now the men who should be charging are sitting in the trenches. Yushin is thirty-four, a banner captain. His white horse doesn’t even have a name.
blocks.ko: 가을. 신라군이 부서지고 있다. 고구려군은 성벽 뒤에 머물 생각도 하지 않았다. 언덕을 내려와 구덩이 줄 뒤에 진을 쳤고, 돌격해야 할 병사들은 지금 참호에 주저앉아 있다. 유신은 서른넷, 깃발 하나를 맡은 대장이다. 그의 흰 말에는 아직 이름도 없다.

blocks.html: A Goguryeo wall that is about to make somebody famous.
blocks.ko: 곧 누군가를 유명하게 만들 고구려의 성벽.

blocks.speaker: A spearman in the trench
lines: 성에서 나왔습니다, 나리. 아예 나와 버렸어요. 나와도 되는 줄 아는 거죠.
en: They came out of the fort, sir. Right out. They knew they could.

blocks.html: He rides back to his father’s command post, gets down, and takes off his helmet, which is how a son asks permission in front of an army.
blocks.ko: 그는 아버지의 지휘소로 말을 몰아 돌아와 내리고, 투구를 벗는다. 군대 앞에서 아들이 허락을 구하는 방식이다.

lines: 옷깃을 쥐고 떨쳐야 갖옷이 바로 서고, 벼리를 들어야 그물이 펴진다고 했습니다.
en: Father. We’re losing.
They say you shake a coat by the collar to make it hang straight, and lift the head-rope to open a net.
…Let me be the collar.
…Put your helmet on.
Then go.

blocks.html: The white horse takes the trench in one jump that the men in it will describe for the rest of their lives, usually with their hands. Mud to the girth. A horn somewhere, too late. The Goguryeo line bends where he hits it, like a wall that has just remembered it is made of men. In, out. In again. The third time Yushin comes back there is something heavy hanging from his saddle, and the men in the trench are already climbing out after him.
blocks.ko: 흰 말은 단번에 참호를 뛰어넘는다. 그 안에 있던 병사들이 평생, 대개는 손짓까지 해 가며 이야기하게 될 도약이다. 뱃대끈까지 차오르는 진흙. 어딘가에서 뒤늦은 뿔피리. 그가 부딪친 자리에서 고구려의 줄이 휜다. 제가 사람으로 쌓였다는 걸 막 떠올린 성벽처럼. 들어갔다, 나왔다. 다시 들어간다. 세 번째로 유신이 돌아올 때 안장에는 묵직한 것이 매달려 있고, 참호의 병사들은 벌써 그를 따라 기어 나오고 있다.

blocks.html: He brings the weight on his saddle back to the command post and sets it down in the mud in front of his father, wrapped in a torn banner, because he does not know what else a son is supposed to do with a general’s head. The staff officers wait for the speech. Seohyun looks at the bundle, then at the boy, for long enough that someone coughs.
blocks.ko: 그는 안장에 매달린 것을 지휘소로 가져와 아버지 앞 진흙 위에 내려놓는다. 찢긴 깃발에 싸여 있다. 장군의 머리를 아들이 어떻게 해야 하는지, 그는 모른다. 참모들이 연설을 기다린다. 서현은 보따리를 보고, 아들을 본다. 누군가 헛기침을 할 만큼 오래.

en: …Your helmet’s crooked.

blocks.html: He reaches up and straightens it himself, both hands, the way you fix a boy’s collar before a feast, and then turns away and shouts for his officers before anyone can see his face. It is the most Kim Seohyun has ever said to his son about anything, and Yushin will carry it longer than the helmet.
blocks.ko: 그는 손을 뻗어 직접 바로잡는다. 두 손으로, 잔치 전에 아이 옷깃을 매만지듯. 그리고 누가 얼굴을 보기 전에 돌아서서 장교들을 부른다. 김서현이 아들에게 무엇에 대해서든 해 준 말 중 가장 긴 말이다. 유신은 그것을 투구보다 오래 지니고 다닌다.

blocks.html: Nobody waits for the officers. The trench climbs out after the white horse, uphill, and by dusk the Goguryeo line is lying in the field. The fort on the hill opens its gate before anyone knocks.
blocks.ko: 장교들을 기다리는 사람은 없다. 참호가 흰 말을 따라 언덕 위로 기어 나오고, 해 질 녘이면 고구려의 줄은 들판에 누워 있다. 언덕 위 성은 누가 두드리기도 전에 문을 연다.

blocks.speaker: A Silla spearman
lines: 저 흰 말 누구야? 누구 집 아들이냐고?
en: Who was that? The white horse— whose son is that?

blocks.html: That night he asks the groom what the white horse is called. The groom says it has no name; it came from the royal stable as a spare. Yushin looks at it for a long time, at the mud on its chest and the way it still will not quite stand still.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 그는 마부에게 흰 말의 이름을 묻는다. 이름은 없다고, 왕실 마구간에서 여벌로 온 말이라고 마부가 답한다. 유신은 오래도록 말을 바라본다. 가슴팍의 진흙을, 아직도 가만히 서 있지 못하는 모양을.

en: Hangyul.
…It means steady. It came back steady. All three times.

blocks.html: The few who get out of Nangbi walk north for nine days with the story, and it grows a little at every well. By Pyongyang the white horse has cleared the trench at a gallop with a general’s head in one hand and a banner in the other, and the man on it has a name the Goguryeo clerks must write down for the first time.
blocks.ko: 낭비성을 빠져나간 몇 안 되는 자들이 이야기를 들고 아흐레를 북으로 걷는다. 이야기는 우물을 지날 때마다 조금씩 자란다. 평양에 닿을 무렵 흰 말은 한 손에 장군의 머리, 한 손에 깃발을 들고 전속력으로 참호를 넘었고, 그 위의 사내에게는 고구려 서기들이 처음으로 받아 적어야 하는 이름이 생겨 있다.

blocks.label: The Pyongyang Court
blocks.ko: 평양 조정

blocks.html: In Pyongyang the report is read to the king twice, the second time because he asks for it. At the back of the hall the Yeon heir, twenty-four, stands with his arms folded, the way he stands everywhere.
blocks.ko: 평양에서 보고는 왕 앞에서 두 번 읽힌다. 두 번째는 왕이 다시 읽으라 해서다. 전각 뒤편에서 연씨 가문의 후계자, 스물넷이 팔짱을 끼고 서 있다. 그는 어디서나 그렇게 선다.

en: Kim Yushin… a banner captain.
We have never heard the name.

lines: 놈 하나가 도랑 하나 넘었는데 우리 오천이 드러누웠소. 그게 당주요? 칼이지.
en: You’ll hear it again.
One man jumps one ditch and five thousand of ours lie down. That’s a captain? That’s a sword.
Silla’s sword.

blocks.label: The High Commander’s House
blocks.ko: 막리지의 집

blocks.html: Gesomun’s family lives in the big house below the palace hill. His father, Yeon Taejo, has run the Summit for ten years. Long enough to outlive most of the men who voted for him. None of the ones who voted against. Most nights he comes home in a silence the servants have learned to walk around.
blocks.ko: 개소문의 집안은 왕궁 언덕 아래 큰 집에 산다. 아버지 연태조는 십 년째 회의의 윗자리를 지키고 있다. 그를 밀어준 사람들이 대부분 먼저 죽을 만큼 긴 세월이다. 반대한 사람들은 하나도 안 죽었다. 거의 매일 밤 그는 말없이 돌아오고, 하인들은 그 침묵을 비켜 다니는 법을 익혔다.

blocks.html: Tonight he does not take off his boots. He sits at the low table with a copy of the Nangbi report, the one the king asked to hear twice, and reads it a third time with his finger under the lines.
blocks.ko: 오늘 밤 그는 신도 벗지 않는다. 낮은 상 앞에 앉아, 왕이 두 번 읽으라 한 낭비성 보고의 사본을 펼쳐 놓고, 손가락으로 줄을 짚어 가며 세 번째로 읽는다.

en: Father. You’re still on that?
It’s one fortress. We take it back by spring.

lines: …오천 수급이다. 한 번 뛰어들어서. 그런 놈을 몇이나 봤느냐?
en: Sit.
…Five thousand heads. Off one charge. How many men have you seen do that?
One.
You. At the Colossal River.

lines: 나한텐 삼만 군사가 있었고, 강도 우리 편이었고, 을지 공이 명을 내렸다.
이놈은 도랑 하나에 말 한 필이다.
en: I had thirty thousand men, a river on my side, and Ulchi giving the orders.
He had a ditch and a horse.

blocks.html: Gesomun has seen his father angry, drunk and bleeding, and once, when he was seven, riding home from the Colossal River with a Sui banner rolled under his arm like a bolt of cloth. He has never seen him frightened of a piece of paper. He finds he does not know where to put his hands.
blocks.ko: 개소문은 아버지가 화내는 것도, 취한 것도, 피 흘리는 것도 보았다. 일곱 살 때는 수나라 깃발을 비단 한 필처럼 옆구리에 말아 끼고 살수에서 돌아오는 것도 보았다. 종이 한 장을 두려워하는 아버지는 처음 본다. 손을 어디 둬야 할지 모르겠다.

lines: 서른넷에 아직 당주다. 신라 놈들이 가야 손자를 더 빨리 올려 줄 리가 없지.
썩히고 있는 거다. 언제까지나 썩히진 않을 거고.
en: Thirty-four, and still a banner captain. Silla won’t let a Gaya grandson climb any faster.
They’re wasting him. They won’t waste him forever.

lines: 그럼 그 전에 제가 죽이면 됩니다.
en: Then I’ll kill him before they stop.

lines: 잘 들어라. 그놈이 고른 땅에선 절대 싸우지 마라. 화났을 때도 마라. 그리고 이 도성이 그놈을 고작 당주라고 하거든, 믿지 마라.
en: You’ll try.
Listen to me. Never on a field he picked. Never when you’re angry. And when this city tells you he’s only a captain, don’t believe it.
His Majesty already did.

lines: 전하는 두 번 들으시고 회의에 물으셨지.
회의가 뭘 했는지 아느냐? 성 다시 쌓는 값을 누가 낼지 반나절을 싸웠다. 아무도 그놈 이름을 입에 안 올렸어. 한 번도.
십 년을 그 방에 앉아 있었다. 저것들은 곳간 하나씩 이 나라를 잃어버릴 거다. 그러고는 신중했다고 하겠지.
en: His Majesty heard it twice and asked the Summit what to do.
Do you know what the Summit did? Argued half a day over who pays to rebuild the fort. Nobody said his name. Not once.
Ten years I’ve sat in that room. They’ll lose this country one granary at a time and call it caution.

blocks.html: Each of them learns his country at home. Euija learns the great clans at his father’s table. Chunchu learns the council from the day it walked his grandfather off the throne. And Gesomun learns this city here, from an old man reading one report three times by lamplight. Nobody else in the city would read it once.
blocks.ko: 셋 다 나라를 집에서 배운다. 의자는 아버지의 밥상머리에서 큰 가문들을 배운다. 춘추는 회의가 할아버지를 왕좌에서 걸어 내려보낸 그날에서 회의를 배운다. 그리고 개소문은 여기서 이 도시를 배운다. 등불 아래 같은 보고서를 세 번 읽는 늙은이에게서. 이 도시의 누구도 한 번 읽지 않을 보고서를.

en: …Kim Yushin.

blocks.html: That’s where the name comes from. Not from his own capital, which likes its titles stamped and filed. From the people he beat. Goguryeo calls him the Sword of Silla first, and means it as a warning. On the border, mothers use it to get children indoors before dark.
blocks.ko: 그 이름은 거기서 나왔다. 칭호에 도장 찍어 철해 두기 좋아하는 제 나라 도읍에서가 아니다. 그에게 진 사람들에게서다. 고구려가 먼저 그를 신라의 검이라 부른다. 경고의 뜻으로. 국경의 어머니들은 해 지기 전 아이들을 불러들일 때 그 이름을 쓴다.

blocks.html: Thirteen years later, Gesomun hears that sword is riding for the Silla envoy in his prison, and opens the cell. A few months after that, a laughing king says the name across a table. Gesomun’s cup stops an inch from his mouth. Now you know why.
blocks.ko: 십삼 년 뒤, 개소문은 그 검이 자기 감옥의 신라 사신을 구하러 온다는 소식을 듣고 옥문을 연다. 몇 달 뒤, 잘 웃는 왕 하나가 술상 너머로 그 이름을 입에 올린다. 개소문의 잔이 입 앞 한 치에서 멈춘다. 이제 왜인지 아실 것이다.

blocks.html: Thirteen years on, the banner captain has a queen, a title, and forty fortresses Baekje just took from her. He wants them back…!
blocks.ko: 십삼 년이 지나, 그 깃발 대장에게는 여왕과 칭호가 있다. 그리고 백제가 방금 그 여왕에게서 빼앗은 성 마흔 개. 그는 그걸 되찾고 싶다…!

logline.en: In Baekje’s markets they spit when they say his title. They add, quietly, that Gyebek hasn’t met him yet.
logline.ko: 백제 저잣거리에서는 그의 이름을 말할 때 침을 뱉는다. 그리고 조용히 덧붙인다. 계백은 아직 그를 만나지 않았다고.

Face matches the attached portrait only as a beard-and-scar sliver at the top edge. Confucian blue #2A5FB8 as the single accent on silk sleeve and a thin rim on the ring. Striking silky court-military, few hues. Flat charcoal void. No army. No palace clutter. No clouds. No second sword. No text. No watermark. Graphic color-blocking, anime-painterly. NOT photoreal. NOT busy.

FACE matches the attached Kim Yushin portrait; a sliver of grey steel lamellar and blue cloth at the collar. Pure black void, rain streaks catching light. One hard cold key from high right, carving the brow, cheek and wet beard; Confucian marshal blue #2A5FB8 as the specular on wet steel and his catchlight — real light, NOT a glow aura. Crushed blacks. Other cavalry are black brush silhouettes behind the trees. The horse is flat paper-white, the color of an unpainted horse, not shining, not emissive. Pine trunks are black strokes. High contrast. No text, no seal, no watermark.

images.at: The water at home still tastes

Between campaigns: Kim Yushin reaches from cyan water for his robe — webtoon cartoon, CLEAN-SHAVEN, wet loose hair, bare shoulders. Across the lake, painterly Narim, Golhwa, Hyullé watch him leave again (glowing eyes, colored chima). Setting matches attached cavern. No genitals. No text. No watermark.

images.at: Kim Yushin is the Greatest Blade of Samhan
images.alt: Donatello’s St George: Yushin square in the dark, sword point-down between his boots, both hands stacked on the ring
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. POSE: Donatello’s St George. Low worm’s-eye from the stone floor of a dark fortress gatehouse at night: Kim Yushin stands square in contrapposto, weight on one leg, head turned a little aside with a level stare, his ring-pommel sword point-down on the flagstone between his boots, both gauntleted hands stacked on the small ring. One narrow shaft from a high arrow-slit falls on him from the side and runs straight down the blade to the floor. Steel lamellar plates catch the key; blue cloth at the collar; the gatehouse arch dissolves into black. Encased in darkness: at least 80% of the frame is near-black umber void, the figures pulled out of it by one hard raking key. Old-master tenebrist canvas (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour oil brushwork, glazed umber-black darks, impasto on the brightest highlight, canvas grain; silk brushed in loaded strokes; only faces and hands keep clean webtoon ink line. The steel glistens: the key runs down every blade as one long white-hot streak with a tiny star-glint on the edge. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — KIM YUSHIN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_kim_yushin.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Tall, broad-shouldered, long black hair in a high topknot-ponytail with trailing Silla-blue cloth tails; level hard brows, deep-set eyes. Dress: Silla-blue po and trousers, plum-violet sash knotted at the waist, white inner collar, dark wrapped forearms. Off duty: plain blue po, no jewelry. Now: Marshal: full black beard and moustache; a blue ribbon in the topknot instead of the headband. Demeanor: Confucian: he STANDS — never sits in lotus. Weighs, counts, frowns at sums; tight jaw, rare dry half-smile. Grief shows as stillness, not tears. The most feared warrior in all of Samhan: a line goes quiet when the tall Silla helm and the white horse appear. Massive, deliberate, terrifying at a walk; by Hwangsan (65) heavier and slower than Gyebek but still the man armies are built around. Armor: Silla kit: steel lamellar cuirass and skirt, tall pointed jonghyeongju helm with a short plume. Battle armor: plates are METALLIC GRAY STEEL lamellar copied from the attached lamellar ref, cloth peeking at collar, sleeves, skirt, sash and plume-cord in the wearer's color only. Ignore labels and watermarks on armor refs. Not Japanese kabuto, not fantasy plate, not a gold-painted suit. Sword: Fish sword — Ring-pommel fish sword — Gaya fish on the pommel, Silla blue in the fuller. Pommel motif fish inside the small ring (name only; do not attach the pommel ECU). Carry: One fish-ring sword at the left hip. Never two blades. Fighting: Orthodox FORWARD one-hand grip, ring at the heel of the fist; square upright stance, short economical straight cuts and thrusts — the drill-yard form he teaches. Mounted, he cuts down from the saddle on the off side. #2A5FB8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: sitting in lotus or holding prayer beads; katana, tsuba or curved blade (ignore the sword drawn on his portrait); two swords at once; blue glow aura. | HANGYUL (한결, yushin's horse) — attached board /obj_hangyul.png: Pure white war horse, long flowing white mane, powerful galloping build — match the board. Eighteen years under Yushin since Nangbi; puts his nose into Yushin's chest and waits. | HORSE ANATOMY is a centrepiece: the whole horse body reads clearly and beautifully — arched neck, deep chest, sloping shoulder, round haunch, clean long legs in a correct gait, every muscle modelled by the one hard key with a bright edge along the topline and deep shadow under the belly; the horse is never cropped into a blob, never hidden behind dust, never stiff like a toy; mane and tail as flowing painted strokes; the coat colour exactly as the board. | Kingdom banners: copy field colour and emblem from the attached flag_*.png ref onto period silk war-banners — tall poles behind each side, long streamers, small pennants on spear-tips and saddle-backs. Painted silk, wind-whipped, torn and smoke-stained in battle; never a flat modern flag graphic. Each side's banner colour is the clearest colour on its half of the frame, so the kingdom reads at a glance. Silla banners: blue silk with a white crescent moon. Attached flag /flag_silla.png. | SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Baekje took forty Silla fortresses in one autumn. Silla’s answer reaches Sabi at breakfast.
blocks.ko: 백제는 한 가을에 신라 성 마흔 개를 빼앗았다. 신라의 대답은 아침상에 맞춰 사비에 닿는다.

en: I-i-it’s Kim Yushin!!
You’ve never heard of Kim Yushin…?

lines: 이 바보야 — 김유신이 삼한 최강의 칼이야…!
연개소문, 계백 장군 — 다 비키라고 해. 아니면 계백에게 그 칭호가 아직 다툼 중이라고 해. 웃지 않을 거다.
en: You fool — Kim Yushin is the Greatest Blade of Samhan…!
Yeon Gesomun, General Gyebek — tell them all to stand aside. Or tell Gyebek the title is still disputed. He will not laugh.

blocks.html: In Baekje’s markets they spit when they say his title. At home they toast it. Both sides add, quietly, that Gyebek hasn’t met him yet. Until he does, “greatest blade” is a tavern argument with two right answers.
blocks.ko: 백제 장터에선 그의 칭호를 말할 때 침을 뱉는다. 고향에선 축배를 든다. 양쪽 다 누군가 조용히 덧붙인다. 계백과는 아직 붙어 보지 않았다고. 붙기 전까지 ‘최강의 칼’은 정답이 둘인 주점 논쟁이다.

blocks.caption: Forty fortresses, along a border nobody could draw the same way twice.
blocks.ko: 두 번 같게 그릴 수 없는 국경을 따라, 마흔 개의 성.

blocks.html: What reached Sabi had started a week earlier, in Surabol.
blocks.ko: 사비에 닿은 그것은 한 주 전 서라벌에서 시작되었다.

blocks.label: The Moon Palace
blocks.ko: 월성

en: Forty, Yushin.
I’ll start with one, Majesty.
Which one?

lines: 저쪽 것으로요. 저들이 제일 안전하다고 여기는 것.
en: One of theirs. The one they think is safest.
And the forty?

lines: 백제는 이제 성 마흔을 지켜야 합니다, 폐하. 곳간 마흔. 겨울 마흔.
en: Baekje has forty forts to hold now, Majesty. Forty granaries. Forty winters.
Let them feed it.

lines: 조정에 우리가 그걸 내버려 둔다고 말하란 말인가?
en: You want me to tell the court we’re letting them keep it?
Tell the court I’m busy.
…That, they’ll believe.

blocks.label: The Gate
blocks.ko: 대문

blocks.html: He rides out that afternoon. The road runs past his own gate, and his household is lined up outside it, hoping. He does not turn his head. Fifty paces on he stops and sends a spearman back to the house for a cup of water.
blocks.ko: 그는 그날 오후 떠난다. 길은 제 집 대문 앞을 지나고, 집안 사람들이 혹시나 하고 대문 밖에 줄지어 서 있다. 그는 고개를 돌리지 않는다. 오십 걸음쯤 가서 말을 세우고, 창병 하나를 집으로 보내 물 한 잔을 떠 오게 한다.

lines: 우리 집 물은 아직도 옛 맛이 나는구나.
en: The water at home still tastes the way it used to.
He didn’t even look at the house.
…He drank the water, though.

blocks.html: Chunchu is waiting at the city gate, as if by accident.
blocks.ko: 춘추가 성문에서 기다리고 있다. 우연인 척.

lines: 자네 부인이 대문 앞에 서 있더군. 내가 봤네.
잠깐 들를 수도 있었잖나. 안에서 한 잔.
en: Your wife was at the gate. I saw her.
You could have stopped. One cup, inside.

lines: …멈추면, 멈춘 이유를 저들이 알아서 지어낼 테니.
en: …If I stopped, they would invent a reason for my stopping.

lines: 이유는 내가 지어 주지. 그건 내가 더 잘하네.
en: Then don’t stop.
I’ll invent the reasons for you. I’m better at it.

blocks.label: The River Fort
blocks.ko: 강가의 성

blocks.html: The fort sits on a bluff over a crossing, the kind of post a Baekje sentry gets sent to for a rest. Two of them are dicing by the brazier.
blocks.ko: 성은 나루 위 벼랑에 앉아 있다. 백제 보초가 쉬러 보내지는 그런 자리다. 둘이 화로 곁에서 주사위를 던지고 있다.

lines: 신라가 여기까진 안 와. 성 마흔 개 잃고 우느라 바쁠걸.
en: Silla won’t come this far. They’re busy crying over forty forts.
Throw.

blocks.html: The other one does not throw. He is looking at the ridge. There is a pale horse on it, standing very still, and then there isn’t.
blocks.ko: 다른 하나는 던지지 않는다. 능선을 보고 있다. 거기 흰 말 한 마리가 아주 가만히 서 있다. 그리고 없다.

blocks.html: An hour earlier, at the foot of the bluff, an officer had looked up at the rock and then at his general.
blocks.ko: 한 시진 전, 벼랑 밑에서 장교 하나가 바위를 올려다보다가 제 장군을 보았다.

en: Sir. Nobody climbs that side.
Then nobody is watching it.

blocks.html: They go up in their socks, swords tied flat to their backs so nothing rings on the stone. Yushin goes third. Not first, which would be vanity. Not last, which would be worse.
blocks.ko: 그들은 버선발로 오른다. 칼은 등에 납작하게 묶어 바위에 쇳소리가 나지 않게 한다. 유신은 세 번째로 오른다. 맨 앞은 허세다. 맨 뒤는 더 나쁘다.

blocks.html: Yushin’s men come up the bluff in the dark, where nobody climbs because nobody can. By the time the brazier is kicked over they are on the wall.
blocks.ko: 유신의 군사들은 어둠 속에서 벼랑을 오른다. 아무도 못 오르니 아무도 안 지키는 자리다. 화로가 걷어차일 무렵 그들은 이미 성벽 위에 있다.

en: K-… IT’S KIM YUSHIN!!

blocks.html: The defence breaks before it starts. In the storehouse a young Baekje officer is trying to fire the rice before Silla can eat it. His hands shake too much for the flint.
blocks.ko: 방어는 시작되기도 전에 무너진다. 곳간에서는 백제의 젊은 장교 하나가 신라가 먹기 전에 쌀에 불을 지르려 애쓰고 있다. 손이 너무 떨려 부싯돌이 안 맞는다.

lines: 내려놓게. 오늘 밤엔 아무도 아무것도 태우지 않네.
en: Put it down. Nobody burns anything tonight.
…You’re not going to kill me?
Go home. Tell them who sent you.
Who— who do I say it was?
They’ll know.

blocks.html: It is not one of the forty. It is one of Baekje’s own, and that is the message. He has never been in a hurry about anything except a charge.
blocks.ko: 마흔 중 하나가 아니다. 백제 제 성이다. 그게 전하는 말이다. 그는 돌격 말고는 무엇에도 서두른 적이 없다.

blocks.html: Autumn, ninth month. The queen made him Supreme General and sent him with troops against seven Baekje fortresses, Gahye, Seongyeol, Donghwa and the rest. He won a great victory and opened the Gahye crossing.
blocks.ko: 가을 9월, 왕이 그를 상장군으로 삼아 군사를 이끌고 백제의 가혜성·성열성·동화성 등 일곱 성을 치게 하니, 크게 이기고 이어 가혜 나루를 열었다.
blocks.hanja: 秋九月，王命為上將軍，使領兵伐百濟加兮城、省熱城、同火城等七城，大克之，因開加兮之津。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biographies — Kim Yushin I, Queen Seondeok yr. 13 (644)

blocks.label: Sabi
blocks.ko: 사비

blocks.html: The young officer comes home. He tells it the way he was told to.
blocks.ko: 젊은 장교가 돌아온다. 시킨 그대로 전한다.

en: He sent you home? With your sword on?

lines: 무장한 장교를 그냥 보냈답니다, 폐하. 신라가 물러졌습니다.
en: He let an officer walk out armed, Majesty. Silla’s gone soft.
Soft? He sent me a messenger with a sword on.
That’s a man saying, next time bring more.

lines: 자네 이름만 들어도 우리 애들이 밥을 안 먹어.
en: Yushin, my friend~~
My men stop eating at the sound of your name.
Gyebek. How many did he take?

lines: 하나입니다, 폐하. 우리 성 하나. 마흔 중엔 하나도 없습니다.
en: One, Majesty. One of ours. None of the forty.
…He isn’t taking them back.
He’s sending me the bill.
Could you beat him?
I have not met him.
Then go and meet him.
Not yet, Majesty.
He picked this field.

blocks.html: Euija laughs, because it is the most honest answer anyone has given him all morning.
blocks.ko: 의자가 웃는다. 오늘 아침 누구한테 들은 대답보다 정직했으니까.

blocks.html: One star over Samhan tonight. Three men are looking up at it, and every one of them wants to be the King for All…!
blocks.ko: 오늘 밤 삼한 위에 별 하나. 세 사내가 그 별을 올려다본다. 셋 다 “삼한왕검”이 되고 싶다…!

logline.en: He doesn’t ask forgiveness for the hall. He asks for witnesses.
logline.ko: 그는 그 연회장의 일로 용서를 빌지 않는다. 증인을 청한다.

blocks.html: There is a hill above Surabol where two boys once lay on their backs and argued about a star. Thirty years on, they climb it again.
blocks.ko: 서라벌 위에는 언덕이 하나 있다. 옛날 두 소년이 거기 드러누워 별 하나를 두고 다퉜다. 삼십 년 뒤, 둘이 다시 그 언덕을 오른다.

blocks.html: Yushin still has river-fort mud on his boots. Chunchu’s left hand is still in its sling. Neither of them mentions either.
blocks.ko: 유신의 장화엔 아직 강가 성의 진흙이 묻어 있다. 춘추의 왼손은 아직 천에 걸려 있다. 둘 다 그 얘기는 꺼내지 않는다.

blocks.html: Chunchu was nine that first night, and Yushin seventeen and already too serious for stars. They were both supposed to be at lessons.
blocks.ko: 그 첫날 밤 춘추는 아홉 살이었다. 유신은 열일곱, 별을 보기엔 이미 너무 진지했다. 둘 다 글방에 있어야 할 시간이었다.

en: You were supposed to be at lessons.
So were you, brother. You were supposed to be teaching them.
Well — is it enough now?
We have given Baekje a proper beating…
So then… do you mean to drag the King of Baekje back too?

lines: 그런데 뭔가 다른 것이 움직이고 있고, 그건 제가 움직이는 게 아닙니다.
en: Brother… the grudge is mine. I know that.
But something else is moving, and it is not me moving it.
Brother… I had little interest in any of it.
A wife I loved, a peaceful household.
I believed that much would be enough.
But the world—
Chunchu, what on earth are you saying…
The eastern star shines especially bright tonight…
Brother… let us go and take it now.
That old palace of ours…
the dream we had when we were young…
The “King for All”, I mean…!
…I told you. That one is a planet.
Thirty years and you are still saying that.

lines: 형님, 저는 그 자리를 원합니다. 여기서 한 번만 말하겠습니다. 별만 듣는 데서.
대야는 제가 없던 방이었습니다. 다시는 방 밖에 서 있지 않겠습니다.
en: I want the chair, brother. I’ll say it once, up here, where only the star can hear.
Daeya was a room I wasn’t in. I won’t stand outside the room again.
Then I will stand beside you.

blocks.html: He said that once before, on this hill, when he was seventeen and it cost nothing. It costs something now. He says it in exactly the same voice.
blocks.ko: 예전에 이 언덕에서 한 번 한 말이다. 열일곱이었고, 아무 값도 들지 않던 때였다. 지금은 값이 든다. 그는 꼭 같은 목소리로 말한다.

en: You don’t even like the chair.

lines: 좋아할 필요는 없네. 곁에 서 있기만 하면 되지.
en: I don’t have to like it. I have to stand next to it.

blocks.label: Sabi
blocks.ko: 사비

lines: 계백아. 너는 저 궁 안에서 자랐다.
의자 하나 잡겠다고 미쳐 가는 사내들을 숱하게 봤겠지.
왕관 쓴 노비도 있고, 서문 앞에서 빌어먹는 임금도 있다.
en: Gyebek. You grew up inside that palace.
You have watched men go mad reaching for a chair.
A man is one of two things — a king, or a slave.
There are slaves in crowns and kings begging at the west gate.
One request.
I will obey.

lines: 내가 언젠가 어리석은 명을 내릴 게다. 한 번이 아닐 게고.
왕관은 내가 쓴다. 그래도 네 삶의 임금은 너다…!
en: No. Do not follow me.
One day I will give you a stupid order. More than one.
Judge it yourself.
I wear the crown. You are still the king of your own life…!

lines: 폐하... 이 얘기를 저에게 왜 해 주시는 겁니까?
en: Your Majesty… why are you telling me this?

lines: 계백아… 사내는 더 큰 꿈을 품어야지.
en: Gyebek… a man should hold a larger dream.
The “King for All”, I mean…!

lines: 평양에서 개소문이 제게 말을 한 필 주겠다 했습니다.
약조를 했습니다. 스스로 판단하라 하셨지요. 판단했습니다.
en: Your Majesty.
In Pyongyang, Gesomun offered me a horse.
I gave my word. You said to judge for myself. I judged.

blocks.html: Euija opens his mouth to laugh, and for once does not. He looks at Gyebek a long moment. Then he pours two cups and pushes one across the table, which a king does not do.
blocks.ko: 의자는 웃으려고 입을 열다가, 웬일로 웃지 않는다. 한참 계백을 본다. 그러고는 잔 둘을 따라 하나를 상 건너로 밀어 준다. 왕은 그런 걸 하지 않는다.

blocks.html: Then he goes to the window with his own cup. The eastern star is very bright over the river tonight. He raises his cup to it, a little drunk, the way you toast a rival you have not met yet.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 제 잔을 들고 창가로 간다. 오늘 밤 강 위의 동쪽 별이 유난히 밝다. 그는 조금 취한 채 그 별에 잔을 든다. 아직 만나 보지 못한 맞수에게 건배하듯.

lines: 오늘 밤 너를 올려다보는 다른 놈들에게.
en: To whoever else is looking at you tonight.
May he trip on the stairs.

blocks.label: The Sacred Cave
blocks.ko: 수혈

blocks.html: The banquet hall has been scrubbed for three nights. Yeon climbs to a cave in the hill above the river. Nobody prays there lightly. The marches say the stone still remembers bowstrings.
blocks.ko: 연회장의 피를 씻어 낸 지 사흘 밤. 연은 강 위 언덕의 동굴로 오른다. 그곳에선 아무도 가볍게 빌지 않는다. 변방 사람들은 그 돌이 아직 활시위 소리를 기억한다고 믿는다.

blocks.html: Gesomun climbs with the five blades still on his back. They are heavy. He has decided they should be.
blocks.ko: 개소문은 다섯 자루 칼을 등에 멘 채 오른다. 무겁다. 무거워야 한다고 그는 정했다.

blocks.html: He kneels at the mouth and lays a crow-stamped ring-pommel on the stone. He does not ask forgiveness for the hall. He asks for witnesses.
blocks.ko: 그는 동굴 입구에 무릎을 꿇고, 삼족오가 찍힌 환두대도를 돌 위에 내려놓는다. 전각의 일로 용서를 구하지는 않는다. 증인을 구한다.

blocks.html: Dosuryu waits outside the cave mouth with the horses. He has never liked caves. He likes even less what men promise inside them.
blocks.ko: 도수류는 동굴 어귀 밖에서 말을 잡고 기다린다. 동굴은 예전부터 싫었다. 사내들이 그 안에서 하는 약속은 더 싫다.

blocks.html: East of the capital there is a great cave called the Sacred Tunnel. Every tenth month the king sacrifices there himself.
blocks.ko: 도성 동쪽에 큰 굴이 있으니 신수라 부른다. 해마다 10월이면 왕이 몸소 제사를 지낸다.
blocks.hanja: 國城東有大穴，名神隧，皆以十月，王自祭之。
blocks.source: Jiu Tangshu (舊唐書) bk. 199上, Eastern Barbarians — Goguryeo

en: The Holy King forged a country here.
I too… will forge one with my own hands.

lines: …평생을, 제가 무엇에 쓰일 것인지 모르고 살았습니다.
사람은 대개 태어나서, 얼마쯤 살다가, 죽습니다.
en: …All my life I did not know what I was for.
Most men are born, and live a while, and die.
Holy King, you gave me monsters.
Thank you for giving me a direction.

lines: 제 몸의 뼈가 다 부서질 때까지.
제 마음의 구슬이 다 금 갈 때까지.
en: Until every bone in me is broken.
Until every jewel in my heart is cracked through.
I will not let go of this.
The “King for All”, I mean…!
Done talking to your ancestors?
They don’t talk back.
That’s why I like them.
I talk back.

lines: 아오, 형님. 그래서 곁에 두는 거요.
en: I know, old man. That’s why I keep you.

blocks.html: Gesomun wants a country. Far to the west, the man who owns half the world is trying to pronounce his name…!
blocks.ko: 개소문은 나라를 원한다. 저 멀리 서쪽, 천하의 절반을 가진 사내가 그 이름을 입속으로 굴려 보는 중이다…!

toneNote: A short audience in Chang'an — silk over iron.
title: Epilogue

logline.en: Far to the west, a man who owns half the world hears a new name. He turns it over on his tongue, like a grape he hasn’t decided to eat.
logline.ko: 저 멀리 서쪽, 천하의 절반을 가진 사내가 새 이름 하나를 듣는다. 그는 삼킬지 말지 아직 정하지 않은 포도알처럼 그 이름을 혀 위에서 굴린다.

blocks.html: Far to the west, a man who owns half the world hears a new name. He turns it over on his tongue, like a grape he hasn’t decided to eat.
blocks.ko: 저 멀리 서쪽, 천하의 절반을 가진 사내가 새 이름 하나를 듣는다. 그는 삼킬지 말지 아직 정하지 않은 포도알처럼 그 이름을 혀 위에서 굴린다.

blocks.html: Half the world sends tribute here and calls it friendship.
blocks.ko: 세상의 절반이 조공을 바치고, 그걸 우정이라 부르는 곳.

blocks.html: The grapes are from Gaochang. Three summers ago it was a kingdom. Now it is a province with very good grapes.
blocks.ko: 포도는 고창에서 왔다. 세 해 전 여름만 해도 나라였다. 지금은 포도가 아주 좋은 고을이다.

en: From Yingzhou, Majesty. Urgent.

lines: 영주에서 오는 건 다 급보로다. 이리 다오.
en: Everything from Yingzhou is urgent. Give it here.

blocks.html: The courier has ridden from the far north-east with a report in a lacquered tube. The emperor reads it himself, which his ministers dread. He reads the name twice.
blocks.ko: 파발은 머나먼 동북에서 옻칠한 통에 보고서를 넣어 달려왔다. 황제가 그것을 몸소 읽는다. 신하들이 제일 두려워하는 일이다. 그는 그 이름을 두 번 읽는다.

blocks.html: On the dingsi day, Zhang Jian, Governor-General of Yingzhou, reported that Quan Gai Suwen*, Great Man of Goguryeo's Eastern Division, had murdered his king, Wu†.
blocks.ko: 정사일, 영주도독 장검이 아뢰기를, 고구려 동부 대인 천개소문*이 그 왕 무†를 시해하였다고 하였다.
blocks.hanja: 丁巳，營州都督張儉奏高麗東部大人泉蓋蘇文弒其王武。
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 196, Tang Taizong, Zhenguan 16 (642), 11th month

notes.html: Quan (泉) is Tang’s stand-in for Yeon (淵), a character it could not write. Gai Suwen is Gaesomun read in Chinese. Together: Yeon Gesomun.
notes.ko: 천(泉)은 당이 쓸 수 없던 연(淵) 대신 쓴 글자다. 곧 연개소문이다.

notes.html: Wu is Geonmu (建武), the king this book calls Yeongnyu.

blocks.html: In autumn, the ninth month, the great minister Iri Kasumi murdered the great king, and killed Iri Kosesi and others with him, more than a hundred and eighty men.
blocks.ko: 가을 9월, 대신 이리가수미가 대왕을 시해하고, 이리거세사 등 180여 명을 함께 죽였다.
blocks.hanja: 秋九月，大臣伊梨柯須彌弑大王，并殺伊梨渠世斯等百八十餘人。
blocks.source: Nihon Shoki (日本書紀) bk. 24, Empress Kōgyoku — yr. 1 (642), 2nd month, the Goguryeo envoys’ report

blocks.html: One character of that name nobody in this palace may write, because it belonged to the emperor’s late father. So a clerk wrote another one. The man in Pyongyang will be furious when he hears. That is a story for later.
blocks.ko: 그 이름의 한 글자는 이 궁에서 아무도 쓸 수 없다. 황제의 선친 이름자이기 때문이다. 그래서 서기가 다른 글자를 썼다. 평양의 그 사내가 들으면 노발대발할 것이다. 그건 나중 이야기다.

blocks.caption: The Second Emperor of Tang. He owns half the world, and he is curious about the other half.
blocks.ko: 당의 두 번째 황제. 세상의 절반을 가졌고, 나머지 절반이 궁금하다.

blocks.html: He has never lost a battle he led himself. He mentions this rarely, and only to people who already know.
blocks.ko: 그는 몸소 이끈 싸움에서 져 본 적이 없다. 그 얘기는 좀처럼 하지 않는다. 이미 아는 사람에게만 한다.

blocks.label: The Night Audience
blocks.ko: 밤의 알현

blocks.caption: The court diarist. He writes down everything the emperor says, which makes him the bravest man in the room.
blocks.ko: 궁중의 사관. 황제가 하는 말을 빠짐없이 적는다. 그래서 이 방에서 제일 용감한 사람이다.

lines: 제 임금을 죽이고 나라를 틀어쥐었다. 참으로 참을 수 없도다.
en: Gai… Suwen.
He murdered his lord and seized the government. It is truly not to be borne.

lines: 보고는 구월 자로 되어 있사옵니다, 폐하. 오는 데 여름이 꼬박 걸렸습니다.
en: The report is dated the ninth month, Majesty. It took the summer to arrive.

blocks.html: You may notice who is saying “not to be borne.” He did not get his own chair by waiting for it either. Nobody at this court mentions that. Nobody is allowed to.
blocks.ko: "참을 수 없다"고 말하는 이가 누구인지 눈치채셨을 것이다. 그도 제 자리를 얌전히 기다려서 얻은 사람은 아니다. 이 조정에서 아무도 그 얘기를 하지 않는다. 할 수가 없다.

lines: 오늘 가진 군사로 그곳을 취하기는 어렵지 않으리라.
허나 백성을 수고롭게 하고 싶지 않노라. 우선은 거란과 말갈을 시켜 그를 어지럽히라. 경은 어찌 보는가?
en: With what we have today, taking the place would not be hard.
But I do not wish to wear out the people. For now, let the Khitan and the Mohe harass him. What do you say?

lines: 거란은 지난봄에 비단을 받았사옵니다, 폐하. 그리고 말갈을 어지럽혔습니다.
폐하께서 누구에게 어찌 보느냐 물으신 것은 고창이 떨어진 그 봄이 마지막이었사옵니다. 날짜도 적어 두었습니다.
en: The Khitan were given silk last spring, Majesty. They harassed the Mohe.
The last time Majesty asked what anyone said was the spring Gaochang fell. I have the date.

lines: 짐이 모든 것을 취하고 나면, 짐에게 아니라 할 자가 하나도 남지 않으리라.
en: When I have taken everything, nobody will be left to tell me no.
…That was a joke.
It is noted, Majesty. As a joke.
Who else lives on that peninsula?

lines: 두 나라가 더 있사옵니다, 폐하. 셋 다 조공을 바치고, 셋 다 서로를 헐뜯사옵니다.
en: Two more kingdoms, Majesty. All three send tribute. All three complain about each other.
Silla sends the most letters.
Then Silla wants something.

lines: 신라는 늘 무언가를 원하옵니다, 폐하. 올해는 군사이옵니다.
en: Silla always wants something, Majesty. This year it is soldiers.

lines: 앞선 왕조가 그 나라에 네 번 갔사옵니다. 날짜도 있습니다.
en: The last dynasty went to that country four times. I have the dates.
The last dynasty was led by a fool.
…Who beat them at the river?

lines: 을지라는 신하였사옵니다, 폐하. 이 보고서의 사내는 그날 그 줄에 아비가 서 있었습니다.
en: A minister named Ulchi, Majesty. The man in this report had a father in the line that day.
It was a fine day, I am told. For them.

lines: 그렇다면 그 아들은 짐을 미워할 까닭이 있도다.
en: Then the son has a reason to hate us.
And we have a reason to hurry.

blocks.html: Before bed he does something he has not done in years. He asks for the old map of the north-east, the one the last dynasty drew, with the river crossings marked in dead men’s hands.
blocks.ko: 잠들기 전, 그는 몇 해 동안 안 하던 일을 한다. 동북의 옛 지도를 가져오라 한다. 앞선 왕조가 그린 것, 강 나루마다 죽은 자들의 손으로 표시가 된 지도다.

en: Where is the river?

lines: 저기이옵니다, 폐하. 먹이 제일 짙은 곳.
서기들이 그 선을 자꾸 고쳐 그렸사옵니다. 사람들이 자꾸 그 위에서 죽었으니까요.
en: There, Majesty. Where the ink is thickest.
The clerks kept redrawing the line. Men kept dying on it.

blocks.html: He puts his finger on the thick ink and leaves it there a while, the way you test whether a stove is still warm.
blocks.ko: 그는 짙은 먹 위에 손가락을 얹고 한참 둔다. 화로가 아직 따뜻한지 대 보듯이.

blocks.html: Down the hall a lamp still burns where his generals sleep when they are in the capital. He does not send for them. Not yet. A man who owns half the world can afford to sleep on a decision.
blocks.ko: 복도 끝, 장수들이 도읍에 머물 때 자는 방에 아직 등불이 켜져 있다. 그는 그들을 부르지 않는다. 아직은. 천하의 절반을 가진 사내는 결정을 하룻밤 묵힐 여유가 있다.

blocks.html: The grape bowl is empty. He did not notice eating them. The diarist did, and writes nothing down, which at this court is a kind of courage.
blocks.ko: 포도 그릇이 비었다. 그는 먹은 줄도 몰랐다. 사관은 알았고, 아무것도 적지 않는다. 이 조정에서 그건 일종의 용기다.

blocks.html: Half the world is asleep when he goes to bed. The name is still on his tongue. He hasn’t decided to eat it yet.
blocks.ko: 그가 잠자리에 들 때 천하의 절반은 이미 자고 있다. 그 이름은 아직 혀 위에 있다. 삼킬지는 아직 정하지 않았다.

blocks.html: He has his excuse. What he doesn’t have yet is a war worth leading himself. For that he’ll need four dragons…!
blocks.ko: 구실은 생겼다. 아직 없는 건 몸소 이끌 만한 전쟁이다. 그러려면 용 네 마리가 필요하다…!

toneNote: Iliad-scale: catalogues of hosts, epithets for heroes, gods watching from the walls.
title: The Seventh Invasion

logline.en: The Heaven-Sent General. The Khan of Heaven. He has many names, and he is running out of countries.
logline.ko: 하늘이 내린 장군. 하늘의 칸. 이름은 많고, 접어 넣을 나라는 거의 다 떨어졌다.
