images.alt: Ink-painted poster: the gold dragon coils out of black storm ink around the Second Emperor on the Hanyuan terrace, his hand resting on its snout
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; heads and the dragon’s head stay inside the central band; no title, no lettering. Night on the top terrace of the Hanyuan Hall at the Daming Palace, the palace roofs below dissolving into black ink. Low angle. TWO SUBJECTS: a human-scale emperor AND a huge dragon. INTERACTION: the gold Tang dragon Huanglong (gold ink-brush dragon from the attached board, three claws) pours out of a black ink storm in one great S around and behind the Second Emperor and lowers its huge head right beside him, jaws closed, whiskers drifting like brush strokes; the emperor stands at the balustrade scowling toward the east, one hand resting flat on the dragon’s snout. One lamp-fire key (#c97a2e) from below catches his gold thread, his beard and the dragon’s jaw; everything else is ink-black. TANG RENDER: predominantly DARK and INTIMIDATING Chinese ink painting (shuimohua) on rice paper — heavy black and grey ink washes, wet-on-wet ink bleeding, splashed ink smoke and storm, dry calligraphic brush strokes for roofs, columns, robes and cloud, ink splatters and drips at the frame edges, bare paper only where the edges dissolve; the gold ink-brush dragon is the main colour in the dark, with a few small vermilion and flame accents. THE ONE EXCEPTION: the Second Emperor himself is a full-colour Korean webtoon figure — clean ink linework, drawn face matching the attached portrait, warm skin, imperial yellow robe-cape over black brocade, black futou — a coloured man inside an ink empire; nothing else in the frame is in full colour. Movie-poster key art: bold iconic silhouette, big dark masses, one bright break of light, NO text, NO title, NO credits, NO logo, NO seal stamp, no calligraphy characters. Not photoreal, not 3D, not a realistic scaled dragon. No glow aura, no halo — the accent is real light. One of each named person. No watermark. CANON — THE SECOND EMPEROR — FACE and garments from attached /ch_taizong.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Bearded Tang emperor: black futou cap with an upright pin, thick black beard and moustache, fierce scowl. Dress: Imperial yellow robe-cape over black brocade. Demeanor: Commands; never asks. Conqueror's contempt that curdles at Ansi. Presence: THE SON OF HEAVEN — every frame he is in bends around him. He is SHROUDED IN DARKNESS: the black of the hall gathers around him like a mantle. One close practical light (a lamp, a brazier, a lamp-tree) rakes across him from below or from the side and SCULPTS him — the heavy yellow silk breaks into deep protruding folds brushed in loaded oil strokes that follow each fold, gold thread flicked in with impasto, the beard and cheekbones carved — and then falls off into black across his body and half his face; that falloff is the darkness, never a flat backlit silhouette. The camera sits BELOW his eyeline (low angle or worm’s-eye) and he is always placed HIGHER than anyone near him — on the dais, on a step, standing while others kneel or sit. He reads larger than life through lens and staging, not as a giant: broad shoulders, the robe spreading wide and heavy into the dark like a mountain, his shadow enormous on walls and floor. Unhurried, heavy stillness — never fidgeting, never casual, never a colleague at someone’s shoulder; when he smiles or laughs it is a predator’s ease, and the room goes quiet around it. Everyone else in frame is smaller, lower, less lit, turned toward him. The aura is darkness, scale and the hush around him — never a glow, never a halo, never rays behind his head. #c97a2e as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: Korean ring-pommel sword; Korean lamellar. | HUANGLONG (황룡, taizong's yellow dragon, guardian of the Tang throne) — attached board /obj_yellow_dragon.png: TANG-DYNASTY dragon painted in gold ink-brush: lean long-necked serpentine body in an S-curve, four lean leonine legs striding, THREE claws on each foot, long open-jawed snout with fangs, two backswept horns, whiskers and mane flung out as dry calligraphic gold brush strokes, whip tail ending in a flame tuft; burnished gold-yellow scales with ochre-umber shading — match the board, not a later Ming/Qing five-claw dragon, never a realistic scaled 3D dragon. Divine render: numinous through scale and atmosphere, coiling through black ink cloud and lamp smoke; light catches the scales as real light, never a glow outline. Its stills are predominantly dark and intimidating Chinese ink painting: splashed black ink, smoke, the gold dragon the main colour in the dark; every figure is ink-painted except the Second Emperor, who stays a full-colour webtoon figure. Owned by no one but sits behind whoever holds the dais; it coils over Chang'an and turns its head only for the Son of Heaven. | PLACE Chang’an (장안) — attached board /pl_daming_night.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Tang palace of Chang'an, drawn from the Daming Palace (大明宮) site and reconstruction models: Hanyuan Hall's concave ensemble — an eleven-bay hall with a double-eaved hipped roof of dark grey tiles and curled owl-tail ridge ends (chiwei), red columns, white plaster walls, lattice windows, raised on three tiers of rammed-earth terraces faced in ochre-red plaster and edged with white stone balustrades; the Dragon Tail Way ramps folding up the terraces; forward on each side the Xiangluan and Qifeng que-towers (three stepped pavilions on tall battered grey-brick piers) joined to the hall by long roofed corridors; a vast paved square below, entered through the five-doored Danfeng Gate. Wide low Tang proportions, deep eaves on massive bracket sets. Tang palette is VERMILION and WHITE (red columns, white walls); roofs are black-grey tile trimmed with green-glazed ridge and eave tiles (a little yellow and blue tricolour glaze); balustrade posts painted red, blue and green. YELLOW belongs to the emperor's robe; gold is gilt-bronze fittings, lamp-trees and firelight on vermilion. Interiors: dark polished stone floors, rows of vermilion columns, gauze hangings, a raised dais with a painted screen behind the throne. Never the Forbidden City, never all-yellow glazed roofs, never the modern reconstruction or a city skyline. Mood: TANG RENDER: predominantly DARK and INTIMIDATING Chinese ink painting (shuimohua) — black and grey ink washes, wet-on-wet ink bleeding into rice paper, dry calligraphic brush for roofs, columns, smoke and robes, the vermilion and gold reduced to small accents in a world of ink; officials, guards and other Tang figures are ink figures too. The ONE exception is the Second Emperor himself: he keeps the house webtoon figure render in full colour (yellow robe, black futou, drawn face), a coloured man inside an ink empire. Staged like a Chinese historical drama (Legend of the Demon Cat, The Longest Day in Chang'an) but lit as full Heewon tenebrism: night or blue hour; ONE dominant hard key per shot — a backlight through open doors or lattice, or one lamp-tree — and 75% of the frame crushed black with no fill; colour contrast — gold-yellow flame highlights against cool blue-green in the few lit shadows; the other flames (lamp-trees, silk lanterns with no writing, braziers) are small points and round bokeh IN the black, never lighting the room evenly; red lantern light through lattice as one pattern on the floor; incense haze only inside the key shaft; polished dark floors reflecting the flames. Staged like a drama, at true human scale: camera at eye or knee height on a dolly or crane; court officials in two lines facing inward along the central aisle with tablets; banquet tables in two long facing rows with dancers in the centre and the emperor on the dais at the head; exteriors are real-scale terraces and corridors, the hall large but never a fantasy fortress. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. blocks.html: In Chang’an there is one word nobody says. It is the emperor’s name.
blocks.ko: 장안에는 아무도 입에 올리지 않는 말이 하나 있다. 황제의 이름이다.

blocks.html: He never quite forbids it. The two characters of his given name simply vanish from the empire, quietly: a ministry renamed because one of them sat in its title, a bodhisattva’s name shortened by a syllable, scribes copying old books leaving one stroke off — and everyone understands.
blocks.ko: 그가 금하는 일은 끝내 없다. 다만 그의 이름 두 글자가 제국에서 조용히 치워질 뿐이다. 부(部)의 이름에 한 글자가 들어 있다는 이유로 부의 이름이 바뀌고, 보살의 이름은 한 음절이 짧아지고, 옛 책을 베끼는 서리들은 그저 획 하나를 빼놓는다 — 그리고 모두가 알아듣는다.

blocks.html: He has plenty of other names, and those you may say all day. The Heaven-Sent General. The Khan of Heaven.
blocks.ko: 다른 이름은 많다. 그건 하루 종일 불러도 된다. 하늘이 보낸 장군. 하늘의 칸.

blocks.html: Tell that to a herald from Samhan. Watch his face.
blocks.ko: 삼한에서 온 전령에게 이 말을 해 보라. 얼굴이 볼만하다.

en: …They don’t say his name? At all?
Nor written, sir. We leave off a stroke.
It saves everyone a great deal of trouble.

blocks.html: So the Second Emperor of the West is a man who has not heard another person say his own name since he was crowned, and there is nobody left alive who is allowed to.
blocks.ko: 그리하여 서토의 황제는, 즉위한 뒤로 다른 사람이 제 이름을 부르는 것을 들어 본 적 없는 사내다. 그리고 그럴 수 있도록 허락된 사람은 이제 살아 있지 않다.

blocks.html: The Imperial Minister is dying. At the foot of the bed the court diarist, Chu Suiliang, writes down everything the emperor says.
blocks.ko: 황제의 대신이 죽어 가고 있다. 침상 발치에서는 기거주를 맡은 저수량이 황제의 말을 하나도 빠짐없이 받아 적는다.

blocks.caption: The emperor’s minister. His job is to say no, and he is very good at his job.
blocks.ko: 황제의 대신. 그의 일은 ‘아니 되옵니다’라고 말하는 것이고, 그는 일을 아주 잘한다.

lines: 폐하. 신이 죽으면, 폐하께 «아니되옵니다»라고 말할 사람이 없습니다.
en: Your Majesty. When I am gone, there will be no one left to tell you no.

zhLatn: Bìxià. Chén sǐ zhī hòu, zài wú rén gǎn duì Bìxià yán “bùkě” yǐ.

en: Why else do you think I put up with you for twenty years.
zh: 不然朕何苦容忍你二十年。
zhLatn: Bùrán zhèn hékǔ róngrěn nǐ èrshí nián.

lines: 구리로 거울을 삼으면 의관을 바로 하고,
en: With bronze for a mirror, a man straightens his robes.
With history for a mirror, he sees the rise and fall of states.
With a man for a mirror, he sees his own faults.
…Today I lose one of my mirrors.
zhLatn: Yǐ tóng wéi jìng, kěyǐ zhèng yīguān;
Yǐ gǔ wéi jìng, kěyǐ zhī xīngtì;
Yǐ rén wéi jìng, kěyǐ míng déshī.
…Zhèn jīnrì shī yī jìng yǐ.

blocks.html: All that month the eastern reports keep coming in. In Goryeo, a king has been murdered by his own minister.
blocks.ko: 그달 내내 동방의 보고가 올라온다. 고려에서 왕이 제 신하 손에 죽었다고 한다.

lines: 그 이름을 한 달째 혀끝에서 굴리고 있노라. 굴릴수록 달아지지 않는구나.
en: Gai Suwen.
I have been turning that name over for a month. It does not get any sweeter.

blocks.html: Chang’an writes the name without the Yeon. Yeon was the given name of the emperor’s late father, so the word is gone from the palace. A whole family loses its surname to a dead man’s dignity. It is an old family, too. Older than Goguryeo, if you ask them. They will tell you anyway.
blocks.ko: 장안은 그 이름을 ‘연’ 자 없이 적는다. 연은 황제 선친의 이름자라, 궁에서 그 글자는 사라졌다. 한 집안이 죽은 사람의 체면 때문에 성을 잃는다. 게다가 오래된 집안이다. 물어보면 고구려보다 오래됐다고 한다. 안 물어봐도 말해 준다.
blocks.art: One panel: Yeon Tabal in his hall in Jolbon, looking down at the soaked Jumong on his knees (callback to the Jumong side story).

en: The King of Goryeo was a friend I valued.
His name… ah…
…Yeongnyu! King Yeongnyu!
zhLatn: Gāolí wáng shì zhèn suǒ zhòng zhī yǒu.
Qí míng… ā…
…Róngliú! Róngliú Wáng!

blocks.html: Everything is in place. It has been for some time; he was simply waiting to be bored enough.
blocks.ko: 판은 다 짜였다. 사실 진작에 짜여 있었고, 그는 다만 충분히 지루해지기를 기다렸을 뿐이다.

lines: 폐하, 벌써 여섯 번이나 쳐들어갔습니다. 또 가자는 말씀이십니까?
en: Majesty, we have invaded six times already — and you would go again?
zh: 陛下，已征六次——還要再去？
zhLatn: Bìxià, yǐ zhēng liù cì——hái yào zài qù?

en: Because I have not gone myself.
Life is not theory. It is practice.
zhLatn: Yīnwèi zhèn shàngwèi qīnzhēng.
Rénshēng fēi lǐlùn, nǎi shíjiàn.

blocks.label: The Third Leg
blocks.ko: 세 번째 다리

blocks.html: In the third month an envoy arrives from Pyongyang with a request nobody in the Ministry of Rites has seen before. The new master of Goguryeo would like some Daoists.
blocks.ko: 삼월, 평양에서 사신이 온다. 예부의 누구도 본 적 없는 청을 들고. 고구려의 새 주인이 도사를 좀 보내 달라는 것이다.

blocks.speaker: Goguryeo envoy
lines: 막리지께서 이르시길, 솥은 다리 셋으로 선다 하셨습니다.
천자께서 하나 내어 주실 수 있다면, 셋째 다리를 청하신답니다.
en: The Mangniji says a cauldron stands on three legs.
We have the Buddha. We have Confucius.
He would like the third leg, if the Son of Heaven can spare one.
zh: 莫離支言：三教譬如鼎足，闕一不可。
zhLatn: Mòlízhī yán: sān jiào pìrú dǐng zú, quē yī bù kě.
Jīn yǒu fó, yǒu rú.
Wéi quē dàojiào, qǐ tiānzǐ cì zhī.

lines: 줘라. 어차피 우리 집안이 그 노인네 후손이다. 고구려가 짐의 조상한테 절하면서 그걸 도라고 부르게 두어라.
en: He wants Laozi?
Give him Laozi. Our house descends from the old man anyway. Let Goguryeo bow to my ancestor and call it theology.
zh: 給他老子。朕家本是老君之後。讓高麗拜朕的祖宗，還叫它作道。
zhLatn: Tā yào Lǎozǐ?
Gěi tā Lǎozǐ. Zhèn jiā běn shì Lǎojūn zhī hòu. Ràng Gāolí bài zhèn de zǔzōng, hái jiào tā zuò dào.

blocks.html: Eight Daoists go east with a copy of the Daodejing. In Pyongyang the Mangniji gives them lodgings, and the lodgings he gives them are temples. The monks are moved out the same week, with their bells.
blocks.ko: 도사 여덟이 도덕경 한 질을 들고 동쪽으로 간다. 평양에서 막리지는 그들에게 숙소를 내주는데, 내준 숙소가 절이다. 같은 주에 승려들이 쫓겨난다. 종까지 들려서.

blocks.html: A young monk named Shinsung carries the smallest bell down the hill himself, to a lesser house that has no frame to hang it from, and sets it on the floor. He does not complain to anyone. The bell stays on the floor for twenty-five years.
blocks.ko: 신성이라는 젊은 승려가 제일 작은 종을 손수 지고 언덕을 내려가, 종 걸 틀도 없는 작은 절에 바닥에 내려놓는다. 아무에게도 불평하지 않는다. 종은 이십오 년 동안 바닥에 놓여 있다.

blocks.html: All conditioned things are impermanent; this is the law of arising and passing away. … When arising and passing away have themselves passed away, that stillness is bliss.
blocks.ko: 모든 지어진 것은 덧없으니, 이것이 나고 사라지는 법이다. …… 나고 사라짐이 다 사라지고 나면, 고요히 사라짐이 즐거움이 된다.
blocks.hanja: 「諸行無常，是生滅法。」……「生滅滅已，寂滅為樂。」
blocks.source: Nirvana Sutra (大般涅槃經) fasc. 14, Noble Practice (聖行品), tr. Dharmakṣema · T12n0374, pp. 450a, 451a · Sanskrit: the same verse in the Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra (Waldschmidt ed.)
blocks.native: अनित्या बत संस्कारा उत्पादव्ययधर्मिणः । उत्पद्य हि निरुध्यन्ते तेषां व्युपशमः सुखम् ॥
blocks.nativeLatn: anityā bata saṃskārā utpādavyayadharmiṇaḥ | utpadya hi nirudhyante teṣāṃ vyupaśamaḥ sukham ||

blocks.label: Three Choices
blocks.ko: 세 가지 안

blocks.html: In the ninth month an envoy comes from Silla, which is losing fortresses to Baekje faster than it can count them, and asks for an army. The Second Emperor offers him a choice of three.
blocks.ko: 구월, 신라에서 사신이 온다. 백제에게 성을 세는 것보다 빨리 잃고 있는 나라다. 군대를 청한다. 황제는 세 가지 중에 고르라 한다.

lines: 하나. 거란과 말갈을 요동에 풀어, 고구려가 한 해 동안 북쪽만 보게 하겠다.
둘. 붉은 군복 몇천 벌과 당의 깃발을 주겠다. 성벽에 세워 두어라. 백제가 보면 짐이 온 줄 알고 달아날 게다.
en: One. I send the Khitan and the Mohe into Liaodong, and Goguryeo looks north for a year.
Two. I give you a few thousand red coats and Tang banners. Stand them on your walls. Baekje will think I have come, and run.
Three.
zh: 其一，朕發契丹、靺鞨直入遼東，使高麗北顧一年。
其二，朕給爾絳袍丹幟數千，立於城上，百濟見之，以為朕至，必走。
zhLatn: Qí yī, zhèn fā Qìdān, Mòhé zhí rù Liáodōng, shǐ Gāolí běi gù yì nián.
Qí èr, zhèn gěi ěr jiàngpáo dānzhì shù qiān, lì yú chéng shàng, Bǎijì jiàn zhī, yǐwéi zhèn zhì, bì zǒu.
Qí sān.

lines: 너희 나라는 여인이 다스린다. 이웃들이 업신여기는 게 그 때문이다. 그래서 자꾸 쳐들어오는 거고.
짐의 종친 하나를 너희 왕으로 보내 주마. 지킬 병사 몇과 함께. 나라가 편안해지면, 그때 돌려받아라.
en: Your country is ruled by a woman, and your neighbours despise you for it. That is why they keep coming.
I could send you one of my own clan to be your king, with a few soldiers to look after him. When the country is safe, you may have it back.
zh: 爾國以婦人為主，為鄰國所輕，故寇不息。
朕遣一宗支，與為爾國主，自將兵以衛之，待爾國安，任爾自守。
zhLatn: Ěr guó yǐ fùrén wéi zhǔ, wéi línguó suǒ qīng, gù kòu bù xī.
Zhèn qiǎn yì zōngzhī, yǔ wéi ěr guó zhǔ, zì jiāng bīng yǐ wèi zhī, dài ěr guó ān, rèn ěr zì shǒu.

blocks.html: The envoy says yes, and then no, and then nothing at all. The emperor watches him for a while.
blocks.ko: 사신은 예, 했다가, 아니, 했다가, 끝내 아무 말도 못 한다. 황제는 한동안 그를 지켜본다.

lines: 용렬한 자로구나. 물에 빠진 나라가 보낼 위인은 아니다.
en: A mediocre man. Not the sort a country sends when it is drowning.
zh: 庸鄙之人，非乞師告急之才也。
zhLatn: Yōngbǐ zhī rén, fēi qǐ shī gàojí zhī cái yě.

blocks.html: The report reaches Surabol in the twelfth month. The Harmony Council has the third option read aloud twice. Bidam reads it once, and folds it small.
blocks.ko: 보고는 섣달에 서라벌에 닿는다. 화백회의는 세 번째 안을 두 번 소리 내어 읽게 한다. 비담은 한 번 읽고, 작게 접는다.

lines: 떠돌이 개한테 절밥 내놓듯이 왕을 내주겠다는군.
…그런데 이 방엔 그 밥그릇에 절할 사람도 있지.
en: He offers us a king the way a temple puts out rice for a stray.
…And there are men in this hall who would bow for the bowl.

blocks.label: Five Hundred Li
blocks.ko: 오백 리

blocks.html: In the new year the emperor sends a man to Pyongyang to tell Goguryeo to leave Silla alone. Gesomun receives him standing up, and does not offer a mat.
blocks.ko: 새해가 되자 황제는 평양에 사람을 보내, 신라를 그만 건드리라고 이른다. 개소문은 선 채로 그를 맞는다. 자리도 내주지 않는다.

blocks.speaker: Tang envoy
lines: 천자께서 고구려더러 신라를 그만 괴롭히라 하셨소.
en: The Son of Heaven asks that Goguryeo stop troubling Silla.
They are his vassals. As you are.

lines: 수나라 놈들이 우리 가슴팍에 올라타 있을 때, 신라가 슬그머니 기어들어 와서 우리 땅 오백 리를 집어갔소.
en: Vassals. Ha!
When the Sui were sitting on our chest, Silla crept in and took five hundred li of our land.
Give back the dirt. Then talk to me about peace.

blocks.speaker: Tang envoy
lines: 다 지난 일이오. 묵은 일로 다툴 게 뭐 있소?
en: That was long ago. Why quarrel over old things?

lines: 흙이야. 흙은 안 묵어, 이 양반아.
en: Old?
It’s dirt. Dirt doesn’t get old, you fool.
Go tell him that. Use small words.

blocks.html: The envoy carries it west word for word. The Second Emperor has it read to him twice and smiles. A refusal in writing is worth an army. Now he can raise one.
blocks.ko: 사신은 그 말을 한 자도 빼지 않고 서쪽으로 가져간다. 황제는 두 번 읽게 하고 웃는다. 글로 받은 거절은 군대 하나만큼 값어치가 있다. 이제 군대를 일으킬 수 있다.

blocks.label: The Muster
blocks.ko: 출정

blocks.html: He launches the Seventh Invasion of Goguryeo. It’s the seventh army out of the West, and the first he leads himself. The clerks need three days to read the muster aloud. Horse from the frontier. Foot from the rivers. Five hundred hulls riding low with a year of grain.
blocks.ko: 그는 고구려 일곱 번째 침공을 일으킨다. 서쪽에서 온 일곱 번째 군대이고, 그가 직접 이끄는 첫 군대다. 서기들이 소집 명부를 소리 내어 읽는 데만 사흘이 걸린다. 변방의 기병. 강가 고을의 보병. 한 해 치 곡식을 싣고 낮게 뜬 배 오백 척.

blocks.title: Handwritten edict to the realm
blocks.hanja: 高麗蓋蘇文弒主虐民，情何可忍！今欲巡幸幽、薊，問罪遼、碣，所過營頓，無為勞費。……昔隋煬帝殘暴其下，高麗王仁愛其民，以思亂之軍擊安和之眾，故不能成功。今略言必勝之道有五：一曰以大擊小，二曰以順討逆，三曰以治乘亂，四曰以逸敵勞，五曰以悅當怨，何憂不克！佈告元元，勿為疑懼！
blocks.html: Gesomun of Goguryeo has murdered his lord and savages his people. Who could bear it? We mean to ride out to You and Ji and call Liao and Jie to account. Wherever We camp or halt, let nothing be wasted and no one be burdened. … Emperor Yang of Sui was cruel to those beneath him, and the king of Goguryeo was kind to his people. An army that longed for revolt struck a people at peace, and so it failed. Now, in short, there are five ways We are certain to win. One: the great strikes the small. Two: the loyal punishes the rebel. Three: order rides down disorder. Four: the rested meets the weary. Five: the glad meets the bitter. Why fear we will not prevail? Tell it to all the people. Let no one doubt, and no one be afraid.
blocks.ko: 고구려의 개소문이 임금을 죽이고 백성을 학대하니, 어찌 참을 수 있으랴! 이제 유주와 계주로 나아가 요동과 갈석에 죄를 묻고자 한다. 지나는 곳마다 진을 치고 머무는 데 헛된 수고와 비용이 없게 하라. …… 옛날 수 양제는 아랫사람에게 잔인하였고 고구려 왕은 백성을 아꼈다. 난을 꿈꾸는 군대로 편안하고 화목한 무리를 쳤으니 이기지 못한 것이다. 이제 반드시 이기는 길 다섯 가지를 대략 말한다. 첫째, 큰 것으로 작은 것을 친다. 둘째, 순리로 역적을 친다. 셋째, 다스려진 것으로 어지러운 것을 탄다. 넷째, 편안한 몸으로 지친 적을 맞는다. 다섯째, 기쁜 마음으로 원망하는 자를 상대한다. 어찌 이기지 못할까 걱정하랴! 백성에게 널리 알려 의심하거나 두려워하지 말게 하라!
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 197, Tang Taizong, Zhenguan 18 (644), eleventh month · cf. Samguk Sagi bk. 21 (以理乘亂)

blocks.html: Four dragon banners go up over the muster: white, red, blue and black.
blocks.ko: 소집 위로 용의 깃발 넷이 오른다. 흰 용, 붉은 용, 푸른 용, 검은 용.
blocks.art: Draw the Four Dragons table (next block) as these four banners over the muster, each general’s name sewn under his dragon; no table on the page.

blocks.caption: The Blue Dragon. The emperor’s most patient general, which is its own kind of danger.
blocks.ko: 청룡. 황제의 장수 가운데 가장 참을성이 많다. 그것도 일종의 위험이다.

blocks.html: The fifth banner has no name on it at all. Everyone knows whose it is.
blocks.ko: 다섯째 깃발에는 아예 이름이 없다. 그래도 그게 누구 것인지 모르는 사람은 없다.

blocks.title: The Seventh Invasion
blocks.caption: Three roads in and five hundred hulls. Goguryeo’s wall was built to stop one army at a time.
blocks.ko: 들어오는 길 셋, 배 오백 척. 고구려의 성벽은 한 번에 한 군대씩 막으라고 쌓은 것이다.

blocks.html: Two of the four dragons were born on the steppe. The Red Dragon keeps felt tents inside the capital walls and sleeps better in them. The White Dragon walked his whole tribe across the border as a boy. He has been proving it was worth it ever since. The Black Dragon is the empress’s brother. He argued against this war in council. He’s riding to it anyway.
blocks.ko: 네 마리 용 가운데 둘은 초원에서 났다. 적룡은 도성 성벽 안에 펠트 천막을 치고 거기서 더 잘 잔다. 백룡은 소년 시절 부족 전체를 이끌고 국경을 넘어왔다. 그 뒤로 그게 잘한 일이었음을 줄곧 증명하는 중이다. 흑룡은 황후의 오라비다. 조정에서 이 전쟁에 반대했다. 그래도 간다.

blocks.label: Longmen Field
blocks.ko: 용문

blocks.html: In a poor field at Longmen, a farmer named Xue Rengui is planning to rebury his ancestors. Millet, rammed earth, a hut that doesn’t pretend to be anything. He has the right soil for graves. He doesn’t yet know he has the wrong year for quiet.
blocks.ko: 용문의 척박한 밭에서 설인귀라는 농부가 조상의 무덤을 다시 쓰려 한다. 조밭, 다진 흙, 아무것도 아닌 척하지 않는 오두막. 무덤 쓸 흙은 제대로 골랐다. 조용히 살 해를 잘못 골랐다는 건 아직 모른다.

blocks.caption: A poor farmer with good soil for graves. His wife thinks he could do better.
blocks.ko: 무덤 쓰기 좋은 땅을 가진 가난한 농부. 아내는 그가 더 큰일을 할 사람이라고 본다.

blocks.html: The cloth on his back is plain yellow peasant hemp, the cheapest dye the village still sells, the colour of millet at the wrong hour. He hoes. His wife, Liu, keeps the hut door.
blocks.ko: 등에 걸친 것은 평범한 노란 농부의 삼베다. 마을이 아직 파는 가장 싼 물감, 잘못된 시각의 기장 빛. 그는 호미질한다. 아내 유씨가 흙집 문을 지킨다.

blocks.html: The Son of Heaven is calling up troops for Liaodong. The edict reaches villages that have never seen a palace, and wives who have never left the furrow.
blocks.ko: 천자가 요동으로 군사를 부른다. 조서는 궁을 본 적 없는 마을과, 이랑을 떠나 본 적 없는 아내들에게 닿는다.

blocks.html: The edict comes on red paper, pasted to the well-house wall at the height of a man’s eyes: SERVE THE EMPEROR. Under it, in smaller characters, the quota. It does not ask for him by name. It asks for one man from every household with the right number of hands, and any man with hands will do.
blocks.ko: 칙령은 붉은 종이로 온다. 우물가 담벼락, 사람 눈높이에 붙는다. 〈천자를 위해 봉사하라〉. 그 아래 작은 글씨로 할당량. 칙령은 그의 이름을 부르지 않는다. 손이 제대로 달린 사내를 집마다 하나씩 부를 뿐이고, 손만 있으면 누구라도 된다.

en: The mounds… they’re not done.
Not the dirt. The hands.
The edict — I heard it. I did.
zhLatn: Fén hái méi yuán.
Búshì quē tǔ. Shì quē shǒu.
Zhàoshū——tīngjiàn le. Tīngjiàn le.

blocks.caption: A farmer’s wife. The farmer has no idea what she has planned for him.
blocks.ko: 농부의 아내. 농부는 아내가 자기를 두고 무슨 계획을 세웠는지 전혀 모른다.

lines: 손 없다고 무덤이 기다려 주진 않아요.
당신은 호미가 아니라… 극을 들 사람이에요. 내가 아는 한.
en: Mounds don’t wait because a man is short of hands.
And the edict doesn’t wait either.
You’re not a hoe. You’re a ji. As far as I can tell.
zh: 你不是鋤。你是戟。就我看。
zhLatn: Quē shǒu, fén yě bù huì děng.
Zhàoshū gèng bù huì děng.
Nǐ búshì chú. Nǐ shì jǐ. Jiù wǒ kàn.

en: The ji is in the shed.
The yellow clothes are here.
Liu. If I go — this door.
zhLatn: Jǐ zài péng lǐ.
Huángyī zài zhèr.
Liǔshì. Wǒ ruò zǒu——zhè mén.

lines: 때를 만나야 빛이 나는 법이에요. 지금이 그 때면 — 가면 돼요.
en: I’ll shut the door.
Don’t you start worrying about doors.
Talent needs its hour. If this is the hour — then go.
zh: 才須遇時。若是此時——便去。
zhLatn: Mén wǒ guān.
Nǐ bié cāoxīn mén.
Cái xū yù shí. Ruò shì cǐ shí——biàn qù.

blocks.html: He goes. She is right, and a man who can lift a ji should not spend the invasion stacking earth for the dead.
blocks.ko: 그는 간다. 아내 말이 맞고, 극을 들 수 있는 사내가 침공의 해를 죽은 자 흙 쌓는 데 쓰면 안 된다.

en: …Ancestors. Wait a little longer.
Until I come back carrying this ji.
The yellow clothes — I’ll leave them here.
zhLatn: …Lièzǔ lièzōng. Zài shāo dài piànkè.
Zhízhì wǒ chí cǐ jǐ guīlái.
Huángyī——jiù liú zài zhèr.

blocks.html: He presents himself to general Zhang Shigui and signs his name under the Tang muster. The clerk writes Xue Rengui. The clerk does not look up. History will.
blocks.ko: 장군 장사귀 앞에 나가 당의 병적에 이름을 올린다. 서기는 설인귀라 적는다. 서기는 고개를 들지 않는다. 역사는 들 것이다.

blocks.html: Yodong has never opened its gates to the West. Not for the Sui. Not in three summers. Here come the dragons…!
blocks.ko: 요동성은 서쪽에 문을 열어 준 적이 없다. 수나라에게도. 세 번의 여름 내내. 이제 용들이 온다…!

logline.en: Goguryeo spent fourteen years building a wall. The Blue Dragon simply walks around it.
logline.ko: 고구려는 열네 해 동안 성벽을 쌓았다. 청룡은 그냥 돌아서 간다.

images.alt: the Guardian of Ansi curses the emperor from the wall — a butcher's name for history
images.prompt: Cinematic historical illustration of ansi court, Three Kingdoms of Samhan / Tang era (645), scene: Eastern Fortress, painterly digital art, dramatic natural light, rich period costume, no modern elements, no text, no watermark, --ar 3:2 --stylize 250

blocks.html: Every wall assumes the enemy will knock. Goguryeo has spent fourteen years building a wall of forts along the river. The Blue Dragon simply walks around it. He shows his banners on the middle road, then turns north in the night. By morning his horse are across an unwatched ford. The first fortress shuts its gates. It holds exactly as long as the gates do.
blocks.ko: 모든 성벽은 적이 문을 두드릴 거라고 믿는다. 고구려는 십사 년 동안 강을 따라 성의 벽을 쌓았다. 청룡은 그 벽을 그냥 돌아간다. 가운데 길에 깃발을 보여 주고, 밤에 북으로 꺾는다. 아침이 되자 그의 기병은 아무도 지키지 않던 여울을 건너 있다. 첫 성이 문을 닫는다. 딱 그 문이 버티는 만큼만 버틴다.

blocks.html: Envoys went to the Great Tang and said: “Goguryeo and Baekje trample on your servant’s country. We are attacked again and again, and have lost dozens of forts. The two countries have joined their armies and swear to take us, and they will march in force this ninth month. Our altars will not survive. We send this envoy to submit to the great country, and beg for a detachment to save us.”
blocks.ko: 사신을 대당에 보내 아뢰었다. “고구려와 백제가 신의 나라를 침범하여 여러 차례 공격을 받아 수십 성을 잃었습니다. 두 나라가 군사를 합쳐 기어이 빼앗으려 하며, 이번 9월에 크게 일어나려 합니다. 저희 나라의 사직은 반드시 온전하지 못할 것이니, 삼가 배신을 보내 대국에 목숨을 맡기오며, 군사 얼마를 빌려 구원해 주시기를 청합니다.”
blocks.hanja: 遣使大唐上言：「高句麗、百濟侵凌臣國，累遭攻襲數十城。兩國連兵，期之必取，將以今玆九月大擧。下國社稷必不獲全，謹遣陪臣歸命大國，願乞偏師，以存救援。」
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 5, Silla Annals — Queen Seondeok, yr. 12 (643), 9th month

blocks.html: The emperor said: “Gai Suwen murdered his lord, butchered his ministers and tortures his people. Now he defies Our edict and preys on his neighbours. He cannot go unpunished.”
blocks.ko: 황제가 말하였다. “개소문은 그 임금을 시해하고 대신들을 해쳤으며 백성을 잔혹하게 학대하였다. 이제 또 짐의 조명을 어기고 이웃 나라를 침략하니, 치지 않을 수 없다.”
blocks.hanja: 上曰：「蓋蘇文弒其君，賊其大臣，殘虐其民，今又違我詔命，侵暴鄰國，不可以不討。」
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 197, Tang Taizong, Zhenguan 18 (644)

blocks.html: Gai Suwen said to the envoy Xuanjiang: “Silla and I have hated each other a long time. When the Sui invaded us, Silla took its chance and seized five hundred li of our land, every walled town on it. Unless they give back what they took, I doubt the fighting can stop.”
blocks.ko: 개소문이 현장에게 말하였다. “우리와 신라는 원한이 쌓인 지 오래다. 지난날 수나라가 쳐들어왔을 때 신라가 그 틈을 타 우리 땅 오백 리를 빼앗아 성읍을 모두 차지하였다. 빼앗은 땅을 돌려주지 않는 한, 싸움은 그치지 않을 것이다.”
blocks.hanja: 蓋蘇文謂玄獎曰：「我與新羅怨隙已久。往者隋人入寇，新羅乘釁奪我地五百里，城邑皆據有之。自非歸我侵地，兵恐未能已。」
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 197, Tang Taizong, Zhenguan 18 (644)

blocks.caption: Banners on the middle road, horses at the northern ford. Goguryeo watched the banners.
blocks.ko: 깃발은 가운데 길에, 말은 북쪽 여울에. 고구려는 깃발을 보고 있었다.

blocks.html: The New Fortress doesn’t fall. The emperor’s cousin spends ten days under its walls and leaves with nothing. So the Blue Dragon posts a guard on it and turns south. The next fort lasts a little over ten days. Seven hundred men Yeon sent to hold it are taken in the gate. They ask to serve the emperor instead.
blocks.ko: 신성은 무너지지 않는다. 황제의 사촌이 열흘을 성 아래 머물다 빈손으로 물러난다. 그래서 청룡은 신성에 감시병을 남기고 남으로 돈다. 다음 성은 열흘 남짓 버틴다. 연이 지키라고 보낸 칠백 명이 성문에서 붙잡힌다. 그들은 대신 황제를 섬기겠다고 청한다.

lines: 짐을 위해 싸우면, 막리지가 처자식을 다 죽일 게다.
한 사람의 힘을 얻자고 한 집안을 없애는 짓은 짐이 차마 못 하겠다. 돌려보내거라.
en: Their homes are all in Gasi, I am told.
If they fight for Us, the Mangniji will kill every wife and child they have.
To gain one man’s arm by wiping out his house — that We cannot bring Ourselves to do. Send them home.
zh: 若為朕而戰，莫離支必盡殺其妻子。
得一人之力而滅一家，朕不忍也。遣之歸。
zhLatn: Tīngshuō tāmen jiā dōu zài Jiāshī.
Ruò wèi zhèn ér zhàn, Mòlízhī bì jìn shā qí qīzǐ.
Dé yī rén zhī lì ér miè yī jiā, zhèn bùrěn yě. Qiǎn zhī guī.

blocks.html: They go home with grain for the road. It is a kindness, and it is also arithmetic: seven hundred men who have seen the size of this army will describe it to Gasi better than any envoy could.
blocks.ko: 그들은 길양식까지 받아 집으로 돌아간다. 자비이기도 하고 셈이기도 하다. 이 군대의 크기를 제 눈으로 본 칠백 명은 어떤 사신보다도 그것을 가시성에 잘 전할 것이다.

blocks.html: Between the army and the walls lies the Liao marsh. Two hundred li of mud. A Sui host once went in up to the knee and came out as a song. The emperor’s engineer lays a road of earth across it as the column walks, wide enough for carts. The Blue Dragon is already under Yodong’s walls, waiting for him.
blocks.ko: 군대와 성벽 사이에 요하의 늪이 있다. 이백 리의 진흙. 수나라 대군이 무릎까지 빠져 들어갔다가 노래가 되어 나온 곳이다. 황제의 장인이 대열이 걷는 대로 그 위에 수레가 다닐 만한 흙길을 깐다. 청룡은 벌써 요동성 아래서 그를 기다린다.

blocks.speaker: Tang lookout
lines: 아니, 길이 둘이야. 북쪽하고 동쪽. 저건 순찰이 아니라 군대다.
en: Dust! North road—
No. Two roads. North and east. That’s not a patrol, that’s an army.

blocks.html: Goguryeo has sent forty thousand to break the siege. The emperor’s cousin has four thousand, and orders to dig in and wait. He charges instead. His line breaks. He climbs a rise, sees their ranks in a muddle, and goes back in.
blocks.ko: 고구려가 포위를 풀러 사만을 보냈다. 황제의 사촌에게는 사천과, 참호를 파고 기다리라는 명이 있다. 그는 대신 돌격한다. 줄이 무너진다. 그는 언덕에 올라 저쪽 대열이 엉망인 걸 보고, 다시 들어간다.

lines: …머리가 천이요, 명은 어겼다. 길게 꾸짖어야겠구나. 저녁을 든 뒤에.
en: He was told to wait for Us.
…A thousand heads, and he disobeyed. We shall have to scold him at length. After dinner.

blocks.html: When the last wagon is over the marsh, the emperor has the road torn up. Nobody goes home the way they came. He wants every man in the column to know it.
blocks.ko: 마지막 수레가 늪을 건너자 황제는 길을 걷어 내게 한다. 아무도 왔던 길로 돌아가지 못한다. 그는 대열의 모든 병사가 그걸 알기를 바란다.

blocks.html: Then Yodong itself, the Eastern Fortress. It held off the last dynasty for three summers and never opened. The Blue Dragon has already driven one sortie back through the gate when the emperor arrives. He rides to the moat with a sack of earth across his saddle and throws it in. His officers can’t be seen carrying less than him. They carry two. The army rings the walls a hundred deep and beats the drums until the ground answers.
blocks.ko: 그리고 요동, 동쪽의 성 그 자체. 지난 왕조를 세 번의 여름 동안 막아 내고 끝내 열리지 않은 성이다. 황제가 도착했을 때 청룡은 이미 한 번의 출격을 성문 안으로 밀어 넣은 뒤다. 황제는 안장에 흙 자루 하나를 얹고 해자 끝까지 달려가 그것을 던져 넣는다. 장수들은 황제보다 적게 나르는 모습을 보일 수 없다. 그래서 두 자루씩 나른다. 군대는 성을 백 겹으로 둘러싸고 땅이 대답할 때까지 북을 친다.

blocks.html: The gate the West keeps knocking on.
blocks.ko: 서쪽이 자꾸 두드리는 문.

blocks.label: The Shrine
blocks.ko: 사당

blocks.html: Inside the walls there is a shrine to the Holy King. Ask the town who he was and they say Jumong, as if that settles it. A coat of chain mail hangs in it, and a long sharp spear, and the town will tell you both came down from heaven. By the eighth day stones are coming over the parapet. The elders choose a girl from the town, wash her, paint her, dress her in red silk and a bride’s crown, and walk her up to the shrine to be given to the god.
blocks.ko: 성안에는 성왕의 사당이 있다. 성 사람들에게 그가 누구냐고 물으면 주몽이라고 한다. 그거면 다 설명된다는 듯이. 사당에는 쇠사슬 갑옷 한 벌과 날 선 긴 창이 걸려 있는데, 성 사람들은 둘 다 하늘에서 내려온 것이라고 말한다. 여드레째가 되자 성가퀴 너머로 돌이 날아든다. 어른들은 성안에서 처녀 하나를 골라 씻기고, 단장시키고, 붉은 비단과 신부의 관을 입혀, 신에게 바치러 사당으로 데려간다.

en: It’s… heavy. The dress.
…Tell my mum. Tell her I didn’t cry.
The Holy King… is smiling.
He has taken his bride! This city will stand whole!

blocks.html: They close the shrine door on her. The town sleeps better that night. She doesn’t.
blocks.ko: 그들은 아이를 들여보내고 사당 문을 닫는다. 그날 밤 성은 조금 편히 잔다. 아이는 못 잔다.

blocks.html: The Holy King isn’t consulted again. Towers roll up to the parapet. On the twelfth day a south wind rises. They fire the south-west tower, and the wind carries it into town.
blocks.ko: 성왕께 다시 묻는 사람은 없다. 공성탑이 성가퀴에 붙는다. 열이틀째 남풍이 인다. 그들이 서남쪽 망루에 불을 지르자 바람이 불길을 성안으로 실어 간다.

blocks.speaker: Yodong soldier
lines: 망루는 놔둬! 집, 집이야— 애들 집에서 끌어내!
en: Wind’s turned— it’s coming in!
Leave the tower! The houses— get the children out of the houses!

blocks.html: The fire takes the town street by street. The shrine is stone, so it is the last roof standing when the gate gives. A Tang squad kicks its door in, looking for gold.
blocks.ko: 불은 거리를 하나씩 삼킨다. 사당은 돌집이라, 성문이 무너질 때 서 있는 마지막 지붕이 된다. 당군 한 무리가 금붙이를 찾아 사당 문을 걷어찬다.

blocks.html: They find a girl in red silk sitting under the chain mail, holding the god’s spear the wrong way round.
blocks.ko: 그들이 찾은 건 쇠사슬 갑옷 아래 앉은 붉은 비단의 처녀 하나다. 신의 창을 거꾸로 쥐고 있다.

en: Don’t.
I’m married.

blocks.html: The soldiers laugh. Then the emperor’s horse is in the doorway, and nobody laughs.
blocks.ko: 병사들이 웃는다. 그러다 문간에 황제의 말이 들어서고, 아무도 웃지 않는다.

en: Whose bride is this?

lines: 저들 신의 신부랍니다, 폐하. 저 갑옷 주인이요.
en: Their god’s, Majesty. The one who owns the armour.

lines: 그렇다면 남의 아내는 취하지 않는다. 죽은 자의 아내라도.
그에게 두어라. 저들의 신이 그녀에게 무엇을 해 줄 수 있는지, 이 성이 보게 하라.
en: Then We do not take another man’s wife. Not even a dead man’s.
Leave her to him. Let the city see what its god can do for her.

blocks.html: When the fighting stops, the clerks count ten thousand dead, then lose interest and count the grain. The fortress a million men couldn’t open has lasted twelve days.
blocks.ko: 싸움이 그치자 서기들은 죽은 자를 만까지 세다가, 흥미를 잃고 곡식을 센다. 백만 대군이 열지 못한 성이 열이틀을 버텼다.

blocks.html: Veterans spit and say the real argument is still ahead, at Ansi.
blocks.ko: 늙은 병사들은 침을 뱉으며 말한다. 진짜 싸움은 아직이라고. 안시에서.

blocks.label: Below Ansi
blocks.ko: 안시성 아래

blocks.html: Then the Second Emperor rides on to look at Ansi, and the man who holds it comes out onto the wall to look back. Nobody on the Tang side ever writes down his name.
blocks.ko: 그러고 나서 황제는 안시를 보러 말을 몬다. 안시를 지키는 사내가 성벽 위로 나와 그를 마주 본다. 당 쪽의 누구도 끝내 그의 이름을 적지 않는다.

blocks.caption: The man who holds Ansi. The other side never learns his name, and he never offers it.
blocks.ko: 안시를 지키는 사람. 저쪽은 끝내 그의 이름을 모르고, 그도 알려 주지 않는다.

lines: 짐은 용서할 자의 이름은 알아 두는 편이다.
en: You. On the wall. Your name.
We like to know whom We are about to forgive.

lines: 듣자 하니 그쪽은 이름 불리는 거 질색이라며.
en: You will simply… have to call me the man on the wall.
I hear you don’t care for names anyway.

lines: 역사는 너를 기억하는 수고를 하지 않으리라. 역사는 짐이 쓰는 것이니.
en: A nameless man, then.
History will not trouble itself to remember you. We are the one writing it.

lines: 그쪽 뒤엔 이백 리 진흙에, 돌아갈 길도 없잖아. 난 성벽 하나랑 가을 한 철이 통째로 있고.
en: Write fast, then.
You’ve got two hundred li of mud behind you and no road home. I’ve got a wall and all autumn.

blocks.html: The emperor does not ask twice. Nobody has ever made him ask twice. He turns his horse and starts looking at the ground around Ansi the way a cook looks at a goose.
blocks.ko: 황제는 두 번 묻지 않는다. 누구도 그에게 두 번 묻게 만든 적이 없다. 그는 말머리를 돌리고, 요리사가 거위를 보듯 안시 주변의 땅을 살피기 시작한다.

blocks.label: The Rest of the Line
blocks.ko: 남은 성들

blocks.html: The rest of the line comes down like roof tiles. At White Cliff, Yeon’s riders break out and put a spear into the White Dragon’s waist. He has it bound and is back in the saddle by evening, laughing.
blocks.ko: 나머지 방어선은 기왓장처럼 무너져 내린다. 백암성에서는 연의 기병이 뛰쳐나와 백룡의 허리에 창을 꽂는다. 백룡은 상처를 동여매고 저녁이 되기 전에 다시 안장에 오른다. 웃으면서.

blocks.speaker: Lord of White Cliff
lines: 저놈 다시 말에 올랐어. 구멍 난 채로.
…성문 열어라. 창 맞고 웃는 놈하고는 못 싸운다.
en: He’s back on his horse. With a hole in him.
…Open the gate. I’m not fighting a man who laughs at spears.

blocks.html: Of all the forts Yeon spent fourteen years hauling stone for, two still fly Goguryeo’s banners. One of them is Ansi.
blocks.ko: 연이 십사 년 동안 돌을 날라 쌓은 성들 가운데, 아직 고구려 깃발을 단 곳은 둘뿐이다. 그중 하나가 안시다.

blocks.title: The rest of the line
blocks.caption: A spear in the White Dragon, a fleet on the cape. The tiles keep falling anyway.
blocks.ko: 흰 용의 허리에 창 하나, 곶에는 함대 하나. 기왓장은 그래도 계속 떨어진다.

blocks.label: Pyongyang
blocks.ko: 평양

blocks.html: In Pyongyang, Gesomun reads the Yodong report twice and feeds it to the brazier.
blocks.ko: 평양에서 개소문은 요동의 보고를 두 번 읽고 화로에 던져 넣는다.

lines: 수나라 놈들은 그 성 앞에서 여름을 세 번 났어. 이놈은 열이틀이야!
고연수. 그믐까지 몇이나 끌고 나갈 수 있나?
en: Twelve days.
The Sui sat outside that wall for three summers. This one does it in twelve days!
Go Yeonsu. How many can you march by the new moon?
A hundred and fifty thousand, Supreme Commander. With the Mohe horse.

lines: 좋아. 안시로 가. 들판에서 맞붙어서 박살 내.
내 아들놈들도 치중대에 딸려 보내. 황제가 도망치는 꼴 좀 보게.
en: Good. Go to Ansi. Meet him in the open and break him on the plain.
And take my boys with the baggage. Let them watch an emperor run.

blocks.html: An old officer at the end of the table clears his throat. He has been clearing it for forty years. This time he finishes.
blocks.ko: 탁자 끝의 늙은 장교가 헛기침을 한다. 사십 년째 하는 헛기침이다. 이번에는 끝까지 한다.

blocks.speaker: The old officer
lines: 마지막으로 들판에서 제국의 군대를 맞은 임금은… 땅을 보지 않으셨지요.
en: The open field, sir? With respect.
The last king who met an empire in the open… didn’t look at the ground.

lines: 그럼 가는 길에 고연수한테 해 줘. 나흘이다. 짧게.
en: Then tell Go Yeonsu on the road. You’ve got four days. Make it short.

blocks.html: On the road to Ansi, the old man tells it anyway. Once, a king won twice and went back for a third…!
blocks.ko: 안시로 가는 길에서 노인은 끝내 이야기를 꺼낸다. 옛날, 두 번 이긴 왕이 세 번째를 하러 나갔다…!

logline.en: A king picks a fight over a diplomatic spat. Then he picks a battlefield he hasn’t looked at.
logline.ko: 임금이 외교 말다툼 하나로 싸움을 건다. 그러고는 한 번도 살펴보지 않은 땅을 싸움터로 고른다.

blocks.html: The old officer starts with the part kings like to hear. Goguryeo won. Twice.
blocks.ko: 늙은 장교는 왕들이 듣기 좋아하는 대목부터 꺼낸다. 고구려가 이겼다. 두 번.

blocks.caption: A king who starts a war over a letter. This time, someone writes back.
blocks.ko: 편지 한 장으로 싸움을 거는 임금. 이번엔 답장이 온다.

blocks.html: Four hundred years back, King Dongcheon picked a fight with the northern empire of Wei. Wei sent its most famous general to explain why that was a mistake. Goguryeo met him at the Boiling River and won. Then it chased him west up a valley and won again.
blocks.ko: 사백 년 전, 동천왕은 북쪽의 위나라에 싸움을 걸었다. 위는 그게 왜 실수인지 설명하라고 가장 이름난 장수를 보냈다. 고구려는 비류수에서 그를 맞아 이겼다. 그리고 서쪽 골짜기로 그를 쫓아가 또 이겼다.

lines: 그 이름난 장수란 놈? 그놈 목숨은 내 손바닥 안에 있다.
en: Wei’s great army is worse than our small one.
Their famous general? His life is in the palm of my hand.
Five thousand horse. We ride now.

blocks.speaker: The captain
lines: 전하, 강 건너 땅은— 아무도 달려 보지 않았습니다.
척후를 보내게 해 주십시오. 반나절이면 됩니다.
en: Majesty, the ground past the river— nobody’s ridden it.
Let me send scouts. One afternoon.
One afternoon is all I need to win.

blocks.html: So the king took five thousand horse out to win a third time, on ground he had not looked at. The Wei general formed a square on a slope that ran his way, and waited.
blocks.ko: 그렇게 왕은 세 번째 승리를 거두러 철기 오천을 끌고 나갔다. 들여다본 적도 없는 땅으로. 위의 장수는 제 쪽으로 기운 비탈에 방진을 치고 기다렸다.

blocks.speaker: The captain
en: Majesty, they’re not running.
Why aren’t they running?

blocks.html: The square held. The horses didn’t. Eighteen thousand men died in an afternoon.
blocks.ko: 방진은 버텼다. 말들은 버티지 못했다. 한나절 만에 만 팔천이 죽었다.

en: …I did not look at the ground.

blocks.html: Hwando is burned. The king runs east with a handful of men, and the Wei riders are one valley behind and closing.
blocks.ko: 환도성이 불탄다. 왕은 한 줌의 사람을 데리고 동쪽으로 달아나고, 위의 기병은 골짜기 하나 뒤에서 좁혀 온다.

blocks.html: At a ford in the rain, the captain who asked for scouts holds out his hand.
blocks.ko: 빗속의 여울목에서, 척후를 청했던 그 장교가 손을 내민다.

blocks.speaker: The captain
lines: 놈들은 임금의 옷을 쫓고 있습니다. 하나 잡게 해 주지요.
en: Your robe, Majesty.
They’re chasing a king’s robe. Let them catch one.

lines: …네 이름. 내가 네 이름도 묻지 않았구나.
en: …Your name. I never even asked your name.

blocks.speaker: The captain
en: You didn’t look at the ground either, Majesty.
Go.

blocks.html: He rides back up the valley in the king’s robe, slowly, so they can see it. They see it. Nobody on either side writes down his name.
blocks.ko: 그는 임금의 옷을 입고 골짜기를 거슬러 천천히 올라간다. 저들이 볼 수 있게. 저들은 본다. 어느 쪽에서도 그의 이름을 적어 두지 않는다.

blocks.html: A mountain capital, built for the day the plain is lost.
blocks.ko: 들판을 잃는 날을 위해 지은 산 위의 수도.

blocks.html: Goguryeo takes forty years to be a kingdom again. It is the first time in this story that a Samhan capital burns because of one bad afternoon, and it is not the last, and every king in this record has heard about it.
blocks.ko: 고구려가 다시 나라 꼴을 갖추는 데 사십 년이 걸린다. 이 이야기에서 하루 오후의 잘못으로 삼한의 도성이 불탄 첫 번째 일이고, 마지막은 아니며, 이 기록의 모든 임금이 그 이야기를 들어 알고 있다.

blocks.html: On the road to Ansi, the young general hears him out politely, the way you let a grandfather finish.
blocks.ko: 안시로 가는 길에서, 젊은 장수는 끝까지 공손히 듣는다. 할아버지 얘기를 끊지 않고 들어 드리듯이.

lines: 그런데 그 임금은 기병 오천이었지요. 저는 십오만입니다.
en: Good story, grandfather.
But he had five thousand horse. I have a hundred and fifty thousand men.

blocks.speaker: The old officer
en: …So did Wei.

blocks.html: A hundred and fifty thousand men march toward an open plain. On a hill above it, the emperor is waiting…!
blocks.ko: 십오만 대군이 탁 트인 들판으로 나아간다. 그 위 언덕에서 황제가 기다리고 있다…!

logline.en: A farmer in a white coat walks onto the field as a name on a muster roll. The Emperor is watching.
logline.ko: 흰 옷을 입은 농부 하나가 군적부의 이름 한 줄로 싸움터에 들어선다. 황제가 지켜보고 있다.

images.alt: Caravaggio’s Calling of St Matthew: the Emperor points out of the dark at the kneeling farmer in white
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. POSE: Caravaggio’s Calling of Saint Matthew. Inside the Emperor’s dark campaign pavilion at dusk: from the right, in shadow, the Second Emperor stretches out his arm and points across the frame; Li Shiji at his shoulder. Left, Xue Rengui kneels on one knee in dirt-streaked white armour, looking up, the fangtian ji upright in his fist, its crescent blade wet and glistening. A single hard shaft of low sun slants in through the open tent flap above the Emperor’s pointing hand and lands on Xue’s face and the ji; the rest of the pavilion is black. Encased in darkness: at least 80% of the frame is near-black umber void, the figures pulled out of it by one hard raking key. Old-master tenebrist canvas (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour oil brushwork, glazed umber-black darks, impasto on the brightest highlight, canvas grain; silk brushed in loaded strokes; only faces and hands keep clean webtoon ink line. The steel glistens: the key runs down every blade as one long white-hot streak with a tiny star-glint on the edge. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — XUE RENGUI — FACE and garments from attached /ch_xue_rengui.png (face only; invent a new pose). Demeanor: Tang's white-robed champion; showman of the charge. Carry: Fangtian ji halberd — no ring sword at all. #e8e3d5 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: ring-pommel sword. | THE SECOND EMPEROR — FACE and garments from attached /ch_taizong.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Bearded Tang emperor: black futou cap with an upright pin, thick black beard and moustache, fierce scowl. Dress: Imperial yellow robe-cape over black brocade. Demeanor: Commands; never asks. Conqueror's contempt that curdles at Ansi. Presence: THE SON OF HEAVEN — every frame he is in bends around him. He is SHROUDED IN DARKNESS: the black of the hall gathers around him like a mantle. One close practical light (a lamp, a brazier, a lamp-tree) rakes across him from below or from the side and SCULPTS him — the heavy yellow silk breaks into deep protruding folds brushed in loaded oil strokes that follow each fold, gold thread flicked in with impasto, the beard and cheekbones carved — and then falls off into black across his body and half his face; that falloff is the darkness, never a flat backlit silhouette. The camera sits BELOW his eyeline (low angle or worm’s-eye) and he is always placed HIGHER than anyone near him — on the dais, on a step, standing while others kneel or sit. He reads larger than life through lens and staging, not as a giant: broad shoulders, the robe spreading wide and heavy into the dark like a mountain, his shadow enormous on walls and floor. Unhurried, heavy stillness — never fidgeting, never casual, never a colleague at someone’s shoulder; when he smiles or laughs it is a predator’s ease, and the room goes quiet around it. Everyone else in frame is smaller, lower, less lit, turned toward him. The aura is darkness, scale and the hush around him — never a glow, never a halo, never rays behind his head. #c97a2e as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: Korean ring-pommel sword; Korean lamellar. | BLUE DRAGON — FACE and garments from attached /ch_blue_dragon.png (face only; invent a new pose). #4b78c9 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.at: He finds the ji on a rack in the yard
images.alt: Xue Rengui in torn white armour seizes his ji from the fortress yard and scales the wall by night
images.prompt: Cinematic historical illustration of a night escape from a mountain fortress, Three Kingdoms of Samhan / Tang era (645), scene: Xue Rengui in dirtied white armour, chains broken at his wrists, snatching his fangtian ji from a weapon rack in a torch-lit Goguryeo fortress yard and vaulting the stone rampart, startled guards below, cold moonlight and torch flame, motion like water finding a crack, painterly digital art, dramatic natural light, rich period costume, no modern elements, no text, no watermark, --ar 3:2 --stylize 250

images.prompt: Minimal iconic 9:16 poster. Xue Rengui, Tang white-armored general, standing in the RIGHT THIRD in profile LOOKING LEFT into a vast empty pale-ivory plane (#e8e3d5). UNIQUE LAYOUT: edge-gaze — figure cropped to the right edge, the rest of the frame is one hard empty color plane. Face matches the attached portrait. Striking silky pale lamellar and a premium white silk sash, few hues, high contrast. ONE accent: a small white-dragon emblem catching sheen. Flat pale void, monumental emptiness. No army. No fortress. No palace clutter. No clouds. No text. No watermark. Graphic color-blocking, anime-painterly, monumental.

images.alt: A rider in the green mountains
images.at: At Stallion Mountain the Second Emperor

images.alt: Xue Rengui charges through the snow with the ji

blocks.html: Go Yeonsu liked the old man’s story. He just didn’t think it was about him.
blocks.ko: 고연수는 노인의 이야기가 마음에 들었다. 다만 그게 자기 얘기라고는 생각하지 않았다.

blocks.html: Named for where an emperor stopped. Emperors name a lot of things.
blocks.ko: 황제가 멈춰 선 자리라 붙은 이름. 황제들은 이름 붙이길 좋아한다.

blocks.caption: Goguryeo sends a hundred and fifty thousand down the crow road. The emperor sends himself.
blocks.ko: 고구려는 까마귀 길로 십오만을 내려보낸다. 황제는 자기 자신을 보낸다.

blocks.html: At Stallion Mountain the Second Emperor does not wait behind the line.
blocks.ko: 주필산에서 황제는 진 뒤에서 기다리지 않는다.

en: I myself am the vanguard…!
zhLatn: Zhèn jí shì xiānfēng…!

blocks.html: The relief army comes down the crow road under banners that think numbers are an argument. Go Yeonsu and Go Hyejin ride at the front. The emperor sends a thousand Turkish horse to meet them and tells them to lose. They lose beautifully, all the way west to the foot of a mountain. Across the plain, under a ridge, the Tang look like a single army of fifteen thousand.
blocks.ko: 구원군은 숫자가 곧 논리라고 믿는 깃발을 앞세우고 까마귀 길을 내려온다. 고연수와 고혜진이 맨 앞에서 달린다. 황제는 돌궐 기병 천을 내보내 맞서게 하고, 지라고 이른다. 그들은 아주 보기 좋게 진다. 서쪽으로, 산기슭까지 내내. 들판 건너 고개 아래, 당군은 만오천짜리 군대 하나로 보인다.

blocks.speaker: The old officer
lines: 황제가 고작 만오천 데리고 여기까지 오진 않습니다. 진을 치십시오. 군량을 끊고 싸움은 겨울한테 맡기십시오.
en: Since when do Turks run?
That isn’t all of them.
An emperor doesn’t come this far with fifteen thousand. Dig in. Cut his grain. Let winter do the fighting.

lines: 겨울은 아직 안 왔소, 어르신. 저자는 왔지. 몸소.
황제 목을 칠 기회가 이보다 좋을 순 없소.
en: Winter isn’t here, grandfather. He is. In person.
We will never get a better chance at an emperor’s head.

blocks.html: Nobody tells Go Yeonsu about the valley behind him. In the night the Black Dragon takes a second army round the north of the mountain and into it. The emperor climbs the mountain with his drums, banners furled.
blocks.ko: 고연수 뒤편 골짜기 얘기는 아무도 해 주지 않는다. 밤사이 흑룡이 또 한 무리를 이끌고 산 북쪽을 돌아 그 골짜기로 든다. 황제는 북을 데리고, 깃발을 눕힌 채 산에 오른다.

blocks.speaker: Goguryeo picket
lines: 장군. 산 위에 뭐가 움직입니다. 많이요.
en: Sir. Something’s moving on the mountain. A lot of something.
No banners, though.

lines: 가서 자. 아침엔 황제를 먹을 거니까.
en: No banners, no army. Deer.
Go to sleep. We’re having an emperor for breakfast.

blocks.html: At dawn, drums start on the mountain above the field. The emperor is up there with his horns and his flags, playing the battle like a court orchestra.
blocks.ko: 새벽, 들판 위 산에서 북이 울리기 시작한다. 황제가 그 위에서 뿔나팔과 깃발로, 궁중 악단 부리듯 싸움을 연주한다.

blocks.label: The Tang Line
blocks.ko: 당군 진영

blocks.html: In the Tang line stands a guard captain whose accent still has the sea in it. Sul Gedu left Silla twenty-four winters ago, in the hold of a merchant ship. When the emperor called for volunteers, he put his own name down. It’s the only way a foreigner gets a captain’s sash. Across the field, the enemy’s banners are close enough to read.
blocks.ko: 당나라 진영의 근위 대장들 사이에, 말투에 아직 바다가 묻어 있는 사내가 하나 있다. 설계두는 스물네 해 전 상선 짐칸에 숨어 신라를 떠났다. 황제가 지원자를 부르자 그는 제 이름을 써넣었다. 이방인이 대장의 띠를 받는 길은 그것뿐이다. 들판 건너편, 적의 깃발이 글자가 읽힐 만큼 가깝다.

lines: 어이, 설 과의. 저쪽 놈들 말이오… 삼한 사람들이라던데.
en: Hey, Captain Xue. That lot over there… they say they’re Samhan men.
Aren’t you from Samhan as well?
zh: 喂，薛果毅。對面那些人……聽說是三韓人。
zhLatn: Wèi, Xuē guǒyì. Duìmiàn nàxiē rén… tīngshuō shì Sānhán rén.
Nǐ bù yě shì Sānhán lái de ma?

lines: 신라에선 사람 쓸 때 뼈부터 따져. 재주가 아무리 크고 공이 아무리 커도, 뼈가 아니면 못 넘어. 그냥 못 넘어.
그래서 바다 건너왔지. 천자 곁에서 관 쓰고 띠 두르고 칼 차고 드나들어 보려고.
en: Samhan. Silla.
In Silla they count your bones before they hire you. Doesn’t matter how big your talent is or how big your deeds — wrong bones, and you don’t get over the wall. You just don’t.
So I crossed the sea. To walk in and out at the Son of Heaven’s side with a cap and a sash and a sword.
…That’ll do me.
zh: 新羅用人，先論骨頭。才再大、功再高，骨頭不對，就是過不去。就是過不去。
所以我渡海來了。想在天子身邊，戴冠束帶、佩劍出入。
zhLatn: Sānhán. Xīnluó.
Xīnluó yòng rén, xiān lùn gǔtou. Cái zài dà, gōng zài gāo, gǔtou bú duì, jiùshì guò bú qù. Jiùshì guò bú qù.
Suǒyǐ wǒ dù hǎi lái le. Xiǎng zài tiānzǐ shēnbiān, dài guān shù dài, pèi jiàn chūrù.
……Zhè jiù gòu le.

blocks.html: The soldier laughs, not sure he was meant to. Sul Gedu ties off his helmet cord and does not look at the banners again.
blocks.ko: 병사는 웃어도 되는 건지 모른 채 웃는다. 설계두는 투구 끈을 묶고, 다시는 그 깃발 쪽을 보지 않는다.

blocks.html: In the Tang line a low officer decides the field needs a mark it cannot look away from. He puts on white armour — not for mourning, for visibility — hangs two bows at his waist, takes up the fangtian ji, and rides into the front so hard the relief army has to notice him or die without knowing why.
blocks.ko: 당진의 낮은 장교 하나가, 이 벌판에 눈을 떼지 못할 표식이 필요하다고 판단한다. 흰 갑옷을 입는다 — 상중이 아니라, 보이려고 — 허리에 활 둘을 차고 방천화극을 들어, 구원군이 알아채거나 모른 채 죽게 되도록 선두로 달린다.

en: Make a path.
If you will not — the ji will.
zhLatn: Ràng lù.
Ruò bù ràng——jǐ zì huì ràng.

blocks.html: No one in the Goguryeo line stops him for long. Then the drums on the mountain change, and the Black Dragon’s banners come out of the valley behind them. The relief army turns to face the wrong way twice. The formation breaks. The mountain learns a new colour.
blocks.ko: 고구려 진에서 그를 오래 막아서는 자는 없다. 그때 산 위의 북소리가 바뀌고, 뒤편 골짜기에서 흑룡의 깃발이 쏟아져 나온다. 구원군은 엉뚱한 쪽으로 두 번 돌아선다. 진이 무너진다. 산이 새로운 색 하나를 배운다.

blocks.html: Just then came thunder and lightning. Xue Rengui, a man of Longmen, in strange clothing, broke into the enemy line with a great shout, and nothing could stand before him. The Goguryeo troops gave way; the main army followed through, and the Goguryeo troops broke completely…
blocks.ko: 마침 천둥과 번개가 쳤는데, 용문 사람 설인귀가 기이한 옷을 입고 크게 소리치며 적진을 무너뜨리니 향하는 곳마다 대적할 자가 없었다. 고구려 군사가 쓰러지듯 흩어지자 대군이 그 틈을 타니, 고구려 군사가 크게 무너졌다…
blocks.hanja: 會有雷電，龍門人薛仁貴著奇服，大呼陷陳，所向無敵；高麗兵披靡，大軍乘之，高麗兵大潰…
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 198, Tang Zhenguan 19 (645), 6th month

en: Who is that man in white armour.
The one at the tip of the spear.
zhLatn: Nà báijiǎ shì hérén.
Máojiān nà hànzi.

en: Xue Rengui, Your Majesty.
A soldier… who was a farmer.
zhLatn: Xuē Rénguì, Bìxià.
Yī jiè… céng wéi nóngfū zhī bīng.

blocks.html: They bring him up. Dirt on the white. Blood on the crescent of the ji. He kneels like a man who has never been in a palace and does not intend to apologise for it.
blocks.ko: 그를 앞으로 불러낸다. 흰옷에 흙. 극의 초승달에 피. 그는 궁에 들어와 본 적 없는 사람처럼 무릎을 꿇고, 그걸 사과할 생각은 없어 보인다.

lines: 변경의 일을 맡길 날랜 장수를 고르려 하거늘 — 경만 한 자가 없도다.
짐은 요동을 얻은 것보다, 경을 얻은 것이 더 기쁘다.
en: My old generals are all aged.
I have been looking for a fierce one to entrust the frontier to — and I find none better than you.
I am less happy about gaining Liaodong than about gaining you.
zh: 欲擇猛將托邊事——無有過於卿者。
朕得遼東之喜，不及得卿。
zhLatn: Zhèn jiùjiàng jiē lǎo yǐ.
Yù zé měngjiàng tuō biānshì——wú yǒu guòyú qīng zhě.
Zhèn dé Liáodōng zhī xǐ, bùjí dé qīng.

lines: 다만 이 극이, 폐하의 길을 조금 넓혀 드렸을 뿐입니다.
en: A farmer… how could he dare.
This ji only widened Your Majesty’s road a little.
zh: 此戟不過略開陛下之路罷了。
zhLatn: Nóngfū… ān gǎn.
Cǐ jǐ bùguò lüè kāi Bìxià zhī lù bàle.

blocks.html: They give him gold, silk, a general’s title, and a place among the men who stand at the northern gate. The white coat stays. So does the ji.
blocks.ko: 금과 비단과 장군의 호와, 북문을 지키는 자리까지 내린다. 흰옷은 남는다. 극도 남는다.

blocks.html: That night he has a clerk write home for him. Two lines. The mounds can be finished properly now. Liu should buy the good stone.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 그는 서기를 시켜 집에 편지를 쓴다. 두 줄이다. 이제 무덤을 제대로 마무리할 수 있다. 유씨는 좋은 돌을 사라.

blocks.html: Go Yeonsu pulls what is left onto a hill to regroup. Behind the hill, the Tang have already burned the bridges. Nobody goes home the way they came. The emperor likes that trick.
blocks.ko: 고연수는 남은 군을 수습하려고 언덕 위로 물린다. 언덕 뒤의 다리는 당군이 이미 불태웠다. 왔던 길로 돌아가는 자는 없다. 황제가 아끼는 수법이다.

blocks.html: When the dust settles, the two relief commanders walk into the Tang camp on their knees. Their army walks in behind them.
blocks.ko: 먼지가 가라앉자 구원군의 두 장수가 무릎걸음으로 당나라 진영에 들어간다. 그들의 군대가 뒤를 따라 들어온다.

lines: …그 양반 살아 있나? 누가 좀 알아봐. 사과할 게 있어.
en: The old man said dig in.
…Is he alive? Somebody find out. I owe him an apology.

blocks.html: The officers are sent inland, to be subjects far from any border. The common soldiers are sent home. The Mohe riders who came south with them are marched into a valley and buried alive.
blocks.ko: 장교들은 국경에서 먼 내지로 보내져 당의 백성이 된다. 병졸들은 집으로 돌려보내진다. 그들과 함께 남하한 말갈 기병은 골짜기로 끌려가 산 채로 묻힌다.

blocks.html: Go Yeonsu does not live out the year. The records say he died of grief, which is the only cause of death the Tang ever let a surrendered general keep.
blocks.ko: 고연수는 그해를 넘기지 못한다. 기록은 그가 울화로 죽었다고 적는다. 항복한 장수에게 당이 남겨 준 사인은 그것 하나뿐이다.

blocks.label: The Field at Night
blocks.ko: 밤의 들판

blocks.html: There is another foreigner in the reckoning that night. Riding over the ground where the Goguryeo centre stood, the emperor finds Sul Gedu farther in than any of his own men got, face down among the dead he made.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 공을 헤아리는 자리에는 이방인이 하나 더 있다. 고구려 중군이 서 있던 땅을 말을 타고 지나던 황제는, 자기 군사 누구보다 깊이 들어간 자리에서, 제가 쓰러뜨린 시신들 사이에 엎어져 있는 설계두를 찾는다.

en: Who is this?
He is further in than any of Ours.

lines: 동료들 말이, 폐하 곁에서 관과 띠와 칼을 받는 게 평생 소원이었답니다.
en: A Silla man, Majesty. Sul Gedu.
His friends say he wanted a cap, a sash and a sword. At your side.

lines: 짐의 군사들은 죽음이 두려워 두리번거리며 나아가지 않는데, 이방 사람이 짐을 위해 죽었구나.
벼슬을 내려라. 예를 갖추어 장사 지내라.
en: Our own men look about them and will not advance. A foreigner dies for Us.
Give him the rank. Bury him with full rites.

blocks.html: Then he takes off the imperial robe and lays it over the dead man himself.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 손수 어포를 벗어 죽은 이 위에 덮는다.

blocks.html: The cap, the sash and the sword, more or less. He gets them lying down.
blocks.ko: 관과 띠와 칼, 대강 그것이다. 그는 그것을 누워서 받는다.

blocks.html: Fame is a short leash. Before the army even settles into the Ansi siege, Goguryeo stops trying to kill the man in white in the open and starts trying to keep him.
blocks.ko: 명성은 짧은 밧줄이다. 군이 안시 포위에 자리를 잡기도 전에, 고구려는 흰옷의 사내를 벌판에서 죽이려 하기보다 가두려 한다.

blocks.label: The Cell Under the Wall
blocks.ko: 성벽 밑 옥

blocks.html: They take him in a night fight east of the Liao — nets, numbers, the ji knocked from his hands — and drag him inland to a lesser fortress that is not Ansi and does not want to be famous. Iron on the wrists. A cell under the wall. The white coat cut off him like a trophy.
blocks.ko: 요하 동쪽의 밤싸움에서 그를 잡는다 — 그물, 머릿수, 손에서 떨어진 극 — 그리고 안시가 아닌, 유명해지고 싶지 않은 작은 성으로 끌고 간다. 손목의 쇠. 성벽 아래 감방. 하얀 옷은 전리품처럼 벗겨진다.

lines: 오늘 밤. 흰옷 입은 놈을 은으로 사 가겠다고. 성왕이시여, 굽어살피소서.
en: The Second Emperor… is coming this way.
Tonight. With silver, to buy back the man in white. Holy King, look down.
…Before His Majesty arrives.
I will have to be out.
zhLatn: …Bìxià jiàdào zhī qián.
Wǒ děi chūqù.

blocks.html: He breaks the irons. He breaks the door. The white coat only made him easy to see.
blocks.ko: 쇠사슬을 부순다. 문을 부순다. 하얀 옷은 그를 보이게만 했을 뿐이다.

blocks.html: He finds the ji on a rack in the yard, still sticky from someone else’s hands, and takes the wall the way water takes a crack. By the time the Second Emperor’s banners show on the ridge, the cell is empty and the fortress is explaining itself to no one.
blocks.ko: 마당 시렁에서 남의 손이 묻은 극을 찾아 들고, 물이 틈을 찾듯 성벽을 넘는다. 황제의 깃발이 능선에 보일 즈음, 감방은 비어 있고 성은 아무에게도 설명을 하지 못한다.

en: …That white coat again.
Arriving before Us, I see.
zhLatn: …Yòu shì nà shēn báiyī.
Jìng bǐ zhèn xiān dào.

lines: 폐하를 오래 기다리게 할 수 없었습니다.
en: I could not keep Your Majesty waiting.
The chains… were impolite.
zhLatn: Bù gǎn ràng Bìxià jiǔ hòu.
Nàxiē suǒliàn… tài wúlǐ le.

blocks.html: The Second Emperor laughs once — short, relieved — and does not ask how. A sovereign who has to ask how has already lost the man.
blocks.ko: 황제는 짧게, 안도하며 한 번 웃고, 어떻게 했는지는 묻지 않는다. 어떻게를 물어야 하는 군주는 이미 그 사내를 잃은 것이다.

blocks.label: Two Boys
blocks.ko: 두 소년

blocks.html: Among the prisoners taken at the mountain are two boys, eleven and eight: Gesomun’s sons, the careful one and the one who never backs down first. Their father sent them with the baggage to watch an emperor run.
blocks.ko: 주필산에서 잡힌 포로 가운데 열한 살, 여덟 살 난 사내아이 둘이 있다. 개소문의 아들들이다. 조심성 많은 맏이와, 먼저 물러서는 법이 없는 둘째. 황제가 도망치는 꼴을 보라며 아버지가 치중대에 딸려 보낸 아이들이다.

lines: 너희 아비는 임금을 죽였다. 짐은 형제를 죽였고.
en: So. Gai Suwen’s sons.
Your father killed his king. I killed my brothers.
So you see, he and I understand one another.
zh: 如此，朕與他倒有相通之處。
zhLatn: Yuánlái shì Gàisūwén zhī zǐ.
Ěr fù shā jūn. Zhèn shā xiōngdì.
Rúcǐ, zhèn yǔ tā dào yǒu xiāngtōng zhī chù.

lines: 무릎을 꿇고 대당의 신하가 되겠다 하면, 둘 다 관작을 주마.
장안의 집, 비단, 이름. 고려에서는 평생 못 가질 것들이다.
en: Here is my offer.
Kneel, call yourselves servants of the Great Tang, and I will give you both titles.
A house in Chang’an, silk, a name. Things Goryeo will never give you.
zh: 跪稱大唐臣子，朕賜爾二人官爵。
長安宅第、絲綢、名號。高麗永不能予者。
zhLatn: Zhèn yǒu yī yì.
Guì chēng Dà Táng chénzǐ, zhèn cì ěr èr rén guānjué.
Cháng'ān zháidì、sīchóu、mínghào. Gāolí yǒng bùnéng yǔ zhě.

en: Brother.

blocks.html: Namseng is eleven. He works out, quite quickly, that the Second Emperor wants two and will settle for one, and that only one of them has to be the one who refuses.
blocks.ko: 남생은 열한 살이다. 그는 꽤 빠르게 계산해 낸다. 황제는 둘을 원하지만 하나로도 만족할 것이고, 거절하는 역할은 둘 중 하나만 맡으면 된다는 것을.

lines: 폐하. 제 아우는 어립니다. 아무것도 모릅니다.
거절하는 건 접니다. 벌은 저에게 주십시오.
en: Your Majesty. My brother is small. He understands nothing.
It is I who refuse. Give the punishment to me.
…You are the elder?
zhLatn: …Nǐ shì xiōngzhǎng?

en: I am.

blocks.html: They flog him in front of his brother and send them both back across the Liao in the spring, as a gesture. Namgun does not speak for the whole journey.
blocks.ko: 그들은 아우가 보는 앞에서 그를 매질했고, 봄이 되자 아량이라며 둘 다 요하 너머로 돌려보냈다. 남건은 돌아오는 내내 한마디도 하지 않았다.

en: You took it for me.
I am the elder.

blocks.label: Pyongyang
blocks.ko: 평양

blocks.html: The news reaches Pyongyang in two pieces. The field army is gone. The boys are in the emperor’s tent.
blocks.ko: 소식은 두 토막으로 평양에 닿는다. 들판의 군대는 사라졌다. 아이들은 황제의 막사에 있다.

en: Both of them?

blocks.speaker: Rider
lines: 둘 다입니다, 대막리지. 황제가 아이들에게 너그럽게 하겠다고 전해 왔습니다.
en: Both, Supreme Commander. The emperor sends word he will be kind to them.

lines: 제 형제를 죽인 놈이 내 아들들한테 너그럽겠다고.
en: Kind.
A man who killed his brothers is being kind to my sons.

blocks.html: The hall waits for him to break something. He doesn’t. He calls for a map and puts his thumb on the one fort still flying the old king’s colours. The fort that refused him.
blocks.ko: 대청은 그가 뭔가 부수기를 기다린다. 그는 부수지 않는다. 지도를 가져오게 하고, 아직 옛 왕의 깃발을 단 성 하나에 엄지를 얹는다. 그를 거부한 성이다.

lines: 내가 일곱 살 때, 아버지가 살수에서 수나라 깃발을 옆구리에 끼고 돌아왔어. 난 깃발이 황제한테서 열리는 열맨 줄 알았지.
깊이 들어오라 그래. 저번 놈도 그랬어.
en: Ansi. That madman.
When I was seven, my father came home from the Colossal River with a Sui flag under his arm. I thought flags grew on emperors.
Let him come deep. The last one did.

blocks.html: Why isn’t Gesomun afraid? Go back thirty-three years, to a general who surrendered seven times and won…!
blocks.ko: 개소문은 왜 두려워하지 않는가? 서른세 해 전으로 가 보자. 일곱 번 항복하고 이긴 장수가 있었다…!

logline.en: Ulchi Munduk surrenders seven times on the way south. Every time, the river gets closer.
logline.ko: 을지문덕은 남쪽으로 내려가며 일곱 번 항복한다. 그때마다 강이 가까워진다.
