images.prompt: Cinematic historical illustration of salsu flashback, Three Kingdoms of Samhan / Tang era (612), scene: Great River, painterly digital art, dramatic natural light, rich period costume, no modern elements, no text, no watermark, --ar 3:2 --stylize 250

images.at: Ulchi Munduk surrenders seven times on the way south.
images.alt: The endless Sui host crosses the Liao on pontoon bridges while Ulchi Munduk watches from a ridge
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE battle frame. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. The Battle of the Colossal River (Salsu), summer 612: a broad shallow river over pale gravel bars between low pine hills in northern Goguryeo. Sui banners are dull gold and black, Goguryeo banners red, their marks illegible brush strokes. The Sui host crossing the Liao River on three long pontoon bridges: a sea of spears and gold-and-black banners under towering dust clouds lit orange by the low sun, columns stretching to the horizon. In the dark foreground on a pine ridge, Ulchi Munduk on horseback, small, watching. Device: the three bridges as long diagonals across the water. HEEWON BATTLE STYLE — this is a battle frame, and every still of this battle shares ONE look so the set plays as one film. Copy the BRUSHWORK AND STYLIZATION of the two attached style_battle boards ONLY — never their ships, flags, figures or composition (the painted board shows 19th-century steam and sailing ships; this battle is 7th-century East Asia). The look is the background art of a hand-painted 2D animated epic crossed with an East Asian woodblock battle scroll. SMOKE AND CLOUD are the big shapes: towering sculpted columns and rolling banks painted as broad soft gouache masses, lit warm orange from the fires underneath and cooling to slate and charcoal at the top; where they curl they break into stylised scroll-cloud spirals outlined in thin ink, like a painted screen. WATER is Hokusai: heavy slate-teal swells with claw-like cream-white foam crests drawn in ink line, spray as stippled dots. FIRE is flat curling ribbons of vermilion and orange with darker red edges licking up hulls, sails and banners — never photographic flame. BANNERS are long silk ribbons whipping in the wind, kingdom colour only, their marks illegible brush strokes. FIGURES are many small drawn silhouettes — soldiers packed in boats, oars, spears, shields — read as massed shapes, the nearest ones dark against the bright smoke; named heroes are drawn larger with clean webtoon faces. DEPTH is layered like stage flats: dark foreground waves, boats and figures; midground ships or ranks in clear silhouette; background smoke, haze and a pale sky that fades like cream paper; a few seabirds or embers. PALETTE is fixed for the whole battle: cream-paper sky, slate blue-grey and teal water, charcoal smoke, vermilion-and-orange fire, ink black, plus each kingdom's banner colour — no purple sunset, no neon, no other hues. Painted texture everywhere (gouache grain, dry-brush, ink line on waves and clouds); not photoreal, not 3D, not a map or satellite view, not a manga speed-line panel. SHIPS are 7th-century only: Tang multi-storey louchuan tower-ships with stacked timber cabins, rows of oars and battened junk sails; Yamato and Baekje open oared war-boats with a single mast — never European hulls, cannon, funnels or square-rigged masts. OVERRIDES of the house rules below for battle frames: massed hosts and fleets are allowed as silhouetted masses; daylight through smoke is allowed (the dark masses are the smoke, the bright break is the pale sky or the fire); still ONE device (a waterline, a smoke column, a ring of hulls, a ford) and big quiet areas of smoke or sky. CANON — ULCHI MUNDUK — FACE and garments from attached /ch_ulchi_munduk.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Lean, weathered Goguryeo general: narrow watchful eyes, thin moustache and small chin beard, calm unreadable face of a man counting the enemy. Dress: Steel lamellar with a round bronze boss on the chest, a red scarf wound at the throat, red cloth sleeves and skirt; red-winged steel helm with a red plume. Demeanor: The Defender: patient, sly, unhurried — retreats on purpose, writes the enemy a poem, then springs the river. Armor: Goguryeo kit: steel lamellar with red-edged plates and RED WING shoulder-flaps, peaked helm with plume — red cloth, never gold plate. Battle armor: plates are METALLIC GRAY STEEL lamellar copied from the attached lamellar ref, cloth peeking at collar, sleeves, skirt, sash and plume-cord in the wearer's color only. Ignore labels and watermarks on armor refs. Not Japanese kabuto, not fantasy plate, not a gold-painted suit. Fighting: Commands from the saddle with a long spear; a ring sword at the hip, rarely drawn. #e0503f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: Chinese general armor; katana. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Goguryeo: attached /ref_hanbok_goguryeo.png. | Kingdom banners: copy field colour and emblem from the attached flag_*.png ref onto period silk war-banners — tall poles behind each side, long streamers, small pennants on spear-tips and saddle-backs. Painted silk, wind-whipped, torn and smoke-stained in battle; never a flat modern flag graphic. Each side's banner colour is the clearest colour on its half of the frame, so the kingdom reads at a glance. Goguryeo banners: red silk with the black three-legged crow inside a studded black sun-ring. Attached flag /flag_goguryeo.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE battle frame. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. The Battle of the Colossal River (Salsu), summer 612: a broad shallow river over pale gravel bars between low pine hills in northern Goguryeo. Sui banners are dull gold and black, Goguryeo banners red, their marks illegible brush strokes. Bird’s-eye from high above an autumn plain: a small band of Goguryeo riders with red banners wheeling away at a gallop, and behind them the long Sui column snaking after through its own dust; far ahead a silver ribbon of river. BANNERS are long silk ribbons whipping in the wind, kingdom colour only, their marks illegible brush strokes. FIGURES are many small drawn silhouettes — soldiers packed in boats, oars, spears, shields — read as massed shapes, the nearest ones dark against the bright smoke; named heroes are drawn larger with clean webtoon faces. DEPTH is layered like stage flats: dark foreground waves, boats and figures; midground ships or ranks in clear silhouette; background smoke, haze and a pale sky that fades like cream paper; a few seabirds or embers. PALETTE is fixed for the whole battle: cream-paper sky, slate blue-grey and teal water, charcoal smoke, vermilion-and-orange fire, ink black, plus each kingdom's banner colour — no purple sunset, no neon, no other hues. Painted texture everywhere (gouache grain, dry-brush, ink line on waves and clouds); not photoreal, not 3D, not a map or satellite view, not a manga speed-line panel. SHIPS are 7th-century only: Tang multi-storey louchuan tower-ships with stacked timber cabins, rows of oars and battened junk sails; Yamato and Baekje open oared war-boats with a single mast — never European hulls, cannon, funnels or square-rigged masts. OVERRIDES of the house rules below for battle frames: massed hosts and fleets are allowed as silhouetted masses; daylight through smoke is allowed (the dark masses are the smoke, the bright break is the pale sky or the fire); still ONE device (a waterline, a smoke column, a ring of hulls, a ford) and big quiet areas of smoke or sky. CANON — ULCHI MUNDUK — FACE and garments from attached /ch_ulchi_munduk.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Lean, weathered Goguryeo general: narrow watchful eyes, thin moustache and small chin beard, calm unreadable face of a man counting the enemy. Dress: Steel lamellar with a round bronze boss on the chest, a red scarf wound at the throat, red cloth sleeves and skirt; red-winged steel helm with a red plume. Demeanor: The Defender: patient, sly, unhurried — retreats on purpose, writes the enemy a poem, then springs the river. Armor: Goguryeo kit: steel lamellar with red-edged plates and RED WING shoulder-flaps, peaked helm with plume — red cloth, never gold plate. Battle armor: plates are METALLIC GRAY STEEL lamellar copied from the attached lamellar ref, cloth peeking at collar, sleeves, skirt, sash and plume-cord in the wearer's color only. Ignore labels and watermarks on armor refs. Not Japanese kabuto, not fantasy plate, not a gold-painted suit. Fighting: Commands from the saddle with a long spear; a ring sword at the hip, rarely drawn. #e0503f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: Chinese general armor; katana. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Goguryeo: attached /ref_hanbok_goguryeo.png. | Kingdom banners: copy field colour and emblem from the attached flag_*.png ref onto period silk war-banners — tall poles behind each side, long streamers, small pennants on spear-tips and saddle-backs. Painted silk, wind-whipped, torn and smoke-stained in battle; never a flat modern flag graphic. Each side's banner colour is the clearest colour on its half of the frame, so the kingdom reads at a glance. Goguryeo banners: red silk with the black three-legged crow inside a studded black sun-ring. Attached flag /flag_goguryeo.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Ulchi Munduk surrenders seven times on the way south. Every time, the river gets closer.
blocks.ko: 을지문덕은 남쪽으로 내려가는 길에 일곱 번 항복한다. 그때마다 강이 가까워진다.

blocks.caption: Nine armies over the Liao, a fleet up the Taedong. The Sui planned everything except the walk home.
blocks.ko: 요하를 건너는 아홉 군단, 대동강을 오르는 함대. 수나라는 돌아가는 길만 빼고 다 계획했다.

blocks.html: Gesomun is seven that summer. The last dynasty’s emperor has sent three hundred thousand men at Pyongyang. Goguryeo sends one man to look at them.
blocks.ko: 그해 여름 개소문은 일곱 살이다. 지난 왕조의 황제가 삼십만 대군을 평양으로 보냈다. 고구려는 그들을 구경하라고 사람 하나를 보낸다.

blocks.html: Ask a Goguryeo grandfather. He will raise a cup first.
blocks.ko: 고구려 할아버지에게 물어보라. 잔부터 들 것이다.

blocks.label: The Sui Camp
blocks.ko: 수나라 진영

blocks.html: Munduk walks into the enemy camp himself first, to look at them. He brings a white flag, a polite face and no guards. He has come, he says, to surrender.
blocks.ko: 을지문덕은 먼저 몸소 적진으로 걸어 들어가 그들을 살핀다. 흰 깃발 하나, 공손한 얼굴 하나, 호위는 없다. 항복하러 왔다고 한다.

blocks.speaker: Sui general
en: Goguryeo surrenders? Just like that?

lines: 저희는 작은 나라고, 장군께선 아주 큰 군대시니까요.
…병사들이 제 군량을 지고 다닌 지 얼마나 됐습니까? 다들 지쳐 보이는군요.
en: Just like that, General.
We are a small country. You are a very large army.
…How long have your men carried their own rice? They look tired.

blocks.html: A hundred days of rice each, on their own backs. At night most of them bury half of it under the tent to lighten the load. Munduk notices the fresh dirt.
blocks.ko: 한 사람당 백 일 치 쌀을 제 등에 졌다. 밤이면 대부분 짐을 덜려고 막사 밑에 절반을 묻는다. 을지문덕은 갓 뒤집힌 흙을 본다.

blocks.speaker: Sui general
lines: 황상의 명은, 네가 오면 붙잡으라는 것이다.
en: The emperor’s orders are to seize you if you come.

blocks.speaker: Sui officer
lines: 장군— 항복하러 온 사신을 잡으면 앞으로 아무도 우리한테 항복하지 않을 겁니다.
en: General— if we seize an envoy who came to surrender, nobody will ever surrender to us again.

blocks.html: So they let him walk out. He has seen everything he came for. By evening the general regrets it and sends a rider after him: come back, there is more to discuss.
blocks.ko: 그래서 그들은 그를 걸어 나가게 둔다. 그는 보러 온 것을 다 보았다. 저녁이 되자 장군은 후회하고 기병 하나를 뒤쫓아 보낸다. 돌아오라, 더 의논할 것이 있다.

en: Tell the general I’m flattered.
Tell him we can discuss it further south.

blocks.label: Seven
blocks.ko: 일곱 번

blocks.html: He surrenders seven times on the way south and runs seven times. Each time the Sui win a small fight, plant a flag and feel wonderful. Each running pulls them further from their buried rice and closer to Pyongyang.
blocks.ko: 그는 남쪽으로 가는 길에 일곱 번 항복하고 일곱 번 달아난다. 그때마다 수나라는 작은 싸움에서 이기고, 깃발을 꽂고, 기분이 아주 좋다. 달아날 때마다 그들은 묻어 둔 쌀에서 멀어지고 평양에 가까워진다.

blocks.speaker: Sui general
lines: 하루에 일곱 번 이겼다! 받아 적어라.
en: Seven victories in a day! Write that down.

blocks.speaker: Sui officer
lines: 장군… 일곱 번 이겼는데 얻은 게 없습니다. 곳간 하나도요.
en: General… we have won seven times and taken nothing. Not one granary.

blocks.title: The walk home
blocks.caption: They marched to within thirty li of Pyongyang. Munduk had been counting on exactly that.
blocks.ko: 평양 삼십 리 앞까지 왔다. 을지문덕이 바란 게 바로 그거였다.

blocks.html: The Colossal River is low that summer. They wade it without losing a man and nobody thinks about it twice. Thirty li from Pyongyang, the army stops and looks at the walls. The walls look back.
blocks.ko: 그해 여름 살수는 얕다. 그들은 한 명도 잃지 않고 걸어서 건넌다. 아무도 그걸 두 번 생각하지 않는다. 평양 삼십 리 앞에서 군대는 멈춰 성벽을 바라본다. 성벽도 마주 본다.

blocks.speaker: Sui officer
en: General, we have no ladders up here, and no rice to wait with.
lines: 장군, 여기엔 사다리도 없고, 버틸 쌀도 없습니다.

blocks.html: Then a letter arrives from Munduk. It is a poem.
blocks.ko: 그때 을지문덕의 편지가 온다. 시다.

blocks.title: Poem sent to the Sui general
blocks.hanja:
神策究天文
妙算窮地理
戰勝功旣高
知足願云止
blocks.html:
Your godlike strategy has searched out the patterns of heaven;
your wondrous reckoning has mastered the lie of the land.
Your victories have already won you high merit —
know it is enough, and I pray you stop.
blocks.ko:
그대의 귀신 같은 계책은 하늘의 이치를 다 헤아렸고
신묘한 계산은 땅의 이치를 통달했다
전쟁에 이겨 쌓은 공이 이미 높으니
만족함을 알고 그치기를 바라노라
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 44, Biographies — Eulji Mundeok

blocks.speaker: Sui general
en: Is he… praising me?

blocks.speaker: Sui officer
en: He’s telling you to go home, General.

blocks.html: A second note follows, plainer. If the Sui turn around, the king of Goguryeo will come and bow to their emperor in person. It is the eighth surrender. The general takes it, because it is the only one he can carry home.
blocks.ko: 두 번째 편지가 뒤따른다. 이번엔 쉬운 말이다. 수나라가 군을 돌리면 고구려 왕이 몸소 황제께 나아가 절하겠다. 여덟 번째 항복이다. 장군은 받아들인다. 집에 들고 갈 수 있는 건 그것뿐이니까.

blocks.label: The River
blocks.ko: 살수

blocks.html: They turn for home starving, in squares, with Goguryeo riders on every side. At the Colossal River the water is still low and wide, and the army starts back across.
blocks.ko: 그들은 굶주린 채 방진을 짜고 돌아선다. 사방에 고구려 기병이 붙는다. 살수의 물은 여전히 얕고 넓다. 군대가 다시 건너기 시작한다.

en: Wait.
…Wait.
Now. While their feet are wet.

blocks.html: When the army is halfway over, Goguryeo comes down on the rearguard. Men on the far bank can’t come back. Men on the near bank can’t get over. The ones in the middle find out how deep a shallow river is.
blocks.ko: 군대가 절반쯤 건넜을 때 고구려가 후군을 덮친다. 건너편에 닿은 자들은 돌아올 수 없다. 이쪽에 남은 자들은 건너갈 수 없다. 한가운데 있던 자들은 얕은 강이 얼마나 깊은지 알게 된다.

blocks.speaker: A Sui soldier
en: It was knee-deep! It was knee-deep on the way down—

blocks.html: When the nine armies crossed the Liao there were three hundred and five thousand of them. When they got back to the Liaodong fortress there were two thousand seven hundred. Stores and weapons by the tens of thousands were lost, every one.
blocks.ko: 처음 아홉 군대가 요수를 건넌 것이 모두 30만 5천이었는데, 요동성으로 돌아온 것은 겨우 2천 7백 명이었다. 수만을 헤아리던 군량과 기계도 모두 잃어버렸다.
blocks.hanja: 初，九軍渡遼，凡三十萬五千，及還至遼東城，唯二千七百人，資儲器械巨萬計，失亡蕩盡。
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 181, Sui Daye 8 (612), 7th month

blocks.html: Munduk is honored with the title “The Defender” after the battle.
blocks.ko: 문덕은 전투 후 «수호신»이라는 칭호를 받는다.

blocks.html: Gesomun’s father rides home through the Pyongyang gate with a Sui banner rolled under his arm like a bolt of cloth. The boy at the gate decides, then and there, what emperors are for.
blocks.ko: 개소문의 아버지는 수나라 깃발을 비단 필처럼 옆구리에 말아 끼고 평양 성문으로 돌아온다. 성문에 선 아이는 그 자리에서 정한다. 황제란 무엇에 쓰는 것인지.

blocks.speaker: The boy
en: Is that the emperor’s?

blocks.speaker: His father
lines: 도망칠 때 흘리고 가거든. 자. 비단 말고 장대를 잡아라.
en: One of them. Emperors have plenty.
They drop them when they run. Here. Hold it by the pole, not the silk.

blocks.html: Yodong fell. The forts fell. One wall is left, held by a madman whose name nobody wrote down…!
blocks.ko: 요동이 무너졌다. 성들이 무너졌다. 남은 성벽은 하나. 그 성을 지키는 미치광이의 이름은 아무도 적어 두지 않았다…!

logline.en: The Guardian of Ansi refused Yeon to his face. Now the Emperor of the West is at his gate.
logline.ko: 안시성주는 연에게 대놓고 고개를 저었다. 이제 서토의 황제가 그의 성문 앞에 있다.

blocks.html: The Guardian of Ansi Fortress is an eccentric man. When Yeon took the country, the Guardian refused him to his face. He kept the old king’s colours on the wall. Yeon had drowned a whole court for less. He looked at that wall, weighed the siege, and rode away. Ansi answers to no one.
blocks.ko: 안시성의 성주는 괴짜다. 연이 나라를 쥐었을 때, 성주는 그의 면전에서 복종을 거부했다. 성벽 위에는 옛 왕의 깃발을 그대로 두었다. 연은 그보다 못한 일로 조정 하나를 물에 잠기게 한 사내다. 그는 그 성벽을 바라보고, 공성의 값을 셈해 본 뒤, 말머리를 돌렸다. 안시는 누구의 명도 받지 않는다.

blocks.html: One small fortress, and one stubborn man on top of it.
blocks.ko: 작은 성 하나, 그 위에 고집 센 사내 하나.

blocks.html: Nobody writes his name down. To the people inside the walls he is just the chief, and that turns out to be enough.
blocks.ko: 누구도 그의 이름을 적어 두지 않았다. 성 안 사람들에게 그는 그저 성주였고, 결국 그것으로 충분했다.

blocks.caption: The emperor wants Pyongyang. One small fortress is in the way.
blocks.ko: 황제는 평양을 원한다. 작은 성 하나가 길을 막고 있다.

en: Ansi… so that man is still alive.
He dares refuse the Supreme Commander’s order?
I have heard that a true man needs only
one person to cherish,
and one person to serve,
and that is enough.

blocks.label: The Earthen Mountain
blocks.ko: 토산

blocks.html: The Second Emperor tries the wall first. The Blue Dragon’s rams go at the west wall six or seven times a day. Every tower they knock down is a timber fence by dark.
blocks.ko: 황제는 먼저 성벽을 쳐 본다. 청룡의 충차가 하루 예닐곱 번 서쪽 성벽에 붙는다. 무너진 망루는 해 질 녘이면 나무 울타리가 되어 있다.

blocks.speaker: Ansi soldier
lines: 누런 깃발이다! 저놈이다— 북 쳐, 북!
어이, 천자 양반! 우리 울타리가 너네 망루보다 높다!
en: Yellow banners! That’s him— drums, drums!
Hey, Son of Heaven! Our fence is taller than your tower!

blocks.html: When the wall does not work he tries the ground, which is the sort of thing only an empire can afford to try. His cousin starts piling earth against the south-east corner, and the emperor moves his camp south to watch it grow. The archers on the parapet watch every basket.
blocks.ko: 성벽이 안 되자 그는 땅을 쳐 본다. 제국이나 되어야 해 볼 수 있는 짓이다. 사촌이 동남쪽 모서리에 흙을 쌓기 시작하고, 황제는 그게 자라는 걸 보려고 진영을 남쪽으로 옮긴다. 성가퀴의 궁수들은 흙짐 하나하나를 지켜본다.

en: How many baskets is that now?
blocks.speaker: Tang hauler
blocks.art: Tang haulers on the mound’s slope at dusk, baskets of earth on their backs.

en: Don’t count. It gets heavier when you count.
blocks.speaker: Another hauler

lines: 성주님, 저놈들 벌써 예순 날째 저럽니다.
en: Chief, that’s sixty days they’ve been at it.
blocks.speaker: Ansi soldier
blocks.art: Night. Torches on the inner wall; the garrison passing stones hand to hand, raising the wall course by course while the mound’s black shoulder looms outside.

lines: 그럼 우리는 예순 밤째다. 돌 넘겨.
en: Then it’s sixty nights for us. Pass the stone.

blocks.html: Inside the walls the stone runs out first. Then the doors. Then the roof beams of the houses nearest that corner. Families sleep in the open and pass their own lintels up the ladder.
blocks.ko: 성안에서는 돌이 먼저 떨어진다. 다음은 문짝이다. 그다음은 그 모서리 가까운 집들의 서까래다. 사람들은 한데서 자고, 제 집 문지방을 사다리 위로 올려 보낸다.

blocks.html: Five hundred thousand man-days, sixty days of hauling, and the mountain’s crown stands higher than the wall. From up there you can count the cook fires.
blocks.ko: 연인원 오십만, 예순 날의 흙짐. 마침내 흙산 꼭대기가 성벽보다 높아진다. 거기 서면 성안의 밥 짓는 불까지 셀 수 있다.

blocks.speaker: Ansi soldier
lines: 성주님. 저 위에서 우리 밥솥까지 보이겠는데요.
en: Chief. They can see our rice pots from up there.

lines: 그럼 냄새 좋은 거 해. 저놈들도 한번 배고파 보라고.
en: Then cook something that smells good. Let them be hungry for a change.

blocks.title: Ansi Fortress, sixth to ninth month, 645
blocks.note: Every night the defenders built their wall higher than the mound had grown that day. The siege became a race between shovels.

blocks.html: Then it rains, and the mountain slumps — sideways, into the wall it was built to overlook, taking a stretch of Ansi down with it. Both sides stare at the gap.
blocks.ko: 그러다 비가 온다. 산이 무너진다. 내려다보려 쌓은 그 성벽 쪽으로 옆으로 무너지며, 안시성 한 자락을 함께 무너뜨린다. 양쪽 모두 그 틈을 바라본다.

en: Chief, the wall—
blocks.speaker: Ansi soldier

lines: 벽은 됐고. 저 위에 지금 누가 있냐?
en: Never mind the wall. Who’s up on that thing right now?

blocks.html: The officer who was supposed to be holding the mound has stepped away.
blocks.ko: 흙산을 지켜야 할 장수는 자리를 비운 참이었다.
blocks.art: Cut to the mound’s crown: an empty command stool in the rain.

en: …There’s nobody up there.
blocks.speaker: Ansi soldier

en: Then it’s ours.

blocks.html: A few hundred men are standing on sixty days of Tang work. They pile timber on its slopes and set it alight. By noon there is a Goguryeo banner on top.
blocks.ko: 수백 명이 당군의 예순 날 위에 서 있다. 그들은 비탈에 나무를 쌓아 불을 지른다. 한낮이 되자 꼭대기에 고구려 깃발이 선다.

lines: …짐의 산 위에 걸린 저 깃발은 누구의 것이냐?
en: Sixty days.
…Whose banner is that, on Our mountain?

blocks.speaker: Tang officer
lines: 저들 것이옵니다, 폐하. 부복애가… 잠시 자리를 비웠다 하옵니다.
en: Theirs, Majesty. Fu Fuai had… stepped down from it.

blocks.html: The emperor has Fu Fuai beheaded, very courteously, and orders three days of assault on the mound.
blocks.ko: 황제는 아주 정중하게 부복애의 목을 베고, 흙산에 사흘간의 총공격을 명한다.

blocks.html: The emperor rides up to watch. Too close.
blocks.ko: 황제가 지켜보러 다가온다. 너무 가까이.

blocks.html: On the second day the Guardian sees him: a yellow parasol on the near slope, closer than any emperor should be. He takes the bow from the archer beside him.
blocks.ko: 이틀째, 성주의 눈에 그가 들어온다. 가까운 비탈 위의 누런 일산. 어느 황제도 그렇게 가까이 와선 안 된다. 성주는 옆의 궁수에게서 활을 받아 든다.

en: Hold still, you.

blocks.html: The arrow takes the helmet clean off. The lacquered bowl leaves his head and rings once on packed earth, then keeps rolling. For the first time in the siege, the two men look straight at each other.
blocks.ko: 화살이 투구를 깨끗이 벗겨 낸다. 옻칠한 투구가 머리를 떠나 다진 흙 위에서 한 번 울리고는 계속 굴러간다. 포위가 시작된 뒤 처음으로, 두 사내가 서로를 똑바로 바라본다.

en: …That man.
Find out his name.

blocks.html: Nobody can. A cut over the emperor’s eye bleeds into his beard. The surgeons say it is nothing, and he lets them.
blocks.ko: 아무도 알아 오지 못한다. 황제의 눈썹 위 상처에서 피가 수염으로 흘러든다. 의원들은 별것 아니라 하고, 그는 그렇게 믿어 준다.

blocks.label: The Retreat
blocks.ko: 회군

blocks.html: Then the cold comes early. Sixty days of hauling earth were sixty days of horses eating the plain, and the plain is bare. There is nothing left to feed them.
blocks.ko: 그러다 추위가 일찍 온다. 흙을 나른 예순 날은 말들이 들판을 뜯어 먹은 예순 날이기도 했다. 들판은 맨땅이다. 말을 먹일 것이 남지 않았다.

blocks.html: On the morning he turns for home, the emperor parades his army under the wall one last time, so the wall can see what it beat. Inside, nobody shows a face. Then one man climbs the parapet and bows.
blocks.ko: 회군하는 날 아침, 황제는 마지막으로 성 아래에서 군을 사열한다. 성이 무엇을 이겼는지 보라는 듯이. 성안에서는 아무도 얼굴을 내밀지 않는다. 그러다 한 사내가 성가퀴에 올라 절을 한다.

blocks.html: A proper bow, from the waist. The kind you give a guest who stayed too long.
blocks.ko: 허리를 굽힌 제대로 된 절이다. 너무 오래 머문 손님에게 하는 그런 절.

lines: 제 주군을 잘 섬긴 자에게 주는 것이다. 짐의 천하 모든 성이 듣게 하라.
그리고 이름을 물어라. 한 번 더.
en: Bring up the silk. A hundred bolts.
For a man who serves his lord well. Let every wall in Our empire hear of it.
And ask him his name. Once more.

lines: 그리고 이것도. 수가 많은 것도 알고, 머리가 좋은 것도 알겠소.
그런데 당신들은 절대로 우리보다 미치지는 못할 거요…!
en: Tell him thanks for the silk.
And tell him this. You may outnumber us. You may outthink us.
But you will never be crazier than we are…!
blocks.art: On the wall the day the Tang turn for home, the bolts of silk at his feet.

blocks.html: The silk goes up the wall on a rope. The name does not come down.
blocks.ko: 비단은 밧줄에 매달려 성벽을 올라간다. 이름은 내려오지 않는다.

blocks.html: Then the marsh. Two hundred li of mud, and the road across it is the road he tore up himself. Nobody goes home the way they came. He said that.
blocks.ko: 그리고 늪이다. 이백 리 진흙. 그 위를 건너던 길은 그가 손수 걷어 낸 길이다. 왔던 길로 돌아가는 자는 없다. 그가 한 말이다.

blocks.html: Snow comes down on the column in the mud. The emperor gets off his horse and cuts brush with his own hands to fill the ruts. His officers can’t be seen carrying less.
blocks.ko: 진흙 속 행렬 위로 눈이 내린다. 황제는 말에서 내려 손수 덤불을 베어 바퀴 자국을 메운다. 장수들은 황제보다 적게 나르는 모습을 보일 수 없다.

lines: 내가 천하의 군사를 가지고도 작은 오랑캐에게 곤욕을 당한 것은 무엇 때문인가?
…그 노신이 살아 있었다면, 짐을 결코 오게 두지 않았을 것을.
en: With all the armies under heaven, how was I humiliated by so small a barbarian land?
…If the old minister were alive, he would never have let me come.
Somebody tell me no. Anybody.

blocks.html: Nobody does. That was the whole trouble.
blocks.ko: 아무도 말하지 않는다. 처음부터 그게 문제였다.

blocks.title: The Seventh Invasion, start to finish
blocks.caption: All those arrows in, and two dotted lines out. One small wall did that.
blocks.ko: 들어간 화살은 저렇게 많은데, 나온 건 점선 두 줄. 작은 성벽 하나가 한 일이다.

blocks.label: The Gate
blocks.ko: 성문

blocks.html: Three weeks later a rider in red comes up the empty road from Pyongyang, alone. The last time he came, he looked at this wall and rode away.
blocks.ko: 세 주쯤 뒤, 붉은 옷의 기수 하나가 평양에서 텅 빈 길을 홀로 올라온다. 지난번에 왔을 때 그는 이 성벽을 보고 말머리를 돌렸다.

lines: 대막리지 나리! 일 다 끝났으니 이제 내 목 가지러 왔나?
en: Supreme Commander! Come for my head, now the work’s done?
Madman…
Still — you did what had to be done.

lines: 목은 갖고 있어. 옛 깃발도 달고 있고. 성문도 닫아 두든가, 상관없어.
뭐가 그놈을 막았나 보러 왔어. 생각보다 작네.
en: Keep your head. Keep your old colours. Keep your gate shut, I don’t care.
I came to see what stopped him. It’s smaller than I thought.
So’s the emperor, up close.

blocks.html: Gesomun laughs, a laugh like a slap, and turns his horse. He does not ask to come in. The Guardian does not offer.
blocks.ko: 개소문은 따귀 같은 웃음을 터뜨리고 말머리를 돌린다. 들여보내 달라고 하지 않는다. 성주도 권하지 않는다.

blocks.label: Yodong
blocks.ko: 요동

blocks.html: He rides home by way of Yodong. The Tang marched its people west when they left, seventy thousand of them, roped in lines. What is left is ash, and a stone shrine on the hill with its door open.
blocks.ko: 그는 요동을 거쳐 돌아간다. 당군은 물러가며 성 사람들을 서쪽으로 끌고 갔다. 칠만 명을 줄줄이 엮어서. 남은 건 재와, 언덕 위 문 열린 돌 사당 하나다.

blocks.html: Under the chain mail sits a girl in red silk gone the colour of rust. A lamp beside her. She has kept it lit for three months on what the soldiers left behind.
blocks.ko: 쇠사슬 갑옷 아래, 녹슨 빛이 된 붉은 비단의 처녀 하나가 앉아 있다. 곁에 등잔이 있다. 병사들이 버리고 간 것으로 석 달째 불을 지켜 왔다.

en: You’re not him either.
Who?

lines: 내 신랑이요. 다른 사람들은 다 서쪽으로 갔어요. 황제가 나는 그분 거라고 해서 나만 두고 갔어요.
…그분이 누군지 아무도 안 알려 줬어요. 그냥 나를 줬어요.
en: My husband. Everybody else went west. The emperor said I belonged to him, so they left me here.
…Nobody ever told me who he is. They just gave me to him.

lines: …하. 좀 비켜 앉아. 얘기가 길어. 신 하나가 강물 속 계집애를 내려다본 데서 시작하지.
en: Nobody told you.
…Ha. Move over. It’s a long one. It starts with a god looking down at a girl in a river.

blocks.html: Who was the Holy King, and why does Goguryeo give him brides? Seven hundred years back, the sun looked down…!
blocks.ko: 성왕은 누구였고, 고구려는 왜 그에게 신부를 바치는가? 칠백 년 전, 해가 내려다보았다…!

logline.en: Every day the sun crosses the sky on the same road. Today he looks down.
logline.ko: 해는 날마다 같은 길로 하늘을 건넌다. 오늘, 그가 내려다본다.

Poster key art at the misty pond of Gonyeon: King Geumwa rests his forehead against the old brown horse that found him, the boulder at the water's edge behind them
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; no title, no lettering. Dusk at the reed-ringed pond of Gonyeon on the Buyeo plain: still black water, mist, one great grey boulder at the water's edge. Poster composition: the king and the horse fill the frame together as one bold silhouette on the right two-thirds, seen from a low angle at the water line. INTERACTION: King Geumwa, gold crown and red-burgundy court robe, stands pressed against the old chocolate-brown steppe horse Gonyeon, his forehead resting on the horse's broad forehead, eyes closed, one ringed hand cupping its cheek under the shaggy forelock; the horse leans into him with its eyes half shut, breath steaming between them — an old man and the animal that found him under a stone. The boulder looms behind them on the left, reflected in the pond. Above, half the frame is a splashed-ink storm sky with one break of low gold sunset; that gold light (#a89a72) rakes in from the left and catches the crown, the king's cheek, the horse's mane and the gold frog charm on its halter; the rest falls into ink-black and indigo. Reeds as dark dry-brush strokes in the near foreground. Tiny far off, the timber palisade of Buyeo dissolving in mist. CANON — KING GEUMWA — FACE and garments from attached /ch_geumwa.png (face only; invent a new pose). #a89a72 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | GONYEON (곤연, geumwa's brown horse, guardian of Buyeo) — attached board /obj_gonyeon.png: Stocky, powerful northern steppe horse — deep-bodied and shorter-legged than a war horse, thick crested neck, round barrel, heavy quarters, broad forehead, large kind dark eyes; coat an even deep CHOCOLATE BROWN (not red bay, not black) with a lighter mealy tan muzzle; THICK SHAGGY dark-brown mane falling both sides, long full tail nearly to the ground; plain old leather halter with one small gold frog charm at the brow band — match the board. Old, patient and wise. Stopped at the pond of Gonyeon and wept at a boulder until King Haeburu had it turned over, and the gold-frog child Geumwa was underneath; it has walked beside him ever since. | HORSE ANATOMY is a centrepiece: the whole horse body reads clearly and beautifully — arched neck, deep chest, sloping shoulder, round haunch, clean long legs in a correct gait, every muscle modelled by the one hard key with a bright edge along the topline and deep shadow under the belly; the horse is never cropped into a blob, never hidden behind dust, never stiff like a toy; mane and tail as flowing painted strokes; the coat colour exactly as the board. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS are a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST room (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt) painted in that same wash-and-glaze: a warm umber-to-black ground, walls, timber, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft with soft sfumato falloff — the webtoon figures are set INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.alt: Five dragons pull Haemosu’s chariot across the noon sky
images.prompt: Ink painting of the myth. Five dragons in one yoke pull a small chariot in a great arc across the sky; Haemosu stands in it, laughing; the dragons are huge black coils with flying-white whiskers; the Amnok river is a thin pale line far below. ONE device: the dragon arc across the sky. MYTH INK — this beat is myth, not history, so it is painted as a STRIKING Korean ink painting (sumukhwa), not the house colour style. Joseon sumi ink on raw hanji paper with EXTREME LIGHT AGAINST DARK: huge saturated masses of black ink set against blinding bare paper; light is always the unpainted paper itself, never painted white; almost no mid-grey; hard edges where light meets dark, wet bleeding edges everywhere else. Splashed ink (pomuk), dry-brush flying white, ink spatter, mist left as untouched paper. Monumental emptiness and ONE graphic device carrying the frame; a dramatic angle (worm’s-eye, bird’s-eye, dutch). Gods, giants, beasts and wonders may fill the frame; mortals stay small inside the wonder. Figures in confident calligraphic brush line; named faces match the attached portraits, translated into a few ink strokes. Black ink and paper only, except at most ONE small translucent wash of a single colour on the one symbolic object the scene names. Not photoreal, not webtoon shading, not watercolor landscape, not oil, no glow, no halo. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. No text, no calligraphy, no seal stamp, no watermark.

blocks.html: The sky is empty first. Then come five dragons in the yoke, gold, crimson, azure, jade and white, and behind them a small gold chariot cutting the noon on the run they make every day. From the ground it is a fleck and a wheel, nothing a bather could call a face. The driver stands in it the way a man stands in a doorway he owns, one palm on the rail, laughing at nothing in particular.
blocks.ko: 하늘이 먼저 비어 있다. 그러고 멍에를 멘 용 다섯이 온다. 금빛, 진홍, 푸른빛, 비취, 흰빛. 그 뒤로 작은 금 수레가 매일 하는 그 운행으로 한낮을 가른다. 땅에서 보면 금빛 점 하나와 바퀴 하나, 목욕하는 사람이 얼굴이라 부를 만한 것은 없다. 몰이꾼은 제 문간에 선 사내처럼 수레에 서서, 난간에 손바닥을 얹고, 딱히 누구한테랄 것 없이 웃는다.

blocks.html: Dawn, noon, dusk, night, always the same route. Below, the Amnok is a line he is not supposed to break: wet stone, morning shallows with no boat in them, rocks that are only rocks.
blocks.ko: 새벽, 한낮, 해질녘, 밤, 늘 같은 길이다. 아래로 압록은 그가 넘으면 안 되는 선이다. 젖은 돌, 배 한 척 없는 아침 여울, 그냥 바위일 뿐인 바위.

blocks.html: Every god’s road crosses it. Most of them keep going.
blocks.ko: 신들의 길은 모두 이 강을 건넌다. 대개는 그냥 지나간다.

blocks.html: Haemosu, god of the sun, has kept this hour since before the river had daughters. Today the Amnok flashes under the wheel. He looks down, and the hour breaks.
blocks.ko: 태양신 해모수는 강에 딸이 생기기 전부터 이 시각을 지켜 왔다. 오늘은 바퀴 아래로 압록이 번뜩인다. 그가 내려다보고, 시각이 깨진다.

blocks.caption: The sun god. Punctual since before the rivers, until this afternoon.
blocks.ko: 태양신. 강이 생기기 전부터 시간을 지켰다. 오늘 오후까지는.

blocks.html: In the shallows, three river-daughters are bathing: Yuhwa and her two sisters. Wet hair down their backs, the river at their hips. Nobody dressed for heaven. He falls in love and in lust in the same glance.
blocks.ko: 얕은 물에서 강의 딸 셋이 멱을 감는다. 유화와 두 언니다. 젖은 머리칼은 등을 타고 흐르고, 강물은 허리까지 찼다. 아무도 하늘을 위해 옷을 차려입지 않았다. 그는 한눈에 사랑과 욕정에 동시에 빠진다.

blocks.caption: The river’s youngest daughter, a nymph of the Amnok. Heaven is about to ruin her afternoon, or make it.
blocks.ko: 강의 막내딸, 압록의 물의 요정. 하늘이 그녀의 오후를 망치려 한다. 아니면 만들어 주거나.

blocks.caption: The eldest river-daughter. First into the water, every time.
blocks.ko: 강의 맏딸. 물에 들어가는 건 언제나 그녀가 먼저다.

blocks.caption: The middle sister. She laughs first and dives second.
blocks.ko: 둘째. 먼저 웃고, 그다음에 뛰어든다.

blocks.html: Hwahye and Wihye have left their silk on the rocks. The eldest folded hers once; the middle did not bother. Yuhwa’s ice-blue is still on her shoulder, wet.
blocks.ko: 화혜와 위혜의 비단은 바위 위에 있다. 언니는 한 번 접어 두었고, 둘째는 귀찮아했다. 유화의 얼음빛은 아직 어깨에, 젖은 채로 있다.

blocks.html: Yuhwa kneels in the shallows with her hair in one fist like a dark rope and rinses the river out of it without hurrying. Heaven can wait on a rinse; she has decided that without saying it. With her back to the sky she looks over her shoulder, as if someone up there had said her name.
blocks.ko: 유화가 여울에 무릎을 꿇고, 검은 밧줄 같은 머리채를 한 손에 쥔 채 서두르지 않고 강물을 헹궈 낸다. 하늘은 헹굼쯤 기다려도 된다. 말은 안 했지만 그렇게 정했다. 하늘을 등진 채, 위에서 누가 이름이라도 부른 것처럼 어깨 너머로 돌아본다.

en: …Stop. Stop the chariot.
Those thighs…
The water…
Unni.
Go. I’m here.
…I was going to say don’t look up.
Hey. In.
Now. You hear me?

blocks.html: Hwahye dives first and does not look back. The eldest treats the sky like a timetable she will not miss.
blocks.ko: 화혜가 먼저 잠수하고 뒤를 안 본다. 언니는 하늘을 놓치면 안 되는 시간표처럼 다룬다.

en: Pfft— wait up.
You, seriously—
Whatever, I’m going—

blocks.html: Wihye laughs and follows, a splash that is mostly amusement.
blocks.ko: 위혜가 웃으며 따라간다. 물보라의 대부분이 재미다.

blocks.html: Two wakes cut the shallows and close. Yuhwa stays. She gets up off her knees, looks straight up as if she had been waiting for heaven to notice, and draws her wet hair over one shoulder.
blocks.ko: 물살 두 줄이 여울을 가르고 닫힌다. 유화는 남는다. 무릎을 펴고 일어나, 하늘이 알아채기를 기다리던 사람처럼 위를 똑바로 올려다보고, 젖은 머리를 한쪽 어깨로 넘긴다.

blocks.html: She draws the wet silk higher, one hip and then the other, and lets the sun finish looking.
blocks.ko: 젖은 비단을 더 끌어올린다. 한쪽 엉덩이, 그리고 다른 쪽. 해가 보기를 끝내게 둔다.

lines: 왜 안 숨어? 그렇게 쳐다보면… 나 내려간다.
en: Hey—
Wait. Hey. You.
Why aren’t you hiding? Look at me like that and I’m coming down.
Heaven looks down every day.
So today I’m supposed to blush?
…Come closer, if you want to see.
Into the water.
And decide… where your hands are going.
…Your name.
I need it… before I come down.
Or… I kiss you without one.
Come down first.
From the sky it’s an order.
At the water… I’ll hear it as a request.
Ask with your mouth… and I’ll answer with my name.

blocks.html: He forgets how to swallow, a god doing a mortal’s small panic. Then he grins, and the grin arrives before the plan. He leaves the rail and the hour in the same motion, the dragons keep the joke going without him, and the water takes him at the knee.
blocks.ko: 삼키는 법을 잊는다. 신이 인간의 작은 공황을 겪는다. 그러고 웃는데, 계획보다 웃음이 먼저 온다. 난간과 시각을 한 동작으로 떠나고, 용들은 그 없이 농담을 잇고, 물이 무릎에서 그를 받는다.

blocks.html: He wades close. She does not run. He stops where a stranger should stop. Then he doesn’t.
blocks.ko: 가까이 걸어 들어온다. 그녀는 도망가지 않는다. 낯선 사람이 설 자리에서 선다. 그러고 안 선다.

en: Why didn’t you run away?
Your sisters did.
…Didn’t see any reason.
The water’s cold. You’re warm. That’s all there is to it.
lines: 물은 차갑고, 당신은 따뜻하고. 그게 다예요.

en: Look straight at the sun
and you burn.
Oh, is that so?
Then I should blink.
It’ll burn your eyes out.
I’m not a lamp.
I like what I see.
I’m looking anyway. You came down.
Don’t make me say it twice.

blocks.html: He swallows. The grin survives it. Barely.
blocks.ko: 그가 삼킨다. 웃음은 산다. 간신히.

blocks.html: She tips her mouth and asks whether the sun likes what it sees, silk already losing the argument with the water.
blocks.ko: 입을 기울여 묻는다. 해는 보이는 게 좋으냐고. 비단은 이미 물과의 말다툼에서 지고 있다.

en: This way. The bank.
The sky has too many sisters.

blocks.html: He follows like the hour had been her idea.
blocks.ko: 시각이 그녀의 생각이었다는 듯이 따라간다.

blocks.html: The copper room rises on the bank like a kiln. He builds it the same afternoon, because the open sky has become too many witnesses.
blocks.ko: 구리 방이 강턱에 가마처럼 올라온다. 같은 날 오후 짓는다. 열린 하늘이 너무 많은 증인이 되어서.

lines: 구리에 기대면… 어디에 데었는지 구분 못 하실 거예요.
en: Copper gets hot in summer.
…You’ll know if you touch it.
My back, too.
If you press me to it… you won’t tell which burned you.
I know.
That’s why I can’t take my hands off you.
Or my mouth.
Then don’t.
Not while heaven is watching.
And while it watches… deeper.

blocks.html: She kisses him with river still on her mouth. The kiss tastes like the shallows. He makes a sound he will deny.
blocks.ko: 입에 강이 남은 채로 그를 입 맞춘다. 키스는 여울 맛이다. 그는 나중에 부인할 소리를 낸다.

blocks.html: Inside, the copper has kept the afternoon’s heat. She leans into it and does not look away from him. Gold lies across wet skin in a hard bar, and the ice-blue silk slips from one shoulder, then gives up the other.
blocks.ko: 안에서 구리는 오후의 열을 간직하고 있다. 그녀는 거기 기대어 그에게서 눈을 떼지 않는다. 젖은 살 위로 금빛이 단단한 띠처럼 눕고, 얼음빛 비단이 한쪽 어깨에서 흘러내리더니, 이윽고 다른 쪽도 내준다.

en: If you want it, say so.
I’m not asking twice.
Give me— all of it.
Don’t save any.

blocks.html: He puts her back to it anyway. The river-silk is gathered at her hip and her thighs close around a sun-god who has never learned to be gentle with an hour. She takes him in with the same wet hand that washed her hair for heaven, and when he is all the way inside her she laughs, as if this were what she had meant by looking.
blocks.ko: 그래도 그는 그녀의 등을 거기 댄다. 강의 비단이 허리께에 모이고, 시각을 살살 다룰 줄 모르는 태양신을 그녀의 허벅지가 감싼다. 하늘을 위해 머리를 감던 그 젖은 손으로 그를 이끌어 들이고, 그가 끝까지 들어오자, 올려다본 게 이거였다는 듯이 웃는다.

en: Haa— is heaven always this heavy?
More— against the copper— don’t stop—
I broke the hour.
I don’t care.
Your name— now—
Yuhwa— ah— it’s Yuhwa—
Stay— stay inside me—
All of it— the whole sun—

blocks.html: He takes her through the heat of the wall, gold on wet skin, and every stroke knocks a sound out of her that the river throws back. She comes first and loudly, looking up as if heaven were still watching. Then he spills into her, a god’s whole careless heat, and does not draw back, because she told him not to, and because the hour is already ruined.
blocks.ko: 벽의 열 속에서 그가 그녀를 안는다. 젖은 살 위에 금빛이 앉고, 한 번 움직일 때마다 그녀에게서 터져 나오는 소리를 강이 되던진다. 그녀가 먼저, 크게 끝에 닿는다. 하늘이 아직 보고 있는 것처럼 위를 올려다보며. 그러고 그가 그녀 안에 쏟는다. 신의 무심한 열 전부를. 그리고 물러나지 않는다. 그러지 말라고 했으니까. 시각은 이미 깨졌으니까.

blocks.html: The copper keeps the afternoon. Outside, the river goes on being a river.
blocks.ko: 구리가 오후를 간직한다. 밖에서는 강이 계속 강이다.

blocks.html: Up on the road, the dragons have hauled an empty chariot to dusk on their own. Half the world got its evening late. Heaven noticed.
blocks.ko: 하늘 길 위에선 용들이 빈 수레를 저희끼리 끌고 해 질 녘까지 갔다. 세상 절반이 저녁을 늦게 맞았다. 하늘이 알아챘다.

en: They’re calling.
I’m late. I’m never late.

lines: …내일 또 와요. 같은 시각에. 이번엔 내가 깨 줄게요.
en: Go, then.
…Come back tomorrow. Same hour. I’ll break it for you this time.

lines: 두 번은 안 내려 보내 줘. 해 떠 있는 동안은.
야. 그런 눈으로 보지 마. 방법 찾을게.
en: They won’t let me come down twice. Not while I’m up there.
Hey. Don’t look at me like that. I’ll find a way.

blocks.html: He goes up in a flash of copper. Heaven fines the sun the only way it can: while he is in the sky, he may not set foot on the earth. He may look. He may talk. That is all.
blocks.ko: 그는 구릿빛 섬광 속에 올라간다. 하늘이 해에게 내릴 수 있는 벌은 그것뿐이다. 하늘에 떠 있는 동안에는 땅을 밟지 못한다. 볼 수는 있다. 말할 수도 있다. 거기까지다.

blocks.label: Habek's Court
blocks.ko: 하백의 조정

blocks.html: The copper is still warm when the river notices. The Amnok keeps its own court: Habek, god of the river and father of three daughters, stands on the wet stones as if the current were a hall. Mist is the dais. He does not need a chair.
blocks.ko: 구리가 아직 따뜻할 때 강이 알아챈다. 압록에는 제 조정이 있다. 강의 신이자 세 딸의 아버지인 하백이 여울이 대청이라도 되는 듯 젖은 돌 위에 선다. 안개가 대좌다. 의자는 필요 없다.

blocks.caption: The Amnok’s river god. He keeps his borders the way kings do, and his daughters the same way.
blocks.ko: 압록의 강신. 국경을 지키듯 딸들도 지킨다.

en: Who stopped the chariot. Say a name.
lines: 수레를 멈춘 게 누구냐. 이름을 대라.

en: I… looked up.
I just— looked. That’s all it was.
You don’t sleep in my mist after that.
You smell like copper.
lines: 그 다음엔 내 안개에서 자지 못한다.

en: Go. The bank is closed.

blocks.html: Hwahye and Wihye do not argue the sentence. The eldest watches the current. The middle one watches the copper glow die. Neither looks at their father’s face.
blocks.ko: 화혜와 위혜는 판결을 논하지 않는다. 언니는 여울을 본다. 둘째는 죽어 가는 구리 빛을 본다. 둘 다 아버지 얼굴은 안 본다.

blocks.html: Habek kicks Yuhwa out with a look, not a foot. The bank understands.
blocks.ko: 하백이 유화를 내쫓는다. 발이 아니라 눈으로. 강턱이 알아듣는다.

blocks.html: The pavilion walkway does not catch her. Habek’s sleeve is already the closed door. She hits packed earth with ice-blue still wet from the copper.
blocks.ko: 누각 복도가 받아주지 않는다. 하백의 소매가 이미 닫힌 문이다. 구리가 덜 마른 얼음빛으로 다진 흙에 엎어진다.

blocks.html: For a while nobody comes. The mist that used to be a bed is just weather. She sits where the river can see her and does not look up.
blocks.ko: 한동안 아무도 안 온다. 침대였던 안개가 그냥 날씨다. 강이 보이는 자리에 앉아서, 올려다보지 않는다.
blocks.art: Episode break: side story S1 ends here.

blocks.html: The sky talks first. She hears him before she sees anything with paws.
blocks.ko: 하늘이 먼저 말한다. 발 달린 걸 보기 전에 그 목소리를 듣는다.

en: Hey.
Wait. Don’t sit in the dust.
Follow the fox.

blocks.html: The fox is already on the packed earth, pale gold-white, looking back once as if she might miss the joke. Yuhwa follows it south, barefoot, the ice-blue gone dull with dust: pine shade, a river-bend that is not the Amnok, a pass of bare stone where she is smaller than the ridge. The fox does not explain the map.
blocks.ko: 여우가 이미 다진 흙 위에 있다. 창백한 금빛 흰 털, 농담을 놓칠까 봐 한 번 돌아본다. 유화는 맨발로, 먼지에 탁해진 얼음빛으로 그 뒤를 따라 남쪽으로 간다. 소나무 그늘, 압록이 아닌 강굽이, 능선보다 그녀가 작아지는 벗은 돌 고개. 여우는 지도를 설명하지 않는다.

blocks.label: Buyeo
blocks.ko: 부여

blocks.html: From the river, Buyeo’s capital is a palisade of timber teeth and a hill of grey roofs. The studded doors open. King Geumwa, the gold-frog king, comes out to the yard himself.
blocks.ko: 강에서 보면 부여의 도읍은 나무 이빨 같은 목책과 잿빛 기와 언덕이다. 징 박힌 문이 열린다. 금개구리 왕 금와가 몸소 마당으로 나온다.

blocks.caption: The gold-frog king. Found under a rock, raised in a palace, kind to strays.
blocks.ko: 금개구리 임금. 바위 밑에서 발견되어 궁에서 자랐고, 떠돌이에게 너그럽다.

blocks.html: An old kingdom that takes in strays and keeps count.
blocks.ko: 떠돌이를 받아 주고, 셈은 해 두는 오래된 나라.

en: Come in. I’ve got a room free.
The yard can learn your name later.

blocks.html: A sun-shaft finds her where she kneels to wring the river out of her sleeve. When she crosses the yard at night it moves with her, a bar of gold keeping her sleeve.
blocks.ko: 해 한 줄기가, 소매에서 강을 짜내려 무릎 꿇은 그녀를 찾아낸다. 밤에 마당을 건너면 그 빛이 따라 움직인다. 소매를 지키는 금빛 막대.

blocks.html: Yuhwa’s ice-blue sleeve is the first roof the boy will remember, though he is not a boy yet.
blocks.ko: 유화의 얼음빛 소매가 첫 지붕이다. 아이는 그걸 기억할 것이다. 아직 아이가 아닌데.

blocks.html: In time Yuhwa lays a great egg. Geumwa has the egg taken from her before the court has agreed what a river-daughter is allowed to bear.
blocks.ko: 때가 되어 유화가 커다란 알을 낳는다. 금와가 알을 빼앗아 간다. 조정은 강의 딸이 무엇을 낳아도 되는지 아직 합의하지 못했다.

blocks.html: Dogs won't eat it. An axe won't split it. What on earth is inside Yuhwa's egg…?
blocks.ko: 개도 먹지 않는다. 도끼로도 쪼개지지 않는다. 유화의 알 속에는 대체 무엇이 들어 있는가…?

logline.en: Dogs won’t eat it. Hooves step around it. An axe won’t split it. Nobody in the hall wants to say what it is.
logline.ko: 개도 먹지 않는다. 말굽도 비켜 간다. 도끼로도 쪼개지지 않는다. 그게 무엇인지 궁 안의 누구도 말하고 싶어 하지 않는다.

Bird’s-eye over a wide black river: fish and turtles rise to form a curving bridge of shells; Jumong, clean-shaven, gallops across with three companions; on the far bank the pursuers’ horses rear at the water. ONE device: the curve of shells across the river. MYTH INK — this beat is myth, not history, so it is painted as a STRIKING Korean ink painting (sumukhwa), not the house colour style. Joseon sumi ink on raw hanji paper with EXTREME LIGHT AGAINST DARK: huge saturated masses of black ink set against blinding bare paper; light is always the unpainted paper itself, never painted white; almost no mid-grey; hard edges where light meets dark, wet bleeding edges everywhere else. Splashed ink (pomuk), dry-brush flying white, ink spatter, mist left as untouched paper. Monumental emptiness and ONE graphic device carrying the frame; a dramatic angle (worm’s-eye, bird’s-eye, dutch). Gods, giants, beasts and wonders may fill the frame; mortals stay small inside the wonder. Figures in confident calligraphic brush line; named faces match the attached portraits, translated into a few ink strokes. Black ink and paper only, except at most ONE small translucent wash of a single colour on the one symbolic object the scene names. Not photoreal, not webtoon shading, not watercolor landscape, not oil, no glow, no halo. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. No text, no calligraphy, no seal stamp, no watermark.
