blocks.label: The Egg
blocks.ko: 알

blocks.html: Buyeo tries very hard to get rid of the egg. The egg declines.
blocks.ko: 부여는 그 알을 치우려고 무진 애를 쓴다. 알은 사양한다.

blocks.html: Dogs and pigs will not eat it; the sty refuses the guest, and the ministers pretend that is a kind of answer. In the road, cattle and horses step around it, hooves knowing better than the hall. In the open field, birds cover it with their wings instead of pecking, and the yard goes quiet at that.
blocks.ko: 개와 돼지가 먹지 않는다. 돼지우리가 손님을 거절하고, 신하들은 그걸 대답인 척한다. 길에 버리면 소와 말이 피해서 간다. 발굽이 대청보다 낫다. 들에 두면 새들이 쪼지 않고 날개로 덮는다. 마당이 그걸 보고 조용해진다.

blocks.html: An axe is brought. The axe will not split the egg. The edge sings and the shell does not bother to crack.
blocks.ko: 도끼를 가져온다. 도끼로도 알이 안 깨진다. 날이 울고, 껍질은 갈라질 생각도 안 한다.

blocks.html: Someone winds up with both arms and hurls it off the palisade. It meets the stones and stays whole.
blocks.ko: 누군가 두 팔로 자세를 잡더니 목책 밖으로 내던진다. 알은 돌에 부딪히고도 멀쩡하다.

blocks.html: Yuhwa wraps it warm in her own sleeve and takes it back upstairs, and nobody reaches for the axe again.
blocks.ko: 유화가 제 소매로 따뜻하게 싼다. 다시 위층으로 가져간다. 다시 도끼에 손대는 사람이 없다.

blocks.html: Then the shell gives, and out comes a baby boy, wet and furious, already trying to focus. He looks up as if the room had owed him an explanation.
blocks.ko: 그러고 껍질이 열리고 사내아이가 나온다. 젖고, 화가 나 있고, 벌써 초점을 맞추려 한다. 방이 해명이라도 빚진 것처럼 올려다본다.

blocks.html: They name him Jumong, the good shot, because in those days people were named for what heaven had plainly already decided. He grows up with Geumwa’s sons, Daeso and Galsa.
blocks.ko: 그들은 아이를 주몽, 활 잘 쏘는 이라 부른다. 그 시절엔 하늘이 이미 정해 둔 것을 이름으로 붙였다. 아이는 금와의 아들 대소, 갈사와 함께 자란다.

blocks.html: They are boys first, three princes at one stake in one square, before anybody is an heir on purpose. They shoot with borrowed bows, too long in the arm.
blocks.ko: 처음에는 그냥 아이들이다. 마당 하나, 말뚝 하나에 왕자 셋. 누가 일부러 태자가 되기 전이다. 빌린 활로 쏜다. 팔보다 긴 활이다.

blocks.html: Jumong can find a fly’s wing with an arrow before the bow fits his arm.
blocks.ko: 팔에 활이 맞기도 전에, 주몽은 화살로 파리의 날개를 찾아낸다.

blocks.caption: The best archer in Buyeo. The princes have noticed.
blocks.ko: 부여에서 활을 제일 잘 쏘는 아이. 왕자들도 눈치챘다.

blocks.hanja: 骨表英奇。年甫七歲，嶷然異常，自作弓矢射之，百發百中。扶餘俗語，善射爲朱蒙，故以名云。
blocks.html: His frame and face were striking and strange. At seven he was already unlike other children; he made his own bow and arrows, and of a hundred shots, a hundred hit. In the Buyeo tongue a good archer is called jumong, and so they named him.
blocks.ko: 골격과 생김새가 빼어나고 기이하였다. 나이 겨우 일곱에 의젓함이 남달랐는데, 스스로 활과 화살을 만들어 쏘면 백 번 쏘아 백 번 맞혔다. 부여 말에 활 잘 쏘는 이를 주몽이라 하므로, 그렇게 이름 지었다고 한다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 13, Goguryeo Annals — King Dongmyeong

en: I’ll take the fly.

blocks.html: Daeso teaches the grip, then resents the hit. The lesson ends the moment the arrow is better than the teacher.
blocks.ko: 대소가 쥐는 법을 가르치고, 맞히면 분을 낸다. 화살이 스승보다 나아지는 순간 수업이 끝난다.

blocks.html: The yard hears the wood take it, a clean tick, and the praise does not arrive. Daeso keeps his hands on his own bow as if applause were a confession. Galsa looks at the dirt instead of the hit.
blocks.ko: 마당이 나무가 화살을 받는 소리를 듣는다. 깨끗한 딱 소리. 칭찬은 오지 않는다. 대소는 박수가 자백이라도 되는 듯 손을 제 활에 둔다. 갈사는 맞은 자리 대신 흙을 본다.

blocks.html: They sleep in a pile like dogs under one quilt, and in the morning the quilt has taken sides. Jumong steals the last millet and grins through it, which is worse than the theft.
blocks.ko: 개들처럼 이불 하나에 뭉쳐 자고, 아침이면 이불이 편을 든다. 주몽은 마지막 기장을 훔치고, 훔치면서 웃는다. 도둑질보다 그게 더 나쁘다.

blocks.html: Yuhwa watches from the hall door, ice-blue sleeve on the post, not stepping into the boys’ weather.
blocks.ko: 유화가 대청 문에서 본다. 기둥에 얼음빛 소매. 아이들 날씨 안으로 들어가지 않는다.

blocks.html: Only two come back talking from the stake. The third has already started a country in his head.
blocks.ko: 말하면서 돌아오는 건 둘뿐이다. 셋째는 이미 머릿속에서 나라를 시작했다.

blocks.label: The Mark-Stake
blocks.ko: 과녁 말뚝

blocks.html: Grown, they still shoot at the princes’ mark-stake. Daeso stands too close when Jumong’s arrow lands.
blocks.ko: 다 자라서도 왕자들은 과녁 말뚝에 쏜다. 주몽의 화살이 꽂힐 때 대소는 너무 가까이 서 있다.

blocks.caption: Buyeo’s crown prince. Good with a bow, until someone is better.
blocks.ko: 부여의 태자. 활을 잘 쏜다. 누가 더 잘 쏘기 전까지는.

lines: 먹여 주는 집보다 멀리 쏘지 마라.
en: Do not outshoot the house that feeds you.
Then put the mark farther.

blocks.caption: Geumwa’s younger son. He smiles at everything, for now.
blocks.ko: 금와의 둘째 아들. 아직은 무엇에든 웃는다.

en: If it lands, I meant to applaud.

blocks.html: Jumong keeps the grin because grinning is cheaper than asking why, and Daeso hates the price.
blocks.ko: 주몽은 웃음을 유지한다. 왜냐고 묻는 것보다 웃음이 싸서. 대소는 그 값을 싫어한다.

blocks.html: Jumong’s arranged marriage to Lady Ye is a hall’s solution: a wife, a lamp, a door that still opens onto Buyeo.
blocks.ko: 주몽의 정략혼은 대청의 해법이다. 아내, 등잔, 아직 부여로 열리는 문.

blocks.html: Lady Ye gets pregnant with their son Yuri while the yard is still pretending the foundling is a guest.
blocks.ko: 예씨부인이 아들 유리를 밴다. 마당은 아직 그 주워 온 아이를 손님인 척한다.

blocks.label: The Side Room
blocks.ko: 곁방

blocks.html: Geumwa will not take the heir’s counsel, so Daeso takes the ministers into a side room. Lamp low. If they write it down, the scandal arrives before the knife.
blocks.ko: 금와가 태자의 말을 받지 않아서, 대소가 신하들을 곁방으로 부른다. 등잔은 낮고. 적으면 칼보다 소문이 먼저 온다.

en: Do it before the next hunt.
Quiet is fine.

blocks.html: Geumwa answers his heir the way tired kings answer. He refuses the knife and gives the foundling a chore instead: Jumong is sent to the royal stables, which in Buyeo is where a hall keeps a prince it would rather not see at dinner.
blocks.ko: 금와는 지친 왕들이 답하는 식으로 맏아들에게 답한다. 칼은 거절하고, 주워 온 아이에게는 일거리를 준다. 주몽은 왕의 마구간으로 보내진다. 부여에서 마구간은, 저녁상에서 마주치고 싶지 않은 왕자를 두는 곳이다.

blocks.html: The stables come with three boys who smell worse than he does. Oi, who is always already packing. Mari, who asks why. Hyupbo, who carries the extra. By the end of the month they are his.
blocks.ko: 마구간에는 그보다 냄새 고약한 사내아이 셋이 딸려 있다. 늘 짐부터 싸 두는 오이. 왜냐고 묻는 마리. 남는 짐을 드는 협보. 달이 다 가기 전에 셋은 그의 사람이 된다.

blocks.label: The Stable
blocks.ko: 마구간

blocks.html: Yuhwa comes to the stable after the lamps are out, a river-daughter in a frog-king’s straw, and finds her son brushing the best horse in Buyeo as if he could apologise to it in advance.
blocks.ko: 등잔이 꺼진 뒤 유화가 마구간에 온다. 개구리 왕의 짚더미에 선 강의 딸. 아들은 부여에서 제일 좋은 말을 빗질하고 있다. 미리 사과라도 해 두려는 듯이.

en: This one, isn’t it?
The fast one.
…How’d you know?
I didn’t tell anyone.

lines: 너 이 녀석만 빗질을 오래 하잖아.
나중에 미안하다 하고, 배 터지게 먹이고.
en: You brush this one longer than the others.
I’ll give you a needle. Put it in his tongue.
Say sorry later, and feed him till he bursts.
Mother, you’re terrifying.
…For how many days?
Until Daeso’s done sharpening.

blocks.html: By the next moon the fastest horse in the yard looks like a rack of kindling with a mane, and the slow ones shine like lacquer. Geumwa walks the stalls, picks the fattest for himself, and tosses the thin one to the foundling with a joke about how well they match. Daeso laughs loudest, which is a pity, because he is the one man in Buyeo who should have looked twice.
blocks.ko: 다음 달이 되자 마구간에서 제일 빠른 말은 갈기 달린 장작더미가 되어 있고, 느린 말들은 옻칠한 듯 번들거린다. 금와는 마구간을 돌며 제일 살찐 말을 자기 몫으로 고르고, 여윈 말은 주워 온 아이에게 던져 준다. 둘이 참 닮았다는 농담과 함께. 대소가 제일 크게 웃는다. 안됐다. 부여에서 두 번 쳐다봤어야 할 사람은 그 하나뿐이었는데.

lines: 둘 다 내 밥을 먹고도 마르는구나.
en: Suits you.
You both eat my rice and still stay thin.
Thank you, Majesty.
I’ll take good care of him.

blocks.html: He pulls the needle out that night. The horse eats until dawn.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 그는 바늘을 뽑는다. 말은 새벽까지 먹는다.

blocks.label: The Knife
blocks.ko: 칼

blocks.html: Before the next hunt, a knife comes through the dark of his room. Lady Ye’s lamp is still lit, so the shadow moves on the wall before the man does. Jumong rolls. The blade goes into the quilt up to the hilt.
blocks.ko: 다음 사냥이 오기 전, 어둠 속에서 칼 하나가 그의 방으로 들어온다. 예씨 부인의 등잔이 아직 켜져 있어, 사내보다 그림자가 먼저 벽 위에서 움직인다. 주몽이 구른다. 칼날이 손잡이까지 이불에 박힌다.

blocks.html: The man runs. He wears a palace sleeve, and he runs toward Daeso’s end of the hall.
blocks.ko: 사내는 달아난다. 궁의 소매를 입었고, 대소의 처소 쪽으로 달린다.

blocks.caption: A Buyeo girl with a steady hand and a long memory.
blocks.ko: 손이 야무지고 기억이 긴 부여의 처녀.

en: Leave Buyeo. Tonight.
I’ll keep the lamp.

blocks.html: He takes his sword down from the wall and breaks it across the seven-sided stone under the pine pillar. It takes two tries. He is not a swordsman.
blocks.ko: 그는 벽에서 칼을 내려, 소나무 기둥 밑 일곱 모 주춧돌에 대고 꺾는다. 두 번 만에 부러진다. 그는 칼잡이가 아니다.

lines: 반은 여기 둬. 기둥 밑 틈에.
아들이면 말해 줘. 소나무 아래, 일곱 모 돌 위. 알아서 찾을 거야.
en: Half stays. In the crack, under the pillar.
If it’s a boy, tell him: under the pine, on the seven-sided stone. He’ll work it out.
And if it’s a girl?
Then she’ll work it out faster.
Leave the door half open.
So I know which way is still yours.
lines: 어느 쪽이 아직 네 건지 알게.

blocks.html: Night at the palisade. Iron studs, a red sleeve, and a wife who does not come out to wave.
blocks.ko: 목책의 밤. 쇠 못, 붉은 소매, 손 흔들러 나오지 않는 아내.

blocks.html: His friends Oi, Mari and Hyupbo take the hills with him. Behind them come the riders Daeso sent, less a hunt than a net, and under the pines it closes from above.
blocks.ko: 벗 오이, 마리, 협보가 그와 함께 산으로 든다. 뒤로 대소가 보낸 기병이 따라붙는다. 사냥이라기보다 그물이고, 소나무 아래에서 그물은 위에서부터 조여 온다.

blocks.caption: Buyeo behind him, Daeso’s riders behind that, and a river ahead with no bridge on it. Yet.
blocks.ko: 등 뒤엔 부여, 그 뒤엔 대소의 기병, 앞엔 다리 하나 없는 강. 아직은.

blocks.label: The Flight
blocks.ko: 달아남

blocks.html: They split in the pines before the river, four men and one horse between them, the one Geumwa thought was thin.
blocks.ko: 강 앞 소나무 숲에서 넷이 갈라진다. 사람은 넷, 말은 한 마리. 금와가 여위었다고 여긴 그 말이다.

en: We’ll take the ridge.
Find us when you still have a bow.

lines: 능선 길은 너희가 더 멀어. 강은 내가 혼자 건널게.
en: Take him.
Your road over the ridge is longer. I’ll do the river alone.
Are you crazy? He’s your horse.
Exactly. Fatten him up for me.
…I’ll come find you.

blocks.html: He runs until the pines smear. Behind him the net is spears in the dark, points only, no faces he is allowed to know.
blocks.ko: 소나무가 번질 때까지 뛴다. 뒤에서 그물은 어둠 속의 창이다. 날만 있고, 알아도 되는 얼굴은 없다.

blocks.html: Something keeps pace with him above the trees, black on black, going from branch to branch without seeming to hurry. A crow. He is too frightened to count its legs.
blocks.ko: 나무 위로 무언가가 그와 나란히 간다. 검은 위의 검은 것, 서두르는 기색도 없이 가지에서 가지로. 까마귀다. 다리를 셀 정신이 그에게는 없다.

blocks.html: Jumong reaches the water alone, his death already written down for that day. No ford. No boat. The friends are a ridge away, on purpose.
blocks.ko: 주몽이 홀로 물에 닿는다. 그날 죽기로 이미 적혀 있는 목숨이다. 여울도 배도 없다. 벗들은 일부러 능선 하나 떨어져 있다.

blocks.html: Haewonmek, the reaper who collects each day’s dead, is already in the air. He skims the river toward him. Black hat, black silk, mouth bound shut. Jumong doesn’t see him. He’s looking at the water and the rain.
blocks.ko: 그날의 죽은 자를 거두는 저승사자 해원맥이 벌써 공중에 떠 있다. 그는 강물 위를 스치듯 날아 그에게 다가온다. 검은 갓, 검은 비단, 꽁꽁 묶인 입. 주몽은 그를 보지 못한다. 그는 물과 빗줄기만 보고 있다.

blocks.caption: A fetch of the underworld. Black hat, black silk, and a mouth bound shut so he can’t haggle.
blocks.ko: 저승의 차사. 검은 갓, 검은 비단, 흥정 못 하게 묶인 입.

blocks.html: A root takes his foot. He goes down on the wet stones, pine needles in his mouth, the bow a pace off as if it had been the first thing taken. Haewonmek crouches over him to collect what is owed, and the blow is already coming down.
blocks.ko: 뿌리가 발을 잡는다. 젖은 돌 위로 넘어지고, 입에는 솔잎, 활은 먼저 빼앗긴 것처럼 한 걸음 떨어져 있다. 해원맥이 거둘 것을 거두러 그 위에 엎드리고, 일격은 이미 내려오고 있다.

blocks.html: The cloak arrives before the face. Rain fills it. A hand closes on Haewonmek’s wrist from behind, and the strike simply stops — the way an elder stops a sleeve that has gone too far.
blocks.ko: 망토가 얼굴보다 먼저 온다. 비가 그것을 채운다. 뒤에서 손이 해원맥의 손목을 잡고, 일격은 그냥 멈춘다 — 너무 멀리 간 소매를 맏이가 멈추듯.
blocks.art: Episode break: side story S2 ends here.

blocks.html: Jumong’s cheek is in the mud. Haewonmek looks back. Behind him, in a dark hood, the sun god is holding his wrist and laughing, as if the night had grabbed the wrong man. The night is Haewonmek’s road. The joke is Haemosu’s.
blocks.ko: 주몽의 뺨은 진흙에 있다. 해원맥이 돌아본다. 그 뒤에서 검은 두건을 쓴 태양신이 그의 손목을 잡은 채 웃고 있다. 밤이 사람을 잘못 집었다는 듯이. 밤은 해원맥의 길이다. 농담은 해모수의 것이다.

en: Haemosu…
The night is not your domain…!

lines: 바다를 건너다 네가 오는 소리가 들리더군.
en: Heh…
Do you really think the sun disappears at night?
I was just crossing the ocean when I heard you coming over.
This man is fated to die today…
You are not to interfere with Yumla’s domain…!

lines: 넌 내 아우고, 이 일 맡은 지 이레도 안 됐지. 살살 해 줄게.
염라가 할 말 있으면, 직접 와서 보라 해라.
en: Hey, Haewonmek.
You’re my little brother and it’s your first week. I’ll go easy on you.
But this is my son.
And he still hasn’t completed his purpose in this world.
And besides… I outrank you.
If Yumla has any complaints, tell him to come see me himself.

blocks.html: He puts Haewonmek aside and leans to Jumong’s ear. Jumong cannot see him, only the night, the river, a warmth that should not be there. The idea arrives as breath.
blocks.ko: 해원맥을 옆으로 밀어 두고 주몽의 귀에 입을 댄다. 주몽은 그를 보지 못한다. 밤과 강과, 거기 있어서는 안 될 온기뿐. 생각은 숨결로 온다.

blocks.label: The Crossing
blocks.ko: 건넌 강

lines: 나는 태양의 주인, 위대한 해모수의 아들이다!
en: I am the son of the great Haemosu, the lord of the sun!
Make way for me!

blocks.html: The river answers. Tortoises rise and lock shell to shell in the dark. Jumong runs the wet backs as if they had always been a road.
blocks.ko: 강이 응답한다. 자라들이 떠올라 어둠 속에서 등딱지를 잇는다. 주몽이 젖은 등 위를 달린다 — 원래부터 길이었던 것처럼.

blocks.html: Of old, the founder King Chumo laid the foundations. He came out of North Buyeo, son of the Heavenly Emperor; his mother was Habek’s daughter; he broke the egg and came down into the world… The king came to the ford and said: “I am King Chumo, son of August Heaven, whose mother is Habek’s daughter. Link the reeds and float the turtles for me.” At his voice the reeds linked and the turtles floated, and so he crossed.
blocks.ko: 옛날 시조 추모왕이 나라의 터를 열었다. 북부여에서 나왔으니 천제의 아들이요, 어머니는 하백의 딸로, 알을 깨고 세상에 내려왔다… 왕이 나루에 이르러 말하였다. “나는 황천의 아들이요, 어머니는 하백의 딸인 추모왕이다. 나를 위하여 갈대를 잇고 거북을 띄워라.” 그 소리에 응하여 곧 갈대가 이어지고 거북이 떠오르니, 그제야 건넜다.
blocks.hanja: 惟昔始祖，鄒牟王之創基也。出自北夫餘，天帝之子，母河伯女郎，剖卵降世…王臨津言曰：「我是皇天之子，母河伯女郎，鄒牟王，為我連葭浮龜。」應聲，即為連葭浮龜，然後造渡。
blocks.source: Gwanggaeto Stele (廣開土王碑) face I, opening lines (414)

blocks.html: The two brothers stay on the near stones. Jumong is already a red speck on the far dark. Haemosu throws an arm across Haewonmek’s shoulder and laughs like the job is done. Haewonmek’s gat is still askew — the look of a clerk whose ledger just walked off.
blocks.ko: 두 형제는 가까운 쪽 돌에 남는다. 주몽은 이미 먼 어둠의 붉은 점이다. 해모수가 해원맥의 어깨에 팔을 걸치고, 일이 끝난 듯이 웃는다. 해원맥의 갓은 아직 비뚤다 — 명부가 제 발로 걸어 나간 서기의 얼굴.

en: He is still mortal…

lines: 허나 말이야… 사람은 누구나 이승에 온 까닭이 있다.
때가 되면, 그때는 네가 데려가게 두지.
en: Yes, of course.
But you know… every man comes into this world for a purpose.
He’s going to do great things.
When his time comes, I’ll let you take him.
Look at him go.
That's my boy.
You just robbed a ledger.
I borrowed a day.
I'll give it back.
Yumla isn’t going to like this…
blocks.art: Grumbling.

blocks.html: The bird that watches him is not an ordinary crow. On Goguryeo’s banners it will stand on three legs under a red sun, the samjoko, the bird that can look at the day without blinking.
blocks.ko: 그를 지켜보는 새는 여느 까마귀가 아니다. 훗날 고구려의 기에서 그 새는 붉은 해 아래 세 다리로 설 것이다. 삼족오, 해를 깜빡이지 않고 바라보는 새.

blocks.html: It is sitting on a rock on the far bank when he comes off the last shell, soaked, laughing like an idiot because he is alive. This time he counts.
blocks.ko: 마지막 등껍질에서 내려섰을 때 그것은 건너편 강가 바위에 앉아 있다. 그는 흠뻑 젖어서, 살아 있다는 게 우스워 바보처럼 웃고 있다. 이번에는 센다.

en: …One, two.
Three?
Hey. Why’ve you got three legs?

blocks.html: The crow looks at him without blinking, which is either rude or holy, then drops off the rock, flies ten paces into the pines, lands again, and looks back.
blocks.ko: 까마귀는 눈도 깜박이지 않고 그를 본다. 무례하거나 신령하거나 둘 중 하나다. 그러고는 바위에서 내려앉아 소나무 숲으로 열 걸음 날아가 다시 앉고, 돌아본다.

lines: ……너 나 곰한테 데려가면 진짜 구워 먹는다.
en: Follow you?
…If you’re leading me to a bear, I swear I’m roasting you.
Three legs. There’d be one to spare.

blocks.html: He follows it all afternoon, uphill, through pines that stop being Buyeo’s and start being nobody’s. It keeps ten paces ahead and never once lets him catch up. At dusk it lands on a stone lip above a dark opening in the hill and stays there, folded, like a doorman whose shift is over.
blocks.ko: 그는 오후 내내 그것을 따라 오르막을, 부여의 것이기를 그만두고 누구의 것도 아니게 된 소나무 숲을 간다. 까마귀는 늘 열 걸음 앞에 있고 한 번도 따라잡히지 않는다. 해 질 녘 그것은 산허리에 난 어두운 입구 위 돌턱에 내려앉아, 날개를 접고 그대로 있다. 교대를 마친 문지기처럼.

en: …Here?
Thanks. Really.
Can’t roast you now, can I.

blocks.html: Before the valley has a name for him he goes in, into stone and leaf-light and a country-shaped dark. In what will be called the Jumong cavern, he prays for a roof of his own.
blocks.ko: 골짜기가 그를 부를 이름을 갖기도 전에, 그는 그 안으로 들어간다. 돌과 잎빛과 나라 모양의 어둠. 훗날 국동대혈이라 불릴 그곳에서, 제 지붕 하나를 빈다.

blocks.html: A soaked exile, a hall full of spears, and a chieftain's daughter who won't look at him. Jumong's luck is about to get complicated…!
blocks.ko: 흠뻑 젖은 망명자, 창이 가득한 전각, 그리고 끝까지 그를 쳐다보지 않는 족장의 딸. 주몽의 운이 복잡해지기 시작한다…!

logline.en: He’s still wet from the river when the spears find him. The chieftain’s daughter is sharper than the spears.
logline.ko: 강물이 채 마르기도 전에 창끝이 그를 찾아낸다. 족장의 딸은 그 창보다 날카롭다.

images.alt: High crane: the five Jolbon chieftains sit on five animal hides around one fire in Tabal's hall — crow feathers, horse, cow, pig, dog
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE watercolor painting, minimal iconic 2:1 still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop with nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Night inside Tabal's timber hall at Jolbon: packed-earth floor, rough timber posts, a smoke hole in the dark roof, ONE low fire pit at the exact centre as the only light. High crane angle looking steeply down. ONE device: FIVE ANIMAL HIDES laid flat on the earth floor in a ring around the fire like five petals, each a different skin: a spread mat of glossy BLACK CROW FEATHERS; a chestnut HORSE hide with a strip of black mane; a brown-and-white COW hide; a bristly dark grey-black PIG hide; a shaggy pale grey-white DOG pelt. EXACTLY FIVE men, one sitting cross-legged on each hide, facing the fire, nobody else in the hall: Yeon Tabal on the crow feathers (red headband, black beard); the Horse Ka, heavy and bearded, dark robe with a red sash, on the horse hide; the Cow Ka, youngest, red headband and white feathers in his long hair, on the cow hide; the Pig Ka, thick and heavy, on the pig hide; the Dog Ka, the eldest, white beard and grey headband, on the dog pelt. FACES ONLY from the attached chieftain portraits: IGNORE the tiger pelts and bear heads drawn on the portraits — nobody wears a tiger or bear skin; they wear plain hemp and leather tunics, wrapped forearms and their headbands, and the only animal skins in the frame are the five hides on the floor. Unstrung bows lie flat beside them. They lean in and argue — one stabbing a finger at the dirt, one with arms folded, one laughing, one weighing with his palms — not posing. Ember-orange firelight as the one hard key from below, faces carved out of total darkness, the five men's long shadows thrown outward across the floor like spokes, smoke rising into black. images.prompt: Minimal iconic 2:1 still composed like a symbolic old-master history painting — the LAID-BACK, CHARMING KING AND THE DOTING, HOT-BLOODED, CLINGY TSUNDERE QUEEN. INTIMATE CLOSE-UP, faces fill the frame: Sosuno (high topknot with gold binyeo, thin red jewelled headband, dusty-rose hanbok, red wrist wraps) leans down over Jumong gripping the front of his red silk robe in both fists, blushing to the ears, glaring, teeth clenched. Jumong (red headband, clean-shaven, no crown) lies back on grain sacks with a lazy, delighted grin, hands open and relaxed. ONE DEVICE: her two fists on his chest and the hand-width gap between the faces. Hearth fire below rakes up across both; background black with ember bokeh and, deep in blur, the empty carved chair. Not kissing. Faces drawn, matching the attached portraits. No text. CANON — JUMONG — FACE and garments from attached /ch_dongmyung.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Lean archer; black hair half-bound under a knotted red headband with long tails; dark warm eyes, easy grin. CLEAN-SHAVEN before he is king — ignore the moustache and chin hair on his portrait. Dress: Red silk jeogori and po over a charcoal underlayer, rope-tied sash, wrapped forearms; bow across his back. Demeanor: Fun: grins, laughs, winks, easy eyes when Sosuno is mean; scared and a little stupid when it matters. Carry: Bow always (his object board); crow bow-knife at the belt. #e8563f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: facial hair before he is king; grim founder-statue face; sword-duel hero pose. | SOSUNO — FACE and garments from attached /ch_sosuno.png (face only; invent a new pose). Hair ornament matches attached /bn_sosuno.png when the head is visible. Look: Long straight black hair with a high topknot pinned by her gold binyeo, a thin red headband with a center jewel; sharp brows, cool appraising eyes. Dress: Dusty-rose hanbok over white sleeves, black wrap sash with red cords, red-wrapped wrists; bow and quiver on her back. Her hex is lamplight or a ground stamp — never gold robes. Demeanor: Sharp, quick, too much, then covering; a merchant's appraising glance. #e8a04a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: gold robes; meek downcast pose. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). Ordinary skin, NO red mark, NO glowing spot on the cheek, NO lamp painted on the face. Dusk light only. Clean manhwa line, cel shading, NOT photoreal. No text, no watermark, no halo, no glow.

No seal, no calligraphy, no signature, no red stamp, no second person, no facial hair detail.

blocks.label: The Scouts
blocks.ko: 척후

blocks.html: He is still wet from the river when the pines stop being empty. Two men in Yeon leather, spears too casual to be hunting, too careful to be lost. Jolbon scouts find him first. The bow is already in the pine needles. His hands are empty and shaking anyway.
blocks.ko: 강물기가 채 마르기 전에 소나무가 빈 곳이 아니게 된다. 연씨 가죽 두 사람, 사냥이라기엔 창이 너무 대충이고, 길 잃었다기엔 너무 조심스럽다. 졸본 척후가 먼저 찾는다. 활은 이미 솔잎 위. 손은 비었는데도 떤다.

blocks.html: Pine valleys, crow clans, and nobody waiting for a king.
blocks.ko: 소나무 골짜기, 까마귀 가문, 그리고 임금을 기다리는 이는 아무도 없다.

blocks.caption: From a borrowed stable to a valley of five roofs. The turtles handled the middle part.
blocks.ko: 빌린 마구간에서 지붕 다섯 개의 골짜기까지. 가운데 구간은 거북이들이 맡았다.

blocks.speaker: Scout
en: Stop— stop stop—
Bow—

blocks.speaker: Second scout
en: I got him I got—
Red. That’s not ours.
Down. It’s down.
Don’t— spear. Please.
Water—

blocks.speaker: Scout
en: Hands. Hands where I can see.
You deaf?
Yeah. Yeah look.
Just— I ran. River. That’s it.

blocks.speaker: Second scout
en: Name. Fast.
If Tabal has to come out here I’m blaming you.
lines: 타발 어른이 여기까지 나오면 너 탓이다.

en: Jumong.
Jumong. That’s— that’s the name.

blocks.html: They bring him in at dusk, not as a guest. One scout keeps looking back like the pines might grow more men. The valley opens under grey giwa. On the porch Yeon Tabal, chieftain of Jolbon, holds a cup he is not drinking.
blocks.ko: 해질녘에 그를 데려오지만 손님으로는 아니다. 척후 하나가 소나무에서 사람이 더 자라 나오기라도 할 것처럼 자꾸 뒤를 본다. 회색 기와 아래 골짜기가 열린다. 누대에는 졸본의 족장 연타발이 잔을 들고 있다. 마시지는 않는다.

blocks.label: Tabal’s Hall
blocks.ko: 연타발의 대청

blocks.html: Tabal walks him across the packed earth like a man showing a storeroom to a thief: grain porch, well, pine, five roofs that will not share a yard.
blocks.ko: 타발은 도둑에게 곳간을 보여 주듯 그를 데리고 다진 흙을 걷는다. 곡식 누대, 우물, 소나무, 마당을 나누지 않는 지붕 다섯.

blocks.caption: The chief of Jolbon. He shows thieves his storeroom on purpose.
blocks.ko: 졸본의 우두머리. 일부러 도둑에게 곳간을 보여 준다.

blocks.html: Inside, the hall is torches and a man who has not offered a mat. They put Jumong on his knees, packed earth in the weave of his red silk. He tries a grin. It does not survive the torches.
blocks.ko: 안으로 들어가면 대청은 횃불뿐이고, 자리를 내주지 않은 남자가 있다. 그들이 주몽을 무릎 꿇린다. 붉은 비단 결에 다진 흙이 밴다. 웃어 본다. 웃음은 횃불 앞에서 살아남지 못한다.

en: So who sent you.
Nobody sent me.
Your men grabbed me. I was just— here.
lines: 당신 사람들이 잡았어요. 그냥… 여기 있었어요.

en: I asked for a name.
Jumong.
That’s the name.
Your clothes don’t look like anything nearby.
Mohe? Khitan? Or the commandery?
lines: 네 옷은 이 근처 어디에도 안 닮았다.

blocks.html: At Tabal’s shoulder stands a woman in dusty-rose silk with a tally-stick in her hand. She has not looked at him once.
blocks.ko: 타발의 어깨 곁에 회분홍 비단 차림의 여자가 셈 막대를 쥐고 서 있다. 그를 한 번도 쳐다보지 않았다.

en: Pretty. Just—
Eyes. Front.
Count the dirt.
Not him.
Ow— I said it.

blocks.html: Tabal notices the bow. The wood is wrong for every hand in the room except one.
blocks.ko: 타발이 활을 알아본다. 이 방의 손들 중 하나를 빼고는 다 맞지 않는 나무.

blocks.html: They put Jumong’s bow in Tabal’s hands. He cannot pull the string, and the limb does not do him the courtesy of bending.
blocks.ko: 주몽의 활을 타발 손에 쥐여 준다. 시위를 당길 수가 없다. 몸통은 휠 예의도 없다.

en: Stop!
Hands off him.
…Whose son are you.
Son of Haemosu.
The bow knows. I didn’t ask it to.
lines: 활이 알아요. 제가 부탁한 건 아닌데.

blocks.html: He gives it back, and the wood stays as it was, which is worse than if it had snapped.
blocks.ko: 돌려준다. 나무는 원래대로 남는다. 부러진 것보다 그게 더 나쁘다.

en: Wife?
…One. In Buyeo. She told me to run.
So I ran.

blocks.html: At her father’s shoulder, the woman with the tally-stick makes a small mark she did not need to make.
blocks.ko: 아버지 어깨 옆에서, 셈대를 든 여자가 굳이 안 해도 될 금을 하나 긋는다.

en: You're a slave. My daughter's.
Shed. You hunt, you eat.
I do not want ash tracked into my hall.
lines: 내 마루에 재 끌어들이고 싶지 않다.

blocks.html: For a week Tabal uses him like a tool he has not paid for. West millet has a boar. Two cousins have a ditch and a knife each. Jumong hits both problems and sits in the dirt until someone tells him to stand. Tabal does not thank him. He just stops inventing work.
blocks.ko: 일주일 동안 연타발은 값을 안 매긴 연장처럼 그를 쓴다. 서쪽 조에 멧돼지. 사촌 둘은 도랑 하나와 칼 하나씩. 주몽은 둘 다 맞히고 일어서라는 말을 기다리듯 흙에 앉는다. 연타발은 고맙다는 말을 안 한다. 일만 안 만든다.

en: The millet likes you. I don’t.
Stay anyway.
Shed stays the shed.
Yes sir.
…The well’s nicer though.
Then go fetch. Out.
blocks.art: Episode break: side story S3 ends here.

blocks.label: The Hunt Muster
blocks.ko: 사냥 점고

blocks.html: Tabal’s daughter Sosuno, a widow, is already on the grain porch, running Jolbon before she has priced the exile: spear-count, west line, who eats, who rides. The yard answers her first and her father second.
blocks.ko: 연타발의 딸 소서노는 과부다. 그녀는 이미 곡식 누대에 있고, 망명객의 값을 매기기도 전에 졸본을 굴리고 있다. 창 점고, 서쪽 줄, 누가 먹고 누가 타는지. 마당은 아버지보다 그녀에게 먼저 대답한다.

blocks.caption: Tabal’s daughter. She has priced every man in the yard, and she has not finished with this one.
blocks.ko: 타발의 딸. 마당의 사내 값을 모두 매겼고, 이 사내는 아직 셈이 안 끝났다.

en: West line. Two short.
You. Spear. Not that one, the one that isn’t bent.
We leave at first light. If you’re late I leave you.
lines: 너. 창. 그거 말고, 안 휜 거.

blocks.speaker: A hunter
en: Yes—
Not yes. The count.
East, you’re overlapping. Split.
If I have to say it twice you sit the hunt out.
lines: 두 번 말하게 하면 사냥 빠져.

blocks.speaker: A hunter
en: —Split. Sorry.

blocks.html: Then the wet man is in the yard. Red silk. A back she has not counted. The yard goes quiet. Nobody dropped a spear. They just stopped being loud, because she did.
blocks.ko: 그때 젖은 사내가 마당에 있다. 붉은 비단. 세지 않은 등. 마당이 조용해진다. 창을 떨어뜨린 사람은 없다. 그녀가 먼저 입을 다물어서, 다들 따라 다물었을 뿐이다.

blocks.html: Something in her goes stupid while the chin stays up. His father’s name she heard in the hall and filed under nonsense. The line of a shoulder she cannot file anywhere. She will deny all of this to the millet.
blocks.ko: 턱은 그대로인데 그녀 안의 무언가가 바보가 된다. 그의 아버지 이름은 대청에서 듣고 헛소리로 치워 두었다. 어깨 선은 치워 둘 데가 없다. 이 모든 걸 기장한테는 부인할 것이다.

en: …Next.
I said next.
Don’t look at me. Look at the line.
Sosuno.
The line.
I have the line.
West is short two. I said that.
Sun’s in my eyes.

blocks.html: She starts calling him names because looking is worse. Big idiot is the one that sticks. He answers to it on the third day, cheerful, which makes it worse.
blocks.ko: 보기보다 싼 게 욕이라서 욕을 시작한다. 큰 바보가 남는다. 사흘째에 그가 그 이름으로 대답한다. 기분 좋게. 그게 더 싫다.

blocks.html: Soon the porch has a name for him too: Sosuno’s worker. She hates how easily it fits.
blocks.ko: 곧 누대도 그를 부르는 이름이 생긴다. 소서노의 일꾼. 그녀는 그게 너무 쉽게 맞아떨어지는 게 싫다.

en: That’s my worker.
Not yours to stare at.

blocks.html: One morning she dumps a bucket at his boots and does not bother pretending it slipped. He laughs. Then he says it like it is nothing.
blocks.ko: 어느 아침, 그녀는 그의 신발에 두레박을 쏟고 미끄러진 척도 하지 않는다. 그는 웃는다. 그러고는 아무것도 아닌 것처럼 말한다.

en: Watch it.
Or don’t. Drown. Whatever.
Hey.
You’re pretty when you’re mean.
Like— actually. Sorry. Not sorry.
Ha—!?
Who’s— pretty, what—
It’s not like that!!
Big idiot. Go. Go go—
lines: 이 큰 바보. 가. 가 가—

en: Going. Going.
Sleeve’s wet. Thanks.

blocks.html: He wrings the sleeve on the way to the shed. She waits until the yard is empty. Then she hides her whole face in the dusty-rose, red to the hairline, whispering idiot at nobody.
blocks.ko: 그는 헛간으로 가며 소매를 짠다. 마당이 빌 때까지 기다린다. 그제야 회분홍에 얼굴을 묻고, 머리끝까지 빨개진 채로, 없는 사람을 향해 바보라고 한다.

blocks.label: Upstairs
blocks.ko: 윗방

blocks.html: She does not stay in the yard. Chin still up, she takes the loft stairs two at a time like a woman with grain to count. The window faces the millet: his shirt off, red silk knotted at the hip, a back doing work. Whose son he is can wait. The muscles cannot.
blocks.ko: 마당에 남지 않는다. 턱은 든 채, 곡식 세러 가는 여자처럼 다락 계단을 두 칸씩 오른다. 창은 기장밭을 향한다. 저고리를 벗고, 붉은 비단을 허리에 묶은, 일하는 등. 누구 아들인지는 나중 문제다. 근육은 아니다.

blocks.html: Another afternoon. The dusty-rose is hiked, her thighs apart on the timber, one hand over her mouth and the other talking to the part of her that does not run a hunt: Little Sosuno.
blocks.ko: 또 다른 오후. 회분홍을 걷어 올리고 나무 바닥에 허벅지를 벌린 채, 한 손으로 입을 막고, 다른 손으로는 사냥을 돌리지 않는 쪽의 자신에게 말을 건다. 작은 소서노.

en: Idiot. Don’t grin in my head.
This is your fault, big idiot.
Little Sosuno… you’re hungry today aren’t you…
I don’t blame you…. mmm! look at him…
Those big muscles…. chest…. back….
Ah fuck dripping wet again…
Out hunting for meat…
I want you to fill me up with some of that meat….

blocks.html: Tabal is in the doorway of the yard, not the loft, and his voice still climbs the stairs.
blocks.ko: 타발이 마당 문간에 있다. 다락이 아니다. 목소리는 그래도 계단을 올라온다.

en: Sosuno!
West count. Now.
Don’t make me climb.

blocks.html: She freezes mid-breath. She smooths the dusty-rose, wipes her hands on her sleeve, and takes the stairs with her chin up. By the packed earth she is the chieftain’s eldest again.
blocks.ko: 숨이 중간에 멎는다. 회분홍을 쓸어내리고, 소매에 손을 닦고, 턱을 든 채 계단을 내려간다. 다진 흙에 닿을 즈음엔 다시 족장의 맏딸이다.

en: West is short two.
I counted. Twice.
Don’t send the exile. He’ll get lost.
He hit the boar.
You just don’t like his back.
I don’t like his anything.
Can we do the millet.

blocks.label: Other Daughters
blocks.ko: 다른 딸들

blocks.html: Word gets out that the exile hits what he aims at and looks like a sun when he works shirtless. Jolbon women find reasons to fetch water. Other chieftains mention daughters. Sosuno is suddenly everywhere those reasons are. She finds a flaw every time.
blocks.ko: 망명객이 겨눈 걸 맞히고, 저고리 벗으면 해처럼 보인다는 소문이 난다. 졸본 여자들이 물을 뜨러 온다. 다른 족장들이 딸 이야기를 꺼낸다. 소서노는 그 이유들이 있는 곳에 갑자기 있다. 매번 흠을 찾는다.

blocks.speaker: A chieftain
en: My girl can count.
Strong arms. Good hall.
He walks into buckets.
Can’t wring a sleeve. Talks to millet.
You’d be bored in a week. Big idiot. Next.
lines: 소매도 못 짜요. 조한테 말 걸어요.

blocks.html: He flirts at the wrong well, which is any well she can see from the porch, and the girls laugh too long at a sentence he did not finish.
blocks.ko: 그는 잘못된 우물에서 농을 한다. 누대에서 보이는 우물은 전부 잘못된 우물이다. 여자들은 그가 끝내지도 않은 말에 너무 오래 웃는다.

en: Hey big boy~
blocks.speaker: Teal

en: You’re— yeah. Funny. Too funny.
Don’t look at Sosuno. Look at me.
blocks.speaker: Teal

en: Don’t follow me.
Unless you are.
blocks.speaker: Teal

blocks.html: Teal hikes her hem at his well like a dare, the rope between them a bad idea, and leans hip first on the beam. The timber takes her weight. His ears take the rest.
blocks.ko: 청록이 그의 우물에서 내기라도 하듯 치맛단을 걷어 올린다. 둘 사이의 줄은 나쁜 생각이다. 엉덩이부터 들보에 기댄다. 무게는 나무가 받는다. 나머지는 그의 귀가 받는다.

blocks.html: A Sosuno-shaped shadow falls across the rim before her voice does. She is holding an empty bucket she does not need. The girls notice the shadow first, and the laugh dies.
blocks.ko: 목소리보다 소서노 모양의 그림자가 먼저 우물 테에 드리운다. 필요도 없는 빈 두레박을 들고 있다. 여자들이 그림자를 먼저 알아보고, 웃음이 죽는다.

en: Get. Off.
Get off my well.
This well’s ours.
Ditch is that way.
He doesn’t need help. He needs to work.
I was just—
You. Shed.
Don’t smile at them.
Don’t smile at me either.

blocks.html: He waits until the girls are gone. Then he does not go to the shed. He follows her to the grain post and says it like weather.
blocks.ko: 여자애들이 갈 때까지 기다린다. 그런데 헛간으로 안 간다. 곡식 기둥까지 따라와서, 날씨처럼 말한다.

en: So.
You keep chasing them off.
BECAUSE YOU WERE HANGING WITH THOSE OTHER BITCHES—
The well girls. That chieftain’s kid. You told her I talk to millet.
lines: 우물 애들. 그 족장 딸. 조한테 말 건다고 했지.

en: BECAUSE YOU DO—
WHO ASKED YOU—
I don’t— they’re in the WAY—
This is MY yard— MY well—
Okay. Okay.
You’re screaming.
I’m just asking why I can’t say hi.
lines: 인사하면 안 되는 이유만 물은 거야.

en: DON’T HI THEM.
DON’T HI ME.
BIG IDIOT. GET— get off my post—
lines: 이 큰 바보. 내— 내 기둥에서 떨어져—

blocks.html: She is screaming mad and pink to the hairline and everyone on the porch can hear the hide crack. He grins. That is worse. She leaves him the post. The well she keeps for tomorrow.
blocks.ko: 소리를 지르며 화가 났고 머리끝까지 분홍이고, 누대에 있는 사람 누구나 껍질이 깨지는 소리를 듣는다. 그는 웃는다. 그게 더 싫다. 기둥은 그에게 두고 간다. 우물은 내일을 위해 남겨 둔다.

blocks.label: The Well
blocks.ko: 우물

blocks.html: They keep meeting there as if the rim were a coincidence.
blocks.ko: 둘은 우물 테가 우연이라도 되는 듯 자꾸 거기서 만난다.

en: Rope’s being a villain.
Want me to—
Pull or don’t.
Talking doesn’t fill it.
Don’t look at my face.
…Sosuno.
There. Now pull.
Sosuno.
Cute name.
Your ears are pink.
Wind.
Don’t— look.
You’re so dumb. Pull.

blocks.html: He keeps ending up thirsty at the same hour. She keeps being there. On the fourth morning he stops pretending the rope is the problem and kisses her at the well-beam.
blocks.ko: 그는 같은 시각마다 목이 마르고, 그녀는 늘 거기 있다. 나흘째 아침, 그는 줄이 문제인 척을 그만두고 우물 들보 곁에서 그녀에게 입을 맞춘다.

blocks.html: She does not pull away first. When she turns, the dusty-rose is wet at the waist from the rope, and she looks back over her shoulder.
blocks.ko: 먼저 떼지 않는다. 돌아설 때 회분홍은 줄에 젖어 허리께가 축축하고, 그녀는 어깨 너머로 돌아본다.

en: You—
How dare you.
My father’s well—
I will kill you.
After. Move.
You kissed back.
Just saying.

blocks.html: He takes the full bucket and actually goes. She stands at the rim until he is a red speck at the shed. Then both hands over her face, furious, shaking.
blocks.ko: 그는 두레박을 들고 진짜 간다. 소서노는 그가 헛간 쪽 붉은 점이 될 때까지 테두리에 선다. 그제야 두 손으로 얼굴을 가린다. 화가 나고, 떤다.

blocks.html: She has been collecting him: a thread, a fletch, a length of well-rope, a scrap of his headband, folded into a cloth behind the grain-porch post. He finds it. He holds it up.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 그를 모아 왔다. 실 한 올, 깃 하나, 우물 새끼 한 토막, 그의 머리띠 조각. 곡식 누대 기둥 뒤 보자기에 접어 두었다. 그가 그걸 찾아낸다. 들어 올린다.

en: Hey.
Mice don’t fold headbands.
You hide these like a thief.

blocks.html: She goes so red the dusty-rose looks pale. She snatches and misses.
blocks.ko: 얼굴이 너무 달아 회분홍이 창백해 보인다. 뺏으려다 놓친다.

en: Those are— inventory.
Trash. I’ll burn them.
Don’t grin. If you grin I— give it—
You’re keeping a little me in a cloth.
Want it back so you can steal it again?
lines: 천 쪼가리에 나 하나 쟁여 놨네.

en: Keep— ha— keep you?
Go get kept somewhere else. Buyeo. Somebody’s keeping a lamp lit for you there, right? A wife with a lamp.
I’m not your— I’m not anybody’s spare bucket.
lines: 딴 데 가서 간직돼. 부여. 거기 등잔 켜 놓고 기다리는 사람 있잖아. 등잔 든 마누라.
난 니— 난 누구 여분 두레박 아니거든.

blocks.html: He stops smiling. Not angry. Done. He doesn’t lie about the lamp. He has never once lied to her, which is its own kind of problem. He unslings the bow and lays it on packed earth at the well-rim. Then he walks.
blocks.ko: 그는 웃음을 거둔다. 화난 게 아니다. 끝난 거다. 등잔 얘기에 거짓말하지 않는다. 그는 그녀에게 한 번도 거짓말을 한 적이 없고, 그게 또 문제다. 활을 풀어 우물 가장자리 다진 흙 위에 내려놓는다. 그리고 걷는다.

en: She told me to run. I ran.
I’m not gonna stay in your yard as something you hide behind a post.
Keep the bow. Tell the millet thanks.
lines: 그 사람이 도망치라 했고, 난 도망쳤어.
네 마당에서 기둥 뒤에 숨겨 두는 물건으로 살진 않을래.
활은 가져. 기장한테 고맙다고 전해 줘.

blocks.html: She does not call stay. She picks the bow up too fast: the bow her father could not bend. She bends it. One arrow. The timber well-beam beside his ear takes it. He stops.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 가지 말라고 부르지 않는다. 너무 서둘러 활을 집어 든다. 아버지도 당기지 못한 그 활이다. 그녀는 당긴다. 화살 하나. 그의 귀 옆 우물 들보에 박힌다. 그가 멈춘다.

en: Wait— wait wait—
Don’t. Don’t turn around.
If you look I can’t—

blocks.html: The confession comes like a tooth she has been biting since the porch. She talks to the dirt, the bow, anything but his mouth.
blocks.ko: 고백은 누대에서부터 깨물고 있던 이처럼 나온다. 흙에게, 활에게, 그의 입만 빼고 아무 데나 대고 말한다.

blocks.html: The bird pin comes out in her own fingers. Her hair falls in a sheet, and she sits in the dirt with the bow by her knee and talks into the ground, because his face is a luxury she has not paid for.
blocks.ko: 새 모양 비녀가 제 손가락 사이에서 빠져나온다. 머리가 막처럼 쏟아진다. 그녀는 활을 무릎 옆에 두고 흙바닥에 앉아 땅에 대고 말한다. 그의 얼굴은 아직 값을 치르지 않은 사치라서.

en: I don’t— I don’t like you.
Then I’m going.

blocks.html: Then he grins, smaller than the yard grin, asking.
blocks.ko: 그러고 웃는다. 마당에서 짓던 것보다 작은, 묻는 웃음이다.

en: I wasn’t going to say it.
I was gonna let you leave. Stupid. Fine.
Then you put the bow down and I—
I want you. There. Stay.
Don’t make me— I can’t twice.
Big idiot. Other ear. I swear.
lines: 두 번은 못 해. 시키지 마.
이 큰 바보. 다른 귀야. 진짜.

en: Hey. Hey I’m here.
Look. Still here.
Come here. You’re shaking.
blocks.art: Episode break: side story S4 ends here.

blocks.label: The Grain Room
blocks.ko: 곳간

blocks.html: They do not make it to a feast. The grain-room lamp is closer than pride.
blocks.ko: 잔치까지는 못 간다. 곡식방 등잔이 자존심보다 가깝다.

en: Hey.
Numbers later.
Your throat’s brighter than the lamp. Sorry. Not sorry.
lines: 목이 촛불보다 밝아. 미안. 안 미안.

en: I am not your wife yet.
Don’t— my hands.
Counting hand or me.
…Big idiot.
It’s not like that.
From the first look.
Buyeo was a hall’s idea. This one’s mine.
Give me your mouth… first.
Country later.
lines: 부여는 대청이 정해 준 거고. 이건 내가 고른 거야.

en: Then take it.
Don’t put a price on it.
I already lost the count.
Now come here before I take it back.

blocks.html: She hits his chest, once, not hard enough. Then she is on his mouth like she is angry at it.
blocks.ko: 그의 가슴을 한 번 친다. 세게는 아니다. 그다음엔 그 입이 밉기라도 한 듯 입에 달려든다.

blocks.html: The dusty-rose hiked, she braces against the sacks with her back to him, pulls him in by the collar and tells him she hates him in the same breath. Then she feels the weight of him, and the hate gets specific. Love and spite in one grip.
blocks.ko: 회분홍을 걷어 올리고, 그에게 등을 보인 채 가마니에 몸을 기댄다. 깃을 잡아 끌어당기면서 같은 숨에 밉다고 한다. 그다음 그의 무게를 느끼고, 미움이 구체적이 된다. 사랑과 미움이 한 손에.

en: It won’t— ah— fit—
Hate me then.
Harder.
God you’re— look at you.
Look— look at you— that chest— that back— those hips I watched from the loft—
That sound. Wet. Slap. That’s— that’s Little Sosuno, she’s— ah— dripping, she—
Take it. That sexy— man meat— I said take it and— destroy my tight little ass—
Beat her up. Beat up Little Sosuno till she’s just wet. Nothing left. That’s all she is—
lines: 봐— 봐봐— 그 가슴— 그 등— 그 엉덩이 다락에서 봤거든—
그 소리. 젖은. 철썩. 그게— 작은 소서노야, 얘가— 아— 흘리고, 얘가—
가져와. 그 섹시한— 그 고기— 가져와서— 내 꽉 끼는 엉덩이 박살내—
두들겨 패. 작은 소서노 패. 젖은 것만 남게. 아무것도 없게. 그게 얘야—

en: Little Sosuno.
Cute.
I’ve got both of you.
Don’t NAME her don’t— ah— she can hear— she likes it she likes it—
Deeper. The meat. All of it. Don’t you dare pull out—
AHH— DON’T STOP—
DUMB BIG IDIOT—
lines: 이름 부르지 마— 아— 듣거든— 좋아하거든 좋아하거든—
더 깊이. 그 고기. 다. 빼지 마—

blocks.html: He spends himself in her against the grain sacks, and she bites his shoulder so she will not have to hear herself. It does not help. The loft-voice is still in the room.
blocks.ko: 곡식 가마니에 기댄 채 그가 그녀 안에서 끝낸다. 그녀는 제 소리를 듣지 않으려고 그의 어깨를 문다. 소용없다. 다락의 목소리가 아직 방 안에 있다.

en: I didn’t— you didn’t hear destroy— I don’t talk like—
Little Sosuno isn’t— I don’t have a—
Forget it. Get out. Don’t look at me.
lines: 그런 말— 박살— 안 했어. 그렇게 말 안 하거든—

en: I heard.
You can talk like that.
It’s you. It’s hot. I’m keeping you. Both.

blocks.html: Later the lamp has burned down to a bead, and he is still holding on to her as if she were something that might spill.
blocks.ko: 나중에, 등잔은 구슬만 하게 타들어 가 있고, 그는 그녀가 쏟아지기라도 할 것처럼 아직 붙들고 있다.

en: Hey.
You’re beautiful.
Water. You want?

blocks.html: He goes for water. The door shuts. She lasts three breaths. Then she slides down the sacks with both palms over her mouth, scarlet, furious at a word he already left. Beautiful.
blocks.ko: 물을 뜨러 간다. 문이 닫힌다. 숨 세 번. 그다음 가마니를 타고 주저앉아 두 손으로 입을 막는다. 새빨개지고, 두고 간 그 단어들이 밉다. 예쁘다.

blocks.label: The Hundred Paces
blocks.ko: 백 보

en: The pine.
Hundred paces. Now.
Hit, he eats. Miss, I throw him.
I am not pleased. I am also not blind.

blocks.html: The pine stands a hundred paces off across packed earth. Sosuno grips the porch rail, knuckles white, chin up.
blocks.ko: 소나무는 다진 흙 건너 백 보 밖에 서 있다. 소서노는 누대 난간을 쥐고 있다. 손마디가 하얗고, 턱은 들려 있다.

blocks.html: The best men hit bark. Tabal hits the knot. Jumong splits Tabal’s arrow down the shaft, and the hall hears the wood cry.
blocks.ko: 장수들은 껍질을 맞힌다. 연타발은 옹이를 맞힌다. 주몽은 그 화살을 자루째 가르고, 대청이 나무 우는 소리를 듣는다.

en: …Yeah.
Still here.

blocks.html: Then Tabal laughs, short and unwilling.
blocks.ko: 그러자 타발이 웃는다. 짧게, 마지못해.

en: Eat.
Road can wait.
My daughter bent your bow, I hear. I couldn’t—
lines: 내 딸이 네 활을 당겼다더군. 난 못 했는데—

en: The bow is the bow.
Don’t.
I only— lost the count.
Big idiot. Stop smiling.
Ha.
River was supposed to take him. Daughter ran after it.
Sosuno. You picked. You keep. No feast.
Jumong. Hurt her, bow won’t save you.
Eat. Stay. Grumble like the rest of us.
lines: 강이 데려가는 줄 알았더니 딸이 쫓아가네.
소서노. 네가 골랐으면 네가 지켜. 잔치 없다.

blocks.html: Tabal sets a vermilion cord where a feast would have been, a short red line, two people who have already spent the night.
blocks.ko: 연타발이 주홍 끈을 놓는다. 잔치가 있었을 자리에. 짧은 붉은 선. 이미 밤을 보낸 두 사람.

blocks.label: Five Tribes
blocks.ko: 오부

blocks.html: Jolbon is five roofs that will not share a yard. Cousins cut cousins over a ditch, a ford, a winter store. Jumong watches it for a week and then says it in the hall, easy, the way he hauls sacks.
blocks.ko: 졸본은 마당을 안 나누는 지붕 다섯이다. 사촌이 사촌을 벤다. 도랑, 여울, 겨울 곳간 때문에. 주몽은 일주일을 보다가 대청에서 말한다. 가마니 나르듯, 쉽게.

en: You keep cutting each other.
A ditch is not a country.
I crossed a river on turtles. You fight over who owns the mud.
lines: 나는 자라 타고 강을 건넜소. 여기는 진흙 주인 싸움이오.

en: …Watch your mouth.
Those are my cousins.
They have been mine longer than you have been dry.
Then make them one hall.
Five fires, one roof.
Or keep the ditches. I can leave a bow on dirt again.
lines: 아니면 도랑이나 지키시오. 활은 또 흙에 둘 수 있소.

blocks.html: He does not conquer them. He walks the five yards with the same grin he used on Sosuno. At the worst ditch, two cousins stand with a knife each. Jumong climbs down between them and sits in the mud, bow unstrung.
blocks.ko: 그는 그들을 정복하지 않는다. 소서노에게 쓰던 그 웃음을 달고 다섯 마당을 돈다. 가장 고약한 도랑에는 사촌 둘이 칼을 하나씩 들고 서 있다. 주몽은 그 사이로 내려가 진흙에 주저앉는다. 활은 풀어 둔 채다.

blocks.speaker: Crow cousin
en: Out of the ditch, slave.
This is family.
Okay, okay. I’m just sitting.
Nice ditch. Who dug it?

blocks.speaker: Cliff cousin
en: …Our grandfathers. Together.

lines: 할아버지들은 삽 하나를 나눠 썼는데, 너넨 물웅덩이 하나를 못 나누네.
en: Huh. Together.
So they could share a shovel, and you two can’t share a puddle.

blocks.html: Nobody says anything for a while. Then the Crow cousin laughs, because the alternative is looking stupid, and the knives go back in the belts.
blocks.ko: 한동안 아무도 말이 없다. 그러다 까마귀 집 사촌이 웃음을 터뜨린다. 안 그러면 바보가 되니까. 칼이 허리띠로 돌아간다.

blocks.html: What he calls a talk, the valley will call the first summit of the five tribes. For once the smoke agrees.
blocks.ko: 그가 얘기라고 부른 것을, 골짜기는 다섯 부족의 첫 회의라고 부를 것이다. 이번만은 연기도 한쪽으로 오른다.

blocks.html: That week three men ride into Jolbon on one very fat horse.
blocks.ko: 그 주에 사내 셋이 아주 뚱뚱한 말 한 마리에 올라타고 졸본으로 들어온다.

en: You said fatten him up.
We fattened him up.
Okay. Okay. He’s beautiful.
…He can’t run anymore, can he.

lines: 못 뛰어. 못 올라. 먹기는 대청만큼 먹고.
너 찾느라 한 달 걸렸다. 우리 지붕은 어디야?
en: Can’t run. Can’t climb. Eats like a hall.
Took us a month to find you. Where’s our roof?

blocks.label: The First King
blocks.ko: 초대 왕

blocks.html: After the marriage the five tribes sit in Tabal’s hall and do the thing they hate more than a ditch: they agree. They vote Jumong first king. Nobody remembers him asking; the grin had already become a roof.
blocks.ko: 혼인 뒤에 다섯 부족이 연타발의 대청에 앉아 도랑보다 싫은 일을 한다. 합의다. 주몽을 첫 왕으로 뽑는다. 그가 청했다고 기억하는 사람은 없다. 그 웃음이 이미 지붕이 되어 있었다.

en: …Fine.
King, then.
If the ditches start again I will say I told you.
Eat. Stay. Wear it.
lines: 도랑이 다시 열리면 내가 그랬다고 한다.

en: I will.
Not for the chair.
For the roof.

blocks.html: Sosuno is the first queen of a country that still smells like millet. The cord is still new. The sacks have not learned to be tribute.
blocks.ko: 소서노는 아직 기장 냄새 나는 나라의 첫 왕비다. 끈은 아직 새것이다. 가마니는 조공을 아직 배우지 못했다.

blocks.label: Dawn in the Cavern
blocks.ko: 동굴의 새벽

blocks.html: Later he goes back to the mouth in the hill to pray, the way a man prays when a hall has named him and he still does not quite believe the name. At dawn the light breaks through.
blocks.ko: 얼마 뒤 그는 언덕의 굴 어귀로 돌아가 기도한다. 대청이 이름을 붙여 줬는데도 아직 그 이름을 다 믿지 못하는 사람의 기도. 새벽에 빛이 뚫고 들어온다.

en: Father!
If you’re listening— they made me king. Me. Of a whole valley. What am I supposed to do with it?
lines: 듣고 계시면… 저더러 왕을 하래요. 제가요. 골짜기 하나를요. 이걸 어떻게 해야 돼요?

blocks.html: Gold where the dark had been, and too tall for a lamp. Haemosu lets himself be seen at last: silver-white hair, the sun’s hour delayed on purpose, looking at his son the way he once looked down from a chariot rail.
blocks.ko: 어둠이던 자리에 금빛이 들고, 등잔이라기엔 너무 크다. 해모수가 마침내 모습을 드러낸다. 은빛 흰 머리, 일부러 늦춘 태양의 시각, 한때 수레 난간에서 내려다보던 눈으로 아들을 본다.

en: Jumong…. my son…
Father… are you even listening to me?
lines: 아버지... 제 말을 듣기는 하시는 거예요?

en: It is to build a new world.
Build a world of your own…. my son…!

blocks.html: He comes out of the cavern a king the valley already voted for, and a son who finally saw the face that had been the hour. This morning is only a roof, a grin, and a gold break in the stone.
blocks.ko: 골짜기가 이미 뽑은 왕으로, 시각이던 얼굴을 드디어 본 아들로, 동굴에서 나온다. 이 아침은 지붕과 웃음과, 돌 틈의 금빛뿐.

blocks.label: The Moon
blocks.ko: 달

blocks.html: Thirteen winters pass. Word comes from Buyeo. Yuhwa has stopped. The hall that took her in keeps the body. The door that opens next is not a mortal door.
blocks.ko: 열세 해 겨울이 지난다. 부여에서 소식이 온다. 유화가 멈췄다. 그녀를 거둔 대청이 몸을 지킨다. 다음에 열리는 문은 사람 문이 아니다.

blocks.html: Heat in a room that had gone cold. Gold where the lamp had failed. Haemosu is simply there — chariot left in the yard like a horse someone could not bear to stable.
blocks.ko: 식은 방에 열기가 든다. 등잔이 죽은 자리에 금빛. 해모수가 그냥 있다 — 마당에 세워 둔 수레는, 차마 외양간에 넣지 못한 말처럼.

en: Yuhwa.
I didn’t give this to my little brother.
Your hand.
You’re late.
The copper room… stayed warm. Even when you weren’t in it.

lines: 빈 자리가 하나 있다. 내가 지는 쪽에.
en: That time I came down.
This time you come up.
There’s an empty seat. On the side where I set.

lines: 그 빛… 여울에서 올려다보던 거랑은 다르네요.
en: That light… it isn’t the one I looked up at from the shallows.
It’s cold.
Still… across from you is fine.
Then come.
The chariot yields the night.

blocks.html: He does not ask a question. She takes the hand that once could not let go of her. Buyeo keeps a grave. Its records say a river-daughter died. The sky, which keeps poorer records, has a moon the next night.
blocks.ko: 그는 묻지 않는다. 한때 그녀를 놓지 못하던 그 손을, 유화가 잡는다. 부여는 무덤을 지킨다. 그곳 기록은 하백의 딸이 죽었다고 한다. 하늘은 기록을 덜 남기는 편이라, 이튿날 밤부터 달이 있다.

blocks.html: Jumong spends the rest of his life driving the western commanderies from the river valleys, and the country grows the way countries grow in old stories: one bowshot, one bride, one sworn brother at a time. Later halls will call him Dongmyung, Bright of the East. The walls just call him the Holy King.
blocks.ko: 주몽은 남은 생을 중원의 군현을 강가 골짜기에서 몰아내는 데 쓰고, 나라는 옛이야기 속 나라들이 자라는 방식으로 자란다. 화살 한 발, 신부 한 사람, 의형제 한 명씩. 훗날의 대청들은 그를 동명, 동쪽의 밝음이라 부를 것이다. 성벽들은 그냥 성왕이라 부른다.

blocks.label: Yodong
blocks.ko: 요동

blocks.html: In the burned shrine at Yodong, the lamp is down to a bead. Gesomun has told it badly, with his boots on, the way his family always tells it.
blocks.ko: 불탄 요동의 사당에서 등잔불은 콩알만 하게 줄었다. 개소문은 신발도 안 벗고 서툴게 얘기를 마쳤다. 그 집안이 늘 하던 식으로.

lines: 그럼 아무도 그 여자를 그분한테 준 게 아니네요.
소서노요. 그 여자가 골랐어요. 활까지 쐈고.
en: So nobody gave her to him.
Sosuno. She picked him. She shot at him.

lines: 쏘고 나서 시집갔지. 우리 집안 여자들이 그래.
타발은 그 활을 못 당겼어. 그거 가지고 칠백 년째 속 끓이는 중이야.
en: Shot at him, then married him. The women in my family are like that.
Tabal couldn’t bend that bow, you know. We’ve been sore about it for seven hundred years.

lines: 그럼 왜 그분한테 여자애들을 바쳐요? 왜 나예요?
en: Then why do they give him girls? Why me?

lines: 처음으로 골짜기 하나가 그한테 여자를 줬을 때, 그 골짜기가 나라가 됐거든. 성벽도 버텼고.
겁먹은 성들은 그 반쪽만 기억해. 고른 게 그 여자였다는 건 까먹고.
en: Because the first time a valley handed him a girl, the valley turned into a country, and the walls held.
Scared towns remember that half. They forget she did the picking.
…So I can pick.
Pick, then.

blocks.html: She takes off the bride’s crown and sets it on the floor under the chain mail, carefully, the way you put down something borrowed. Then she walks out into the ash, toward whatever is left of her mother’s street.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 신부의 관을 벗어 쇠사슬 갑옷 아래 바닥에 내려놓는다. 빌린 물건을 돌려놓듯 조심스럽게. 그러고는 재 속으로 걸어 나간다. 엄마가 살던 골목에 무엇이 남았든, 그쪽으로.

lines: 이 큰 바보 양반아. 당신 이름 걸고 저것들이 무슨 짓을 하는지 좀 보쇼.
en: …Holy King.
You big idiot. Look what they do in your name.

blocks.html: Back in Surabol, the queen is failing and the council must name who's next. It only takes one hand to lock the door…!
blocks.ko: 다시 서라벌. 여왕은 기울고, 화백은 다음 왕을 정해야 한다. 문을 잠그는 데는 손 하나면 충분하다…!

toneNote: Deliberation chambers and countdown nights — politics as a contact sport, with young flowers training at the edges.
title: The Chunchu Era

logline.en: Bidam takes the Council’s first chair and keeps his hand down alone against the queen’s cousin. The queen falls, the gate shuts, and on the first day the black headbands go up on the Radiance wall.
logline.ko: 비담은 화백의 첫 자리에 앉아, 홀로 여왕의 사촌에게 손을 내리지 않는다. 여왕이 쓰러지고 문이 닫히고, 첫째 날 명활성 성벽에 검은 머리띠가 오른다.

images.at: Nobody writes any of this down, which is why it needs saying.
images.alt: Ink genre painting after Shin Yun-bok: an empty floor of pale paper, Munhee tiny and kneeling at one edge knotting a travel bundle, one pink ribbon the only color
images.prompt: A Korean genre painting in the manner of Shin Yun-bok (Hyewon), fine elegant ink line with pale washes on aged hanji, wide horizontal album leaf. ICONIC MINIMAL LAYOUT: almost the whole leaf is empty pale paper standing for a bare wooden floor, one thin ink line for the edge of a folding screen at the far right. ONE device: a long low row of neatly tied travel bundles (bojagi cloth bundles) receding across the lower third like stepping stones, each one a quiet tan wash. At the near end, MUNHEE (face and garments from the attached portrait, a mature noblewoman) kneels, head bowed, pulling the knot of the last bundle tight with both hands, sleeves folded back; her dusty-pink #E07FA8 chima and the pink ribbon on the knot are the only colour. No other figures, no writing brush, no paper on the floor. One blank red seal square. PARODY RULES: always a hand-made PAINTING, never photoreal. Reproduce the original work’s composition, poses and signature look so it reads instantly as that exact work, with our characters swapped in. If the original is a painting, mural, print or scroll, match its medium, surface and brushwork. If the original is a photograph, film poster, album cover, anime frame or statue, PAINT it: a painterly illustration of that image with visible brushstrokes, simplified forms and anime-adjacent faces, NOT a photo, NOT photoreal skin or pores, NOT a 3D render, NOT a CGI statue. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portraits, recognizable but restyled into the medium; never the portrait’s standing clasped-hands stance. Character hex lives only as real color inside the work (pigment, cloth, light), never a glow aura, halo, emissive skin or neon outline. If a sword is visible it is the ring-pommel 환두대도 (small ring pommel at the heel of the fist, short grip, long straight blade, handle:blade 1:3), never a katana, never a tsuba. No readable text, no title, no credits, no legible inscriptions or signatures (red seal stamps only as blank red squares), no logos, no watermark.

images.at: Nothing moves unless the circle closes.
images.alt: Straight down onto the Harmony Council's round low table: seven men kneeling in a ring around one lamp
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE watercolor painting, minimal iconic 2:1 still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop with nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Night, a dark Silla palace hall in Surabol. Camera on a crane straight DOWN. ONE device: a ROUND LOW lacquered table on the floor, a perfect dark circle, with one small oil lamp and one lacquer voting cup at its exact centre. Seven men kneel on floor cushions in a closed ring around it: the Premier and six Councillors in silky Silla court robes with deep blue #2A5FB8 catching the lamplight, sleeves spread on the floorboards like petals. Bidam kneels with 108 prayer beads on his wrist; Yushin sits upright opposite him. No chairs, no rectangular table, no hwarang headbands. Background and foreground are a Renaissance tenebrist oil painting: umber-to-black floorboards and pillars modelled in glazed oil, the ring of figures pulled out of total darkness by the single lamp, sfumato into black at the frame edges; the webtoon figures are painted into that oil space in watercolor washes under the same key. CANON — BIDAM — FACE and garments from attached /ch_bidam_old.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Tall, handsome, clean-shaven; short slicked-back black hair; warm brown eyes, faint self-amused smile. Dress: Long white outer robe whose sleeves are embroidered with galloping horses, over a plum-magenta inner robe and white sash. Navy #141C2E lives in the room and on the beads, not on his clothes. Now: Older Sangdaedeung (stage portrait): grey at the temples, same smile. Demeanor: Buddhist: 108 beads wrapped on the wrist or rolling through his fingers, lotus seat, incense, a sutra under his breath; calm, ironic, never hurried. In anger the smile stays and the eyes go flat. #141C2E as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: headband; Confucian rank tablet; navy glow aura; dual swords. | KIM YUSHIN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_kim_yushin.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Tall, broad-shouldered, long black hair in a high topknot-ponytail with trailing Silla-blue cloth tails; level hard brows, deep-set eyes. Dress: Silla-blue po and trousers, plum-violet sash knotted at the waist, white inner collar, dark wrapped forearms. Off duty: plain blue po, no jewelry. Now: Marshal: full black beard and moustache; a blue ribbon in the topknot instead of the headband. Demeanor: Confucian: he STANDS — never sits in lotus. Weighs, counts, frowns at sums; tight jaw, rare dry half-smile. Grief shows as stillness, not tears. The most feared warrior in all of Samhan: a line goes quiet when the tall Silla helm and the white horse appear. Massive, deliberate, terrifying at a walk; by Hwangsan (65) heavier and slower than Gyebek but still the man armies are built around. #2A5FB8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: sitting in lotus or holding prayer beads; katana, tsuba or curved blade (ignore the sword drawn on his portrait); two swords at once; blue glow aura. | ALCHUN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_alchun.png (face only; invent a new pose). Demeanor: Silla's senior general and Yushin's peer; steady, dry, loyal to the throne over factions. #8fb3e0 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | PLACE Surabol (서라벌 (경주)) — attached board /pl_eastern_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Seorabeol palace: Silla giwa halls, packed-earth yards, timber verandas. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER canvas, composed like a Romanticist master painting. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is painted with European old-master technique — Renaissance and Baroque oil (Titian, Rembrandt, Tiepolo, Turner): visible broken-colour brushwork, skies scumbled from short loaded dabs, layered glazes in the darks, sfumato edges, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlights — over watercolor wet-in-wet blooms, pigment granulation and faint paper grain; edges of the frame dissolve into paint. BACKGROUND AND FOREGROUND are a high-contrast Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST OIL PAINTING in their own right (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt, late Titian): a warm umber-to-black ground; walls, timber, stone, drapery, tables and the dark foreground shapes modelled in glazed oil and pulled out of the darkness by the one candle, lamp or window, with soft sfumato falloff into black — the webtoon figures are set INTO that old-master oil space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is Romanticism (Delacroix, Géricault, Friedrich, Goya, Turner): heroic diagonal or pyramid composition, small figures against a sublime storm sky or vast field, extreme foreshortening (worm’s-eye from the dirt or straight down from above), one break in the clouds or one shaft as the key. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength (Caravaggio, Rembrandt, night-interior cinema): an extreme value range — inky blacks right beside small near-white highlights, almost no middle grey; 70–80% of the frame in deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo and black); ONE hard directional key (a lamp, a single cloud-break, a low sun shaft, firelight) carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

Black rafters above dissolving into darkness. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

He sits on a temple veranda at night, one knee up, looking aside, tired and a little wry. FACE matches the attached portrait; ignore portrait clothes. Navy #141C2E only as the color of the night wood, a small oil lamp is the key. Clean manhwa line, cel shading, NOT photoreal. No text, no watermark, no halo, no glowing eyes.
