blocks.label: DAY 2
blocks.ko: 둘째 날

blocks.html: Of course he comes. Yushin has never once refused Bidam a rematch. Between the camps a small pavilion goes up, open on every side, so nobody can say the other side hid archers. A low table. Tea already poured. A half moon in an empty sky. They meet the way they used to after sparring: gloves off, courtesy on.
blocks.ko: 물론 그는 온다. 유신은 비담의 재대결 청을 한 번도 거절한 적이 없다. 두 진영 사이에 사방이 트인 작은 정자가 선다. 어느 쪽도 상대가 궁수를 숨겼다고 말하지 못하게. 낮은 탁자 하나. 차는 이미 따라져 있다. 빈 하늘에 반달. 그들은 예전 대련이 끝난 뒤처럼 만난다. 장갑은 벗고, 예의는 갖추고.

lines: …육촌이 서라벌을 세울 때 — 이, 최, 정, 손, 배, 설.
en: Yushin.
Tea first.
…When the Six Elders raised Surabol — Lee, Choi, Jeong, Son, Bae, Seol.
Park came from an egg.
There was no Kim.
…And?

lines: 그리고 지금 이 성 안의 두 김 가문은 —
en: And now the two Kim houses inside this wall —
Surabol Kim, Alji Kim —
both imports.
I alone… am Six-Elder blood.

blocks.html: The tea cools between them. Neither man drinks enough to call it peace. Bidam smiles as if nothing ugly had been said — the same smile he wore when he crowned a woman king. Yushin sets his cup down unfinished.
blocks.ko: 차가 그 사이 식는다. 둘 다 평화라 부를 만큼은 마시지 않는다. 비담은 못된 말을 한 적 없는 것처럼 웃는다 — 여왕을 세울 때 쓰던 그 미소다. 유신은 잔을 비우지 않은 채 내려놓는다.

en: Alchun sends his regards. From the middle of the field.
He’s eating alone again.

lines: 그분은 늘 우리 둘 사이에서 먹었소.
en: He always did eat between us.

blocks.html: Three Hwarang. One princess. The yard remembers what the Council never wrote down.
blocks.ko: 화랑 셋. 공주 하나. 연무장은 화백이 끝내 적지 않은 것을 기억한다.

blocks.html: Bidam, Alchun, and Yushin — same Hwarang line, same bruised knuckles, same impossible orbit around Princess Dukman. They do not say the word love. The gyuku field says it for them, badly.
blocks.ko: 비담, 알천, 유신 — 같은 화랑 계보, 같은 멍든 손등, 덕만공주를 도는 같은 불가능한 궤도. 사랑이라는 말은 하지 않는다. 격구장이 대신 서툴게 말한다.

lines: 성골에 남자가 바닥나면, 가장 총명한 여자를 고르시오.
나는 어린 시절부터 덕만을 안다. 총명함에는 성별이 없다.
en: If the Sacred Bone runs out of men, pick the cleverest woman.
I have known Dukman since we were children. Cleverness is not a gender.
Well stood.
Tomorrow on the yard — the hundred-and-ninth is mine.

lines: 너희 둘은 점수 때문에 서로를 죽일 거다.
나는 가운데 있는 아이 때문에 나를 죽일 거다.
en: You two will kill each other over a score.
I will kill myself over the girl in the middle.
…That was a joke. File it as a joke.
If you three are finished deciding my life—
the ball is still on the field.

blocks.html: Even their names take sides. Bidam’s sounds like this soil and its sutras. Chunchu’s is a foreign classic. Any clerk across the sea could file it without asking. Nobody notices yet. Names are patient.
blocks.ko: 이름들조차 편을 든다. 비담의 이름은 이 땅과 그 경전의 소리가 난다. 춘추의 이름은 남의 나라 고전이다. 바다 건너 어느 서기라도 묻지 않고 철해 둘 수 있다. 아직은 아무도 눈치채지 못한다. 이름은 참을성이 많다.

lines: 너희 중 누가 사소한 이유로 저 아이를 울리면 — 얼굴로 점수를 맞추겠다.
en: Yushin.
Alchun.
If either of you ever makes her cry for a small reason — I will even the score on your face.

blocks.label: DAY 3
blocks.ko: 셋째 날

blocks.html: Arrows trade across the open ground between the camps. Each morning the palace blue comes up the road, the black headbands come down to meet it, and by dusk both are home again. Messengers lie; the Harmony Council discovers it can convene without deciding anything, which is its highest form. Chunchu’s clerks call the unanimity rule quaint. Bidam calls it ours. Inside the palace, the stewards count eight days of grain.
blocks.ko: 두 진영 사이 빈 땅으로 화살이 오간다. 아침마다 궁의 푸른 띠가 길을 올라오고, 검은 머리띠가 내려와 맞서고, 해 질 녘이면 둘 다 제자리로 돌아간다. 전령은 거짓말하고, 화백회의는 아무것도 결정하지 않고도 모일 수 있음을 발견한다. 그것이 회의의 최고 형태다. 춘추의 서기들은 만장일치 규칙을 예스럽다고 부른다. 비담은 우리 것이라고 부른다. 궁 안에서 집사들은 여드레 치 곡식을 센다.

lines: 어이. 어제 그 도랑이다. 내일도 그 도랑일 끼고.
둘 중 하나라도 진심이면 그때 깨워라.
en: Oi. Same ditch as yesterday. Same ditch tomorrow.
Wake me when one of you means it.

blocks.html: Third night. Same pavilion. Same half moon. Bidam has brought a map — not of the siege, of the roads west.
blocks.ko: 셋째 밤. 같은 정자. 같은 반달. 비담은 포위도가 아니라 — 서쪽 길 지도를 가져왔다.

lines: 삼한은 피로도, 마음으로도 식민지가 되고 있어.
유신 — 네 눈 색은 예쁘다. 서쪽에서 온 색이다.
…내가 먼저 일어섰을 때는, 그들이 나를 개화파라 불렀지.
en: Samhan is being colonized — in blood, and in the mind.
Tang sends institutions. India sends…
…through Queen Heo’s blood, sutras.
Yushin — your eyes are handsome. They are a western colour.
…When I stood first, they called me the liberal.

lines: 열다섯 해 전, 네가 그렇게 말했을 때 — 일어나라고 했소.
en: Gaya blood came from the west too.
I… stood up.
Fifteen winters past, when you spoke — you told me to stand.
That was when you were weak.
…A joke. Drink your tea.

blocks.html: On the wall Bidam looks west and remembers a cleaner war — Jade Gate Valley, when the enemy still had the courtesy to be foreign.
blocks.ko: 성벽 위에서 비담은 서쪽을 보며 더 깨끗했던 전쟁을 떠올린다 — 옥문곡, 적이 아직 외국인이라는 예의를 지키던 때.

blocks.html: Baekje sends five hundred armoured men to slip through a valley in the dark and bite a fortress from behind. In midwinter the toads in the palace pond start croaking, which toads do not do. The queen listens for one night. Then she sends steel instead of prayers.
blocks.ko: 백제가 갑옷 입은 오백 명을 보낸다. 어둠을 틈타 골짜기를 지나, 성 하나를 뒤에서 물어뜯으라고. 한겨울에 궁 연못의 두꺼비들이 울기 시작한다. 두꺼비는 겨울에 울지 않는다. 여왕은 하룻밤을 듣는다. 그리고 기도 대신 칼을 보낸다.

lines: 비담 — 왼쪽 능선. 나는 마른 시내.
저쪽 장수가 안장을 풀면, 위원회를 기다리지 않는다.
en: Bidam — left ridge. I take the dry creek.
If their captain loosens a saddle, we do not wait for a committee.
Finally — an enemy I am allowed to hate in public.
Alchun. On my mark.

blocks.html: They fall on the Baekje camp at dusk. Their captain climbs a boulder and empties a quiver; the quiver ends before the argument does. Alchun takes the general. Bidam takes the valley’s silence.
blocks.ko: 해 질 녘 백제 진영을 덮친다. 저쪽 장수는 큰 돌 위에 올라가 화살을 비운다. 화살이 먼저 바닥난다. 알천이 장군을 잡고, 비담이 골짜기의 침묵을 갖는다.

lines: 목표가 성 밖이면 우리는 좋은 짝이다.
en: We make a good pair when the target is outside the wall.
Inside the wall… we will see.
Inside the wall is still the sacred country.
I do not miss.

blocks.html: Eleven years later, on Radiance’s rampart, Bidam will remember the Jade Gate as the last time Alchun stood on his side without hesitating.
blocks.ko: 십일 년 뒤 명활성 성벽에서, 비담은 옥문곡을 — 알천이 망설임 없이 자기 편에 섰던 마지막 순간으로 — 기억할 것이다.

blocks.html: Before the fourth night’s tea, the Moon Palace tries a quieter weapon. Chunchu sends his son Bupmin, twenty-one, to the steam — the water that shows a man’s inner conscience, the past that is driving his hand. Yushin is told only to keep him talking.
blocks.ko: 넷째 밤의 차 전에, 월성은 더 조용한 무기를 쓴다. 춘추가 스물한 살 아들 법민을 김으로 보낸다 — 사람의 속마음과, 그 손을 움직이는 과거를 보여주는 물. 유신에게는 말만 붙들어 두라고만 한다.

blocks.html: Chunchu is home from the islands. They kept him just long enough to be rude about it, then sent him back with compliments and no ships.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 섬에서 돌아왔다. 섬나라는 무례하다 싶을 만큼만 그를 붙잡아 두었다가, 칭찬만 들려 배 한 척 없이 돌려보냈다.

lines: 샘은 네 외숙이 아는 곳이다. 네가 김씨니까 문이 열릴 거다.
en: Bupmin.
Take a jar.
The spring is a place your uncle knows. You’re a Kim — the door will open.
Splash him.
Father…
What does the water do to a man…
I understand. I’ll go.

blocks.label: The Steam Cavern
blocks.ko: 온천 동굴

blocks.html: This is the first time the cavern goddesses meet Bupmin. He is twenty-one. He does not yet have a king’s name. He has a jar and Chunchu’s weather.
blocks.ko: 동굴 여신들이 법민을 만나는 첫날이다. 스물하나. 아직 왕의 이름은 없다. 항아리와, 춘추의 날씨만 있다.

lines: 너… 너는 양쪽의 최선이야. 어깨는 가야. 입은 서라벌. 서 있으면 골화가 타고 오를 거야. 앉아.
en: A Kim.
Sit. No — the jar first.
You… He is the best of both. Gaya in the shoulders. Surabol in the mouth. Golhwa is going to climb you if you stay standing. Sit.

lines: 물 받아. 양심이 달라붙어. 트라우마. 원한. 그 손을 움직이는 거.
en: Oh.
A Kim we haven’t had. He’s both.
Take the water. Conscience sticks to it. Trauma. Grudge. Whatever’s driving the hand.
…And stop standing like that.

lines: 나 언덕이려 하는데, 너는 무릎 위에 두고 싶은 문제처럼 생겼어.
en: I’m trying to be a hill and you are shaped like a problem I want in my lap.
…Be careful.
If you splash it, you see why he’s doing it.
If you don’t see anything… that’s its own answer.
…He’s pretty. I’ll be quiet. I won’t be calm.
Goddesses…
Thank you. I was only—
I’ll just take the water.

blocks.html: He fills the jar. He does not stay for the lake’s other lessons. He is the best of both, and he leaves because his father told him to.
blocks.ko: 항아리를 채운다. 호수의 다른 수업은 받지 않는다. 그는 양쪽의 최선이고, 아버지가 시키니까 돌아간다.

blocks.label: DAY 4
blocks.ko: 넷째 날

blocks.html: Seven days of grain. The Moon Palace’s wells drop. Rumour rises to replace them. Chunchu files contingency letters the way other men file prayers.
blocks.ko: 이레 치 곡식. 월성의 우물이 준다. 소문이 그 자리를 채운다. 춘추는 다른 사람이 기도를 정리하듯 비상 서한을 정리한다.

blocks.html: Fourth night. Same low table under the half moon. Bidam reads a rumoured draft — never enough secretariat, never enough emperor. His voice stays pleasant. The sentences do not.
blocks.ko: 넷째 밤. 반달 아래 같은 낮은 상. 비담은 소문난 초안을 읽는다 — 집사부는 늘 부족하고, 황제는 늘 부족하다. 목소리는 여전히 부드럽다. 문장만 그렇지 않다.

lines: 화백의 만장일치 — 우리가 남긴 유일한 것 — 을 태울 셈이지.
en: What Chunchu wants…
is a country that fits inside a Tang envelope.
Central rule. Emperor. Clerks.
He would burn the Harmony Council’s unanimity — the one thing we kept.
Baekje comes with swords, not sentences.

lines: …그 여인이 즉위하던 해엔 나도, 여주를 위해 일어선 개화파였는데.
지금은 삼한 피를 지키는 자라 부르는구나. 아이러니하지, 유신?
en: Yes — and that is why you always win.
On the yard, and here.
Effort… speaks louder than my blood.
…The year they crowned her, I was the liberal who stood for the woman king.
Now they call me the blood-and-soil man. Ironic, Yushin?
…That young Hwarang is still here.
Where?

blocks.html: He folds the rumoured draft. The next sentences have been waiting in the sleeve all night.
blocks.ko: 그는 소문난 초안을 접는다. 다음에 올 문장은 밤 내내 소매 안에 있었다.

lines: 승만공주와, 김춘추의 횡포 — 둘 다 반대다.
저 파가 이기면 삼한은 그 천 해를 중국의 번국으로 살게 된다.
제 앞날을 제 손으로 정하지 못하는 나라로.
en: Princess Seungman, and the tyranny of Kim Chunchu — I stand against both.
He speaks of a thousand-year kingdom.
If his faction wins, Samhan will spend those thousand years as a Chinese vassal.
A country that never again turns its own wheel.

lines: 승만공주 아래 이 개혁이 서면, 몇 해 안에 신라가 삼한에서 제일 강한 나라가 될 수 있소.
en: Under Seungman, with these reforms, Silla could be the strongest country in Samhan in a few harvests.

lines: 이웃이 서로의 이름을 아는 나라를 원하지.
한 담장을 나누는 남이 아니라 — 진짜 겨레.
en: I do not need the strongest nation.
I want neighbours who still know one another’s names.
The young lifting the old.
A true people — not strangers who happen to share a wall.

lines: 신라가 백제와 고려에 뒤처지면, 고개로 들어오는 것은 칼과 기근이오.
en: The people’s livelihood hangs on the nation’s fullness.
Fullness hangs on institutions — on a government that can still stand.
If Silla falls behind Baekje and Goryeo, what comes through the pass is spear and famine.
Then tell me how the neighbours keep their names.

lines: 왕실이 도성 밖에서 한 해라도 살아 봤느냐. 춘추가?
저 밖에선 아무도 남의 황제 멍에를 원하지 않는다.
en: Yushin.
Has the royal house spent one year outside the capital? Has Chunchu?
I have.
Out there, nobody wants a foreign emperor’s yoke.

lines: 바깥사람 이야기로 치자면, 비담 공, 바깥사람은 평생 공이 아니라 나일 것이오.
육촌의 피를 이은 공은 이 땅을 일군 집들을 그리 얕보는데,
정복당한 나라의 막내아들인 나는 이 땅을 위해 죽을 각오가 돼 있소.
en: As for outsiders, Lord Bidam, I will always be more outsider than you.
You, of Six-Elder blood, speak poorly of the halls that raised this land,
while I, last son of a conquered kingdom, would die for it.

blocks.html: Yushin does not close the argument. He asks again about the pass, about names, about harvests — anything that keeps Bidam’s back to the dark. Behind the pavilion, Bupmin’s jar ticks once against a post.
blocks.ko: 유신은 논쟁을 닫지 않는다. 고개, 이름, 수확 — 비담의 등이 어둠을 향하게 붙들어 두는 것이면 된다. 정자 뒤에서 법민의 항아리가 기둥에 한 번 닿는다.

lines: 백성이 황제를 원치 않는다. 그 말은 어디서 들었소?
en: Bidam.
Say it once more.
The people have no wish for an emperor. Where did you hear that?

blocks.html: Bupmin comes from behind to splash the water. It is ugly and precise — cavern water as a hard sheet across Bidam’s shoulders, beads and all.
blocks.ko: 법민이 뒤에서 와 물을 끼얹는다. 흉하고 정확하다 — 동굴 물이 비담의 어깨와 염주 위로 딱딱한 면처럼 떨어진다.

en: Ha…
What is this…

lines: 유신 공… 왜 아무 일도 없는데…?
en: Your trauma….
Yushin… why isn’t it doing anything…?

blocks.html: Nothing rises. No childhood. No princess. No grudge-film in the steam. The water runs off the black robe as if it had mistaken a man for a wound. Chunchu, at the pavilion’s edge, does not move. The stoic act holds; the eyes do not.
blocks.ko: 아무것도 안 뜬다. 어린 시절도, 공주도, 김 속의 한 필름도. 물은 흑의를 타고 내린다. 사람을 상처로 착각한 것처럼. 정자 가장자리의 춘추는 움직이지 않는다. 담담한 연기는 유지된다. 눈만 아니다.

lines: 들어 본 적 있어… 이 물이지…?
en: Oh… haha…
I’ve heard of this… this is that water, isn’t it…?
HAHAHAHAHA!

lines: 정녕 내가 무슨 개인적 트라우마가 있어야 한다고 생각했느냐??
한순간이라도… 단 일 초라도… 너희 생각이 그냥 형편없을 가능성…
제정신인 사내라면 누구나 반대할 가능성… 생각해 본 적 있느냐?
아니면 너희가 하는 일은 전부 옳고…
누구든 반대하는 이유는 정신의 병 뿐이라고…
하… 친구들, 오늘 밤 너희가 한 일이라곤 제 논리를 증명한 것뿐이다.
어느 나라도 이끌 자격이 없다는 걸 스스로 증명했어.
en: Behold, the arrogance of the sacred bone class!!
You really thought I had to have some sort of personal trauma??
That that was the reason I was doing all of this?
That I hated the princess? The queen?
That I hated you, Chunchu, or Yushin?
Have you ever… even for a SECOND… considered the POSSIBILITY…
that your ideas are simply terrible?
That they’ll lead this nation to ruin?
That ANY reasonable man would oppose them?
Or are you so ARROGANT to assume… that EVERYTHING you lot do is correct…
and that the ONLY reason for ANYONE to disagree… is because they were suffering some sort of mental disease? Because they were angry and bitter?
Ha… well, my friends, I’m afraid all you’ve done tonight is prove your point.
You’ve proven yourself to be unworthy of leading any country.
So please… my friends… step aside…!

blocks.html: Alchun, arriving late with a lamp, goes pale. An officer asks whether to seize the jar. Nobody answers. Bidam is still laughing, and still alive, and the beads are still counting.
blocks.ko: 늦게 등을 들고 온 알천의 얼굴이 하얘진다. 장교 하나가 항아리를 빼앗을지 묻는다. 대답하는 사람이 없다. 비담은 아직 웃고, 아직 살아 있고, 염주는 아직 세고 있다.

blocks.label: Chunchu’s Rooms
blocks.ko: 춘추의 방

lines: 비담이 이기면 집사부는 고상한 취미가 된다.
비담이 져도, 우리에게는 죽어 가는 여왕과 서쪽의 당 모양 구멍이 남는다.
그 사람은 좋은 생각도 당나라 봉투에 담겨 오면 태울 사람이다. 강령의 전부가 그것이고 — 인기는 좋다.
en: If Bidam wins, the Secretariat becomes a quaint hobby.
If Bidam loses, we still have a dying queen and a Tang-shaped hole in the west.
The man would burn a good idea for arriving in a Tang envelope. That is the whole platform — and it polls well.
Munhee — pack for either weather.

lines: 여왕께서 즉위하시던 해에 쌌어요. 당신은 포위 때만 눈치채시죠.
en: I already packed.
I packed the year the Queen was crowned. You only notice in sieges.

blocks.html: Alchun eats alone between the camps. Both sides send him wine. He drinks neither. Surabol will later call it treason with better stationery.
blocks.ko: 알천은 진영 사이에서 혼자 먹는다. 양쪽이 술을 보낸다. 그는 어느 쪽도 마시지 않는다. 서라벌은 나중에 더 좋은 편지지의 반역이라 부를 것이다.

blocks.label: DAY 5
blocks.ko: 다섯째 날

blocks.html: Fifth night — the pavilion again. They sit on the floor, alone, the way they used to meet on the training ground. The tea is cold before anyone raises a blade. Six days of grain.
blocks.ko: 다섯째 밤 — 다시 그 정자. 두 사람은 바닥에서 단둘이 앉는다. 옛날 연무장에서 만나던 것과 같은 방식으로. 차가 식고 나서야 누군가 칼을 든다. 엿새 치 곡식.

lines: 삼한의 둘째 칼 — 비담이여!! 무기를 내려놓고 푸른 달께 충성을 돌려드려라!!
en: Second Blade of Samhan — Bidam!! Lay down your arms and give your loyalty back to the Blue Moon!!

blocks.html: For a breath they are only the old score again — one hundred and eight to one hundred and eight — two boys who never let the other keep a lead. Then Bidam speaks, and the yard is gone.
blocks.ko: 한순간 둘은 다시 옛 점수판일 뿐이다 — 백팔 대 백팔 — 상대를 앞서 두지 않던 소년 둘. 그러다 비담이 입을 열고, 연무장은 사라진다.

blocks.html: The yard after rain. Two Hwarang, neither willing to leave the mud with the score uneven.
blocks.ko: 비 온 뒤 연무장. 화랑 둘. 점수가 기우는 채로 진흙을 떠나려 하지 않는다.

en: One hundred and eight…!
Today I take the lead, Gaya!

lines: 일어나시오, 형님. 기우는 숫자는 밤에 못 자오.
en: One hundred and eight.
Get up, hyung. An uneven number does not sleep.

lines: 가야 피가 신라 피한테 졌다고 적히면 창피해서 그러시오?
en: Ha!
Afraid it will be written that Gaya blood lost to Silla blood?
Written or not.
Again.

lines: ……그리고 이길 때는 형님 소리 하지 마라.
en: …And don’t call me hyung when you’re winning.

blocks.html: They end the evening even. They always do.
blocks.ko: 그날 저녁도 비긴다. 언제나 그랬다.

lines: 이 나라에서 제일 똑똑한 자들은 이 나라를 미워하고,
en: Yushin.
In this country the smartest people hate this country,
and the most patriotic people… are all stupid.
That’s Silla.
The country you’re trying to sell.
Yushin….
And besides — you…
you were never even of Silla…!
Blood is inevitable.

blocks.html: The tea has not been touched. He says it like a compliment that curdled — still the gentleman, still the black robe, still the voice that once shielded this same man from the yard.
blocks.ko: 차는 손대지 않았다. 상처 주는 칭찬처럼 말한다 — 여전히 군자, 여전히 흑의, 여전히 연무장에서 이 같은 사람을 막아 세던 그 목소리.

lines: 비담 공... 우리는 함께 인생에 맹세로 한 걸로 기억하는데...
en: Lord Bidam… I remember we swore our lives to this together…

lines: 너한테는 원래 나라가 없으니, 이 나라를 팔아먹는 것도 거슬리지 않겠지...
하지만 우리는 다르다. 우리는 이 땅에서 뗄 수 없는 관계야…
내 조상이 세운 나라를 황제한테 넘겨줄 셈이냐...!
en: You never had a country of your own — selling this one must cost you nothing…
But we are different. We cannot be cut from this land…
Would you hand the country my ancestors built to an emperor…!
I am a son of the sacred country.

lines: 춘추 공은 당의 제도를 배우자는 것뿐이오. 백제는 문장이 아니라 칼로 오니까.
en: Selling — I have sold nothing.
Lord Chunchu only asks that we learn Tang’s institutions. Baekje comes with swords, not sentences.

lines: 춘추 — 春秋. 이름부터가 중국 책이다.
그런 자에게 신국의 내일을 쓰게 하겠단 말이냐.
남의 제도를 오래 배우다 보면 — 어느 아침엔, 배운 것만 남아 있을 것이다.
en: Chunchu — 春秋. The man is named after a Chinese book.
And you would let him write the sacred country’s tomorrow.
Learn another country’s institutions long enough — and one morning, the learning is all that is left.
I will raise the sacred country’s glory again,
I will return the sacred country’s future to its own people!

blocks.html: Yushin does not answer the speech. He looks at the cold tea as if the answer were at the bottom of the cup.
blocks.ko: 유신은 그 연설에 대답하지 않는다. 답이 잔 바닥에 있기라도 한 듯 식은 차를 내려다본다.

lines: 염종 말로는 네 증조부가 금관을 수레에 싣고 서라벌에 왔다더군.
할아버지 이야기는 아무도 안 해. 그분은 뭘 넘겼나, 유신?
en: Yumjong says your great-grandfather drove Geumgwan to Surabol in a cart.
Fine. Everyone knows the cart.
Nobody talks about the grandfather. What did he hand over, Yushin?

lines: 죽은 사람은 제 방에 두시오, 비담.
en: Leave the dead in their rooms, Bidam.

lines: 닷새 밤을 내 차를 마시면서, 네 것은 하나도 말하지 않았다.
en: No.
Five nights you’ve drunk my tea and told me nothing that was yours.
Give me one thing. Then call me a traitor.

blocks.html: For a long time the only sound is the wind through the open pavilion. Yushin has not said this aloud in Surabol since he was fifteen.
blocks.ko: 한참 동안, 트인 정자를 지나는 바람 소리뿐이다. 유신은 열다섯 이후로 서라벌에서 이 이야기를 입 밖에 낸 적이 없다.

lines: ……백제에는 관산성 길의 어느 밤을 부르는 이름이 있소.
서쪽 고개 너머 아무 군사에게나 물어보시오. 단이라 부르지.
en: …Baekje has a name for one night on the Gwansan road.
Ask any soldier over the western hills. They call it the Severing.

lines: 그쪽 임금이 목을 잃은 밤. 다 아는 얘기다. 칼은 노비가 들었지.
en: The night their king lost his head. Everyone knows it. A slave held the knife.

lines: 가야 고깔 투구를 쓴 사내가 그쪽 임금을 호상에 앉히고, 앉으라 했소.
en: A slave held the knife.
A man in a Gaya cone helm sat their king on a camp stool and told him to sit.
…That was my grandfather.

blocks.html: Bidam’s beads stop for the second time this winter.
blocks.ko: 비담의 염주가 올겨울 들어 두 번째로 멈춘다.

lines: ……가야 왕자가 삼한에서 가장 오래된 화친을 끊었다.
en: …A Gaya prince broke the oldest peace in Samhan.
For us.

lines: 그리고 그 손자가 공의 상에 앉아, 애초에 신라 사람이 아니었다는 말을 듣고 있소.
en: For Silla.
And his grandson sits at your table and hears he was never of it.
…Drink your tea, Marshal.

blocks.html: Neither of them drinks. Bidam does not ask the grandfather’s name, and Yushin does not offer it. Some names a family keeps in a box.
blocks.ko: 둘 다 마시지 않는다. 비담은 그 할아버지의 이름을 묻지 않고, 유신도 말하지 않는다. 어떤 이름은 집안이 상자에 넣어 둔다.

blocks.html: A cone helm, a king on a camp stool, and a name Yushin won’t say. Who was his grandfather…?
blocks.ko: 고깔 투구, 호상에 앉은 임금, 그리고 유신이 입에 올리지 않는 이름. 그의 할아버지는 누구였나…?

logline.en: The youngest son in the cart surrenders Gaya on one condition, then spends his life riding for Silla. Even south.
logline.ko: 수레에 탄 막내아들은 조건 하나를 걸고 가야를 넘긴다. 그리고 평생 신라를 위해 말을 탄다. 남으로도.

images.at: For five hundred years the people of Gaya lived by iron
images.alt: Night wide: Gaya mountain seongmun, stone and giwa, one purple iron-spark accent

ONE device: gate as a dark wedge with a purple #8B5CF6 iron-spark seam. Tiny figures lower third. Crushed blacks. No army. No text. No watermark.

images.alt: Dutch night charge: Sadaham in steel lamellar, ice-blue cloth peek, pointed Silla helm
images.prompt: Minimal iconic 16:9. Dutch charge, night tenebrism. ONE Sadaham mid-stride snarl. FACE ch_sadaham. Steel-gray lamellar; ice-blue #6fa8ff cloth peek; pointed Silla helm. Spear as diagonal device. No clone. No text. No watermark.

images.alt: Before the charge, Sadaham grins back over his shoulder at Mugwan as their horses break into a run under a storm sky
images.prompt: Low three-quarter from beside a galloping horse’s churning forelegs, dusk storm on a Gaya ridge. Sadaham, fifteen, in steel lamellar and pointed Silla helm, leans forward over his horse’s neck and looks back over his shoulder with a wide reckless grin; a sword at his hip. Just behind him, Mugwan spurs his own horse to catch up, mouth open mid-shout. One cloud-break shaft lands on the two riders; behind them Silla banners on poles bleed into haze, and far ahead a Gaya seongmun is a dark notch on the ridge. Torn grass and flying mud as dark foreground blur. CANON — SADAHAM — FACE and garments from attached /ch_sadaham.png (face only; invent a new pose). Demeanor: Hwarang taken Gaya at fifteen; ice-blue #6fa8ff cloth on campaign; dies young of grief. Armor: Silla kit: steel lamellar cuirass and skirt, tall pointed jonghyeongju helm with a short plume. Battle armor: plates are METALLIC GRAY STEEL lamellar copied from the attached lamellar ref, cloth peeking at collar, sleeves, skirt, sash and plume-cord in the wearer's color only. Ignore labels and watermarks on armor refs. Not Japanese kabuto, not fantasy plate, not a gold-painted suit. #6fa8ff as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | MUGWAN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_mugwan.png (face only; invent a new pose). #7aa0c8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | Kingdom banners: copy field colour and emblem from the attached flag_*.png ref onto period silk war-banners — tall poles behind each side, long streamers, small pennants on spear-tips and saddle-backs. Painted silk, wind-whipped, torn and smoke-stained in battle; never a flat modern flag graphic. Each side's banner colour is the clearest colour on its half of the frame, so the kingdom reads at a glance. Silla banners: blue silk with a white crescent moon. Attached flag /flag_silla.png. SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

A single moon shaft, like the attached cave dawn beam but moonlight, cuts through mist and hits Kim Sadaham kneeling in the lower third. FACE and clothes from his portrait: young man, long black hair, crescent-moon headband, ice-blue robe #6fa8ff, red sash. Lips parted, quiet, not shouting. The rest of the road is crushed black. images.at: Take the land. Leave the people.
images.prompt: 16:9 ANIME tenebrism still — cel-shaded anime with clean line art and flat hard-edged shadow shapes, NOT photoreal, NOT a realistic oil painting — lit like a Caravaggio: pure black void, one hard shaft of moonlight from above. Young hwarang Sadaham kneeling, head bowed, pressing the back of his fist to his forehead as he whispers the vow again, a single dried flower held in that fist, tears on his cheek. The shaft lights his face, fist, flower and shoulders; everything else falls to pure black. FACE AND GARMENTS match the attached Sadaham portrait. Ice-blue #6fa8ff as the specular on his silk. Extreme contrast, anime cel shading, film grain. No text, no watermark, no halo, no glow aura.

BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: His name was Muryuk. He was the youngest of three sons in a cart, and the only one who looked back.
blocks.ko: 그의 이름은 무력이었다. 수레에 탄 세 아들 중 막내였고, 뒤를 돌아본 건 그 하나뿐이었다.

blocks.caption: Five hundred years of iron, gone in thirty.
blocks.ko: 오백 년의 쇠, 서른 해 만에 사라지다.

blocks.html: For five hundred years the people of Gaya lived by iron and by six eggs, and they enjoyed great peace. Then Silla came shopping.
blocks.ko: 오백 년 동안 가야 사람들은 쇠와 여섯 알로 살며 태평을 누렸다. 그러다 신라가 장을 보러 왔다.

blocks.label: The Surrender
blocks.ko: 항복

blocks.html: The lord of Geumgwan did the arithmetic first. Baekje to the west, Silla to the north, a river of iron and no army worth the name.
blocks.ko: 금관의 임금이 먼저 셈을 했다. 서쪽엔 백제, 북쪽엔 신라. 쇠의 강은 있는데 군대라 할 만한 것은 없다.

blocks.html: The cart is slow. The road to Surabol is long enough for a boy to change his mind several times.
blocks.ko: 수레는 느리다. 서라벌 가는 길은 아이가 마음을 여러 번 바꿀 만큼 길다.

blocks.speaker: The lord of Geumgwan
en: Face front, Muryuk.
Your brothers are facing front.
Somebody should remember what it looked like.
…The harbour. Before.

blocks.speaker: The lord of Geumgwan
lines: 그럼 조용히 기억해라. 임금들은 자기가 산 걸 상기받는 걸 싫어한다.
en: Then remember it quietly. Kings don’t like being reminded what they bought.

blocks.html: He keeps looking back until the river bends out of sight.
blocks.ko: 그는 강이 굽어 보이지 않을 때까지 뒤를 돌아본다.

blocks.hanja: 金官國主金仇亥 與妃及三子 以國帑寶物來降
blocks.ko: 금관국주 김구해가 왕비 및 세 아들과 더불어 나라의 곳간과 보물을 가지고 와서 항복하였다.
blocks.html: The lord of Geumgwan, Kim Guhae, came with his queen and three sons, bringing the treasury and precious things of the country, and surrendered.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 4, Silla Annals — King Beopheung, yr. 19 (532); Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 1, p. 86

blocks.caption: The youngest son in the cart. Gaya handed over its crown. It did not hand over him.
blocks.ko: 수레에 탄 막내아들. 가야는 왕관을 내주었다. 그까지 내준 건 아니다.

blocks.html: The king on the dais has bought harbours before. He has never bought one that talks back.
blocks.ko: 단 위의 임금은 포구를 사 본 적이 있다. 말대꾸하는 포구를 사 본 적은 없다.

lines: 제 아버지의 아들들이 신라에서 부끄럽지 않게 살게 해 주십시오…
en: If we are to surrender, I have one condition…
Let my father’s sons live in Silla without shame…
And what do you mean by that?

lines: 신라에서는... 사람의 성분이 모든 걸 좌지우지한다고 알고 있습니다...
성골, 진골... 이미 다 알고 있습니다...
제 자손... 수로왕과 허왕후의 아들과 딸들이 좋은 자리에 자리잡을 수만 있다면...
저 또한 신라를 목숨을 바칠 준비가 되어있습니다...
en: In Silla… I know a man’s blood decides everything…
Sacred Bone, True Bone… I know it all…
If my descendants — the sons and daughters of Suro and Heo — can take a worthy place…
then I too am ready to give Silla my life…

lines: 알겠다. 너희 후손들은 신라의 진골로 추대해주마.
en: Very well. Your descendants shall be raised as True Bones of Silla.

lines: 대신 자네는 나를 위해 말을 타야 하네. 북으로, 서로. 국경이 가려운 곳이면 어디든.
en: In return you ride for me. North, west. Wherever the border itches.
…Even south.
…Even south.

blocks.html: Three generations later, his grandson will still be told he is not really one of them.
blocks.ko: 세 대가 지난 뒤에도, 그의 손자는 여전히 «진짜 우리 편은 아니다»라는 말을 듣게 된다.

en: Your grace is boundless… Your Majesty…!

blocks.label: The Night Road
blocks.ko: 밤길

blocks.html: Twenty-two years later he is a Silla governor in a Gaya helm, because nobody has managed to make him take it off. One night on the Gwansan road, the King of Baekje rides into his ditch.
blocks.ko: 스물두 해 뒤, 그는 가야 투구를 쓴 신라 군주다. 아무도 그 투구를 벗기지 못했다. 관산성 길의 어느 밤, 백제 임금이 그의 도랑으로 말을 몰아 들어온다.

blocks.html: You have seen that night from the king’s side. From the cone’s side it is shorter. A man who once begged at a king’s feet sits another king on a camp stool and does not draw his sword. The slave does the rest.
blocks.ko: 그 밤은 임금 쪽에서 이미 보았다. 고깔 쪽에서 보면 더 짧다. 한때 임금의 발치에서 청하던 사내가 다른 임금을 호상에 앉히고, 칼을 뽑지 않는다. 나머지는 노비가 한다.

blocks.hanja: 祖武力，爲新州道行軍摠管，嘗領兵獲百濟王及其將四人，斬首一萬餘級。父舒玄，官至蘇判大梁州都督安撫大梁州諸軍事。
blocks.html: His grandfather Muryeok was Commander of the Army of the Sinju Circuit; he once led troops that captured the king of Baekje and four of his generals and took more than ten thousand heads. His father Seohyun rose to the rank of Sopan, Governor-General of Daeyang Province and Pacifier of all the armies of Daeyang Province.
blocks.ko: 할아버지 무력은 신주도 행군총관이 되어, 일찍이 군사를 거느리고 백제 왕과 그 장수 넷을 사로잡고 1만여 급의 목을 베었다. 아버지 서현은 벼슬이 소판 대량주도독 안무대량주제군사에 이르렀다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biography of Kim Yushin, part 1

blocks.html: Ten thousand heads, says the record, and makes him a hero. He goes home and does not eat for two days.
blocks.ko: 만 급이라고 기록은 말하고, 그를 영웅으로 만든다. 그는 집에 가서 이틀을 먹지 않는다.

blocks.html: Before that, the slave who did the cutting comes to his tent with the king’s knife, because nobody else will take it.
blocks.ko: 그 전에, 목을 벤 노비가 임금의 칼을 들고 그의 막사로 온다. 아무도 그 칼을 받으려 하지 않아서다.

en: My lord. They said give it to the Gaya one.
…That’s you, isn’t it?

lines: 그런 일을 한 번 한 칼은 아들 있는 집에 가면 안 된다.
en: Keep it.
A knife that’s done that once shouldn’t go home to a man with sons.

blocks.label: The Last Gate
blocks.ko: 마지막 성문

blocks.html: Eight years after that, the Cloud King comes for what is left of Gaya. He brings a boy-general, Sadaham. He brings Muryuk.
blocks.ko: 그로부터 여덟 해 뒤, 구름왕이 남은 가야를 치러 온다. 소년 장수 사다함을 데리고. 그리고 무력을 데리고.

en: They said too young.
The gate didn’t.
Don’t die first.
Then keep up.

blocks.html: The tall Gaya cone still fights. The men on Daegaya’s gate wear the same helm Muryuk does.
blocks.ko: 높은 가야 고깔은 아직 싸운다. 대가야 성문 위의 사내들은 무력과 같은 투구를 썼다.

en: Those are my father’s helms.
Let me walk up first. Alone.
They’ll shoot you.
Then keep the gate warm for me.

blocks.html: The wall answers first. Gaya arrows, from Gaya bows, with Gaya iron on the points. Daegaya has been forging Silla’s blades for a generation and is about to find out how good they were.
blocks.ko: 성벽이 먼저 답한다. 가야의 활로 쏜 가야의 화살, 촉에는 가야의 쇠. 대가야는 한 세대 동안 신라의 칼을 벼려 왔고, 이제 그 칼이 얼마나 좋았는지 알게 될 참이다.

blocks.html: Sadaham does not wait for anyone to finish a sentence. He takes five thousand horse at the Jeondan gate while the men above it are still drawing, and goes through before the gate has decided whether it is open.
blocks.ko: 사다함은 누가 말을 끝내기를 기다리지 않는다. 기병 오천을 이끌고 전단문으로 달려드는데, 성 위의 사내들은 아직 시위를 당기는 중이다. 문이 열렸는지 닫혔는지 정하기도 전에 그는 이미 안에 있다.

blocks.speaker: A Daegaya archer
en: That’s a child. They sent a child—
He’s inside. How is he inside?

blocks.html: Inside the walls the fighting is short and mean, street by street, the way it is when everyone knows the end and nobody wants to be the one who says it. Muryuk walks up the main street with his helm in his hand. Nobody on the rooftops knows what to do with a Gaya face under a Silla banner.
blocks.ko: 성안의 싸움은 짧고 독하다. 골목마다, 다들 끝을 알면서 그 말을 먼저 꺼내고 싶지 않을 때의 싸움이다. 무력은 투구를 손에 든 채 큰길을 걸어 올라간다. 지붕 위 누구도 신라 깃발 아래의 가야 얼굴을 어찌해야 할지 모른다.

blocks.html: He finds the old lords of Daegaya in the hall, sitting very straight, the way men sit when they have decided to die well and have not yet been told the price of living.
blocks.ko: 그는 대가야의 늙은 귀족들을 전각에서 찾는다. 다들 꼿꼿이 앉아 있다. 잘 죽기로 마음먹었는데, 살아남는 값은 아직 듣지 못한 사람들의 앉음새다.

blocks.speaker: An old lord of Daegaya
en: Geumgwan’s youngest.
So they sent you to say it.
Nobody sent me. I asked to come.
lines: 보낸 사람 없습니다. 제가 오겠다고 했습니다.

blocks.speaker: An old lord of Daegaya
en: What is it like? Over there.
Cold, for the first ten years.
Then you have grandchildren, and they don’t remember the cold.
lines: 그러다 손주가 생기는데, 그 애들은 추웠던 걸 기억 못 합니다.

blocks.html: The old man looks at him for a long time. Gaya has always listened to a good price.
blocks.ko: 노인은 오래도록 그를 바라본다. 가야는 언제나 좋은 값에는 귀를 기울였다.

blocks.hanja: 九月 加耶叛 王命異斯夫討之 斯多含副之 異斯夫引兵臨之 一時盡降
blocks.ko: 구월에 가야가 배반하니, 왕이 이사부에게 토벌하라 명하고 사다함으로 보좌하게 하였다. 이사부가 군사를 이끌고 이르니, 일시에 모두 항복하였다.
blocks.html: In the ninth month Gaya rebelled. The king ordered Isabu to punish them, with Sadaham as deputy. Isabu brought up the army, and they all surrendered at once.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 4, Silla Annals — King Jinheung, yr. 23 (562), 9th month; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 1, p. 98

blocks.html: The boy took his prize anyway. After the city fell he opened the prize-cages and kept only Alcheon dirt. Take the land. Leave the people.
blocks.ko: 소년은 그래도 상을 받았다. 성이 떨어진 뒤 상으로 받은 우리를 열고 알천의 박토만 받았다. 땅은 가져라. 사람은 놔둬라.

en: Alcheon dirt.
That’s enough.

blocks.html: Muryuk watches the cages open and says nothing. It is the first Silla habit he has ever liked.
blocks.ko: 무력은 우리가 열리는 것을 보며 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 처음으로 마음에 드는 신라의 버릇이다.

blocks.label: The Cut Rope
blocks.ko: 끊긴 밧줄

blocks.html: That night the freed captives sleep in the Silla camp, because they have nowhere else to sleep. Muryuk finds the boy-general sitting on a coil of the rope he cut, eating rice out of his helmet.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 풀려난 포로들은 신라 진영에서 잔다. 달리 잘 데가 없어서다. 무력은 소년 장수가 자기가 끊은 밧줄 더미 위에 앉아 투구에 담은 밥을 먹고 있는 것을 찾는다.

en: You’re the Gaya one.
So they keep telling me.
Were any of them yours? The ones on the rope.
lines: 그중에 아는 사람 있었어요? 줄에 묶였던 사람들.

en: All of them. None of them.
My father sold the harbour before I was old enough to lift a sword for it.
lines: 내가 칼 들 나이가 되기도 전에 아버지가 항구를 넘기셨으니.

en: You walked up to that gate with your helmet off.
I’d have been shot.
lines: 아까 투구 벗고 성문으로 걸어 올라가셨잖아요.

en: You’d have charged it. They were waiting for that.
Why let them go?
lines: 넌 돌격했겠지. 저들은 그걸 기다리고 있었다.

en: Mugwan says I’m showing off.
Are you?
…A little.
Somebody should get to go home. Today it might as well be them.
lines: 누군가는 집에 가야죠. 오늘은 저 사람들이면 되잖아요.

blocks.html: Muryuk sits down on the rope beside him. Across the river, Daegaya’s roofs are still smoking.
blocks.ko: 무력은 그 옆 밧줄 위에 앉는다. 강 건너 대가야의 지붕들에서 아직 연기가 오른다.

en: When I was younger than you, they put me in a cart and told me to face front.
I looked back the whole way. I thought somebody should remember what it looked like.
lines: 너보다 어렸을 때 나를 수레에 태우고 앞만 보라 하더군.
나는 가는 내내 뒤를 봤다. 누군가는 어떤 모습이었는지 기억해야 한다고 생각했지.

en: Then look. Nobody’s stopping you tonight.
I’ll hold your horse.
lines: 그럼 보세요. 오늘 밤엔 아무도 안 말려요.

blocks.html: So he looks. The boy holds the horse and, for once in his short life, does not say anything at all.
blocks.ko: 그래서 그는 본다. 소년은 말을 잡고 서서, 그 짧은 생에 처음으로, 아무 말도 하지 않는다.

en: …There.
Now I can face front.
Live long enough to be embarrassed by tonight, Sadaham.
lines: 오늘 밤이 부끄러워질 만큼 오래 살아라, 사다함.

en: Mugwan will be embarrassed for both of us.
lines: 무관이가 둘 몫으로 부끄러워해 줄 거예요.

blocks.html: Neither of them knows how short a year can be.
blocks.ko: 한 해가 얼마나 짧을 수 있는지, 두 사람 다 아직 모른다.

blocks.label: The Name
blocks.ko: 이름

blocks.html: He grows old in Surabol with a True Bone seal and a Gaya accent he never loses. His son Seohyun is clever and polite, and keeps walking into things while looking at clouds.
blocks.ko: 그는 진골의 인장과 끝내 버리지 못한 가야 말씨로 서라벌에서 늙는다. 아들 서현은 영리하고 예의 바르며, 구름을 보다가 자꾸 무언가에 부딪힌다.

lines: 신라 사람들 마음에 들라고 신라 이름을 지어 주지 마라. 어차피 안 좋아한다.
en: Seohyun. When you have a son—
Don’t give him a Silla name to make them like him. They won’t.
Give him one that keeps faith.

lines: 아버지, 저는 아직— 여자도 없는데, 저—
en: Father, I’m not even— there isn’t even a girl, I—

lines: 생길 거다. 구름 보다가 벽에 부딪히는 놈이니.
그걸 귀엽다 할 여자가 하나는 있을 거다. 딱 하나.
en: There will be. You walk into walls looking at clouds.
Some girl will find that charming. One.

blocks.html: Then he says a name nobody has been given yet.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 아직 아무도 받지 않은 이름을 부른다.

en: Yushin…

blocks.label: DAY 6
blocks.ko: 여섯째 날

blocks.html: On the sixth night there are two cups on the pavilion table. Bidam poured them himself. Last night he found out whose grandson he has been calling a Gaya ox.
blocks.ko: 여섯째 밤, 정자 탁자에 찻잔 둘이 놓여 있다. 비담이 손수 따랐다. 어젯밤 그는 자기가 가야 소라 부르던 사내가 누구의 손자인지 알았다.

blocks.html: Five days of grain. Two cups poured. Will the grandson of the cone helm come to tea…?
blocks.ko: 닷새 치 곡식. 채워 둔 찻잔 둘. 고깔 투구의 손자는 차를 마시러 올 것인가…?

logline.en: The sixth night’s tea turns to insult, the cavern throws Bidam out, a white horse burns for a falling star, and Yushin’s father’s stone goes warm.
logline.ko: 여섯째 밤의 차는 욕설로 끝나고, 동굴은 비담을 내쫓고, 떨어진 별을 위해 흰 말이 바쳐지고, 유신 아버지의 돌이 따뜻해진다.
