blocks.label: DAY 6
blocks.ko: 여섯째 날

blocks.html: Night rain. Five days of grain behind the palace gate. Bidam’s officers want a dawn assault. Bidam wants the score finished properly. He wants Yushin to come out again.
blocks.ko: 밤비. 궁문 안에는 닷새 치 곡식. 비담의 장교들은 새벽 돌격을 원한다. 비담은 점수를 제대로 끝내고 싶다. 유신이 다시 나오기를 원한다.

blocks.html: Sixth night. Yushin does not come to the pavilion. Bidam sends tea anyway — two cups poured, one left steaming.
blocks.ko: 여섯째 밤. 유신은 정자에 오지 않는다. 비담은 그래도 차를 보낸다 — 잔 둘, 하나는 김이 오른 채.

lines: 괜찮아. 여섯 번째 밤까지는 예의를 지켰어.
en: …He is not coming today.
Very well. Courtesy held until the sixth night.

blocks.html: The Hwarang hall, the new boy’s first day. Two seniors lean across his desk.
blocks.ko: 화랑 강당, 새로 온 아이의 첫날. 선배 둘이 그 아이 책상 너머로 몸을 기울인다.

en: So he isn’t even a real True Bone!
blocks.speaker: Senior Hwarang

lines: 너희는 뭐, 잘한 거 있어서 진골이 됐냐?
en: Hey, enough!
What did any of you do to earn True Bone?
You were merely born into it.

blocks.html: He punches the nearer one before the other can answer, then the second for good measure. Then he wipes his knuckles on his own black headband.
blocks.ko: 그는 대답이 나오기도 전에 가까운 놈을 치고, 덤으로 다른 놈도 친다. 그러고는 제 검은 머리띠에 주먹을 닦는다.

en: Thank you.

lines: 이거 가지라. 내 머리띠인데, 이걸 가지고 있으면 아무도 안 괴롭힐 거야.
en: What is there to thank?
Take this headband. Keep it, and no one will trouble you.

blocks.html: Near midnight Yushin comes to the pavilion after all. He does not touch the cup.
blocks.ko: 자정 무렵, 유신이 끝내 정자로 온다. 잔에는 손대지 않는다.

en: You Gaya wretch…!
You dare call yourself the sacred country’s saviour….

lines: 열다섯 해 전, 화백회의에서 — 덕만공주를 위해 일어선 자가 누구였소?
en: Lord Bidam.
Fifteen years past, in the Harmony Council — who was it that stood up for Princess Dukman?

lines: 그 젊은 화랑은 셋 중 가장 총명한 이를 고르겠다고 했소.
그 사람은 어디로 갔소, 비담 공?
en: That young Hwarang said he would choose the cleverest of the three.
Where did that man go, Lord Bidam?

lines: …그 사람은 신국이 아직 나라였을 때 살았지.
en: …That man lived back when the sacred country was still a country.

lines: 그러나 신국에 깃발을 든 것은 내가 아니오…!
en: But it is not I who raised a banner against the sacred country…!

blocks.label: DAY 7
blocks.ko: 일곱째 날

blocks.html: Seven days in, nobody pours. Four days of grain. Last night’s two cups are still on the pavilion table, and one of them was never touched.
blocks.ko: 이레째, 아무도 차를 따르지 않는다. 곡식은 나흘 치. 어젯밤의 찻잔 둘이 정자 탁자에 그대로 있고, 하나는 끝내 아무도 손대지 않았다.

blocks.label: Not a Kim
blocks.ko: 김씨가 아니다

blocks.html: Bidam finds the cavern the way a man finds a rumor. Sword on the lip. Beads in the fist. The navy coat comes off because he has heard Yushin wash here, and a man who wants what Yushin has will copy the wash if he cannot copy the name.
blocks.ko: 비담은 소문을 찾듯 동굴을 찾는다. 칼은 턱에. 염주는 주먹에. 남색 도포가 내린다. 유신이 여기서 씻는다는 말은 들었고, 유신이 가진 것을 원하는 남자는 이름을 베끼지 못하면 씻는 법을 베끼니까.

blocks.html: He walks into the steam with nothing on but water and one hundred and eight beads.
blocks.ko: 물과 백팔 염주만 걸치고 김 속으로 들어간다.

blocks.html: The three sisters are already on the far rock. Narim looks at him the way an eldest looks at a door that opened wrong.
blocks.ko: 세 자매는 이미 저쪽 바위에 있다. 나림은 잘못 열린 문을 보는 언니처럼 그를 본다.
blocks.art: Golhwa on the rock, legs spread wide, chima hiked; Hyullé, knees pressed, eyes down, soaked.

blocks.html: The spring does not hide much. Heat hits him low. He recites. The beads do not help.
blocks.ko: 샘이 감춰 주는 게 없다. 열이 아래서 온다. 염불을 한다. 염주가 도움이 안 된다.

blocks.html: I came to wash. The sutra does not cover this. I am standing in a door I cannot close.
blocks.ko: 씻으러 왔다. 경이 이걸 가리지 못한다. 닫을 수 없는 문에 서 있다.

blocks.html: The beads stop mid-count. He stares. The waterline drops.
blocks.ko: 염주가 세다 만다. 본다. 수선이 내려간다.

en: Wrong door. He brought iron. And that.
lines: 문 잘못 들었어. 쇠를 들고 왔네. 그리고 그것도.

en: He is not a Kim. The steam already knows.
…The mouth. Before the water takes the blade.

blocks.html: They do not stay women.
blocks.ko: 여자로 남지 않는다.

blocks.html: Golhwa goes first — fire unfolding into a tiger the size of the rock, ember pelt, steam off the fangs. Hyullé’s silk becomes a water-serpent, long as the bowl, cyan scales. Narim’s elder-shape thickens into a moss-bear, leaves in the fur, the hill’s weight on four feet.
blocks.ko: 골화가 먼저다 — 불이 바위만 한 호랑이로 펼쳐지고, 불씨 털, 송곳니에서 김. 혈레의 비단이 사발만큼 긴 물뱀이 되고, 청록 비늘. 나림의 언니 형상이 이끼 곰으로 두꺼워진다. 털에 잎, 네 발에 언덕의 무게.

blocks.html: He recoils. The beads jump. The sword is a hard black line he cannot lift in time.
blocks.ko: 뒷걸음친다. 염주가 튄다. 칼은 제때 들지 못하는 단단한 검은 선이다.

blocks.html: They kick him toward the light — tiger-shoulder, serpent-coil, bear-shove. Three beasts, one refusal. The night has him again. The lake keeps Kims. It does not keep slogans.
blocks.ko: 셋이 그를 빛 쪽으로 밀어낸다 — 호랑이 어깨, 뱀의 몸, 곰의 밀침. 짐승 셋, 거절 하나. 밤이 다시 그를 갖는다. 호수는 김씨를 지킨다. 구호는 지키지 않는다.

blocks.label: DAY 8
blocks.ko: 여덟째 날

blocks.html: On the eighth night a star falls toward the Moon Palace — bright enough that both camps look up. Bidam does not invent the omen. He only names it in a useful direction.
blocks.ko: 여덟째 밤, 별이 월성을 향해 떨어진다 — 양쪽 진영이 올려다볼 만큼 밝게. 비담은 징조를 발명하지 않는다. 유용한 방향으로 이름만 붙일 뿐이다.

blocks.hanja: 吾聞落星之下必有流血 此殆女主敗績之兆也
blocks.ko: 내가 듣건대 별이 떨어지는 곳에는 반드시 피가 나리라. 이는 거의 여주가 패할 징조다.
blocks.html: I have heard that where a star falls, blood will surely be shed. This is likely an omen that the woman sovereign will be defeated.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biographies — Kim Yushin; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 2 (Bidam’s rebellion, 647)

lines: 하늘은 이미 여왕의 자리에 반대표를 던졌다.
女主不能善理 — 이제 하늘이 불로 쓴다.
en: You heard it.
Heaven has already voted against a woman on the throne.
女主不能善理 — and now the sky writes it in fire.

blocks.label: The Moon Palace
blocks.ko: 월성

blocks.html: The rebel shout shakes the ground. Inside the Moon Palace Queen Sunduk goes pale. Yushin asks for leave to speak — and for a kite, a torch, and enough lies to edit heaven.
blocks.ko: 반군의 함성이 땅을 흔든다. 월성 안에서 선덕여왕의 얼굴이 창백해진다. 유신은 아뢰기를 청한다 — 연과 횃불, 그리고 하늘을 고칠 만큼의 거짓을.

lines: 별을 읽을 수 있다면, 읽지 못하게 할 수도 있습니다.
en: Your Majesty — do not fear a falling light.
If they can read a star, they can also unread one.

blocks.html: He flies the kite from the palace dark: a burning scarecrow climbing back up the path the star came down, so the night sky seems to take its light back.
blocks.ko: 궁의 어둠에서 연을 띄운다 — 별이 내려온 길을 거슬러 타오르는 허수아비가 올라, 밤하늘이 빛을 도로 가져가는 것처럼.

lines: 하늘이 마음을 바꿨다 — 아니면 우리가 하늘의 필체를 고쳤다.
en: Look up.
Heaven changed its mind — or we changed heaven’s handwriting.
Hwarang, with me.

blocks.label: The Stables
blocks.ko: 마구간

blocks.html: The kite buys one night. A sky can only be argued with for so long, and by midnight both camps are already arguing about what they saw. While the drums are still asleep, Yushin goes down to the palace stables alone and leads out the white horse.
blocks.ko: 연은 하룻밤을 번다. 하늘과는 그리 오래 다툴 수 없고, 자정이 되자 두 진영은 벌써 자기들이 무엇을 보았는지를 두고 다툰다. 북이 아직 잠든 사이, 유신은 홀로 궁의 마구간으로 내려가 흰 말을 끌어낸다.

blocks.html: Hangyul has carried him for eighteen years, since the charge at Nangbi Fortress, to every border the queen sent him to and a few he went to without asking. The groom, a boy of fourteen, works out what the rope in the marshal’s other hand is for before anyone says it, and starts to cry with his mouth shut.
blocks.ko: 한결은 낭비성 돌격 때부터 열여덟 해 동안 그를 태웠다. 여왕이 보낸 모든 국경으로, 묻지 않고 간 몇몇 국경으로. 열네 살 마부 아이는 대장군의 다른 손에 들린 밧줄이 무엇에 쓰일지 누가 말하기도 전에 알아차리고, 입을 꾹 다문 채 운다.

blocks.html: Seventeen, drunk, and asleep in the saddle. His first horse, Hanbyul, does what any good horse does with a sleeping rider and takes him where he always goes. He wakes at the courtesan Cheongwan’s gate with her lantern already lifted and her face already glad.
blocks.ko: 열일곱, 취해서, 안장 위에서 잠든 채. 첫 말 한별은 잠든 주인을 태운 좋은 말이라면 누구나 하는 일을 한다. 늘 가던 곳으로 데려간다. 그가 눈을 뜬 곳은 기생 천관의 문 앞이고, 그녀의 등불은 이미 들려 있고, 얼굴은 이미 반갑다.

en: You came?
…They said you swore to your mother you’d never come again.

blocks.html: He had sworn it. The horse had not. He gets down, draws, and takes Hanbyul’s head off at the gate in one stroke, then walks home past the lantern without looking at it. The song Cheongwan made about that night outlives both of them.
blocks.ko: 맹세는 그가 했다. 말은 하지 않았다. 그는 내려서 칼을 뽑아, 문 앞에서 단칼에 한별의 목을 벤다. 그리고 등불은 쳐다보지도 않고 걸어서 집으로 간다. 그날 밤을 두고 천관이 지은 노래는 두 사람보다 오래 산다.

blocks.label: The Scorched Ground
blocks.ko: 별 떨어진 자리

blocks.html: The star came down past the west wall of the Moon Palace, where the ground is still scorched in a long smear. Yushin walks Hangyul there himself. Chunchu is already waiting with two priests, a bronze basin, and a face that has decided not to argue.
blocks.ko: 별은 월성 서쪽 담 너머에 떨어졌고, 그곳 땅은 아직 길게 그을려 있다. 유신은 한결을 직접 끌고 간다. 춘추는 이미 제관 둘과 청동 대야, 그리고 따지지 않기로 마음먹은 얼굴을 하고 기다리고 있다.

en: …There are other white horses. Three in the stable.
Does it have to be this one?

lines: 저쪽도 다 알아. 내가 무슨 말을 타는지.
남의 말을 바치면 하늘이 웃는 게 아니라 비담이 웃어.
en: They know over there. Everyone knows which horse I ride.
Offer someone else’s horse and it isn’t heaven that laughs. It’s Bidam.

blocks.html: He takes the halter off with his own hands. Hangyul, who has been led to a great many strange places at night, puts his nose into Yushin’s chest and waits for the reason, as he always has.
blocks.ko: 그는 제 손으로 굴레를 벗긴다. 밤마다 낯선 곳으로 수없이 끌려가 본 한결은, 늘 그래 왔듯 유신의 가슴에 코를 묻고 이유를 기다린다.

lines: 낭비성에서 네가 아니었으면 난 거기서 끝났어.
en: Eighteen years.
If it weren’t for you at Nangbi, I’d have ended there.
…I’m sorry. This time I’m the one who brought you.
Yushin.
…Want me to do it?
No.
He’s mine.

blocks.html: He does it the way the rite asks and faster than the rite asks, so the horse never quite finishes turning his head. White goes down into the scorched black. The priests begin the prayer, and Yushin, who has never once let another man finish a sentence for him, lets them.
blocks.ko: 그는 의례가 시키는 대로, 그러나 의례보다 빠르게 한다. 말이 고개를 미처 다 돌리기도 전에. 흰 것이 그을린 검은 땅 위로 무너진다. 제관들이 축문을 시작하고, 평생 남이 제 말을 대신 끝맺게 둔 적 없는 유신이 이번에는 그렇게 둔다.

blocks.html: He slaughtered a white horse and offered it at the place where the star had fallen, and prayed: “In the way of Heaven, yang is firm and yin is yielding; in the way of men, the sovereign is honoured and the subject humble. Should this ever be reversed, there is great disorder.”
blocks.ko: 흰 말을 잡아 별이 떨어진 곳에 제사 지내고 빌었다. “하늘의 도는 양이 굳세고 음이 부드러우며, 사람의 도는 임금이 높고 신하가 낮습니다. 만일 이를 바꾸면 곧 큰 난리가 됩니다.”
blocks.hanja: 刑白馬 祭於星落之地 祝曰 天道則陽剛而陰柔 人道則君尊而臣卑 苟或易之 卽爲大亂
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biographies — Kim Yushin; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 2 (Bidam’s rebellion, 647)

blocks.html: Across the field, on the Radiance wall, Bidam watches the smoke of the offering go up and asks an officer what was burned. When he is told, he puts his beads away for the first time in eight days and goes down to the lines to stand beside his own horse, Bisamun, for a while, saying nothing to anybody.
blocks.ko: 들판 건너 명활성 성벽에서 비담은 제물 연기가 오르는 것을 보고, 무엇을 태웠느냐고 장교에게 묻는다. 대답을 듣자 그는 여드레 만에 처음으로 염주를 거두고, 진영으로 내려가 제 말 비사문 곁에 한동안 서 있다. 아무에게도 아무 말 없이.

blocks.html: Afterwards the groom leads out a young grey, too green for a marshal, the only horse left in the royal stable that nobody has been afraid of all week.
blocks.ko: 그 뒤 마부 아이가 어린 회색 말을 끌고 나온다. 대장군이 타기엔 아직 풋내기, 이번 주 내내 아무도 무서워하지 않은 왕궁 마구간의 마지막 말.

en: Name?

blocks.html: The boy shakes his head. He is still crying.
blocks.ko: 아이는 고개를 젓는다. 아직 울고 있다.

lines: ……부르기 쉽게 지었다. 그만 울고 불러 봐.
en: Hanseul.
…It’s easy to say. Stop crying and try it.

blocks.html: It is the last horse he names. He rides Hanseul out on the tenth day, and across the Yellow Mountain fields thirteen years later, and never once lets a groom catch him brushing it longer than the others.
blocks.ko: 그가 이름을 지어 준 마지막 말이다. 열째 날 그는 한슬을 타고 나가고, 열세 해 뒤 황산벌도 한슬을 타고 건넌다. 그리고 다른 말보다 그 녀석을 오래 빗질하는 모습을, 마부에게 단 한 번도 들키지 않는다.

blocks.label: The Stone
blocks.ko: 돌

blocks.html: Near midnight, at his desk in the palace, Yushin feels something warm against his wrist. He has carried his father’s stone in his sleeve for thirty years. It has never once been warm.
blocks.ko: 자정 무렵, 궁 안 책상 앞에서 유신은 손목에 닿는 따뜻한 것을 느낀다. 아버지의 돌을 소매에 넣고 다닌 지 서른 해. 한 번도 따뜻했던 적이 없다.

blocks.html: He sets it on the desk between the lamp and the grain tally. Chunchu came in to say there are three days of rice left and not to tell the kitchen. He looks at the stone the way he looks at a letter in a script he can’t read.
blocks.ko: 그는 그것을 등잔과 곡식 장부 사이에 내려놓는다. 쌀이 사흘 치 남았으니 부엌엔 말하지 말라고 전하러 들어온 춘추가, 못 읽는 글씨로 쓴 편지를 보듯 그 돌을 본다.

en: …It’s a rock.
Why is your rock warm?

lines: 아버지가 언덕 아래 샘에서 받은 거야. 언덕이 아버지를 부를 때마다 따뜻해졌지.
en: My father had it from a spring under the hill. It warmed when the hill wanted him.
It hasn’t since he died.

lines: 그래서 가겠다고. 성벽엔 역적이 있고 쌀은 사흘 치인데. 샘한테 뭘 물으러.
en: And you’re going. With a rebel on the wall and three days of rice. To ask a spring something.

lines: 비담은 내가 애초에 신라 사람이 아니래.
엿새 밤을 그 말 하게 뒀어. 알고 싶어—
en: Bidam says I was never of Silla.
Six nights I let him say it. I want to know—
…whether I am.
You’re asking a rock.
I’m asking him.

blocks.html: Chunchu doesn’t argue. He has just watched this man kill his own horse for a sky. He pours out the last of the wine, drinks half, and leaves the other half for whoever comes back.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 따지지 않는다. 그는 방금 이 남자가 하늘 하나 때문에 제 말을 죽이는 것을 보았다. 남은 술을 따라 반을 마시고, 나머지 반은 돌아올 사람 몫으로 남긴다.

blocks.html: Yushin puts the stone back in his sleeve. He will go down before light.
blocks.ko: 유신은 돌을 다시 소매에 넣는다. 날이 밝기 전에 내려갈 것이다.

blocks.html: A warm stone, a spring under a hill, and a father who once got very lost on purpose. Who was Kim Seohyun…?
blocks.ko: 따뜻한 돌, 언덕 아래의 샘, 그리고 일부러 아주 크게 길을 잃었던 아버지. 김서현은 누구였나…?

logline.en: Before there is a Yushin there is a road, and a young man on it who should be looking where he is going.
logline.ko: 유신이 있기 전에 길이 있다. 그리고 그 길 위에, 앞을 보고 다녀야 할 젊은이가 하나 있다.

images.at: You’ve ridden past this gate three times today.
images.alt: Long-shadow afternoon: Seohyun rides past the great gate for the third time, looking sideways; Manmyung waits in its shadow, arms folded, hiding a smile
images.prompt: Low dutch angle from the stone threshold of a grand timber gate in late afternoon: Manmyung leans against the gate post in the near foreground, arms folded, eyebrow raised, hiding a smile, looking out; beyond her Seohyun rides past in the street for the third time, twisting in the saddle to look back. Long low shadows rake the street between them. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — KIM SEOHYEON — FACE and garments from attached /ch_kim_seohyun.png (face only; invent a new pose). Demeanor: Yushin's father; Gaya blood, Silla duty, quiet. #3E8EF0 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | LADY MANMYUNG. Look: Young Sacred-Bone noblewoman, oval face, strong dark brows, amused knowing eyes, a stubborn chin; long black hair in a low coiled chignon with a plain gold pin. Dress: Rich plum-violet silk chima with a pale ivory jeogori and a deep plum ribbon; good silk she will ruin in the rain. Demeanor: Teasing, decisive, braver than the men around her; she makes the decisions and lets Seohyun think he did. #c98bb9 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Ember, cyan and leaf motes scatter in the steam. MANGA ACTION FRAME: a single seinen historical-manga action panel painted in ink and oil — bold dry-brush sumi-ink SPEED LINES streaking along the direction of motion, radial FOCUS LINES converging on the face or the blade, motion smears on legs, mane, cloth and steel, flung ink-splatter dirt and dust, extreme foreshortening and a hard dutch tilt so the frame itself feels like it is moving; heavy black ink masses against a few hard highlights, one gold accent. Faces stay clean webtoon ink line with fierce narrowed eyes. Full-bleed single frame: NO panel borders, NO speech bubbles, NO onomatopoeia or sound-effect lettering, NO text of any kind. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. images.alt: Lamplight at Manno: Manmyung sits up with the baby and squints at Seohyun, who is smiling too much, the warm grey stone in his sleeve
images.prompt: Over-the-shoulder from behind Seohyun kneeling just inside the door of a small governor’s house at Manno at night, dutch tilt: his hand in the near foreground turns a warm grey river stone half out of his sleeve; across the floor Manmyung sits up on the quilt with the baby asleep on her arm, squinting at him with suspicion and amusement. blocks.html: Before there is a Yushin there is a road, and a young man on it who should be looking where he is going.
blocks.ko: 유신이 있기 전에 길이 있다. 그리고 그 길 위에, 앞을 보고 다녀야 할 젊은이가 하나 있다.

blocks.html: Kim Seohyun is the son of Gaya’s last prince. In the capital, that’s the kind of fact people bring up just after he leaves the room. His father rode in the cart that handed the kingdom over, then spent his life proving it had been a bargain. On one road he took an enemy king, four generals and ten thousand heads. The family is True Bone now. The rank opens most doors in the capital. It opens the best ones least.
blocks.ko: 김서현은 가야 마지막 왕자의 아들이다. 도읍에서 그건 그가 방을 나서자마자 사람들이 꺼내는 종류의 사실이다. 그의 아버지는 나라를 넘기는 수레에 탔고, 남은 평생 그게 남는 장사였음을 증명했다. 한 길에서 적의 왕 하나, 장수 넷, 머리 만 개를 거두었다. 이제 그 집안은 진골이다. 그 신분은 도읍의 문 대부분을 연다. 가장 좋은 문은 가장 덜 연다.

blocks.html: He is young and polite and so used to being the Gaya boy in the room that he apologises before anyone has accused him of anything. He sits a horse better than he sits a banquet.
blocks.ko: 그는 젊고 예의 바르며, 방 안의 가야 녀석 노릇에 너무 익숙해서 누가 뭐라 하기도 전에 먼저 사과부터 한다. 연회 자리보다 말 등에 더 잘 앉는다.

blocks.html: The best gate on the street belongs to Sukhuljong, the great king’s younger brother. Royal on every side. His daughter Manmyung is standing in it when Seohyun rides past. He looks. The histories, which don’t usually notice such things, record exactly how.
blocks.ko: 그 거리에서 가장 좋은 대문은 대왕의 아우 숙흘종의 것이다. 어느 쪽으로 따져도 왕족이다. 서현이 말을 타고 지날 때, 그의 딸 만명이 그 대문에 서 있다. 그가 쳐다본다. 이런 일을 좀처럼 적지 않는 사서가 그 눈길만은 정확히 적어 두었다.

blocks.hanja: 初，舒玄路見葛文王立宗之子肅訖宗之女萬明，心悅而目挑之，不待媒妁而合。
blocks.html: At first, Seohyun saw on the road Manmyung, daughter of Sukhuljong, son of Galmun-wang Ipjong. His heart was glad, and he courted her with his eyes; and without waiting for a go-between, they came together.
blocks.ko: 처음에 서현이 길에서 갈문왕 입종의 아들 숙흘종의 딸 만명을 보고, 마음에 기뻐하여 눈으로 꾀어, 중매를 기다리지 않고 맺어졌다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biography of Kim Yushin, part 1

blocks.label: The Gate
blocks.ko: 그 문

blocks.html: The first time, he looks and keeps riding and nearly puts his horse into a charcoal cart. The second time he has an errand ready at the far end of the street, which does not exist. By the third the errand has run out, and he is only a man on a horse going the wrong way slowly.
blocks.ko: 처음엔 보고, 계속 가다가, 하마터면 말을 숯 수레에 처박을 뻔한다. 두 번째엔 거리 저 끝에 볼일이 있다는 핑계를 준비해 온다. 그런 볼일은 없다. 세 번째쯤 되자 핑계도 바닥나서, 그는 그냥 엉뚱한 방향으로 천천히 가는 말 탄 사내일 뿐이다.

blocks.speaker: Manmyung’s maid
en: Agassi. It’s him again.
Same horse. Same— he’s pretending he isn’t looking.
lines: 같은 말이에요. 같은— 안 보는 척해요.

en: He’s terrible at it.
Don’t look. …No, look. I want to see what he does.
lines: 보지 마. …아니, 봐. 뭐 하나 보게.

blocks.html: Then she does something nobody on that street has seen a Sacred Bone daughter do. She steps down off the threshold into the dust.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 그 거리 누구도 성골 집 딸이 하는 걸 본 적 없는 일을 한다. 문턱에서 흙바닥으로 내려선다.

en: You’ve ridden past this gate three times today.
Is the road that bad, or are you lost?
lines: 오늘만 이 문 앞을 세 번 지나가셨어요.
길이 그렇게 험해요, 아니면 길을 잃으셨어요?

en: I— the horse—
…It’s lost. I’m only on it.
lines: …말이 길을 잃었소. 나는 타고 있을 뿐이고.

en: It looked fine the first time.
Nearly ate a charcoal cart. But fine.
lines: 숯 수레를 먹을 뻔하긴 했지만. 멀쩡했어요.

en: That was— the cart was in the wrong—
Kim Seohyun. That’s— I should have said that first. Is it rude? I don’t know the rule for this.
lines: 김서현이오. 그게— 그 말부터 했어야 했는데. 무례한 거요? 이럴 땐 법도를 모르겠소.

en: There isn’t one. That’s why it’s fun.
And I know who you are. Everyone on this street knows who you are.
lines: 법도 같은 거 없어요. 그래서 재밌는 거고.
그리고 누군지 알아요. 이 거리 사람은 다 알아요.

en: …Ah.
The Gaya one.
The one with the nice horse.
Then let it get lost again tomorrow. Same hour.
lines: 그럼 내일도 길 잃게 하세요. 같은 시각에.

blocks.speaker: Manmyung’s maid
en: Agassi—!

blocks.label: Getting Lost
blocks.ko: 길 잃기

blocks.html: It gets lost every day for a season. The maid starts timing her errands by it. The charcoal man learns to pull over. Nobody sends a matchmaker, because a matchmaker would have to walk into Sukhuljong’s hall and say the word Gaya out loud.
blocks.ko: 말은 한 철 내내 날마다 길을 잃는다. 하녀는 심부름 시간을 거기에 맞추기 시작하고, 숯장수는 미리 비켜서는 법을 배운다. 아무도 중매쟁이를 보내지 않는다. 중매쟁이라면 숙흘종의 대청에 들어가 가야라는 말을 소리 내어 해야 할 테니까.

blocks.html: By the end of summer they have stopped pretending about the horse. He leaves it at the bottom of the lane and walks up, and she talks to him through the side gate with the bar still down, because a gate with the bar down is technically closed.
blocks.ko: 여름이 끝날 무렵엔 둘 다 말 핑계를 그만둔다. 그는 말을 골목 아래에 매어 두고 걸어 올라오고, 그녀는 빗장을 지른 채로 쪽문 너머로 그와 이야기한다. 빗장이 걸려 있으면, 엄밀히 말해 문은 닫힌 것이니까.

en: You’re late.
The horse?
The horse is fine. The horse is better than me.
They kept us at the Ministry. There’s talk of a posting.
Where?
They haven’t said. North, probably. They send Gaya men north.
Somewhere with a lot of Goguryeo and not much—
lines: 아직 말 안 했소. 아마 북쪽이겠지. 가야 사람은 북으로 보내니.

en: Not much me.
…I was going to say not much rice.
Liar.

blocks.html: Then she lifts the bar. Nobody on that street has seen a Sacred Bone daughter lift her own bar, either.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 그녀가 빗장을 올린다. 그 거리에서 성골 집 딸이 제 손으로 빗장을 올리는 것도 본 사람은 없다.

en: Come in.
Not the front, idiot. The mulberry shed. Nobody goes in there after dark.
lines: 앞문 말고요, 바보. 뽕나무 헛간. 해 지면 아무도 안 가요.

en: Agassi, I— your father— if anyone—
There are rules for this. I don’t know them, but there are—
lines: 이런 데도 법도가 있을 텐데요. 저는 모르지만, 분명히—

en: Then they’ll have something to talk about besides your horse.
lines: 그럼 말 얘기 말고 다른 얘깃거리가 생기겠네요.

blocks.html: The shed smells of leaves and silkworms. She has his collar open before he has finished apologising for it. He is a careful man, and she is not a careful woman, and somewhere past midnight he stops being careful too.
blocks.ko: 헛간에서는 뽕잎과 누에 냄새가 난다. 그가 사과를 다 하기도 전에 그녀는 그의 옷깃을 풀어 놓았다. 그는 조심스러운 사내고, 그녀는 조심 같은 건 모르는 여자다. 자정이 지난 어디쯤에서 그도 조심을 그만둔다.

en: That was— I should have— a go-between, a proper—
Your father should have been asked first.
lines: 방금 그건— 제가 먼저— 중매라도, 제대로—

en: Shh. You talk a lot for a man with no shirt on.
Same hour tomorrow. Bring the horse, so it looks like an errand.
lines: 쉿. 웃통 벗은 남자치고 말이 너무 많아요.
내일 같은 시간. 말도 데려와요. 심부름 온 것처럼 보이게.

blocks.html: He comes the next night, and the next. A go-between would have taken a season. They do not have a season. Some nights they barely have the walk up from the lane.
blocks.ko: 그는 다음 날 밤에도, 그다음 날 밤에도 온다. 중매를 넣었으면 한 철은 걸렸을 것이다. 그들에겐 한 철이 없다. 어떤 밤엔 골목에서 올라오는 길조차 길다.

blocks.html: The posting comes in the autumn: governor of Manno, a county far up the Goguryeo road, a wooden wall and a granary and a great many hills that change hands. He comes to the side gate with the seal still in his sleeve.
blocks.ko: 임지는 가을에 정해진다. 고구려로 가는 길 저 위쪽 고을 만노의 태수. 나무 성벽 하나, 곳간 하나, 그리고 주인이 자꾸 바뀌는 수많은 언덕. 그는 관인을 아직 소매에 넣은 채 쪽문으로 온다.

en: Manno.
It’s— a long way. Ten days if the passes are open. The house is small. I haven’t seen it, but they said small, and the way they said it—
I’m asking badly. I’m asking if you would—
lines: 멀— 멀리 있소. 고개가 열려 있으면 열흘. 관사는 작소. 보진 못했지만 작다고 하더이다, 그 말투가 영—
말을 엉망으로 하고 있소. 내 말은, 혹시 그대가—

en: Yes.
—come with— I haven’t finished.
Then finish. It’s still yes.

blocks.html: The maid tells nobody. The charcoal man tells everybody. Her father knows by the next morning.
blocks.ko: 하녀는 아무한테도 말하지 않는다. 숯장수는 모두에게 말한다. 이튿날 아침이면 그녀의 아버지가 안다.

blocks.label: Sukhuljong’s Hall
blocks.ko: 숙흘종의 대청

blocks.html: Sukhuljong takes the news sitting down, the way he takes most things, without looking up from his cup. He is a king’s son and a king’s brother, and he has never once in his life been the one left standing.
blocks.ko: 숙흘종은 대부분의 일을 받아들이듯 그 소식도 앉은 채로, 잔에서 눈도 떼지 않고 받는다. 그는 왕의 아들이고 왕의 아우이며, 평생 한 번도 서 있는 쪽이었던 적이 없다.

en: Sit.
I’ll stand.
The charcoal man has told the whole street.
Of all the people in this city. The charcoal man.
lines: 숯장수가 온 동네에 다 떠들고 다닌다.
이 서라벌에 사람이 그렇게 많은데. 하필 숯장수가.

en: He does sell good charcoal.
Pregnant with an unknown man’s child… what a disgrace!
lines: 누군지도 모를 사내의 아이를 배다니… 이 무슨 망신이냐!

en: Unknown? Father, you just told me who sold the charcoal.
Half of Surabol watched him ride past our gate. Three times in one morning.
lines: 모를 사내요? 아버지, 숯장수 얘기까지 다 하셨잖아요.
서라벌 절반이 그 사람 말 타고 우리 문 앞 지나가는 거 봤어요. 하루 아침에 세 번.

en: Muryuk’s boy. The cart family.
lines: 무력의 아들. 수레 타고 올라온 집.

en: Grandfather came in a sedan chair. That’s a cart with a roof.
lines: 할아버지는 가마 타고 오셨잖아요. 지붕 달린 수레요.

en: …He leaves for Manno.
I know. I’m going with him.
You’re going to the back house.
Don’t blame him. It was me. He’d still be apologising to the horse.
I lifted the bar myself. Every night.
lines: 그 사람 탓하지 마세요. 저예요. 그 사람은 아직도 말한테 사과하고 있을걸요.

en: …Every night?
Every night.
Take her to the back house.
And somebody fix that bar.
lines: 그리고 누가 그 빗장 좀 고쳐 놔라.

blocks.html: He shuts her in a house apart at the back of the compound and sets men on the door. Surabol has a word for what the two of them did, and it is not a polite one, and for a few weeks it is the only thing the city talks about.
blocks.ko: 그는 딸을 집 뒤편 별채에 가두고 문에 사람을 세운다. 서라벌에는 두 사람이 한 짓을 가리키는 말이 있는데, 점잖은 말은 아니다. 몇 주 동안 도성은 그 이야기만 한다.

blocks.label: The House Apart
blocks.ko: 별채

blocks.html: The guards are two cousins off one of Sukhuljong’s farms, chosen because they cannot be bribed and cannot read, and by the fourth night they have run out of things to say to each other.
blocks.ko: 경비는 숙흘종네 농장에서 데려온 사촌 둘이다. 매수가 안 되고 글을 못 읽어서 뽑혔다. 나흘째 밤이 되자 서로 할 말이 바닥난다.

blocks.speaker: First guard
en: You think he’ll come?

blocks.speaker: Second guard
en: The Gaya one? He says sorry to his own horse.
He’s not coming over a wall.
lines: 가야 놈? 그놈 제 말한테도 미안하다는 놈이야.

blocks.speaker: First guard
en: I heard he leaves for the north day after tomorrow. First light.

blocks.speaker: Second guard
en: Good. Then we go home.

blocks.html: Inside, Manmyung has stopped eating to make a point and started again because the point was only hurting her. She has counted the boards in the ceiling. At the foot of the back wall, where the drain runs out, there is a gap, and she has been looking at it for three days the way her father looks at furniture.
blocks.ko: 안에서 만명은 시위하느라 밥을 끊었다가, 그 시위가 저만 아프게 한다는 걸 알고 다시 먹기 시작했다. 천장 널빤지도 다 세어 보았다. 뒷담 아래, 도랑물이 빠져나가는 자리에 틈이 하나 있다. 그녀는 사흘째 그 틈을, 아버지가 가구를 보듯 쳐다보고 있다.

blocks.html: On the last night it storms. Lightning comes down on the door itself, and the guards do what men do when the sky picks out the house they are guarding, which is run. In the noise Manmyung goes out through a gap in the wall so low that she has to crawl, in her good silk, in the mud.
blocks.ko: 마지막 밤, 폭풍이 친다. 벼락이 바로 그 문에 떨어지고, 하늘이 제가 지키는 집을 골라 내리치면 사람들이 하는 짓을 경비들도 한다. 도망친다. 그 소란 속에 만명은 담장 밑 틈으로 빠져나간다. 기어야 할 만큼 낮은 틈을, 좋은 비단옷을 입은 채, 진흙 속으로.

blocks.speaker: Second guard
en: Heaven— it hit the door, it hit the DOOR—

blocks.speaker: First guard
en: Leave it! It’s burning, leave the door, leave it—

blocks.html: He is at the bottom of the lane with two horses, because he has been there every one of the four nights, in case. He sees a shape come out of the drain on its elbows, stand up and walk toward him through the rain like a woman going to market.
blocks.ko: 그는 말 두 마리를 데리고 골목 아래에 있다. 나흘 밤 내내, 혹시나 해서 거기 있었다. 웬 형체 하나가 팔꿈치로 도랑을 기어 나와 일어서더니, 장에 가는 여자처럼 빗속을 걸어 그에게 온다.

en: Don’t— don’t look at the dress.
Is the horse lost tonight?
You— the lightning— are you hurt? Your hands—
My hands are fine. Answer the question.
…No.
Tonight it knows exactly where it’s going.
lines: 오늘 밤엔 어디로 가는지 똑똑히 알고 있소.

blocks.html: She kisses him before he can get her on the horse. Hard, in the rain, with drain-mud on her chin and both hands in his hair. The horses wait like men who have seen this before.
blocks.ko: 그가 그녀를 말에 올리기도 전에 그녀가 입을 맞춘다. 빗속에서, 세게, 턱에 도랑 진흙을 묻힌 채 두 손을 그의 머리칼에 넣고. 말 두 마리는 이런 걸 전에도 본 사내들처럼 기다린다.

en: …There. Now we can go.
Your father will send riders.
Let him. He’ll pretend to be furious for a year.
Then he’ll write and ask what the baby’s called.
lines: 보내라 그래. 일 년은 화난 척하실 거야.
그다음엔 편지로 애 이름이 뭐냐고 물으시겠지.

en: …What baby?
Ride, Seohyun.

blocks.html: They ride north in the rain. Behind them, two cousins are trying to explain a door to Sukhuljong.
blocks.ko: 둘은 빗속을 달려 북으로 간다. 뒤에서는 사촌 둘이 숙흘종에게 문 이야기를 해명하느라 애쓰고 있다.

blocks.label: Manno
blocks.ko: 만노

blocks.html: Manno is a wooden wall, a granary, a county office with a leaking roof, and hills that have changed hands more often than the clerks can keep up with. She learns the granary. He learns the hills. Neither of them learns to cook, and by the second month the clerk’s wife has taken pity on them.
blocks.ko: 만노는 나무 성벽 하나, 곳간 하나, 지붕 새는 관아 하나, 그리고 아전들이 따라잡지 못할 만큼 자주 주인이 바뀐 언덕들이다. 그녀는 곳간을 익히고, 그는 언덕을 익힌다. 둘 다 밥 짓는 법은 못 익혀서, 두 달째부터는 아전의 아내가 딱하게 여겨 챙겨 준다.

blocks.html: The county house has one room with a door that shuts. The clerks learn not to knock before noon.
blocks.ko: 관아에는 문이 닫히는 방이 하나 있다. 아전들은 정오 전에는 그 문을 두드리지 않는 법을 배운다.

blocks.html: He has a dream on a gyeongjin night and tells nobody for three weeks, because a Gaya man who dreams of stars coming down on him does not say so in a county office. Then, on a sinchuk night, she sits up in the dark and shakes him.
blocks.ko: 그는 경진일 밤에 꿈을 꾸고 삼 주 동안 아무에게도 말하지 않는다. 별이 제게 내려오는 꿈을 꾼 가야 사내는 관아에서 그런 말을 하지 않는 법이다. 그러다 신축일 밤, 그녀가 어둠 속에서 벌떡 일어나 그를 흔든다.

en: Wake up. Wake up, I had— there was a boy.
In gold. Armour, all gold. He came in on a cloud, right into the hall, through the door like he owned the house. He looked at me.
lines: 일어나요. 일어나 봐요, 꿈에— 애가 있었어요.
금빛으로. 갑옷이 온통 금빛. 구름을 타고 들어왔어요, 대청으로, 제집인 것처럼 문으로 쑥. 날 쳐다봤어요.

en: …I had one too. Three weeks ago.
Two stars. A red one and a yellow one. They came down on me. Not on the house. On me.
lines: 별 둘이오. 붉은 놈 하나, 누런 놈 하나. 내게 내려왔소. 집이 아니라. 내게.

en: Three weeks.
Stars fell on you and you didn’t tell me for three weeks.
lines: 별이 떨어졌는데 삼 주 동안 말을 안 했어요?

en: I thought it might be the soup.
Pfft— the soup—
Come here, you. Come here.

blocks.html: She is with child by spring. She is still with child the following spring, and the clerk’s wife, who has delivered half the county, stops coming to check and starts coming to stare.
blocks.ko: 봄이 되자 그녀는 아이를 가진다. 그다음 봄에도 여전히 아이를 가진 채다. 고을 아이 절반을 받아 낸 아전의 아내는 살피러 오던 걸 그만두고 구경하러 오기 시작한다.

blocks.html: Word reaches Surabol before the spring rains do. A Sacred Bone daughter, with child, in a county house, and no wedding anyone was invited to. The city has been waiting for exactly this. Three banquets in a row talk about nothing else.
blocks.ko: 소문은 봄비보다 먼저 서라벌에 닿는다. 성골 집 딸이 아이를 뱄다. 시골 관아에서. 누구도 초대받은 적 없는 혼례로. 서라벌은 바로 이걸 기다리고 있었다. 연회 세 번이 내리 그 얘기뿐이다.

en: They’re saying things in Surabol. About you. About— there was no wedding, and now—
lines: 서라벌에서 말들이 많답니다. 당신에 대해. 그— 혼례도 없었는데, 이제—

en: Let them. They’re only saying what we did.
And we did it very well.
lines: 하라고 해요. 우리가 한 걸 말하는 것뿐인데.

blocks.speaker: The clerk’s wife
en: Twenty months, my lady.
I’ve had cows do it faster.
Either that child is something, or somebody counted wrong at the start, and I won’t say which. You’re the governor’s.
lines: 애가 보통이 아니거나, 처음부터 누가 셈을 틀렸거나. 어느 쪽인지는 말 안 해요. 사또댁이시니까.

en: Say it. I want to hear you say it.
lines: 말해 봐요. 말하는 거 듣고 싶어요.

blocks.speaker: The clerk’s wife
en: …The child’s something.

blocks.html: The boy is born in the county house at Manno. The clerk’s wife turns him over to wash him. She stops with the cloth in her hand.
blocks.ko: 아이는 만노의 관아 집에서 태어난다. 아전의 아내가 씻기려고 아이를 뒤집는다. 그리고 천을 든 채 멈춘다.

blocks.speaker: The clerk’s wife
en: My lady. His back.
Look— there. There’s seven. Like someone pressed them in with a thumb.
lines: 보세요— 여기. 일곱 개예요. 누가 엄지로 꾹꾹 찍은 것처럼.

en: Seven what?

blocks.speaker: The clerk’s wife
en: Stars, sir. The Dipper. On a baby.
I’m going to sit down.

lines: 눈은 먼 옛날 어느 할머니 눈이래요. 서현 말로는 배가 한 척 있었대요.
en: Sit, then. Sit.
And his eyes are some grandmother’s, a long way back. Seohyun says there was a boat.

blocks.hanja: 庾信公以眞平王十七年乙卯生，稟精七曜，故背有七星文，又多神異。
blocks.html: Lord Yushin was born in the eulmyo year, the seventeenth of King Jinpyeong. He was endowed with the essence of the Seven Luminaries, and so his back bore a pattern of seven stars; and there were many other wonders about him.
blocks.ko: 유신공은 진평왕 17년 을묘에 태어났다. 칠요의 정기를 타고났으므로 등에 일곱 별 무늬가 있었고, 또 신이한 일이 많았다.
blocks.source: Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) bk. 1, Marvels — Kim Yushin

blocks.html: Naming him takes longer than carrying him did.
blocks.ko: 이름 짓는 데는 품는 것보다 더 오래 걸린다.

en: Gyeongjin.
I want to call him for the night I dreamed. That’s where he came from.
lines: 꿈꾼 그 밤 이름으로 부르고 싶소. 그 밤에서 왔으니.

en: You can’t name a child after a day.
Even I know that, and I ran away from all my tutors.
lines: 날로 애 이름을 지을 순 없어요.
선생님들한테서 죄다 도망친 나도 그건 알아요.

en: I know. I know.
But gyeong, written down, looks like yu. And jin, said quickly, is nearly sin.
And there was a man in the old books. A scholar. Yu Xin. A good man, they say.
So it isn’t a day. It’s a scholar. Nobody can say anything.
lines: 그런데 경(庚)을 써 놓으면 유(庾)랑 닮았소. 진(辰)은 빨리 말하면 신(信)이랑 거의 같고.
그리고 옛 책에 그런 사람이 있었소. 선비요. 유신. 어진 사람이었다 하더이다.
그러니 날이 아니라 선비 이름이오. 아무도 뭐라 못 하오.

en: You’ve been working on this for months.
…Twenty.

blocks.html: They bury the afterbirth on the high hill behind the county, the way you do with a child you mean to keep, and the hill keeps the name.
blocks.ko: 그들은 아이의 태를 고을 뒤 높은 산에 묻는다. 꼭 붙들어 두고 싶은 아이에게 하듯이. 그리고 산이 그 이름을 지닌다.

en: Yushin.
Say it to my father, next time you’re in Surabol. Say it at his gate.
lines: 다음에 서라벌에 가시거든 우리 아버지께 말씀하세요. 그 문 앞에서.

en: …He won’t open it.
Then say it louder.

blocks.label: The Name at the Gate
blocks.ko: 문 앞의 이름

blocks.html: A few weeks after the birth he rides to Surabol and says the name at Sukhuljong’s gate, loudly, to a street that has stopped to listen. The gate does not open. A steward comes out instead.
blocks.ko: 아이가 태어나고 몇 주 뒤 그는 서라벌로 가서, 숙흘종의 문 앞에서 그 이름을 크게 말한다. 거리가 걸음을 멈추고 듣는다. 문은 열리지 않는다. 대신 청지기가 나온다.

blocks.speaker: Sukhuljong’s steward
en: His lordship is unwell.
He expects to be unwell for some years. He asked me to say it in exactly those words.
lines: 앞으로 몇 해는 편찮으실 것 같다 하십니다. 꼭 이 말 그대로 전하라 하셨습니다.

en: Tell him—
Tell him the boy has his mother’s mouth.
He’ll know what that means.

blocks.speaker: Sukhuljong’s steward
en: …I’ll tell him, sir.
He won’t like it.

blocks.label: The Spring
blocks.ko: 샘

blocks.html: He rides home the long way because he does not want to arrive yet. The road goes over a ridge beyond the city that nobody uses, and by noon he wants water more than he has ever wanted a shrine. When heat breathes out of the hillside he calls it a spring and gets down.
blocks.ko: 그는 아직 도착하고 싶지 않아서 먼 길로 돌아간다. 길은 도성 너머 아무도 쓰지 않는 능선을 넘고, 한낮이 되자 그는 어느 사당보다도 물이 간절하다. 산허리에서 열기가 훅 뿜어져 나오자 그는 그것을 샘이라 부르고 말에서 내린다.

blocks.html: Under the hill three sisters keep the heat in the stone, the water in the dark and the moss on the roots: Golhwa, Hyullé, and Narim, the eldest, who also keeps the rules. They have gone centuries without a man coming down to them, and the hill has just told them about hooves on the road.
blocks.ko: 언덕 아래에서 세 자매가 돌 속의 열기와 어둠 속의 물과 뿌리 위의 이끼를 지킨다. 골화, 혈례, 그리고 규칙까지 지키는 맏이 나림. 몇백 년째 사내 하나 내려온 적이 없는데, 방금 언덕이 길 위의 말발굽 소리를 일러 주었다.

en: Hooves! Unni. Unni, hooves. Someone stopped.
lines: 말발굽! 언니. 언니, 말발굽. 누가 멈췄어.

en: Someone always stops. They drink, they piss in the stream, they leave.
lines: 누군 늘 멈춰. 마시고, 개울에 오줌 누고, 가.

en: …This one’s crying a little.
Crying? Let me see— move your elbow—
Fox. Let’s be a fox. Foxes are fun.
A grandmother. Then he drinks and bows and goes, and nobody… nobody gets hurt.
lines: 할머니. 그럼 마시고 절하고 가고, 아무도… 아무도 안 다쳐.

en: Try both. Then I pick.
lines: 둘 다 해 봐. 그다음에 내가 골라.

blocks.html: They try both. The fox frightens the horse. The grandmother makes him kneel and offer her his waterskin with both hands, which is so polite that Golhwa groans out loud through the rock. Narim picks the last face herself: three young women in white jeogori over moss-green and ember and pale water-blue, sitting on the far rock as if they had always been there.
blocks.ko: 둘 다 해 본다. 여우는 말을 놀라게 한다. 할머니에게는 그가 무릎을 꿇고 두 손으로 물주머니를 바치는데, 그게 하도 공손해서 골화가 바위 너머로 소리 내어 앓는다. 마지막 얼굴은 나림이 직접 고른다. 이끼빛과 불씨빛과 연한 물빛 치마 위에 흰 저고리를 입은 젊은 여자 셋이, 처음부터 거기 있었던 것처럼 건너편 바위에 앉아 있다.

blocks.html: He is still calling it a spring when the ground gives under his boot. He comes down through warm dark into a bowl of black water under stone and stands up coughing in a cloud of steam, soaked to the skin, his sword still somehow in his hand.
blocks.ko: 그가 아직 샘이라고 부르고 있을 때 발밑의 땅이 꺼진다. 따뜻한 어둠을 지나 돌 아래 검은 물웅덩이로 떨어진 그는, 김이 자욱한 속에서 기침을 하며 일어선다. 흠뻑 젖은 채로, 어째선지 칼은 아직 손에 쥐고.

en: Who— forgive me— who lives here?
I was looking for water. There was an old woman just now, up there—
lines: 물을 찾고 있었소. 방금 위에 웬 노파가—

en: …That was me. Sorry.
You found your water. All of it at once.
Put the sword down, please. You’ll cut the steam.
Hi. I’m Golhwa. That’s unni. That’s Hyullé, she won’t say hello unless you look at her first.
What’s your name? Say it slow.
lines: 안녕. 난 골화. 저긴 언니. 저긴 혈례, 먼저 쳐다봐 줘야 인사해.

en: Kim. Kim Seohyun.
Are you… I mean. People?

blocks.html: At the surname all three of them go quiet. Kim is the sound their own steam makes coming off the water, and nobody has ever said it to them as a name.
blocks.ko: 성을 듣는 순간 셋 다 조용해진다. 김은 그들의 물에서 피어오르는 김이 내는 바로 그 소리인데, 누구도 그것을 이름으로 그들에게 말해 준 적이 없다.

en: Kim.
Say it again. No, I heard you. It just… sticks.
lines: 다시 말해 봐. 아니, 들었어. 그냥… 자꾸 붙어.

en: Kim.
…Then the house rules apply. Golhwa. Chin.

blocks.html: Golhwa is across the pool before he can step back, a wet hand under his jaw, turning his face to the light like a horse trader.
blocks.ko: 그가 물러서기도 전에 골화가 웅덩이를 건너와, 젖은 손으로 그의 턱을 받치고 말 장수처럼 얼굴을 빛 쪽으로 돌린다.

en: Smooth. Shaved this morning? For who— oh. For the gate. Poor thing.
Chin passes, unni.
lines: 매끈해. 아침에 밀었네? 누구 보라고— 아. 그 문. 불쌍해라.

en: Second rule. Nobody stands in this water dressed.
The steam doesn’t talk to cloth.
lines: 두 번째 규칙. 이 물엔 옷 입고 서 있는 사람 없어요.

en: I— I have a wife. She’s— we have a son, he’s—
I’m sorry. I should have said that first.
lines: 나는— 아내가 있소. 그 사람이— 아들도 있소, 이제—

en: We didn’t ask about her.
…You can turn around. We won’t— we won’t look.
Speak for yourself.

blocks.html: He turns his back, takes off the wet clothes and folds them badly on a rock, because he does not know what else to do with his hands. Hyullé does not look, mostly. Golhwa does not pretend. Narim waits until he is in the water to the chest and then lets out a breath, which nobody remarks on.
blocks.ko: 그는 등을 돌리고 젖은 옷을 벗어 바위 위에 서툴게 갠다. 손을 달리 어디 둘지 몰라서. 혈례는 대체로 안 본다. 골화는 안 보는 척도 안 한다. 나림은 그가 가슴께까지 물에 들어갈 때까지 기다렸다가 숨을 내쉬는데, 아무도 그 얘기는 하지 않는다.

en: Today we are the mouths the hill uses when it gets tired of being stone.
Ask it one thing, Kim. From the water. Once.
lines: 오늘 저희는 언덕이 돌인 게 지겨울 때 쓰는 입이에요.
하나만 물으세요, 김. 물속에서. 한 번.

blocks.html: He thinks of the gate. He thinks of a girl crawling through a hole in a wall in her good silk.
blocks.ko: 그는 그 문을 생각한다. 좋은 비단옷을 입고 담장 구멍으로 기어 나오던 여자를 생각한다.

en: I have a son. A few weeks old.
My wife’s father won’t say his name. I stood at his gate this morning and said it for him, and—
I don’t know what to ask for him. I don’t know what you ask for a boy like that.
lines: 아내의 아버지는 그 아이 이름을 입에 안 올리오. 오늘 아침 그 문 앞에서 내가 대신 불렀는데—
그 애를 위해 뭘 물어야 할지 모르겠소. 그런 아이를 위해선 뭘 묻는 거요.

blocks.html: Their eyes go solid, green and cyan and ember, and the cave stops being funny.
blocks.ko: 그들의 눈이 통째로 물든다. 초록, 청록, 불씨. 동굴은 더 이상 우습지 않다.

blocks.speaker: The Hill
en: The child will be the measure two countries cannot share.
They will call him a blade and mean a border.
When they say he was never of them, the blade will still be Kim.
He will cut more than he is given. Don’t ask who bleeds.
lines: 그 아이는 두 나라가 나눠 갖지 못하는 자가 될 거예요.
그들이 자기네 사람이 아니라 할 때에도, 그 칼은 김으로 남을 거예요.
받은 것보다 더 자를 거예요. 누가 피를 흘리는지는 묻지 말아요.

blocks.html: Narim puts a river stone in his hand, ordinary and grey and too warm for the cave.
blocks.ko: 나림이 그의 손에 강돌 하나를 쥐여 준다. 평범한 회색 돌인데, 동굴에 있기엔 너무 따뜻하다.

en: Keep it in your sleeve.
When it’s warm, come back. Same road, same water. One question.
When you’re too old to climb, send the boy.
lines: 따뜻해지면 다시 오세요. 같은 길, 같은 물. 질문 하나.
오를 수 없을 만큼 늙으면, 그 아이를 보내세요.

en: Shaved.
…Can I tell his mother?
Tell her it was a spring.
Everybody says that.

blocks.label: Home to Manno
blocks.ko: 다시 만노

blocks.html: He rides north with a stone in his sleeve that will not cool. At Manno, Manmyung is sitting up with the baby in the lamplight, and she asks him where he has been all day, and he tells her he found a spring.
blocks.ko: 그는 식지 않는 돌을 소매에 넣고 북쪽으로 달린다. 만노에서는 만명이 등불 아래 아기를 안고 앉아 있다. 하루 종일 어디 있었느냐고 그녀가 묻자, 그는 샘을 찾았다고 말한다.

en: A spring.
…You’re smiling like a man who found three.
lines: …샘을 세 개쯤 찾은 사람처럼 웃고 계시네요.

en: …It was a very good spring.
Mm.
Your hair’s wet. It hasn’t rained in a week.
lines: 머리가 젖었네요. 일주일째 비 한 방울 안 왔는데.

blocks.label: Fifteen
blocks.ko: 열다섯

blocks.html: The boy grows up at the edge of things, in county houses on the northern road. There’s a younger brother, and two little sisters the house calls by baby names. They’ll grow up to cause a great deal of trouble over a skirt. One of them is Munhee.
blocks.ko: 아이는 변두리에서 자란다. 북쪽 길가 고을 관아들을 옮겨 다니며. 남동생 하나, 그리고 집안에서 아명으로 부르는 어린 누이 둘이 있다. 둘은 자라서 치마 한 벌을 두고 큰 소동을 일으킬 것이다. 그중 하나가 문희다.

blocks.html: At fifteen he is made a hwarang, and the boys who follow him start calling themselves the Dragon-Flower Band. Seohyun hears it from a clerk before he hears it from his son.
blocks.ko: 열다섯에 그는 화랑이 되고, 그를 따르는 아이들은 스스로를 용화향도라 부르기 시작한다. 서현은 그 소식을 아들보다 아전에게서 먼저 듣는다.

blocks.html: The morning Yushin leaves for Surabol, his father stops him at the gate of the county house to look at his headband.
blocks.ko: 유신이 서라벌로 떠나는 아침, 아버지가 관사 문간에서 그를 세워 머리띠를 본다.

en: You’ve got it on crooked.
It’s fine, Father.
It’s crooked. Hold still.
In Surabol they’ll look at the headband before they look at you. They’ll look for anything.
lines: 서라벌에선 너보다 띠부터 볼 거다. 뭐든 찾으려고 볼 거야.

en: Because we’re Gaya.
…Because you’re new.
Mostly because you’re new.

blocks.html: He reties it with both hands, too tight, and then does it a third time. Manmyung watches from the doorway and lets him.
blocks.ko: 그는 두 손으로 다시 맨다. 너무 꽉. 그러고는 세 번째로 또 맨다. 만명은 문간에서 지켜보며 그냥 둔다.

en: Let him go. He’ll be late for his own band.
Mother—
And stop at your grandfather’s gate on the way.
Don’t knock. Just let them see you.
lines: 가는 길에 외할아버지 댁 문 앞에 들러.

blocks.label: Daeyang
blocks.ko: 대량주

blocks.html: Seohyun rises the way a Gaya man rises in the capital. One rank at a time, each signed by someone who remembers the box. By the end he is third rank in the kingdom. He governs the march that faces the enemy, from the fortress at Daeya.
blocks.ko: 서현은 가야 사람이 도읍에서 오르는 방식으로 오른다. 한 계단씩, 매번 그 상자를 기억하는 누군가의 서명을 받으며. 마지막엔 나라의 셋째 품계에 이른다. 그는 대야성에 앉아 적과 마주한 변경을 다스린다.

blocks.html: In the evenings he walks the wall at Daeya. Baekje is a line of hills to the west that the sun goes down behind.
blocks.ko: 저녁이면 그는 대야성 성벽을 걷는다. 백제는 서쪽으로 늘어선 언덕들이고, 해가 그 뒤로 진다.

blocks.speaker: A Daeya officer
en: They say this wall can’t be taken, sir.
lines: 이 성은 못 뺏는다들 합니다, 나리.

en: They say that about— every wall, I think. I’ve heard it about four.
Just— keep the granary dry. And know whose hands the keys are in.
My wife ran the granary at Manno. She’d tell you the same. She’d tell you better.
lines: 그런 말은— 성마다 다 하더이다. 내가 들은 것만 넷이오.
그냥— 곳간이나 마르게 두시오. 열쇠가 누구 손에 있는지 알고.
만노에선 아내가 곳간을 맡았소. 같은 말을 할 거요. 나보다 잘.

blocks.html: The histories do not record the year he died, only how high he got. He climbs the ridge beyond the city whenever the stone in his sleeve is warm, shaved every time, until the climb is too much for him. Then the stone goes to his son. The boy with seven stars on his back finds the same water on his own and bathes in it for thirty years, and the stone in his sleeve stays cold the whole time, as if the hill were waiting for a better question.
blocks.ko: 사서는 그가 죽은 해를 적지 않았다. 얼마나 높이 올랐는지만 적었다. 그는 소매 속 돌이 따뜻해질 때마다 도성 너머 능선을 오른다. 매번 면도를 하고. 오르기 버거워질 때까지. 그 뒤 돌은 아들에게 간다. 등에 일곱 별을 지닌 아이는 혼자 힘으로 같은 물을 찾아내 서른 해를 거기서 씻는다. 그동안 소매 속 돌은 한 번도 따뜻해지지 않는다. 언덕이 더 나은 질문을 기다리기라도 하는 것처럼.

blocks.html: Ninth morning, before light. The stone in his son’s sleeve is warm at last. Down Yushin goes, to the water…!
blocks.ko: 아홉째 날, 동트기 전. 아들의 소매 속 돌이 마침내 따뜻하다. 유신은 물로 내려간다…!

logline.en: Yushin asks the water who he is. Then the gate opens from the inside, the yard’s two best meet between the camps, and the score finally breaks.
logline.ko: 유신은 물에게 자신이 누구인지 묻는다. 그리고 문이 안에서 열리고, 연무장의 두 최고가 진영 사이에서 만나고, 점수가 마침내 깨진다.

When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.alt: Kim Myeong-guk’s Bodhidharma: Bidam in a few furious ink strokes, hooded, glaring, beads in his fist
images.prompt: A parody of Kim Myeong-guk’s DALMADO (달마도, Bodhidharma), painted exactly like the real Joseon Zen ink painting: a handful of explosive, fast, wet-and-dry brushstrokes in black ink on pale paper, the robe done in a few thick sweeping strokes, the face in fine sharp lines, huge empty background. Same composition: a half-length figure in a hooded robe, bushy brows, big glaring eyes, a stubborn scowl. The figure is BIDAM (attached grey-haired portrait: face with thin mustache, the grey hair showing under the hood), glaring straight out with total refusal, a string of prayer beads gripped in one fist, navy-black #141C2E ink. One blank red seal square in a corner. PARODY RULES: always a hand-made PAINTING, never photoreal. Reproduce the original work’s composition, poses and signature look so it reads instantly as that exact work, with our characters swapped in. If the original is a painting, mural, print or scroll, match its medium, surface and brushwork. If the original is a photograph, film poster, album cover, anime frame or statue, PAINT it: a painterly illustration of that image with visible brushstrokes, simplified forms and anime-adjacent faces, NOT a photo, NOT photoreal skin or pores, NOT a 3D render, NOT a CGI statue. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portraits, recognizable but restyled into the medium; never the portrait’s standing clasped-hands stance.
