blocks.label: The Cuiwei Palace
blocks.ko: 취미궁

blocks.html: Two summers earlier, the Son of Heaven is dying the way he did everything else: in front of witnesses.
blocks.ko: 두 해 전 여름, 천자는 다른 모든 일을 해 온 방식대로 죽어 간다. 증인들 앞에서.

blocks.html: The crown prince holds a hand that used to lift a lamp to stone horses. It has nothing left to lift. It still gives orders.
blocks.ko: 태자가 손 하나를 쥐고 있다. 돌말에 등잔을 들어 올리던 손이다. 이제 들어 올릴 것은 없다. 그래도 명은 내린다.

en: Zhi.
The six. When they go up the mountain—
Put the purple one nearest the door. …He hates waiting.
lines: 자줏빛 놈을 문 가장 가까이 두어라. ……기다리는 걸 싫어하니.

en: I know, Father. You told me. You’ve told me every—

blocks.html: The emperor dies in the Cuiwei Palace in the fifth month. He is fifty-one. The room is kept too warm, and the silk on the bed is the colour of late wheat.
blocks.ko: 오월, 취위궁에서 황제가 붕어한다. 쉰한 살. 방은 너무 덥게 데워져 있고, 침상의 비단은 늦은 밀 빛이다.

blocks.hanja: 駕崩
blocks.html: “The carriage collapses.” Nobody in Chang’an may say the emperor died. Kings die. The Son of Heaven’s carriage simply falls, and the whole empire is meant to hear it land.
blocks.ko: ‘수레가 무너진다’. 장안에서는 아무도 황제가 죽었다고 말하지 못한다. 왕은 죽는다. 하늘의 아들은 수레가 내려앉을 뿐이고, 온 제국이 그 소리를 들어야 한다.

blocks.html: The crown prince has been sitting since before dawn. He is twenty-one. He has the shoulders for the armour and not yet the face for the title. When the breathing stops, he does not move for a long time — long enough that the ministers begin to look at one another instead of at the bed.
blocks.ko: 태자는 동이 트기 전부터 앉아 있었다. 스물한 살. 갑옷을 견딜 어깨는 있으나, 아직 그 이름에 맞는 얼굴은 없다. 숨이 멎어도 그는 오래 움직이지 않는다 — 대신들이 침상이 아니라 서로의 얼굴을 보기 시작할 만큼.

en: ……Father.
Not yet——
zhLatn: …Fùhuáng.
Shàngwèi——

blocks.html: Someone touches his elbow. Someone else is already writing. The empire does not wait for grief to finish its sentence.
blocks.ko: 누군가가 팔꿈치를 건드린다. 다른 누군가는 이미 붓을 들고 있다. 제국은 슬픔이 문장을 끝낼 때까지 기다려 주지 않는다.

blocks.html: The court kneels, and the young man rises — the same hands that would not leave the bed now accepting the seal, the edict, the yellow silk that means the West has a new centre.
blocks.ko: 조정이 엎드리고, 젊은이가 일어선다 — 침상을 떠나려 하지 않던 그 손이, 이제 인장과 조서와, 서쪽에 새 중심이 생겼다는 뜻의 노란 비단을 받는다.

en: I receive the late emperor’s last command.
From this day——
……We will listen.
zhLatn: Zhèn shòu xiāndì yízhào.
Zì jīnrì qǐ——
…Zhèn dāng tīng zhī.

blocks.html: He does not say I. He says the word that empties a man of his own name. The hall answers like a single throat.
blocks.ko: 그는 “나”라고 하지 않는다. 사람의 이름을 비워 버리는 그 말을 쓴다. 대전이 하나의 목구멍처럼 대답한다.

blocks.html: The will is long on mourning and short on everything else, except one line, which the new emperor reads twice. The war in Liaodong is to stop.
blocks.ko: 유조는 상례에 대해서는 길고 나머지에 대해서는 짧다. 딱 한 줄만 빼고. 새 황제는 그 줄을 두 번 읽는다. 요동의 전쟁을 그만두라는 것이다.

blocks.html: The great emperor is given a temple name — Taizong. The clerks write it in the register and close the book.
blocks.ko: 위대한 황제에게 묘호 태종이 올려진다. 서리가 등록부에 쓰고 책을 덮는다.

blocks.html: Eighth year, summer, fourth month: Taizong* of Tang died. His testamentary edict called off the Liaodong campaign.
blocks.ko: 8년 여름 4월, 당 태종*이 죽었다. 유조로 요동의 전역을 그만두게 하였다.
blocks.hanja: 八年，夏四月，唐太宗崩。遺詔罷遼東之役。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 22, Goguryeo Annals — King Bojang, yr. 8 (649)

notes.html: Taizong is the temple name Tang gave him after death. In this book he is the Second Emperor.
notes.ko: 태종은 죽은 뒤 받은 묘호다. 이 책에서는 ‘두 번째 황제’다.

blocks.html: The empire is told how to grieve. The edict fixes the days of mourning by rank, and at dusk in every ward of Chang’an the ward chief walks the lanes and listens at the doors, to be sure the weeping inside is of the proper length.
blocks.ko: 제국은 어떻게 슬퍼할지 지시받는다. 칙령은 품계에 따라 상복 입을 날수를 정하고, 해 질 녘이면 장안의 방마다 방정이 골목을 돌며 문에 귀를 댄다. 안의 곡소리가 정해진 길이만큼인지 확인하려고.

blocks.html: Two of his dragons, the Red and the White, both of them Turks, petition to be killed and laid beside him, to guard the tomb the way the six stone horses will. It is the highest loyalty the steppe knows. The court is moved. The young emperor reads the petition twice.
blocks.ko: 그의 용 둘, 적룡과 백룡이 순장을 청한다. 둘 다 돌궐인이다. 죽어서 그의 곁에 묻혀, 여섯 돌말처럼 능을 지키겠다는 것이다. 초원이 아는 가장 높은 충성이다. 조정은 감동한다. 젊은 황제는 그 상소를 두 번 읽는다.

en: Denied.
…Father already has six horses waiting at his door.
He would scold Us for wasting two good generals.
lines: …선제 문 앞엔 이미 말 여섯이 기다리고 있다.
멀쩡한 장수 둘을 버렸다고, 짐을 꾸짖으실 게다.
zh: 他會怪朕白白折了兩員良將。
zhLatn: Bù zhǔn.
……Xiāndì mén qián, yǐ yǒu liù jùn xiāng hòu.
Tā huì guài zhèn báibái shé le liǎng yuán liáng jiàng.

blocks.label: Surabol
blocks.ko: 서라벌

blocks.html: The news crosses the sea in the eighth month. In Surabol, Chunchu reads the will through to the line about Liaodong, and then reads that line again.
blocks.ko: 소식은 팔월에 바다를 건넌다. 서라벌에서 춘추는 유조를 요동 대목까지 읽고, 그 줄을 다시 읽는다.

lines: 나더러 끝내 달라고 약속하게 해 놓고.
en: He made me promise to finish it.
And then he left orders to stop.
…Very well. Then it is mine.

blocks.label: Back at Cuiwei
blocks.ko: 다시 취미궁

blocks.html: In an anteroom a young concubine waits with the other women who must not be seen grieving too loudly. Her name is not yet heavy. Her attention already is. She watches how a seal moves from a dead hand to a living one — and files the lesson where ambition keeps its dry goods.
blocks.ko: 곁방에서 젊은 후궁이, 너무 크게 울면 안 되는 여인들과 함께 기다린다. 이름은 아직 무겁지 않다. 시선은 이미 그렇다. 죽은 손에서 산 손으로 인장이 옮아가는 법을 보고 — 야심이 마른 식량을 두는 곳에 그 수업을 넣는다.

en: (soft, to no one)
So that is how an empire changes owners.
Quietly. With someone else speaking the first sentence.
lines: 조용히. 첫 문장은 남이 말하게 두고.
zh: 原來帝國換主人是這樣。
靜靜地。讓別人說第一句。
zhLatn: (Qīngshēng, duì wú rén)
Yuánlái dìguó huàn zhǔrén shì zhèyàng.
Jìngjìng de. Ràng biérén shuō dì yī jù.

blocks.html: The late emperor’s women who bore him no children are sent to the Ganye Temple, to shave their heads and pray for him for the rest of their lives. Wu goes with them.
blocks.ko: 선제의 후궁 가운데 자식을 낳지 못한 여인들은 감업사로 보내져, 머리를 깎고 평생 그를 위해 기도하게 된다. 무도 그들과 함께 간다.

blocks.label: Ganye Temple
blocks.ko: 감업사

blocks.html: A year later, on the anniversary, the new emperor comes to the temple to burn incense for his father. A nun in grey looks up at him from the second row, and does not look down again.
blocks.ko: 한 해 뒤 기일에, 새 황제가 아버지에게 향을 올리러 그 절에 온다. 둘째 줄의 잿빛 승복 하나가 그를 올려다보고, 다시는 눈을 내리깔지 않는다.

en: Lady Wu.
…They cut your hair.
zhLatn: Wǔ niángzi.
…Tāmen tì le nǐ de tóufa.

en: Hair grows back, Majesty.
(and already the room tilts a degree toward her)
lines: (그리고 이미 방이 그녀 쪽으로 한 치 기운다)
zhLatn: Tóufa huì zhǎng huílái de, Bìxià.
(Ér fángjiān yǐ xiàng tā piān guò yī cùn)

blocks.html: Seven years of a polite queen and a busy nephew. Sooner or later, Silla has to admit who's really sitting in the chair…!
blocks.ko: 칠 년 동안 점잖은 여왕과 바쁜 조카. 언젠가 신라는 그 자리에 정말 누가 앉아 있는지 인정해야 한다…!

logline.en: For seven years the crown has sat on the Queen. The work has sat on her nephew’s table.
logline.ko: 일곱 해 동안 왕관은 여왕의 머리에 있었다. 일은 조카의 탁자 위에 있었다.

images.at: For seven years the crown has sat on
images.alt: Poster key art: Queen Jinduk weaves her ode of peace into silk at a lamp-lit loom while the white heavenly horse watches over her shoulder through the open door
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; crowns, antlers, wings and heads stay well inside the central band; no title, no lettering. Night in a tenebrist Silla palace chamber: one oil lamp, a big wooden loom, a long length of silk with woven lines of verse, the timber door slid open onto a moonlit courtyard. Over-shoulder two-shot. INTERACTION: Queen Jinduk sits at the loom in violet-and-white silk and gold crown, shuttle in hand, mid-throw; the wingless white heavenly horse Chunma has pushed its head and long neck in through the open door and rests its chin on her shoulder, watching the shuttle; without looking she reaches back and scratches its jaw. The woven silk glows only where the lamp touches it. CHUNMA HAS NO WINGS: a wingless white heavenly horse, bare white back and shoulders, nothing feathered anywhere; it rides the air on curling cloud-and-flame streamers trailing from its legs. The lamp is the only key (#9d7bd0 bounce off the silk): it catches her profile, the shuttle, the horse’s eye and muzzle; the room falls into umber-black. Loom frame as a dark foreground shape. STYLE: HEEWON STYLE, more painterly, with hints of Korean ink painting — Korean webtoon figures (clean ink linework, simplified expressive faces matching the attached portrait, watercolor-washed) inside a hand-painted world of watercolor and oil with traditional sumukhwa ink: splashed-ink storm clouds, bold dry calligraphic brush strokes in manes, fur, feathers, robes and grass, ink bleeding into wet wash, small ink splatters and drips near the frame edges, patches of bare rice paper where the edges dissolve; oil glazes only deepen the darks, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. Movie-poster key art: bold iconic silhouette, the two subjects large and close, one dramatic low angle, one bright break of light behind them, big dark masses, few hues plus one accent, film-poster drama but NO text, NO title, NO credits, NO logo, NO seal stamp. Not photoreal, not 3D. No glow aura, no halo, no emissive outline — the accent colour is real light. One of each named person. No watermark. CANON — QUEEN JINDUK — FACE and garments from attached /ch_jinduk.png (face only; invent a new pose). Hair ornament matches attached /bn_jinduk.png when the head is visible. #9d7bd0 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | CHUNMA (천마, hyukgose's heavenly horse, guardian of Silla) — attached board /obj_chunma.png: WINGLESS white heavenly horse in the Cheonmachong saddle-flap style: long arched neck, streaming white mane and tail, legs flung out in a flying gallop. It has NO WINGS — no feathers, no bird wings, nothing growing from the shoulders. It rides the sky on curling cloud-and-flame streamers trailing from its legs and chest, as on the painted birch-bark flap. Divine render: numinous through scale and atmosphere, never a glow outline. Kneels and cries beside the purple egg at Najeong, sees men approach, neighs and rises into the sky. | HORSE ANATOMY is a centrepiece: the whole horse body reads clearly and beautifully — arched neck, deep chest, sloping shoulder, round haunch, clean long legs in a correct gait, every muscle modelled by the one hard key with a bright edge along the topline and deep shadow under the belly; the horse is never cropped into a blob, never hidden behind dust, never stiff like a toy; mane and tail as flowing painted strokes; the coat colour exactly as the board. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS are a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST room (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt) painted in that same wash-and-glaze: a warm umber-to-black ground, walls, timber, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft with soft sfumato falloff — the webtoon figures are set INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.at: The Harmony Council meets to choose a king.
images.alt: Poster key art: Kim Chunchu, newly King Muyeol, walks down the palace stair at dawn with his hand in the white heavenly horse’s mane, talking to it like an old ally
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; crowns, antlers, wings and heads stay well inside the central band; no title, no lettering. Dawn on the long stone stair of the Seorabeol palace, giwa roofs behind, one storm cloud splitting. Low angle up the stair diagonal. INTERACTION: King Muyeol (Kim Chunchu as king — royal crown and magenta-and-gold court robe, older, heavy-lidded clever eyes) walks down the steps beside the wingless white heavenly horse Chunma, one hand buried in its mane, leaning in to murmur something sly into its ear; the horse has turned its head toward him, one ear cocked as if it has heard this sort of thing from him before. Two subjects on the stair diagonal, the rest empty stone. CHUNMA HAS NO WINGS: a wingless white heavenly horse, bare white back and shoulders, nothing feathered anywhere; it rides the air on curling cloud-and-flame streamers trailing from its legs. One magenta-gold sunrise break (#D8258C) from behind the roofs edges his crown, profile and the horse’s neck; the stair falls into blue-grey shadow and ink. STYLE: HEEWON STYLE, more painterly, with hints of Korean ink painting — Korean webtoon figures (clean ink linework, simplified expressive faces matching the attached portrait, watercolor-washed) inside a hand-painted world of watercolor and oil with traditional sumukhwa ink: splashed-ink storm clouds, bold dry calligraphic brush strokes in manes, fur, feathers, robes and grass, ink bleeding into wet wash, small ink splatters and drips near the frame edges, patches of bare rice paper where the edges dissolve; oil glazes only deepen the darks, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. Movie-poster key art: bold iconic silhouette, the two subjects large and close, one dramatic low angle, one bright break of light behind them, big dark masses, few hues plus one accent, film-poster drama but NO text, NO title, NO credits, NO logo, NO seal stamp. Not photoreal, not 3D. No glow aura, no halo, no emissive outline — the accent colour is real light. One of each named person. No watermark. CANON — KING MUYEOL — FACE and garments from attached /ch_muyeol.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Slim and elegant; shoulder-length loose black hair parted in the middle; thin moustache and goatee stubble; amused eyes, small knowing smile. Dress: Magenta-crimson silk po with a charcoal sash, dark layered collar. Silk even on campaign. Now: King Muyeol (stage portrait): royal robes and crown; heavier, tired eyes. Demeanor: Diplomat and strategist: talks with his hands, smiles while calculating, never shouts; half-lidded watchful eyes. #D8258C as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: front-line armored warrior pose; shouting battle face; katana. | CHUNMA (천마, hyukgose's heavenly horse, guardian of Silla) — attached board /obj_chunma.png: WINGLESS white heavenly horse in the Cheonmachong saddle-flap style: long arched neck, streaming white mane and tail, legs flung out in a flying gallop. It has NO WINGS — no feathers, no bird wings, nothing growing from the shoulders. It rides the sky on curling cloud-and-flame streamers trailing from its legs and chest, as on the painted birch-bark flap. Divine render: numinous through scale and atmosphere, never a glow outline. Kneels and cries beside the purple egg at Najeong, sees men approach, neighs and rises into the sky. | PLACE Surabol (서라벌 (경주)) — attached board /pl_eastern_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Seorabeol palace: Silla giwa halls, packed-earth yards, timber verandas. | HORSE ANATOMY is a centrepiece: the whole horse body reads clearly and beautifully — arched neck, deep chest, sloping shoulder, round haunch, clean long legs in a correct gait, every muscle modelled by the one hard key with a bright edge along the topline and deep shadow under the belly; the horse is never cropped into a blob, never hidden behind dust, never stiff like a toy; mane and tail as flowing painted strokes; the coat colour exactly as the board. blocks.html: For seven years the crown has sat on Queen Jinduk. The work has sat on her nephew’s table. Nobody has ever called her foolish. She’s simply outnumbered by seals.
blocks.ko: 칠 년 동안 왕관은 진덕여왕의 머리에 있었다. 일은 그녀 조카의 탁자 위에 있었다. 아무도 그녀를 어리석다 한 적 없다. 그저 도장 수에서 밀렸을 뿐이다.

en: Nephew.
When I die, do not pretend I ruled.
Say I kept the chair warm until the country was ready to admit who was already sitting in it.
lines: 내가 죽거든 내가 다스렸다고 하지 마라.
나라가, 이미 앉아 있던 사람을 인정할 준비가 될 때까지 자리를 따뜻하게 지켜 줬다고 해라.

en: Aunt.
You ruled the only way left to Sacred Bone — by lasting.
lines: 성골에게 남은 유일한 방식으로 다스리셨습니다 — 버팀으로.

blocks.html: Kangrim reads her name three times — Jinduk. Jinduk. Jinduk. — the ledger's habit before a Sacred Bone line closes.
blocks.ko: 강림은 그녀의 이름을 세 번 부른다 — 진덕. 진덕. 진덕. — 성골의 혈통이 닫히기 전 명부의 버릇대로.

en: Majesty.
Sacred Bone ends on your breath. One question.
Did you keep the crown warm for the next hand — or keep it from cooling into a man’s?
lines: 성골이 당신 숨에서 끝납니다. 질문 하나.
다음 손을 위해 왕관을 따뜻이 두셨습니까 — 아니면 사내의 것으로 식지 않게 지키신 겁니까?

en: …I kept a seat from becoming a joke.
That is all the Sacred Bone had left to do.
Then the minutes are clean.
Walk.

blocks.label: The Harmony Council
blocks.ko: 화백회의

blocks.html: The Harmony Council meets to choose a king. For the first time since there was a council, there is no Sacred Bone left to choose.
blocks.ko: 화백회의가 임금을 고르려고 모인다. 회의가 생긴 이래 처음으로, 고를 성골이 남아 있지 않다.

blocks.html: So the room does what rooms do with an empty chair. It offers it to the oldest man present. Alchun is High Councillor. He has been waiting seven years for this, so that he can refuse it.
blocks.ko: 그래서 방은 빈 의자를 두고 방들이 늘 하는 일을 한다. 그 자리에서 가장 나이 든 사람에게 내민다. 상대등은 알천이다. 그는 이 순간을 일곱 해 기다려 왔다. 거절하려고.

en: High Councillor. The room asks you first.
blocks.speaker: Councillor

en: Me?
Your servant is old, and has no virtue worth naming.
I told you lot on the wall. The chair you offered me afterward would be empty.
In virtue and standing nobody here weighs what Lord Chunchu weighs. He’s the one who can save the age.
lines: 신은 늙었고, 칭할 만한 덕행이 없소.
성벽 위에서 말했잖소. 나중에 내게 줄 자리는 비어 있을 거라고.
덕망으로 치면 여기 누구도 춘추공만 못하오. 세상을 건질 사람은 그 사람이오.
다~ 뻔히 춘추인걸 모르는 사람이 없나~~
en: Come now~ is there anyone who doesn’t know it will be Chunchu~~
A True Bone king. The bone has never once—
blocks.speaker: Councillor

lines: 진골이 왕이 되는 건 나라가 선 이래 처음이오.
…그건 누가 좀 적어 둬야 하지 않겠소.
en: A True Bone on the throne. First since there was a throne.
…Somebody had probably better write that down.

blocks.html: Alchun laughs the last hand up. Then everyone looks at the one man in the room who has spent his life sitting anywhere but that chair.
blocks.ko: 알천이 웃어서 마지막 손을 들게 한다. 그러고는 모두가 한 사람을 본다. 평생 그 의자만 빼고 아무 데나 앉아 온 사람.

en: My lords. I have never once wanted to sit there.
lines: 여러분. 나는 저기 앉고 싶었던 적이 한 번도 없소.

en: Then sit in it, and stop making the rest of us stand.
lines: 그럼 앉으시오. 그리고 우리 좀 그만 세워 두시오.

en: This servant can find no reason to object.
Nor could anyone else.
The age of Kim Chunchu begins.

blocks.html: The king was splendid in looks and bearing, and from boyhood he meant to set the world right.
blocks.ko: 왕은 풍채가 영특하고 훌륭하였으며, 어려서부터 세상을 구제할 뜻을 품었다.
blocks.hanja: 王儀表英偉，幼有濟世志。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 5, Silla Annals — King Taejong Muyeol, yr. 1 (654)

blocks.html: Emperor Taizong sent Liu Heng, Chamberlain for the Palace Larder, out past the walls to welcome him. When Chunchu arrived, the emperor saw how splendid his looks and bearing were, and treated him generously.
blocks.ko: 당 태종이 광록경 유형을 교외로 보내 그를 맞아 위로하게 하였다. 도착하자, 태종은 춘추의 풍채가 영특하고 훌륭한 것을 보고 후하게 대접하였다.
blocks.hanja: 唐太宗遣光祿卿柳亨郊勞之。旣至，見春秋儀表英偉，厚待之。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 5, Silla Annals — Queen Jindeok, yr. 2 (648)

blocks.html: Chunchu was handsome, and good at talk and laughter.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 용모가 아름답고 담소를 잘하였다.
blocks.hanja: 春秋美姿顏，善談咲。
blocks.source: Nihon Shoki (日本書紀) bk. 25, Emperor Kōtoku — Taika 3 (647)

blocks.html: Munhee becomes queen. Years ago her sister sold her a dream on a hill. She married in disgrace, to a man with no claim to anything. Now she stands beside his throne.
blocks.ko: 문희가 왕비가 된다. 오래전 언니가 언덕 위에서 그녀에게 꿈을 팔았다. 그녀는 아무것도 물려받을 것 없는 사내에게 망신스럽게 시집갔다. 이제 그 사내의 왕좌 곁에 선다.

lines: 언니가 그 꿈을 비단 치마 한 벌에 팔았습니다. / 지금 생각하면 헐값이었지요.
en: My sister sold me that dream for one silk skirt. / In hindsight she undercharged.

blocks.html: The new king’s first council is about Baekje. It is short.
blocks.ko: 새 임금의 첫 회의 안건은 백제다. 회의는 짧다.

lines: 사적인 원한으로 나라를 망국의 길로 인도하시는 것은 어진 일이 아니라 봅니다...!
en: Your Majesty… even so….
To lead the country down a road of ruin for a private grudge — that is not the act of a wise king…!

lines: 자네들, 나를 진정 그렇게 보고 있었나?
내 딸의 죽음에 미쳐 복수를 가르는 노인으로?
en: ….What? A private grudge?
Is that truly how you have all seen me?
An old man maddened by his daughter’s death, sharpening revenge?
How… disappointing.
I am a man looking at the thousand-year flourishing of the sacred country.
I was raised on the study of kingship from childhood…

lines: 무서워 해야 할지, 동경해야 할 지 모르겠다....
en: I do not know whether to fear him or admire him….
And yet—
Kim Chunchu…

blocks.html: That night a letter leaves Surabol for Chang’an, written in a hand that still remembers the Wei River. It begins without titles: Zhi — I kept the appointment. Do not let the coat eat you.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 서라벌에서 장안으로 편지가 떠난다. 위수를 아직 기억하는 손씨. 존호 없이 시작한다. 治 — 약속 지켰네. 겉옷에게 먹히지는 말게.

blocks.label: Chang’an
blocks.ko: 장안

lines: 말을 보내게. 그리고 여기 먼지엔 불편한 사람 하나 더 들어갈 자리가 있다고 전하게.
en: He became king.
Of course he did.
Send him horses. And tell him the dust here still has room for one more inconvenient man.
zh: 送他馬。並告訴他——這兒的塵土還容得下一個不便之人。
zhLatn: Tā chéng le wáng.
Guǒrán.
Sòng tā mǎ. Bìng gàosu tā——zhèr de chéntǔ hái róng de xià yīgè bùbiàn zhī rén.

blocks.html: Far west, the Third Emperor’s court learns a new gravity. The young woman who once waited in an anteroom now finishes sentences the emperor starts. Clerks say her influence is growing by the day. They say it softly.
blocks.ko: 서쪽 멀리, 고종의 조정은 새 중력을 배운다. 곁방에서 기다리던 젊은 여인이 이제 황제가 시작한 문장을 끝낸다. 서기들은 영향력이 날로 커진다고 한다. 작게 말한다.

blocks.label: The Crown Prince’s Rooms
blocks.ko: 태자의 처소

blocks.html: Late that night the new crown prince is still at his table, with the levy rolls for his father’s war. His wife reads them over his shoulder. She has been doing it for ten years.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 늦게, 새 태자는 아버지의 전쟁에 쓸 징발 장부를 붙들고 아직 탁자 앞에 있다. 아내가 어깨 너머로 그것을 읽는다. 십 년째 해 온 일이다.

en: Your sums are wrong.
The rice for the western forts. You carried a one.
lines: 서쪽 성들 쌀. 하나를 잘못 올렸잖아.

en: …Ten years, and you still say it the same way.
Ten years, and you still carry the one.
lines: 십 년인데, 아직도 하나를 잘못 올리잖아.

blocks.html: The first time she said it, he was eighteen, the quay was wet, and the brush in her hand was stolen…!
blocks.ko: 그녀가 처음 그 말을 했을 때, 그는 열여덟이었고, 부두는 젖어 있었고, 그녀 손의 붓은 훔친 것이었다…!

logline.en: The quay doesn’t care that he’s a prince. She has already decided his arithmetic is sloppy.
logline.ko: 항구는 그가 왕자든 말든 상관없다. 그녀는 이미 그의 셈이 헐겁다고 결론을 내렸다.

images.alt: Bupmin and Jahee under a rain-eave at the quay — almost a kiss, a wet ledger in her hand
images.prompt: Intimate cinematic still, 16:9. Harbour romance. Young adult Bupmin and adult Jahee. Faces match the attached portraits. No text. No watermark.

images.alt: Adult Jahee reaching up to a shelf, body stretched in a long line.
images.prompt: 16:9 painterly webtoon tenebrism. Adult Jahee reaching up to a shelf, body stretched in a long line. Closed hanbok, the sash defining the waist, light along the cloth over shoulder and hip. Modest, opaque, not exposed. Playful frown. FACE matches the portrait, Korean, dark eyes. Binyeo matches the pin. One lamp, crushed dark. No text, no halo.

images.alt: Warehouse lamp: Jahee corrects a tide ledger; Bupmin watches her mouth instead of the numbers
images.prompt: Intimate cinematic still, 16:9. Warehouse lamp. Adult Jahee and young adult Bupmin. Faces match the attached portraits. No text. No watermark.

images.alt: Between them one cloth is a single twisting brush stroke in midair, not yet arrived.
images.prompt: Original sumi on white paper. No pasted couple. Story: Jahee throws a cloth at Bupmin. Two tiny marks far apart. Between them one cloth is a single twisting brush stroke in midair, not yet arrived. A small crimson bleed on the right-hand mark. No text, no seal.

images.at: a stolen brush between their mouths
images.alt: Almost-kiss: a stolen brush as a thin diagonal between Bupmin and Jahee
images.prompt: Intimate cinematic CLOSE-UP still, 16:9. Young adult Bupmin and adult Jahee. Faces match the attached portraits. No text. No watermark.

images.alt: Jahee scolding Bupmin
Bupmin and Jahee under the eaves in the rain
Jahee waves a cloth at a laughing Bupmin

blocks.html: Ten years earlier, at Silla’s only western harbour, the prince is eighteen and losing an argument with a tide book.
blocks.ko: 십 년 전, 신라의 하나뿐인 서쪽 항구. 왕자는 열여덟이고, 조수 장부와의 싸움에서 지는 중이다.

blocks.html: Yushin sent him here for the season, to work under Kim Seonpum, who runs the quay. No yard. No horses. Grain ships, tide marks, and sums that will not close.
blocks.ko: 유신이 그를 이 한 철 동안 이곳에 보냈다. 부두를 맡은 김선품 밑에서 일하라고. 연무장도 없다. 말도 없다. 곡식 배와 물때 표시와, 맞아떨어지지 않는 셈뿐이다.

blocks.html: Silla’s only door to the western sea. Everyone knows which door.
blocks.ko: 서쪽 바다로 난 신라의 단 하나뿐인 문. 다들 그 문이 어딘지 안다.

blocks.html: Seonpum has a daughter who keeps his inkstones. Her name is Jahee. She has watched the prince for three days, and she has already decided his arithmetic is sloppy.
blocks.ko: 선품에게는 그의 벼루를 지키는 딸이 있다. 이름은 자희. 사흘 동안 왕자를 지켜보았고, 그의 셈이 헐겁다고 이미 결론을 내렸다.

blocks.caption: A harbour girl who counts faster than the customs men.
blocks.ko: 세관 관리보다 셈이 빠른 항구의 처녀.

en: Your sums are wrong.
The tide does not care that you are a prince.
Count again.
While I am watching.
…Where.
No — / Please show me.

blocks.html: She corrects the sum with her father’s good brush. She is not supposed to touch it. She took it off his desk an hour ago, because it is the only one that writes small enough. He watches her mouth instead of the numbers, and she lets him, once.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 아버지의 좋은 붓으로 셈을 고친다. 손대면 안 되는 붓이다. 한 시진 전에 아버지 책상에서 슬쩍 가져왔다. 글씨를 그만큼 작게 쓰는 붓은 그것뿐이라서. 그는 숫자 대신 그녀의 입을 보고, 그녀는 한 번 허락한다.

blocks.html: Then a rider comes down the coast road with a letter from Yushin. The army is marching west, against seven Baekje forts. The grain sails on the morning tide. Bupmin is to sail with it.
blocks.ko: 그때 해안 길로 말 탄 전령이 유신의 글월을 들고 내려온다. 군대가 서쪽으로, 백제의 일곱 성을 향해 나선다. 곡식은 아침 물때에 배에 실려 떠난다. 법민도 그 배로 오라는 것이다.

en: The morning tide.
…Then the book has to close tonight.
It won’t. You’re forty sacks short, somewhere between the third ship and the fifth.
Forty sacks is a company that doesn’t eat for a week.
lines: 안 닫혀요. 마흔 섬이 비어요. 셋째 배와 다섯째 배 사이 어딘가에서.
마흔 섬이면 한 부대가 이레를 굶어요.

en: Then show me where.

blocks.html: They count until the lamp needs oil, and then by the light from the warehouse door. Somewhere around the fourth ship she stops correcting him, because he has stopped making mistakes. Neither of them knows what to do with their hands.
blocks.ko: 등잔에 기름이 떨어질 때까지 센다. 그다음엔 창고 문간의 불빛으로 센다. 넷째 배쯤에서 그녀는 그를 고쳐 주기를 멈춘다. 그가 더는 틀리지 않기 때문이다. 둘 다 손을 어디 둬야 할지 모른다.

blocks.html: Rain finds the eave. They stand inside a hard rain-curtain with a wet ledger between them, and almost do the stupid thing, and do not — until there is a stolen brush between their mouths, and then they do.
blocks.ko: 비가 처마를 찾는다. 그들은 젖은 장부를 사이에 두고 단단한 빗줄기 커튼 안에 서서, 바보 같은 일을 거의 하고, 하지 않는다 — 훔친 붓이 입 사이에 놓일 때까지. 그리고 그때는 한다.

en: …That’s my father coughing.
He only coughs like that when he’s pretending not to be there.
…Which is why it has to be now.
Before the tide comes in.
Do not close the book.
If you close it I…
will not know where to go.

blocks.html: Seonpum coughs once from the dark and pretends he did not see a prince learning the harbour by kissing the girl who can count.
blocks.ko: 선품이 어둠에서 한 번 기침하고, 셈할 줄 아는 소녀에게 입 맞추며 항구를 배우는 왕자를 보지 못한 척한다.

blocks.html: They find it at the fifth ship, an hour before dawn. Forty sacks written down by somebody who never loaded them. The grain can sail on time and short, or a day late and whole.
blocks.ko: 새벽 한 시진 전, 다섯째 배에서 찾아낸다. 싣지도 않은 마흔 섬을 누군가 실었다고 적어 두었다. 곡식은 제때 모자란 채로 떠날 수도 있고, 하루 늦게 온전히 떠날 수도 있다.

en: Load them. All forty.
I’ll take the next tide.
Yushin said the morning tide.
Then he can hit me for it.
At least the company that eats will be his.
lines: 그래도 밥을 먹는 부대는 그분 부대일 테니까요.

en: …And you’ll come back and fix your sums?
Only if you’re watching.

blocks.html: Years later the court will call her Jayi. The quay already had the true name.
blocks.ko: 여러 해 뒤 조정은 그녀를 자의라 부를 것이다. 항구는 이미 진짜 이름을 가지고 있었다.

blocks.label: The Western Forts
blocks.ko: 서쪽 성들

blocks.html: He reaches the army a day late, with forty sacks of rice nobody else knew were missing. Yushin is waiting at the edge of the camp.
blocks.ko: 그는 하루 늦게 군에 닿는다. 아무도 비는 줄 몰랐던 쌀 마흔 섬과 함께. 유신이 진영 끝에서 기다리고 있다.

en: You missed the tide.
Yes, Marshal. The fifth ship was forty sacks short. I stayed and loaded them.
lines: 예, 대장군. 다섯째 배가 마흔 섬이 비었습니다. 남아서 실었습니다.

blocks.html: Yushin hits him once, open-handed, because the order was the morning tide. Then he sends the forty sacks to the company that was going to go without.
blocks.ko: 유신은 손바닥으로 그를 한 대 친다. 명은 아침 물때였으니까. 그러고는 마흔 섬을 굶을 뻔한 부대로 보낸다.

en: Marshal.
When I said king for all — did I mean every kingdom, or every person who bleeds for one?
lines: 모두를 위한 임금이라 했을 때 — 모든 나라를 말한 겁니까, 아니면 하나를 위해 피 흘리는 모든 사람을 말한 겁니까.

en: Ask the yard again tomorrow.
If the answer is only a speech, you are still six.
If it costs you a bruise — you are becoming Hwarang.
lines: 멍이 값이면 — 화랑이 되어 가는 거다.

blocks.label: The Quay, Again
blocks.ko: 다시, 포구

blocks.html: He comes back in the spring to fix his sums. The sums are fine. By midsummer Jahee is not fine, in the way that shows, and her father picks the busiest hour on the quay to notice.
blocks.ko: 그는 봄에 셈을 고치러 돌아온다. 셈은 멀쩡하다. 한여름이 되자 자희가 멀쩡하지 않다. 눈에 띄는 쪽으로. 아버지는 포구가 가장 붐비는 시각을 골라 그걸 알아챈다.

en: Pregnant with an unknown man’s child… what a disgrace!
In front of the whole harbour!
lines: 누군지도 모를 사내의 아이를 배다니… 이 무슨 망신이냐!

en: Father. Everyone on this quay can count.
You taught them.
lines: 아버지. 이 포구 사람들 다 셈할 줄 알아요.

en: Not a word from you. Whose is it? Name him!
lines: 넌 입 다물어라. 누구냐? 이름을 대!

en: …Mine. Sir. I’m the— it’s mine.
I’m the unknown man.
The prince. Well.
What a terrible shock.

blocks.html: He has had wedding silk folded in a chest since the night of the forty sacks. In the Marshal’s family this is practically a proposal. The prince’s mother managed hers with a bonfire. His grandmother did it through a drain.
blocks.ko: 그는 마흔 섬이 빈 그 밤부터 혼례 비단을 궤짝에 접어 넣어 두었다. 대장군 집안에서는 이게 거의 청혼이다. 왕자의 어머니는 모닥불로 해냈고, 할머니는 하수구로 해냈다.

blocks.label: The Coronation Year
blocks.ko: 즉위하던 해

blocks.html: Ten years later the bruise is long gone. The girl from the quay is the crown prince’s wife. The whole court stands in the palace yard in Tang silk to watch his father crowned.
blocks.ko: 십 년 뒤, 멍은 진작 사라졌다. 부두의 그 아가씨는 태자비가 되었다. 온 조정이 당의 비단을 입고 궁 마당에 서서 그의 아버지가 왕관 쓰는 것을 지켜본다.

blocks.html: This king has a Secretariat, an emperor for a friend, and an army that answers to one brush. He means to make three kingdoms one. Everybody in the yard can feel a new age starting.
blocks.ko: 이 임금에게는 집사부가 있고, 벗이라 부르는 황제가 있고, 붓 한 자루에 움직이는 군대가 있다. 그는 세 나라를 하나로 만들 작정이다. 마당의 누구나 새 시대가 시작되는 것을 느낀다.

blocks.html: Along the back row stand the oldest houses in Surabol, the six families who were here before there was a king. They wear the new robes because the Secretariat says so. They wear them like borrowed skin.
blocks.ko: 뒷줄에는 서라벌에서 가장 오래된 집안들이 서 있다. 임금이 있기 전부터 여기 있던 여섯 가문이다. 집사부가 입으라니 새 관복을 입었다. 빌린 살가죽처럼 입었다.

en: In my grandfather’s day a king wore what his grandfather wore.
In the first king’s day he came out of an egg.
Now he comes out of a Secretariat.
lines: 우리 할아버지 때는 임금이 제 할아버지 옷을 입었소.
blocks.speaker: The old houses

en: Uncle. Why do they mind so much?
It’s only a robe.
Nothing in this country is only a robe, lad.
Their grandfathers chose the first king. So did mine.
Ask how the first one got here. Then you’ll know what they’re muttering about.
lines: 이 나라에 옷일 뿐인 건 없다, 얘야.
저 양반들 할아버지가 첫 임금을 골랐다. 내 할아버지도.
첫 임금이 어디서 왔는지 물어봐라. 그럼 저 양반들이 뭘 투덜대는지 알 게다.

blocks.html: Silla’s newest king wears Tang silk. To see why the old houses mind, go back to a white horse kneeling in the grass…!
blocks.ko: 신라의 새 임금은 당의 비단을 입는다. 늙은 가문들이 왜 그걸 못마땅해하는지 알려면, 풀밭에 무릎 꿇은 흰 말에게로 거슬러 올라가야 한다…!

logline.en: A white horse kneels by a well and cries. Six chiefs start digging.
logline.ko: 흰 말 한 마리가 우물가에 무릎 꿇고 운다. 여섯 촌장이 땅을 파기 시작한다.

images.alt: Six chiefs in a circle around a glowing blue egg and white horse — cool blue versus warm gold
images.prompt: Anime-painterly egg-and-horse gathering, hard blue/gold split, flat color fields, not photoreal mountains.

images.alt: A white winged horse kneels crying beside Najeong well under a hanging shaft of light
images.at: a white horse folded onto its knees
images.prompt: Ink painting of the myth. Bird’s-eye from the pine crowns over Najeong well: a white winged horse kneels beside a round stone well-mouth in a small clearing, neck bent, crying up at the sky; the horse is left as blinding bare paper inside a ring of splashed black pine forest; one thin column of lightning-mist hangs straight down from the sky onto the well. Six tiny chiefs in wide-sleeved robes crouch at the forest edge. ONE device: the vertical shaft of light dropping into the circular well. MYTH INK — this beat is myth, not history, so it is painted as a STRIKING Korean ink painting (sumukhwa), not the house colour style. Joseon sumi ink on raw hanji paper with EXTREME LIGHT AGAINST DARK: huge saturated masses of black ink set against blinding bare paper; light is always the unpainted paper itself, never painted white; almost no mid-grey; hard edges where light meets dark, wet bleeding edges everywhere else. Splashed ink (pomuk), dry-brush flying white, ink spatter, mist left as untouched paper. Monumental emptiness and ONE graphic device carrying the frame; a dramatic angle (worm’s-eye, bird’s-eye, dutch). Gods, giants, beasts and wonders may fill the frame; mortals stay small inside the wonder. Figures in confident calligraphic brush line; named faces match the attached portraits, translated into a few ink strokes. Black ink and paper only, except at most ONE small translucent wash of a single colour on the one symbolic object the scene names. Not photoreal, not webtoon shading, not watercolor landscape, not oil, no glow, no halo. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. No text, no calligraphy, no seal stamp, no watermark.

images.alt: A chicken-dragon coils at Alyeongjeong well; a baby girl comes from its rib
images.prompt: Ink painting of the myth. At the stone mouth of Alyeongjeong well, a gyeryong (chicken-dragon: rooster head and comb, long serpent-dragon body in dry-brush scales) coils around the well-mouth; from its left side a newborn girl emerges into a burst of bare paper light, wrapped in nothing but mist. Worm’s-eye from the well stones. ONE device: the dragon’s coil around the round well. MYTH INK — this beat is myth, not history, so it is painted as a STRIKING Korean ink painting (sumukhwa), not the house colour style. images.alt: Adult King Hyukgosé and Queen Alyoung in a close moonlit kiss — blue silk, porcelain-gold hairpin, her hand on his chest
images.prompt: Intimate cinematic CLOSE-UP still, 16:9. Adult founding king Hyukgosé (dark side-parted hair, light-blue hanbok) and adult Queen Alyoung (black bun, porcelain-gold floral binyeo, blue silk) in a close moonlit kiss, her hand on his chest, collarbones catching moonlight. Personal, not tiny figures under a huge moon, not silhouettes. No text, no watermark.

images.alt: Photoreal Hyukgosé mostly in shadow, a broken eggshell-arc and cerulean rim-light the only accent
images.prompt: Minimal iconic 3:4 poster. Hyukgosé, photoreal demigod founder. ONE geometric device: a BROKEN EGGSHELL as an incomplete white arc. Photoreal face matches the attached portrait, mostly in shadow; pale-blue #6f9fe8 rim. No horse. No egg-circle. No army. No text. No watermark. Graphic color-blocking, photoreal demigod face, monumental.

images.at: crown him king while he is still a boy
images.alt: The six chiefs crown the thirteen-year-old Hyukgose on a riverbank mound at dusk
images.prompt: History, not myth: the six village chiefs of Saro crown the boy king. Low three-quarter worm’s-eye on a packed-earth ritual mound above the Alcheon river at dusk, 57 BC: no palace yet, only thatch, timber and earth. The six chiefs in plain wide-sleeved robes and black jougwan stand in a half-ring; the eldest, white-bearded, raises the gold crown in both hands over a THIRTEEN-YEAR-OLD boy, Hyukgose, kneeling on a straw mat with his head up and unafraid (his face is a boy’s version of the attached portrait). A brazier just outside the frame at lower right rakes firelight up across the boy’s face, the chiefs’ sleeves and the raised gold; behind them the river and the six villages’ thatched roofs dissolve into blue dusk haze, small lamps as bokeh. ONE device: the half-ring of chiefs converging on the raised crown. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

Pines of Mount Yang as black masses at the frame edge. ONE device: the lightning seam. Splashed ink (pomuk), dry-brush flying white, ink spatter, mist left as untouched paper. Figures in confident calligraphic brush line; named faces match the attached portraits, translated into a few ink strokes.
