blocks.html: Seven hundred years before anyone in Surabol wore Tang silk, six old men creep up on a horse.
blocks.ko: 서라벌의 누구도 당의 비단을 입기 칠백 년 전, 늙은이 여섯이 말 한 마리에게 살금살금 다가간다.

blocks.html: They are village chiefs, from six valleys in the hills. Their people came south over the mountains, from a kingdom in the north that stopped being a kingdom. That is another story, and an older one. This morning the six valleys have no king, and they keep arguing about it.
blocks.ko: 그들은 산골 여섯 골짜기의 촌장이다. 그들의 백성은 북쪽, 더는 나라가 아니게 된 어느 나라에서 산을 넘어 내려왔다. 그건 다른 이야기, 더 오래된 이야기다. 오늘 아침 여섯 골짜기에는 임금이 없고, 그 일로 늘 다툰다.

blocks.html: The chroniclers disagree about the colour of the egg and agree about the horse. Before anyone dug, the six chiefs saw it from the ridge of Mount Yang: a light hanging down beside Najeong like lightning that had forgotten to leave, and under it a white horse folded onto its knees, as if someone important were waiting in the grass.
blocks.ko: 알의 빛깔을 두고는 사서들이 다투지만, 말에 대해서는 다투지 않는다. 땅을 파기도 전에 여섯 촌장은 양산 능선에서 그것을 보았다. 나정 곁으로 떠나기를 잊은 번개처럼 빛이 드리워 있고, 그 아래 흰 말 한 마리가, 풀숲에 귀한 이라도 기다리는 듯 무릎을 꿇고 있었다.

en: That’s… a horse, right?
Why’s a horse kneeling? Who to?

lines: 날개 달린 말 본 적 있어? 난 없어.
en: You ever seen a horse with wings? I haven’t.
…That one’s got wings, though.
Slow. Go slow. If it spooks—

blocks.html: It does not spook. It lets them come close enough to see that its wings are folded the way a bird folds them and that its eyes are on the grass, not on them. Then it looks up and sees six grown men creeping at it through the pines with their sleeves held out like nets.
blocks.ko: 말은 놀라지 않는다. 새가 날개를 접듯 날개를 접고 있다는 것, 눈이 그들이 아니라 풀숲에 가 있다는 것이 보일 만큼 가까이 오게 둔다. 그러다 고개를 들고, 다 큰 사내 여섯이 그물처럼 소매를 벌린 채 소나무 사이로 기어 오는 것을 본다.

blocks.html: Six chiefs stand in a wet field with their arms still out, holding nothing. Much later, when the country has a name and a calendar and a clerk for everything, the horse will be painted on a saddle-flap and buried with a king and called Chunma, the heavenly horse. That morning nobody calls it anything. Alpyung is the first to look down at what it was kneeling over.
blocks.ko: 여섯 촌장이 젖은 들판에 팔을 벌린 채, 아무것도 쥐지 못하고 서 있다. 한참 뒤, 나라에 이름과 달력과 무엇에나 서기가 생긴 뒤, 그 말은 말다래에 그려져 어느 왕과 함께 묻히고 천마라 불릴 것이다. 그날 아침엔 아무도 그것을 무어라 부르지 않는다. 발밑, 말이 꿇어앉아 있던 자리를 처음 내려다본 것은 알평이다.

lines: 파 봐. 다들 뭐 해, 파 보라니까.
en: …It left something.
Dig. What are you all doing? Dig.

blocks.html: They dig with their hands, then with somebody’s hoe. Under the grass is an egg the size of a gourd, and the same shape. When it cracks there is a boy inside, already looking at them as if they were late.
blocks.ko: 처음엔 손으로, 다음엔 누군가의 괭이로 판다. 풀 밑에 박만 한 알이 있다. 생김새도 박이다. 알이 갈라지자 사내아이가 있다. 벌써, 늦게 온 사람들을 보듯 그들을 쳐다본다.

en: It’s a gourd. We dug up a gourd with a baby in it.
Then that’s his name. Park. Gourd.

blocks.html: They call him Park, for the gourd, and Hyukgose, to rule with brightness. Then six practical men look at each other and crown him king while he is still a boy. A boy, they reason, cannot have taken sides yet.
blocks.ko: 박에서 나왔으니 박, 세상을 밝게 다스리라고 혁거세. 그러고는 실속 있는 사내 여섯이 서로를 보고, 아직 어린아이인 그를 임금으로 세운다. 아이라면 아직 어느 편도 들지 않았을 테니까.

blocks.caption: Hyukgose. Born from an egg, crowned before his voice broke.
blocks.ko: 혁거세. 알에서 태어나, 목소리가 굵어지기도 전에 왕관을 썼다.

blocks.hanja: 浴於東泉，身生光彩，鳥獸率舞，天地振動，日月淸明。
blocks.html: They bathed him in the eastern spring. His body gave off light, the birds and beasts danced together, heaven and earth shook, and the sun and moon turned clear and bright.
blocks.ko: 동천에서 목욕시키니 몸에서 광채가 나고, 새와 짐승이 함께 춤추며, 하늘과 땅이 진동하고, 해와 달이 맑고 밝아졌다.
blocks.source: Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) bk. 1, Wonders — Silla’s Founder Hyeokgeose

blocks.label: Alyeong Well
blocks.ko: 알영정

blocks.html: A few years later, at Alyeongjeong well, a dragon with a chicken’s head leaves a girl behind. She has a beak where her lips should be, until they wash her in the north stream and it falls off. They name her Alyoung, after the well.
blocks.ko: 몇 해 뒤, 알영정 우물가에서 닭 머리를 한 용이 여자아이 하나를 두고 간다. 입술 자리에 부리가 달려 있었는데, 북쪽 시내에 씻기자 떨어져 나간다. 우물 이름을 따 알영이라 부른다.

blocks.caption: Lady Alyoung. Born from a dragon’s rib, and the one person in Surabol who can tell the king no.
blocks.ko: 알영부인. 계룡의 갈비뼈에서 났고, 서라벌에서 임금에게 안 된다고 말할 수 있는 단 한 사람.

en: One from an egg, one from a chicken.
…Did this country start in a kitchen?

blocks.html: At the wedding feast the six chiefs stand up. They have a plan.
blocks.ko: 혼인 잔치에서 여섯 촌장이 일어선다. 그들에겐 계획이 있다.

en: We’re going to make a brand new country.
Every family cares for the others like one great house. Nobody left outside the gate.
The royals watch over the people like their own children. The nobles are wise and righteous, and decide for the good of the nation.
And everyone else we divide into six ranks, according to their virtues.
A new unity…! Silla!
lines: 우리는 아주 새로운 나라를 만들 것이오.
가문들이 한집안처럼 서로 돌보고, 누구도 문밖에 버려지지 않는 나라.
왕족은 백성을 제 자식처럼 보살피고, 귀족은 지혜롭고 의롭게 나라를 위해 판단하오.
그리고 백성은 그 덕에 따라 여섯 등급으로 나누겠소.

en: According to their virtues.
Who measures the virtue?
Well— we do. The six of us.
Then say “by whoever is sitting at this table.”
It’s shorter. And in three generations you’ll mean it.
lines: 그럼 “이 상에 앉은 사람 마음대로”라고 하시오.
더 짧소. 그리고 세 대만 지나면 정말 그 뜻이 될 테니.

blocks.html: The chiefs laugh, because it is a wedding. The boy king does not laugh. He looks at his bride as if somebody had finally said something interesting.
blocks.ko: 촌장들은 웃는다. 혼인 잔치니까. 소년 임금은 웃지 않는다. 마침내 누군가 재미있는 말을 했다는 듯 신부를 바라본다.

blocks.html: Six families end up running everything. In every new country, six families always do.
blocks.ko: 여섯 가문이 정치를 쥔다. 새 나라는 어디든, 결국 여섯 가문이 쥔다.

en: I have heard that a true man needs only
one person to cherish,
and one person to serve,
and that is enough.

blocks.html: They write the ranks down their way anyway. Alyoung is right, the way queens usually are, a few generations early. Ranks by virtue become ranks by birth. Ranks by birth become ranks by bone.
blocks.ko: 그래도 그들은 등급을 자기들 식대로 적는다. 알영이 옳다. 왕비들이 대개 그렇듯, 몇 세대 일찍. 덕에 따른 등급은 태생에 따른 등급이 된다. 태생에 따른 등급은 뼈에 따른 등급이 된다.

blocks.html: Here is how bones work in Surabol. The egg’s line marries the rib’s line, and marries it again, until a child is royal on every side. That child is Sacred Bone. Royal on one side only is True Bone. Below that, the ranks go down like steps, and every step knows exactly who is above it.
blocks.ko: 서라벌에서 뼈가 어떻게 돌아가는지 말해 주지. 알의 핏줄이 갈비뼈의 핏줄과 혼인하고, 또 혼인한다. 그러다 사방 어디로 보나 왕족인 아이가 난다. 그 아이가 성골이다. 한쪽만 왕족이면 진골이다. 그 아래로 등급이 계단처럼 내려가고, 계단마다 제 위에 누가 있는지 정확히 안다.

blocks.html: And the six who dug up the egg? Their grandchildren keep the oldest names in the country and, a few kings later, not the highest chairs. Kings arrive in eggs, chests and boxes. The six just came up out of the ground, like rice.
blocks.ko: 그럼 알을 파낸 여섯은? 그 손자들은 이 나라에서 가장 오래된 성씨를 지킨다. 그리고 몇 임금 뒤에는, 가장 높은 자리는 지키지 못한다. 임금들은 알에서, 궤짝에서, 상자에서 온다. 여섯은 그냥 땅에서 올라왔다. 벼처럼.

blocks.label: The Five Tombs
blocks.ko: 오릉

blocks.html: Sixty-one years later, the chronicle says, the king went up into the sky, and seven days after that his body came down again in five pieces, scattered over the ground. Nobody records a horse. Everybody in Surabol says there was one.
blocks.ko: 예순한 해 뒤, 편년은 말한다. 왕이 하늘로 올라갔고, 이레 뒤 그 몸이 다섯 조각으로 땅에 흩어져 내려왔다고. 말이 있었다고 적은 사람은 없다. 서라벌 사람들은 모두 있었다고 말한다.

blocks.label: The Coronation Year
blocks.ko: 즉위하던 해

blocks.html: Back in the coronation yard, Alchun finishes the story the way the old houses always do, a little too pleased with the ending.
blocks.ko: 다시 즉위식 마당. 알천은 늙은 가문들이 늘 하듯 이야기를 끝맺는다. 결말이 조금 지나치게 흐뭇한 얼굴로.

en: So that’s the Six Elders, lad. My grandfather’s grandfather was one of them. So was Bidam’s.
When Bidam said he was Six-Elder blood, he meant he was here before the egg. Before any of you.
lines: 그게 육촌이다, 얘야. 내 윗대 할아버지가 그중 하나였다. 비담네도 그랬고.
비담이 육촌 피라 한 건, 알보다 먼저 여기 있었다는 소리다. 너희 누구보다도 먼저.

en: He also said there was no Kim.
There wasn’t. Not that morning.
Ask your father about that one. He likes a story.
lines: 그건 네 아버지한테 물어라. 이야기 좋아하잖냐.

en: The egg is the polite one, Bupmin.
The next house to wear this crown came in on the tide, and stole the house we’re standing in.
lines: 이 왕관을 쓴 다음 집안은 밀물을 타고 왔다. 그리고 우리가 지금 서 있는 이 집을 훔쳤지.

blocks.html: A chest rides the tide in, a magpie screaming over it. Whatever is inside needs a house. Preferably someone else’s…!
blocks.ko: 밀물을 타고 궤짝 하나가 들어온다. 까치 한 마리가 그 위에서 울어 댄다. 안에 든 놈은 집이 필요하다. 되도록이면 남의 집이…!

logline.en: A chest washes in on the tide with a magpie crying over it. What climbs out is a con man.
logline.ko: 밀물에 궤짝 하나가 밀려오고, 그 위로 까치가 운다. 거기서 나온 건 사기꾼이다.

images.at: a chest comes in on the tide at
images.alt: A chest rides the tide into Ajinpo under a crying magpie
images.prompt: Ink painting of the myth. A heavy timber chest rides a towering ink swell into the cove at Ajinpo, the sea splashed black with claw-shaped crests of bare paper; a black magpie wheels and cries above it; the shore is a dry-brush strip with one tiny old woman holding a rope. ONE device: the long diagonal of the wave carrying the chest. MYTH INK — this beat is myth, not history, so it is painted as a STRIKING Korean ink painting (sumukhwa), not the house colour style. Joseon sumi ink on raw hanji paper with EXTREME LIGHT AGAINST DARK: huge saturated masses of black ink set against blinding bare paper; light is always the unpainted paper itself, never painted white; almost no mid-grey; hard edges where light meets dark, wet bleeding edges everywhere else. Splashed ink (pomuk), dry-brush flying white, ink spatter, mist left as untouched paper. Monumental emptiness and ONE graphic device carrying the frame; a dramatic angle (worm’s-eye, bird’s-eye, dutch). Gods, giants, beasts and wonders may fill the frame; mortals stay small inside the wonder. Figures in confident calligraphic brush line; named faces match the attached portraits, translated into a few ink strokes. Black ink and paper only, except at most ONE small translucent wash of a single colour on the one symbolic object the scene names. Not photoreal, not webtoon shading, not watercolor landscape, not oil, no glow, no halo. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. No text, no calligraphy, no seal stamp, no watermark.

images.at: standing in the middle of the hall with feathers on his shoulders
images.alt: In King Suro’s hall: Talhae, a man again, bows with feathers drifting off his shoulders; Suro on the throne, feathers settling, pale with relief
images.prompt: Inside King Suro’s torchlit Gaya hall at night, worm’s-eye from the floor, hard dutch tilt: a burst of brown sparrow feathers explodes outward around Talhae as he lands back in his own body, already dropping into a lopsided bow, grinning; behind and above him on the dais King Suro, falcon feathers still swirling off his shoulders, grips the throne arms, pale with relief. Feathers fly at the lens. MANGA ACTION FRAME: a single seinen historical-manga action panel painted in ink and oil — bold dry-brush sumi-ink SPEED LINES streaking along the direction of motion, radial FOCUS LINES converging on the face or the blade, motion smears on legs, mane, cloth and steel, flung ink-splatter dirt and dust, extreme foreshortening and a hard dutch tilt so the frame itself feels like it is moving; heavy black ink masses against a few hard highlights, one gold accent. Faces stay clean webtoon ink line with fierce narrowed eyes. Full-bleed single frame: NO panel borders, NO speech bubbles, NO onomatopoeia or sound-effect lettering, NO text of any kind. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — SEOK TALHAE. Look: Very tall (nine cheok), long-limbed and sea-weathered, tanned, broad easy grin, sly narrow eyes; black hair in a loose topknot with salt-stiff strands; clean-shaven as a young man, a short grey beard when he is old and king. Dress: Young: plain undyed hemp jeogori and trousers, sleeves rolled, a fisherman’s cord belt. King: deep sea-green silk robe with a gold-ringed belt and a low gold diadem. Demeanor: A con man who became a king and never stopped enjoying the joke. Deadpan when caught, delighted when he wins. #5a7fa8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | KING SURO — FACE and garments from attached /ch_suro.png (face only; invent a new pose). #e0a33c as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.alt: The queen of Dapana lays her egg in a chest at the night shore
images.prompt: Ink painting of the myth. Night shore of Dapana: a queen in layered robes kneels at the waterline, forehead pressed to a huge silk-wrapped egg lying inside an open chest among a few treasures; the chest lid is a black diagonal; the night sea is one solid mass of black ink and the moon a bare paper circle; far up the beach the king is a small black back walking away. ONE device: the open lid’s diagonal. MYTH INK — this beat is myth, not history, so it is painted as a STRIKING Korean ink painting (sumukhwa), not the house colour style. Joseon sumi ink on raw hanji paper with EXTREME LIGHT AGAINST DARK: huge saturated masses of black ink set against blinding bare paper; light is always the unpainted paper itself, never painted white; almost no mid-grey; hard edges where light meets dark, wet bleeding edges everywhere else. Splashed ink (pomuk), dry-brush flying white, ink spatter, mist left as untouched paper. Monumental emptiness and ONE graphic device carrying the frame; a dramatic angle (worm’s-eye, bird’s-eye, dutch). Gods, giants, beasts and wonders may fill the frame; mortals stay small inside the wonder. Figures in confident calligraphic brush line; named faces match the attached portraits, translated into a few ink strokes. Black ink and paper only, except at most ONE small translucent wash of a single colour on the one symbolic object the scene names. Not photoreal, not webtoon shading, not watercolor landscape, not oil, no glow, no halo. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. No text, no calligraphy, no seal stamp, no watermark.

blocks.html: Late in the first king’s reign, a chest comes in on the tide at a fishing beach. A magpie flies over it, crying.
blocks.ko: 첫 임금의 치세도 저물 무렵, 밀물을 타고 궤짝 하나가 갯마을 바닷가로 들어온다. 그 위로 까치 한 마리가 울며 난다.

blocks.html: It has come a long way. A thousand li north-east of Wa, the islands across the sea, the queen of a country called Dapana carried a child for seven years and was delivered of an egg. The king said a person who lays an egg is an ill omen and should get rid of it. She could not. She wrapped it in silk, packed it in a chest with treasure, and gave it to the sea.
blocks.ko: 먼 길을 왔다. 바다 건너 섬나라 왜에서 동북쪽으로 천 리, 다파나라는 나라의 왕비가 아이를 일곱 해 품고는 알을 낳았다. 왕은 사람이 알을 낳는 것은 상서롭지 못하니 버리라 했다. 왕비는 그러지 못했다. 알을 비단에 싸서 보물과 함께 궤짝에 넣고, 바다에 맡겼다.

blocks.html: It reaches Gaya first. The people of Golden Gaya see a strange chest bobbing off their beach and, being sensible, leave it there.
blocks.ko: 궤짝은 먼저 가야에 닿는다. 금관가야 사람들은 이상한 궤짝이 바닷가에 떠다니는 것을 보고, 분별 있게도, 그냥 둔다.

blocks.html: Gaya tells it differently, and with more nerve. In the Gaya chronicle Talhae comes ashore a grown man, walks into King Suro’s hall, and asks for the throne.
blocks.ko: 가야는 이 이야기를 다르게, 더 배짱 좋게 한다. 가야의 기록에서 탈해는 다 큰 사내로 뭍에 올라 수로왕의 전각으로 걸어 들어가서는, 왕좌를 내놓으라고 한다.

blocks.caption: Seok Talhae. He arrived in a chest and talks like he owns the beach.
blocks.ko: 석탈해. 궤짝에 실려 왔는데, 말투는 해변 주인이다.

blocks.hanja: 身長九尺，風神秀朗，智識過人。
blocks.html: He stood nine feet tall, fine and bright in bearing, and cleverer than other men.
blocks.ko: 키가 아홉 자요, 풍채가 빼어나고 환하였으며, 지혜와 식견이 남보다 뛰어났다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 1, Silla Annals — Talhae Isageum

en: I’ve come for your throne.
You can fight me for it, or you can save us both the afternoon.
lines: 겨루어도 좋고, 서로 오후를 아껴도 좋소.

en: …Heaven gave it to me.
I— it isn’t mine to give. Or to… lose.
lines: 과인이— 내줄 수 있는 것이 아니오. 잃을 수 있는 것도…

blocks.html: So they fight the way kings fight in that country. Talhae becomes a hawk, and Suro becomes an eagle. Talhae becomes a sparrow, and Suro becomes a falcon. When Talhae is a man again he is standing in the middle of the hall with feathers on his shoulders, and he bows.
blocks.ko: 그래서 둘은 그 나라에서 왕들이 겨루는 방식으로 겨룬다. 탈해가 매가 되자 수로는 독수리가 된다. 탈해가 참새가 되자 수로는 새매가 된다. 탈해가 다시 사람이 되었을 때 그는 어깨에 깃털을 얹은 채 전각 한가운데 서 있다. 그리고 절을 한다.

en: …That was a falcon.
Fine. I’ll find a country with a smaller king.
lines: 좋소. 왕이 좀 작은 나라를 찾아보지.

blocks.label: Ajinpo
blocks.ko: 아진포

blocks.html: Either way, the chest goes on. At Ajinpo an old woman on the shore hauls it in with a rope and opens it, and there is a little boy inside, sitting among the treasure as if it were his luggage.
blocks.ko: 어느 쪽이든 궤짝은 계속 간다. 아진포 바닷가에서 한 노파가 밧줄로 궤짝을 끌어올려 열어 보니, 안에 사내아이 하나가 보물 사이에 짐 보따리라도 되는 듯 앉아 있다.

en: Well.
You’re not a fish.
No.
Is this the country?

blocks.html: She names him herself, since there is nobody else to ask. A magpie followed the chest in, so she takes the bird out of the character for magpie, and what is left, Seok, is his surname. He got loose from the chest and came out of it, so he is Talhae, the one who got loose.
blocks.ko: 달리 물어볼 사람도 없으니 이름은 그녀가 짓는다. 까치가 궤짝을 따라왔으니 까치 작(鵲) 자에서 새 조(鳥)를 떼어 낸다. 남은 석(昔)이 그의 성이다. 궤짝을 풀고 나왔으니 탈해(脫解), 풀려난 아이다.

blocks.html: He grows nine cheok tall, fishes to feed the old woman and never once complains about it, and when she tells him that a boy with bones like his should study, he studies geography. Mostly the part about where the good ground is.
blocks.ko: 그는 아홉 자로 자라고, 고기를 낚아 노파를 먹이며 한 번도 싫은 내색을 하지 않는다. 너 같은 골격을 가진 아이는 공부를 해야 한다고 노파가 말하자, 그는 지리를 공부한다. 주로 좋은 땅이 어디 있는지에 관한 부분을.

blocks.label: The Crescent House
blocks.ko: 반월의 집

blocks.html: Looking over the city, he picks the best ground in it, a crescent-shaped rise above the river, and finds that someone already lives there. The house belongs to Hogong, a minister who came over the sea from Wa long ago with a gourd tied at his waist to float on, and has the name to prove it.
blocks.ko: 도성을 내려다보며 그는 그 안에서 가장 좋은 땅을 고른다. 강 위로 반달 모양으로 솟은 언덕. 그런데 이미 누가 살고 있다. 집주인은 호공이다. 오래전 허리에 박을 매달고 왜에서 바다를 건너온 대신으로, 그 이름이 증거다.

blocks.hanja: 瓠公者，未詳其族姓，本倭人，初以瓠繫腰渡海而來，故稱瓠公。
blocks.html: As for Hogong, his clan and surname are not known. He was a man of Wa, and at first he crossed the sea with a gourd tied at his waist; hence he was called Hogong, Lord Gourd.
blocks.ko: 호공은 그 족성을 자세히 알 수 없다. 본래 왜인으로, 처음에 박을 허리에 매고 바다를 건너왔으므로 호공이라 불렀다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 1, Silla Annals — Hyeokgeose, yr. 38

blocks.html: Talhae does not have a house. He has a plan. One night he buries a whetstone and a sack of charcoal beside Hogong’s gate, and in the morning he goes to the magistrate and says the house was his family’s, taken while they were away.
blocks.ko: 탈해에게는 집이 없다. 계획이 있다. 어느 밤 그는 호공의 대문 옆에 숫돌과 숯 한 자루를 묻고, 아침이 되자 관아에 가서 그 집이 원래 자기 집안 것이었는데 집을 비운 사이 빼앗겼다고 아뢴다.

en: I have lived in that house thirty years!
lines: 내가 저 집에서 삼십 년을 살았소!

en: And my family lived there before you. We were smiths.
Dig by the gate, if you don’t believe me.
lines: 그 전에는 우리 집안이 살았소. 대장장이였지.
못 믿겠거든 대문 옆을 파 보시오.

blocks.html: They dig. The whetstone and the charcoal come up out of the ground, black and convincing, and the magistrate gives Talhae the house.
blocks.ko: 파 본다. 숫돌과 숯이 땅속에서 나온다. 시커멓고, 그럴듯하게. 관아는 집을 탈해에게 준다.

en: …You buried those last night.
Prove it.

blocks.html: The ground becomes the Moon Palace, where every king of Silla after him will live, which means every king of Silla lives in a stolen house, including the one who has just moved in. Nobody in the palace likes it when you mention this.
blocks.ko: 그 땅이 월성, 반월성이 된다. 그 뒤 신라의 모든 왕이 그곳에 산다. 다시 말해 신라의 모든 왕은 훔친 집에 산다. 방금 이사 들어온 임금까지. 궁에서는 누가 이 말을 꺼내면 다들 싫어한다.

blocks.label: Two Kings Later
blocks.ko: 두 임금 뒤

blocks.html: King Namhae hears about the clever young man in the crescent house and marries him to his daughter. Two kings later Talhae is sixty-two and on the throne himself, and one of the first things he does is make Hogong his chief minister, which is either an apology or the best joke in the annals.
blocks.ko: 남해왕은 반달 언덕 집의 영리한 젊은이 이야기를 듣고 딸을 그에게 시집보낸다. 왕이 두 번 바뀐 뒤, 예순둘의 탈해가 몸소 왕위에 오른다. 그가 맨 먼저 한 일 가운데 하나는 호공을 대보로 삼은 것이다. 사과이거나, 아니면 사서 전체에서 가장 좋은 농담이거나.

blocks.hanja: 二年春正月，拜瓠公爲大輔。
blocks.html: Second year, spring, first month: he appointed Hogong Grand Minister.
blocks.ko: 이년 봄 정월, 호공을 대보로 삼았다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 1, Silla Annals — Talhae Isageum

en: …Grand Minister.
You know the best ground in the city. I could use a man like that.
lines: 도성에서 제일 좋은 땅을 아는 사람 아니오. 그런 사람이 필요하오.

en: I knew it. You did bury them.
Prove it.

blocks.label: The Moon Palace
blocks.ko: 월성

blocks.html: Seven hundred years later, King Muyeol spends his first night in the stolen house awake. He keeps listening for someone digging by the gate.
blocks.ko: 칠백 년 뒤, 무열왕은 훔친 집에서의 첫날 밤을 뜬눈으로 보낸다. 누가 대문 옆을 파는 소리가 나지 않나 자꾸 귀를 기울인다.

en: Nobody is digging, Your Majesty. Go to sleep.
And if a rooster crows, it’s a rooster.

blocks.html: “Hogong. There’s a rooster in the woods.” It is the middle of the night. Roosters don’t crow at night…!
blocks.ko: “호공. 숲에서 닭이 운다.” 한밤중이다. 닭은 밤에 울지 않는다…!

logline.en: Roosters don’t crow at night. In the woods west of the city, one does.
logline.ko: 닭은 밤에 울지 않는다. 도성 서쪽 숲에서, 한 마리가 운다.

images.at: I came in a box too
images.alt: The old king Talhae crouches over the opened golden box, grinning; the small boy inside looks back at him as if the king were the strange one
images.prompt: Point of view from inside the opened golden box looking up: old King Talhae, short grey beard, leans down over the rim grinning, his face foreshortened and huge; at the bottom edge of the frame the small boy’s tiny hand and white silk sleeve reach up. Courtiers lean in blurred behind the king; a lattice shaft of morning light falls past him into the box. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — SEOK TALHAE. Look: Very tall (nine cheok), long-limbed and sea-weathered, tanned, broad easy grin, sly narrow eyes; black hair in a loose topknot with salt-stiff strands; clean-shaven as a young man, a short grey beard when he is old and king. Dress: Young: plain undyed hemp jeogori and trousers, sleeves rolled, a fisherman’s cord belt. King: deep sea-green silk robe with a gold-ringed belt and a low gold diadem. Demeanor: A con man who became a king and never stopped enjoying the joke. Deadpan when caught, delighted when he wins. #5a7fa8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | KIM ALJI. Look: A small boy of about four, round solemn face, bright wide-awake black eyes, short black hair tied in a tiny tuft. Dress: Wrapped in a little white silk cloth with a thin gold thread edge. Demeanor: Unafraid; looks at kings as if they were the strange ones. #d4b86a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. images.at: wakes to a rooster crowing in the woods west of the city
images.alt: At night a band of cloud hangs into Sirim wood and a rooster crows
images.prompt: Ink painting of the myth. Night over Sirim: a long band of cloud hangs straight down out of a black ink sky into the wood like a lowered scroll; at its foot, among black trunks, the small silhouette of a rooster crowing; the city’s roofs tiny and black in the far distance with one lit window. ONE device: the vertical cloud band. MYTH INK — this beat is myth, not history, so it is painted as a STRIKING Korean ink painting (sumukhwa), not the house colour style. Joseon sumi ink on raw hanji paper with EXTREME LIGHT AGAINST DARK: huge saturated masses of black ink set against blinding bare paper; light is always the unpainted paper itself, never painted white; almost no mid-grey; hard edges where light meets dark, wet bleeding edges everywhere else. Splashed ink (pomuk), dry-brush flying white, ink spatter, mist left as untouched paper. Monumental emptiness and ONE graphic device carrying the frame; a dramatic angle (worm’s-eye, bird’s-eye, dutch). Gods, giants, beasts and wonders may fill the frame; mortals stay small inside the wonder. Figures in confident calligraphic brush line; named faces match the attached portraits, translated into a few ink strokes. Black ink and paper only, except at most ONE small translucent wash of a single colour on the one symbolic object the scene names. Not photoreal, not webtoon shading, not watercolor landscape, not oil, no glow, no halo. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. No text, no calligraphy, no seal stamp, no watermark.

blocks.html: Bidam said there was no Kim. He was right for about a hundred and twenty years. Then, one spring night, King Talhae wakes to a rooster crowing in the woods west of the city.
blocks.ko: 비담은 김씨가 없었다고 했다. 백이십 년쯤은 그 말이 맞았다. 그러다 어느 봄밤, 탈해왕이 도성 서쪽 숲에서 닭이 우는 소리에 잠을 깬다.

en: Hogong. There’s a rooster in Sirim.
Go and see what it wants.
Majesty, it’s a rooster. It wants—
…Yes, Majesty. Going.

blocks.html: At first light Hogong walks into Sirim with a lantern he no longer needs, and finds a small box of gold hanging from a branch, and a white rooster underneath it, crowing at nothing.
blocks.ko: 날이 밝을 무렵 호공은 이제 필요도 없는 등불을 들고 시림으로 들어간다. 나뭇가지에 작은 금빛 궤짝이 걸려 있고, 그 아래에서 흰 닭 한 마리가 아무것도 없는 데를 향해 울고 있다.

blocks.html: They bring the box to the king and open it, and inside is a little boy, handsome and wide awake, who looks at the king as if the king were the one who had turned up in a box.
blocks.ko: 궤짝을 왕 앞에 가져와 여니, 안에 잘생기고 눈이 말똥말똥한 사내아이가 있다. 아이는 궤짝에서 나타난 쪽이 왕이기라도 한 것처럼 왕을 쳐다본다.

en: Well.
I came in a box too, you know. Mine was bigger.
lines: 나도 궤짝 타고 왔다. 내 건 더 컸지.

blocks.hanja: 瓠公還告，王使人取櫝開之，有小男兒在其中，姿容奇偉。上喜，謂左右曰：「此豈非天遺我以令胤乎！」乃收養之。
blocks.html: Hogong came back and reported it. The king had the chest brought and opened, and inside was a little boy of remarkable looks. The king was glad and said to those around him: “Is this not Heaven sending me a fine heir?” And he took him in and raised him.
blocks.ko: 호공이 돌아와 아뢰자, 왕이 사람을 시켜 궤짝을 가져와 열게 하니, 그 안에 작은 사내아이가 있었는데 생김새가 뛰어났다. 왕이 기뻐하여 좌우에 말하였다. “이 어찌 하늘이 내게 훌륭한 아들을 보내 준 것이 아니겠는가!” 그리고 거두어 길렀다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 1, Silla Annals — Talhae Isageum

blocks.html: Because he came out of a golden box, he is given the surname Kim, gold. Because he is a child, he is called Alji. The wood where the rooster crowed is renamed Gyerim, Rooster Wood, and for a while the whole country goes by that name.
blocks.ko: 금빛 궤짝에서 나왔으니 성은 김, 금이다. 아이이니 이름은 알지다. 닭이 울던 숲은 계림, 닭의 숲으로 이름이 바뀌고, 한동안은 나라 전체가 그 이름으로 불린다.

blocks.html: The boy grows up in the palace, quick and easy to like. The court notices. Talhae has sons of his own. He also has ministers who can count.
blocks.ko: 아이는 궁에서 자란다. 영리하고, 미워하기 어렵다. 조정이 눈여겨본다. 탈해에게는 제 아들들이 있다. 셈할 줄 아는 대신들도 있다.

en: Alji. The ministers say Heaven sent you to me as an heir.
Heaven sends a great many things. It sent me a magpie.
So. Do you want the chair?
lines: 알지. 대신들이 하늘이 그대를 내 후사로 보냈다 하오.
하늘은 이것저것 많이도 보내지. 나한텐 까치를 보냈어.

en: …No, Majesty.
Your sons were here first.
Ha! First. I came in a chest. You came in a box.
Nobody in this palace was here first except six old men, and they don’t want the chair either.
lines: 하! 먼저라. 나는 궤짝 타고 왔고, 그대는 상자 타고 왔소.
이 궁에서 먼저 와 있던 건 늙은이 여섯뿐인데, 그 양반들도 이 의자는 마다하오.

en: Then I’ll wait.
How long?
As long as it takes. Gold doesn’t rust, Majesty.
lines: 걸리는 만큼요. 금은 녹슬지 않으니까요, 폐하.

blocks.html: So Alji does not get the throne, and by every account he never asks again. It takes his line seven generations to reach the crown. When they do, they keep it for six hundred years, call themselves the Kims of Surabol, and look down on a family from Gaya who have the same name for a different reason. Many generations after that, one of them is a man named Chunchu.
blocks.ko: 그래서 알지는 왕위를 받지 않고, 어느 기록을 보아도 다시는 청하지 않는다. 그의 핏줄이 왕관에 닿기까지 일곱 대가 걸린다. 닿고 나서는 육백 년을 지키고, 스스로를 서라벌 김씨라 부르며, 다른 이유로 같은 성을 가진 가야 출신 집안을 내려다본다. 그로부터 또 여러 대 뒤, 그 가운데 하나가 춘추라는 사내다.

blocks.html: Under a certain hill beyond the city, the steam says the same word every time it leaves the water. Kim. It will be a long time before anybody answers it.
blocks.ko: 도성 너머 어느 언덕 아래에서는, 김이 물을 떠날 때마다 같은 말을 한다. 김. 누군가 그 말에 대답하기까지는 아직 오래 걸릴 것이다.

blocks.label: Gyerim
blocks.ko: 계림

blocks.html: In the coronation year the wood is still there, beside the Moon Palace. After dark the new king walks his son through it.
blocks.ko: 즉위하던 해에도 그 숲은 월성 곁에 그대로 있다. 해가 지면 새 임금이 아들과 함께 그 숲을 걷는다.

en: Park came out of an egg. Seok came out of a chest and stole a house. We came out of a box and waited seven generations for a chair.
Every house that ever wore this crown arrived in something. That’s why they count bones here, Bupmin.
The people who were here first need something to count.
lines: 박씨는 알에서 나왔다. 석씨는 궤짝에서 나와 집을 훔쳤고. 우리는 상자에서 나와 의자 하나를 일곱 대나 기다렸다.
이 왕관을 쓴 집안은 모두 무언가를 타고 왔다. 그래서 여기서는 뼈를 세는 거다, 법민아.
먼저 와 있던 사람들한테는 셀 것이 있어야 하거든.

en: And you, Father? You didn’t come out of anything.
lines: 그럼 아버님은요? 아무것도 타고 오지 않으셨잖습니까.

en: No. Tired men in Tang silk voted me in.
So I’ll have to earn it the vulgar way. Three kingdoms, one crown.
Starting with the one that keeps knocking.
lines: 그래. 나는 당나라 비단 입은 지친 사내들이 뽑았지.
그러니 천한 방식으로 벌어야지. 세 나라, 왕관 하나.

blocks.html: Across the border in Sabi, a funeral bell. For three years the king can’t sign a thing. The clans already have a list…!
blocks.ko: 국경 너머 사비에 상종이 울린다. 삼 년 동안 임금은 도장 하나 찍지 못한다. 가문들 손에는 이미 명단이 있다…!

toneNote: A grandmother's fireside cycle on Tamla, braided against a court rotting from the inside.
title: The Fall of Euija

logline.en: Three years of mourning, by the rite. Everyone in Sabi knows exactly what can be done inside them.
logline.ko: 예법대로라면 삼년상이다. 사비 사람이라면 그 삼 년 안에 무엇을 할 수 있는지 정확히 안다.

Plain dark tack, a yellow cord at the bridle. The fastest horse in Samhan: at full gallop his body stretches long and low, neck level, ears pinned, mane and tail streaming flat behind, hooves barely touching. Named for Gomanaru (Ungjin); stands by its master's planted sword after the field. | HORSE ANATOMY is a centrepiece: the whole horse body reads clearly and beautifully — arched neck, deep chest, sloping shoulder, round haunch, clean long legs in a correct gait, every muscle modelled by the one hard key with a bright edge along the topline and deep shadow under the belly; the horse is never cropped into a blob, never hidden behind dust, never stiff like a toy; mane and tail as flowing painted strokes; the coat colour exactly as the board. | Kingdom banners: copy field colour and emblem from the attached flag_*.png ref onto period silk war-banners — tall poles behind each side, long streamers, small pennants on spear-tips and saddle-backs. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Medium close, low three-quarter, a stone-carver's yard beside a temple in a Baekje fortress at blue hour in the first month, frost on packed earth. ONE device: the tall upright slab of a grey granite stele as a vertical on the left third, its fresh-cut face raked by the light (the carved strokes shallow and blurred, nothing readable). Old Satek Jijuk, FACE ONLY from the attached portrait, wearing the Baekje great-clan crown from the attached board, kneeling on a straw mat before the stone, one palm flat against the cut surface, head bowed, eyes wet and unblinking; the carver's chisel and mallet lie by his knee. Foreground: out-of-focus brazier embers. Background: a half-built pagoda in timber scaffolding and a temple hall's giwa eaves dissolving into blue mist. Key: a brazier low at the right raking warm gold across the stone, his hands and silk. CANON — MINISTER SATEK — FACE and garments from attached /ch_satek_minister.png (face only; invent a new pose). Crown: the great-clan gilt crown (see NOBLE CROWN), no jougwan. #c2a24a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | NOBLE CROWN: Baekje great-clan lord’s gilt-bronze crown (금동관), as the attached crown (ignore its museum stand and black backdrop): a tall pointed gilt cap shaped like a peaked hood, pierced all over with openwork dragon-and-flame scrolls, a broad engraved band across the brow, a curved openwork crest arching over the top, two small cup-shaped finials on thin stems rising at the back, a pointed bud finial at the crown, and a flat openwork leaf-plume at the front. Worn high over the topknot on court and assembly days; burnished gold-bronze catching the key light. It replaces the jougwan. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Baekje: attached /ref_hanbok_baekje_gaya.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill.
