images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Night in the Satek clan hall at Sabi: a low lacquered table, ONE oil lamp on it. Minister Satek at the head, scarred face lit from below, leaning forward on his fists; three older Satek lords leaning in along the sides. Every man wears the tall gilt-bronze noble crown, gold catching the lamp; their shadows climb the plaster wall behind. Low angle from the end of the table. Device: the table as a dark wedge toward the lamp. CANON — MINISTER SATEK — FACE and garments from attached /ch_satek_minister.png (face only; invent a new pose). Crown: the great-clan gilt crown (see NOBLE CROWN), no jougwan. #c2a24a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | NOBLE CROWN: Baekje great-clan lord’s gilt-bronze crown (금동관), as the attached crown (ignore its museum stand and black backdrop): a tall pointed gilt cap shaped like a peaked hood, pierced all over with openwork dragon-and-flame scrolls, a broad engraved band across the brow, a curved openwork crest arching over the top, two small cup-shaped finials on thin stems rising at the back, a pointed bud finial at the crown, and a flat openwork leaf-plume at the front. Worn high over the topknot on court and assembly days; burnished gold-bronze catching the key light. It replaces the jougwan. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Baekje: attached /ref_hanbok_baekje_gaya.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). blocks.html: He calls the assembly the way a gambler calls a final hand — smiling, sleeves perfect, already knowing which tiles he slipped into the set.
blocks.ko: 그는 마지막 패를 부르는 노름꾼처럼 어전회의를 소집한다 — 웃고, 소매는 반듯하고, 패 속에 자기가 섞어 둔 패가 무엇인지 이미 아는 얼굴로.

blocks.html: Mourning ends at dawn. By breakfast Euija has called the Ministers’ Assembly to the Rock of Politics. The rock is dry. Someone forgot the brine, or remembered it and chose not to.
blocks.ko: 상은 새벽에 끝난다. 아침상이 들어오기도 전에 의자는 정사암으로 회의를 소집한다. 바위는 말라 있다. 소금물을 잊었거나, 기억하고도 바르지 않았다.

blocks.html: Look at the room while it still looks like this. Eight senior benches, one to a great house. Four generations, the same eight houses. Satek and Yunbi sit highest. The Premier’s chair belongs to Satek, the way the brine does.
blocks.ko: 이 방이 아직 이 모양일 때 잘 봐 두라. 좌평 자리 여덟, 대성 한 집에 한 자리. 네 대째 같은 여덟 가문이다. 사택과 연비가 가장 높이 앉는다. 상좌평 자리는 사택의 것이다. 소금물이 그렇듯이.

blocks.title: The Rock of Politics, before · 정사암, 그 전
blocks.caption: Eight senior benches, eight houses, and a Satek in the Premier’s chair.
blocks.ko: 좌평 여덟 자리에 여덟 가문, 상좌평 자리에는 사택.

lines: 우리 백성의 자유와 행복을 약탈하는 파렴치한 친당 반국가세력을 일거에 척결하기 위해 —
en: Beloved people.
As Eraha, I appeal to you with a heart that spits blood.
To eradicate in one stroke the shameless pro-Tang anti-state forces that plunder our people’s freedom and happiness —
I hereby declare emergency martial law.

blocks.html: Somebody coughs. Nobody looks at the rock. On the Satek bench a young man leans to his elder and whispers, loud enough to carry two benches over.
blocks.ko: 누군가 기침을 한다. 아무도 바위를 보지 않는다. 사택 쪽 자리에서 젊은 사내 하나가 어른 쪽으로 몸을 기울여 속삭인다. 두 자리 건너까지 들릴 만큼.

lines: 회의 전에 포고문을 찍어 두셨네. 먹 냄새 나요.
en: King Onjo preserve us — he’s lost his mind…
Also he printed the proclamation before the session. I can smell the ink.
The characters for “in one stroke” are still wet.

lines: 이 나라의 법도를 믿고 따라 온 선량한 백성들께 다소 불편이 있을 수 있소.
en: There may be some inconveniences for the good people who have followed the lawful order of this country.
We will strive to minimize such inconveniences.
I place my trust solely in you.
Please trust me.
Majesty. For how long?

lines: 임시란 — 영구라고 말하기 두려울 때 영구가 시작되는 방식이지.
en: This is temporary.
Temporary is how permanent things begin when you are afraid to say permanent.

blocks.html: Then he unrolls a second scroll — shorter, denser, the kind of law that fits on one sheet because the power is in what it erases. The clerks name it before he does: the Law to Remedy the Distress of the People and the Country.
blocks.ko: 이어 두 번째 두루마리를 펼친다 — 더 짧고, 더 빽빽하고, 지우는 것에 힘이 있어서 한 장으로 충분한 법. 서리들이 그보다 먼저 이름을 붙인다. 백성과 나라의 곤경을 덜기 위한 법.

lines: 백제의 법은 회의가 정한 절차 외에, 어라하의 명으로도 제정할 수 있다.
그 법은 옛 관례에서 벗어날 수 있다 — 회의 그 자체를 폐하지 않는 한.
회의의 존립은 위태롭지 않다. 상좌평의 자리도 그대로 둔다.
en: Laws of Baekje may also be enacted by the Eraha’s command.
Such laws may deviate from old custom — insofar as the Assembly as such is not abolished.
The existence of the Assembly is not endangered. The Premier’s chair remains undisturbed.
Your Majesty. That is… a law for emptying the Assembly.
It keeps the name. It changes the people.

lines: 이제 여러분 스스로 고르시오. 평화인가, 전쟁인가.
en: If the name remains, the country remains.
If the people remain, the people eat the country.
May you now choose for yourselves — peace, or war.

blocks.html: Nobody chooses war out loud. Choosing peace means raising a sleeve for the scroll, and for a long moment nobody does that either. Then a sleeve goes up on the Satek bench. It belongs to Satek Chunbok, the young man who was whispering about wet ink.
blocks.ko: 아무도 큰 소리로 전쟁을 고르지 않는다. 평화를 고르려면 두루마리에 소매를 들어야 하는데, 한참 동안 그것도 아무도 하지 않는다. 그때 사택 쪽 자리에서 소매 하나가 올라간다. 젖은 먹 냄새를 속삭이던 그 젊은이, 사택춘복이다.

en: Chunbok. Put your arm down.

lines: 어르신께서도 잘 아시다시피, 폐하께서는 평화냐 전쟁이냐를 물으셨습니다.
en: As my lord well knows, His Majesty asked for peace or war.
I am choosing peace.

blocks.html: The old men try to rally, Satek calling in four generations of favors. Too late. The other houses, the ones Satek kept out of the light for a century, raise their sleeves one after another, delighted. Some are already paid. Some are already afraid. Some are the king’s own sons, waiting in the corridor.
blocks.ko: 늙은 대신들이 판을 되돌리려 한다. 사택은 사 대에 걸친 빚을 한꺼번에 불러들인다. 너무 늦었다. 백 년 동안 사택에 가려 그늘에 있던 다른 가문들이 신이 나서 하나씩 소매를 든다. 이미 삯을 받은 자, 이미 겁난 자, 그리고 복도에서 기다리던 왕의 아들들.

blocks.html: A face-off only works if you know your opponent’s style, and Euija has spent twenty years teaching them his. They lined up for a duel. He had already changed who was sitting.
blocks.ko: 맞대결은 상대의 수를 알 때나 통한다. 의자는 이십 년 동안 그들에게 자기 수를 가르쳐 왔다. 그들은 결투하려고 줄을 섰다. 그는 이미 앉는 사람을 바꿔 놓았다.

blocks.html: Euija names forty-one of his own sons to the Assembly, firing every single existing member. Eight houses spent four generations sharpening tricks on each other. Marriages. Roads. Clerks planted in rival counting-rooms. In one morning the king clears the board. He simply changes the pieces. By noon nobody has an answer.
blocks.ko: 의자는 제 아들 마흔하나를 좌평에 앉히고, 기존 인사를 모조리 내친다. 여덟 가문은 네 대에 걸쳐 서로를 겨눈 수를 갈아 왔다. 혼인. 길. 상대 계산방에 심어 둔 서기. 왕은 하루아침에 판을 쓸어 버린다. 그냥 말을 바꿔 버린 것이다. 정오가 되어도 받아칠 말이 없다.

blocks.html: Satek Chunbok is named Premier. His own clan watches him walk to the chair. The Enabling Law did not abolish the chair. It only changed who sits in it.
blocks.ko: 사택춘복이 상좌평에 오른다. 제 가문이 그가 그 자리로 걸어가는 것을 지켜본다. 수권법은 그 자리를 없애지 않았다. 앉는 사람만 바꿨을 뿐이다.

blocks.title: The Rock of Politics, after · 정사암, 그 후
blocks.caption: The same benches. Every one of them a son.
blocks.ko: 같은 자리. 전부 아들이다.

blocks.caption: A Satek in the Satek chair, sitting for the king.
blocks.ko: 사택의 자리에 앉은 사택. 왕을 위해 앉았다.

blocks.html: Forty-one sons need forty-one seats. None goes to the Ye family. They have held Bear Fortress for four generations and never once been asked to court. Ye Sikjin reads the list at home, twice. Then he puts it in a drawer.
blocks.ko: 아들 마흔하나에게는 자리 마흔하나가 필요하다. 예씨 몫은 하나도 없다. 네 대째 웅진성을 지켜 왔건만 조정에 한 번도 불려 간 적 없는 집안이다. 예식진은 집에서 명단을 두 번 읽는다. 그리고 서랍에 넣는다.

blocks.html: Four generations of the Ye family, and not one invitation.
blocks.ko: 예씨 가문 사 대, 초대장은 한 장도 없었다.

blocks.html: Then he hands out the quiet money that really runs Baekje. Harbour warehouses. River pilot fees. The stamp a ship needs before it sails east. The martial law was the noise. The stamps are what change.
blocks.ko: 그다음 그는 백제를 실제로 굴리는 조용한 돈을 다시 나눈다. 바닷가 창고. 강의 도선료. 동쪽으로 떠나는 배에 찍는 도장. 계엄은 소음이었다. 바뀌는 건 도장이다.

blocks.html: He cannot do what Yeon did. Baekje would not forgive it, and more to the point, he would not. He does not need a banquet. He needs a majority that looks like kinship.
blocks.ko: 연개소문이 한 짓은 하지 못한다. 백제가 용서하지 않을 것이고, 더 중요한 건 — 그 자신도 하지 않을 것이다. 잔치는 필요 없다. 혈연처럼 보이는 다수가 필요할 뿐이다.

blocks.label: That Night
blocks.ko: 그날 밤

blocks.html: That night he writes one letter himself, with no clerk in the room. It is short, because the man it is for cannot read. A boatman will have to say it to him aloud.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 그는 서기도 물리고 손수 편지 한 장을 쓴다. 짧다. 받을 사람이 글을 못 읽기 때문이다. 뱃사공이 소리 내어 일러 줘야 할 것이다.

lines: 오늘 밤이다, 춘복. 늙은이들이 잃은 걸 다 세기 전에.
en: Tamla. The fastest boat in the harbour.
Tonight, Chunbok. Before the old men finish counting what they lost.

lines: 폐하… 폐하께서도 잘 아시다시피, 오늘 밤 가문들은 셈을 하고 있습니다.
자리가 식기도 전에 탐라로 배가 떠나면, 저들은 그것을 전쟁으로 읽을 것입니다.
먼저 지는 데 익숙해지게 두십시오. 한 달입니다. 그다음에 부르십시오.
en: Your Majesty… as Your Majesty well knows, the houses are counting tonight.
If a boat leaves for Tamla before the benches are cold, they will read it as war.
Let them get used to losing first. A month. Then send for him.

lines: 좋다. 한 달. 그놈은 기다리는 건 잘해. 세거든.
en: …A month.
Fine. A month. He’s good at waiting. He counts.

blocks.html: He folds the letter into his sleeve. It will stay there a good deal longer than a month.
blocks.ko: 그는 편지를 접어 소매에 넣는다. 그 편지는 한 달보다 훨씬 오래 거기 머물 것이다.

lines: 폐하. 오늘은 몇 분이나 자르셨습니까? / …저희는 몇이나 남기시려고요.
en: Your Majesty. How many did you dismiss today? / …And how many of us will you keep.
All of them. / You… I keep.

lines: …무서워라. / 그런데 어쩌죠. 그런 폐하가… 더 가깝게 느껴져요.
en: …How frightening. / And yet — that kind of Majesty… feels nearer.
…What was your name again.

lines: 아직 없습니다. / 오늘 밤에 하나 지어 주세요. / 계백 장군한테 하셨듯이 — 오래.
en: I don’t have one yet. / Make me one tonight. / As you did for General Gyebek — take your time.

blocks.html: Eleven of them by morning.
blocks.ko: 아침이 오기 전에 열하나가 된다.

blocks.html: Months later, the new Premier is in Chang’an, talking too much. A spy who learns his trade that well rarely works for only one house.
blocks.ko: 몇 달 뒤, 새 상좌평은 장안에서 말이 많다. 일을 그만큼 잘 배운 첩자는 한 집만 섬기는 법이 드물다.

blocks.label: Chang’an
blocks.ko: 장안

en: So… Baekje? What of Baekje—
zhLatn: Nàme… Bǎijì? Bǎijì yòu rúhé——

en: Do not trouble yourself over Baekje.

lines: 백제 족속들은 가문 싸움을 좋아해서, 서로 시기하다가 망할 것입니다.
en: Baekje will fall on its own.
Where blood ties are strong, the state grows weak.
The Baekje clans love a family feud — they will envy each other into ruin.
Then why am I needed at all?
zhLatn: Nà zhèn yòu hébì cúnzài?

lines: 아무리 약해도, 한 번의 충격은 줘야죠.
당군이 쳐들어온다고 하면, 그 소문만으로도 나라의 기세가 기울어질 것입니다.
en: However weak it is, it still needs one shock.
Say the Tang army is coming — the rumour alone will tip the country’s spirit.

blocks.html: He beat eight houses in one morning. Now he can’t sleep. In his dreams, somebody keeps counting…?
blocks.ko: 하루아침에 여덟 가문을 꺾었다. 그런데 이제 잠이 오지 않는다. 꿈속에서 누군가 자꾸 수를 센다…?

logline.en: Eight grudges, forty-one sons, and not one loyalty he didn’t create by decree.
logline.ko: 원한 여덟, 아들 마흔하나, 그리고 칙령으로 만들지 않은 충성은 하나도 없다.

images.alt: Poster key art: King Euija slumps drunk on his throne in the dark hall while the guardian stag stands behind him and lowers its head to his shoulder
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; crowns, antlers, wings and heads stay well inside the central band; no title, no lettering. Night in the dark Sabi throne hall, tenebrist: red columns sinking into black, one brazier, an empty floor. Low dutch angle from the floor. INTERACTION: King Euija sprawls sideways on the throne, crimson robe loose, yellow-gold headband askew, a wine jar hanging from two fingers; the tall white-gold stag Sinrok stands behind the throne, its antlers rising above his head like a second crown, and lowers its muzzle to nudge his cheek; he leans his head against its face without opening his eyes, a bitter little smile. The two of them alone in the huge hall. The stag is a solid painted animal — no glow, no luminous outline. The brazier is the one key (#e08a2e): it catches his face, the jar, the stag’s muzzle and the antler tips; everything else is umber-black. Brazier sparks as painted bokeh. STYLE: HEEWON STYLE, more painterly, with hints of Korean ink painting — Korean webtoon figures (clean ink linework, simplified expressive faces matching the attached portrait, watercolor-washed) inside a hand-painted world of watercolor and oil with traditional sumukhwa ink: splashed-ink storm clouds, bold dry calligraphic brush strokes in manes, fur, feathers, robes and grass, ink bleeding into wet wash, small ink splatters and drips near the frame edges, patches of bare rice paper where the edges dissolve; oil glazes only deepen the darks, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. Movie-poster key art: bold iconic silhouette, the two subjects large and close, one dramatic low angle, one bright break of light behind them, big dark masses, few hues plus one accent, film-poster drama but NO text, NO title, NO credits, NO logo, NO seal stamp. Not photoreal, not 3D. No glow aura, no halo, no emissive outline — the accent colour is real light. One of each named person. No watermark. CANON — KING EUIJA — FACE and garments from attached /ch_buyeo_euija.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Broad, bearded king; black hair in a topknot with a yellow-gold headband whose tails trail; heavy brows, cynical eyes. Dress: Crimson robe with a dark charcoal collar and gold trim; a steel lamellar pauldron peeking at one shoulder. Demeanor: Licensed wit: drinks, smirks, slumps on the throne, speaks in polished aphorisms. Fatalist. #e08a2e as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: heroic battle pose; smiling innocence. | SINROK (신록, guardian deer of Baekje, guide of onjo and biryu) — attached board /obj_sinrok.png: Pale white-gold stag with tall branching antlers — match the board's animal, but ignore its glow outline: light catches the antlers and coat as real light. Owned by no one; leads the brothers south and stays with Onjo. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS are a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST room (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt) painted in that same wash-and-glaze: a warm umber-to-black ground, walls, timber, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft with soft sfumato falloff — the webtoon figures are set INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. blocks.label: Nightmares
blocks.ko: 악몽

blocks.html: He starts dreaming about the Rock of Politics. In the dream it is dry, and he is rubbing it with brine, and the brine will not stay. Every time he lifts the cloth the stone is dry again, and the eight elders are standing round it waiting for it to sweat.
blocks.ko: 그는 정사암 꿈을 꾸기 시작한다. 꿈속에서 바위는 말라 있고, 그는 소금물을 문지르는데 소금물이 배지 않는다. 천을 들 때마다 돌은 다시 말라 있고, 여덟 원로가 그 둘레에 서서 바위가 땀 흘리기를 기다린다.

blocks.html: Some nights it is the white deer, come back out of the dark it was kept in, and too big for the hunting ground. Some nights it is a boat on the water with a man sitting very straight in the stern, not rowing, counting.
blocks.ko: 어떤 밤은 흰 사슴이다. 가둬 두었던 어둠에서 다시 나왔는데, 사냥터에 들기엔 너무 크다. 어떤 밤은 물 위의 배 한 척이고, 고물에 한 사내가 아주 꼿꼿이 앉아 있다. 노는 젓지 않고, 센다.

Your new Assembly is a made thing.
Heungsu. Is this a sermon or a memorial?

lines: 겨울이 오기 전에 사택과 윤비 사람들을 자리로 돌려놓으십시오. 신라가 온다면 탄현으로 옵니다. 당이 온다면—
en: Both, Majesty. The sermon is free.
Bring the Satek and Yunbi men back to the benches before winter. If Silla comes, it comes over Tanhyeon. If Tang comes—

lines: —강으로 온다. 그래. 과인도 지도는 읽을 줄 안다.
목소리 좋구나, 흥수. 고마미지에는 그걸 들어 줄 사람이 없지. 가서 그들에게 경이나 읽어 주거라.
en: —it comes up the river. Yes. I can read a map.
You have a lovely voice, Heungsu. Gomamiji has nobody to hear it. Go and read them sutras.

blocks.html: Euija calls it a temporary posting. The court knows better. The paper names a county far to the south: packed earth, a magistrate’s hut, and a long way from anyone who matters.
blocks.ko: 의자는 잠시 내려보내는 것이라 한다. 조정은 다 안다. 종이에 적힌 곳은 먼 남쪽 고을이다. 다져진 흙, 원님 오두막 하나, 그리고 중요한 사람들에게서 아주 먼 곳.

blocks.label: Gomamiji
blocks.ko: 고마미지

blocks.html: Gomamiji is a posting, not a retirement. He sits on the threshold until the dust on the hem looks like the hem. His office sword hangs on the doorpost. Nobody from Sabi writes.
blocks.ko: 고마미지는 부임지다. 은퇴가 아니다. 그는 문지방에 앉아 있다. 옷자락의 먼지가 옷자락처럼 보일 때까지. 관직 칼은 문설주에 걸려 있다. 사비에서는 아무도 편지하지 않는다.

blocks.label: The Banquet Hall
blocks.ko: 연회장

blocks.html: He stops holding court. The wine comes earlier each day, and then it stops being tied to the day at all.
blocks.ko: 그는 조회를 열지 않는다. 술은 날마다 조금씩 더 이른 시각에 올라오다가, 이윽고 시각과 상관없어진다.

blocks.html: Hundreds, by now. Nobody keeps the roll. They no longer have separate duties — only who pours, who steadies his wrist, who is still there when the wine runs out, and who is bold enough to speak while his mouth is busy elsewhere.
blocks.ko: 이제는 수백이다. 명부를 적는 사람이 없다. 소임은 없다 — 누가 따르는지, 누가 손목을 붙드는지, 술이 떨어지면 누가 남아 있는지, 그리고 폐하의 입이 다른 데에 있는 동안에도 감히 말하는 자가 누구인지뿐.

blocks.html: The hems keep time better than the roll. A pour, a step, a kneel — the long court silk opens, and he watches that before he watches the wine.
blocks.ko: 명부보다 자락이 시각을 지킨다. 따르고, 오르고, 무릎을 굽히면 — 긴 조정 비단이 열리고, 그는 술보다 그것을 먼저 본다.

blocks.html: The feast is no longer a feast. The stories say three thousand. The room is not that. It is still too many, a harem so packed the lamp never finds a wall. Robes open early. The maids show him their bodies the way other courts show tribute, and he studies them the way he once studied a map.
blocks.ko: 연회는 더 이상 연회가 아니다. 이야기로는 삼천이라 한다. 방이 그만큼은 아니다. 그래도 너무 많다. 등불이 벽에 닿지 못할 만큼 빽빽한 후궁이다. 옷고름은 일찍 풀린다. 궁녀들은 다른 조정이 조공을 바치듯 그에게 몸을 내보이고, 그는 예전에 지도를 들여다보던 눈으로 그것을 들여다본다.

blocks.html: He is half-undressed by the second jar and does not bother to hide what the wine has done to him. They climb into his lap two at a time. They hike the silk and laugh when he looks. They toast until the lamps blur. On rainy nights the party spills out onto the night veranda, and he follows a hip down the night corridor as if it were the last order anyone will ever give him.
blocks.ko: 두 번째 단지쯤이면 그는 반쯤 벗었고, 술이 제 몸에 한 일을 굳이 감추지도 않는다. 궁녀들은 둘씩 그의 무릎에 오른다. 비단 자락을 걷어 올리고, 그가 보면 웃는다. 등불이 번질 때까지 잔을 든다. 비 오는 밤이면 잔치는 밤 툇마루로 넘쳐 나가고, 그는 누군가의 허리를 따라 밤 복도를 걷는다. 그것이 세상에 남은 마지막 명령이라도 되는 듯이.

blocks.html: Here is what the lamps do not show. The headband is gone, and nobody tells him to put it back on. The prince who could read a room in one glance cannot read past the next fold of silk. Every one of them flatters him. He knows it, and he likes knowing it. It is the only sum left in Sabi that always comes out in his favour.
blocks.ko: 등불이 보여 주지 않는 것이 있다. 머리띠는 사라졌고, 다시 매라고 말하는 사람은 없다. 한 번 훑어보면 방 하나를 다 읽던 왕자가, 이제는 다음 비단 주름 너머를 읽지 못한다. 모두가 그에게 아첨한다. 그도 안다. 알아서 좋다. 사비에 남은 셈 가운데 언제나 그에게 유리하게 떨어지는 셈은 그것 하나뿐이다.

lines: 폐하. 어제 하신 말씀을 오늘 또 하셨습니다.
en: Your Majesty. You said that yesterday, and again today.
…With the same breath on us.
The same teeth… at our collarbones.
Was it good?
Or… was it a good night.

lines: 폐하가 멈추라고 하셔도… 허리가 먼저 대답해요.
en: …It was, yesterday.
The body still remembers.
Even if Your Majesty says stop… the hips answer first.

lines: 폐하. 젊으실 때 얘기 좀 해 주십시오.
en: Your Majesty. Tell us about when you were young.
Before you… undo anything.
No —
While you undo it.
One word per knot.
…What is it you want to know.

lines: 삼신께서 폐하 몫 장부를 따로 두시나 봐요. 부엌에선 그게 어찌 가능한가 내기까지 붙었어요.
en: They say you have more than fifty sons.
Samsin must keep a whole ledger just for Your Majesty. The kitchens have a wager going on how.
Nightly.
…That was the thirtieth Eraha. My father.

lines: 아, 그럼 폐하는 아직 여유가 있으시네요.
en: Ah. Then Your Majesty still has room to work with.
We can testify to it.
We knew already, in fairness.
Asking was only manners.

blocks.html: He laughs for the first time in four months. It is the last recorded instance.
blocks.ko: 넉 달 만에 처음으로 그가 웃는다. 기록에 남은 마지막 웃음이다.

blocks.html: Somewhere in the third year he stops going out to the hall, and some time after that they stop sending for him. The distance between those two things is the rest of the reign.
blocks.ko: 삼 년째 어느 무렵 그는 대전에 나가지 않게 되고, 그 얼마 뒤에는 부르러 오지도 않게 된다. 그 둘 사이의 거리가 남은 치세의 전부다.

blocks.html: Every season Chunbok asks the same question, in front of witnesses, the way a careful man pays a small tax. It buys him a name for loyalty. He already knows the answer.
blocks.ko: 철마다 춘복은 사람들 앞에서 같은 질문을 한다. 조심성 많은 사람이 작은 세금을 내듯이. 그걸로 충신이라는 이름을 산다. 답은 이미 알고 있다.

en: Your Majesty…

lines: 계백 장군을 데려오는 게 최선 아니겠습니까?
en: Would it not be best to bring back General Gyebek?

blocks.html: The letter is still in the king’s sleeve. It has gone soft at the folds.
blocks.ko: 편지는 아직 왕의 소매 속에 있다. 접힌 자리가 보드라워졌다.

en: That… who?
You there! Bring more wine!
Ahh~~ over here, Your Majesty~~
Your Majesty. The ministers are waiting outside.
…Let them wait.
Until when?

blocks.html: He does not answer. After a while the question stops being asked, and after a while longer the ministers stop coming to the door. He notices none of it, and it is the first thing in his life he has not arranged on purpose.
blocks.ko: 그는 대답하지 않는다. 얼마 뒤 그 물음이 사라지고, 다시 얼마 뒤 재상들이 문 앞에 오지 않게 된다. 그는 그중 아무것도 알아채지 못한다. 평생 처음으로, 그가 일부러 꾸미지 않은 일이다.

blocks.html: Sungchung comes while the wine is still being poured. He does not wait for a gap. He is the councillor who used to read the tides for the king, and he still wears his office sword as if there were an office.
blocks.ko: 성충은 술이 아직 따라지는 중에 온다. 틈을 기다리지 않는다. 왕을 위해 물때를 읽던 좌평이다. 아직 관직이 있다는 듯 허리에 관직 칼을 차고 있다.

en: Your Majesty. Open court. Today.
We opened it.
With the cup.
There is a tide.
If you miss it—

blocks.html: He does not finish. The king is already on his feet.
blocks.ko: 끝내지 못한다. 왕은 이미 일어서 있다.

lines: 조회를 열라고? 하루 종일 떠들 수 있는 방을 하나 내줘라.
en: Take his belt.
He wants open court? Give him a room where he can talk all day.

blocks.html: The belt comes off in the aisle, and his rank goes with it. The guards walk him to a cell. After that, nobody else tries to speak.
blocks.ko: 허리띠가 복도에서 벗겨지고, 품계도 함께 벗겨진다. 군졸들이 그를 옥으로 끌고 간다. 그 뒤로는 아무도 입을 열려 하지 않는다.

blocks.label: The Cell
blocks.ko: 옥

blocks.html: Sungchung starves in a cell within earshot of the feast. His office sword hangs on the post outside. With the last of his ink he writes the king one page.
blocks.ko: 성충은 연회 소리가 들리는 옥에서 굶어 간다. 관직 칼은 바깥 기둥에 걸려 있다. 마지막 남은 먹으로, 왕에게 종이 한 장을 쓴다.

blocks.html: In the cell where he starved, Kangrim reads his name three times — Sungchung. Sungchung. Sungchung. — loud enough for the feast next door to hear, or not hear.
blocks.ko: 굶어 죽어 가던 칸 안에서, 강림은 그의 이름을 세 번 부른다 — 성충. 성충. 성충. — 옆 연회가 들을지, 못 들을지 모를 만큼 크게.

en: Councillor Sungchung.
You chose the cell over silence. Was that loyalty to the king — or loyalty to being right?
lines: 침묵 대신 옥을 고르셨군요. 임금에 대한 충성이었습니까 — 아니면 옳음에 대한 충성이었습니까?

en: …Being right is the only loyalty left when a king stops listening.
The paper is for him. Not for you.
lines: 종이는 그이를 위한 것이오. 공이 아니오.

en: I will keep the minutes. Walk.

blocks.hanja: 忠臣死不忘君，願一言而死。臣常觀時察變，必有兵革之事。凡用兵，必審擇其地，處上流以延敵，然後可以保全。若異國兵來，陸路不使過沈峴，水軍不使入伎伐浦之岸，擧其險隘以禦之，然後可也。
blocks.ko: 충신은 죽어도 임금을 잊지 않으니, 한마디 아뢰고 죽고자 합니다. 신이 늘 때를 보고 변화를 살폈는데, 반드시 전쟁이 있을 것입니다. 무릇 군사를 쓸 때는 반드시 그 땅을 잘 가려야 하니, 상류에 자리 잡고 적을 끌어들여야 보전할 수 있습니다. 만일 다른 나라 군사가 오거든, 육로로는 침현을 넘지 못하게 하고 수군은 기벌포 기슭에 들어오지 못하게 하여, 험하고 좁은 곳에 의지해 막아야 합니다.
blocks.html: A loyal servant does not forget his king even in death, so let me say one thing and die. I have always watched the times and studied their changes, and there will surely be war. Whoever uses soldiers must choose his ground with care: take the upper stream and draw the enemy to you, and you can keep the country whole. If foreign soldiers come, do not let them cross Chimhyeon by land, and do not let their ships into the banks of Final Ford. Hold the narrow, difficult places, and stop them there.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 28, Baekje Annals — King Uija, yr. 16, dying memorial of Seongchung; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 1, p. 384

blocks.html: The page reaches the banquet hall folded inside a guard’s glove. The king reads the first line. Then he sets it under a wine jar, and does not take it in.
blocks.ko: 그 종이는 군졸의 장갑 속에 접힌 채 연회장에 닿는다. 왕은 첫 줄을 읽는다. 그러고는 술 단지 밑에 깔아 두고, 마음에 들이지 않는다.

blocks.html: Foxes in the Assembly. Toads in the treetops. A river running red. Nine signs, and a king who swears he doesn’t believe in signs…!
blocks.ko: 정사암에 여우 떼. 나무 꼭대기에 두꺼비. 핏빛으로 흐르는 강. 징조가 아홉, 그리고 징조 따윈 믿지 않는다는 임금…!

logline.en: Every omen is real, in the sense that people saw it. That was always the only sense that mattered.
logline.ko: 징조는 모두 진짜다. 사람들이 보았다는 의미에서. 중요한 건 언제나 그 의미뿐이었다.

images.alt: A blood-marked hand — first of the nine omens over Sabi
images.prompt: Historical manhwa: bloody omen hand / Nine Plagues. Match Euija era. Refs: Euija. No text, --ar 3:2

images.alt: Lightning breaks over Sabi palace as the people cry that Baekje falls
images.prompt: Historical manhwa: lightning over Sabi palace — Baekje falls omen. Refs: Euija, Sabi. No text, --ar 3:2

images.alt: In a torchlit pit in the Sabi palace yard, diggers lift out a living turtle with faint carved marks on its shell where a ghost sank into the earth.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Ninth of the nine omens, 659. TOP-DOWN BIRD'S-EYE into a freshly dug square pit in the inner yard of Sabi palace at night (attached pl_sabi_palace board: stone paving and giwa eaves at the frame edges). ONE DEVICE: the square black pit as a hard frame-within-the-frame in the centre. At its bottom, two Baekje palace laborers in hemp hanbok with topknots, no brimmed hats, crouch with iron spades, recoiling, as one lifts a living turtle out of the dark soil; on its shell faint carved marks, illegible, not readable text. A thin trail of pale grey mist sinks into the earth at the pit's edge where the ghost went down. A pine torch jammed into the spoil heap is the practical key raking across the shell and the men's faces. Foreground: the blurred edge of a minister's dark sleeve at the rim. Crushed blacks, long torch shadows on the pit walls, gold #facc15 as the specular on the wet shell, NOT a glow aura. No text. No watermark. CANON — PLACE Sabi (사비 (부여)) — attached board /pl_sabi_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Sabi palace on the Baengma river bluffs; Baekje giwa halls and pavilions. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Baekje: attached /ref_hanbok_baekje_gaya.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. blocks.html: Every one of the nine signs is real, in the sense that people saw it. That was always the only sense that mattered, and the man who taught Baekje so is about to find out how much he meant it.
blocks.ko: 아홉 가지 징조는 모두 진짜다. 사람들이 보았다는 의미에서. 중요한 건 언제나 그 의미뿐이었고, 백제에 그것을 가르친 사람은 이제 자기가 그 말을 얼마나 진심으로 했는지 알게 될 참이다.

blocks.html: Foxes walk into the Assembly hall in a pack, and a white one sits down on the Premier’s desk. A hen mates with a sparrow. A dead fish as long as a boat washes up on the river. Then a dead woman, longer than the fish.
blocks.ko: 여우 떼가 회의장에 들어오고, 흰 여우 한 마리가 상좌평의 책상에 올라앉는다. 암탉이 참새와 교미한다. 배만 한 죽은 물고기가 강가에 떠오른다. 그다음엔 죽은 여인이, 물고기보다 더 길게.

blocks.html: The palace trees weep at night. The White River turns red with blood. Toads gather in the tops of the trees by the ten thousand. Storm winds, rain, lightning, and black clouds fighting like dragons over the temples. Last, a ghost runs into the palace shouting, and burrows into the ground. They dig, and find a turtle.
blocks.ko: 밤이면 궁궐의 나무가 운다. 백강이 피처럼 붉게 물든다. 두꺼비 수만 마리가 나무 꼭대기에 모인다. 폭풍과 비와 번개, 그리고 절 위에서 용처럼 싸우는 검은 구름. 마지막으로, 귀신 하나가 소리치며 궁으로 뛰어들어 땅속으로 파고든다. 파 보니 거북 한 마리가 나온다.

blocks.html: They bring the turtle to the king in a lacquer box. He turns it over in his hands like a forgery he is pricing.
blocks.ko: 사람들이 거북을 옻칠한 상자에 담아 왕에게 가져온다. 그는 값을 매기는 위조품처럼 그것을 손안에서 뒤집어 본다.

lines: 내 궁 밑, 석 자 아래라.
en: Three feet down, under my own palace.
Who buried you, little one?
…Hm. Somebody with good taste in shells.

blocks.title: A room in Surabol, some months earlier

lines: 의자는 스무 해 동안 백성한테 기적을 팔았소. / 용이니 흰 사슴이니 하는 것들.
en: For twenty years Euija has been selling his people miracles. / Dragons. White deer.
Knowing they were false?

lines: 만든 사람이 본인인데. / 그러니 이제 그자는 세상에서 징조를 제일 못 읽는 사람이오. / 한평생 징조가 사람 손으로 만들어진다는 걸 알면서 살았으니까.
en: He made them himself. / Which makes him the worst reader of signs alive. / He has spent his whole life knowing that signs are made by hands.
…Then why would it work on him?

lines: 그자한테 통할 필요가 없소. / 그자의 백성한테만 통하면 되지.
en: It doesn’t have to work on him. / It only has to work on his people.

blocks.html: He does not order any of it, exactly. He asks for men who can travel, he asks what the markets of Sabi are frightened of, and he asks how deep one has to bury a turtle shell for the finding of it to look like an accident.
blocks.ko: 그는 딱히 무엇을 명하지는 않는다. 다닐 만한 사람을 구하고, 사비의 저잣거리가 무엇을 무서워하는지 묻고, 거북 등껍질을 얼마나 깊이 묻어야 찾아낸 것이 우연처럼 보이는지를 묻는다.

lines: 나라를 무너뜨리는 데 군대는 마지막에나 필요하오. / 먼저 필요한 건 소문이고. / 소문은 백성이 이미 두려워하는 것으로 만들면 되지.
en: An army is the last thing you need to bring down a country. / First you need a rumour. / And you build a rumour out of what the people are already afraid of.
Baekje falls! Baekje falls!

blocks.label: The Shaman
blocks.ko: 무당

blocks.html: He keeps a shaman on retainer the way other kings keep song-girls. He likes watching someone else believe the sky talks; he has told Gyebek the gods are cheap civil servants, and told Gesomun the same with wine on his breath. The shaman thinks he is frightened. He lets her.
blocks.ko: 그는 다른 임금들이 가창꾼을 두듯 무당을 둔다. 하늘이 말한다고 믿는 사람을 보는 재미가 있다. 계백에게는 신을 값싼 관리라 했고, 개소문에게도 술 취해 같은 말을 했다. 무당은 그가 겁먹었다고 생각한다. 그는 그냥 둔다.

en: I came for amusement today.
There are nine. / Read them.

lines: 큰 여인의 주검 — 백성이 그 탓에 신음합니다.
en: The foxes — the politicians are corrupt.
The hen and the sparrow — public morals have declined.
The great fish — the economy is in decline.
The great woman’s corpse — the people suffer for it.

lines: 나무 위의 두꺼비 — 거짓 장사치들만 목청이 큽니다.
용의 구름 — 나라가 저희끼리 싸우기 시작합니다.
en: The ghost-screams — the forgotten common man cries out.
The blood-red river — the public sphere is polluted.
The toads in the trees — only lying peddlers have loud voices.
The dragon-clouds — the nation begins fighting itself.
…The turtle. / From the shell.

blocks.hanja: 得一龜 背有文曰 百濟同月輪 新羅如月新
blocks.ko: 거북 하나를 얻으니, 등에 글이 있어 이르되, 백제는 보름달과 같고, 신라는 초승달과 같다.
blocks.html: They obtained a tortoise; on its back was writing that said: Baekje is like the full moon; Silla is like the new moon.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 28, Baekje Annals — King Uija, yr. 20 (660); Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 1, p. 386

lines: 보름달 같다는 것은 가득 찬 것이니, 가득 차면 기울며 —
초승달 같다는 것은 가득 차지 못한 것이니, 가득 차지 못하면 점점 차게 됩니다.
en: To be like a full moon is to be full — and what is full must wane —
to be like a crescent is to be not yet full — and what is not yet full grows fuller.
Baekje wanes. Silla fills.
You wretch!!!

blocks.html: The blade is out before the last word cools. He cuts her down where she sits. The turtle’s sentence stays in the room.
blocks.ko: 마지막 말이 식기 전에 칼이 나온다. 그는 그가 앉은 자리에서 벤다. 거북의 말은 방에 남는다.

blocks.html: People start saying it out loud in the markets, which is how you know it is already over.
blocks.ko: 저잣거리에서 사람들이 그 말을 소리 내어 하기 시작한다. 그쯤 되면 이미 끝난 것이다.

lines: 폐하. 지금 필요하신 건 술이 아닙니다.
en: Your Majesty. What you need right now is not wine.
Your Majesty…
Say one name.
I will go and bring him.
…That name was one I made up.
When I was a prince on a mudbank.
…Your Majesty.
What are they saying in the markets these days.
…That Baekje is the full moon.
…Yes.
Well made.

blocks.html: He never says that the signs were made. He could name the price of every piece of it. To say a man made this one is to say it about the dragon over the Sabi, and the white deer, and the twenty years in between.
blocks.ko: 그는 그 징조들이 만들어졌다는 말을 하지 않는다. 한 조각 한 조각의 값까지 댈 수 있으면서도. 이것은 사람이 만든 것이다라고 말하는 순간, 사비강의 용에 대해서도, 흰 사슴에 대해서도, 그 사이 스무 해에 대해서도 그렇게 말하는 것이 되기 때문이다.

blocks.html: The best lie a man ever tells is the one he cannot afford to expose.
blocks.ko: 사람이 하는 가장 훌륭한 거짓말은, 스스로 들출 수 없게 된 거짓말이다.

blocks.label: The White River
blocks.ko: 백마강

blocks.html: That night he leaves the palace the way he left it as a boy — without asking, without banners. The White River is waiting where it always waited. The omen said it ran red. Under the moon it is only black water and the smell of wet stone.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 그는 소년 때처럼 궁을 나선다 — 묻지 않고, 깃발 없이. 백강은 늘 기다리던 자리에 있다. 징조는 붉다 했고, 달 아래에서는 검은 물과 젖은 돌 냄새뿐이다.

blocks.html: He has spent years drowning on dry land: wine, women, and a letter he never sent to the man he never sent for. The river does not care. It knew him before the crown.
blocks.ko: 그는 여러 해를 마른 땅에서 익사하며 보냈다. 술, 여자, 그리고 끝내 부르지 않은 사람에게 끝내 보내지 않은 편지. 강은 상관하지 않는다. 강은 왕관 이전의 그를 알았다.

en: I named you here.
I will not die drunk on the bank of my own invention.
lines: 내 발명품 강둑에서 취해 죽지는 않겠다.

blocks.html: He jumps. The cold takes the wine off him. When he surfaces he is coughing, furious, awake — the promising prince the eight clans once feared, scraped clean by the same river that taught him friendship.
blocks.ko: 뛰어든다. 추위가 술을 벗겨 낸다. 물 밖으로 나올 때 그는 기침하고, 분노하고, 깨어 있다 — 대성팔족이 한때 두려워하던 촉망받는 왕자, 우정을 가르친 바로 그 강에 긁혀 깨끗해진.

en: Summon Gyebek…!

blocks.html: Chunbok has followed him down with a lamp, the way a careful man follows a king who might be about to do something historic. He holds out a dry robe. The king does not take it.
blocks.ko: 춘복이 등불을 들고 뒤따라 내려와 있다. 역사에 남을 짓을 할지도 모르는 임금을 조심성 많은 사람이 따라다니듯이. 그가 마른 옷을 내민다. 왕은 받지 않는다.

lines: 폐하께서도 잘 아시다시피, 탐라까지 배는 시간이 걸립니다.
그리고 저잣거리에서는… 송구합니다. 저잣거리에서는 그가 돌아올 백제가 남아 있겠느냐고들 합니다.
en: Majesty, you’ll catch your death—
As Your Majesty well knows, a boat to Tamla takes time.
And the markets… forgive me. The markets are asking whether there will be a Baekje for him to come home to.

lines: 우린 처음부터 작은아들네 집이었다, 춘복. 고구려가 대청을 가졌고, 우리는 남쪽 길을 가졌지.
빌린 길 위에서 칠백 년이다. 그래도 아직 여기 있다.
en: Let them ask.
We were a younger son’s house from the very start, Chunbok. Goguryeo got the hall. We got the road south.
Seven hundred years on a borrowed road, and we’re still here.
…For now, Majesty.

lines: 맨 처음 그분한테도 딱 그렇게들 말했지.
en: ‘For now.’ Ha.
That’s exactly what they told the first one, too.

blocks.html: Will Baekje survive? To answer that, go back to how it began: a mother, two sons, and a father who already had one…!
blocks.ko: 백제는 살아남을까? 그 답을 알려면 처음으로 돌아가야 한다. 어머니 하나, 아들 둘, 그리고 이미 아들이 있던 아버지…!

logline.en: Nobody in their father’s hall ever mentions Buyeo. Then a boy with a sling turns up.
logline.ko: 아버지의 궁에서는 누구도 부여 이야기를 꺼내지 않는다. 그러다 새총을 든 소년 하나가 나타난다.

images.prompt: 16:9 over-the-shoulder still from behind Biryu's drawn bow: sharp foreground of his shoulder, the bent bow and taut string, an arrow nocked. Midground on a narrow mountain ridge path, the pale white-gold stag Sinrok stands broadside, calm, looking straight back, antlers branching against a pale break in the clouds. Onjo's hand enters from the right, pressing down on Biryu's bow arm, his face urgent. Far peaks in blue wash bokeh. Low contre-jour sun catching the antlers as the key. CANON — BIRYU — FACE and garments from attached /ch_biryu.png (face only; invent a new pose). Demeanor: Elder brother, sea-hungry and proud; wants the coast at Michuhol and will not listen. #d8b276 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | ONJO — FACE and garments from attached /ch_onjo.png (face only; invent a new pose). Demeanor: Younger brother, steadier; listens to the ten ministers and stays inland at Wirye. The Sinrok deer stays with him. #f0c04a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | SINROK (신록, guardian deer of Baekje, guide of onjo and biryu) — attached board /obj_sinrok.png: Pale white-gold stag with tall branching antlers — match the board's animal, but ignore its glow outline: light catches the antlers and coat as real light. Owned by no one; leads the brothers south and stays with Onjo. HEEWON STYLE: a hand-painted ANIME film frame composed like a Romanticist master painting. FIGURES are anime: clean ink linework, simplified anime faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is watercolor and oil: skies, dust, ground and light are visibly hand-painted — wet-in-wet blooms, pigment granulation, soft bleeding edges, dry-brush dust, rich oil glazes in the darks, faint paper grain; edges of the frame dissolve into wash. LAYOUT is Romanticism (Delacroix, Géricault, Friedrich, Goya, Turner): heroic diagonal or pyramid composition, small figures against a sublime storm sky or vast field, extreme foreshortening (worm’s-eye from the dirt or straight down from above), one break in the clouds or one shaft as the key. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength (Caravaggio, Rembrandt, night-interior cinema): an extreme value range — inky blacks right beside small near-white highlights, almost no middle grey; 70–80% of the frame in deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo and black); ONE hard directional key (a lamp, a single cloud-break, a low sun shaft, firelight) carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock: anamorphic movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain. A CAMERA in a real Korean place — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D archviz, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portrait — NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: dutch, crane, worm’s-eye, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key + long shadows — not even daylight wash. ICONIC MINIMAL: ONE architectural device a lens can see; empty negative space; tiny figures or lower-third; the world stays in the shot. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor portrait garments gold. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Not a katana, not a tsuba, not a short jian, not a ball pommel. Real Korean architecture: grey giwa, timber, packed earth. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: movie frame in a real place, not a graphic poster; iconic one-device layout, empty frame, lower-third; high contrast chiaroscuro, not even wash; 2D animated cel-painterly, no photoreal; cinematography: dutch, wide, bokeh, mise-en-scène. Never: halo / bloom / glow aura / emissive skin around figures; graphic split-screen or black-triangle overlay; photoreal live-action or 3D archviz; busy extras crowding an iconic frame; copy-pasted reference as a fashion plate; flat even-daylight postcard wide; katana / tsuba / random sabre length instead of sw_bidam 환두대도.

blocks.html: Every child in Baekje can tell you this story. Most of them get the beginning wrong.
blocks.ko: 백제 아이라면 누구나 이 이야기를 할 줄 안다. 대부분은 첫머리를 틀리게 한다.

blocks.html: Onjo and Biryu grow up princes in their father’s hall. Nobody there ever mentions Buyeo.
blocks.ko: 온조와 비류는 아버지의 궁에서 왕자로 자란다. 거기서는 아무도 부여 얘기를 꺼내지 않는다.

blocks.label: Buyeo
blocks.ko: 부여

blocks.html: In Buyeo, Lady Ye has raised Jumong’s first son alone.
blocks.ko: 부여에서는 예씨부인이 주몽의 첫아들을 홀로 키워 왔다.

blocks.html: Yuri is a boy with a sling and bad aim, or good aim and bad luck. The pebble cracks a woman’s water jar on her way back from the well.
blocks.ko: 유리는 새총을 든 아이다. 겨냥이 나쁜 건지, 겨냥은 좋은데 운이 나쁜 건지. 돌멩이가 우물에서 돌아오던 여자의 물동이를 깬다.

blocks.caption: Yuri. Bad aim or bad luck, and a mother who will not answer one question.
blocks.ko: 유리. 조준이 나쁘거나 운이 나쁘거나. 그리고 질문 하나에 대답하지 않는 어머니.

lines: 어느 집 자식이야, 대체? 애비 없이 자라서 버릇도 없지.
en: Whose son are you, anyway? No father, no manners.
blocks.speaker: Water-carrier

lines: 우리 아버지는 어떤 사람입니까? 지금 어디에 계십니까?
en: What kind of man was my father? Where is he now?

lines: 네 아버지는 보통 사람이 아니었다. 이 나라가 그를 담지 못했지.
일곱 모 난 돌 위 소나무 밑에 뭔가를 두고 갔다.
en: Your father was no ordinary man. The country couldn’t hold him.
He went south and made himself a king.
He left something under the pine on the seven-sided stone.
Find it, and he’ll know you.

blocks.html: There is no pine on any hill he climbs. He finds it at home: the house’s pine pillar stands on a seven-sided foundation stone, and in the crack beneath it lies half a sword.
blocks.ko: 오르는 산마다 소나무는 없다. 그는 집에서 찾는다. 집의 소나무 기둥이 일곱 모 주춧돌 위에 서 있고, 그 밑 틈에 부러진 칼 반쪽이 있다.

en: Yuri….!

blocks.html: With his friends, three boys as stubborn as he is, he walks his father’s road backwards, south.
blocks.ko: 그만큼 고집 센 친구 셋과 함께, 그는 아버지의 길을 거꾸로, 남쪽으로 걷는다.

blocks.label: The Half Sword
blocks.ko: 부러진 칼

blocks.html: In the hall at Jolbon he lays the half-sword on the boards. Jumong goes to a chest nobody has opened since the river, takes out the other half, and kneels. The two halves click.
blocks.ko: 졸본 대청에서 유리가 칼 반쪽을 마루에 놓는다. 주몽이 강을 건넌 뒤로 아무도 열지 않은 궤짝에서 나머지 반쪽을 꺼내 무릎을 꿇는다. 두 쪽이 딸깍 맞물린다.

en: Father…!

blocks.html: Onjo and Biryu watch from the porch rail. The rail already knows what the hall will decide.
blocks.ko: 온조와 비류가 누대 난간에서 본다. 대청이 무엇을 정할지, 난간은 이미 안다.

blocks.label: The Last Night
blocks.ko: 마지막 밤

blocks.html: When Yuri is named crown prince, Sosuno does not fight the hall. She packs her dusty-rose silk. She packs the boys. She leaves the well.
blocks.ko: 유리가 태자로 책봉되자, 소서노는 대청과 싸우지 않는다. 빛바랜 장밋빛 비단을 싼다. 아이들을 챙긴다. 우물은 두고 간다.

blocks.html: Jumong finds her at the old well, two buckets that have outlived the argument. Twenty winters in the same yard. He is still grinning. She is still pretending she came for water.
blocks.ko: 주몽이 옛 우물에서 그녀를 찾는다. 싸움보다 오래 버틴 두레박 둘. 같은 마당에서 스무 겨울. 그는 아직 웃고 있다. 그녀는 아직 물 뜨러 온 척한다.

en: Hey.
You’re packed.
That’s… a lot of buckets for one road.
Not buckets.
Grain. Boys. Me.

lines: 소나무 밑에 쇠붙이 하나 두고 왔을 뿐인데. 그게 자라서 걸어 들어올 줄은—
en: I left iron under a pine. I didn’t think it would grow up and walk in—
Don’t— don’t make a speech. I’ll hit you.
Wasn’t going to.
Well’s still here.
I kept it. For you. Stupid, I know.
lines: 남겨 뒀어. 너 때문에. 바보인 거 알아.

en: Don’t be nice.
I’ll get stupid.
Yuri can have the chair. I’m not sitting in a footnote.
You know that. You always knew.
lines: 의자는 유리가 가져. 난 각주로 안 앉아.

en: Yeah.
South, then.
Take the glow. Leave me the well.
…Come here. Please. One night. I’m still thirsty.
Big idiot.
The boys are asleep.
If you compliment me I will scream.
…That’s not a no.

blocks.html: They do not make it to a feast. They make it to the grain room that has been theirs since the first night, and she kisses him before the door is shut.
blocks.ko: 잔치까지는 못 간다. 첫날 밤부터 둘의 것이던 곡식방까지 가서, 문이 닫히기도 전에 그녀가 입을 맞춘다.

blocks.html: Older. Hungrier. The hide has been off for years and she is worse now, not better.
blocks.ko: 나이가 들었고, 더 고프다. 껍질은 몇 해 전에 벗었고, 지금은 나아지기는커녕 더 심하다.

en: Still you.
Still that mouth.
Look at you. Older. Better. Sorry. Not sorry.
lines: 봐라. 나이 먹고. 더 좋아졌어. 미안. 안 미안해.

en: Don’t— ha— don’t you dare be sweet now.
Twenty winters, and you still breathe like you ran here.
…Slower. No. Not slower.
I want to remember this one. I’m not getting another.
lines: 하지 마— 하— 지금 다정하게 굴기만 해 봐.
스무 해 겨울을 지나고도 꼭 뛰어온 사람처럼 숨을 쉬네.
이번 건 기억할 거야. 다음은 없으니까.

en: Then don’t count.
I’ll count.
You know I’m bad at it.
lines: 나 세는 거 못하는 거 알잖아.

en: I hate you. I hate you, don’t stop—
…Say it. The thing you never say.
Say it now, while I can’t hit you.
lines: …말해. 너 한 번도 안 한 그 말.
지금 해. 내가 못 때릴 때.

blocks.html: He says it into her hair. Even the sky looks away for this part. She laughs, and then she doesn’t, and the lamp burns down to a coal.
blocks.ko: 그는 그녀의 머리칼에 대고 말한다. 이 대목에서는 하늘도 고개를 돌린다. 그녀는 웃다가, 이내 웃지 않고, 등잔은 숯불이 될 때까지 타들어 간다.

en: There.
Now you have to come back someday and hit me for it.
lines: 이제 언젠가 돌아와서 그걸로 날 때려야 해.

blocks.html: Before dawn the lamp is out, and neither of them has slept.
blocks.ko: 새벽이 오기 전에 등잔은 꺼져 있고, 둘 다 한숨도 자지 않았다.

en: Don’t be nice.
I’ll get stupid.
…I’m already stupid.
Keep the well. I’m taking the glow.
Take it.
You’re beautiful.
Go found the other one. I’ll be here. Grinning. Like an idiot.
lines: 가서 다른 거 세워. 난 여기 있을게. 웃으면서. 바보처럼.

blocks.label: The Road South
blocks.ko: 남쪽 길

blocks.html: At dawn ten men start packing carts before anyone tells them to. Onjo and Biryu take their mother south. She walks like a woman who has been thoroughly answered and will not explain it to a deer, a son, or a chronicle.
blocks.ko: 새벽, 누가 시키기도 전에 열 명의 사내가 수레를 꾸린다. 온조와 비류가 어머니를 모시고 남쪽으로 간다. 그녀는 제대로 대답을 들은 여자처럼 걷고, 그 대답을 사슴에게도, 아들에게도, 연대기에게도 설명하지 않는다.

blocks.html: Three days south of the river, on a ridge path too narrow for the cart, a stag is standing in the way. Pale as mulberry paper, gold wherever the light touches it, antlers branching like a winter tree somebody decided to keep. It does not run. It looks at the three of them as if it had been told to expect three.
blocks.ko: 강을 건너 사흘 남쪽, 수레가 지나기엔 너무 좁은 능선 길에 수사슴 한 마리가 길을 막고 서 있다. 닥종이처럼 희고, 빛이 닿는 곳마다 금빛이며, 뿔은 누군가 남겨 두기로 한 겨울나무처럼 갈라져 있다. 달아나지 않는다. 셋을 기다리라는 말을 들은 듯 세 사람을 바라본다.

lines: 열 신하 저녁거리다. 저 뿔만 해도 한 달은—
en: Don’t move.
That’s dinner for ten ministers. The antlers alone, a month of—
Hyung. Hyung, wait.
…That look like dinner to you? Really?
Looks like antlers to me. Meat with antlers.
Biryu. Lower it.
…Listen to your mother. Bow down.

blocks.html: Biryu lowers the bow the way an elder son does, slowly enough that everyone understands it was his own idea. The stag turns, walks ten paces up the ridge, and stops to look back. When they do not follow, it waits. When they do, it walks on. It keeps that up for nine days.
blocks.ko: 비류는 맏아들답게 활을 내린다. 제 생각이었다는 걸 모두가 알아볼 만큼 천천히. 사슴은 돌아서서 능선을 열 걸음 오르더니 멈춰 서서 돌아본다. 따라가지 않으면 기다린다. 따라가면 다시 걷는다. 그렇게 아흐레를 간다.

en: It wants us to follow, right?
…A deer knows the way, Mother?

lines: 너희 아버지는 거북이 등 밟고 강 건넜어.
en: Your father crossed a river on turtles’ backs.
A deer’s practically civilised.

blocks.label: Mount Buak
blocks.ko: 부아악

blocks.html: On the ninth day it takes them up Mount Buak, and from the top the brothers see all of it: a river looped across the plain like a belt somebody has unbuckled, high peaks at their backs, wet green flats to the south and, somewhere past the haze, the sea. Biryu smells the salt before he sees it.
blocks.ko: 아흐레째 사슴은 그들을 부아악 위로 데려가고, 꼭대기에서 형제는 그 모두를 본다. 누가 풀어 놓은 허리띠처럼 들판을 감아 도는 강, 등 뒤의 높은 봉우리들, 남쪽의 젖은 푸른 벌, 그리고 안개 너머 어딘가의 바다. 비류는 바다를 보기도 전에 소금 냄새부터 맡는다.

lines: 바다 냄새 나지. 나 저기로 간다.
강 끼고 산 등지고, 다 좋아. 근데 배를 못 띄우잖아.
en: Smell that? Sea. I’m going there.
River in front, mountains behind, sure, lovely. You can’t float a ship on it.

lines: ……열 사람이 다 틀릴 수도 있긴 한데, 열 사람이 다—
en: Hyung, all ten of them say here.
…I mean, ten people can all be wrong, but all ten—

lines: 그럼 열 사람은 여기 살라 그래.
en: Then the ten can live here.
And Mother? Who’s Mother coming with?
…Don’t ask me that.

blocks.html: Nobody answers him. The stag, which has stood a little apart all morning, crosses the summit and lies down in the grass at Onjo’s feet, facing the river. Biryu laughs too loudly and says the deer has no taste, and takes his half of the people down to Michuhol and the salt flats. The stag stays. Baekje will call it Sinrok, the guardian deer, for as long as Baekje has anything to call.
blocks.ko: 아무도 대답하지 않는다. 아침 내내 조금 떨어져 서 있던 사슴이 꼭대기를 가로질러 와서, 강을 바라보며 온조의 발치 풀밭에 엎드린다. 비류는 너무 크게 웃으며 사슴이 보는 눈이 없다고 하고, 제 몫의 백성을 이끌고 미추홀의 소금벌로 내려간다. 사슴은 남는다. 백제는 그것을 신록, 나라를 지키는 사슴이라 부를 것이다. 백제가 무언가를 부를 수 있는 동안은.

blocks.html: Salt flats and sea wind. Biryu calls it a view.
blocks.ko: 갯벌과 바닷바람. 비류는 그걸 경치라 부른다.

lines: 열 부족의 땅이라… 십제라! 이봐, 더 크게 가자고. 백 부족의 땅… 백제! 그래, 그게 낫지….
en: The land of ten tribes… Sipje! Hey, c’mon… we can think bigger than that. The land of a HUNDRED tribes… Baekje! Now that’s more like it….
“Baekje” — how does that sound?

blocks.html: Biryu takes the sea. Onjo takes the river. Up north, their half-brother Yuri keeps the chair, and his line keeps it after him.
blocks.ko: 비류는 바다를 갖는다. 온조는 강을 갖는다. 북쪽에서는 이복형 유리가 자리를 지키고, 그 뒤로도 그의 핏줄이 지킨다.

blocks.html: So that is the family joke Euija and Gesomun used to throw at each other over wine. Goguryeo and Baekje are one father’s sons. One got the hall. One got the road. Neither has forgiven the other since.
blocks.ko: 의자와 개소문이 술자리에서 서로에게 던지던 집안 농담이 바로 이것이다. 고구려와 백제는 한 아버지의 아들들이다. 하나는 대청을 가졌고, 하나는 길을 가졌다. 그 뒤로 어느 쪽도 상대를 용서하지 않았다.

blocks.html: Seven hundred years later, the road ends at a riverbank in Sabi. Onjo’s heir is wringing the White River out of his sleeves. He once said a country is a territory governed by a single story. This was the story. He is about to learn who else can tell it.
blocks.ko: 칠백 년 뒤, 그 길은 사비의 강둑에서 끝난다. 온조의 후손이 소매에서 백강 물을 짜내고 있다. 그는 언젠가 나라란 하나의 이야기가 다스리는 땅이라고 말했다. 이것이 그 이야기였다. 이제 그는 그 이야기를 누가 또 할 줄 아는지 알게 될 참이다.

blocks.html: Back to Sabi. Two armies are on the road, the boat for Gyebek still hasn’t sailed, and the king wants to know why…!
blocks.ko: 다시 사비. 두 군대가 이미 길 위에 있고, 계백을 데리러 갈 배는 아직 떠나지 않았다. 왕은 그 까닭을 알고 싶다…!

logline.en: Two armies are coming for the capital, one by sea and one over the hills. The markets already have a name for it.
logline.ko: 두 군대가 도성으로 오고 있다. 하나는 바다로, 하나는 산을 넘어. 저잣거리는 벌써 이름을 붙였다.

images.alt: Seongchung, Heungsu, and Gyebek — the three loyalists of Baekje
images.at: Who is the Eraha of this country?!
images.prompt: Historical manhwa: Seongchung, Heungsu, Gyebek — three loyalists. No text, --ar 3:2

blocks.html: The war reaches Sabi the way bad news always does: through the fish market first.
blocks.ko: 전쟁은 나쁜 소식이 늘 그렇듯 사비에 닿는다. 어시장부터.

blocks.html: Two armies are coming for the capital, one by sea and one over the hills. The fishwives already have a name for it: the Chunchu Army. The king hears it from a maid, who heard it from a fishwife.
blocks.ko: 두 군대가 도성으로 오고 있다. 하나는 바다로, 하나는 산을 넘어. 생선 장수 아낙들은 벌써 이름을 붙였다. 춘추군. 왕은 그 말을 궁녀에게서 듣고, 궁녀는 생선 장수에게서 들었다.

blocks.label: The Hall
blocks.ko: 전각

blocks.html: Euija holds court for the first time in three years. Half the benches are his sons. They watch him the way sons watch a father who has come home sober: politely, and counting the exits.
blocks.ko: 의자가 세 해 만에 처음으로 조회를 연다. 자리 절반이 그의 아들들이다. 아들들은 술 깨고 돌아온 아버지를 보듯 그를 본다. 공손하게, 그리고 문이 몇 개인지 세면서.

lines: 과인이 강둑에서, 흠뻑 젖은 채로, 보는 눈들 앞에서 내린 명이다.
en: The boat for Gyebek.
I gave that order on a riverbank, soaking wet, in front of witnesses.
Where is he?

lines: 폐하… 폐하께서도 잘 아시다시피, 겨울 뱃길은—
en: Your Majesty… as Your Majesty well knows, the winter crossings are—
And then the spring winds were—

lines: 춘복. 과인을 바보로 아느냐, 술주정뱅이로 아느냐?
en: The winds. A whole year of winds.
Chunbok. Do you take me for a fool, or for a drunk?

lines: 폐하, 온조묘에 걸고 아뢰오니, 계백 장군에게 딸려 보낼 군사가 너무 적습니다!
사택가가 잃은 것은 자리이지 사병이 아닙니다. 사택 공의 군사를 기다리시는 것이…
en: Majesty, by Onjo’s shrine, we have too few troops to send General Gyebek!
The Satek house lost its benches, not its levies. Better to wait for Lord Satek’s men…
Who is the Eraha of this country?!
Buyeo Euija?
Or Minister Satek?
Send him NOW!

blocks.html: Chunbok bows very low, which is what he does instead of answering. A boat leaves for Tamla that afternoon. It is the fastest in the harbour. It is a year late.
blocks.ko: 춘복은 아주 깊이 절한다. 대답 대신 하는 일이다. 그날 오후 탐라로 배 한 척이 떠난다. 포구에서 가장 빠른 배다. 한 해 늦었다.

blocks.label: The Letter
blocks.ko: 편지

blocks.html: That night the king does something he has not done in three years. He goes looking for a piece of paper.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 왕은 세 해 동안 하지 않던 일을 한다. 종이 한 장을 찾으러 간다.

blocks.html: It is where he left it in the banquet hall, under a wine jar, with a red ring where the jar stood. The maids watch him lift the jar. Nobody giggles.
blocks.ko: 종이는 그가 둔 자리, 연회장의 술 단지 밑에 있다. 단지가 놓였던 자리에 붉은 테가 져 있다. 궁녀들이 그가 단지를 드는 것을 지켜본다. 아무도 킥킥대지 않는다.

lines: 폐하… 그건 그 좌평 나리 것이에요.
en: Majesty… that’s the councillor’s.
We didn’t throw it away.
We didn’t know if we were allowed to.
Read it to me.
My eyes are— just read it.

lines: ‘육로로는 침현을 넘지 못하게 하고, 수군은 기벌포에 들이지 마소서.’
en: ‘A loyal servant does not forget his king even in death—’
Majesty, then it’s a river and a pass.
‘Do not let them cross Chimhyeon by land. Do not let their ships into Final Ford.’
…Then just his name.

lines: 세 해 전에 고개와 강을 일러 주었다. 굶어 가면서. 저 벽 너머에서.
그런데 과인은 그 위에 술 단지를 올려놓았다.
en: Chimhyeon. The soldiers call it Tanhyeon.
He told me the pass and the river three years ago. Starving. Through that wall.
And I put a jar on him.
Majesty—

lines: 누가 또 이 말을 했어. 저 사람보다 먼저. 날 보고 웃으면서, 경을 읊으면서—
en: Somebody else said this. Before him. Smiling at me, quoting sutras—
…Heungsu.

blocks.label: The Back of the Hall
blocks.ko: 전각 뒤편

blocks.html: Next morning the provincial lords are summoned too, even the ones nobody has ever summoned.
blocks.ko: 이튿날 아침에는 지방의 성주들도 불려 온다. 한 번도 불린 적 없는 이들까지.

blocks.html: At the back of the hall, the lord of Bear Fortress says nothing. Ye Sikjin is doing the sum every provincial lord is doing. How many days from the river mouth to the capital? And how many from the capital to his own gate?
blocks.ko: 대전 뒤편에서 웅진성 성주는 한마디도 없다. 예식진은 방 안의 지방 성주들이 다 하는 셈을 하고 있다. 강어귀에서 도성까지 며칠인가. 그리고 도성에서 제 성문까지는 며칠인가.

lines: 예 공! 웅진성! 사 대 동안 한 번도 조정에 부르지 않았구나. 과인의 실수다.
en: Lord Ye! Bear Fortress! Four generations and I never once asked you to court. My mistake.
How many men can you give me?

lines: 웅진성은 꼭 필요한 만큼 하겠습니다, 폐하. 숫자는 길에 달렸습니다.
en: Your Majesty is generous to say so.
Bear Fortress will do exactly what is needed, Majesty. The number depends on the road.

lines: 숫자야 다 길에 달렸지. 하나만 대 봐라.
en: Every number depends on the road. Give me one.
…As many as the road allows, Majesty.

blocks.html: Euija laughs, because a king has to laugh at something before noon. Ye Sikjin bows exactly as low as the man beside him. That afternoon he rides home to Bear Fortress and opens a drawer.
blocks.ko: 의자는 웃는다. 임금은 낮이 되기 전에 뭐라도 웃어야 하니까. 예식진은 옆 사람과 꼭 같은 깊이로 절한다. 그날 오후 그는 웅진성으로 돌아가 서랍 하나를 연다.

blocks.html: One man might still know what to do. Euija sent him away too. Somebody ride. Now…!
blocks.ko: 어찌해야 할지 아는 사람이 하나 남았을지 모른다. 그도 의자가 내쫓았다. 누가 말을 달려라. 지금…!

logline.en: The king sends for the one man he sent away for being right.
logline.ko: 왕은 옳은 말을 했다는 죄로 내보낸 단 한 사람을 부른다.
