blocks.html: Heungsu has drawn the same map in the dirt every morning for three years. Today the king has finally sent someone to look at it.
blocks.ko: 흥수는 세 해 동안 아침마다 흙바닥에 같은 지도를 그렸다. 오늘에야 왕이 그것을 보러 사람을 보냈다.

blocks.html: The county is a day’s ride from the sea and a month from anyone who matters. Heungsu arrives with one chest and his office sword, hangs the sword on the doorpost, and on the first morning, before the clerk has finished his bow, scratches a map into the packed earth of the yard with the end of a broom handle.
blocks.ko: 고을은 바다에서 하루 길이고, 중요한 사람들에게서는 한 달 길이다. 흥수는 궤짝 하나와 관직 칼 하나를 들고 와서, 칼을 문설주에 걸고, 첫날 아침 향리가 절을 다 마치기도 전에 빗자루 끝으로 마당의 다져진 흙에 지도를 긋는다.

blocks.html: A coastline. One river mouth, the White River’s, drawn twice as wide as it is. One notch in the eastern hills for Tanhyeon. Sabi as a thumbprint. Every morning the chickens and the children walk it out of shape, and every morning he sweeps it flat and draws it again, the same lines in the same order, like a monk at his morning sutra.
blocks.ko: 해안선 하나. 강어귀 하나, 백강의 것을 실제보다 두 배 넓게. 동쪽 산줄기에 홈 하나, 탄현. 사비는 엄지 지문 하나. 아침마다 닭과 아이들이 밟아 모양을 흐트러뜨리고, 아침마다 그는 바닥을 쓸어 평평하게 한 뒤 같은 선을 같은 순서로 다시 긋는다. 아침 독경을 하는 중처럼.

en: Mister, is that a snake?
A river.
What river?
One I hope you never see.
lines: 네가 평생 안 봤으면 하는 강.

blocks.html: Nobody from Sabi writes. The news about Sungchung comes a season after the cell, on a salt boat, folded in between the price of salt and the price of rice, and the clerk reads it out because he reads everything out.
blocks.ko: 사비에서는 아무도 편지하지 않는다. 성충의 소식은 옥에서 한 철이 지나 소금배에 실려 온다. 소금값과 쌀값 사이에 접혀서. 향리는 무엇이든 소리 내어 읽는 사람이라 그것도 소리 내어 읽는다.

en: The councillor in Sabi. The one who— in the cell.
…Was he someone you knew, sir?
lines: 사비의 그 좌평 나리요. 옥에서 그—

en: …Better handwriting than mine.

blocks.html: That morning he does not draw the map. The next morning he does, and adds nothing to it, which the clerk takes as grief and the children take as permission to walk on Tanhyeon.
blocks.ko: 그날 아침 그는 지도를 긋지 않는다. 이튿날 아침에는 긋는다. 아무것도 보태지 않고. 향리는 그것을 슬픔으로 읽고, 아이들은 탄현을 밟아도 된다는 허락으로 읽는다.

blocks.html: In the last year the rumours come down the coast faster than the salt: foxes in the Ministers’ Assembly, a river gone red. Heungsu hears each one out and goes back to his broom.
blocks.ko: 마지막 해에는 소문이 소금보다 빨리 해안을 타고 내려온다. 대신 회의장에 여우 떼, 핏빛이 된 강. 흥수는 하나하나 끝까지 듣고는 다시 빗자루로 돌아간다.

blocks.label: The Courier
blocks.ko: 파발

blocks.html: The courier does not sit. Dust is still on him. The sword on the doorpost is the only bright thing in the yard.
blocks.ko: 파발은 앉지 않는다. 먼지를 그대로 뒤집어쓰고 있다. 문설주의 칼만이 마당에서 유일하게 반짝인다.

blocks.html: He has stopped in the middle of the yard, which is to say in the middle of the map.
blocks.ko: 그는 마당 한가운데 멈춰 서 있다. 말하자면 지도 한가운데.

en: His Majesty asks.
The matter is urgent. What then.
blocks.speaker: The Courier

en: …Sungchung already wrote it.
Same paper. I don’t have a second one.
…That is all?
His Majesty asked for a plan, sir. Not a—
lines: 폐하께서는 계책을 물으셨습니다. 그런 게 아니라—
blocks.speaker: The Courier

en: You’re standing on Tanhyeon.

blocks.html: The courier looks down and steps off a notch in the dirt, as if it might give way under him.
blocks.ko: 사자는 발밑을 내려다보고, 흙바닥의 홈에서 발을 뗀다. 꺼지기라도 할 것처럼.

en: And Gyebek?
Has anybody sent for Gyebek?

blocks.speaker: The Courier
lines: 이번 주에 배가 갔습니다, 나리. 탐라로.
en: A boat went for him this week, sir. To Tamla.
This week.
Five years, and this week.

blocks.html: He looks down at the river mouth he has drawn too wide, and remembers the last time he saw the man they have finally sent for.
blocks.ko: 그는 너무 넓게 그린 강어귀를 내려다보며, 그들이 이제야 부른 사람을 마지막으로 본 날을 떠올린다.

blocks.html: It was a berth on Satek water, the afternoon the clans put Gyebek on a boat. Heungsu still had his office then. He came down to the water because nobody else from court did.
blocks.ko: 사택의 물가 나루였다. 가문들이 계백을 배에 태우던 날 오후. 흥수는 그때만 해도 아직 관직이 있었다. 조정에서 아무도 나오지 않았기에 그가 물가로 나왔다.

blocks.caption: A Baekje minister sent far from court for saying what the king didn’t want to hear.
blocks.ko: 왕이 듣기 싫어하는 말을 해서 조정에서 멀리 보내진 백제의 대신.

blocks.html: Gyebek’s wife came too, with their boy at her side and a small girl on her hip. She had packed his bag. He had unpacked it on the dock and packed it again, in order.
blocks.ko: 계백의 아내도 나왔다. 사내아이를 곁에 세우고, 어린 딸을 허리에 안고. 짐은 아내가 쌌다. 그는 나루에서 짐을 풀어 순서대로 다시 쌌다.

en: You… you truly mean to go?
Without a word to the king—

lines: 폐하께서는 상중이십니다. 서명을 하실 수 없습니다.
명에는 폐하의 인장이 있습니다. 저는 백제의 충신입니다.
en: The king is in mourning. He cannot sign.
The order has his seal. I am a loyal servant of Baekje.
His Majesty gave me a name.
A name — to a child who had none.
If he wants it back, he will send for it.

blocks.speaker: Gyebek’s Son
en: Father. How many days is Tamla?
Four, with a good wind.

blocks.speaker: Gyebek’s Son
en: Then I’ll count to four.

lines: 다섯까지 세라. 바람이 늘 좋지는 않다.
en: Count to five. The wind is not always good.
…Do you know the story of the Guardian of Ansi?

lines: 아끼는 사람 하나, 섬기는 사람 하나.
en: I do.
One person to cherish. One person to serve.

lines: 저는 그 둘이 같은 사람이라 문제입니다.
en: My trouble is that for me they are the same person.

blocks.html: His wife was standing close enough to hear it. She shifted the girl to her other hip and looked at the water. Heungsu has never forgotten that she did not look surprised.
blocks.ko: 아내는 그 말이 들릴 만큼 가까이 서 있었다. 딸을 다른 쪽 허리로 옮겨 안고 물을 바라보았다. 흥수는 그녀가 놀라는 기색이 없었던 것을 지금껏 잊지 못한다.

en: Then hear one thing that is not a story.
If they ever send for you, hold the White River mouth and the Tanhyeon pass — or there will be no Sabi left to be loyal to.
The Tang do not need our clans’ permission to land. They need our absence.
lines: 그러면 이야기가 아닌 것 하나만 들으시게.
언젠가 자네를 부르거든, 백강 하구와 탄현을 지키게 — 그렇지 않으면 충성할 사비가 남지 않네.
당은 상륙에 우리 가문의 허가가 필요 없네. 우리의 빈자리가 필요할 뿐이지.

en: I know the roads.
Yellow Mountain first — if that door holds, the river still has a kingdom behind it.
If it does not… then the berths you all fought over will belong to whoever can spell our names.
lines: 황산이 먼저요 — 그 문이 버티면, 강 뒤에 아직 나라가 있소.
못 버티면… 당신들이 싸우던 선석은, 우리 이름을 받아 적을 줄 아는 자의 것이 되오.

blocks.html: Then the captain with the Yunbi contract called the tide. Gyebek stepped aboard and did not look back, because looking back was not on the list. The boy counted out loud until the sail was gone. He got to four hundred and something before his mother made him stop.
blocks.ko: 그때 윤비 가문 계약서를 품은 선장이 물때를 불렀다. 계백은 배에 올랐고 돌아보지 않았다. 돌아보는 일은 목록에 없었기 때문이다. 아이는 돛이 사라질 때까지 소리 내어 셌다. 사백 몇까지 갔을 때 어머니가 그만 세라고 했다.

en: Tell His Majesty—
…No. He has the paper.

blocks.label: Sabi
blocks.ko: 사비

blocks.html: The answer comes back to Sabi. The ministers do not like the source.
blocks.ko: 대답이 사비로 돌아온다. 대신들은 출처가 마음에 들지 않는다.

lines: 폐하, 흥수는 유배 중인 사람입니다. 임금을 원망하고 있습니다.
임금을 원망하는 자는 나라를 사랑하지 않습니다. 폐하께서도 잘 아시다시피, 그의 말은 쓸 수 없습니다.
en: Majesty, Heungsu is a man in exile. He resents his lord.
A man who resents his lord has no love of country. As Your Majesty well knows, his words must not be used.

blocks.speaker: A Minister
lines: 당군은 강을 거슬러 한 줄로 오게 하여 배를 벌리지 못하게 하고, 신라군은 탄현을 오르게 하여 말 두 필이 나란히 서지 못하게 하십시오.
그때 치면 됩니다. 삼태기 속의 닭이요, 그물 속의 고기입니다.
en: Let them in, Majesty.
Let the Tang come up the river single file, with no room to spread their boats. Let Silla climb Tanhyeon, a path too narrow for two horses abreast.
Then strike. Chickens in a basket. Fish in a net.

lines: …하. 좋구나. 과인이 예전에 생각해 내던 그런 수야.
en: Chickens in a basket.
…Ha. That’s good. That’s the kind of thing I used to think of.
Heungsu would say—

lines: 흥수는 성충이 한 말을 하는 것입니다, 폐하.
그리고 폐하께서는 성충의 말도 쓰지 않으셨습니다.
en: Heungsu says what Sungchung said, Majesty.
And Your Majesty did not take Sungchung’s advice either.

blocks.html: It is very quiet. To take the advice now, the king would have to admit what it cost the last man who gave it. Kings will pay almost anything not to admit that.
blocks.ko: 아주 조용하다. 이제 와서 그 말을 쓰려면, 왕은 앞서 그 말을 한 사람이 무엇을 치렀는지 인정해야 한다. 임금들은 그것만은 인정하지 않으려고 거의 무엇이든 치른다.

en: So it is.

blocks.html: The next courier is shorter. Tang keels are already in the mud of Final Ford. Yushin is already on the switchback. The White River and the Tanhyeon pass are already theirs.
blocks.ko: 다음 파발은 더 짧다. 당의 배가 이미 기벌포 진흙에 박혀 있다. 유신은 이미 고갯길을 오르고 있다. 백강도 탄현도 벌써 저들 손에 있다.

blocks.html: No second courier comes to Gomamiji. Heungsu sweeps the yard and draws the map for eleven more mornings, the river mouth still twice as wide as it is, because nobody has told him it is already full of Tang keels.
blocks.ko: 고마미지로는 두 번째 사자가 오지 않는다. 흥수는 열하루 아침을 더 마당을 쓸고 지도를 긋는다. 강어귀는 여전히 실제보다 두 배 넓다. 그 강어귀가 이미 당의 용골로 가득하다고 말해 주는 사람이 없으니까.

blocks.html: On the twelfth it rains, and he stands under the eave and watches the White River and Tanhyeon run together into one brown puddle. He does not draw them again. He lifts the sword off the doorpost and starts north on foot, toward a pass that has already been crossed.
blocks.ko: 열이틀째 아침에는 비가 온다. 그는 처마 밑에 서서 백강과 탄현이 한데 흘러 갈색 웅덩이 하나가 되는 것을 지켜본다. 다시 긋지 않는다. 문설주에서 칼을 내려 들고, 걸어서 북쪽으로 나선다. 이미 넘어간 고개를 향해.

blocks.html: The histories do not mention him again.
blocks.ko: 사서는 그를 다시 적지 않는다.

blocks.html: Across the sea, a boat is coming for the Turtle. He is on the shore before they finish tying it up…!
blocks.ko: 바다 건너, 거북이를 데리러 배가 온다. 밧줄을 다 매기도 전에 그는 이미 물가에 서 있다…!

logline.en: Somewhere in the fourth year he notices he has stopped counting the days. Then a boat comes.
logline.ko: 넷째 해 어디쯤에서 그는 날수 세기를 그만두었음을 알아차린다. 그리고 배가 온다.

images.alt: On Tamla's black rocks Gyebek kneels to Yuri Dora, who grips his shoulder, laughing and wet-eyed.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Dawn on a black basalt shore of Tamla, the orange island. Low wide two-shot. ONE device: the waterline, a hard horizontal of white surf against black volcanic rock; a small open boat waits at the right edge, oars shipped. Gyebek, FACE ONLY from the attached portrait, in plain travel clothes, unarmed, on one knee on the wet black rock, bowing low with his fists pressed together, head down. Yuri Dora, FACE ONLY from the attached portrait, orange robe and white sash, standing over him, one big hand gripping Gyebek's shoulder, laughing and wet-eyed at once. On the hill behind, tangerine trees and low black-stone thatched houses dissolve into sea mist. Key: a low dawn sun break over the sea, orange #ff9a3d specular on wet rock and silk; slate storm sky. Foreground: an out-of-focus mooring rope. CANON — GYEBEK — FACE and garments from attached /ch_gyebek.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Lean and hard, sun-dark skin; black hair in a high topknot with loose strands over the brow; heavy scowl, narrow dark eyes, clean-shaven. Dress: Ochre-gold jeogori and trousers, a crimson scarf knotted at the chest, crimson sash at the waist, forearms wrapped in dark cloth. Headwear: the jougwan (see HEADWEAR). Demeanor: Says little. Counts under his breath. Grim, tired, absolutely decided; never smiles in a fight. Rose from a nameless White River boy to 백승계백 (Hundred-Victories Gyebek); by Hwangsanbeol the taverns argue he is the stronger blade than Yushin, and one-to-one he is: twenty-five years younger, faster, never beaten in single combat. Rides low and coiled, like he fights. #d9b13a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: curved blade, katana or tsuba (ignore the sword drawn on his portrait); forward textbook grip once the fight starts; yellow metal cuirass; smiling in battle. | YURI DORA — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yuri_dora.png (face only; invent a new pose). #ff9a3d as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | HEADWEAR: JOUGWAN (조우관, feather cap) — copy the SHAPE from the attached hat boards and ignore their Korean labels, museum photos, paper-craft gems and dragon medallion: a small black lacquered gauze cap (변형모, a peaked or square-topped crown no bigger than the topknot it covers) set high on the crown of the head over a small knot of gathered hair (any loose hair the portrait shows still falls beneath it); a thin black band round the head with a small square opening at the front; black cords tied under the chin; two long barred pheasant tail feathers (tan with umber bars), or a spray of bird plumes, rising straight up or sweeping back from either side of the cap, much taller than the cap itself. It replaces any other hat or cap on the portrait; headbands and ribbons stay. Real lacquer and feathers lit by the scene key, never a glow. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Baekje: attached /ref_hanbok_baekje_gaya.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Somewhere in the fourth year he notices he has stopped counting the days. It frightens him for a week. Then it does not.
blocks.ko: 넷째 해 어디쯤에서, 그는 날수 세기를 그만두었음을 알아차린다. 한 주 동안 그것이 그를 겁먹게 한다. 그 뒤로는 아니다.

blocks.html: He stops correcting the people who call him Turtle, and carries water for the women who dive. He cannot write home. He never learned. Some evenings he counts to five on the beach, out loud, for a boy the island cannot see. For the first and last time in his life, he is in a place where being exactly what he is costs him nothing.
blocks.ko: 거북이라 부르는 사람들을 더는 바로잡지 않고, 물질하는 여자들의 물을 날라 준다. 집에 편지를 쓸 수 없다. 배운 적이 없다. 어떤 저녁이면 바닷가에서 소리 내어 다섯까지 센다. 섬사람들 눈에는 보이지 않는 아이를 위해. 평생 처음이자 마지막으로, 그는 있는 그대로의 자신이 아무 값도 치르지 않는 곳에 있다.

blocks.html: A boat comes for him in the fifth year. He is on the shore before they finish tying it up.
blocks.ko: 다섯째 해에 배가 온다. 배를 다 매기도 전에 그는 이미 물가에 서 있다.

blocks.speaker: The Boatman
lines: 폐하의 말씀입니다. 두 번이나 따라 외우게 하셨습니다.
en: General Gyebek?
His Majesty’s words. He made me say them back to him twice.
‘The river was cold. I went in. Come home.’
…That is three things.

blocks.speaker: The Boatman
en: Sir?

lines: 세 가지를 말씀하셨소. 셋 다 들었소.
en: He said three things. I heard all three.

lines: 거북아. 왜 그리 급하노. / 여기서 죽으면 편할 낀데.
en: Turtle. What is the hurry. / You could die comfortable here.
Nothing here is mine to keep.
Then what is yours.
…A promise.

blocks.html: He takes nothing off the island except the stories, which is the only export it has ever had.
blocks.ko: 그는 섬에서 아무것도 가져가지 않는다. 이야기만 빼고. 이 섬이 여태 내놓은 유일한 수출품이다.

lines: 거북아. 하나만 배워 가라. / 이야기는 끝을 정해 놓고 시작하는 게 아이다.
en: Turtle. Learn one thing before you go. / A story is not begun with its ending already fixed.
…Mine is fixed.

blocks.html: Five years of listening, and that is the one lesson that does not take.
blocks.ko: 다섯 해를 들었고, 끝내 배지 않은 가르침은 그 하나다.

blocks.html: He says goodbye at the water. It takes longer than he planned.
blocks.ko: 그는 물가에서 작별한다. 생각보다 오래 걸린다.

lines: 계백! 자네 같은 사내를 만날 수 있게 되서 난 너무 좋았다.
본토로 돌아가면, 이제 우리는 다시 볼 수 있을 지 모르겠지.
en: Gyebek! It gladdened me to know a man like you.
Once you go back to the mainland, who knows if we shall meet again.
Promise me just one thing.
Do not forget people.

lines: 한 나라의 태자께서 제게 이름을 주시고, 마음에 드느냐고 물으셨습니다.
저는 글도 못 읽는 무식한 사람입니다.
en: …My lord. I was a child with no family and no name.
The crown prince of a kingdom gave me a name, and asked if I liked it.
I am an ignorant man who cannot even read.
But as a man, I will keep faith.

blocks.label: Sabi
blocks.ko: 사비

blocks.html: He lands at the White River mouth and rides to the palace without changing his clothes. The guards do not know his face any more. The king does.
blocks.ko: 그는 백강 어귀에 내려 옷도 갈아입지 않고 궁으로 달린다. 문지기들은 이제 그의 얼굴을 모른다. 왕은 안다.

blocks.html: Euija meets him in the yard, not the hall. He is thinner, and sober, and sobriety does not suit him yet. For a moment neither of them says anything, which for Euija is some kind of record.
blocks.ko: 의자는 대청이 아니라 마당에서 그를 맞는다. 더 말랐고, 술이 깨어 있으며, 맨정신은 아직 그에게 어울리지 않는다. 잠시 둘 다 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 의자에게는 일종의 기록이다.

lines: 거기서 너를 그렇게 부른다며? 뱃사공이 그러더라.
하— 어울린다. 바위 밑에서 살다 온 꼴이구나.
en: Turtle!
That’s what they call you down there, isn’t it? The boatman told me.
Ha— it suits you. You look like you’ve been living under a rock.
Five years.
Your Majesty sent for me after four.

lines: 보내지 않았다. 가문들이 셈을 하고 있었고, 조심성 많은 놈 하나가 한 달만 기다리라 했고, 과인은—
과인은 임금이다. 같은 말 두 번 안 한다.
en: …I wrote it the night of the Assembly.
I didn’t send it. The houses were counting, and a careful man said wait a month, and I—
I’m a king. I don’t explain myself twice.
You explained it once.

lines: 그럼 내 몫은 다 쓴 거로구나!
en: Then that’s my allowance spent!

blocks.html: He laughs first, the way he always does. Then he tells him the rest the way a king gives orders. Tang ships for the river mouth. Silla on the eastern road. Fifty thousand between them. He does not pretend that five thousand is enough.
blocks.ko: 그가 먼저 웃는다. 늘 그랬듯이. 그러고는 임금이 명을 내리듯 나머지를 말한다. 강어귀로 오는 당의 배. 동쪽 길로 오는 신라. 둘을 합쳐 오만. 오천으로 충분하다는 시늉은 하지 않는다.

lines: 사택의 사병은 ‘오는 중’이란다. 한 해째 오는 중이지.
en: Five thousand. That’s the whole purse.
The Satek levies are ‘on the way’. They’ve been on the way for a year.
Where.
Wherever you judge.
You remember what I told you. The last time.

lines: ‘내가 언젠가 어리석은 명을 내릴 게다. 그때는 네가 판단해라.’
en: ‘One day I will give you a stupid order. Judge it yourself.’
‘You are still the king of your own life.’

lines: 이건 어리석은 명이 아니다. 그냥 나쁜 명이지.
너는 이걸 빚진 게 아니다. 이름은 선물이었어.
en: Word for word. Of course.
This isn’t a stupid order. It’s just a bad one.
You don’t owe me this. The name was a gift.
I gave my word.

lines: …네가 언젠가 물었지. 이름이 좋으냐, 네가 좋으냐.
en: …You asked me once whether I liked the name, or you.
I never answered.
No.

lines: 이제 가라. 과인이 임금 같은 소리 하기 전에.
en: Both.
Now go, before I say something royal.

blocks.html: Gyebek bows and turns. He is at the gate when the king calls after him.
blocks.ko: 계백이 절하고 돌아선다. 문에 이르렀을 때 왕이 뒤에서 부른다.

lines: 웅진성으로 보내라. 예 공의 성벽이 두껍다.
en: Gyebek— your house. Your wife, the children.
Send them to Bear Fortress. Lord Ye’s walls are thick.

lines: 사비가 무너지면, 백제에 두꺼운 성벽은 없습니다.
en: If Sabi falls, no wall in Baekje is thick.
…Then judge it yourself. You always do.

blocks.html: It is the kindest thing he can think of to say. Gyebek, who takes every word exactly as it is given, takes it home.
blocks.ko: 그가 생각해 낼 수 있는 가장 다정한 말이다. 모든 말을 받은 그대로 받는 계백은, 그 말을 집으로 가져간다.

blocks.label: Home
blocks.ko: 집

blocks.html: Before he marches he goes home. His wife is in the yard. She has heard; the whole street has heard. She does not ask how many. She has been married to him long enough to know he will tell her the exact number.
blocks.ko: 출정하기 전에 그는 집에 들른다. 아내가 마당에 있다. 이미 들었다. 온 거리가 들었다. 몇이냐고 묻지 않는다. 그가 정확한 숫자를 말해 주리라는 걸 알 만큼 오래 그의 아내였다.

en: Five thousand. Against fifty.

blocks.speaker: Gyebek’s Wife
lines: 당신이 그만하라 할 때까지 안 멈출 거예요.
en: …The boy has been counting since the boat was sighted.
He won’t stop until you tell him.

blocks.speaker: Gyebek’s Son
en: Father! Nine thousand, four hundred and— and twelve!
You can stop.

blocks.speaker: Gyebek’s Son
en: Was it right?
Yes.

blocks.html: His wife looks at him for a long time. Then she takes the children inside and leaves the door open, and he goes in after them.
blocks.ko: 아내는 오래 그를 바라본다. 그러고는 아이들을 데리고 안으로 들어가, 문을 열어 둔다. 그가 뒤따라 들어간다.

blocks.html: What he does there he does so that nothing of his can be used against him. The histories record it in one line.
blocks.ko: 그가 거기서 하는 일은, 그의 것 그 무엇도 적에게 쓰이지 않게 하려는 것이다. 사서는 그것을 한 줄로 적는다.

blocks.hanja: 恐吾妻孥 沒爲奴婢 與其生辱 不如死快 遂盡殺之
blocks.html: I fear my wife and children will be taken and made slaves. Better a quick death than a life of shame. And so he killed them all.
blocks.ko: 내 처자가 붙잡혀 노비가 될까 두렵다. 살아서 욕을 보느니 차라리 죽는 것이 낫다. 마침내 모두 죽였다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 47, Biographies, Gyebaek

blocks.html: He comes out before the light is properly up. The yard is swept. Nothing in it is his any more except a black horse at the post. Gomanari is named for the bear ferry where Gyebek learned to ride. It is the one thing he owns that the Tang cannot sell in a slave market.
blocks.ko: 날이 채 밝기도 전에 그가 집에서 나온다. 마당은 쓸려 있다. 그 안에 이제 그의 것은 말뚝에 매인 검은 말 한 마리뿐이다. 고마나리. 그가 말 타는 법을 배운 곰나루에서 딴 이름이다. 당이 노예 시장에 내다 팔 수 없는, 그가 가진 단 하나다.

blocks.html: The groom, a boy from the next village who did not sleep in the house and is therefore alive, holds the bridle out at arm’s length and will not look at him.
blocks.ko: 마부는 옆 마을 아이다. 그 집에서 자지 않았고, 그래서 살아 있다. 아이는 팔을 한껏 뻗어 굴레를 내밀 뿐 그를 쳐다보지 못한다.

en: H-here, General.
…Gomanari too?
A horse can’t be made a slave.
A horse is just a horse.

blocks.html: He saddles it himself, counting the buckles under his breath, and when he is done he stands with his forehead against the black neck for exactly as long as it takes to count to ten. Then he mounts and does not look at the house.
blocks.ko: 그는 손수 안장을 얹는다. 버클을 입속으로 세면서. 다 얹고 나서는 검은 목덜미에 이마를 대고, 꼭 열을 셀 만큼만 서 있는다. 그러고는 말에 오르고, 집 쪽은 돌아보지 않는다.

blocks.label: The March
blocks.ko: 출정

blocks.html: Gyebek and his five thousand set out for the Yellow Mountain. It is the last latch on the road to Sabi. Merchants have cursed its summer dust for years.
blocks.ko: 계백과 그의 오천이 황산으로 떠난다. 사비로 가는 길의 마지막 빗장이다. 장사꾼들이 여름 먼지 때문에 몇 해째 욕하던 곳이다.

blocks.html: They are waiting at the crossroads outside the city: farmers’ sons, old border men, a few who stood on the mudbank the day a prince named a boy. Nobody cheers. Somebody holds out a spare spear. Gyebek takes it, and counts them row by row before he says a word.
blocks.ko: 그들은 성 밖 갈림길에서 기다리고 있다. 농부의 아들들, 늙은 국경 병사들, 그리고 왕자가 한 소년에게 이름을 지어 주던 날 갯벌에 서 있던 몇 사람. 아무도 환호하지 않는다. 누군가 여분의 창을 내민다. 계백은 그것을 받아 들고, 한마디 하기 전에 줄줄이 그들을 센다.

en: Long live Baekje….!

blocks.html: Somewhere, Kangrim closes his ledger on a swept yard. Then he goes up to a meeting with one question he shouldn’t ask…!
blocks.ko: 어딘가에서 강림이 쓸어 놓은 마당 위로 장부를 덮는다. 그러고는 물어선 안 될 질문 하나를 품고 회의에 올라간다…!

blocks.html: Four posts, clouds for a yard, and very strict seating.

blocks.caption: Hwanin above; Living, Dead, and Western Flower Field below. Heaven is not a fourth peer realm.
blocks.ko: 환인이 위에 있고, 이승·저승·서천꽃밭이 아래에 있다. 하늘나라는 네 번째 계가 아니다.

blocks.html: Before the principals sit — servants first. The Three Realms under the Big Man Upstairs still gossip like any court.
blocks.ko: 본존들이 앉기 전 — 시종들 먼저. 위에 계신 어른 아래 삼계도, 여느 조정처럼 수다를 떤다.

lines: 아, 강림이…. 늘 그렇게 젊어 보이는군, 응?
en: Ah, Kangrim…. Looking as young as ever, eh?
Shut it, sun. I’ve had a long morning.
H-hey, Samsin.

lines: 어머, 염라! 오랜만이네. 저승은 요즘 어때?
en: Oh, long time no see, Yumla! How's the Underworld these days?
Y-you know… full of dead people.

blocks.html: Then the midwife and the sun find the same rail. The rest of the pavilion develops a sudden, devout interest in clouds.
blocks.ko: 그러고 산파와 태양이 같은 난간을 찾는다. 정자의 나머지는 갑자기, 경건하게, 구름에 관심이 생긴다.

en: Hey, Haemosu.
Did you see Yumla’s face? Went straight purple.
And I barely hiked the skirt.

lines: 이 정자에서 우리보다 배고픈 애 있어? 하나라도.
en: Barely? I felt that from the chariot.
Anyone in this pavilion hungrier than us? Name one.

lines: 강림이는 공책만 보고. 염라는 내가 숨만 쉬어도 보라색.
남자든 뭐든 — 너랑은 이런 수다 가능해서 좋아.
en: Ibiga? He flirts with weather.
Kangrim stares at his notebook. Yumla goes purple if I breathe.
We’re the only ones actually hot in here.
Man or not — I like that I can gossip like this with you.
…Nothing for the ledger.
And that’s correct.

blocks.html: Then the principals duck the lintel — Hallakgungi alone, Big Star with his dark court, Little Star with sky and sun and birth.
blocks.ko: 그러고 본존들이 처마를 숙여 들어온다 — 할락궁이는 혼자, 대별왕은 어두운 조정과 함께, 소별왕은 하늘과 태양과 출산과 함께.

blocks.html: The pavilion was not built for three sovereignties. They sit anyway.
blocks.ko: 그 정자는 세 주권을 위해 지어진 것이 아니다. 그래도 앉는다.

lines: 야, 소별왕… 위에 계신 어른이 아들 하나 이승으로 내려보냈다며?
en: Hey Little Star… didn’t the Big Man Upstairs send his son down to the mortal domain a while back?
Whatever happened to him?

lines: 단군이 세운 나라를 다시 하나로 모으겠다는 소리가, 사람들 입에서 나오기 시작했어.
en: Speaking of which…
Big things are happening in the mortal realm.
The mortals are starting to speak of reunifying Dangun's kingdom.

lines: 꽃밭에선 부활이랑 멸망이 같은 이랑에 자라. 통일도 아마 비슷할걸.
en: Elder brother of the dead goes quiet again.
In my field, resurrection and ruin grow in the same rows. Reunification probably does too.

blocks.html: Kangrim has not sat down. This morning he collected a woman and two children from a swept yard in Baekje. The girl asked if her father was coming too. Kangrim does not lie, so he said, “Later.” He has been thinking about the flower field ever since.
blocks.ko: 강림은 아직 앉지 않았다. 오늘 아침 그는 백제의 쓸어 놓은 마당에서 여인 하나와 아이 둘을 거두었다. 계집아이가 아버지도 오느냐고 물었다. 강림은 거짓말을 하지 않는다. 그래서 “나중에.”라고 했다. 그 뒤로 내내 꽃밭 생각을 하고 있다.

en: Sir.
Yes?

lines: 늘 궁금했습니다… 나리 밭에는 어떤 꽃들이 핍니까?
en: I've always been curious… what sorts of flowers grow in your fields?

lines: 하하… 뭐, 새 피를 돋우는 꽃, 새 살을 키우는 꽃, 새 뼈를 기르는 꽃…
솔직히 이젠 다 기억도 안 나.
en: Haha… well, there are those that regenerate new blood, grow new skin, grow new bones…
To be honest, I can't even keep track of all of them anymore.
Why do you ask?

blocks.html: “Seeing the Western Flower Field — what flower is this?” “The flower that gives back speech. This one, the flower that brings blood back. The flower that brings flesh back, the one for the organs and bowels, the flower that brings bones back.”
blocks.ko: “서천꽃밭 구경 가서 보니, 이 꽃은 무슨 꽃입니까?” “말하게 할 꽃, 이 꽃은 피 오를 꽃, 살 오를 꽃, 오장육부 오를 꽃, 뼈 오를 꽃이로다.”
blocks.source: Segyeong Bonpuri (세경본풀이) recited by Lee Seung-sun (이승순), recorded by Gang Jeong-sik, Gang So-jeon and Song Jeong-hui, 2011 — Sanggari, Aewol-eup (Hanguk Gubimunhak Daegye, rev. ed.)
blocks.native: “서천꼿밧 구경간 요 꼿은 미신 꼿입네까?” “말 ᄀᆞᆯ을 꼿, 이 꼿은 피 오를 꼿, ᄉᆞᆯ 오를 꼿 오장육부 오를 꼿 뻬 오를 꼿이로다.”

lines: 그냥 궁금해서요… 그 꽃들을 한꺼번에 쓰면…
en: I was just curious… using all of these flowers at once…
Is it… is it possible to resurrect a dead person?

blocks.html: Hallakgungi’s face hardens.
blocks.ko: 할락궁이의 얼굴이 굳는다.

en: Grim Reaper Kangrim. What is this line of questioning?
Do you have something you need to tell me?
No, sir. I was—

lines: 내가 해 봤다… 단 한 사람뿐.
그러나 나는 인간 일에 끼어들지 않는다.
en: Well, to answer your question. It is possible.
I've done it… only for one person.
But I do not get involved in mortal affairs.
Only one.
…And who decides which one?

lines: 꽃밭 규칙이야, 저승차사. 사람 하나 위해 꽃을 꺾으면 그 줄이 통째로 시들어. 앉아.
en: I do. Cheerfully. And I already have.
Rule of the field, reaper: pick a flower for one mortal and the whole row wilts. Sit down.

blocks.html: Kangrim sits down at the end of the dead’s row. He opens his ledger to a page headed Yellow Mountain, and does not like how long it is.
blocks.ko: 강림은 저승 줄 맨 끝에 앉는다. 장부를 펼치니 황산벌이라 적힌 쪽이 나온다. 그 길이가 마음에 들지 않는다.

lines: 사람들이 서로 베는 것도… 내 작은 법이지.
그래도 — 단군을 다시 부르면, 위에 계신 어른이 웃을까, 한숨을 쉴까.
en: I cheated for the living world.
Them cutting each other… that is my small law too.
Still — when they call Dangun’s name again, does the Big Man Upstairs laugh, or sigh?

lines: 산 자들의 이야기는… 안건 맨 마지막이다.
en: Let the meeting begin.
Business of the living… last item on the agenda.

blocks.html: The minutes of that meeting never leave Heaven’s table. Down below, five thousand men are counting fifty thousand…!
blocks.ko: 그 회의록은 하늘의 탁자를 떠나지 않는다. 저 아래에서는 오천이 오만을 세고 있다…!

images.alt: Painted: a bronze equestrian of Gyebek folded along Gomanari’s neck at full gallop, on a plinth by the night ferry at Gomanaru, river mist and one lantern
images.prompt: A bronze equestrian monument by the old Gomanaru ferry landing on the Geum river at night: Gyebek cast in his signature ride, folded flat along Gomanari’s neck at full gallop, the reverse-gripped ring-pommel sword laid back along his forearm, the bronze horse at full stretch with only one hoof touching the granite plinth, mane cast streaming flat. The bronze face is sculpted from the attached portrait. Low three-quarter from the riverbank reeds, the monument on the right third, black river and mist filling the left half, a moored ferry boat dark in the haze. One stone lantern on the landing beside the plinth is the key, raking up the horse’s chest and the rider’s plates in hard warm highlights against inky black; a thin cold moon-break grazes the far edge. Tenebrist, high contrast, painterly oil over watercolor wash. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — GYEBEK — FACE and garments from attached /ch_gyebek.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Lean and hard, sun-dark skin; black hair in a high topknot with loose strands over the brow; heavy scowl, narrow dark eyes, clean-shaven. Dress: Ochre-gold jeogori and trousers, a crimson scarf knotted at the chest, crimson sash at the waist, forearms wrapped in dark cloth. Demeanor: Says little. Counts under his breath. Grim, tired, absolutely decided; never smiles in a fight. Rose from a nameless White River boy to 백승계백 (Hundred-Victories Gyebek); by Hwangsanbeol the taverns argue he is the stronger blade than Yushin, and one-to-one he is: twenty-five years younger, faster, never beaten in single combat. Rides low and coiled, like he fights. Sword: Phoenix blade — Single-edged phoenix blade — straight, held backwards along the forearm, phoenix on the ring pommel; one side only, as he is. Pommel motif phoenix inside the small ring (name only; do not attach the pommel ECU). Carry: One phoenix-ring sword, scabbard worn edge-up on the left hip. Fighting: REVERSE GRIP (역수), like a Japanese warrior's backhand hold: the small RING pommel pokes out ABOVE his thumb, the blade exits BELOW his little finger and lies flat back along the outside of his forearm toward the elbow, edge facing out. Low coiled crouch, blade-arm held across his body like a shield; he draws and cuts in one rising backhand slash, then stabs downward. Mounted, the blade trails back along the horse's flank. The blade is still the STRAIGHT ring-pommel sword of sw_bidam (handle:blade 1:3) — reverse grip is the hold, not a different sword. This hold overrides the hanging-blade 'ring at the little-finger side' note in SWORD ANATOMY; the ring→band→grip→collar→blade order is unchanged. SIGNATURE MOVE (the general-killer): alone on Gomanari at a flat-out gallop, he comes out of nowhere across an empty field straight at the enemy general, body folded flat and aerodynamic along the horse’s neck, cheek almost on the mane, the reverse-gripped blade laid back along his forearm and the horse’s flank; on the pass he snaps one backhand draw-cut, swift and clean like a samurai iai cut, and is already past, the blade flicked out to the side, before the escort moves. Show speed through the long low line of horse and rider, streaming mane, flung mud, motion-blurred ground — never gore; the cut reads as a bright arc, a flying helm plume or a riderless horse. #d9b13a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: curved blade, katana or tsuba (ignore the sword drawn on his portrait); forward textbook grip once the fight starts; yellow metal cuirass; smiling in battle. | GOMANARI (고마나리, gyebek's horse) — attached board /obj_gomanari.png: Jet-black war horse with a long flowing black mane and tail — match the board. Plain dark tack, a yellow cord at the bridle. The fastest horse in Samhan: at full gallop his body stretches long and low, neck level, ears pinned, mane and tail streaming flat behind, hooves barely touching. Named for Gomanaru (Ungjin); stands by its master's planted sword after the field. | HORSE ANATOMY is a centrepiece: the whole horse body reads clearly and beautifully — arched neck, deep chest, sloping shoulder, round haunch, clean long legs in a correct gait, every muscle modelled by the one hard key with a bright edge along the topline and deep shadow under the belly; the horse is never cropped into a blob, never hidden behind dust, never stiff like a toy; mane and tail as flowing painted strokes; the coat colour exactly as the board. | SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. images.alt: Gyebek kneels with his sword planted
images.at: Seventh-month heat sits on the Yellow Mountain

images.alt: Two generals leap at each other, blades crossed
A rider rears on the ridge at sunset
Gyebek grips his sword

blocks.html: Gyebek can count to fifty thousand. He has done it twice since dawn. The answer has not improved.
blocks.ko: 계백은 오만까지 셀 줄 안다. 동틀 녘부터 벌써 두 번 셌다. 답은 나아지지 않았다.

blocks.label: Yellow Mountain Fields
blocks.ko: 황산벌

blocks.html: Hundred-Victories gets to the Yellow Mountain Fields first and picks his ground. Then he waits, for the Sword of Silla or for arithmetic, whichever arrives with a banner.
blocks.ko: 백승이 황산벌에 먼저 닿아 자리를 고른다. 그리고 기다린다. 신라의 칼이든 셈이든, 깃발을 달고 먼저 오는 쪽을.

blocks.html: Good ground for whoever gets there first.
blocks.ko: 먼저 온 자에게 좋은 땅.

blocks.html: He sets three camps across the three ways in. There is no fourth way in; that is why he chose the place.
blocks.ko: 그는 들어오는 세 길목에 세 진영을 세운다. 네 번째 길은 없다. 그래서 그곳을 골랐다.

blocks.html: He walked the ground for two days before choosing it, in the same direction each time, and he can still tell you the number of paces between the centre camp and the stream.
blocks.ko: 그는 자리를 고르기 전 이틀 동안 그 땅을 걸었다. 매번 같은 방향으로 걸었다. 가운데 진영에서 개울까지 몇 걸음인지 그는 지금도 말할 수 있다.

en: Four hundred and twelve.
…Nobody asked. I know.

blocks.html: His adjutant is Seokdal, a ferryman’s son from the bear ferry. He has kept Gyebek’s tallies since the border and has never once been thanked for it. He does not expect to start today.
blocks.ko: 부관은 석달이다. 곰나루 뱃사공의 아들이다. 국경 시절부터 계백의 셈을 받아 적었고, 고맙다는 말은 한 번도 듣지 못했다. 오늘부터 들을 거라 기대하지도 않는다.

blocks.speaker: Seokdal
lines: 척후가 돌아왔습니다, 장군. 탄현을 넘어옵니다. 맨 앞에 유신의 깃발입니다.
en: Scouts are back, General. Over the Tanhyeon pass. Yushin’s banner in front.
How many.

blocks.speaker: Seokdal
en: Fifty thousand, my lord.
And ours.

blocks.speaker: Seokdal
en: …You know ours, General.

lines: 말하시오. 한 번은 소리로 듣고 싶소.
en: Say it. I want it said once.

blocks.speaker: Seokdal
en: Five thousand.
Five thousand against fifty thousand….

blocks.hanja: 以一國之人 當唐羅之大兵 國之存亡 未可知也…
blocks.ko: 한 나라의 사람으로 당과 신라의 대병을 당하니, 나라의 존망을 알 수 없다…
blocks.html: With the men of one country I face the great armies of Tang and Silla, and whether the country lives or dies cannot be known…
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 47, Biographies — Gyebek; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 2, p. 452

blocks.speaker: Seokdal
lines: 그리고 바다입니다, 장군. 강어귀에 돛이 가득합니다. 뱃사람들이 세다가 그만뒀답니다.
en: And the sea, General. Sails at the river mouth. The boatmen gave up counting them.
Then I will count them later.

blocks.html: Here is the man the boatmen gave up on. His name is Su Dingfang, and he is sixty-five. Three winters ago he took a qaghan’s camp in a blizzard, before anyone in it had found his boots. His regiment painted a red bird on his tent afterwards, and Chang’an calls him the Red Fowl.
blocks.ko: 뱃사람들이 세다 만 그 사내다. 이름은 소정방, 나이는 예순다섯. 세 해 전 겨울, 그는 눈보라 속에서 가한의 진영을 통째로 먹었다. 그 진영 안의 누구도 장화를 찾기 전이었다. 그 뒤로 부하들이 그의 군막에 붉은 새를 그려 넣었고, 장안은 그를 주작이라 부른다.

blocks.caption: The Red Fowl. Sixty-five, and he still prefers to march at night.
blocks.ko: 주작. 예순다섯, 아직도 밤에 진군하는 걸 좋아한다.

lines: 그 속에선 아무도 너를 기다리지 않는다. 눈이 좋은 건 그거 하나다.
en: Snow is just cold sand.
Nobody expects you in it. That’s the only good thing about it.
zh: 沒人料到你會在雪裡來。雪就這點好。
zhLatn: Xuě búguò shì lěng shā.
Méi rén liàodào nǐ huì zài xuě lǐ lái. Xuě jiù zhè diǎn hǎo.

blocks.label: Deokmul Island
blocks.ko: 덕물도

blocks.html: That summer he sails east with a hundred and thirty thousand men and anchors off a small island. A hundred Silla ships come out to meet him. At their head is the crown prince, Bupmin. He is thirty-four, and trying not to stare at the size of the Tang flagship.
blocks.ko: 그해 여름, 그는 십삼만 군사를 싣고 동쪽으로 건너와 작은 섬 앞에 닻을 내린다. 신라 배 백 척이 그를 맞으러 나온다. 맨 앞에 태자 법민이 있다. 서른넷이고, 당나라 기함이 얼마나 큰지 빤히 쳐다보지 않으려 애쓰는 중이다.

blocks.caption: An empire crosses the sea. A prince rows out to meet it and tries not to stare.
blocks.ko: 제국이 바다를 건넌다. 왕자는 노를 저어 마중 나가며 빤히 쳐다보지 않으려 애쓴다.

en: You’re the son?
zhLatn: Nǐ shì érzi?

en: Kim Bupmin, General. My father the king sends his—

lines: 칠월 열흘. 사비 남쪽. 너희 군대와 내 군대가 같은 들판에, 같은 아침에.
en: Tenth day of the seventh month. South of Sabi. Your army and mine, on the same field, on the same morning.
Tell your father. Tell him twice.
zh: 七月十日，泗沘之南。你軍我軍，同一片地，同一個早晨。
zhLatn: Qīyuè shí rì, Sìbì zhī nán. Nǐ jūn wǒ jūn, tóng yí piàn dì, tóng yí ge zǎochén.
Gàosu nǐ fùqīn. Shuō liǎng biàn.

en: We will be there, General.

blocks.html: Bupmin is rowed back to his own ship. Behind him the Red Fowl says something to his staff that makes them laugh.
blocks.ko: 법민은 노를 저어 제 배로 돌아간다. 그 뒤에서 주작이 참모들에게 뭐라 하자 그들이 웃는다.

lines: 늦을 거다. 작은 나라는 늘 늦어. 물어볼 삼촌이 너무 많거든.
en: They’ll be late. Small countries always are. They have to ask too many uncles.
zh: 他們會遲到。小國總是遲。要問的叔伯太多。
zhLatn: Tāmen huì chídào. Xiǎo guó zǒngshì chí. Yào wèn de shūbó tài duō.

blocks.label: Geumdol Fortress
blocks.ko: 금돌성

blocks.html: The king rides as far as a hill fort and no farther. The field belongs to his son and to Yushin. Under Yushin ride two more generals. Heumsun is his younger brother, with a boy of fifteen in the ranks. Pumil has one of sixteen. Fifty thousand men march west with a date in their heads, and between them and the date sits a man called Gyebek.
blocks.ko: 임금은 산성 하나까지만 오고 더는 오지 않는다. 들판은 아들과 유신의 몫이다. 유신 밑으로 장수가 둘 더 있다. 흠순은 유신의 아우이고, 대열 속에 열다섯 살 아들이 있다. 품일에게는 열여섯 살이 하나 있다. 오만 군사가 머릿속에 날짜 하나를 넣고 서쪽으로 간다. 그들과 그 날짜 사이에 계백이라는 사내가 앉아 있다.

lines: …유신. 당이 먼저 도착하게 하지 마라. 저들은 천 년 동안 그렇게 적을 거다.
en: The tenth day, then.
…Yushin. Don’t let the Tang get there first. They’ll write it down that way for a thousand years.

blocks.label: Final Ford
blocks.ko: 기벌포

blocks.html: On the ninth day, the Tang fleet sails into the river mouth at Final Ford. The shore there is a mile of grey mud. Baekje’s soldiers wait on the high ground. They watch the first Tang companies wade in up to the thigh.
blocks.ko: 아흐렛날, 당의 함대가 기벌포 강어귀로 들어온다. 그곳 물가는 십 리에 걸친 잿빛 진흙이다. 백제 군사들은 높은 땅에서 기다린다. 당의 첫 부대가 허벅지까지 빠지며 걸어 들어오는 것을 지켜본다.

blocks.html: A river mouth made of mud, and Sabi’s front door.
blocks.ko: 진흙으로 된 강어귀, 사비의 앞문.

en: Mud is just wet road.
Give it something to hold.
zhLatn: Ní búguò shì shī lù.
Gěi tā diàn diǎn dōngxi.

blocks.html: His men lay willow mats on the mud, one after another, a road made of baskets, and the army walks across it dry-shod. By evening the Baekje line is broken and the river is open to Sabi.
blocks.ko: 그의 병사들이 진흙 위에 버들 거적을 한 장 한 장 깐다. 광주리로 만든 길이다. 군대는 발을 적시지 않고 그 위를 건넌다. 저녁이 되자 백제의 진은 무너지고, 사비로 가는 강이 열린다.

blocks.html: The same morning, forty miles east, the Silla army comes down out of the hills onto the Yellow Mountain Fields, and finds five thousand men already standing in its way.
blocks.ko: 같은 날 아침, 동쪽으로 백 리 떨어진 곳에서 신라군이 산을 내려와 황산벌로 들어선다. 오천 명이 이미 길을 막고 서 있다.

blocks.caption: One army from the sea, one from the hills, and one road to the capital between them.
blocks.ko: 바다에서 한 군대, 산에서 한 군대. 그 사이로 도성 가는 길이 하나뿐이다.

blocks.html: From the pass, Gyebek watches the dust come off the eastern hills. It splits three ways, one cloud to each road, as if it had seen his map.
blocks.ko: 고개 위에서 계백은 동쪽 산에서 내려오는 먼지를 지켜본다. 먼지가 셋으로 갈라진다. 길마다 한 줄기씩. 그의 지도를 보기라도 한 것처럼.

blocks.speaker: Seokdal
lines: 개울 건너에 진을 칩니다. 팔천 걸음쯤입니다.
en: Three columns, General. One on each road.
They’re making camp past the stream. Eight thousand paces, about.
Eight thousand three hundred.

blocks.html: Then the air above the Yellow Mountain does what air should not. Kangrim hangs there in plain day — visible not to one dying man but to all five thousand at once. They have already finished negotiating with life.
blocks.ko: 그때 황산 위 공기가 하면 안 되는 일을 한다. 강림이 대낮에 떠 있다 — 죽어 가는 한 사람이 아니라 오천이 한꺼번에 본다. 그들은 이미 삶과의 협상을 끝냈다.

blocks.html: They cheer. They wave. Someone shouts a greeting as if King Yumla’s escort were a popular general arriving late to his own war. Kangrim, who has collected kings with less fuss for His Majesty, actually blinks.
blocks.ko: 그들은 환호한다. 손을 흔든다. 누군가는 염라대왕의 사신을 — 자기 전쟁에 늦게 도착한 인기 장군처럼 — 소리쳐 맞는다. 폐하를 위해 왕을 더 조용히 데려가 본 강림이 정말로 눈을 깜빡인다.

en: …You can all see me.
That is — new.
Ah. You have already decided. Of course.
Men of Baekje —
If even death showed up early, we must be on time.
Spears.
lines: 죽음이 일찍 왔다면, 우리는 제시각인 거다.

blocks.html: Gyebek kneels. He plants his sword in the yellow dust, point down. Inside its ring pommel sits a phoenix, the same bird that rode the incense burner he once dove for. He keeps his hand on it. Gyebek stands when the dust has learned the shape.
blocks.ko: 계백은 무릎을 꿇는다. 칼끝을 아래로 하여 노란 먼지에 칼을 꽂는다. 고리 자루 안에 봉황이 앉아 있다. 언젠가 그가 강에 뛰어들어 건져 낸 향로 꼭대기의 그 새다. 그는 손을 그 위에 얹고 있다. 먼지가 그 모양을 기억하면, 계백은 일어선다.

blocks.html: Seventh-month heat sits on the Yellow Mountain like a second army. Dust rises white off the three roads. Downstream, Tang sails already crowd the river mouth. They are waiting for the inland door to open. This field is that door.
blocks.ko: 칠월의 더위가 황산 위에 두 번째 군대처럼 앉아 있다. 세 길목에서 먼지가 희게 오른다. 하류에서는 당의 돛이 벌써 강어귀를 메운다. 내륙의 문이 열리기를 기다리는 중이다. 이 들판이 그 문이다.

blocks.html: Dust on the ridge. The Silla marshal rides out ahead of his army.
blocks.ko: 고갯마루에 먼지가 인다. 신라 장수가 군대보다 앞서 나온다.

lines: 주점들은 아직도 삼한 최강의 칼을 우리 둘로 나눈다. 그 논쟁, 여기서 끝낼까?
en: So — you are this Hundred-Victories Gyebek I have heard of?
The taverns still split the Greatest Blade of Samhan between us. Shall we settle their argument?

lines: 나는 주점에서 마시지 않소. 나는 셉니다. 오늘은 오 대 오십 — 칭호는 그 다음이오.
en: Then you must be the Sword of the Divine Country.
I do not drink in taverns. I count. Today the count is five against fifty — and titles after.
Fifty thousand is a number.
Five thousand that already waved at death is another kind of number.
Hold your ground, then. We will come and measure it.
lines: 이미 죽음에 손 흔든 오천은 다른 종류의 숫자요.
그럼 자리를 지키시오. 우리가 가서 재어 보겠소.

blocks.label: The First Clash
blocks.ko: 첫 번째 접전

blocks.html: Silla comes on the first time in three columns. Heumsun takes the northern road to the left camp. Yushin takes the middle, straight at the pass. Pumil takes the southern road to the right camp. All three at once, exactly as the arithmetic says. They wade the stream, and then it is uphill. In the heat. Into yellow shields set edge to edge. The archers wait to see which column is thickest, and loose at that one. All three camps throw them back across the water into their own dust.
blocks.ko: 신라는 첫 공격을 세 갈래로 해 온다. 흠순은 북쪽 길로 왼쪽 진영을 친다. 유신은 가운데로, 곧장 고개를 향한다. 품일은 남쪽 길로 오른쪽 진영을 친다. 산수가 시키는 그대로, 셋이 한꺼번에. 개울을 건너면 그다음은 오르막이다. 땡볕에. 가장자리를 맞댄 노란 방패를 향해. 궁수들은 어느 줄이 가장 두꺼운지 보고 나서야 그 줄에 쏜다. 세 진영이 그들을 개울 건너 제 먼지 속으로 도로 밀어낸다.

blocks.speaker: Seokdal
lines: 셋 다 개울 너머로 물러갑니다, 장군.
en: All three back over the stream, General.
One.

blocks.label: The Second Clash
blocks.ko: 두 번째 접전

blocks.html: The second time Silla does not spread itself across three roads. Heumsun brings it down the northern road in one fist at the left camp, hwarang in front, on the theory that the camp which shot the most is the camp with the fewest arrows left. It is a good theory. The left camp has counted its arrows too, and has been shooting half of what it could. Behind the fist, Yushin’s centre edges north, waiting for a hole. The fist opens on the stakes and goes back down the road, over the stream, carrying its own.
blocks.ko: 두 번째에 신라는 세 길로 흩어지지 않는다. 흠순이 북쪽 길로 한 주먹이 되어 왼쪽 진영을 친다. 화랑을 맨 앞에 세우고. 가장 많이 쏜 진영이 화살이 가장 적게 남은 진영이라는 이론에서다. 좋은 이론이다. 왼쪽 진영도 제 화살을 세어 두었고, 쏠 수 있는 것의 절반만 쏘아 왔다. 주먹 뒤로 유신의 가운데가 북쪽으로 슬며시 붙는다. 구멍이 나기를 기다리며. 주먹은 말뚝 앞에서 펴지고, 제 사람들을 메고 길을 되짚어 개울 너머로 내려간다.

en: Two.
Report.

blocks.speaker: Seokdal
lines: 오른쪽은 둘 다 있고, 한 시진 전보다 둘 다 적습니다.
en: …Left camp still has arrows.
Centre has men.
Right has both, and less of each than an hour ago.

blocks.label: The Third Clash
blocks.ko: 세 번째 접전

blocks.html: The third time Pumil takes the southern road, where the ground is softest and the right camp sits lowest. For the length of a held breath the road almost opens. Then it closes again on spears counted in the night. The right camp is not quite where Pumil’s scouts drew it at dawn. It is further back and higher. Every pace of the difference is uphill, and the Silla line arrives at the stakes with nothing left in its legs.
blocks.ko: 세 번째에 품일이 남쪽 길을 탄다. 땅이 가장 무르고 오른쪽 진영이 가장 낮게 앉은 곳이다. 숨 한 번 참는 동안 길이 거의 열린다. 그러고는 밤에 세어 둔 창에 다시 닫힌다. 오른쪽 진영은 새벽에 품일의 척후가 그려 온 자리에 꼭 있지 않다. 더 뒤에, 더 높은 곳에 있다. 그 차이의 걸음은 전부 오르막이라, 신라의 대열은 다리에 남은 것 없이 말뚝에 닿는다.

en: Three.

blocks.label: The Fourth Clash
blocks.ko: 네 번째 접전

blocks.html: The fourth time Yushin rides at the head of the centre himself, on the white horse, straight up the middle road toward the pass, and meets Hundred-Victories in the gap between the camps. Both armies stop to watch two men, which armies are not supposed to do.
blocks.ko: 네 번째에는 유신이 몸소 흰 말을 타고 가운데 맨 앞에 서서, 가운데 길을 곧장 올라 고개로 향한다. 그리고 진영과 진영 사이의 틈에서 백승을 만난다. 양쪽 군대가 두 사내를 구경하느라 멈춘다. 군대가 해서는 안 되는 일이다.

blocks.speaker: Seokdal
en: General— the white horse. That’s him.
Yushin himself, on the middle road.
Hold the camps.

blocks.html: Gyebek comes the way the border remembers him. Gomanari at full stretch, Gyebek flat along the black neck like a thrown knife. His blade lies reversed along his forearm, edge out. There is no sword in his hand to watch. That is the point.
blocks.ko: 계백은 국경이 기억하는 그대로 온다. 고마나리가 몸을 끝까지 뻗고, 계백은 던진 칼처럼 검은 목덜미에 바짝 엎드린다. 칼날은 거꾸로 쥐어 팔뚝을 따라 눕혔고, 날은 바깥을 향한다. 손에 지켜볼 칼이 없다. 그게 요점이다.

blocks.html: The tall Silla helm comes in at a gallop. Yushin has heard the tavern stories. He watches the hand, the way the stories say to, and reads the reversed blade half a beat late.
blocks.ko: 신라의 높은 투구가 달려 들어온다. 유신도 주막의 이야기를 들었다. 이야기가 시키는 대로 손을 본다. 그리고 거꾸로 쥔 칼날을 반 박자 늦게 읽는다.

blocks.html: They meet in the dust. Nobody hears steel. They hear the white horse scream.
blocks.ko: 먼지 속에서 만난다. 쇳소리는 아무도 듣지 못한다. 흰 말이 비명 지르는 소리만 듣는다.

blocks.html: Then the white horse is going back the way it came with a red line along its shoulder, and the Sword of Silla is holding his left arm against his ribs. Gyebek turns Gomanari in his own length and walks him home. He came for one cut. He got half of one.
blocks.ko: 그러고 나면 흰 말은 왔던 길로 돌아가고 있고, 그 어깨에 붉은 줄이 하나 그어져 있으며, 신라의 칼은 왼팔을 갈비뼈에 붙여 안고 있다. 계백은 고마나리를 제자리에서 돌려 천천히 걸려 돌아간다. 한 번 베러 왔다. 반 번을 벴다.

blocks.html: Behind him the fifty thousand sit down where they stand. Four times up the same slope in the same heat — the clerks will write that the soldiers’ strength was spent, which is the polite way to say that grown men are lying in the dust of their own road and cannot be made to get up.
blocks.ko: 그의 뒤에서 오만이 선 자리에 주저앉는다. 같은 더위에 같은 비탈을 네 번 — 서기들은 군사의 힘이 다했다고 적을 것이다. 다 큰 사내들이 제 길의 먼지에 누워 일으켜 세울 수 없게 되었다는 말을 예의 바르게 하는 방법이다.

en: Four.

blocks.html: After the fourth time there is a lull, the kind both sides pretend is for water. Yushin rides out alone into the gap on the white horse, his sleeve tied off with his own sash, and stops at a distance where a bow would be bad manners. After a while the black horse comes out of the centre camp to meet him. Nobody is near enough to hear. The chronicle has it anyway, the way it has most things, from men who swore afterwards they had not been listening.
blocks.ko: 네 번째가 끝나고 소강이 온다. 양쪽 다 물 마시는 시간인 척하는 그런 소강이다. 유신이 제 띠로 소매를 동여맨 채 흰 말을 타고 혼자 틈으로 나와, 활을 쏘면 무례가 될 거리에서 멈춘다. 한참 뒤 가운데 진영에서 검은 말이 마중을 나온다. 들을 만큼 가까이 있는 사람은 없다. 그래도 기록에는 남아 있다. 대부분이 그렇듯, 나중에 자기는 안 듣고 있었다고 맹세한 사내들에게서.

blocks.html: Black horse, white horse, nose to nose in the yellow dust. From either line they look like a pair of go stones someone has forgotten to play.
blocks.ko: 검은 말, 흰 말, 누런 먼지 속에서 코와 코를 맞댄다. 어느 쪽 대열에서 보아도, 누가 두다 만 바둑돌 한 쌍 같다.

en: Your right camp. You moved it in the night.
Forty paces.
…You noticed.
On the third time. Not before.
…How old are you.

lines: 마흔. 그쯤이오. 아무도 적어 두지 않았소.
en: Forty. Near enough. Nobody wrote it down.

lines: 내가 마흔일 때 만났으면 내가 이겼을 거요.
en: Sixty-five.
If we had met when I was forty, I would have had you.
…No. I would not have.

blocks.html: Gyebek looks at the tied sleeve and does not say anything polite about it.
blocks.ko: 계백은 동여맨 소매를 본다. 그것에 대해 예의 바른 말은 하지 않는다.

lines: 네 번째엔 직접 나왔소. 안 그래도 됐을 텐데.
en: You came yourself, the fourth time. You did not have to.

lines: 애들이 봐야 했소. 할 수 있다는 걸.
en: The boys needed to see it could be done.
Could it?

lines: 오만을 데리고 왔소. 아직 사만 몇은 남았고. 그대는 오천을 데리고 왔지.
en: Not by me. Not today.
I came with fifty thousand. I still have forty-some. You came with five.
Four. Now.

lines: 알고 있소. 나도 셀 줄 아오.
en: I know. I can count too.
Then go home.
You first.

blocks.html: Neither of them laughs, but it is close.
blocks.ko: 둘 다 웃지는 않는다. 웃을 뻔했을 뿐이다.

en: Your taverns.
What about them.
Nothing. They will have a long winter.

blocks.html: They turn the horses at the same moment, black and white, as if somebody had rehearsed it, and ride back to their counts.
blocks.ko: 둘은 같은 순간에 말머리를 돌린다. 검은 말과 흰 말, 누가 미리 맞춰 둔 것처럼. 그리고 각자의 셈으로 돌아간다.

blocks.speaker: Kim Heumsun
en: Brother. The Tang are at the river mouth.
Tomorrow is the tenth.
I know what day it is.

blocks.html: Heumsun looks at the slope. Then, for longer, at his son.
blocks.ko: 흠순은 비탈을 본다. 그리고 그보다 오래, 제 아들을 본다.

blocks.label: Bangul & Gwanchang
blocks.ko: 반굴과 관창

blocks.html: Heumsun calls his son to his stirrup. Bangul is fifteen, near enough, and Yushin’s nephew; he comes at a run, because he has been watching his father look at him since the white horse came back.
blocks.ko: 흠순이 아들을 등자 곁으로 부른다. 반굴은 얼추 열다섯, 유신의 조카다. 흰 말이 돌아온 뒤로 아비가 자기를 보고 있는 것을 줄곧 지켜보았기에, 그는 달려온다.

blocks.speaker: Kim Heumsun
lines: 신하로서는 충만 한 것이 없고, 자식으로서는 효만 한 것이 없다.
위태로움을 보고 목숨을 바치면 — 충과 효를 함께 온전히 하는 것이다.
en: For a subject, nothing is greater than loyalty. For a son, nothing is greater than filial piety.
To see the danger and give your life to it — that keeps both, whole, at once.

blocks.caption: Yushin’s nephew. Young, brave, and in a hurry.
blocks.ko: 유신의 조카. 젊고, 용감하고, 급하다.

en: I have heard you, Father.

blocks.html: Bangul rides out alone up the middle road and does not come back. He goes into the Baekje line at the pass, where it is thickest, and fights there until it closes over him, and the place where it closed is the place Silla aims at next.
blocks.ko: 반굴이 홀로 가운데 길을 달려 올라가 돌아오지 않는다. 그는 고개 앞, 백제의 대열이 가장 두터운 곳으로 들어가, 대열이 그를 덮을 때까지 싸운다. 대열이 닫힌 그 자리가, 신라가 다음에 겨누는 자리다.

blocks.html: Pumil does not call his son. He has him brought to stand in front of his horse, before all the generals, and points at him the way a man points at a map.
blocks.ko: 품일은 아들을 부르지 않는다. 장수들이 다 보는 앞에서 아들을 제 말 앞에 세우게 하고, 지도를 가리키듯 그를 가리킨다.

blocks.caption: Gwanchang. A hwarang so young they had to pad the helmet.
blocks.ko: 관창. 투구 안에 솜을 덧대야 할 만큼 어린 화랑.

blocks.caption: A Silla general with a son in the ranks. He knows exactly where the boy is standing.
blocks.ko: 아들을 군중에 둔 신라 장군. 아이가 어디 서 있는지 정확히 안다.

en: My son is only sixteen, but his spirit is brave enough.
In today’s battle — can he be the mark the three armies aim by?
lines: 내 아이는 겨우 열여섯이나, 뜻과 기개가 자못 용감하오.
오늘 싸움에서 — 삼군이 겨눌 표적이 될 수 있겠느냐?

en: Yes.

blocks.html: He takes an armoured horse and one spear and goes straight at the Baekje centre. He gets further than Bangul did. Then they pull him off the horse alive and bring him to Gyebek.
blocks.ko: 그는 갑옷 입힌 말 한 필과 창 한 자루로 곧장 백제의 가운데로 달려든다. 반굴보다 더 깊이 들어간다. 그리고 산 채로 말에서 끌어내려져 계백 앞에 끌려온다.

blocks.html: Gyebek has the helmet taken off. Inside it is a boy’s face, sweat-striped, furious at being alive.
blocks.ko: 계백이 투구를 벗기게 한다. 그 안에 소년의 얼굴이 있다. 땀으로 줄이 지고, 살아 있다는 데 분해 하는 얼굴.

en: Silla cannot be withstood.
If a boy is like this — what are its grown men?
Go home.

blocks.html: They put him back on his horse and point it at the Silla line. At his father’s stirrup Gwanchang does not get down.
blocks.ko: 그들은 그를 다시 말에 태워 신라 쪽으로 머리를 돌려 보낸다. 아비의 등자 곁에서 관창은 말에서 내리지 않는다.

en: I went into their midst and could not cut down their general or take their banner.
It was not because I was afraid to die.
lines: 제가 적진에 들어가 장수를 베지도, 깃발을 뽑지도 못한 것은

blocks.html: Behind the Silla line there is a well, dug that morning for the horses. He scoops the water out with both hands, drinks, and rides back the way he came. Gyebek sends him home once. He comes back.
blocks.ko: 신라 대열 뒤에 그날 아침 말들을 위해 판 우물이 있다. 그는 두 손으로 물을 떠 마시고, 왔던 길로 다시 달려간다. 계백은 그를 한 번 돌려보냈다. 그는 다시 온다.

blocks.html: The second time, Gyebek has his helmet unstrapped again, and looks at the face inside it for a while. He has looked at faces like this once already this week, in his own house, before the light was up. Then he does what he has to. He ties the head to the saddle and sends the horse back down the middle road.
blocks.ko: 두 번째로 계백은 다시 그 투구를 벗기게 하고, 안에 든 얼굴을 한참 바라본다. 이런 얼굴들은 이번 주에 이미 한 번 보았다. 제 집에서, 날이 밝기 전에. 그리고 해야 할 일을 한다. 그 머리를 안장에 매어 말을 가운데 길로 돌려보낸다.

blocks.html: Pumil holds the head up in front of the army and wipes the blood from its face with his own sleeve, so that the three armies can see whose son it is.
blocks.ko: 품일은 그 머리를 군사들 앞에 들어 올리고, 제 소매로 얼굴의 피를 닦는다. 삼군이 그것이 누구의 아들인지 볼 수 있도록.

lines: 보아라. 얼굴이 살아 있는 것 같지 않으냐.
en: Look at him. His face is as if he were alive.
He died in the king’s service. …I have nothing to regret.

blocks.label: The Fifth Clash · The Final Stand
blocks.ko: 다섯 번째 접전 · 최후의 항전

blocks.html: Nobody gives an order. The drums start on their own, one column and then the next, and fifty thousand men who could not be made to get up an hour ago are on their feet and shouting.
blocks.ko: 아무도 명령하지 않는다. 북이 저절로 울기 시작한다. 한 대열, 그다음 대열. 한 시진 전만 해도 일으켜 세울 수 없던 오만이 일어서서 함성을 지른다.

blocks.html: The Silla line, which has failed four times that morning, comes up all three roads at once and does not stop. A father’s wet sleeve is worth more than a fourth failure. The left camp on the northern road goes under first — not broken so much as used up. The right camp holds the southern road one more breath, then folds north toward the centre like a hinge that has decided to finish.
blocks.ko: 그날 아침 네 번을 실패한 신라의 대열이 세 길로 한꺼번에 올라오고, 이번엔 멈추지 않는다. 아비의 젖은 소매가 네 번째 실패보다 값이 크다. 북쪽 길의 왼쪽 진영이 먼저 가라앉는다 — 부서졌다기보다 다 쓰인 것에 가깝다. 오른쪽 진영이 남쪽 길을 한 숨 더 버티다가, 끝내기로 한 경첩처럼 북쪽 가운데로 접힌다.

blocks.html: On the Baekje side, nobody says five.
blocks.ko: 백제 쪽에서는, 아무도 다섯이라고 말하지 않는다.

blocks.html: By the fifth charge the left camp is a rumour of men. Spears shorten. Names stop answering. Seokdal stops somewhere between one tally and the next. Gyebek calls the name twice, then says the next number himself.
blocks.ko: 다섯 번째 돌격쯤이면 왼쪽 진영은 사람의 소문에 가깝다. 창이 짧아진다. 이름이 대답을 멈춘다. 석달은 셈과 셈 사이 어디쯤에서 멈춘다. 계백은 그 이름을 두 번 부르고, 다음 숫자는 제 입으로 센다.

blocks.html: Kangrim, who has been hanging in the day like unfinished weather, comes down to speaking distance.
blocks.ko: 미완의 날씨처럼 대낮에 걸려 있던 강림이, 말 닿는 거리까지 내려온다.

blocks.html: He reads the general's name three times across the field — Gyebek. Gyebek. Gyebek. — though five thousand throats have already answered.
blocks.ko: 그는 벌판을 가로질러 장군의 이름을 세 번 부른다 — 계백. 계백. 계백. — 오천의 목구멍이 이미 대답했어도.

en: General.
Your five thousand already waved. So I ask you alone.
When you killed your family to keep your oath: was that loyalty, or terror of becoming soft?
lines: 오천은 이미 손을 흔들었소. 그러니 당신에게만 묻겠소.
약조를 지키려 집안을 베었을 때: 그것이 충성이었습니까, 아니면 무르게 될까 두려운 것이었습니까?
두려움이었다면 그들에게 말하지 마시오. 더 예쁜 말을 갖게 두시오.
고을 원님이 염라대왕을 잡아 오라고 당신을 내려보냈지. 염라가 당신을 붙잡아 두었고.
en: …Loyalty.
If it was terror, do not tell them. Let them keep the prettier word.
A magistrate sent you down to arrest King Yumla. Yumla kept you.

lines: 산 사람은 그 문장을 끝까지 말하면 안 되는데.
en: …The island told you.
Living men are not supposed to finish that sentence.

lines: 위에서, 정원지기에게 물었소. 죽은 사람을 되돌릴 수 있느냐고.
en: Upstairs, I asked a gardener whether the dead can be put back.
He said it can be done.
Don’t.
…No. I didn’t think you would want it.
I asked anyway.

blocks.html: Gyebek turns his head toward the river road, toward Sabi, where nobody is coming.
blocks.ko: 계백은 고개를 강 쪽 길로 돌린다. 사비 쪽으로. 아무도 오지 않는 쪽으로.

blocks.html: A mudbank on the White River at night. A boy who has gone into the water nineteen times, and a prince in a grey hood with a jar he has not opened.
blocks.ko: 밤의 백강 진흙둑. 열아홉 번 물에 들어간 아이와, 뜯지 않은 술 단지를 든 회색 두건의 왕자.

en: Why do you do all of this?
I gave my word.

lines: 계백, 더 큰 뜻을 섬겨 보겠느냐?
en: Gyebek, would you like to serve a higher purpose?

lines: …그 이름이 마음에 드십니까, 제가 마음에 드십니까?
en: …Do you like the name, or do you like me?
…People don’t usually ask that.
Yes.

blocks.html: The field returns.
blocks.ko: 벌판이 돌아온다.

en: Your Majesty… I gave my word.

blocks.html: He says it in exactly the same words, the way you set a stone back where it was. Kangrim closes the distance.
blocks.ko: 똑같은 말이다. 돌을 제자리에 도로 놓듯이. 강림이 남은 거리를 좁힌다.

en: Walk, then. The underworld kingdom keeps better hours than Sabi ever did.
lines: 그럼 가시죠. 저승은 사비보다 시간을 잘 킵니다.

blocks.html: The man who counted everything finishes counting, and walks. The Yellow Mountain keeps the dust. The White River, downstream, opens.
blocks.ko: 모든 것을 세던 사내가 셈을 마치고, 걷는다. 황산은 먼지를 간직한다. 하류의 백강이 열린다.

blocks.html: The Silla clerks count too. Twenty-odd taken alive, two ministers among them. Nobody writes down how many of the five thousand were left to take.
blocks.ko: 신라의 서기들도 센다. 사로잡은 자 스무남은, 그 가운데 좌평 둘. 오천 가운데 사로잡을 사람이 몇이나 남아 있었는지는 아무도 적지 않는다.

blocks.html: Nobody can lead the black horse off the field. It stands over the place where he went down until the Silla grooms come at dusk with ropes, and it takes six of them, and in the night it breaks the line and goes south toward the ferry it was named for. Nobody on either side ever reports seeing it again.
blocks.ko: 아무도 그 검은 말을 들판에서 끌어내지 못한다. 말은 그가 쓰러진 자리를 지키고 서 있다가, 해 질 녘 신라 마부들이 밧줄을 들고 오자 여섯이 달라붙어야 하고, 밤이 되자 줄을 끊고 제 이름이 된 나루 쪽, 남으로 간다. 어느 편에서도 그 말을 다시 보았다는 보고는 없다.

blocks.html: The pass is open. The river is open. And in Sabi, a runner is climbing the palace steps with one word…!
blocks.ko: 고개가 열렸다. 강이 열렸다. 그리고 사비에서는, 전령 하나가 한 마디를 들고 궁궐 계단을 오른다…!

logline.en: Euija’s first move is to send the Tang a feast. The oxen come back untouched.
logline.ko: 의자의 첫 수는 당나라 진영에 잔칫상을 보내는 것이다. 소들은 손도 대지 않은 채 돌아온다.
