images.alt: Poster key art: King Muyeol rides the white heavenly horse through the smoke of fallen Sabi, reining it in at the broken gate
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; crowns, antlers, wings and heads stay well inside the central band; no title, no lettering. Smoke-black dusk at the broken gate of Sabi on the Baengma river bluff; Baekje giwa halls burning low in the distance. Worm’s-eye from the ash. INTERACTION: King Muyeol rides bareback on the wingless white heavenly horse Chunma, reining it in hard at the gate; the horse rears half up, forelegs high, and he leans forward along its neck with one hand flat on its shoulder to steady it, his face grim and spent rather than triumphant. Cloud streamers off its hooves curl into the smoke. CHUNMA HAS NO WINGS: a wingless white heavenly horse, bare white back and shoulders, nothing feathered anywhere; it rides the air on curling cloud-and-flame streamers trailing from its legs. Firelight from the burning halls (#D8258C magenta-orange) is the one key on his crown, face and the horse’s white chest; the gate and the sky are ink-black smoke. Ash flakes as painted bokeh. STYLE: HEEWON STYLE, more painterly, with hints of Korean ink painting — Korean webtoon figures (clean ink linework, simplified expressive faces matching the attached portrait, watercolor-washed) inside a hand-painted world of watercolor and oil with traditional sumukhwa ink: splashed-ink storm clouds, bold dry calligraphic brush strokes in manes, fur, feathers, robes and grass, ink bleeding into wet wash, small ink splatters and drips near the frame edges, patches of bare rice paper where the edges dissolve; oil glazes only deepen the darks, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. Movie-poster key art: bold iconic silhouette, the two subjects large and close, one dramatic low angle, one bright break of light behind them, big dark masses, few hues plus one accent, film-poster drama but NO text, NO title, NO credits, NO logo, NO seal stamp. Not photoreal, not 3D. No glow aura, no halo, no emissive outline — the accent colour is real light. One of each named person. No watermark. CANON — KING MUYEOL — FACE and garments from attached /ch_muyeol.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Slim and elegant; shoulder-length loose black hair parted in the middle; thin moustache and goatee stubble; amused eyes, small knowing smile. Dress: Magenta-crimson silk po with a charcoal sash, dark layered collar. Silk even on campaign. Now: King Muyeol (stage portrait): royal robes and crown; heavier, tired eyes. Demeanor: Diplomat and strategist: talks with his hands, smiles while calculating, never shouts; half-lidded watchful eyes. #D8258C as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: front-line armored warrior pose; shouting battle face; katana. | CHUNMA (천마, hyukgose's heavenly horse, guardian of Silla) — attached board /obj_chunma.png: WINGLESS white heavenly horse in the Cheonmachong saddle-flap style: long arched neck, streaming white mane and tail, legs flung out in a flying gallop. It has NO WINGS — no feathers, no bird wings, nothing growing from the shoulders. It rides the sky on curling cloud-and-flame streamers trailing from its legs and chest, as on the painted birch-bark flap. Divine render: numinous through scale and atmosphere, never a glow outline. Kneels and cries beside the purple egg at Najeong, sees men approach, neighs and rises into the sky. | PLACE Sabi (사비 (부여)) — attached board /pl_sabi_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Sabi palace on the Baengma river bluffs; Baekje giwa halls and pavilions. | HORSE ANATOMY is a centrepiece: the whole horse body reads clearly and beautifully — arched neck, deep chest, sloping shoulder, round haunch, clean long legs in a correct gait, every muscle modelled by the one hard key with a bright edge along the topline and deep shadow under the belly; the horse is never cropped into a blob, never hidden behind dust, never stiff like a toy; mane and tail as flowing painted strokes; the coat colour exactly as the board. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS are a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST room (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt) painted in that same wash-and-glaze: a warm umber-to-black ground, walls, timber, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft with soft sfumato falloff — the webtoon figures are set INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. blocks.html: The runner has one word. Euija makes him say it twice.
blocks.ko: 전령이 가져온 말은 한 마디다. 의자는 그 말을 두 번 하게 한다.

blocks.html: He has run all night, and he falls on the palace steps instead of kneeling. The court hears about the Yellow Mountain Fields before the king does. Courts always do.
blocks.ko: 밤새 달려온 전령은 무릎을 꿇는 대신 궁궐 계단에 쓰러진다. 조정은 임금보다 먼저 황산벌 소식을 듣는다. 조정은 늘 그렇다.

blocks.speaker: Runner
en: Hwangsan, Majesty.
Again.

blocks.speaker: Runner
en: Hwangsan. The Yellow Mountain Fields.

lines: 그래서? 몇이나 돌아왔느냐. 얼굴 말고, 숫자를 대라.
en: And? How many came back? Don’t give me a face, boy. Give me a number.

blocks.speaker: Runner
en: …There’s nobody left to count them, Majesty.
The man who counts—
Yes. I know who counts.

blocks.html: Euija sits down on the top step, in front of everyone, which kings do not do. The court waits for an order. For the first time in twenty years he does not have one ready. So he reaches for the next thing he owns, which is an idea.
blocks.ko: 의자는 모두가 보는 앞에서 맨 윗계단에 주저앉는다. 임금이 해서는 안 되는 일이다. 조정은 명을 기다린다. 스무 해 만에 처음으로 그에게는 준비된 명이 없다. 그래서 그다음으로 가진 것에 손을 뻗는다. 꾀다.

blocks.html: Before noon a second runner comes up the road from the river mouth, muddy to the waist, with what is left of the river-mouth line behind him.
blocks.ko: 정오가 되기 전, 두 번째 전령이 강어귀 길을 따라 올라온다. 허리까지 진흙투성이고, 그 뒤로 강어귀 방어선의 남은 자들이 따라온다.

lines: …바다에서 오래 있었지. 배에서 내린 놈들은 늘 배가 고파.
배부른 놈은 성을 안 태운다. 먹여라. 원하는 건 그다음에 얘기하자.
en: …They’ve been at sea. Men off boats are always hungry.
Nobody burns a city on a full stomach. Feed them. Then we’ll talk about what they want.

blocks.html: So his first move is to send the Tang camp a feast: oxen, wine, three cartloads of rice cakes. The court is told this is diplomacy.
blocks.ko: 그래서 그의 첫 수는 당의 진영에 잔칫상을 보내는 것이다. 소, 술, 떡 세 수레. 조정에는 이것이 외교라고 알린다.

blocks.caption: Two arrows, one capital, and a king who has decided the answer is oxen.
blocks.ko: 화살 둘, 도성 하나, 그리고 답은 소 떼라고 정한 왕.

blocks.html: The oxen come back that afternoon, untouched, with the drovers walking behind them.
blocks.ko: 황소들은 그날 오후, 손도 안 댄 채, 몰이꾼들을 뒤에 달고 되돌아온다.

blocks.label: The Red Fowl’s Tent
blocks.ko: 주작의 군막

blocks.html: The Silla army reaches the Tang camp two days late. The Red Fowl has the Silla supply officer, Kim Munyeong, dragged to his tent gate. They open his collar for the sword.
blocks.ko: 신라군이 약속보다 이틀 늦게 당의 진영에 닿는다. 주작은 신라의 군량 장교 김문영을 군막 문 앞으로 끌어낸다. 칼 받을 목깃을 풀게 한다.

lines: 열흘. 사비 남쪽. 두 번 말했다.
en: The tenth day. South of Sabi. I said it twice.
Take his head. Then we can start.
zh: 七月十日，泗沘之南。我說了兩遍。
zhLatn: Qīyuè shí rì, Sìbì zhī nán. Wǒ shuō le liǎng biàn.
Zhǎn le. Ránhòu kāishǐ.

blocks.html: Kim Yushin walks into the tent with a battle-axe in his hand.
blocks.ko: 김유신이 손에 큰 도끼를 들고 군막 안으로 걸어 들어온다.

lines: 늦었다는 걸 죄로 삼겠다면, 죄 없이 욕을 받을 수는 없소. 당군과 먼저 결판을 내고, 백제는 그다음에 치겠소.
en: The general did not see the Yellow Mountain Fields.
If you mean to punish us for being late, I will not be shamed for a crime I did not commit. I will fight the Tang first, and Baekje after.

blocks.hanja: 乃杖鉞軍門 怒髮如植 其腰間寶劍自躍出鞘
blocks.html: Then he stood at the camp gate leaning on his axe; his angry hair stood up like planted stakes, and the precious sword at his waist leapt of itself from its scabbard.
blocks.ko: 이에 도끼를 짚고 군문에 서니, 성난 머리털이 꽂아 세운 듯하고, 허리에 찬 보검이 저절로 칼집에서 뛰쳐나왔다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 5, Silla Annals — King Muyeol, yr. 7 (660), seventh month

blocks.html: The Red Fowl’s second-in-command steps on his commander’s foot.
blocks.ko: 주작의 부장이 제 장군의 발을 슬쩍 밟는다.

blocks.speaker: Dong Baoliang
en: (low) The Silla army is about to turn on us, General.
zhLatn: (Dīshēng) Xīnluó bīng jiāng yǒu biàn yě.

blocks.html: Kim Munyeong’s collar is closed again. Nobody in the tent mentions the date for the rest of the war.
blocks.ko: 김문영의 목깃이 다시 여며진다. 그 전쟁이 끝날 때까지 군막 안의 누구도 날짜 이야기를 꺼내지 않는다.

blocks.html: Next morning the allies come at the city together, the Tang up from their camp in the south, Silla down the road from the east. Baekje puts everything it has left on the plain between them. Euija watches from the wall.
blocks.ko: 이튿날 아침 두 동맹군이 함께 도성으로 온다. 당군은 남쪽 진영에서 올라오고, 신라군은 동쪽 길로 내려온다. 백제는 남은 것을 전부 그 사이 벌판에 내놓는다. 의자는 성벽 위에서 지켜본다.

lines: 저거 봐라. 남은 놈들이 전부 한 벌판에 있다.
하… 세어 주지 마라. 나도 셀 줄 안다.
en: Look at that. Every man I had left, on one plain.
Ha… Don’t count them for me. I can count.

blocks.label: Night Flight
blocks.ko: 야반도주

blocks.html: Euija leaves Sabi at night for Bear Fortress, upriver to the north-east, with fewer men than he expected to have.
blocks.ko: 의자는 밤에 사비를 떠나 강을 거슬러 북동쪽, 웅진성으로 향한다. 데리고 갈 수 있는 사람은 생각보다 적었다.

blocks.html: On the river he sits in the bow and says nothing for a long time. The boatmen will remember it, because nobody had ever seen him do that before.
blocks.ko: 강 위에서 그는 뱃머리에 앉아 오래도록 아무 말이 없다. 사공들은 그걸 기억할 것이다. 그가 그러는 걸 본 사람이 아무도 없었으니까.

lines: 성충이 그랬지. 고개를 막아라. 강어귀를 막아라. 옥에서, 다 떨리는 손으로 적어 보냈다.
이걸 봤으면 좋아했을 게다. 꼴 보기 싫게 굴었겠지.
en: Seongchung said hold the pass. Hold the river mouth. Wrote it out for me from his cell, in a hand that was going.
I put him in that cell. …Ha.
He’d love this. He’d be unbearable.

blocks.label: The City Gate
blocks.ko: 사비 성문

blocks.html: Back in Sabi, the king’s second son, Tae, puts on a crown the next morning and means to fight. His nephews don’t. They go down the wall on a rope with their households, and half the city follows them down it.
blocks.ko: 사비에서는 이튿날 아침 임금의 둘째 아들 태가 스스로 관을 쓰고 싸우겠다고 한다. 조카들은 생각이 다르다. 그들은 식솔을 데리고 밧줄을 타고 성벽을 내려가고, 성의 절반이 그 밧줄을 따라 내려간다.

blocks.html: The crown prince comes out of the gate. Chunbok walks a careful pace behind him. Bupmin has the prince knelt in the dirt before his horse, and spits in his face.
blocks.ko: 태자가 성문을 나온다. 천복이 조심스레 한 걸음 뒤에서 따른다. 법민은 태자를 제 말 앞 흙바닥에 꿇리고, 그 얼굴에 침을 뱉는다.

lines: 내 누이. 고타소. 네 아비의 장수가 대야성에서 죽이고 옥 바닥에 묻었다.
열여덟 해를 그걸 안고 살았다. 그 이름을 말할 때는 나를 봐라.
en: Look at me.
My sister. Gotaso. Your father’s general killed her at Daeya and buried her under a prison floor.
Eighteen years I’ve carried that. Look at me when I say her name.

blocks.html: Yung lies flat on the ground and says nothing.
blocks.ko: 융은 땅에 엎드려 아무 말도 하지 않는다.

blocks.html: It was Chunbok who opened the gate. He would like that understood as a favour.
blocks.ko: 성문을 연 것은 춘복이다. 그는 그것이 호의로 받아들여지기를 바란다.

lines: 장군들께서도 헤아리시겠지만, 성문은 백성을 위하여, 그리고 전적으로 그 뜻에 따라—
en: As the generals will surely appreciate, the gate was opened for the sake of the people, and in full accordance with—

blocks.label: Falling Flower Rock
blocks.ko: 낙화암

blocks.html: When the gate opens the palace women do not wait to be counted. They go out the back of the palace and up the ridge path to the cliff above the White River, where the rock drops straight into the water, and the soldiers coming up behind them find nobody at the top.
blocks.ko: 성문이 열리자 궁의 여인들은 세어지기를 기다리지 않는다. 궁 뒤로 빠져나가 백마강 위 벼랑까지 능선 길을 오른다. 바위가 물속으로 곧장 떨어지는 곳이다. 뒤따라 올라온 군사들은 꼭대기에서 아무도 찾지 못한다.

blocks.html: The stories that gave Euija three thousand women give them this cliff as well, and three thousand is the number they say went over it, their skirts opening on the way down like petals. Nobody who was there wrote down how many it really was. There was no one left on the cliff to count.
blocks.ko: 의자에게 삼천 궁녀를 붙여 준 이야기들은 이 벼랑도 그들에게 준다. 그 위에서 떨어진 것이 삼천이었다고, 떨어지는 동안 치마가 꽃잎처럼 벌어졌다고 말한다. 그 자리에 있던 누구도 실제로 몇이었는지 적지 않았다. 벼랑 위에는 셀 사람이 남아 있지 않았다.

blocks.html: Two of them go together, holding hands. They are the two who sat in a prince’s garden with a go board and a jar of wine, a lifetime ago. Nobody counts them. Nobody has counted them for years. It had been two, once, and a joke, and a modest number a man was proud of.
blocks.ko: 그중 둘은 손을 잡고 함께 간다. 아주 오래전, 바둑판과 술 단지를 놓고 왕자의 후원에 앉아 있던 그 둘이다. 아무도 세지 않는다. 여러 해 동안 아무도 세지 않았다. 한때는 둘이었고, 우스개였고, 한 사내가 자랑스러워하던 소박한 수효였다.

en: He’ll reach for us today, like yesterday.
He isn’t here today. / …But the body remembers.

blocks.html: The rock is called the Falling Flowers afterwards, Nakhwaam, which is a kind way of saying it, and Baekje’s last invention.
blocks.ko: 뒷날 그 바위는 낙화암, 꽃이 떨어진 바위라 불린다. 부드럽게 이르는 말이고, 백제가 마지막으로 지어낸 것이다.

blocks.label: Ungjin
blocks.ko: 웅진성

blocks.html: Bear Fortress belongs to the king the way a borrowed house belongs to a guest. The Ye family has held it for four generations. Ye Sikjin gives the king his own rooms, and goes up on the wall every morning to count the Tang sails on the river.
blocks.ko: 웅진성이 왕의 것인 건 빌린 집이 손님의 것인 것과 같다. 예씨 집안이 네 대째 지켜 온 성이다. 예식진은 왕에게 제 방을 내주고, 아침마다 성벽에 올라 강 위의 당나라 돛을 센다.

lines: 식진아! 좋은 놈. 네 할아비가 내 할아비 위해 이 바위를 지켰지?
다시 지키는 거다. 주작이 언제까지 진흙탕에 앉아 있겠냐.
en: Sikjin! Good man. Your grandfather held this rock for my grandfather, eh?
We’ll hold it again. The Red Fowl can’t sit in the mud forever.
My grandfather held it, Majesty.
…For whoever was king.

blocks.html: The first morning he counts forty sails. The second morning, sixty-two. He writes both numbers on the wall in charcoal, because that is what he does with numbers.
blocks.ko: 첫날 아침 그는 돛 마흔 개를 센다. 이튿날 아침에는 예순둘. 그는 두 숫자를 숯으로 성벽에 적어 둔다. 숫자를 보면 그렇게 하는 사람이다.

lines: 예순둘? 하! 뱃전에 대고 토하는 놈들이 예순두 척이로구나.
식진아, 멀미하는 소로는 밭을 못 간다. 하하!
술 가져오너라. 좋은 잔으로. 수비대 잔 말고.
en: Sixty-two? Ha! Sixty-two boatloads of men throwing up over the side.
Sikjin, you can’t plough with a seasick ox. Ha!
Bring wine. The good cups. Not the garrison ones.
The good cups are in Sabi, Majesty.
…I’ll bring the garrison ones.

blocks.html: On the third day a boatman comes up the river with Sabi still on his face. Ye Sikjin hears him out alone, on the wall. Then he takes him to the king, because that is the order things are done in.
blocks.ko: 사흗날, 사비에서 본 것이 아직 얼굴에 남은 사공 하나가 강을 거슬러 올라온다. 예식진은 성벽 위에서 혼자 그 말을 끝까지 듣는다. 그런 다음 그를 왕에게 데려간다. 일은 그 순서로 하는 것이니까.

lines: 태가 왕관을 썼다고? 그놈은 호박에 갓도 못 씌우는 놈이다!
…좋다. 꿇은 아들도 아들이지. 성을 되찾으면 한 달은 마당에 세워 두마. 하하!
en: Tae put on a crown? That boy couldn’t get a hat on a pumpkin!
And Yung… knelt.
…Fine. A son on his knees is still a son. When I take the city back, he can stand in the yard for a month. Ha!

blocks.html: That night his elder brother comes in by the river gate. Ye Gun is the family’s talker. He has been downriver all day, he says, looking at the weather. It has rained since noon. He comes back dry.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 형이 강 쪽 문으로 들어온다. 예군은 집안에서 말을 맡은 사람이다. 종일 강 아래로 날씨를 보러 갔었다고 한다. 정오부터 비가 왔다. 그는 젖지 않은 채 돌아온다.

lines: 그 장군은 진흙 얘기를 날씨 얘기하듯 하더라. 진흙은 젖은 길일 뿐이라나.
그리고 이 성에 방이 몇 개냐고 묻더군. 아우한테 물어봐야 한다고 했다. 세는 건 너니까.
en: That general talks about mud the way other men talk about weather. Mud is just wet road, apparently.
And he asked how many rooms this fortress has. I said I’d have to ask my brother. You’re the one who counts.
Thirty-nine, brother.
Counting the king’s.
And men?
Depends on the room.

lines: 수비대 술도 마시다 보니 정이 드는구나, 식진아!
끝나면 너는 조정으로 올라온다. 진짜 자리로. 앞줄로. 배 세는 짓은 그만이다.
얼굴이 왜 그러냐? 농담 아니다. 마셔라!
en: Garrison wine! It grows on you, Sikjin!
When this is over, you’re coming to court. A real seat. Front row. No more counting boats.
What’s that face? That wasn’t a joke. Drink!
You honour me, Majesty.
…Which seat?

lines: 하! 들었느냐? 어느 자리냐니! 아무 데나 골라라.
en: Ha! Listen to him. Which seat! Take your pick.
I’ve got forty-one of them.

blocks.html: That night he opens the drawer. The list is where he left it. Forty-one names. None of them his. He reads it a third time, being careful with numbers, and puts it back. He does not close the drawer. One day a Tang stonecutter will carve his father and grandfather into Baekje’s first rank. Neither of them was ever asked to court. Tombstones are generous that way.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 그는 서랍을 연다. 명단은 넣어 둔 그대로다. 이름 마흔하나. 그의 이름은 없다. 숫자에 꼼꼼한 사람이라, 그는 세 번째로 읽고 도로 넣는다. 서랍은 닫지 않는다. 언젠가 당나라 석공 하나가 그의 아버지와 할아버지를 백제의 일품으로 새겨 줄 것이다. 둘 다 조정에 한 번 불려 간 적 없는 사람들이다. 묘비란 그렇게 너그럽다.

blocks.html: On the fifth night he comes into the king’s rooms with his brother and twenty men, and the king understands before anyone speaks.
blocks.ko: 닷새째 밤, 그는 형과 장정 스물을 데리고 왕의 방으로 들어온다. 왕은 누가 입을 열기도 전에 알아차린다.

en: …Which seat. Ha.
The list. You read the list.

lines: 세 번 읽었습니다, 폐하. 숫자는 조심해서 봐야 하니까요.
en: Three times, Majesty. I am careful with numbers.

lines: 사람은 자기가 믿고 싶은 것의 증거는 절대 검사하지 않아.
내가 한 말이다. 열아홉 해 전에. 너 같은 놈들로 꽉 찬 전각에서.
…뭘 보느냐? 밧줄은 좋은 걸로 가져와라. 수비대 것 말고.
en: Nobody inspects the evidence for a thing they already want to believe.
I said that, you know. Nineteen years ago, in a hall full of men like you.
…Well? Bring the good rope, at least. Not the garrison one.

blocks.html: By morning the king is on the river again, bound, going back down it toward the Red Fowl’s tent. The Ye brothers watch the boat from the wall.
blocks.ko: 아침이 되자 임금은 묶인 채 다시 강 위에 있다. 이번에는 강을 따라 내려가, 주작의 군막으로. 예씨 형제가 성벽에서 그 배를 지켜본다.

en: You can stop counting sails now.
…One more.
Going down.

blocks.html: His name was Sikjin, a man of Ungcheon in Baekje. His grandfather, Minister Yeda, and his father, Minister Saseon, both held the first rank of that vassal court. … Upright from birth and early marked for righteousness, he read the wind in a foreign land and went toward the sun in Chang’an.
blocks.ko: 공의 휘는 식진이요, 백제 웅천 사람이다. 할아버지 좌평 예다와 아버지 좌평 사선은 모두 번국 관직 정일품이었다. … 일찍이 곧은 법도를 타고나 의로운 절개를 드러내니, 이역에서 바람을 점치고 장안의 해를 향해 나아갔다.
blocks.hanja: 公諱寔進百濟熊川人也 祖佐平譽多父佐平思善竝蕃官正一品 … 夙禀貞規早標義節占風異域就日長安
blocks.source: Epitaph of Ye Sikjin (禰寔進墓誌), Tang, 672

blocks.html: Back in the palace, the winners want their wine poured.
blocks.ko: 궁에서는 이긴 쪽이 술을 따르라 한다.

blocks.label: The Victory Feast
blocks.ko: 승전 잔치

blocks.html: Chunchu finally arrives at the scene. He makes Euija pour his wine, and the Tang general’s beside it.
blocks.ko: 마침내 춘추가 당도한다. 그는 의자에게 제 잔에, 그리고 그 옆 당 장수의 잔에 술을 따르게 한다.

lines: 내가 너를 잡아들이려고 얼마나 고생했는지 아나?
거의 내 인생을 썼다, 이 자식아.
en: So… you are Euija.
The one who started all of this… Buyeo Euija.
Do you know what it cost me to bring you in?
Nearly my whole life, you bastard.

blocks.html: A cup is put into Euija’s hands, and he is made to pour.
blocks.ko: 의자의 손에 잔이 들려지고, 그는 술을 따르도록 강요당한다.

blocks.html: He pours for the Red Fowl first, slowly, with a small host’s bow, and only then turns to the Silla king.
blocks.ko: 그는 먼저 주작의 잔에 따른다. 천천히, 주인이 손님에게 하듯 살짝 고개를 숙이며. 그러고 나서야 신라 임금 쪽으로 돈다.

lines: 제일 멀리서 온 손님부터 따르는 법이지. 그게 예의다.
en: Guests who came furthest are served first. That’s manners.
You live next door. You can wait.
…Do you know what I said to Gesomun, once.
“I do not fear a man who kneels to another man.”

lines: 그 말을 들은 사람이 바로 나였으니까.
en: I know.
I was the man he said it about.
…And so — who is kneeling today?

lines: 나다. 이 잔 하나 받으려고 황제 앞에 무릎을 꿇었고, 다음 잔을 위해서라면 또 꿇을 게다.
무릎 꿇은 사람은 다시 일어난다, 의자. 너는 늘 그 대목을 안 보고 자리를 떴지.
en: I am. I knelt to an emperor for this cup, and I would kneel again for the next one.
A man who kneels gets up afterwards, Euija. You never stayed to watch that part.

lines: 너도 언젠가는 누군가 앞에 꿇을 거다.
en: Chunchu…
One day you will kneel before someone too.
Take this man away.

blocks.html: There is one more prisoner. He has been kept for the end of the feast, the way a host keeps back the dish he cares about.
blocks.ko: 포로가 하나 더 있다. 잔치 끝까지 남겨 둔 자다. 주인이 정말 아끼는 음식을 마지막까지 남겨 두듯이.

blocks.html: Gumil is older. The yellow sleeve is gone. Eighteen years in Baekje have not taught him to stand up straight, and they have not taught him to stop talking.
blocks.ko: 검일은 늙었다. 누런 소매도 없다. 백제에서 보낸 열여덟 해는 그에게 허리 펴는 법도, 입 다무는 법도 가르쳐 주지 않았다.

lines: 저 양반한테 뭐가 들었냐고 묻는 거 다 들었어. 해 봐. 나한테도.
en: Ah~ so the father came after all.
I heard you ask him what it cost. Go on, then. Tell me.
From the start. All of it. Don’t leave any out.
No.

lines: 아니래? 아이고~ 신라 제일가는 말쟁이가, 아니래.
그 성 놈들 다 쓰레기였어. 당신 사위가 내 마누라를 데려갔고, 나머지는 구경만—
en: No? Aigo~ the great talker of Silla, and he says no.
Everyone in that fortress was trash, you know. Your son-in-law took my wife, and the rest of them watched—
My daughter was in that fortress.

blocks.html: Gumil opens his mouth, and for once in eighteen years nothing comes out of it.
blocks.ko: 검일은 입을 연다. 그리고 열여덟 해 만에 처음으로, 아무 말도 나오지 않는다.

lines: 너는 나한테서 이야기 한 줄 못 얻는다. 네 이야기는 아무도 하지 않을 게다.
en: You’ll get no story from me. Nobody is going to tell yours.
Take him down to the river.

blocks.html: They put him to death on the riverbank before the wine is finished. Chunchu does not go down to watch. He drinks the cup Euija poured him instead, slowly, the way you finish a thing that took twenty years to pour.
blocks.ko: 술이 다 비기 전에 그들은 강가에서 그를 죽인다. 춘추는 내려가 보지 않는다. 대신 의자가 따라 준 잔을 마신다. 천천히. 따르는 데 스무 해가 걸린 것을 비우듯이.

blocks.label: The Pagoda
blocks.ko: 정림사 탑

blocks.html: A month later the Tang carve their victory into a stone pagoda. They put it low, where anyone walking round has to read it. It calls the conquest a deliverance. About Baekje’s king it says:
blocks.ko: 한 달 뒤, 당은 돌탑에 제 승리를 새긴다. 탑을 도는 사람이면 누구든 읽을 수밖에 없는 낮은 자리다. 비문은 정복을 구원이라 부른다. 백제의 임금에 대해서는 이렇게 적는다.

blocks.hanja: 外棄直臣 內信妖婦
blocks.html: Abroad he cast off his upright ministers; at home he trusted a bewitching woman.
blocks.ko: 밖으로는 곧은 신하를 버리고, 안으로는 요사한 여인을 믿었다.
blocks.source: Datang ping Baekje guo beiming (大唐平百濟國碑銘), carved on the five-storey stone pagoda of Jeongnimsa, Buyeo (660)

en: Harmonized.

blocks.html: Then the Tang divide Baekje into five commanderies, with a Tang governor over each and Baekje men under them. Nothing in the arrangement is labelled Silla.
blocks.ko: 그러고 나서 당은 백제를 다섯 도독부로 나누고, 저마다 당의 도독을, 그 아래에 백제 사람들을 앉힌다. 그 배치 어디에도 신라라는 이름표는 없다.

lines: 아버님. 평양 이남과 백제 땅 전부. 그 말들 앞에서 그렇게 말했다고, 아버님이 그러셨잖습니까.
en: Father. Everything south of Pyongyang and the whole of Baekje. He said it in front of the horses. You told me.

lines: 천자의 말이 곧 문서라고도 했다. 붓을 챙겨 갈 걸 그랬어.
en: I did.
He also said an emperor’s word was the writing. I should have brought a brush.

blocks.label: Two Camps
blocks.ko: 두 진영

blocks.html: In the Tang lines the Red Fowl’s staff officers are seen pacing out the distance to the Silla camp, which is not a thing allies measure. In the Silla council a man proposes that their soldiers put on Baekje clothes and fall on the Tang by night.
blocks.ko: 당의 진에서 주작의 참모들이 신라 진영까지의 거리를 걸음으로 재는 것이 보인다. 동맹끼리 잴 거리는 아니다. 신라의 군의에서 누군가가, 우리 군사에게 백제 옷을 입혀 밤에 당을 치자고 한다.

lines: 그러나 주인이 발을 밟으면 뭅니다. 개도 그쯤은 압니다.
en: A dog fears its master, Majesty.
But step on its foot and it bites. Even a dog knows that much.

blocks.html: Word of the conversation reaches the Red Fowl’s tent, as it was meant to.
blocks.ko: 그 대화는 의도한 대로 주작의 군막에 전해진다.

blocks.html: A month later the Red Fowl sails home with Euija, his sons and twelve thousand captives. He leaves ten thousand men to hold the city. Beside them sits a Silla army that has stopped smiling.
blocks.ko: 한 달 뒤, 주작은 의자와 그 아들들, 포로 만 이천을 싣고 귀국길에 오른다. 성에는 군사 만 명을 남긴다. 그 곁에는 더는 웃어 주지 않는 신라군이 있다.

blocks.html: Across the sea, a confession is waiting for Euija. It is already written, in a lovely hand. It only needs his name…!
blocks.ko: 바다 건너, 의자 앞으로 자백서 한 장이 기다린다. 고운 글씨로 이미 다 써 두었다. 이름 하나만 비어 있다…!

logline.en: In the Tang capital, a confession is already written. There’s a space at the bottom for his name.
logline.ko: 당나라 도성에는 자백서가 이미 쓰여 있다. 맨 아래에 그의 이름을 쓸 자리가 비어 있다.

images.prompt: 2:1 drama power shot, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop. HIGH ANGLE OVER THE SHOULDER of THE THIRD EMPEROR on the throne dais: sharp dark foreground of his shoulder, black futou cap edge and yellow robe, lit warm by a gilt-bronze lamp-tree beside him. Below and far down the hall at true scale, KING EUIJA kneels alone on the polished dark stone floor, head up, glaring at the throne — one plain undyed WHITE robe, barefoot, long grey-streaked hair LOOSE over his shoulders, no headband, no topknot — two Tang guards with halberds a step behind him. Two lines of officials in dark robes and black caps face inward along the aisle between vermilion columns. The hall doors are open behind Euija: HARD COLD BLUE BACKLIGHT floods in around him, his long shadow stretching up the aisle toward the dais, his white robe and loose hair edged with cold light, the only pale shape in the hall. Incense haze makes the door light visible; candles along the columns reflect in the floor. Colour contrast: warm gold dais vs cold blue doorway. No writing. CANON — KING EUIJA — FACE ONLY from attached /ch_buyeo_euija.png; ignore the portrait's clothing, headgear, jewelry and hair styling — dress exactly as "Now" below (invent a new pose). Now: PRISONER IN THE TANG CAPITAL: broad bearded old king, heavy brows, cynical eyes. One plain undyed WHITE hemp robe and nothing else — no headband, no topknot, no crown, no gold, no crimson, no armor, no belt ornament, barefoot; his long black hair streaked grey hangs LOOSE and unbound past his shoulders; beard unkempt. Demeanor: Licensed wit: drinks, smirks, slumps on the throne, speaks in polished aphorisms. Fatalist. #e08a2e as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: heroic battle pose; smiling innocence. | THE THIRD EMPEROR — FACE and garments from attached /ch_gaozong.png (face only; invent a new pose). #b8935a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | PLACE Chang’an (장안) — attached board /pl_daming_night.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Tang palace of Chang'an, drawn from the Daming Palace (大明宮) site and reconstruction models: Hanyuan Hall's concave ensemble — an eleven-bay hall with a double-eaved hipped roof of dark grey tiles and curled owl-tail ridge ends (chiwei), red columns, white plaster walls, lattice windows, raised on three tiers of rammed-earth terraces faced in ochre-red plaster and edged with white stone balustrades; the Dragon Tail Way ramps folding up the terraces; forward on each side the Xiangluan and Qifeng que-towers (three stepped pavilions on tall battered grey-brick piers) joined to the hall by long roofed corridors; a vast paved square below, entered through the five-doored Danfeng Gate. Wide low Tang proportions, deep eaves on massive bracket sets. Tang palette is VERMILION and WHITE (red columns, white walls); roofs are black-grey tile trimmed with green-glazed ridge and eave tiles (a little yellow and blue tricolour glaze); balustrade posts painted red, blue and green. YELLOW belongs to the emperor's robe; gold is gilt-bronze fittings, lamp-trees and firelight on vermilion. Interiors: dark polished stone floors, rows of vermilion columns, gauze hangings, a raised dais with a painted screen behind the throne. Never the Forbidden City, never all-yellow glazed roofs, never the modern reconstruction or a city skyline. Mood: Staged like a Chinese historical drama (Legend of the Demon Cat, The Longest Day in Chang'an) but lit as full Heewon tenebrism: night or blue hour; ONE dominant hard key per shot — a backlight through open doors or lattice, or one lamp-tree — and 75% of the frame crushed black with no fill; colour contrast — gold-yellow flame highlights against cool blue-green in the few lit shadows; the other flames (lamp-trees, silk lanterns with no writing, braziers) are small points and round bokeh IN the black, never lighting the room evenly; red lantern light through lattice as one pattern on the floor; incense haze only inside the key shaft; polished dark floors reflecting the flames. Staged like a drama, at true human scale: camera at eye or knee height on a dolly or crane; court officials in two lines facing inward along the central aisle with tablets; banquet tables in two long facing rows with dancers in the centre and the emperor on the dais at the head; exteriors are real-scale terraces and corridors, the hall large but never a fantasy fortress. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER canvas, composed like a Romanticist master painting. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is painted with European old-master technique — Renaissance and Baroque oil (Titian, Rembrandt, Tiepolo, Turner): visible broken-colour brushwork, skies scumbled from short loaded dabs, layered glazes in the darks, sfumato edges, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlights — over watercolor wet-in-wet blooms, pigment granulation and faint paper grain; edges of the frame dissolve into paint. LAYOUT is Romanticism (Delacroix, Géricault, Friedrich, Goya, Turner): heroic diagonal or pyramid composition, small figures against a sublime storm sky or vast field, extreme foreshortening (worm’s-eye from the dirt or straight down from above), one break in the clouds or one shaft as the key. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength (Caravaggio, Rembrandt, night-interior cinema): an extreme value range — inky blacks right beside small near-white highlights, almost no middle grey; 70–80% of the frame in deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo and black); ONE hard directional key (a lamp, a single cloud-break, a low sun shaft, firelight) carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock: anamorphic movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain. A CAMERA in a real Korean place — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D archviz, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portrait — NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: dutch, crane, worm’s-eye, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key + long shadows — not even daylight wash. ICONIC MINIMAL: ONE architectural device a lens can see; empty negative space; tiny figures or lower-third; the world stays in the shot. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor portrait garments gold. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Fatalist. #e08a2e as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: heroic battle pose; smiling innocence. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: An empire is not finished with a king until he has signed something.
blocks.ko: 제국은 왕에게서 서명 하나를 받아 내기 전까지는, 그 왕과 끝난 게 아니다.

blocks.html: In Chang’an, on the first morning of winter, Euija is brought forth before the Third Emperor.
blocks.ko: 장안, 겨울의 첫 아침. 의자가 세 번째 황제 앞에 끌려 나온다.

blocks.html: First, paperwork. A palace clerk hands the prisoner a confession, already written out in a fair hand. There is a space at the bottom for his name.
blocks.ko: 먼저 서류다. 궁의 서기가 포로에게 자백서를 건넨다. 단정한 글씨로 이미 다 써 놓았다. 맨 아래에 이름 쓸 자리만 비어 있다.

blocks.speaker: Tang clerk
en: Aloud, please. Clearly. The scribes are taking it down.
lines: 소리 내어 읽으시오. 또박또박. 사관들이 받아 적고 있소.
zh: 請高聲宣讀，字字清楚。史官在記。
zhLatn: Qǐng gāoshēng xuāndú, zìzì qīngchu. Shǐguān zài jì.

en: ‘I, the criminal Euija, having been liberated by the Great Tang—’
Liberated. Hm. So that’s what that was.
‘—confess with gratitude that without the Great Tang there would be no New Baekje—’
There isn’t one. You burned it.
‘—and resolve to serve the Emperor for ten thousand years.’
Ten thousand? I’m sixty. Ambitious fellow, your clerk.
lines: ‘—대당이 없었다면 새 백제도 없었음을 감사히 자백하며—’
만세? 내가 예순이다. 야심 한번 크구먼, 너희 서기.

en: It’s a bad story. Nobody’s afraid of anything, there’s no villain, and the hero is a building.
Who wrote this? I’ve done better drunk.
lines: 형편없는 이야기다. 겁나는 것도 없고, 악당도 없고, 주인공이 건물이야.
누가 썼냐? 난 취해서도 이보단 잘 썼다.

blocks.speaker: Tang clerk
en: Your name, please. Here.
zhLatn: Qǐng shǔmíng. Zhèlǐ.

blocks.html: He signs in a hand so large the name runs off the edge of the paper, and gives it back. The clerk files it without looking. A confession only needs a name, and has never much minded whose.
blocks.ko: 그는 이름이 종이 끝을 넘어갈 만큼 큼직하게 서명하고 돌려준다. 서기는 보지도 않고 철해 둔다. 자백서에 필요한 건 이름 하나뿐이고, 그게 누구 이름인지는 늘 별로 상관하지 않았다.

blocks.html: Eleventh month, first day. The emperor went up to the Zetian Gate tower to receive the Baekje captives, and released them all, from their king Euija down.
blocks.ko: 11월 초하루 무술일, 황제가 칙천문 누각에 나아가 백제의 포로를 받고, 그 왕 의자 이하를 모두 풀어 주었다.
blocks.hanja: 十一月，戊戌朔，上御則天門樓，受百濟俘，自其王義慈以下皆釋之。
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 200, Tang Gaozong, Xianqing 5 (660), eleventh month

en: Kim Chunchu…
KIM CHUNCHU!!!

blocks.html: Across the sea, in Surabol, King Muyeol is eating his supper.
blocks.ko: 바다 건너 서라벌에서, 무열왕이 저녁을 들고 있다.

en: Hm?

lines: 삼한의 땅으로 당을 끌어들이는 이 비랄한 만고의 역적아!!
en: Kim Chunchu, you wretch!!
You vile traitor of the ages, who dragged a foreign power onto the soil of Samhan!!
Heaven’s punishment will find you!!

blocks.html: The shouting burns out. What remains is a man who has finally run out of stories to sell — and one last story he cannot afford to keep.
blocks.ko: 고함이 사그라든다. 남은 것은 팔 이야기가 바닥난 사내 — 그리고 더는 쥐고 있을 수 없는 마지막 이야기 하나.

lines: 김춘추 — 네가 끝낸 것을… 끝내지 못하게…!
en: Let someone… avenge me…!
Let someone… raise Baekje again…!
Chunchu — what you finished… may it never stay finished…!

blocks.html: He is shouting at the man who won. Across the sea, a quiet son with lovely handwriting is still waiting to be needed.
blocks.ko: 그는 이긴 사내를 향해 소리치고 있다. 바다 건너에서는, 글씨가 고운 조용한 아들 하나가 아직도 누군가 자기를 필요로 해 주기를 기다리고 있다.

blocks.html: Then the room fills with men only he can see.
blocks.ko: 그때 방이 그에게만 보이는 이들로 찬다.

en: Gods are props. Spirits are lighting.
Heh… so you guys are real after all…
Any last words?

blocks.html: Euija waits. He has always been good at making a room lean in.
blocks.ko: 의자는 기다린다. 그는 언제나 방을 기울게 만드는 데 능했다.

en: No.

blocks.html: Kangrim reads his name three times in the Tang capital — Euija. Euija. Euija. — the underworld's receipt before the humiliation finishes.
blocks.ko: 강림은 당의 도읍에서 그의 이름을 세 번 부른다 — 의자. 의자. 의자. — 능욕이 끝나기 전 저승의 영수증처럼.

lines: 사람들은 당신을 해동증자라 불렀소. 당신은 구경꾼들 보라고 사비강 위에 용을 띄웠고. 어느 쪽이었소?
en: Eraha. King.
One question, then we walk.
They called you the Zengzi of the East. You hung a dragon over the Sabi for a crowd. Which were you?

lines: 용은 수백 명이 봤다. 증자가 뭘 하는 건 아무도 못 봤고.
en: …The dragon. Obviously.
Several hundred people saw the dragon. Nobody ever saw a Zengzi do anything.

lines: 당신이 준 이름이 아직 명부에 있소.
en: The boy at the White River.
The name you gave him is still in the ledger.
…A friend.
Put the miracle on the cheap side of the page.

blocks.html: A jar in a hedge, and a prince who ought to be at his own investiture.
blocks.ko: 울타리 밑의 술 단지 하나. 제 책봉식에 가 있어야 할 왕자 하나.

blocks.html: A grey hood at the back of a crowd. A boy going into black water on a rope.
blocks.ko: 구경꾼들 맨 뒤의 회색 두건. 밧줄 하나에 매달려 검은 물로 들어가는 아이.

en: How many times have you gone in?
Nineteen.

blocks.html: A pale deer in the reeds, standing where nobody else is up to see it.
blocks.ko: 갈대숲의 흰 사슴 한 마리. 아무도 깨어 있지 않은 자리에 서 있다.

lines: …그 이름이 마음에 드십니까, 제가 마음에 드십니까?
en: …Do you like the name, or do you like me?

lines: 너였다, 이 바보야. 이름은 그냥 그때 내가 가진 것 중에 제일 좋은 거였고.
en: …You.
It was you, you idiot. The name was just the best thing I had on me.

lines: 그는 나루에서 기다리고 있소. 직접 말해 주시오. 그 사람은 정확히 말해 줘야 알아들으니.
그렇다면 당신은 기록이 인정하는 것보다 부자로 죽는 거요.
en: He is waiting at the ford. Tell him yourself. He will want it said exactly.
Then you die richer than the record will admit.
Come.

blocks.html: Euija dies, vengeful and emptied. Then, at the very last, neither.
blocks.ko: 의자는 원한에 차고, 텅 빈 채로 죽는다. 그리고 맨 마지막 순간에는, 둘 다 아니다.

blocks.html: Thus was the end of Buyeo Euija.
blocks.ko: 그리하여 부여의자의 생은 끝났다.

blocks.html: A man the court once called the Zengzi of the East.
blocks.ko: 한때 조정이 «해동증자»라 부르던 사내였다.

blocks.html: Euija served his parents with a devotion people talked about, and was kind to his brothers; men of his time called him the Zeng and Min of the East. He reached the capital and died a few days later.
blocks.ko: 의자는 어버이를 효성으로 섬겨 이름이 났고 형제와 우애하니, 당시 사람들이 ‘해동의 증자·민자’라 불렀다. 경사에 이르러 며칠 만에 죽었다.
blocks.hanja: 義慈事親以孝行聞，友于兄弟，時人號「海東曾、閔」。及至京，數日而卒。
blocks.source: Jiu Tangshu (舊唐書) bk. 199A, Eastern Barbarians — Baekje

blocks.html: — Buyeo Euija —
blocks.ko: — 부여의자 —

blocks.html: Seongchung told him. He put Seongchung in a cell. Heungsu told him. He had already exiled Heungsu. Gyebek would have told him, and he had put Gyebek on a boat. A man does not fall because nobody warned him. He falls because he arranged, patiently and over years, to be somewhere the warnings could not reach.
blocks.ko: 성충이 말했다. 그는 성충을 옥에 가두었다. 흥수가 말했다. 그는 이미 흥수를 내쫓은 뒤였다. 계백이라면 말했을 것이다. 그리고 그는 계백을 배에 태워 보냈다. 사람은 아무도 경고하지 않아서 무너지지 않는다. 여러 해에 걸쳐 참을성 있게, 경고가 닿을 수 없는 곳에 제 자리를 마련해 두었기 때문에 무너진다.

blocks.html: The Zengzi of the East. They called him that when he was young, and they meant it. The name was neither flattery nor wrong. He was never a fool. He was a clever man who won, and kept winning, until winning was the only instrument he had left, and then he tried to play a dying country on it.
blocks.ko: 해동증자. 젊은 시절 사람들은 그를 그렇게 불렀고, 진심이었다. 아첨도 아니고 틀린 말도 아니었다. 그는 결코 어리석지 않았다. 그는 이기고 또 이긴 영리한 사람이었고, 마침내 이기는 것 말고는 남은 악기가 없어졌을 때, 죽어 가는 나라를 그것으로 연주하려 했다.

blocks.html: Baekje is gone. Goguryeo still stands. And the man who arranged both can no longer get out of bed…?
blocks.ko: 백제는 사라졌다. 고구려는 아직 서 있다. 그리고 그 둘을 꾸민 사내가, 더는 자리에서 일어나지 못한다…?

logline.en: The man who arranged all of it is fifty-eight, and cannot get out of bed.
logline.ko: 이 모든 것을 꾸민 사내는 쉰여덟이고, 침상에서 일어나지 못한다.

images.at: The road is long, and you will want to talk the whole way.
images.alt: Tiny Chunchu walks alone into a magenta underworld road — monumental emptiness, no escort
images.prompt: Minimal iconic 16:9 poster. Kim Chunchu walks to the afterlife ALONE. ONE geometric device: a MAGENTA RIBBON of road receding into a flat charcoal-rose underworld void — the ribbon is the whole composition. Tiny silky hanbok figure walking AWAY from camera, by himself, no psychopomp, no family. Face matches the attached portrait only as a tiny likeness. Chunchu magenta #D8258C as the plane and the single accent. Otherworld: symbolic flat color, no naturalistic sun or moon weather. Monumental emptiness. Callback to an earlier long-road still of a father carrying a child: same road-ribbon, now empty of the child. No army. No clutter. No text. No watermark. Graphic color-blocking, anime-painterly, monumental.

images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Interior late night, a quiet temple side hall at the edge of Surabol. Low WORM'S-EYE from the floor at the foot of the sick-mat. ONE device: a single thread of incense smoke rising straight up from a bronze burner on the floor. Munhee, FACE ONLY from the attached portrait, fifty-five, hair dressed with the attached binyeo, sitting very upright beside the mat, one hand resting on the blanket over his hand, eyes on him, dry-eyed and steely. King Muyeol (Chunchu), FACE ONLY from the attached portrait, lying under the blanket, head turned toward her, a faint tired smile; his crown rests on a stand in the shadow. A clay lamp on the floor rakes gold up across her face and the folds; magenta #D8258C as a small specular on his silk collar. Background: a dim gilt Buddha barely readable in the dark. CANON — QUEEN MUNMYUNG — FACE and garments from attached /ch_munmyung.png (face only; invent a new pose). Hair ornament matches attached /bn_munhee.png when the head is visible. Crown: Silla gold crown, as the attached crown: a gold band with three tree-shaped uprights stepped like the character 出 and two antler uprights at the back, hung with round gold spangles and curved green jade gogok, long gold pendants at the temples. ref_muyeol shows it worn with the king's red robe and gold-scroll collar (ignore its painted backdrop). Demeanor: Yushin's younger sister, Chunchu's wife; quick and warm, the one who bought the dream. #E07FA8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: fantasy tiara instead of her binyeo. | KING MUYEOL — FACE and garments from attached /ch_muyeol.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Slim and elegant; shoulder-length loose black hair parted in the middle; thin moustache and goatee stubble; amused eyes, small knowing smile. Dress: Magenta-crimson silk po with a charcoal sash, dark layered collar. Silk even on campaign. Crown: Silla gold crown, as the attached crown: a gold band with three tree-shaped uprights stepped like the character 出 and two antler uprights at the back, hung with round gold spangles and curved green jade gogok, long gold pendants at the temples. ref_muyeol shows it worn with the king's red robe and gold-scroll collar (ignore its painted backdrop). Now: King Muyeol (stage portrait): royal robes and crown; heavier, tired eyes. Demeanor: Diplomat and strategist: talks with his hands, smiles while calculating, never shouts; half-lidded watchful eyes. #D8258C as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: front-line armored warrior pose; shouting battle face; katana. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Silla: attached /ref_hanbok_silla.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Chunchu has talked his way out of every room in Samhan. This one has no other door.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 삼한의 모든 방에서 말로 빠져나왔다. 이 방에는 다른 문이 없다.

blocks.label: The Sickroom
blocks.ko: 병석

blocks.html: It is the sixth month of 661. Baekje has fallen, Goguryeo has not, and the man who arranged both is fifty-eight and cannot get out of bed.
blocks.ko: 661년 유월이다. 백제는 무너졌고 고구려는 아직 서 있으며, 그 둘을 모두 꾸민 사내는 쉰여덟에 자리에서 일어나지 못한다.

blocks.html: Yushin comes in the afternoon, still in his riding boots, and stands where a marshal stands, which is too close to the door.
blocks.ko: 유신은 오후에 온다. 아직 승마 장화를 신은 채, 장수가 서는 자리에 선다. 문에 너무 가까운 자리다.

en: The Tang want us at Pyongyang by winter.
I told them you were busy.

lines: 바쁘지요. 죽는 것도 하루 품이 꽉 차는 일이더군요.
형님, 오늘은 좀 앉으시오. 형님이 서 있으면 방이 성문 같소.
en: Busy. Yes. Dying turns out to be a full day’s work.
Brother, sit down for once. You make the room look like a gate.
I’ll stand.

lines: …북으로 데려가 주시오. 법민을. 저 애는 성벽에 돌격하고 싶어 할 거요. 돌격하게 두지 마시오.
en: Of course you will.
…Take him north for me. Bupmin. He’ll want to charge the walls. Don’t let him charge the walls.
I won’t.

blocks.html: That is the whole goodbye. They have been saying the rest of it for forty years.
blocks.ko: 작별은 그게 다다. 나머지는 마흔 해 동안 이미 해 왔다.

blocks.html: Munhee (55) sits where she has sat since the spring. Outside the door a monk who knows when not to speak keeps the incense going. Forty years ago she bought a dream off her sister for a silk skirt. This is where the dream comes out: a sickroom, a husband, and a son at the foot of the bed.
blocks.ko: 문희(55)는 봄부터 앉아 있던 그 자리에 앉아 있다. 문밖에서는 말을 아낄 줄 아는 스님 하나가 향을 지킨다. 마흔 해 전, 그녀는 비단 치마 한 벌로 언니의 꿈을 샀다. 그 꿈이 닿은 곳이 여기다. 병실 하나, 남편 하나, 그리고 침상 발치에 선 아들 하나.

en: Munhee. Have I… paid all of it?
Not yet. I’ll pay the rest.
Do you remember the skirt?
It was a very good skirt.
Don’t make me cry in front of the boy.
Best bargain in Silla.

lines: 두 번째지요. 법민아, 문간에 서 있지 말고. 들어와.
en: Second best. Bupmin, don’t stand in the door. Come in.

blocks.html: He looks past her, to the boy who is no longer a boy. Bupmin (35) has his mother’s stillness and his father’s hunger, and for a moment the room holds all three of them the way a hill once held a promise.
blocks.ko: 그는 문희 너머로, 더 이상 아이가 아닌 아이를 본다. 법민 (35)에게는 어머니의 고요와 아버지의 허기가 있다. 잠시, 방이 예전 언덕이 약속을 품듯 셋 모두를 품는다.

en: Bupmin.
Father.

lines: 사람들은… 이 전쟁이 오직 네 누나를 위한 줄 알 거다.
그것도 맞다. 대야는 하루도 이 방을 나간 적이 없다.
en: People will say… this whole war was only for your sister.
Gotaso.
And they will not be wrong. Daeya never left this room for a single day.

lines: 하지만 그게 내가 갚던 유일한 빚은 아니었다.
언젠가 언덕에서, 네 외숙과 함께, 내가 한 말이 있다. “만인의 왕.”
en: But that was never the only debt.
On a hill once, with your uncle, I said a thing. “A king for all.”
Not a king of Silla. Of everyone.

lines: 그걸 제가 훔쳤지요. 여섯 살 때. 밥상머리에서 그 말만—
en: And I stole it. I was six. I used to say it at dinner—

lines: 너는 그 말을 틀리게 했지. 입 안에서 말이 삐뚤게 앉아 있었다.
내가 먼저 했다. 네가 가져갔고. 아이들은 그렇게 훔친다. 방 안에서 제일 큰 것을 가져가지.
나는 백제까지 길을 텄다. 고구려는 아직 서 있고, 당은 웃고 있을 게다.
나머지는 — 왕으로서 걸어라. 내 복수로서가 아니라. 네가 여섯 살 때 바라던 나라로서.
en: You said it wrong. The word sat crooked in your mouth.
I said it first. You took it. That is how children steal. They take the largest thing in the room.
I cleared the road as far as Baekje. Goguryeo is still standing, and the Tang will be smiling.
The rest — walk it as king. Not as my revenge. As the country you wanted when you were six.
…I promise.
Bupmin… I love you.

blocks.html: The escort arrives on schedule.
blocks.ko: 호위가 시간에 맞춰 도착한다.

blocks.html: Kangrim reads the name three times — Muyeol. Muyeol. Muyeol. The room still knows him as Chunchu.
blocks.ko: 강림이 그 이름을 세 번 부른다 — 무열. 무열. 무열. 방 안은 아직 그를 춘추로 안다.

lines: 전에 만난 적이 있소. 대야성에서. 당신은 나를 보지 않았지. 이름 적힌 명단을 보고 있었으니.
en: King Muyeol.
We have met before, at Daeya. You weren’t looking at me. You were looking at a list of names.

lines: 의자가 하늘이 나를 찾아낼 거라 저주했지.
en: Euija swore heaven would find me.
…Is this heaven?

lines: 아니오. 이건 열병이오. 하늘은 왕진을 오지 않소. 오는 건 나요.
질문 하나 하고 갑시다. 고타소를 위해서였소, 아니면 만인의 왕을 위해서였소?
en: No. This is a fever. Heaven does not make house calls. I do.
One question, then we walk. Was it for Gotaso, or for the king for all?
…Yes.
That is not one of the two.

lines: 바둑에서 돌 하나를 한 가지 이유로 놓는 사람은 없소.
두 칸에 다 적으시오. 장부에 칸이 둘은 있을 테니.
en: In go, nobody plays a stone for one reason.
Write it in both columns. Your ledger has two, I assume.

lines: 갑시다. 길이 머니, 가는 내내 말하고 싶을 거요.
en: It does. I will.
Come. The road is long, and you will want to talk the whole way.

blocks.html: King Muyeol (58) dies.
blocks.ko: 무열왕 (58)이 승하한다.

lines: …다들한테 무릎을 꿇은 양반이야. 연개소문한테도, 황제한테도. 문 잡아 줄 사람이면 누구한테든.
일어나라, 법민아. 이제 네가 왕이다. 왕은 침상 옆에서 무릎 꿇는 거 아니다.
en: …He knelt to everyone. Gesomun. The emperor. Anyone who would hold a door.
Never once to Baekje.
Get up, Bupmin. You’re the king. Kings don’t kneel by beds.

blocks.html: He died with Baekje gone and Goguryeo still standing. Halfway. The last two names he said were his daughter’s and his son’s. Not the kingdom’s.
blocks.ko: 그는 백제가 사라지고 고구려는 아직 서 있는 채로 죽었다. 절반에서. 그가 마지막으로 부른 두 이름은 딸의 이름과 아들의 이름이었다. 나라의 이름이 아니었다.

blocks.html: Twelve years earlier an emperor had told him that Goguryeo was the one failure of his life, and that Baekje would be Chunchu’s. Only one of them was wrong.
blocks.ko: 십이 년 전, 한 황제가 그에게 고려는 제 인생의 유일한 실패이며 백제는 그대의 실패가 될 것이라 했다. 둘 중 한 사람만 틀렸다.

blocks.html: They give him a name for the dead: Muyeol. His temple name is Taejong, the same name the Tang gave their Second Emperor. Chang’an will notice.
blocks.ko: 그에게 죽은 자의 이름이 붙는다. 무열. 묘호는 태종이다. 당이 두 번째 황제에게 붙인 바로 그 이름이다. 장안이 그냥 넘어가지 않을 것이다.

blocks.hanja: 姿表英特，聰明多智略。
blocks.html: He was striking in looks and bearing, quick-witted and full of stratagems.
blocks.ko: 자태와 풍채가 영특하고, 총명하여 지략이 많았다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 6, Silla Annals — King Munmu, accession notice

blocks.html: Bupmin takes the throne. They will call him Munmu.
blocks.ko: 법민이 왕위에 오른다. 사람들은 그를 문무라 부를 것이다.

blocks.html: Silla won the war. So why does the emperor’s new edict call its king a clerk…?
blocks.ko: 전쟁은 신라가 이겼다. 그런데 황제의 새 칙서는 왜 신라 왕을 고을 원님으로 적는가…?

logline.en: The Tang throw a net over the country. A sixty-year-old in white comes to mend it.
logline.ko: 당은 이 나라에 그물을 던진다. 흰 옷을 입은 예순 노인이 그 그물을 기우러 온다.
