images.at: launches the Eighth Invasion of Goguryeo
images.alt: Ink-painted poster: the Third Emperor, in grey ink wash, points east from a palace terrace as the gold dragon spirals up out of a black ink storm
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; heads and the dragon’s head stay inside the central band; no title, no lettering. Storm dusk on a high terrace of the Daming Palace: balustrades and owl-tail roof ridges as black calligraphic strokes, a sky of splashed black ink. Worm’s-eye from the terrace floor. TWO SUBJECTS: a human-scale emperor AND a huge dragon. INTERACTION: the Third Emperor, young and uncertain, stands at the balustrade with his arm thrown out pointing east; the gold Tang dragon Huanglong (gold ink-brush dragon from the attached board, three claws) spirals up past him into the black storm, its body curling once loosely around his outstretched arm before it uncoils skyward, its head turned east along his pointing hand. One gold break in the storm (#b8935a) catches his face, his arm and the dragon’s coils. TANG RENDER: predominantly DARK and INTIMIDATING Chinese ink painting (shuimohua) on rice paper — heavy black and grey ink washes, wet-on-wet ink bleeding, splashed ink smoke and storm, dry calligraphic brush strokes for roofs, columns, robes and cloud, ink splatters and drips at the frame edges, bare paper only where the edges dissolve; the gold ink-brush dragon is the main colour in the dark, with a few small vermilion and flame accents. Every figure, the Third Emperor included, is ink-painted in the same black-and-grey wash with only a thin wash of dull yellow on his robe; no full-colour figure in the frame. Movie-poster key art: bold iconic silhouette, big dark masses, one bright break of light, NO text, NO title, NO credits, NO logo, NO seal stamp, no calligraphy characters. Not photoreal, not 3D, not a realistic scaled dragon. No glow aura, no halo — the accent is real light. One of each named person. No watermark. CANON — THE THIRD EMPEROR — FACE and garments from attached /ch_gaozong.png (face only; invent a new pose). #b8935a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | HUANGLONG (황룡, taizong's yellow dragon, guardian of the Tang throne) — attached board /obj_yellow_dragon.png: TANG-DYNASTY dragon painted in gold ink-brush: lean long-necked serpentine body in an S-curve, four lean leonine legs striding, THREE claws on each foot, long open-jawed snout with fangs, two backswept horns, whiskers and mane flung out as dry calligraphic gold brush strokes, whip tail ending in a flame tuft; burnished gold-yellow scales with ochre-umber shading — match the board, not a later Ming/Qing five-claw dragon, never a realistic scaled 3D dragon. Divine render: numinous through scale and atmosphere, coiling through black ink cloud and lamp smoke; light catches the scales as real light, never a glow outline. Its stills are predominantly dark and intimidating Chinese ink painting: splashed black ink, smoke, the gold dragon the main colour in the dark; every figure is ink-painted except the Second Emperor, who stays a full-colour webtoon figure. Owned by no one but sits behind whoever holds the dais; it coils over Chang'an and turns its head only for the Son of Heaven. | PLACE Chang’an (장안) — attached board /pl_daming_night.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Tang palace of Chang'an, drawn from the Daming Palace (大明宮) site and reconstruction models: Hanyuan Hall's concave ensemble — an eleven-bay hall with a double-eaved hipped roof of dark grey tiles and curled owl-tail ridge ends (chiwei), red columns, white plaster walls, lattice windows, raised on three tiers of rammed-earth terraces faced in ochre-red plaster and edged with white stone balustrades; the Dragon Tail Way ramps folding up the terraces; forward on each side the Xiangluan and Qifeng que-towers (three stepped pavilions on tall battered grey-brick piers) joined to the hall by long roofed corridors; a vast paved square below, entered through the five-doored Danfeng Gate. Wide low Tang proportions, deep eaves on massive bracket sets. Tang palette is VERMILION and WHITE (red columns, white walls); roofs are black-grey tile trimmed with green-glazed ridge and eave tiles (a little yellow and blue tricolour glaze); balustrade posts painted red, blue and green. YELLOW belongs to the emperor's robe; gold is gilt-bronze fittings, lamp-trees and firelight on vermilion. Interiors: dark polished stone floors, rows of vermilion columns, gauze hangings, a raised dais with a painted screen behind the throne. Never the Forbidden City, never all-yellow glazed roofs, never the modern reconstruction or a city skyline. Mood: TANG RENDER: predominantly DARK and INTIMIDATING Chinese ink painting (shuimohua) — black and grey ink washes, wet-on-wet ink bleeding into rice paper, dry calligraphic brush for roofs, columns, smoke and robes, the vermilion and gold reduced to small accents in a world of ink; officials, guards and other Tang figures are ink figures too. The ONE exception is the Second Emperor himself: he keeps the house webtoon figure render in full colour (yellow robe, black futou, drawn face), a coloured man inside an ink empire. Staged like a Chinese historical drama (Legend of the Demon Cat, The Longest Day in Chang'an) but lit as full Heewon tenebrism: night or blue hour; ONE dominant hard key per shot — a backlight through open doors or lattice, or one lamp-tree — and 75% of the frame crushed black with no fill; colour contrast — gold-yellow flame highlights against cool blue-green in the few lit shadows; the other flames (lamp-trees, silk lanterns with no writing, braziers) are small points and round bokeh IN the black, never lighting the room evenly; red lantern light through lattice as one pattern on the floor; incense haze only inside the key shaft; polished dark floors reflecting the flames. Staged like a drama, at true human scale: camera at eye or knee height on a dolly or crane; court officials in two lines facing inward along the central aisle with tablets; banquet tables in two long facing rows with dancers in the centre and the emperor on the dais at the head; exteriors are real-scale terraces and corridors, the hall large but never a fantasy fortress. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: In Chang’an, the cheapest way to conquer a country is to rename it.
blocks.ko: 장안에서 나라 하나를 정복하는 가장 싼 방법은, 그 나라의 이름을 바꾸는 것이다.

blocks.label: Chang’an
blocks.ko: 장안

blocks.html: The Red Fowl is home with his captives. The emperor asks him a question in front of the whole court, which is how emperors ask questions they already know the answer to.
blocks.ko: 주작이 포로들을 데리고 돌아왔다. 황제는 온 조정 앞에서 그에게 묻는다. 황제들은 답을 이미 아는 질문을 그렇게 묻는다.

lines: 경이 군대를 끌고 거기 있었는데, 어째서 내친김에 신라까지 치지 않았소?
en: You were there with an army. Why didn’t you take Silla while you were at it?
zh: 卿既在彼，何不因而伐新羅？
zhLatn: Qīng jì zài bǐ, hé bù yīn ér fá Xīnluó?

lines: 그 임금은 어질어 백성을 아끼고, 신하들은 충성으로 나라를 섬기며, 아랫사람은 윗사람을 아비와 형처럼 섬깁니다.
작은 나라이나, 꾀로 도모할 수는 없습니다.
en: Their king is kind and loves his people. His ministers serve the country loyally. Below, they serve those above like fathers and elder brothers.
It is a small country, Majesty. But it cannot be schemed against.
zh: 新羅其君仁而愛民，其臣忠以事國，下之人事其上如父兄。
zhLatn: Xīnluó qí jūn rén ér ài mín, qí chén zhōng yǐ shì guó, xià zhī rén shì qí shàng rú fù xiōng.
Suī xiǎo, bù kě móu yě.

lines: 그럼 꾀 말고 글로 하지요. 그 나라 임금을 우리 도독으로 삼으면— 아니. 뺨 때리는 소리 같군요.
en: Can’t be schemed against. Hm.
Then we won’t scheme. We’ll write. Make their king a governor of ours — no. That sounds like a slap.
…Write it anyway.

lines: 절하면서 받아야 하는 뺨 한 대가, 되돌려 칠 수 있는 뺨 두 대보다 값져요.
en: Make it sound like an honour, Majesty.
A slap they have to bow for is worth two they can return.

blocks.label: Gyerim
blocks.ko: 계림

blocks.html: Then an edict arrives for the new king. It makes him Grand Commander of the Gyerim Prefecture. Gyerim is his country’s oldest name, the wood where a rooster crowed over a golden box. In the edict it is one province of the empire. And the king is its governor.
blocks.ko: 이윽고 새 임금 앞으로 칙서가 온다. 그를 계림주 대도독으로 삼는다는 내용이다. 계림은 이 나라의 가장 오래된 이름이다. 닭이 금궤 위에서 울던 숲. 칙서 안에서 그곳은 제국의 한 고을이다. 그리고 임금은 그 고을 원이다.

lines: 주라 하오, 외숙. 아버님의 나라를 주로 만들고, 나를 그 고을 원으로 삼았소.
en: A prefecture, Uncle. They have made my father’s country into a prefecture, and me its clerk.
Then sign as its clerk, Majesty.
And keep a copy.

blocks.html: The court is angrier than the king. Men in the Council hall who have not agreed on anything since the old queen died agree that a prefecture is an insult, and say so loudly, in rooms where no Tang officer is present.
blocks.ko: 조정은 왕보다 더 화가 났다. 옛 여왕이 죽은 뒤로 무엇 하나 합의해 본 적 없는 회의장의 사내들이, 주라니 모욕이라는 데에는 뜻을 모은다. 그리고 당의 관리가 없는 방에서 큰 소리로 그렇게 말한다.

blocks.html: Only Daeto, a smooth councillor who always urges the softer word, keeps his voice down.
blocks.ko: 부드러운 말을 권하는 게 일인 매끄러운 신하, 대토만이 목소리를 낮춘다.

lines: 그쪽 역법 보셨어요? 하루하루가 딱딱 맞아떨어집니다. 우리 책력은 동지가 언제인지도 저 혼자 우기는데.
en: They’re not wrong about everything, you know.
Have you seen their calendar? Every day accounted for. Our almanac can’t even agree with itself about the solstice.

blocks.html: Nobody answers him. A few men remember afterwards that he said it.
blocks.ko: 아무도 대꾸하지 않는다. 몇몇은 뒷날 그가 그 말을 했다는 것을 기억해 낸다.

blocks.label: The Black Tortoise
blocks.ko: 현무

blocks.html: Someone has to hold what the Tang broke. Nobody in Chang’an expected to see Liu Rengui in uniform again. He is sixty. Last year he lost a grain fleet in a storm and was stripped of office. Now he comes east as a commoner in white, to earn it back. In his baggage: the Tang calendar, and the list of names nobody may write.
blocks.ko: 당이 부순 것을 누군가는 붙들고 있어야 한다. 장안의 누구도 유인궤가 다시 군복을 입으리라 생각하지 않았다. 그는 예순이다. 지난해 폭풍에 군량선단을 잃고 관직을 빼앗겼다. 이제 그는 흰옷 입은 평민으로 동쪽에 와서 그것을 되찾으려 한다. 짐 속에는 당의 달력과, 아무도 써서는 안 되는 이름들의 목록이 들어 있다.

blocks.caption: The Black Tortoise. Sixty, disgraced last year, and in an excellent mood.
blocks.ko: 현무. 예순, 작년에 파직당했고, 기분이 아주 좋다.

lines: 하늘이 이 늙은이를 부귀하게 하시려나 보오.
이 나라에 쓸 역서를 보내 주시오. 써서는 안 될 이름 목록도. 동쪽을 쓸어 평정할 거라면, 동쪽도 적어도 지금이 몇 년인지는 알아야지.
en: Heaven means to make an old man rich, it seems.
Send me the calendar for this country, and the list of names one must not write. If we are going to sweep the east clean, the east should at least know what year it is.
zh: 請頒曆及宗廟諱。吾欲掃平東夷，頒大唐正朔於海表。
zhLatn: Tiān jiāng fùguì cǐ wēng ěr.
Qǐng bān lì jí zōngmiào huì. Wú yù sǎopíng dōngyí, bān Dà Táng zhēngshuò yú hǎibiǎo.

blocks.html: Between skirmishes the Black Tortoise does what he actually came for, which is paperwork. He counts the households of Baekje village by village and writes them down as numbers. He mends dykes and bridges. He posts the Tang calendar at every crossroads, with the list of names that may not be written, so that the people of Baekje will know which characters to leave out of their letters home.
blocks.ko: 싸움과 싸움 사이에 현무는 정말로 하러 온 일을 한다. 서류다. 백제의 호구를 마을마다 세어 숫자로 적는다. 둑과 다리를 고친다. 갈림길마다 당의 달력을 붙이고, 써서는 안 되는 이름의 목록도 함께 붙인다. 백제 사람들이 집에 보내는 편지에서 어떤 글자를 빼야 하는지 알도록.

lines: 올해가 몇 년인지 아는 마을은 세금을 제때 내오.
나루에도 하나 붙이시오. 사람은 배를 기다리면서 읽으니까.
en: A village that knows what year it is pays its tax on time.
Put one up at the ferry as well. People read while they wait for the boat.
zh: 渡口也貼一張。人等船時會讀。
zhLatn: Zhī niánsuì zhī cūn, nàshuì bú wù.
Dùkǒu yě tiē yì zhāng. Rén děng chuán shí huì dú.

blocks.label: The Ferry
blocks.ko: 나루

blocks.html: The ferry calendar lasts four days. On the fifth morning it is still on its post, untouched, which is worse. Someone has added a line to the bottom of the list of names one must not write. The charcoal is still soft.
blocks.ko: 나루의 달력은 나흘을 버틴다. 닷새째 아침에도 그것은 기둥에 멀쩡히 붙어 있다. 그게 더 나쁘다. 누군가 써서는 안 되는 이름 목록 맨 아래에 한 줄을 보탰다. 숯이 아직 무르다.

blocks.speaker: Tang clerk
en: Shall I scrape it off, General?
Read it to me first.

blocks.speaker: Tang clerk
en: “Buyeo Pung.” And under it: “Gwishil Boksin, who sends his regards.”

lines: 왕자 하나, 그리고 쪽지에 제 이름을 적는 사내 하나라.
en: A prince, and a man who signs his notes.
Who is the prince?

blocks.speaker: Tang clerk
lines: 의자의 아들입니다, 장군. 조용한 놈이요. 어릴 때 왜 조정에 보냈답니다.
en: Euija’s son, General. The quiet one. They sent him to the Yamato court as a boy.

lines: 그럼 내가 곧 쓰지 못하게 될 이름을 미리 알려 주는 셈이군.
베껴 두시오. 두 벌. 원본은 그대로 붙여 두고. 내가 읽었다는 걸 그자가 알도록.
en: Then they are telling me which name I will soon be forbidden to write.
Copy it. Twice. And leave the original up. I want him to know I read it.

blocks.label: The Fires
blocks.ko: 불

blocks.html: That night the hills around Sabi light up. One fire, then forty. Boksin has brought the restoration to the Tang’s front door, and the garrison inside has ten days of rice.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 사비를 둘러싼 산들에 불이 켜진다. 하나, 그리고 마흔. 복신이 부흥군을 당의 앞문까지 끌고 왔고, 성 안 수비대에게는 열흘 치 쌀이 남았다.

blocks.html: The Black Tortoise has no cavalry to speak of and no reputation left to lose. What he has is a census. He counted those villages a month ago. He knows which of them fed the fires, and which are short of men tonight.
blocks.ko: 현무에게는 내세울 기병도, 더 잃을 명성도 없다. 그에게 있는 것은 호적이다. 한 달 전에 그 마을들을 세었다. 어느 마을이 저 불에 쌀을 댔는지, 오늘 밤 어느 마을에 사내가 모자란지 안다.

lines: 쌀 나르는 길을 막으시오. 정중하게. 수레는 하나하나 다 적고.
en: Not the hills. The villages behind them.
Close the roads they bring the rice on. Politely. Write down every cart.

blocks.html: It takes nine days. On the tenth the fires around Sabi go out one by one, the way they were lit, and the rebels walk back up into the hills to a fortress called Imjon. They are not beaten. They are waiting for somebody.
blocks.ko: 아흐레가 걸린다. 열흘째, 사비를 둘러싼 불들이 켜질 때처럼 하나씩 꺼지고, 부흥군은 임존이라는 성으로 산을 걸어 올라간다. 진 게 아니다. 누군가를 기다리는 것이다.

lines: 다시 올 거요. 먼저 왕을 모셔 와야 하니.
en: He’ll be back. He has to fetch a king first.

blocks.label: The Maps
blocks.ko: 지도

blocks.html: In Chang’an the Third Emperor is told that Baekje is finished and that its king has died in the capital of a broken heart, and he takes out his father’s maps.
blocks.ko: 장안에서 세 번째 황제는 백제가 끝났고 그 왕이 도성에서 상심하여 죽었다는 말을 듣는다. 그리고 아버지의 지도를 꺼낸다.

lines: 아버님은 동쪽에 세 번 가셨다가 기침을 하며 돌아오셨지.
백제는 고구려 등 뒤의 칼이었고, 이제 그 칼을 우리가 쥐었어 — 아니. 이건 아버님이 하실 말 같군. 그래도 적어 두게.
en: Father went east three times and came home coughing.
Baekje was the knife at Goguryeo’s back, and now we’re holding it — no. That sounds like something he would say. Write it down anyway.

lines: 장수 넷이요. 지도 네 귀퉁이에 하나씩. 그래야 아무도 혼자 했다고 우기며 돌아오지 못하죠.
en: Then don’t say it like him. Say it like you.
Four generals. One for each side of the map, so none of them can come home claiming he did it alone.

blocks.html: That is how the Four Beasts are chosen: by a woman who knows how generals talk at banquets.
blocks.ko: 사신(四神)은 그렇게 뽑힌다. 장수들이 잔치에서 무슨 말을 하는지 아는 여자에 의해.

blocks.label: The Four Beasts
blocks.ko: 사신

blocks.html: The Third Emperor launches the Eighth Invasion of Goguryeo — his father’s war, inherited along with everything else.
blocks.ko: 황제가 제8차 고구려 원정을 일으킨다. 다른 모든 것과 함께 물려받은, 아버지의 전쟁이다.

blocks.title: Four Beasts · 사신
blocks.caption: Gaozong’s expeditionary colours: White Tiger, Red Fowl, Blue Dragon, Black Tortoise.
blocks.ko: 고종의 동정 색깔. 백호, 주작, 청룡, 현무.

blocks.html: Samhan never learns their names. It learns their banners, which is the entire purpose of a banner.
blocks.ko: 삼한은 끝내 그들의 이름을 배우지 않는다. 깃발을 배운다. 깃발이란 원래 그러라고 있는 것이다.

blocks.html: The Silla envoy is still in the hall. The emperor turns to him last.
blocks.ko: 신라 사신이 아직 전각에 있다. 황제는 마지막으로 그를 돌아본다.

lines: 백제는 끝났소. 그대 왕의 근심은 내가 덜어 주었소.
이제 고구려요. 돌아가서 왕에게 군사를 이끌고 북으로 오라 전하시오.
이제 우리 달력이 있으니, 날짜도 전하시오.
en: Baekje is done. I have taken your king’s worry off his hands.
Now Goguryeo. Go home and tell him to bring his army north.
He has our calendar now. Tell him the date.

blocks.html: Baekje has no king. Across the sea, an exiled prince is packing his bags…!
blocks.ko: 백제에는 임금이 없다. 바다 건너, 쫓겨난 왕자 하나가 짐을 꾸린다…!

logline.en: Baekje is finished, says everyone except Baekje. Its last prince has lived across the sea for twenty years.
logline.ko: 백제는 끝났다고 다들 말한다. 백제만 빼고. 마지막 왕자는 스무 해째 바다 건너에 살고 있다.

images.alt: In the hall at Juryu, Gwishil Boksin lowers the black-and-gold Baekje crown onto Pung’s head
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Juryu Fortress: a rough Baekje mountain fortress of piled grey stone on a pine ridge above the western sea, timber gate-house with a plain giwa roof. Inside its rough stone hall at night, ONE brazier on the floor in the foreground. Worm’s-eye past the brazier: Pung, in the red royal robe of a Baekje king, kneeling upright with his eyes closed; Gwishil Boksin standing over him in steel lamellar, lowering the black silk cap with twin gold flame ornaments onto Pung’s topknot with both hands; behind them, in the dark, refugees and soldiers kneeling as silhouettes. The crown’s gold catches the brazier. Device: the crown held at the apex of a pyramid of arms. CANON — KING PUNGJANG — FACE and garments from attached /ch_pungjang.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Prince years: smooth beardless face, soft eyes, black hair in a topknot bound with a red-and-gold cord and a gold pin. Dress: Red robe with black sleeves striped in gold, gold-brocade crossed collar, braided red-and-gold cord sash. Crown: Baekje king, as the attached crown (ignore its studio backdrop and logo): a tall rounded black silk cap (오라관) with a plain black band at the brow, and a pair of tall openwork gold flame-and-leaf ornaments (금제관식) pinned to either side of the cap, rising above it like twin flames — thin gold blades fanning upward with leaf buds and curls; the king’s red robe and wide-sleeved layers as the Baekje king on the costume chart. Now: King Pungjang (stage portrait): sharper face, a small chin goatee, loose strands falling from the topknot; red king's robe with dark-navy-lined sleeves, gold-scroll shoulders and a long gold cord sash. Demeanor: Formal, slightly foreign-accented royal speech, brittle when contradicted; raised in Yamato, crowned by the general he beheaded. #e6c76a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: Tang dress. | GWISHIL BOKSIN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_gwisil_boksin.png (face only; invent a new pose). #a8781f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Baekje: attached /ref_hanbok_baekje_gaya.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.label: The Crossing
blocks.ko: 바닷길

blocks.html: Its last prince is on a Yamato boat off Juryu, with a new cap of rank in a box on his knees. He has been rehearsing one sentence since the islands. It keeps coming out in the wrong language.
blocks.ko: 백제의 마지막 왕자는 주류 앞바다의 왜 배 위에 있다. 무릎 위 상자에는 새로 지은 관이 들어 있다. 섬들을 지나올 때부터 문장 하나를 연습하고 있다. 자꾸 엉뚱한 나라 말로 나온다.

lines: 다쿠쓰. 어떤 곳에 돌아올 때 쓰는 백제 말. 제대로 된 말 말이오.
en: Takutsu. The Baekje word for coming home to a place. The proper one.
…I used to know it.

lines: 저도 모르오, 전하. 그냥 오신 것만 반가워할 거라 들었소.
en: I don’t know it either, Majesty. I am told they will just be glad you came.

blocks.html: He has been losing words for twenty years. He only noticed last winter, in front of the whole Yamato court.
blocks.ko: 그는 스무 해 동안 말을 잃어 왔다. 그걸 알아챈 건 지난겨울, 왜 조정 전체가 보는 앞에서였다.

blocks.title: Asuka, that winter · 아스카, 그해 겨울

blocks.html: Asuka, the winter Sabi falls. A Baekje envoy has come the whole way with frost in his beard and a hundred Tang soldiers roped neck to neck behind him, a present, which is a polite word for proof. The empress is sixty-six. She has buried two husbands, held this throne twice and sat through a great many envoys, and she lets this one finish.
blocks.ko: 아스카, 사비가 무너진 그해 겨울. 백제 사신은 수염에 서리를 얹은 채 먼 길을 왔고, 그 뒤로 당나라 병사 백 명이 목과 목을 밧줄로 엮인 채 서 있다. 선물이다. 증거를 점잖게 부르는 말이다. 여제는 예순여섯이다. 남편 둘을 묻었고, 이 자리에 두 번 올랐고, 사신이라면 질리도록 받아 보았다. 그녀는 이 사신이 말을 끝낼 때까지 둔다.

blocks.html: The court across the cold sea, where favours are counted in ships.
blocks.ko: 차가운 바다 건너의 궁정. 은혜는 배로 센다.

blocks.html: The envoy comes from Gwishil Boksin, who has been raising a dead country in the hills since summer. Boksin wants two things: an army, and the king’s quiet son, who was sent across the sea as a boy and never sent for.
blocks.ko: 사신을 보낸 이는 귀실복신이다. 여름부터 산속에서 죽은 나라를 일으켜 온 사내다. 복신이 청하는 것은 둘이다. 원병, 그리고 어려서 바다를 건너왔다가 한 번도 부름을 받지 못한 임금의 조용한 아들.

blocks.caption: Gwishil Boksin. He raised a dead country once, and he kept the receipts.
blocks.ko: 귀실복신. 쓰러진 나라를 한 번 일으켰고, 영수증은 다 챙겨 두었다.

blocks.caption: The Eastern Prince. He does the arithmetic before anyone asks for it.
blocks.ko: 동쪽의 왕자. 누가 묻기 전에 셈부터 한다.

lines: …그건 첫 장일 뿐이고요. 나머지 셈은 언제 내놓는답니까?
en: A hundred prisoners. Generous.
…That’s the first page, though. When do they show us the rest of the bill?
ja: 捕虜百人とは。気前のよいことだ。
……それは一枚目にすぎぬ。残りの勘定はいつ出てくる。
jaLatn: Horyo hyakunin to wa. Kimae no yoi koto da.
…Sore wa ichimaime ni suginu. Nokori no kanjō wa itsu dete kuru.

blocks.html: The envoy tells him. Soldiers, and the prince. Every head in the hall turns to the prince, who has lived in this palace for twenty years and who discovers that he has been sitting very straight.
blocks.ko: 사신이 답한다. 군사, 그리고 왕자. 전각 안의 모든 고개가 왕자에게로 돌아간다. 이 궁에서 스무 해를 산 그는, 자기가 아까부터 몹시 꼿꼿이 앉아 있었다는 걸 그제야 안다.

blocks.caption: Yamato’s admiral of the cold north. He has fought on ice. He has not fought on this river.
blocks.ko: 북쪽 찬 바다의 야마토 제독. 얼음 위에서는 싸워 봤다. 이 강에서는 아니다.

lines: 보내 주시오! 나는 찬 바다를 건너 본 사람이오.
숙신 놈들 화살도 맞아 봤소. 서쪽 바다는 그냥 좀 따뜻할 뿐이지. 당나라 황제 모자라도 벗겨 오리다!
en: Send me! I’ve crossed the cold sea.
I’ve taken Mishihase arrows. The western sea’s only warmer. I’ll bring you back their emperor’s hat!
ja: わしを遣わされよ！ 冷たい海なら渡ってきた。
粛慎の矢も受けた。西の海はちと暖かいだけよ。唐の帝の冠でも剝いで参ろう！
jaLatn: Washi o tsukawasare yo! Tsumetai umi nara watatte kita.
Mishihase no ya mo uketa. Nishi no umi wa chito atatakai dake yo. Tō no mikado no kanmuri demo haide mairō!

lines: 어머님, 누가 묻기 전에 제가 먼저 묻겠습니다.
왕자. 저들이 원하는 게 그대요, 그대의 이름이오?
en: Before anyone asks him anything, Mother, I will.
Prince. Do they want you, or your name?
ja: 母上、誰より先に私がお尋ねします。
王子。あちらが欲しいのはそなたか、それともそなたの名か。
jaLatn: Hahaue, dare yori saki ni watakushi ga otazune shimasu.
Ōji. Achira ga hoshii no wa sonata ka, soretomo sonata no na ka.

lines: 저는 아직 백제의 아들입니다. 말을 몇 개… 잊었을 뿐이지요.
en: …Both, I expect. The name first.
I am still a son of Baekje. I have only… forgotten some of the words.

blocks.html: The empress has let all of it run: her son’s arithmetic, the admiral’s hat, the prince’s missing words. Then she speaks once.
blocks.ko: 여제는 그 모든 것을 흘려들었다. 아들의 셈도, 제독의 모자도, 왕자가 잃어버린 말들도. 그러고는 한 번 입을 연다.

blocks.caption: The Eastern Empress. She has outlived two reigns and most of her ministers’ opinions.
blocks.ko: 동쪽의 여제. 두 번의 치세와 대신들 의견 대부분보다 오래 살았다.

lines: 내 아들이 우리가 백제에 무엇을 빚졌는지 알고 싶어 하는구나.
그 칼을 가져오너라. 가지가 일곱인 것.
en: My son wants to know what we owe Baekje.
Bring him the sword. The one with seven branches.

blocks.html: Three hundred years ago a Baekje king sent the King of Wa a sword with seven branches. It was a gift. It was also a message.
blocks.ko: 삼백 년 전, 백제의 한 임금이 왜왕에게 가지가 일곱 달린 칼을 보냈다. 선물이었다. 전갈이기도 했다.

blocks.html: It is iron, two and a half feet long, with six branches off a central blade and sixty-one characters inlaid in gold down both sides. It has never been sharpened. It was never going to be.
blocks.ko: 쇠로 되어 있고 길이는 두 자 반, 가운데 몸통에서 가지 여섯이 뻗어 나오며, 앞뒤로 금상감한 글자 예순한 자가 있다. 한 번도 날을 세운 적이 없다. 애초에 세울 물건이 아니었다.

blocks.html: The inscription is the interesting part, because the two countries have spent fifteen hundred years disagreeing about a single verb: whether Baekje presented it upward, or bestowed it downward.
blocks.ko: 흥미로운 것은 명문이다. 두 나라가 천오백 년 동안 동사 하나를 두고 다투어 왔기 때문이다. 백제가 그것을 위로 바친 것인지, 아래로 내린 것인지.

en: Which is it?

lines: 그건 읽는 사람이 어느 나라 사람이냐에 달렸지.
en: That depends on which country is doing the reading.

blocks.html: What is not in dispute: Baekje sent scholars, craftsmen, weavers, horse-handlers, potters and the written word across that water for three hundred years. Nobody on either shore ever sent a bill.
blocks.ko: 다투지 않는 사실은 이렇다. 백제는 삼백 년 동안 그 바다 건너로 학자와 장인과 직공과 말 다루는 이와 옹기장이와 글자를 보냈다. 어느 쪽 바닷가에서도 값을 청구한 적은 없다.

lines: 군사를 청하는 일은 옛날부터 있었다. 쓰러지는 집을 붙드는 일은 그보다 더 오래되었지.
바다도 국경이다, 아들아. 서쪽 지붕에 불이 붙으면, 다음은 우리 처마야.
배를 내주어라. 저 아이에게는 관을 씌우고 아내를 붙여 보내라. 볼모 꼴로 도착하지 않게.
en: Asking for soldiers is old. Holding up a falling house is older.
The sea is also a border, my son. When the western roof catches, our eaves are next.
Give them the ships. Give the boy a cap of rank and a wife, so he does not arrive looking like a hostage.
ja: 援軍を乞うは古くからのこと。傾く家を支えるは、なお古い。
海もまた境ぞ、我が子よ。西の屋根に火がつけば、次はこちらの軒。
船を出せ。あの子には冠を授け、妻を添えて送れ。人質のような顔で着かぬように。
jaLatn: Engun o kou wa furuku kara no koto. Katamuku ie o sasaeru wa, nao furui.
Umi mo mata sakai zo, waga ko yo. Nishi no yane ni hi ga tsukeba, tsugi wa kochira no noki.
Fune o dase. Ano ko ni wa kanmuri o sazuke, tsuma o soete okure. Hitojichi no yō na kao de tsukanu yō ni.

blocks.html: Abe is out of the hall before the edict is copied. The prince goes to find a tailor. The eastern prince, who agrees with his mother on everything she has decided, writes the cost of it down on a separate sheet anyway.
blocks.ko: 칙서가 베껴지기도 전에 아베는 전각을 나가고 없다. 왕자는 재봉사를 찾으러 간다. 어머니가 정한 일이라면 무엇이든 따르는 동쪽 태자는, 그래도 그 값을 따로 한 장에 적어 둔다.

blocks.html: The empress died this summer, on her way west to see the fleet off. Her son keeps her promise anyway. Baekje’s refugees are coming home from everywhere they ran.
blocks.ko: 여제는 올여름, 함대를 배웅하러 서쪽으로 가던 길에 죽었다. 아들은 그래도 어머니의 약속을 지킨다. 백제의 피란민들이 흩어졌던 곳곳에서 돌아오고 있다.

blocks.label: Roll Call
blocks.ko: 점호

blocks.html: Juryu, the ninth month of 661. Prince Pung comes ashore below the fortress with a cap of rank, a Yamato wife, five thousand eastern soldiers and an admiral nobody asked for, and finds the founders of the restoration drawn up on the shingle to meet him. Boksin has written the order of introductions on a tally board. He has made them rehearse it twice.
blocks.ko: 주류, 661년 구월. 부여풍이 성 아래 자갈밭에 내린다. 관을 쓰고, 왜국 아내를 데리고, 동쪽 군사 오천과 아무도 청하지 않은 제독 하나를 거느리고. 부흥군을 세운 장수들이 자갈밭에 줄지어 그를 맞는다. 복신은 소개 순서를 목간에 적어 두었다. 연습도 두 번이나 시켰다.

blocks.html: Bad farmland, good cliffs. Rebels pick the cliffs.
blocks.ko: 농사엔 나쁘고 벼랑은 좋다. 반란군은 벼랑을 고른다.

blocks.html: The board begins with Boksin. The order lasts until Abe no Hirafu, who is not on it, leaps from the gunwale of the first boat into surf up to his knees, flings his arms wide in his wolf-fur and his red cape, and introduces himself to the fortress, the gulls and the Tang scouts on the far ridge.
blocks.ko: 목간은 복신으로 시작한다. 그 순서는, 목간에 이름도 없는 아베노 히라부가 첫 배 뱃전에서 무릎까지 오는 파도 속으로 뛰어내릴 때까지만 간다. 늑대 모피와 붉은 망토 차림으로 두 팔을 활짝 벌리고, 그는 성채와 갈매기들과 건너편 능선의 당나라 척후들에게 자기를 소개한다.

lines: 아베노 히라부요! 북쪽 찬 바다의 장군!
배 백팔십 척으로 에미시를 쓸었고, 숙신 놈들 화살은 이빨로 받았소! 다음은 당나라요! 하하!
en: Abe no Hirafu! General of the cold northern sea!
A hundred and eighty ships against the Emishi, and I caught Mishihase arrows in my teeth! Tang’s next! Ha!
ja: 阿倍比羅夫なり！ 北の冷たき海の将軍！
百八十艘で蝦夷を平らげ、粛慎の矢は歯で受け止めた！ 次は唐よ！ はっはっ！
jaLatn: Abe no Hirafu nari! Kita no tsumetaki umi no shōgun!
Hyakuhachijissō de Emishi o tairage, Mishihase no ya wa ha de uketometa! Tsugi wa Tō yo! Hahha!

en: You’re not on the board, Admiral.
…Lovely entrance, though.

blocks.html: Echi no Takutsu waits until the admiral has finished, which takes a while. Then he walks up the shingle, turns his back on the Baekje generals and bows to the sea he has just crossed, low and long, the tails of his white headband lifting in the wind, before he turns round and says the one thing he has prepared.
blocks.ko: 에치노 다쿠쓰는 제독이 다 끝낼 때까지 기다린다. 한참 걸린다. 그러고는 자갈밭을 걸어 올라가, 백제 장수들에게 등을 돌리고, 방금 건너온 바다를 향해 낮고 길게 절한다. 흰 머리띠 끝이 바람에 들린다. 그런 다음 돌아서서, 준비해 온 단 한 마디를 한다.

blocks.caption: A Yamato captain. Loud, loyal, and fond of a country that isn’t his.
blocks.ko: 야마토의 장수. 시끄럽고, 충성스럽고, 제 나라도 아닌 나라를 아낀다.

lines: 이 나라에서 내 이름을 아는 사람은 없소. 그러니 내 이름 대신 이 나라 이름을 외치겠소.
구다라 만세. 구다라에 목숨이 하나 필요하거든, 내 것부터 쓰시오.
en: No one in this country knows my name. So instead of mine, I will say yours.
Long live Kudara. If Kudara needs a life, begin with mine.
ja: この国に我が名を知る者はおらぬ。ならば我が名の代わりに、この国の名を叫ぼう。
百済万歳。百済に命が一つ要るなら、まず我がものを使われよ。
jaLatn: Kono kuni ni waga na o shiru mono wa oranu. Naraba waga na no kawari ni, kono kuni no na o sakebō.
Kudara banzai. Kudara ni inochi ga hitotsu iru nara, mazu waga mono o tsukaware yo.

en: …He means it.

blocks.html: Dochim introduces himself sitting down. He has found a flat rock above the tideline and settled on it in his red kasaya, the beads running through one hand and the gilt staff across his knees, and he smiles at the new king the way a monk smiles at a donor whose gift has not yet arrived.
blocks.ko: 도침은 앉은 채로 자기를 소개한다. 물때선 위 평평한 바위에 붉은 가사 차림으로 자리 잡고, 한 손으로 염주를 굴리며 금빛 석장을 무릎에 가로놓은 채, 아직 시주가 도착하지 않은 시주자에게 스님이 짓는 웃음을 새 임금에게 짓는다.

blocks.caption: Dochim. A monk with a general’s staff, in no hurry about either.
blocks.ko: 도침. 장수의 지팡이를 든 승려. 둘 다 서두르지 않는다.

lines: 도침입니다. 이제는 어느 절의 중도 아니고, 영군장군이라 불리지요.
부처님께서는 모든 것이 덧없다 하셨습니다. 사비의 당나라 군도 그 모든 것 가운데 하나입니다.
내일 새벽에 떠납니다. 오늘 밤은 푹 주무십시오.
en: Dochim. A monk of no temple, now. They call me General of the Spirit Army.
The Buddha taught that all things are impermanent. The Tang garrison at Sabi is one of those things.
We march at dawn. Do sleep well tonight.

blocks.html: Boksin, who did not write “General of the Spirit Army” on the board, makes a small mark beside it.
blocks.ko: 목간에 ‘영군장군’이라고 쓴 적 없는 복신이, 그 옆에 작은 표시를 하나 한다.

blocks.html: Heukchi Sangji is seven feet tall. The autumn Sabi fell he walked into Imjon with a handful of men and walked out ten days later with thirty thousand, and he regards the whole business of a roll call as a kind of weather. When his turn comes he steps forward exactly one pace.
blocks.ko: 흑치상지는 키가 칠 척이다. 사비가 무너진 가을, 그는 몇 안 되는 사람을 데리고 임존성에 들어가 열흘 만에 삼만을 데리고 나왔다. 그에게 점호 같은 건 날씨 비슷한 것이다. 차례가 오자 그는 정확히 한 걸음 앞으로 나선다.

blocks.caption: Heukchi Sangji. The biggest man on the beach, and the hardest to line up.
blocks.ko: 흑치상지. 해변에서 제일 큰 사내, 그리고 줄 세우기 제일 어려운 사내.

en: Heukchi Sangji. Imjon.
…That’s it.

lines: 장군, 팔. 팔 동작 말입니다. 얘기했잖습니까.
en: The arms, General. We discussed the arms.
You discussed the arms.

blocks.caption: A Satek with harbour money and a general’s patience.
blocks.ko: 항구의 돈과 장군의 인내를 가진 사택.

blocks.html: Satek Sangya has worn the tall gilt cap of his house for the occasion, which is the only concession he makes to it. He does not look up from the ledger.
blocks.ko: 사택상여는 이날을 위해 집안의 높은 금동관을 쓰고 나왔다. 그가 이날에 해 주는 양보는 그게 전부다. 그는 장부에서 눈을 들지 않는다.

lines: 사택상여. 배 마흔 척, 쌀 천백 섬, 화살 삼만, 밧줄은 세다 말았고.
아직 아무도 값을 안 쳤어. 이게 내 인사요.
en: Satek Sangya. Forty boats, eleven hundred bales of rice, thirty thousand arrows, and I stopped counting the rope.
Nobody has paid me yet. That’s my pose.

blocks.html: Then Gwishil Boksin, who wrote the board, steps out in front of all of them, plants the red shaft in the shingle and does the arms exactly as rehearsed.
blocks.ko: 그리고 목간을 쓴 귀실복신이 모두의 앞으로 나와 붉은 자루를 자갈에 꽂고, 연습한 그대로 팔 동작을 해 보인다.

lines: 귀실복신. 나라가 쓰러졌을 때 한 번 일으켰고, 두 번 쓰러지면 두 번 일으킬 사람이오.
선왕께서 바라신 일입니다, 전하. 장안에서, 마지막에. 저희도 들었습니다.
en: Gwishil Boksin. I raised this country once when it fell, and if it falls twice I’ll raise it twice.
Your father asked for this, Majesty. In Chang’an, at the end. We heard.
Welcome home. Your army.

blocks.html: Everyone looks at the king. Nobody has given Pung a line. He has been in the country for less than an hour and has spent most of it being bowed at, and he ad-libs.
blocks.ko: 모두가 왕을 본다. 풍에게 대사를 준 사람은 아무도 없다. 이 땅에 내린 지 한 시진도 안 되었고, 그동안 절만 받았다. 그는 즉석에서 지어낸다.

lines: 나는 부여풍. 의자왕의 아들이고… 백제의, 그… 왕이다.
en: I am Buyeo Pung, son of King Euija, and… king of— of Baekje.
…Is that right? Is “restoration” the word?
Close enough, Majesty.

blocks.html: Boksin counts them in. “Baekje— Restoration— Army!” Takutsu and the admiral land it perfectly, which is embarrassing for everyone else. Dochim does half and goes back to his beads. Sangya is still counting. Sangji folds his arms, which is at least an arm. The new king is a beat late and on the wrong foot.
blocks.ko: 복신이 박자를 센다. “백제— 부흥— 군!” 다쿠쓰와 제독은 완벽하게 해낸다. 나머지 모두가 민망해진다. 도침은 반쯤 하다 말고 염주로 돌아간다. 상여는 아직 세는 중이다. 상지는 팔짱을 낀다. 그래도 팔은 팔이다. 새 임금은 한 박자 늦고, 발도 반대다.

blocks.html: They try it twice more before supper. For the second, Boksin puts the king on a rock in the middle so that everyone is at least pointing at the same man, and Abe lifts Sangji off the ground to make the shape symmetrical, which nobody asked for and Sangji does not forgive. For the third, Dochim declines to stand, Sangya sits down on the rice, and the king, finally, gets the arms right, a beat after everyone else has stopped.
blocks.ko: 저녁 전까지 두 번 더 해 본다. 두 번째에는 복신이 왕을 한가운데 바위 위에 올려 세운다. 적어도 모두가 같은 사람을 가리키게 하려고. 아베는 모양을 맞추겠다며 상지를 땅에서 번쩍 들어 올린다. 아무도 부탁하지 않았고, 상지는 용서하지 않는다. 세 번째에는 도침이 일어서기를 사양하고, 상여는 쌀가마 위에 주저앉고, 왕은 마침내 팔 동작을 제대로 해낸다. 다들 멈추고 한 박자 뒤에.

blocks.title: Restoration Army · 백제부흥군
blocks.caption: King at the apex and four founding generals beneath — five captains, one lost country.
blocks.ko: 왕 아래 네 장군 — 부흥군 오장, 나라 하나.

blocks.html: On the far ridge two Tang scouts watch the whole performance, and that night Liu Rengui files their report under morale.
blocks.ko: 건너편 능선에서 당나라 척후 둘이 이 공연을 처음부터 끝까지 지켜본다. 그날 밤 유인궤는 그 보고를 ‘사기(士氣)’ 항목에 철해 둔다.

blocks.html: That evening, on the wall, the new king finds his general alone.
blocks.ko: 그날 저녁, 성벽 위에서 새 왕은 홀로 있는 장군을 찾아낸다.

lines: 아버님이 나를 보내며 한마디 하셨소. “내가 너를 필요로 할 때까지.”
…다른 사람이 나를 필요로 하게 될 거라고는 말씀하지 않으셨소.
en: My father sent me away with a sentence. “Until I need you.”
…He did not say it would be somebody else who needed me.
Somebody always does, Majesty.
Sleep. We crown you tomorrow.

blocks.html: Pung was the only prince left, so they crowned him the next day, in the fortress hall, in a cap the Yamato tailor made. Boksin did the crowning. The Yamato men call him Pungjang. Baekje learns to.
blocks.ko: 남은 왕자가 풍뿐이라, 이튿날 성의 전각에서, 왜의 재봉사가 지은 관을 씌워 그를 왕으로 세웠다. 관을 씌운 사람은 복신이다. 왜 사람들은 그를 풍장이라 부른다. 백제도 따라 배운다.

blocks.html: The crown is Pung’s. The army is Boksin’s. Everyone can see the arithmetic of that, including both of them.
blocks.ko: 왕관은 풍의 것이고, 군사는 복신의 것이다. 그 셈은 누구 눈에나 보인다. 두 사람 눈에도.

blocks.label: The Tang Walls
blocks.ko: 당군 성벽

blocks.html: Boksin sends a messenger to the Tang walls with a question.
blocks.ko: 복신이 당의 성벽으로 사자를 보내 묻는다.

lines: 날만 말씀하시오. 제대로 배웅해 드리고 싶으니.
en: When are you gentlemen going home, Ambassador?
Name the day. We’d like to see you off properly.

lines: 손님은 주인이 제 집을 건사할 수 있을 때 떠나는 법이오. 이 집 주인은 왕이 둘에 군대가 하나, 지붕은 없소. 저녁은 먹고 가겠소.
en: Tell him we are guests.
Guests leave when the host can keep his own house. This host has two kings, one army and no roof. We’ll stay for dinner.
zh: 主人能守其家，客乃去。此家二主一軍，無屋可遮。我們留下吃晚飯。
zhLatn: Gàosu tā, wǒmen shì kè.
Zhǔrén néng shǒu qí jiā, kè nǎi qù. Cǐ jiā èr zhǔ yì jūn, wú wū kě zhē. Wǒmen liúxià chī wǎnfàn.

blocks.label: Pisong
blocks.ko: 피성

blocks.html: Then Prince Pung wants to move house.
blocks.ko: 그러다 풍왕이 집을 옮기고 싶어 한다.

lines: 이 주류는 농토에서 멀고, 땅은 돌뿐이오. 여기 있다간 백성이 굶소.
en: This Juryu lies far from farmland. The soil is stone. The people will starve up here.

lines: 아래로 내려가면 굶기 전에 먼저 죽을 거요, 전하.
en: They will starve slower than they will die down there, Majesty.

lines: 피성에는 물이 있소. 쌀도 있고. 둘레에 둑도—
en: Pisong has water. Rice. Embankments all round it—
Pisong is one night’s march from the enemy.
I am the king. We move.
Then we move, Majesty.

blocks.html: They move. Two months later Silla takes the towns to the south in an afternoon, and the whole restoration climbs back up to the barren hill it left.
blocks.ko: 그들은 옮긴다. 두 달 뒤 신라가 남쪽 고을들을 한나절 만에 가져가고, 부흥군 전체가 떠났던 그 메마른 산으로 도로 기어오른다.

blocks.html: The men move once, move back, and start looking at each other differently.
blocks.ko: 군은 한 번 옮겼다가 되돌아왔고, 그 뒤로 서로를 보는 눈이 달라진다.

blocks.html: Boksin says nothing on the road back up. He doesn’t need to. Everyone saw who was right, and everyone saw who wore the crown.
blocks.ko: 다시 오르는 길에 복신은 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 할 필요가 없다. 누가 옳았는지 모두 보았고, 누가 관을 썼는지도 모두 보았다.

blocks.html: Baekje has its king back, and a general who already regrets it. Now the emperor turns north, to walls that have never fallen…!
blocks.ko: 백제는 왕을 되찾았고, 벌써 그걸 후회하는 장군도 얻었다. 이제 황제는 북쪽으로, 한 번도 무너진 적 없는 성벽으로 고개를 돌린다…!

toneNote: Sieges, rivers, winters — the war grinds until only endurance is left.
title: The Final Stand

logline.en: A red gate on a grey ridge. There is only one gate anyone remembers.
logline.ko: 회색 능선 위의 붉은 문. 사람들이 기억하는 문은 그 하나뿐이다.

images.alt: Poster key art: Yeon Gesomun stands on the red gate of Pyongyang at dusk with the three-legged crow on his shoulder, both staring west
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; crowns, antlers, wings and heads stay well inside the central band; no title, no lettering. Dusk on the ridge wall of Pyongyang: the red two-storey munru gate pavilion, grey stone ramparts, storm clouds. Low angle from the wall walk. INTERACTION: Yeon Gesomun stands on the parapet in red-and-black robes with his crow swords fanned on his back, one boot up on the stone, and the black three-legged crow Samjogo sits on his shoulder (three legs — exactly three) pressing its head against his cheek; he reaches up with two fingers and strokes its breast, both of them staring west at the coming storm. One red sunset break (#d0362f) under the cloud lights his face, the crow and the gate’s red timbers; the rest falls into ink. STYLE: HEEWON STYLE, more painterly, with hints of Korean ink painting — Korean webtoon figures (clean ink linework, simplified expressive faces matching the attached portrait, watercolor-washed) inside a hand-painted world of watercolor and oil with traditional sumukhwa ink: splashed-ink storm clouds, bold dry calligraphic brush strokes in manes, fur, feathers, robes and grass, ink bleeding into wet wash, small ink splatters and drips near the frame edges, patches of bare rice paper where the edges dissolve; oil glazes only deepen the darks, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. Movie-poster key art: bold iconic silhouette, the two subjects large and close, one dramatic low angle, one bright break of light behind them, big dark masses, few hues plus one accent, film-poster drama but NO text, NO title, NO credits, NO logo, NO seal stamp. Not photoreal, not 3D. No glow aura, no halo, no emissive outline — the accent colour is real light. One of each named person. No watermark. CANON — YEON GESOMUN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_gesomun.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Massive, broad-chested; black hair in a tight topknot tied with red cord; thick black beard trimmed close to the jaw, heavy brows, glaring eyes. Dress: Dark charcoal robe and trousers under red-edged armor, a red cape falling off the shoulders. Demeanor: Arrogant, theatrical, loud; looks down at people (worm's-eye suits him). Laughs while fighting. Sword: High Commander Blade — Ring-pommel High Commander Blade — haetae carved beneath the crow stamp; the 막리지검 of the Summit’s first chair. Pommel motif crow inside the small ring (name only; do not attach the pommel ECU). Carry: FIVE crow-ring swords (身佩五刀): four crossed in a fan on his back with the hilts rising above his shoulders, plus one at the hip. Fighting: DUAL-WIELDS: a crow-ring sword in EACH hand, both forward one-hand grips, ring pommels at the heel of each fist. Wide aggressive stance, arms flung apart, scissoring cross-cuts and windmill slashes; lose one blade and he pulls another off his back. Each blade straight sw_bidam anatomy, 1:3. #d0362f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: one sword in a fight; gold-plated armor; beardless face (except a flashback to youth). | SAMJOGO (삼족오, three-legged crow, guardian of Goguryeo, guide of jumong) — attached board /obj_samjogo.png: Black three-legged crow — always THREE legs visible; red sun motif as the one accent — match the board. Owned by no one; watches from branches and far banks, flies ahead to show Jumong the way. | PLACE pyongyang_fortress — attached board /pl_pyongyang_fortress.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Pyongyang fortress: the same red two-tier munru on the stone ridge in every still. | SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS are a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST room (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt) painted in that same wash-and-glaze: a warm umber-to-black ground, walls, timber, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft with soft sfumato falloff — the webtoon figures are set INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Pyongyang has never fallen. Every child in the city will tell you so, usually twice.
blocks.ko: 평양성은 한 번도 함락된 적이 없다. 성안의 아이라면 누구나 그렇게 말해 준다. 대개 두 번씩.

blocks.html: Red Sun's capital sits on its ridge: a red two-storey gate, grey stone, and clouds that always look about to pick a side. The last emperor tried these walls. So did the one before him. The walls are still here.
blocks.ko: 붉은 해의 도성이 능선 위에 앉아 있다. 붉은 이층 문루, 회색 돌, 어느 편을 들지 막 정하려는 듯한 구름. 지난 황제도 이 성벽을 두드렸다. 그 전 황제도 그랬다. 성벽은 아직 그대로다.

blocks.caption: A fleet up the river, an army at the Amnok, and a winter about to pick a side.
blocks.ko: 강을 거슬러 오르는 함대, 압록강의 군대, 그리고 곧 편을 고를 겨울.

blocks.label: The Wall
blocks.ko: 성벽

blocks.html: Up on the wall, Gesomun's second son is explaining this to a sentry who did not ask.
blocks.ko: 성벽 위에서 연개소문의 둘째 아들이, 묻지도 않은 보초에게 그 이야기를 해 주고 있다.

blocks.caption: Gesomun’s second son. Loud, loyal, and he believes everything he’s told twice.
blocks.ko: 연개소문의 둘째 아들. 목소리가 크고, 충직하고, 들은 말은 두 번씩 믿는다.

lines: 성왕께서 활을 메신 이래 칠백 년 동안 그랬듯이.
en: Pyongyang does not fall.
Not since the Holy King strung his bow. Seven hundred years.
You said that yesterday.
It was true yesterday too.

blocks.html: Their father walks the wall behind them with a scout’s report in his fist. A Mohe man walks one step behind him, as he has for twenty-seven years. Nobody introduces Gulgul. Nobody ever has.
blocks.ko: 그 뒤로 아버지가 정찰 보고를 주먹에 쥔 채 성벽을 걷는다. 말갈 사내 하나가 한 걸음 뒤에서 따라 걷는다. 스물일곱 해째 그 자리다. 아무도 걸걸을 소개하지 않는다. 한 번도 그런 적이 없다.

lines: 짐승 네 마리를 보냈단다. 이제 황제가 짐승을 부려.
그중 한 놈은 아들들을 데려왔다. 열세 놈 전부.
en: Four beasts, it says. The emperor sends animals now.
One of them brought his sons. All thirteen of them.
Thirteen? He brought children to a war?
Not children. Grown men.
They came to watch their father work.

blocks.html: He says it the way other men mention rain. Then he goes down the stairs to send his eldest north, to hold the river.
blocks.ko: 다른 사람들이 비 온다는 말 하듯 그렇게 말한다. 그러고는 계단을 내려가, 맏아들을 북쪽 강으로 보낸다.

blocks.label: Luoyang
blocks.ko: 낙양

blocks.html: In Luoyang the Third Emperor announces that he will lead the next army himself. The Empress sends up a memorial the same night.
blocks.ko: 낙양에서 황제가 다음 원정은 친히 이끌겠다고 선포한다. 황후는 그날 밤 상소를 올린다.

lines: 소릉의 여섯 마리 말한테 어떻게 됐는지 물어보세요.
en: Your father went in person, Majesty.
Ask the six horses at Zhaoling how that went.
zh: 陛下去問昭陵那六匹馬，結果如何。
zhLatn: Xiāndì yì céng qīnzhēng, Bìxià.
Bìxià qù wèn Zhāolíng nà liù pǐ mǎ, jiéguǒ rúhé.

en: …We will send someone.
zhLatn: …Zhèn qiǎn rén qù.

blocks.label: The Taedong
blocks.ko: 대동강

blocks.html: The someone is the Red Fowl, the old steppe horseman who took Sabi. He comes up the Taedong from the sea in the eighth month and takes the river forts one by one. Then he sits down in front of Pyongyang to wait for winter to soften it. Winter has never been on anybody’s side but Goguryeo’s.
blocks.ko: 그 다른 사람이 바로 주작이다. 사비를 무너뜨린 늙은 초원의 기병. 그는 팔월에 바다에서 대동강을 거슬러 올라와 강가의 성들을 하나씩 빼앗는다. 그러고는 평양성 앞에 눌러앉아 겨울이 성을 무르게 해 주기를 기다린다. 겨울은 고구려 말고는 누구 편도 들어 본 적이 없다.

lines: 아버지! 대동강에 돛입니다. 남쪽 성벽 바로 밑까지요!
en: Father! Sails on the Taedong, right up under the south wall!
…They’re sitting down. Why are they sitting down?

lines: 앉으라 그래. 엉덩이가 땅에 얼어붙을 때까지 앉아 있으라 그래.
en: Let them sit. Let them sit till their arses freeze to the ground.

blocks.label: The Frozen River
blocks.ko: 얼어붙은 강

blocks.html: Namseng holds the Amnok. He is twenty-seven, the heir, and he has read every record of every crossing.
blocks.ko: 남생이 압록강을 지킨다. 스물일곱, 후계자, 그리고 지금껏 있었던 모든 도하의 기록을 다 읽은 사람이다.

blocks.html: His orders are simple. Tens of thousands of picked men, one river, nobody across. On the far bank waits the White Dragon, the old emperor’s Turkish general. He once asked to be buried alive beside his master. They told him no. He has been looking for a useful place to die ever since.
blocks.ko: 명령은 간단하다. 정예 수만, 강 하나, 아무도 건너오지 못하게. 건너편 둑에는 백룡이 기다린다. 선제의 돌궐 장수다. 그는 한때 주군 곁에 산 채로 묻히게 해 달라고 청했다. 조정은 허락하지 않았다. 그 뒤로 그는 쓸모 있게 죽을 자리를 찾아다니는 중이다.

blocks.html: Then the ninth month turns cold. Not autumn cold. Wrong cold.
blocks.ko: 그러다 구월에 날이 추워진다. 가을 추위가 아니다. 잘못된 추위다.

blocks.speaker: officer
en: Commander. The shallows are white.
…The middle’s going too.

lines: 구월에 강이 단단히 언 적은 없다.
en: The river has never frozen hard in the ninth month.
Not in any record.

blocks.speaker: officer
en: Sir. The river hasn’t read the records.

blocks.html: At dawn the drums start on the far bank. The White Dragon does not build a bridge. He walks out onto the ice himself, leading his horse, and stamps twice.
blocks.ko: 새벽에 건너편 둑에서 북소리가 시작된다. 백룡은 다리를 놓지 않는다. 그는 말고삐를 쥐고 몸소 얼음 위로 걸어 나와, 발을 두 번 구른다.

blocks.html: It holds. His army follows him across a river that is no longer there, drumming as it comes. The first Goguryeo arrows skitter off the ice. The second volley never comes. Men who were told to guard water do not know how to guard a floor.
blocks.ko: 얼음은 버틴다. 그의 군대가 북을 치며 더는 강이 아닌 강을 건너온다. 고구려의 첫 화살은 얼음 위로 미끄러진다. 두 번째 화살은 끝내 날아가지 않는다. 물을 지키라는 명을 받은 병사들은 마룻바닥을 지키는 법을 모른다.

en: Hold the bank! Hold— the bank is—

blocks.html: There is no bank. There is only ice, and then there is everywhere. Namseng gets away with his life and very little else.
blocks.ko: 둑은 없다. 얼음뿐이고, 그다음엔 사방이 다 길이다. 남생은 목숨만, 그리고 그 밖에는 거의 아무것도 없이 빠져나온다.

blocks.label: The Gate
blocks.ko: 성문

blocks.html: He rides south all the way home and comes in through the fortress gate at dusk, on a borrowed horse. His father is waiting under the red gate. Gulgul holds the lamp.
blocks.ko: 그는 남쪽으로 줄곧 말을 달려, 해 질 녘 빌린 말을 타고 성문을 지나 돌아온다. 아버지가 붉은 문루 아래서 기다리고 있다. 걸걸이 등불을 들고 있다.

lines: 강 하나다, 남생아. 강 하나를 맡겼다.
얼 줄 몰랐다는 소리는 하지 마라. 거긴 해마다 언다.
en: One river, Namseng. I gave you one river.
Don’t tell me you didn’t know it would freeze. It freezes every year.
Not in the ninth month, Father. There is no precedent—
Precedent! The river can’t read, you idiot.

lines: 아버님, 형님이 병사들을 데리고 돌아왔습니다. 절반은—
en: Father, he brought the men home. Half of them—

lines: 절반. 갈 때는 전부 데리고 갔다.
en: Half. He left with all of them.

blocks.html: Nobody speaks. Namseng waits for the blow. He has been waiting for one since he was eleven, at the Liao, when an emperor’s men gave it to him instead.
blocks.ko: 아무도 말하지 않는다. 남생은 매를 기다린다. 열한 살 때 요하에서, 아버지 대신 황제의 사람들에게 매를 맞은 뒤로 그는 줄곧 그 매를 기다려 왔다.

blocks.html: It does not come. Gesomun lays a hand on the iron studs of the gate, the way you would test a horse’s leg.
blocks.ko: 매는 오지 않는다. 개소문은 말의 다리를 짚어 보듯, 성문의 쇠못 위에 손을 얹는다.

lines: 잘 들어. 성벽은 안 무너진다. 이걸 무너뜨린 놈은 아무도 없어.
이제 이 문은 네 거다. 네가 어느 쪽에 서 있는지 잊지 마라.
en: Listen. Walls don’t fall. Nobody’s ever knocked these down.
Gates get opened. From the inside.
This one’s yours now. Remember which side of it you’re standing on.
…Yes, Father.

blocks.html: Remember this gate. All three of his sons will.
blocks.ko: 이 문을 기억해 두시라. 그의 세 아들도 기억할 테니.

blocks.label: The Campfires
blocks.ko: 모닥불

blocks.html: The White Dragon goes back north the way he came, called away to some other war. The Red Fowl’s army freezes in the snow outside the walls. Every night Gesomun counts its campfires from the parapet. Every night there are fewer.
blocks.ko: 백룡은 다른 전쟁에 불려, 왔던 길로 북쪽으로 돌아간다. 주작의 군대가 성 밖 눈 속에서 얼어 간다. 개소문은 밤마다 성가퀴에서 적진의 모닥불을 센다. 밤마다 줄어 있다.

lines: 말을 잡아먹고 있는 거다. 말이 떨어지면 불도 줄지.
계속 세라, 걸걸. 불이 안 줄어드는 밤이 오면, 누가 저놈들을 먹이고 있는 거다.
en: They’re eating the horses. Fires go down when the horses run out.
Keep counting, Gulgul. The night they stop going down, somebody’s feeding them.
…Yes, sir.

blocks.label: Surabol
blocks.ko: 서라벌

blocks.html: In the twelfth month a letter comes down from the north. The Red Fowl is out of rice. Munmu reads it to his generals. Everyone in the room knows that road in winter. Nobody offers.
blocks.ko: 섣달에 북쪽에서 편지가 내려온다. 주작의 군량이 떨어졌다. 문무가 장수들 앞에서 편지를 읽는다. 그 방에 겨울의 그 길을 모르는 사람은 없다. 아무도 나서지 않는다.

lines: 저들이 저기서 굶어 죽으면, 황제는 누가 그렇게 뒀는지 기억할 것이오.
선왕께서 받으신 약속도 저들과 함께 굶어 죽소.
en: If they starve out there, the emperor will remember who let them.
And everything my father was promised starves with them.

blocks.html: Silence. Then Kim Yushin, who is sixty-six, gets up.
blocks.ko: 침묵. 그러다 예순여섯의 김유신이 자리에서 일어난다.

lines: 외숙. 외숙은 안 되오. 젊은 사람을 보내시오.
en: Uncle. Not you. Send someone younger.

lines: 젊은 사람들은 길을 모릅니다, 전하. 한슬이와 저는 압니다.
en: The younger ones don’t know the road, Majesty. Hanseul and I do.
Load the carts.

blocks.caption: Rice for the Red Fowl, through enemy country, in the dead of winter, driven by the oldest general in Silla.
blocks.ko: 주작에게 보낼 쌀. 적국을 가로질러, 한겨울에, 신라에서 가장 늙은 장수가 몬다.

blocks.html: The White Tiger has thirteen sons. Yeon Gesomun can count to thirteen…!
blocks.ko: 백호에게는 아들이 열셋 있다. 연개소문은 열셋까지 셀 줄 안다…!

logline.en: The White Tiger still believes rivers are roads. Yeon Gesomun has been waiting for a man who thinks that.
logline.ko: 백호는 아직도 강이 길이라고 믿는다. 연개소문은 그렇게 생각하는 사내를 기다려 왔다.
