So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.alt: A burning ship, a swordsman on its deck
ONE horizontal loaded brushstroke across the lower third, black sumi, bristles splitting so white paper shows through the stroke (flying white).
images.prompt: Minimal East Asian ink painting. Off-white paper, vast empty. ONE horizontal loaded brushstroke across the lower third, black sumi, bristles splitting so white paper shows through the stroke (flying white). The stroke is a river. A tiny boat is two marks on it, one small standing figure no taller than a fingernail, seen from far away, no face detail. Nothing else. No mountains, no trees, no seal, no calligraphy, no signature, no red stamp. Painterly dry brush, not a drawing, not a photograph.

blocks.html: Four banners come to one river mouth. Only the tide has been here before.
blocks.ko: 네 개의 깃발이 한 강어귀로 모여든다. 이곳에 와 본 것은 밀물뿐이다.

blocks.html: The White River empties into the western sea through sandbars that move like rumours. Whoever holds its mouth holds what is left of Baekje.
blocks.ko: 백강은 소문처럼 자리를 옮기는 모래톱들을 지나 서해로 흘러든다. 그 어귀를 쥔 자가 백제의 남은 것을 쥔다.

blocks.label: Four Banners
blocks.ko: 네 깃발

blocks.html: The Tang come by sea. The Black Tortoise has held the old capital for two winters with too few men. The emperor offered to bring him home. He wrote back that he’d rather not. So the emperor sent more.
blocks.ko: 당은 바다로 온다. 현무는 너무 적은 군사로 두 겨울 동안 옛 도읍을 지켰다. 황제가 돌아오라고 했다. 그는 사양한다는 답장을 썼다. 그래서 황제는 군사를 더 보냈다.

blocks.html: Silla comes by land. King Munmu rides out with Kim Yushin and every general he has. Yushin is sixty-eight and still sits a horse as if the horse had asked him to.
blocks.ko: 신라는 뭍으로 온다. 문무왕이 김유신과 가진 장수를 모두 이끌고 나선다. 유신은 예순여덟, 그런데도 말이 먼저 태워 달라고 청하기라도 한 듯 말 위에 앉아 있다.

blocks.html: Baekje is what is left of it: a hill fort called Juryu, a king raised overseas, and no Boksin.
blocks.ko: 백제는 남은 것이 전부다. 주류라는 산성 하나, 바다 건너에서 자란 왕 하나, 그리고 복신은 없다.

blocks.html: So the East sends sails. Hundreds of them, packed too tight to row. Takutsu is among the captains. He brought Pung home two years ago. Last winter he told him not to move the court down to the plain. He was right, and was thanked for it the way men usually are.
blocks.ko: 그래서 동쪽에서 돛이 온다. 수백 척, 노를 젓기도 힘들 만큼 빽빽하게. 다쿠쓰도 그 장수들 가운데 있다. 두 해 전 풍을 고국으로 데려온 사람이다. 지난겨울에는 도읍을 평지로 옮기지 말라고 왕에게 말했다. 그가 옳았고, 사람들이 대개 그렇듯 그 대가로 고맙다는 말만 들었다.

blocks.label: The King Leaves
blocks.ko: 왕이 떠나다

blocks.html: On the thirteenth day of the eighth month, with the Silla army already on the road to Juryu, the king of Baekje announces that he will leave it.
blocks.ko: 팔월 열사흘, 신라군이 이미 주류로 오는 길 위에 있는데, 백제왕은 주류를 떠나겠다고 선언한다.

en: Yamato’s relief general is crossing the sea with ten thousand men and more.
Generals, make ready for him.
I shall go down to the river mouth myself, and receive them there with a feast.
lines: 야마토의 구원장이 건아 만여를 이끌고 바다를 건너오고 있소.
과인은 몸소 강어귀로 내려가, 그들을 잔치로 맞겠소.

en: Majesty. And Juryu?
Juryu has walls.
…It had a general, too.

blocks.label: The Throat of the River
blocks.ko: 강의 목

blocks.html: At Ungjin the allied generals argue about where to begin. One fortress sits where the road crosses the river, and most of the room wants it first.
blocks.ko: 웅진에서 연합군 장수들은 어디서부터 시작할지를 두고 다툰다. 성 하나가 뭍길과 물길이 엇갈리는 자리에 앉아 있고, 좌중 대부분은 그곳부터 치자고 한다.

en: That fort is steep and strong.
Rush it and we bleed men. Sit under it and we bleed days.
Juryu is the nest. Pull the root, and the branches come down by themselves.
lines: 서두르면 군사를 잃고, 눌러앉으면 날을 잃소.
주류가 소굴이오. 뿌리를 뽑으면 가지는 저절로 떨어지오.

blocks.html: So the armies split. Most of the generals take the land road. The Black Tortoise takes the water: a hundred and seventy warships, heading for the river mouth. On his deck stands Buyeo Yung.
blocks.ko: 그래서 군은 갈라진다. 장수들 대부분은 뭍길을 탄다. 현무는 물을 맡는다. 전선 백칠십 척이 하구를 향해 내려간다. 그 갑판 위에 부여융이 서 있다.

blocks.title: Four banners, one river mouth
blocks.caption: Tang by sea twice, Silla by land, and the East arriving in a hurry. Everyone is headed for the same mud.
blocks.ko: 바다로 두 번 온 당, 땅으로 온 신라, 서둘러 오는 동쪽. 다들 같은 갯벌로 간다.

blocks.html: Euija’s eldest. He knelt at Sabi three summers ago, was taken to Chang’an with his father, and has come back in a Tang officer’s coat to fight his younger brother for the right to tell the survivors what happened to them. Nobody on the deck says this. Everybody on the deck knows it.
blocks.ko: 의자의 맏아들. 세 해 전 여름 사비에서 무릎을 꿇었고, 아버지와 함께 장안으로 끌려갔다가, 이제 당나라 장수의 옷을 입고 돌아와 아우와 싸운다. 살아남은 이들에게 그들에게 무슨 일이 있었는지 말해 줄 권리를 두고. 갑판 위의 누구도 이 말을 하지 않는다. 갑판 위의 누구나 그것을 안다.

en: Your brother’s banner will be on that fleet.
When it comes, can you look at it?
lines: 아우의 깃발이 저 함대에 있을 것이오.
그때가 오면, 그것을 볼 수 있겠소?

blocks.caption: Euija’s eldest son. Born to be crown prince. Born is not the same as stays.
blocks.ko: 의자의 맏아들. 태자로 태어났다. 태어난 것과 남는 것은 다르다.

en: I have looked at worse.
…I looked at my father.

blocks.html: The Black Tortoise has already learned the river's grammar. A narrow mouth. Sandbars that shift like lies. A current that punishes anyone who charges out of line. He anchors his hundred and seventy ships across the throat and waits. On the east bank, Kim Yushin's army keeps the shore from becoming a pier.
blocks.ko: 현무는 이미 강의 문법을 배웠다. 좁은 하구. 거짓말처럼 움직이는 모래톱. 대열 없이 덤비는 자를 벌하는 물살. 그는 백칠십 척을 목구멍에 가로질러 닻을 내리고 기다린다. 동쪽 기슭에서는 김유신의 군대가 그 기슭이 부두가 되지 않게 막는다.

blocks.label: The Shore
blocks.ko: 물가

blocks.html: On the south shore of the mouth the Baekje horsemen guard the landing. They are the last mounted men the restoration can field, drawn up in front of the beached hulls the way you stand in front of a door you cannot afford to lose. Silla’s cavalry comes at them first, out ahead of the Tang foot, because the king of Silla wants it written down later who went first.
blocks.ko: 강어귀 남쪽 기슭에서는 백제 기병이 상륙지를 지킨다. 부흥군이 말에 태울 수 있는 마지막 사람들이다. 잃어서는 안 되는 문 앞에 서듯, 뭍에 끌어올린 배들 앞에 늘어서 있다. 신라 기병이 당의 보병보다 앞서 먼저 들이친다. 누가 먼저 갔는지 훗날 적혀 있기를 신라왕이 바라기 때문이다.

lines: 배를 지키는 자는 그 배로 떠날 생각인 걸세.
en: Good riders. Guarding boats.
Men guard boats when they mean to leave in them.
Riders. With me.
When they write this down in Chang’an, I want Silla in the first line.
lines: 장안에서 이걸 적을 때, 첫 줄에 신라가 있어야 한다.

blocks.html: The shore camp goes in one charge. Yushin watches it from the ridge with the reins loose in one hand, which is how old generals watch something they no longer need to do themselves. Then he takes the foot south down the road to Juryu, and closes the ring.
blocks.ko: 강기슭의 진은 한 번의 돌격으로 무너진다. 유신은 고삐를 한 손에 느슨하게 쥔 채 능선에서 그것을 지켜본다. 이제는 몸소 할 필요가 없는 일을 늙은 장수들은 그렇게 지켜본다. 그러고는 보병을 이끌고 남쪽 길로 내려가 주류의 포위를 닫는다.

en: Those were my last horsemen.
…Then we have ships. Ships do not run.

blocks.label: The Twenty-Seventh Day
blocks.ko: 스무이렛날

blocks.html: The first Yamato ships to arrive do not wait for the rest. They come up out of the south-west and row straight at the Tang line on the evening water, and the Tang line does not move. It does not chase them, either. When the Yamato boats fall back, the hundred and seventy are exactly where they were that morning, in the same order, at anchor.
blocks.ko: 먼저 도착한 야마토의 배들은 나머지를 기다리지 않는다. 남서쪽 바다에서 올라와, 저녁 물을 타고 당의 대열로 곧장 저어 간다. 당의 대열은 움직이지 않는다. 쫓지도 않는다. 야마토의 배들이 물러났을 때, 백칠십 척은 아침에 있던 그 자리에 같은 순서로 닻을 내리고 있다.

blocks.html: The Black Tortoise has seen men of Wa once before, in the emperor's city. They were envoys in court silk, and they bowed in all the right places. The court kept them in a guesthouse for two winters, so they couldn't carry home where the fleet was going. These are their cousins. They row standing up. They shout from too far away. They charge a hundred and seventy anchored hulls in boats built for rice. Nobody in his army has fought them before. He watches the first wave break on his line like a scholar reading a new script. He is looking for the grammar.
blocks.ko: 현무는 왜인을 한 번 본 적이 있다. 황제의 도성에서였다. 비단 조복을 입은 사신들이었고, 절할 자리마다 꼬박꼬박 절했다. 조정은 그들을 두 겨울 동안 객관에 붙잡아 두었다. 함대가 어디로 가는지 고국에 전하지 못하게. 지금 저들은 그 사신들의 사촌쯤 된다. 선 채로 노를 젓는다. 소용없는 거리에서 고함을 지른다. 쌀 나르는 배로, 닻 내린 백칠십 척에 곧장 달려든다. 그의 군대에서 이들과 싸워 본 사람은 없다. 그는 첫 물결이 전열에 부서지는 것을 지켜본다. 처음 보는 글자를 읽는 학자처럼. 문법을 찾으면서.

en: General— those are Wa? They’re…
…they’re rowing standing up.
The last Wa I saw were bowing to the Son of Heaven.
Watch their oars, not their faces. The faces will stay brave all day.
lines: 내가 마지막으로 본 왜인은 천자께 절을 하고 있었지.
얼굴 말고 노를 봐라. 얼굴은 하루 종일 용감할 테니.

en: Nobody chases.
Tomorrow they will all come back together, and they will come angry.
lines: 내일 저들이 한꺼번에 돌아올 것이다. 화가 나서.

blocks.label: The Twenty-Eighth Day
blocks.ko: 스무여드렛날

blocks.html: That night the Yamato captains and the king of Baekje hold council on a deck, and nobody looks at the sky. Abe no Hirafu does most of the talking. He is the rear general, a big man in a wolf-fur mantle who spent three summers chasing the Emishi along the cold northern coast, and he has the habit of men who have lived through bad water: he believes the sea gives way to whoever moves first.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 야마토의 장수들과 백제왕은 갑판 위에서 군의를 연다. 아무도 하늘을 보지 않는다. 말은 대부분 아베노 히라부가 한다. 후장군인 그는 늑대 털 망토를 두른 덩치 큰 사내로, 세 해 여름을 북쪽 찬 바다 해안에서 에미시를 쫓으며 보냈다. 험한 물에서 살아 돌아온 사람들의 버릇이 그에게도 있다. 바다는 먼저 움직이는 쪽에 길을 내준다고 믿는 것이다.

en: Yesterday was the vanguard. Today it’s all of us!
Ha— we go first. Whoever hits first, the other side gives way. That’s the sea. Every sea.
lines: 어제 건 선봉이었소. 오늘은 전부 가는 거요!
하— 우리가 먼저 치는 거요. 먼저 들이받는 쪽 앞에서 저쪽은 물러나게 돼 있소. 바다란 게 그렇소. 어느 바다든.

en: …Yes. First.
Let them see the king’s ship at the front.
lines: 왕의 배가 맨 앞에 있는 것을 저들이 보게 하시오.

en: The tide turns before noon.
…Nobody is listening. Good. Then I will go first too.
lines: …아무도 듣지 않는군. 좋소. 그럼 나도 먼저 가겠소.

blocks.title: The Baekgang, eighth month, 663

units.label: Tang fire & crossbow
units.sub: waiting on the turn of tide

units.label: Buyeo Yung
units.sub: on the Tang deck, against his brother

blocks.note: Four charges into a formed Tang line, against the tide, in a river mouth too narrow for the eastern numbers. Smoke, flame, and a cinnabar sea.

blocks.label: The Tide
blocks.ko: 물때

blocks.html: Takutsu’s ship is in the first line. His rowers pull standing. The Tang hulls come up out of the haze like a wall, and do not move.
blocks.ko: 다쿠쓰의 배는 맨 앞줄에 있다. 노꾼들이 선 채로 노를 당긴다. 안개 속에서 당의 배들이 벽처럼 솟아오르고, 꿈쩍도 하지 않는다.

blocks.html: The first charge hits a wall of hulls and stops dead. Grapnels go over. Crossbows fire down from Tang decks built a man’s height higher. Takutsu’s men climb, fall back, and climb again.
blocks.ko: 첫 돌격이 선체의 벽에 부딪혀 그대로 멈춘다. 갈고리가 넘어간다. 사람 키 하나만큼 높게 지은 당의 갑판에서 쇠뇌가 내리꽂힌다. 다쿠쓰의 군사들이 기어오르다 떨어지고, 다시 기어오른다.

en: Back oars. Form again.
…The water is going slack.

blocks.html: The second charge goes in on slack water and comes out against the ebb, the current turning against them. Now the river is pushing the eastern ships back onto each other. Hulls grind. Oars snap against a neighbour’s oars. Nobody can turn.
blocks.ko: 두 번째 돌격은 물이 멎을 때 들어가 썰물을 거슬러 나온다. 물살이 그들을 거슬러 돌아선 것이다. 이제 강이 왜의 배들을 서로에게 밀어붙인다. 선체가 맞갈린다. 노가 옆 배의 노에 부딪혀 부러진다. 아무도 뱃머리를 돌리지 못한다.

blocks.html: On the Tang flagship, the Black Tortoise has waited all morning for exactly this. He says one word.
blocks.ko: 당의 기함에서 현무는 아침 내내 바로 이 순간을 기다렸다. 그는 한마디만 한다.

en: Now.

blocks.html: The arrows wrapped for flame go up white and come down burning. Ships pressed together turn one burning deck into a neighbourhood. On the third charge and the fourth, fire travels faster than orders. Four hundred eastern ships do not sink so much as spend themselves into light.
blocks.ko: 불을 감은 화살이 하얗게 솟았다가 불타며 떨어진다. 서로 맞붙은 배들 사이에서 불붙은 갑판 하나가 금세 한 동네가 된다. 세 번째, 네 번째 돌격에서는 불이 명령보다 빨리 번진다. 왜의 배 사백 척은 가라앉는다기보다 빛으로 타 없어진다.

blocks.hanja: 焚其舟四百艘 煙焰漲天 海水皆赤
blocks.ko: 그 배 사백 척을 불사르니, 연기와 불꽃이 하늘에 가득하고, 바닷물이 모두 붉었다.
blocks.html: They burned four hundred of their ships; smoke and flame filled the sky, and the seawater was all red.
blocks.source: Jiu Tangshu (舊唐書) bk. 84, Liu Renkui (劉仁軌) — Battle of the White River mouth (663) · cf. Samguk Sagi bk. 28, Baekje Annals: 煙炎灼天 海水爲丹

blocks.html: Then the wings close. The Tang ships that looked like a wall turn out to have been a door with two leaves, and they swing shut from left and right around the Yamato centre, so tight that the eastern ships cannot turn bow or stern, and men who cannot row and cannot climb go into the water in their armour.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 양 날개가 닫힌다. 벽처럼 보이던 당의 배들은 알고 보니 두 짝짜리 문이었고, 그 문이 좌우에서 야마토의 중군을 감싸며 닫힌다. 너무 빽빽해서 왜의 배들은 이물도 고물도 돌리지 못하고, 노를 저을 수도 기어오를 수도 없는 사람들이 갑옷을 입은 채로 물에 뛰어든다.

blocks.html: From the king’s ship Pung can see the Tang flagship. On its deck, in a Tang coat, stands his elder brother.
blocks.ko: 왕의 배에서 풍은 당의 기함을 볼 수 있다. 그 갑판 위에, 당나라 옷을 입고, 그의 형이 서 있다.

lines: 융… 네가 우리 강에서 저들의 옷을 입고 있구나…!
en: Yung… you wear their coat on our river…!
Long live Kudara — Land of the Heavenly Deer….!
ja: 百済万歳……！
jaLatn: Kudara banzai…!

blocks.html: His ship is burning under him and he does not leave it. He fights on the deck until there is not enough deck left to fight on.
blocks.ko: 발밑의 배가 타고 있는데 그는 배를 떠나지 않는다. 싸울 갑판이 남지 않을 때까지 갑판 위에서 싸운다.

en: Baekje must survive….
ja: 百済は生き残らねばならない……。
jaLatn: Kudara wa ikinokoraneba naranai….

blocks.hanja: 朴市田來津仰天而誓，切齒而嗔，殺數十人，於焉戰死。
blocks.html: Echi no Takutsu looked up to heaven and swore an oath, gnashed his teeth in fury, killed some dozens of men, and there fell in battle.
blocks.ko: 에치노 다쿠쓰는 하늘을 우러러 맹세하고 이를 갈며 성내어 수십 명을 죽이고, 거기서 싸우다 죽었다.
blocks.source: Nihon Shoki (日本書紀) bk. 27, Tenji 2 (663), eighth month

en: Hold the line. Let the tide finish what the bowstrings began.
A river mouth is a judge. Today it judged the East.
lines: 대열을 지켜라. 활시위가 시작한 일을 밀물이 끝내게 두어라.

blocks.html: At the back of the fleet Abe no Hirafu’s ships are still afloat. He has seen a lost tide before, on a colder sea. He turns them for home and hauls in every swimmer the hulls will carry, men in half their armour, men with no oars, and he does not laugh again until Tsukushi.
blocks.ko: 함대 맨 뒤에서 아베노 히라부의 배들은 아직 떠 있다. 진 물때는 전에도 본 적이 있다. 더 찬 바다에서. 그는 뱃머리를 고향으로 돌리고, 배가 버틸 수 있는 만큼 헤엄치는 자들을 끌어올린다. 갑옷을 반쯤 벗은 자, 노도 없는 자. 그리고 쓰쿠시에 닿을 때까지 다시는 웃지 않는다.

blocks.label: Brothers
blocks.ko: 형제

blocks.html: In the smoke a small boat gets away from the king’s ship with a handful of men in it and turns north. It is Pung. He leaves behind his fleet, his allies, his capital on the hill, and his sword.
blocks.ko: 연기 속에서 작은 배 한 척이 몇 사람을 태우고 왕의 배를 빠져나와 북쪽으로 머리를 돌린다. 풍이다. 그는 함대도, 동맹도, 언덕 위의 도읍도, 그리고 제 칼도 두고 간다.

blocks.html: They bring the sword to the Tang flagship. It is a Baekje ring-pommel blade with the ring worn smooth, nothing like a king’s, and the Black Tortoise hands it to the one man aboard who would know.
blocks.ko: 칼은 당의 기함으로 올라온다. 고리가 닳아 매끈해진 백제의 환두대도다. 왕의 칼 같은 데는 하나도 없다. 현무는 그것을 배 위에서 알아볼 단 한 사람에게 건넨다.

en: Whose?
…My brother’s.
Our father gave it to him the year they sent him east. He was seven.
lines: 동쪽으로 보내던 해에 아버지께서 주셨소. 일곱 살이었소.

en: Shall I send boats after him?
…North is Goguryeo. Let Goguryeo keep him.
He was always better at being sent away than I was.
lines: 그 애는 늘 나보다 떠나보내지는 데 능했소.

blocks.label: Juryu
blocks.ko: 주류

blocks.html: Juryu holds ten more days without its king. Then it opens its gate. Pung’s younger brothers walk out at the head of what is left: soldiers, women, the Yamato men who missed the boats, and an envoy from Tamla who came up the hill to bargain for an island and is now surrendering for it.
blocks.ko: 주류는 왕 없이 열흘을 더 버틴다. 그러고는 성문을 연다. 풍의 아우들이 남은 것들의 맨 앞에서 걸어 나온다. 군사들, 여자들, 배를 놓친 야마토 사람들, 그리고 섬 하나를 흥정하러 산을 올랐다가 이제 그 섬을 위해 항복하는 탐라의 사신.

blocks.html: The people who are not surrendering go south, to the port where the Yamato ships will take them off. On the road they say the thing to one another that the Yamato chronicle wrote down, because nobody was left in Baekje to write it.
blocks.ko: 항복하지 않는 사람들은 남쪽으로, 야마토의 배가 그들을 태워 갈 포구로 간다. 길 위에서 그들은 서로에게 그 말을 한다. 야마토의 사서가 받아 적은 말이다. 백제에는 그것을 적을 사람이 남지 않았으니까.

blocks.hanja: 州柔降矣，事無奈何。百濟之名，絕于今日。丘墓之所，豈能復往。
blocks.html: Juryu has surrendered. Nothing more can be done. The name of Baekje ends today. The place of our ancestors’ graves — how can we ever go back to it?
blocks.ko: 주류가 항복하였으니 일은 어찌할 수 없다. 백제의 이름은 오늘로 끊어졌다. 조상의 무덤이 있는 곳을 어찌 다시 갈 수 있으랴.
blocks.source: Nihon Shoki (日本書紀) bk. 27, Tenji 2 (663), ninth month

blocks.label: Imjon
blocks.ko: 임존성

blocks.html: One fortress doesn’t hear it. Its commander shuts the gate and holds all autumn, and the siege goes home. Then two Baekje generals walk into the Tang camp and ask for their armour back.
blocks.ko: 한 성만은 그 말을 듣지 않는다. 성주는 문을 닫고 가을 내내 버티고, 포위군은 돌아간다. 그러다 백제 장수 둘이 당의 진영으로 걸어 들어와 제 갑옷을 돌려 달라고 한다.

lines: 흑치상지. 그대 이름은 이미 내 명부에 있소.
살아 있는 편이 기록이 깔끔하오. 왜 지금이오?
en: Heukchi Sangji. Your name is in my register already.
It reads better with you alive. Why now?

lines: 그다음엔 그 손이 북쪽으로 노 젓는 걸 봤고요.
en: I watched the king’s hands at Juryu.
Then I watched them row north.

blocks.html: The Black Tortoise hands back their armour and points them up the slope.
blocks.ko: 현무는 그들에게 갑옷을 돌려주고 비탈 위를 가리킨다.

en: The north wall is the low one.
I built it.

blocks.html: Imjon falls to its own people’s hands. Its commander leaves his wife and children inside and goes north to Goguryeo, which by now is where Baekje’s last kings go.
blocks.ko: 임존성은 제 나라 사람 손에 떨어진다. 성주는 아내와 자식들을 성안에 두고 북쪽 고구려로 간다. 이제 백제의 마지막 왕들이 가는 곳이 그곳이다.

blocks.html: When the water cools to ordinary colour again, the restoration has no fleet worth the word. The Black Tortoise sits down with Kim Yushin. Neither of them believes a word the other says, and they get a great deal done — which is how alliances sound after four hundred ships have paid for the silence.
blocks.ko: 물이 다시 평범한 빛으로 식으면, 부흥에는 함대라 부를 것이 없다. 현무가 김유신과 마주 앉는다. 둘 다 상대의 말을 한마디도 믿지 않으면서, 아주 많은 것을 정한다 — 배 사백 척이 그 침묵의 값을 치른 뒤의 동맹이란 그런 소리다.

blocks.html: Two reapers failed to take Yeon Gesomun at the river. The ledger still has his name in it…!
blocks.ko: 두 저승사자는 강에서 연개소문을 데려가지 못했다. 장부에는 아직 그의 이름이 적혀 있다…!

logline.en: The Eternal General is dying.
logline.ko: 영원의 대장군이 죽어 가고 있다.

images.alt: Aged Gesomun on a timber deathbed talking; calm Yumla stands at the bedside — only these two, one violet lamp
images.prompt: Painterly anime-adjacent cinema, halfway realistic. Intimate 16:9. Pitch-black room, one violet lamp. Aged Gesomun LIES on a low timber deathbed. Yumla STANDS leaning down to talk. Violet #7c3aed. Only these two. No text. No watermark.

images.alt: The attached portrait is a likeness hint only.
images.prompt: Traditional sumi on bare Xuan paper, real brush bones: pressed start, thick belly, dry split tail, flying white. Not a modern graphic. The attached portrait is a likeness hint only. Do not paste it. ONE device: a low horizontal bed-stroke. An old man lies on it, a few bony marks, beard a dry flick. A second tiny figure stands at the head, leaning. One violet-dark lamp speck, real pigment, not a glow. Vast empty paper. No text, no seal, no watermark.

images.alt: The Eternal General on his deathbed, his sons gathered close
images.prompt: Cinematic historical illustration of yeon deathbed, Three Kingdoms of Samhan / Tang era (665), scene: The Death of Yeon Gesomun, painterly digital art, dramatic natural light, rich period costume, no modern elements, no text, no watermark, --ar 3:2 --stylize 250

images.at: That is precisely why I am telling you.
images.alt: Mantegna’s Lamentation: Gesomun dying, foreshortened from his feet, his crow swords on the wall above, his sons at the edge
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. POSE: Mantegna’s Lamentation of Christ. Extreme foreshortening from the foot of the bed: Yeon Gesomun lies on his back on a low bed under a red coverlet, old now, the soles of his bare feet huge in the foreground, his head raised a little on the pillow, eyes open and hard. On the black wall above the bed his five crow-ring swords hang in their scabbards, two drawn a hand-width so the steel shows. At the left edge his sons Namseng and Namgun lean in, faces half lit. One oil lamp beside the pillow is the only light, raking along his body and up the bared steel; the room drowns in black. Encased in darkness: at least 80% of the frame is near-black umber void, the figures pulled out of it by one hard raking key. Old-master tenebrist canvas (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour oil brushwork, glazed umber-black darks, impasto on the brightest highlight, canvas grain; silk brushed in loaded strokes; only faces and hands keep clean webtoon ink line. The steel glistens: the key runs down every blade as one long white-hot streak with a tiny star-glint on the edge. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — YEON GESOMUN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_gesomun.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Massive, broad-chested; black hair in a tight topknot tied with red cord; thick black beard trimmed close to the jaw, heavy brows, glaring eyes. Dress: Dark charcoal robe and trousers under red-edged armor, a red cape falling off the shoulders. Demeanor: Arrogant, theatrical, loud; looks down at people (worm's-eye suits him). Laughs while fighting. Sword: High Commander Blade — Ring-pommel High Commander Blade — haetae carved beneath the crow stamp; the 막리지검 of the Summit’s first chair. Pommel motif crow inside the small ring (name only; do not attach the pommel ECU). Carry: FIVE crow-ring swords (身佩五刀): four crossed in a fan on his back with the hilts rising above his shoulders, plus one at the hip. Fighting: DUAL-WIELDS: a crow-ring sword in EACH hand, both forward one-hand grips, ring pommels at the heel of each fist. Wide aggressive stance, arms flung apart, scissoring cross-cuts and windmill slashes; lose one blade and he pulls another off his back. Each blade straight sw_bidam anatomy, 1:3. #d0362f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: one sword in a fight; gold-plated armor; beardless face (except a flashback to youth). | YEON NAMSENG — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_namseng.png (face only; invent a new pose). Demeanor: Gesomun's eldest; heir who kneels west in 666. Fighting: His father's forward grip with one crow sword — never his father's two. #c25a4e as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | YEON NAMGUN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_namgun.png (face only; invent a new pose). #9e3b32 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.label: King Yumla
blocks.ko: 염라대왕

blocks.html: The Eternal General is dying.
blocks.ko: 영원의 대장군이 죽어 가고 있다.

blocks.html: He is sixty, which in his line of work is an insult to everyone he fought. The room in Pyongyang is small and too warm. His three sons stand at the bed. Gulgul stands by the door with his back to the wall. In his whole life he has never once sat with his back to a door.
blocks.ko: 그는 예순이다. 그의 직업에서 그 나이는 그와 싸웠던 모든 이에게 모욕이다. 평양의 방은 좁고 너무 덥다. 세 아들이 침상 곁에 서 있다. 걸걸은 문 옆에 벽을 등지고 서 있다. 그는 평생 단 한 번도 문을 등지고 앉은 적이 없다.

en: Do not… fight amongst yourselves…

lines: 아버지는 형제를 곁에 두신 적이 없습니다.
하나는 남쪽 국경 끝으로 보내셨고, 나머지는 다 베어 버리셨죠.
en: Father.
You never kept a brother close.
One you sent to the far end of the southern border. The rest you cut down.
…That is precisely why I am telling you.
…He means it, brother.

lines: 아버지는 늘 진심이시지. 그게 문제였던 적은 없어.
en: He always means it. That has never been the trouble.

blocks.html: Then he does something nobody in the room expects. He sits up.
blocks.ko: 그때 그는 방 안의 누구도 예상하지 못한 일을 한다. 몸을 일으킨다.

en: Gulgul. The chair. Put me in the chair.
I’m not meeting anybody lying down.

blocks.html: Gulgul carries him across the room like a sack of grain he is fond of. The swords go on the wall behind the chair, all five, where a visitor will see them.
blocks.ko: 걸걸은 아끼는 곡식 자루를 옮기듯 그를 안아 방을 가로지른다. 칼 다섯 자루가 의자 뒤 벽에 걸린다. 찾아오는 자가 볼 수 있는 자리다.

lines: 내가 한 번 말했지. 뼈가 다 부러질 때까지라고.
세어 봐라, 걸걸. 몇 개 남았냐?
en: I said it once. Until every bone in me is broken.
Count them, Gulgul. How many are left?
Enough, sir.

blocks.html: He expects one of them — Kangrim with his Question, or Haewonmek with his last words. He has been rehearsing a refusal.
blocks.ko: 그는 둘 중 하나를 기대한다. 물음을 든 강림, 아니면 유언을 묻는 해원맥. 거절할 대사는 이미 연습해 두었다.

en: …Which of you failed me at the Snake River?
Come on. Ask. I am ready to say no again.
lines: 자. 물어라. 이번에도 아니라고 할 준비는 됐다.

blocks.html: It is not either of them. Purple of sentence, not crow-dark of the fetch — Yumla himself stands in the room. The judge, not the clerks. A king for a king.
blocks.ko: 둘 중 아무도 아니다. 거둬 가는 자의 까마귀빛이 아니라 판결의 자주빛 — 염라 본인이 방에 서 있다. 서기가 아니라 심판관. 왕에게 왕.

en: Yeon Gesomun.
My two best men could not bring you at the Snake River.
A man like you — only another king could carry you off.
Consider the courtesy returned.
lines: 내 두 최고의 부하가 사수에서 그대를 데려오지 못했지.
그대 같은 사내 — 다른 왕이 아니면 데려갈 수 없다.

en: …Hah.
So the clerks failed, and the boss clocked in.
Fine. I always preferred dealing with the top.
lines: 좋아. 나는 원래 윗사람과 거래하는 편이니까.

en: The minutes will remember the joke.
Now — walk. Judgment keeps better hours than Supreme Commanders.
lines: 이제 — 걷거라. 심판은 대막리지보다 시간을 잘 지킨다.

en: One thing first. My sons—
Are not my department.
…Yet.

blocks.html: At the very end Yeon catches a vision of something. A young man, centuries off, standing in a gate and saying Goryeo as if it had never gone.
blocks.ko: 마지막 순간, 연개소문은 무언가의 환영을 본다. 몇백 년 뒤의 젊은이 하나가 성문에 서서, 한 번도 사라진 적 없다는 듯 고려라고 말하고 있다.

en: …Goguryeo, you idiot. Say the whole thing.

blocks.html: Then he dies in his sleep, sitting up, which is not how anyone expected it to go.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 앉은 채로, 잠든 채로 죽는다. 누구도 그렇게 되리라 생각하지 않았던 방식이다.

lines: 야... 그런 사람도 결국 염라 앞엔 서긴 하네.
en: Well… even a man like that stands before Yumla in the end.

blocks.html: His eldest, Namseng, takes on the title of Supreme Commander. He is thirty-one, and it is very heavy.
blocks.ko: 맏아들 남생이 대막리지의 자리를 잇는다. 서른한 살이다. 그 자리는 아주 무겁다.

blocks.caption: His father’s chair. It was built for one man, and it shows.
blocks.ko: 아버지의 자리. 한 사람을 위해 짠 자리라, 티가 난다.

blocks.label: The Chair
blocks.ko: 의자

blocks.html: Namseng sits in the chair the next morning. It is too big. Everyone pretends not to notice, which is how you know they have.
blocks.ko: 이튿날 아침 남생이 그 의자에 앉는다. 너무 크다. 다들 못 본 척한다. 그래서 다들 봤다는 걸 안다.

lines: 아버지가… 재주 하나는 정말 끝내주셨지, 그렇지?
en: The old man… he really did have a gift, didn’t he.
He had one. We don’t.

blocks.html: Gulgul does not sit at all. He rides north that afternoon, to the border the old man gave him. Nobody tells him to.
blocks.ko: 걸걸은 아예 앉지 않는다. 그날 오후 그는 노인이 맡겨 준 북쪽 국경으로 말을 달린다. 아무도 그러라고 하지 않았다.

blocks.html: He outlasted the Second Emperor’s war. He broke the White Tiger in the Snake River with his own hands. Every victory made the kingdom lean on him a little harder, until the whole weight of it rested on one man’s spine. A spine is a magnificent thing. No one has ever built a house on one.
blocks.ko: 그는 두 번째 황제의 전쟁을 견뎌 냈다. 사수에서 백호를 제 손으로 꺾었다. 이길 때마다 나라는 그에게 조금 더 기댔고, 마침내 나라의 무게 전부가 한 사람의 등뼈 위에 얹혔다. 등뼈는 훌륭한 것이다. 그러나 등뼈 위에 집을 지은 사람은 아무도 없다.

blocks.html: Once, three men looked up at the same star and wanted the same thing. He is the last of them to go.
blocks.ko: 예전에 세 사람이 같은 별을 올려다보며 같은 것을 원했다. 그가 그 가운데 마지막으로 떠난다.

blocks.html: “Do not fight amongst yourselves.” He had three sons. How long do you think that lasts?
blocks.ko: “서로 싸우지 마라.” 아들은 셋이었다. 그 말이 얼마나 갈 것 같은가?

logline.en: Three brothers, one seal, and men whispering in both directions.
logline.ko: 형제 셋, 인장 하나, 그리고 양쪽으로 속삭이는 자들.

blocks.html: Nine months. That is how long it lasts.
blocks.ko: 아홉 달. 딱 그만큼 간다.

blocks.label: The Provinces
blocks.ko: 지방 순시

blocks.html: In the spring Namseng rides out to tour the provinces, as a new Supreme Commander should. He leaves his two younger brothers to keep the capital.
blocks.ko: 봄에 남생은 새 대막리지라면 마땅히 그래야 하듯 지방 순시를 떠난다. 도성은 두 아우에게 맡겨 둔다.

blocks.html: Within a month there are men whispering in both directions. To Namgun and Namsan: your brother means to be rid of you when he comes back. To Namseng, at every post station: your brothers do not mean to let you back in.
blocks.ko: 한 달이 못 되어 양쪽으로 귓속말하는 자들이 생긴다. 남건과 남산에게는, 형님이 돌아오면 너희를 치울 생각이라고. 역참마다 남생에게는, 아우들이 형님을 들이지 않을 생각이라고.

lines: …그래도 한 사람 돌려보내라. 조용히. 저녁 자리에서 무슨 말들을 하는지 알고 싶다.
en: Nonsense. They are my brothers.
…Send someone back anyway. Quietly. I want to know what they say at supper.

blocks.label: The Pyongyang Gate
blocks.ko: 평양성 문

blocks.html: The man he sends is caught at the Pyongyang gate within the week. Namgun reads the orders found on him twice, and the second time he reads them as a confession.
blocks.ko: 그가 보낸 자는 한 주 만에 평양 성문에서 붙잡힌다. 남건은 그 몸에서 나온 지시를 두 번 읽고, 두 번째에는 자백으로 읽는다.

lines: 성문 닫아라! 폐하께 아뢰어라, 대막리지가 반역했다고!
en: He sends spies. To his own brothers.
Shut the gates! Tell the king the Supreme Commander has rebelled!

blocks.html: Namseng’s son is in the capital that spring, with his mother. He is nine years old and wears a little gold ring his grandfather gave him.
blocks.ko: 그해 봄 남생의 아들은 어머니와 함께 도성에 있다. 아홉 살, 할아버지가 준 작은 금가락지를 끼고 있다.

blocks.label: The Shut Gate
blocks.ko: 닫힌 문

blocks.html: He rides back to his own capital and finds the gate shut. His brother comes up onto the wall.
blocks.ko: 그는 제 도성으로 말을 몰아 돌아오고, 성문이 닫혀 있는 것을 본다. 아우가 성벽 위로 올라온다.

en: Open the gate, Namgun.
You are speaking to the Supreme Commander.

lines: 대막리지라! 아우들 저녁상에 첩자를 보내 놓고 그걸 지휘라고 하냐!
en: Supreme Commander! You send spies to your brothers’ supper and call it command!

lines: 너희 안부를 물으라고 사람 하나 보냈다. 너는 그를 목매달았지.
en: I sent a man to ask how you were. You hanged him.

lines: 남건아. 나를 봐라. 요하에서, 매는 누가 맞았냐?
en: Namgun. Look at me. At the Liao, who took the flogging?
…You did.
And why?

lines: 형이 맏이니까. 그날부터 하루도 안 빼고 맏이였지.
그리고 형이 내 목 칠 인장을 들고 돌아온다고 하더라.
en: Because you’re the elder. You’ve been the elder every single day since.
And they told me you were coming back with a seal for my head.
And you believed them. Traitor.
Traitor…? Me?

lines: 문 열어라. 안에 내 처가 있다. 내 아들이—
en: Open the gate. My wife is in there. My son—

blocks.html: Namgun does not answer. He looks at Namsan. Namsan looks at the ground.
blocks.ko: 남건은 대답하지 않는다. 그는 남산을 본다. 남산은 땅을 본다.

blocks.html: Something small comes over the wall and lands in the mud at the horse’s feet. A gold ring, a child’s size.
blocks.ko: 무언가 작은 것이 성벽을 넘어와 말발굽 앞 진흙에 떨어진다. 금가락지. 아이 손가락 크기다.

lines: 형한테 가는 편지를 품고 있었어. 수구문으로 빠져나가다가.
en: He was carrying a letter to you. Out through the water gate.
The guards didn’t— I didn’t—

blocks.html: Namseng gets down from his horse and picks the ring out of the mud. He wipes it on his sleeve. He does not look at the wall again.
blocks.ko: 남생은 말에서 내려 진흙 속의 가락지를 집어 든다. 소매에 닦는다. 다시는 성벽을 쳐다보지 않는다.

blocks.html: That night he rides north to the old capital at Gungnae. From there he sends his other son west, to Chang’an, to ask the Third Emperor for an army.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 그는 북쪽 옛 도읍 국내성으로 간다. 거기서 다른 아들을 서쪽 장안으로 보내, 황제에게 군대를 청한다.

blocks.label: Defection of Yeon Namseng
blocks.ko: 연남생의 투항

blocks.html: Namseng rides west, across the river his father spent a lifetime holding.
blocks.ko: 남생은 서쪽으로 말을 몬다. 아버지가 평생을 걸어 지킨 그 강을 건너서.

blocks.caption: North to the old capital, then west over the Liao. His father spent a lifetime stopping men riding this road the other way.
blocks.ko: 북쪽 옛 도읍으로, 다시 서쪽으로 요하를 건너. 아버지는 평생 이 길을 반대로 달려오는 자들을 막았다.

blocks.label: Chang’an
blocks.ko: 장안

en: Goryeo is nothing but swindlers and thieves —
a people beyond hope.

lines: …아버님께서 요하에서 만난 아이 이야기를 하신 적이 있소.
en: …My father spoke of a boy he met at the Liao.
One who would not kneel.
zh: ……先帝說過，在遼水遇見一個孩子。
zhLatn: …Xiāndì shuō guò, zài Liáoshuǐ yùjiàn yí ge háizi.
Bù kěn xiàguì de.

lines: 스무 해 전입니다, 폐하. 선제와 저. 선제께서 요수를 건너오셨을 때.
en: Twenty years ago, Majesty. Your father and I, when he crossed the Liao.
I did not kneel then.

blocks.html: He is thirty-two years old, and his brother has taken his title, his city and his father’s seat, and this is the second time in his life he has been offered a house in Chang’an. Nobody flogs him for the answer this time.
blocks.ko: 그는 서른둘이고, 아우가 그의 관작과 도성과 아버지의 자리를 빼앗았으며, 장안의 집을 제안받은 것은 평생 두 번째다. 이번에는 그 대답 때문에 매를 맞지 않는다.

lines: 페하께선, 혼자는 결코 삼한정벌은 못 하실 겁니다.
en: Your Majesty will never conquer Samhan alone.
Emperor… Your Majesty… ten thousand years…!

blocks.html: Namseng is given a Tang title, and a vanguard command against his own country.
blocks.ko: 남생은 당의 관작과 함께, 제 나라를 치는 선봉의 지휘를 받는다.

blocks.html: The Third Emperor has wanted this war since he was a boy, watching his father come home from it. Now it arrives with a guide.
blocks.ko: 황제는 아버지가 그 전쟁에서 돌아오는 것을 지켜보던 소년 시절부터 이 전쟁을 원했다. 이제 그 전쟁이 길잡이를 데리고 찾아온다.

blocks.html: In the south their uncle Yeon Jungto, who raised two of them, waits to hear which nephew will send for him. Neither does. He takes twelve cities over to Silla, and the family is finished in three directions at once.
blocks.ko: 남쪽에서는 그 둘을 키운 숙부 연정토가 어느 조카가 자기를 부르러 올지 기다린다. 아무도 오지 않는다. 그는 열두 성을 들고 신라로 넘어가고, 그 집안은 한꺼번에 세 방향에서 끝난다.

blocks.html: Years later, in the emperor’s country, Namseng’s tombstone will tell the story his way.
blocks.ko: 훗날 황제의 땅에서, 남생의 묘지석은 그 이야기를 그의 방식대로 전할 것이다.

blocks.html: His heart was loyal, but matters went wrong at the centre. He had just gone out to comfort the border folk and tour the wild marches, to survey the old lands of the dawn country and ask for new officers to govern them. Then his two younger brothers, Namsan and Namgun, turned vicious and rebellious in a single morning. Heartless to their own blood, they raised troops and shut him out from within. His little son with the gold ring fell suddenly into the whale's jaws, and left the long table and his parents' arms for ever.
blocks.ko: 공은 속마음으로 정성을 다했으나, 일은 조정 한가운데서 어그러졌다. 공이 막 변방 백성을 어루만지고 거친 들을 순시하러 나가, 동쪽 옛 땅을 살피고 새 관원을 청하려 할 때였다. 두 아우 남산과 남건이 하루아침에 흉악하게 패역하여, 혈육도 아랑곳없이 군사를 일으켜 안에서 막아섰다. 금고리를 찬 어린 아들은 졸지에 고래 아가리에 떨어져, 진수성찬 차린 긴 자리와 부모의 품을 문득 떠났다.
blocks.hanja: 公情思內款，事乖中執。方欲出撫邊甿，外巡荒甸，按嵎夷之舊壤，請羲仲之新官。二弟產建，一朝兇悖，能忍無親，稱兵內拒。金環幼子，忽就鯨鯢，玉膳長筵，俄辭顧復。
blocks.source: Epitaph of Yeon Namseng (泉男生墓誌) — Luoyang, 679; transcription in the Korean Ancient History DB (한국 고대 사료 DB)

blocks.html: Namseng knows the road in. Now he rides it home, with the whole Tang army at his back…!
blocks.ko: 남생은 들어가는 길을 안다. 이제 그는 당의 대군을 등 뒤에 달고, 그 길로 집에 돌아온다…!

logline.en: When the ring closes, the city needs one man nobody can buy. They pick a monk.
logline.ko: 포위가 닫히자, 도성에는 아무도 살 수 없는 사내 하나가 필요하다. 그들은 승려를 고른다.

images.prompt: Minimal iconic 3:4 poster. NOT photoreal. NOT busy. Yeon Namgun. ONE geometric device: a broken crimson #9e3b32 ribbon slash diagonal across the void — no seals, no glyphs. Face matches the attached portrait. #9e3b32 as the plane. Flat charcoal-black void. No army. No text. No watermark. Graphic color-blocking, anime-painterly, monumental.

Goguryeo red on the walls. Real siege, real city. Painterly cinema. Flat sky, no clouds. No text, no watermark.

images.prompt: Minimal iconic 16:9 poster. Final siege of Pyongyang, 668. ONE geometric device: a BROKEN RING of Goguryeo-red wall #C30000 — a hard circular rampart with one missing arc at the lower right. REAL Taedong River bend and winter hills inside and below the ring. Tiny silky red court-military specks on the remaining wall, wide sleeves readable even at this scale. Natural winter sky, haze, pale ice on the water. Monumental emptiness. images.prompt: Minimal iconic 9:16 poster. Shinsung, the Buddhist monk who opens Pyongyang from inside. ONE geometric device: a VERTICAL SLIT of cold Tang-gold light cutting a Goguryeo-red #C30000 gate-plane from lintel to frost — the gate opening from the inside. Tiny silky monk silhouette in taupe #8f7b70, wide sleeves, pushing the leaf. Face matches the attached portrait only as a tiny likeness. Real winter stone, snow-fog at the threshold. Monumental emptiness. Graphic color-blocking, anime-painterly, not photoreal, not cartoon. No army. No clutter. No readable text. No watermark.

No watermark. Graphic color-blocking, anime-painterly, monumental.

Foreground bokeh: Munmu’s hand and a blank wooden tablet, no writing. ONE device: the tablet edge as a vertical cutting the cheek. #2A5FB8 rim, #C41E3A a thin accent on the hand.
