images.alt: The Gwanghwamun Admiral Yi statue, painted: old Yushin as the towering bronze general, ring-pommel sword planted, Pyongyang’s walls behind
images.prompt: A painted parody of the ADMIRAL YI SUN-SIN STATUE at Gwanghwamun: an oil painting of the towering dark bronze monument seen from a steep worm’s-eye angle on its tall stone pedestal, thick brushwork, bronze glinting. Same pose: a standing general in armor, feet apart, looking far ahead, a long sword held upright in front of him in its scabbard, both hands resting on it. The general is the old KIM YUSHIN (attached old portrait: face, white beard) in bronze steel lamellar (attached ref), marshal-blue #2A5FB8 cloth peeking at the collar as patina; the sword is the attached ring-pommel 환두대도, small ring pommel up. Behind the pedestal, the red two-tier gate pavilion and stone walls of the attached Pyongyang fortress under a wide autumn sky. PARODY RULES: always a hand-made PAINTING, never photoreal. Reproduce the original work’s composition, poses and signature look so it reads instantly as that exact work, with our characters swapped in. If the original is a painting, mural, print or scroll, match its medium, surface and brushwork. If the original is a photograph, film poster, album cover, anime frame or statue, PAINT it: a painterly illustration of that image with visible brushstrokes, simplified forms and anime-adjacent faces, NOT a photo, NOT photoreal skin or pores, NOT a 3D render, NOT a CGI statue. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portraits, recognizable but restyled into the medium; never the portrait’s standing clasped-hands stance. Character hex lives only as real color inside the work (pigment, cloth, light), never a glow aura, halo, emissive skin or neon outline. If a sword is visible it is the ring-pommel 환두대도 (small ring pommel at the heel of the fist, short grip, long straight blade, handle:blade 1:3), never a katana, never a tsuba. No readable text, no title, no credits, no legible inscriptions or signatures (red seal stamps only as blank red squares), no logos, no watermark.

blocks.html: Every son comes home in the end. Namseng brings the empire with him.
blocks.ko: 아들은 결국 모두 집으로 돌아온다. 남생은 제국을 데리고 온다.

blocks.label: The Ninth Invasion
blocks.ko: 제9차 침공

blocks.html: Three of the emperor’s four beasts come for the city at once. The Blue Dragon leads, the old marshal who has been at this war since the last emperor. The Black Tortoise and the second White Tiger ride behind him.
blocks.ko: 황제의 네 짐승 가운데 셋이 한꺼번에 이 성으로 온다. 청룡이 앞장선다. 지난 황제 때부터 이 전쟁에 있었던 늙은 원수다. 현무와 두 번째 백호가 그 뒤를 따른다.

blocks.caption: Three beasts, three roads, one city.
blocks.ko: 짐승 셋, 길 셋, 성 하나.

en: Breaking a fortress… is like farming.
You know the season, you bring the water, you harvest.
Today is a harvest day.
zhLatn: Pòchéng… rú nóngshì.
Zhī shíjié, yǐn shuǐ, shōugē.
Jīnrì shì shōuchéng zhī rì.

blocks.html: There is no cruelty in him, which is precisely what makes him difficult: the men of Goguryeo can hate a butcher, but they cannot quite hate a farmer who treats siege-work as weather.
blocks.ko: 그에게는 잔인함이 없고, 바로 그래서 상대하기가 어렵다. 고구려 사람들은 학살자라면 미워할 수 있다. 그러나 공성을 날씨처럼 다루는 농부는, 끝까지 미워하기가 어렵다.

blocks.label: Brothers
blocks.ko: 형제

blocks.html: Namseng rides at the head of the column in a Tang coat, down the north-west road, to show the Blue Dragon the way. He knows every gully. He used to hunt them. At the top of the last one he reins in and looks at the red gate.
blocks.ko: 남생은 당나라 옷을 입고 행렬 맨 앞에서 서북쪽 길을 내려온다. 청룡에게 길을 보여 주는 것이다. 골짜기 하나하나를 다 안다. 예전에 거기서 사냥을 했다. 마지막 골짜기 위에서 그는 고삐를 당기고 붉은 문루를 바라본다.

en: At last… I set foot on Pyongyang’s ground—

blocks.html: On the wall, Namgun can see him. Everyone on the wall can see him.
blocks.ko: 성벽 위에서 남건은 그를 볼 수 있다. 성벽 위의 모두가 그를 볼 수 있다.

blocks.caption: Gesomun’s youngest son, and the one who listens at doors.
blocks.ko: 연개소문의 막내아들. 문 앞에서 엿듣는 쪽이다.

lines: 형… 저 사람, 저쪽 옷을 입었어.
en: Brother… he’s wearing their coat.
Goguryeo… never dies….!

blocks.html: That is the only conversation the three of them have that year. A whisper, a shout, and a man on a horse who does not answer.
blocks.ko: 그해 세 형제가 나눈 대화는 그것이 전부다. 속삭임 하나, 고함 하나, 그리고 대답하지 않는 말 위의 사내.

blocks.label: The White Banner
blocks.ko: 흰 깃발

blocks.html: The ring closes. Every few days Namgun sends men out of a gate to break it, and fewer come back. Then the Blue Dragon moves his whole camp round to the south-west, between the walls and the river.
blocks.ko: 포위가 조여든다. 며칠마다 남건이 성문 밖으로 군사를 내보내 뚫어 보지만, 돌아오는 수는 매번 줄어든다. 그러다 청룡이 진영을 통째로 서남쪽, 성벽과 강 사이로 옮긴다.

en: Brother. Silla banners on the far bank.
…That was the last side we had.

blocks.html: A month goes by. Inside, the granaries go down the way the Tang campfires did, seven winters ago, and someone on the wall is counting.
blocks.ko: 한 달이 지난다. 성안의 곳간이, 일곱 겨울 전 당군의 모닥불이 그랬듯 줄어 간다. 그리고 성벽 위의 누군가가 그것을 세고 있다.

blocks.html: Namsan counts best. So it is Namsan who walks out first.
blocks.ko: 셈은 남산이 제일 잘한다. 그래서 먼저 걸어 나가는 것도 남산이다.

blocks.html: He goes out through the south-west gate with the king and ninety-eight officials, carrying a white banner. The king of Goguryeo has worn the crown twenty-six years. For most of them a Yeon told him what to say. Today a Yeon is telling him again.
blocks.ko: 그는 왕과 관리 아흔여덟 명과 함께 흰 깃발을 들고 서남쪽 성문을 나선다. 고구려의 왕은 스물여섯 해 동안 관을 썼다. 그 대부분의 날 동안 연씨 집안 사람이 그에게 할 말을 일러 주었다. 오늘도 연씨 집안 사람이 일러 준다.

lines: 내— 내가 저자에게 꿇는 건가, 아니면 깃발에?
en: Do I— do I kneel to him, or to the banner?

lines: 깃발에 꿇으십시오, 전하. 저 사람은 들고 있을 뿐입니다.
en: To the banner, Majesty. He’s only holding it.

blocks.html: The king kneels. The Blue Dragon accepts the surrender very politely. Then he looks up at the walls, where the gate has already shut again behind them.
blocks.ko: 왕이 무릎을 꿇는다. 청룡은 아주 정중하게 항복을 받는다. 그러고는 성벽을 올려다본다. 그들 뒤에서 성문이 이미 다시 닫혀 있다.

blocks.label: Betrayal from Inside
blocks.ko: 안에서 열린 문

blocks.html: Namgun has not surrendered. He has the walls, the army and the gate. What he needs is one man nobody can buy. He picks a monk. Shinsung has kept a small temple at the foot of the hill for twenty-five years. He has never asked anyone for anything.
blocks.ko: 남건은 항복하지 않았다. 그에게는 성벽과 군대와 성문이 있다. 그에게 필요한 것은 아무도 살 수 없는 사람 하나다. 그는 승려를 고른다. 신성은 언덕 아래 작은 절을 스물다섯 해 지켜 왔다. 누구에게도 무엇 하나 청한 적이 없다.

lines: 스님은 가문도 없고, 파벌도 없고, 자식도 없소.
이 성에서 성을 팔아넘기는 게 상상이 안 되는 사람은 스님뿐이오.
en: You have no clan, no faction, no sons.
You’re the only man in this city I can’t imagine selling it.

lines: 그럼 대막리지의 상상에 걸맞도록 애써 보겠습니다.
en: Then I shall try to be worthy of your imagination, Mangniji.

blocks.html: For five days a novice walks out of the lesser house before dawn with an alms bowl and comes back with it empty, and nobody thinks to ask why a monk’s bowl should come back empty from the direction of the Tang lines. On the fifth night the bell that has sat on the floor of the lesser house since the year the Daoists came is struck once.
blocks.ko: 닷새 동안 한 사미승이 새벽마다 바리때를 들고 작은 절을 나섰다가 빈 바리때로 돌아온다. 스님의 바리때가 왜 당의 진 쪽에서 비어서 돌아오는지 아무도 묻지 않는다. 닷새째 밤, 도사들이 오던 해부터 작은 절 바닥에 놓여 있던 종이 한 번 울린다.

blocks.html: Yeon once tried to starve the temples with the emperor’s Daoists. The monks have waited a generation. Shinsung doesn’t make a speech about doctrine. He opens a gate.
blocks.ko: 연개소문은 한때 황제의 도사들을 들여 절을 굶기려 했다. 승려들은 한 세대를 기다렸다. 신성은 교리를 연설하지 않는다. 그는 문을 연다.

blocks.html: The Tang come in through the south-west gate before the bell has stopped ringing. Quietly at first, then not quietly at all.
blocks.ko: 종소리가 채 그치기도 전에 당군이 서남쪽 성문으로 들어온다. 처음엔 조용히, 그다음엔 전혀 조용하지 않게.

blocks.speaker: Goguryeo guard
lines: 막리지! 서남문이— 문이 열렸습니다! 안에서 열었습니다!
en: Mangniji! The south-west gate— it’s open! They opened it from inside!
Who had the gate?

blocks.speaker: Goguryeo guard
en: …The monk, Mangniji.
The monk…?

blocks.label: Last Words
blocks.ko: 유언

blocks.html: Namgun is thirty-one. He leads the last stand against the Blue Dragon himself.
blocks.ko: 남건은 서른한 살이다. 청룡에 맞선 마지막 항전을 몸소 이끈다.

en: Silla’s sacred blood — rot!
Goguryeo will take the final victory!
You may rule this soil — our name will have the last word!
lines: 이 땅을 다스린다 해도 — 우리 이름이… 마지막에…!

blocks.html: The wall is already lost. He knows it. He says it anyway, to the men who can still hear, and to a bloodline across the river he can’t see.
blocks.ko: 성벽은 이미 졌다. 그도 안다. 그래도 말한다. 아직 들을 수 있는 사람들에게, 강 건너 보이지 않는 핏줄에게.

en: Goguryeo… never dies….!

blocks.html: The gate towers catch one after another, like lamps being lit for a feast. In his own hall, Namgun turns his sword on himself. He does it badly, the first thing he has done badly in the whole war.
blocks.ko: 문루들이 잔치에 등불을 켜듯 하나씩 차례로 불붙는다. 남건은 제 전각에서 스스로를 찌른다. 서툴게 찌른다. 그 전쟁 내내 그가 처음으로 서툴게 한 일이다.

lines: 막리지의 시신은— 살아 있다고? 그럼 의원을 붙이시오.
en: Put out the granaries. Let the towers burn.
And the Mangniji’s body— alive? Then find him a surgeon.
I want him in the register, not the ditch.

blocks.html: The surgeons save him, so that he can be sent alive to the farthest edge of the empire.
blocks.ko: 의원들이 그를 살려 낸다. 산 채로 제국의 가장 먼 끝으로 보내기 위해서다.

blocks.html: In the burning palace, a Mohe man with a border sabre walks into a treasury nobody is guarding any more. He comes out with a piece of gold no longer than a finger, snapped off something that used to be worn on a head. Nobody stops him. Nobody ever looks at Gulgul.
blocks.ko: 불타는 궁궐에서, 국경의 칼을 찬 말갈 사내 하나가 이제 아무도 지키지 않는 보물 창고로 걸어 들어간다. 그는 손가락보다 짧은 금붙이 하나를 들고 나온다. 한때 누군가의 머리 위에 얹혀 있던 것에서 꺾어 낸 조각이다. 아무도 그를 막지 않는다. 걸걸을 쳐다보는 사람은 늘 아무도 없다.

blocks.html: Among the captives is a Baekje king with a Yamato accent. Pung ran north to the last kingdom left. The kingdoms ran out before he did.
blocks.ko: 포로들 가운데 왜 말씨가 섞인 백제의 왕이 하나 있다. 풍은 남은 마지막 나라로 북쪽으로 달아났다. 그보다 나라들이 먼저 바닥났다.

blocks.html: When the city falls, the empire doesn't send a stranger to hold it. It sends Xue Rengui. The white coat becomes a banner over a broken capital. He governs well enough that even the conquered prefer him to chaos.
blocks.ko: 성이 떨어지자, 제국은 낯선 자를 보내지 않는다. 설인귀를 보낸다. 흰 전포가 무너진 도성 위의 깃발이 된다. 그는 정복당한 사람들조차 혼란보다는 그를 택할 만큼 다스린다.

lines: 나는… 여러분의 원수가 되고 싶지 않았습니다.
다만 폐하의 동쪽을, 빈손으로 둘 수는 없었습니다.
en: I… did not wish to be your enemy.
But I could not leave His Majesty’s east empty-handed.
zh: 但不能讓陛下之東空手而歸。
zhLatn: Wǒ… běn bù yuàn yǔ zhūwèi wéi dí.
Dàn bùnéng ràng Bìxià zhī dōng kōngshǒu ér guī.

blocks.html: Goguryeo had stood seven hundred years. The record, for its part, writes only the month and the surrender.
blocks.ko: 고구려는 칠백 년을 섰다. 편년은, 제 몫으로는, 달과 항복만을 적는다.

blocks.label: Zhaoling
blocks.ko: 소릉

blocks.html: Before the captives are shown to the living emperor, the Blue Dragon takes them up the mountain to show them to the dead one. The king of Goguryeo is made to bow at Zhaoling, in front of the door the Second Emperor said his horses would guard. The six stone horses stand in their row. The purple one is nearest the door.
blocks.ko: 포로들을 산 황제에게 보이기 전에, 청룡은 그들을 산 위로 데려가 죽은 황제에게 먼저 보인다. 고구려의 왕은 소릉에서, 선제가 제 말들이 지키리라 했던 그 문 앞에 절하게 된다. 여섯 돌말이 줄지어 서 있다. 자줏빛 말이 문에 가장 가깝다.

blocks.label: The New Rank
blocks.ko: 새 관등

blocks.html: The seventeen grades stop at one another. In the tenth month, after the city is open, King Munmu cuts a rank the grades did not have, and gives it to the man who has been Marshal since the yard.
blocks.ko: 열일곱 관등은 서로에게서 멈춘다. 성이 열린 뒤 열째 달, 문무왕이 그 관등에 없던 자리를 하나 베어, 연무장에서부터 대장군이던 사람에게 준다.

en: Marshal.
Majesty.
You have been Marshal since before I could hold a bow.
The yard still says it.
The seventeen grades do not reach you anymore.
The word is enough.
I know what I am.
There was already a grade above the seventeen.
I had them cut one above that.
Supreme General.

blocks.caption: A rank above every rank. They had to invent it for him.
blocks.ko: 모든 품계 위의 품계. 그를 위해 새로 만들어야 했다.

en: A new name for an old man.

lines: 눈 속을 뚫고 이 전쟁을 먹여 살린 사람의 이름이오.
en: It is the name of the man who fed this war through the snow.
Wear it.
You may keep Marshal for the boys on the yard.
…As you command.

blocks.html: The story isn’t over yet. The Third Emperor still controls large swaths of Samhan. The final war begins…!
blocks.ko: 이야기는 아직 끝나지 않았다. 황제는 여전히 삼한의 넓은 땅을 쥐고 있다. 마지막 전쟁이 시작된다…!

toneNote: Ally turns on ally; victory measured in what survives, not what is won.
title: Silla-Tang War

logline.en: The night Pyongyang falls, Munmu goes to look at an oath. Three summers earlier, the empire made him swear it over his uncle’s white horse.
logline.ko: 평양이 떨어진 밤, 문무는 맹세문 하나를 보러 간다. 세 해 전, 제국은 외숙의 흰 말 위에서 그 맹세를 시켰다.

images.at: cleaning a stall that is empty
images.alt: Old Yushin scrubs Hanseul's empty stall; Munmu stops at the stall door.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Interior night, a timber stable in Surabol. Low three-quarter from the straw. ONE device: a dark wooden stall partition as a hard vertical splitting the frame. Kim Yushin, seventy, FACE ONLY from the attached portrait with the beard gone grey, plain blue po, sleeves tied back, bent over a brush scrubbing the boards of an EMPTY stall; on the peg above him hangs an old halter with a white horsehair caught in it. At the stall door, King Munmu, FACE ONLY from the attached portrait, crimson robe, has stopped with one hand on the gatepost and does not come in. No horse in frame — the empty stall is the subject. A lantern hung on a post rakes gold across the straw, the timber grain and Yushin's knuckles; Silla blue #2A5FB8 catching in his sleeve. Foreground: out-of-focus straw and a wooden water bucket. CANON — KIM YUSHIN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_kim_yushin.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Tall, broad-shouldered, long black hair in a high topknot-ponytail with trailing Silla-blue cloth tails; level hard brows, deep-set eyes. Dress: Silla-blue po and trousers, plum-violet sash knotted at the waist, white inner collar, dark wrapped forearms. Off duty: plain blue po, no jewelry. Headwear: the jougwan (see HEADWEAR). Now: Marshal: full black beard and moustache; a blue ribbon in the topknot instead of the headband. Demeanor: Confucian: he STANDS — never sits in lotus. Weighs, counts, frowns at sums; tight jaw, rare dry half-smile. Grief shows as stillness, not tears. The most feared warrior in all of Samhan: a line goes quiet when the tall Silla helm and the white horse appear. Massive, deliberate, terrifying at a walk; by Hwangsan (65) heavier and slower than Gyebek but still the man armies are built around. #2A5FB8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: sitting in lotus or holding prayer beads; katana, tsuba or curved blade (ignore the sword drawn on his portrait); two swords at once; blue glow aura. | KING MUNMU — FACE and garments from attached /ch_munmu.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Square jaw, goatee and moustache, confident grin; arms folded when he is pleased with himself. Dress: As king: crimson robe with gold dragon embroidery, blue shoulder pieces, gold Silla crown. Earlier: prince/hwarang stage portraits. Crown: Silla gold crown, as the attached crown: a gold band with three tree-shaped uprights stepped like the character 出 and two antler uprights at the back, hung with round gold spangles and curved green jade gogok, long gold pendants at the temples. ref_muyeol shows it worn with the king's red robe and gold-scroll collar (ignore its painted backdrop). Demeanor: Cocky, warm, practical; his father's charm with his uncle's spine. #C41E3A as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: katana; Tang dragon robe in place of Silla court dress. | HEADWEAR: JOUGWAN (조우관, feather cap) — copy the SHAPE from the attached hat boards and ignore their Korean labels, museum photos, paper-craft gems and dragon medallion: a small black lacquered gauze cap (변형모, a peaked or square-topped crown no bigger than the topknot it covers) set high on the crown of the head over a small knot of gathered hair (any loose hair the portrait shows still falls beneath it); a thin black band round the head with a small square opening at the front; black cords tied under the chin; two long barred pheasant tail feathers (tan with umber bars), or a spray of bird plumes, rising straight up or sweeping back from either side of the cap, much taller than the cap itself. It replaces any other hat or cap on the portrait; headbands and ribbons stay. Real lacquer and feathers lit by the scene key, never a glow. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Silla: attached /ref_hanbok_silla.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.label: The Ancestral Temple
blocks.ko: 종묘

blocks.html: The night Pyongyang falls, the king of Silla goes to visit a piece of paper.
blocks.ko: 평양이 떨어진 날 밤, 신라 왕은 종이 한 장을 보러 간다.

blocks.html: It hangs in the ancestral temple, beside his father's tablet. Gold letters on iron. An oath, sworn over a dead horse, to love Baekje's prince like a brother. Goguryeo is gone tonight. Up north, the emperor's clerks are already measuring what is left.
blocks.ko: 그것은 종묘, 아버지의 위패 곁에 걸려 있다. 쇠에 새긴 금 글씨. 죽은 말 위에서, 백제 왕자를 형제처럼 아끼겠다고 한 맹세다. 오늘 밤 고구려는 사라졌다. 북쪽에서는 황제의 서기들이 벌써 남은 땅을 재고 있다.

en: Everything south of Pyongyang, and the whole of Baekje.
My father made me learn it by heart.
The emperor will have learned a sentence too, Majesty.
I know. It’s hanging right here.
Uncle. Do you remember the horse?
lines: 알고 있소. 바로 여기 걸려 있으니까.

en: …Every day, Majesty.

blocks.html: Every war starts with an insult somebody swallowed. Silla swallowed this one three summers ago. To taste it, go back to a hill outside Bear Ford, and the only white horse in the camp.
blocks.ko: 모든 전쟁은 누군가 삼킨 모욕 하나에서 시작된다. 신라는 이 모욕을 세 해 전 여름에 삼켰다. 그 맛을 보려면 웅진 밖 언덕으로, 진영에 단 한 마리뿐이던 흰 말에게로 거슬러 가야 한다.

blocks.label: Bear Ford, Three Summers Earlier
blocks.ko: 세 해 전, 웅진

blocks.html: Two springs after the White River, the empire names a governor for what is left of Baekje. It is Buyeo Yung. He once knelt at Bupmin's horse and was spat on. Then he went to the emperor's city and came back in imperial robes. Now he will rule from the fortress where his father was arrested.
blocks.ko: 백강 싸움이 끝나고 두 번째 봄, 제국은 남은 백제를 맡을 도독을 세운다. 부여융이다. 그는 한때 법민의 말 앞에 꿇어 침을 맞았다. 그러고는 황제의 도성에 갔다가 황제의 관복을 입고 돌아왔다. 이제 그는 아버지가 붙잡혀 간 바로 그 성에서 다스린다.

blocks.html: The court in Surabol hears the name and goes very quiet. Their men died for this ground. An emperor promised it to Chunchu by lamplight. Now a Baekje prince sits on it again, with the emperor's seal in his hand.
blocks.ko: 서라벌 조정은 그 이름을 듣고 아주 조용해진다. 자기 사람들이 이 땅을 위해 죽었다. 황제는 등잔불 아래 이 땅을 춘추에게 약속했다. 그런데 이제 그 위에 다시 백제 왕자가 앉아 있다. 황제의 도장을 쥐고.

blocks.html: Yung moves into the commandery offices in the spring. The rooms his father was taken from have been whitewashed. The Black Tortoise shows him the registers, and the calendar, and the list of names he may not write.
blocks.ko: 융은 봄에 도독부 관아로 들어간다. 아버지가 끌려 나간 방들은 하얗게 회칠이 되어 있다. 현무가 그에게 호적과 역서와, 써서는 안 될 이름 목록을 보여 준다.

lines: 도독의 백성이오. 이제 모두 숫자요. 돌보기가 훨씬 쉬워지지.
en: Your households, Commander. Every one of them a number now. It makes them much easier to look after.
zh: 都督之戶口，今皆為數。易於撫養。
zhLatn: Dūdū zhī hùkǒu, jīn jiē wéi shù. Yì yú fǔyǎng.

en: …My father counted them by name.
He was wrong about most things. Not that.

blocks.label: The Altar
blocks.ko: 제단

blocks.html: That summer, the empire makes the two men who rule the south swear to be brothers. It picks a hill outside Bear Ford. The clerks name it the Mountain Where One Goes for Gain. They mean it kindly.
blocks.ko: 그해 여름, 제국은 남쪽을 다스리는 두 사내에게 형제가 되겠다고 맹세하게 한다. 웅진 밖 언덕 하나를 고른다. 서기들은 그 산을 '이익을 좇아가는 산'이라 적는다. 좋은 뜻으로 지은 이름이다.

blocks.html: A hill outside Bear Ford, named by optimists.
blocks.ko: 웅진 밖의 언덕. 낙관주의자들이 붙인 이름.

blocks.html: An imperial envoy presides. The Black Tortoise wrote the oath. On one side of the altar stands Munmu. On the other stands Yung. Munmu last saw that face at the height of his horse's knees.
blocks.ko: 칙사가 주관하고, 맹세문은 현무가 지었다. 제단 한쪽에 문무가 선다. 다른 쪽에 융이 선다. 문무가 그 얼굴을 마지막으로 본 건 제 말의 무릎 높이에서였다.

blocks.label: The White Horse
blocks.ko: 백마

blocks.html: An oath of this weight needs a white horse. The Tang adjutant has been walking the Silla lines all morning looking for one, and stops in front of the only white horse in the camp.
blocks.ko: 이만한 맹세에는 흰 말이 있어야 한다. 당의 부관이 아침 내내 신라의 진을 돌며 흰 말을 찾다가, 진영에 단 한 마리뿐인 흰 말 앞에서 멈춘다.

blocks.speaker: Tang adjutant
en: That one. Whose is he?
zhLatn: Nà pǐ. Shéi de?

blocks.html: Hanseul is past twenty. He has carried Yushin across the Yellow Mountain. He has carried rice through snow up to his chest. His muzzle has gone grey. On a white horse, only the man who feeds him notices.
blocks.ko: 한슬은 스무 살이 넘었다. 유신을 태우고 황산벌을 건넜다. 가슴까지 차는 눈 속으로 쌀을 날랐다. 주둥이가 하얗게 셌다. 흰 말이라, 먹이를 주는 사람 말고는 아무도 모른다.

lines: 안 되오. 다른 말을 찾으시오. 저건 외숙의—
en: No. Find another. That is my uncle’s—
Let them have him, Majesty.
Uncle.

lines: 흰 말을 달라 했습니다. 갈색 말로 하면 맹세가 초라하지요.
en: A white horse is what they asked for. It would be a poor oath on a brown one.
…I’ll walk him up myself.

blocks.html: He leads Hanseul up the hill by the halter, the way he led Hangyul across the Moon Palace yard eighteen years before, talking to him in the low voice he keeps for horses and uses on no one else. At the altar he holds the head himself.
blocks.ko: 그는 고삐를 잡고 한슬이를 언덕 위로 끈다. 열여덟 해 전 월성 마당에서 한결이를 끌던 그대로, 말에게만 쓰고 사람에게는 한 번도 쓰지 않는 낮은 목소리로 말을 건네면서. 제단 앞에서 그는 말머리를 손수 잡는다.

blocks.html: The knife is Tang. The blood goes into a bowl, and both men touch it to their lips. Yung does it without looking at anyone. Munmu does it looking at his uncle’s hands.
blocks.ko: 칼은 당의 것이다. 피가 사발에 담기고, 두 사내가 그것을 입술에 댄다. 융은 아무도 보지 않고 한다. 문무는 외숙의 손을 보면서 한다.

lines: …형제처럼 지내며 재앙을 나누고 근심을 서로 보살펴, 길이 하나가 될지어다.
이 맹약을 어기는 자는 신명이 굽어보시어 온갖 재앙이 내리고, 자손이 자라지 못하며, 그 사직을 지킬 자가 남지 않으리라.
en: …Let them be as brothers, sharing disaster and pitying each other’s sorrows, forever as one.
Whoever breaks this covenant, may the gods see it; may a hundred calamities fall on him, may his sons not grow, and may no one remain to keep his altars.
zh: ……結為兄弟，分災恤患，永以為好。
有背此盟者，明神鑒之，百殃是降，子孫不育，社稷無守。
zhLatn: …Jié wéi xiōngdì, fēn zāi xù huàn, yǒng yǐ wéi hǎo.
Yǒu bèi cǐ méng zhě, míngshén jiàn zhī, bǎi yāng shì jiàng, zǐsūn bú yù, shèjì wú shǒu.

blocks.html: The covenant is written out three times. One copy is buried at the altar with the horse. One goes to Chang’an. The third is carried to Surabol and laid up in Silla’s ancestral temple, where the kings of Silla will have to walk past it every time they visit their fathers.
blocks.ko: 맹세문은 세 벌 쓰인다. 한 벌은 말과 함께 제단에 묻힌다. 한 벌은 장안으로 간다. 나머지 한 벌은 서라벌로 옮겨져 신라의 종묘에 모셔진다. 신라의 왕들이 선왕을 뵈러 갈 때마다 그 앞을 지나가야 하는 자리다.

blocks.label: Surabol
blocks.ko: 서라벌

blocks.html: On the road home nobody in the Silla column says anything about the horse.
blocks.ko: 돌아오는 길에 신라의 행렬 누구도 그 말 이야기를 꺼내지 않는다.

blocks.html: In Surabol the anger is louder. Men bled for this land in three wars. An emperor promised it to them. Now they have sworn on a dead horse never to take it. The young officers say betrayal in the barracks. The older ones say nothing. They start counting Tang garrisons.
blocks.ko: 서라벌에서는 분노가 더 크다. 사람들은 세 번의 전쟁에서 이 땅을 위해 피를 흘렸다. 황제가 약속한 땅이었다. 그런데 이제 죽은 말 위에서 그 땅을 갖지 않겠다고 맹세했다. 젊은 장교들은 병영에서 배신이라는 말을 한다. 나이 든 장교들은 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 당의 주둔지를 세기 시작한다.

blocks.html: That night the king finds his uncle in the stable, cleaning a stall that is empty.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 왕은 마구간에서 외숙을 찾아낸다. 빈 마구간을 치우고 있다.

lines: 흰 말은 내가 다시 구해 드리겠소, 외숙.
en: I’ll find you another white horse, Uncle.

lines: 말 대신 전쟁을 하나 찾아 주십시오. 또 무슨 맹세를 시키기 전에, 한 번만 더 가 보고 싶습니다.
en: I’m seventy, Majesty. I’ve buried three.
Find me a war instead. I’d like to go to one more before they make me swear to something else.

blocks.label: The Ancestral Temple
blocks.ko: 종묘

blocks.html: Three summers later, the old man got his war. It ended tonight, with a monk at a gate. He stands beside the king in the temple now, and neither of them looks at the iron for long.
blocks.ko: 세 해 뒤, 노인은 전쟁을 얻었다. 그 전쟁은 오늘 밤 끝났다. 한 승려가 문 하나를 열면서. 이제 그는 종묘에서 왕 곁에 서 있고, 둘 다 그 쇠를 오래 쳐다보지 못한다.

en: Uncle. Before the emperors. Before seals, and oaths, and governors with lists.
Who was the first king of this land?
lines: 외숙. 황제들보다 먼저. 도장이니 맹세니, 명단 든 도독이니 하는 것들보다 먼저.

en: Ask your mother. She tells it to every child in the house.
It starts with a bear.
lines: 어머님께 여쭤 보십시오. 집안 아이마다 들려주십니다.

en: A bear.
A patient one. Your mother always looks at me when she gets to that part.
lines: 참을성 많은 곰입니다. 어머님은 그 대목만 오면 꼭 저를 보십니다.

blocks.html: To find the first king of this land, we have to go back before there were kingdoms… to a bear in a cave…!
blocks.ko: 이 땅의 첫 임금을 찾으려면, 나라가 생기기도 전으로 거슬러 올라가야 한다. 동굴 속 곰 한 마리에게로…!

entries.tone: founder fairy tale, then a dark legend
entries.subtitle: 고조선

logline.en: Before there are any kingdoms, there is a son in heaven who keeps looking down.
logline.ko: 나라가 하나도 없던 때, 하늘에 자꾸만 아래를 내려다보는 아들이 있었다.

images.at: A bear and a tiger come to him
images.alt: A bear and a tiger crouch in the cave with mugwort and garlic
images.prompt: Ink painting of the myth. Inside a cave: a bear and a tiger crouch in darkness with a bundle of mugwort and a pile of garlic between them; a single shaft of daylight from the cave mouth stops just short of them; the tiger’s head turns to the light, restless; the bear sits still. ONE device: the light shaft that does not reach them. MYTH INK — this beat is myth, not history, so it is painted as a STRIKING Korean ink painting (sumukhwa), not the house colour style. Joseon sumi ink on raw hanji paper with EXTREME LIGHT AGAINST DARK: huge saturated masses of black ink set against blinding bare paper; light is always the unpainted paper itself, never painted white; almost no mid-grey; hard edges where light meets dark, wet bleeding edges everywhere else. Splashed ink (pomuk), dry-brush flying white, ink spatter, mist left as untouched paper. Monumental emptiness and ONE graphic device carrying the frame; a dramatic angle (worm’s-eye, bird’s-eye, dutch). Gods, giants, beasts and wonders may fill the frame; mortals stay small inside the wonder. Figures in confident calligraphic brush line; named faces match the attached portraits, translated into a few ink strokes. Black ink and paper only, except at most ONE small translucent wash of a single colour on the one symbolic object the scene names. Not photoreal, not webtoon shading, not watercolor landscape, not oil, no glow, no halo. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. No text, no calligraphy, no seal stamp, no watermark.

Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.alt: Poster key art: Dangun rests against the sleeping great bear on the mountain summit at night, his hand on its head as campfires burn far below
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; crowns, antlers, wings and heads stay well inside the central band; no title, no lettering. Night on a bare mountain summit above a besieged valley: tiny enemy campfires scattered far below, a huge starry sky with ink cloud. Low angle across the rock. INTERACTION: Dangun sits with his back against the flank of the huge dark-brown bear lying curled on the summit; the bear has laid its great head across his lap, and he rests one hand on its brow, watching the fires below, calm. Its breath steams in the cold. One warm firelight bounce (#b8956a) from a small brazier at their feet lights his face, his hand and the bear’s muzzle; the rest is indigo and ink, the campfires below as bokeh. STYLE: HEEWON STYLE, more painterly, with hints of Korean ink painting — Korean webtoon figures (clean ink linework, simplified expressive faces matching the attached portrait, watercolor-washed) inside a hand-painted world of watercolor and oil with traditional sumukhwa ink: splashed-ink storm clouds, bold dry calligraphic brush strokes in manes, fur, feathers, robes and grass, ink bleeding into wet wash, small ink splatters and drips near the frame edges, patches of bare rice paper where the edges dissolve; oil glazes only deepen the darks, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. Movie-poster key art: bold iconic silhouette, the two subjects large and close, one dramatic low angle, one bright break of light behind them, big dark masses, few hues plus one accent, film-poster drama but NO text, NO title, NO credits, NO logo, NO seal stamp. Not photoreal, not 3D. No glow aura, no halo, no emissive outline — the accent colour is real light. One of each named person. No watermark. CANON — DANGUN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_dangun.png (face only; invent a new pose). #b8956a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | GOM (곰, dangun's great bear, guardian of Old Joseon) — attached board /obj_bear.png: HUGE dark-brown bear, far bigger than a man — massive shoulder hump, thick shaggy dark chocolate-brown fur with lighter tips catching the light, broad heavy head, small dark eyes, short round ears, long curved claws — match the board. Divine render: numinous through scale and atmosphere, never a glow outline. Ungnyeo's first shape: the bear that kept to the cave for a hundred days on mugwort and garlic and came out a woman. In the shape she left behind it stays near her son: patient, enormous, gentle with him and with no one else. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS are a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST room (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt) painted in that same wash-and-glaze: a warm umber-to-black ground, walls, timber, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft with soft sfumato falloff — the webtoon figures are set INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. images.prompt: Original East Asian ink painting on plain white paper. A gayageum seen from the side, almost all strings cut and hanging as broken hairlines that become one long road-stroke leaving the frame. One string still taut. No person, or only a departed handprint in pale ink. A small bleed of ash-blue only on the one remaining string. Flying white, dry brush, the feeling of a kingdom already gone. No text, no seal, no watermark, no map.

blocks.html: Before there are any kingdoms, there is a son in heaven who keeps looking down. He is Hwanung. His father Hwanin, the Lord of Heaven, notices, looks down himself at a mountain called Taebaek and the people living around it, and decides the world could use his son.
blocks.ko: 나라라는 것이 하나도 없던 때, 하늘에 자꾸 아래를 내려다보는 아들이 있다. 환웅이다. 아버지인 하늘의 임금 환인이 그것을 알아채고, 저도 태백이라는 산과 그 둘레에 사는 사람들을 내려다본 뒤, 세상에 아들이 쓸모 있겠다고 정한다.

blocks.caption: The Lord of Heaven. He has been watching this peninsula since before it had names.
blocks.ko: 하늘의 주인. 이 반도에 이름이 생기기 전부터 내려다보고 있었다.

blocks.title: Old Joseon · 고조선
blocks.caption: Heaven’s mandate made into a capital: Hwanin → Hwanung → Dangun → Asadal.
blocks.ko: 하늘의 명을 수도로 만든 계보. 환인 → 환웅 → 단군 → 아사달.

blocks.html: Hwanin does not plough — he opens the sky. Three seals go down with his son, so that nobody on the ground can mistake him for a prince playing at exile. Every later king in this chronicle will cut seals of his own, and every one of them is copying these.
blocks.ko: 환인은 갈지 않는다 — 하늘을 연다. 아들과 함께 천부인 셋이 내려간다. 땅의 누구도 그를 유배 놀이 하는 왕자로 착각하지 못하게. 이 편년의 후대 임금들은 저마다 제 인장을 새길 것이고, 그 모두가 이것을 베낀다.

blocks.html: Hwanung lands on a mountain under the sacred birch. He names the ground beneath it the Divine City. Three thousand followers come down with him. Among them are the lords of wind, rain and cloud. Someone has to argue with the weather.
blocks.ko: 환웅은 신단수 아래 산에 내려앉는다. 그 밑의 땅을 신시라 부른다. 무리 삼천이 함께 내려온다. 그 가운데 바람과 비와 구름의 우두머리들이 있다. 누군가는 날씨와 말다툼을 해야 하니까.

blocks.caption: Hwanung. A son of heaven who kept looking down until his father let him go.
blocks.ko: 환웅. 자꾸 아래를 내려다보다가, 끝내 아버지가 보내 준 하늘의 아들.

blocks.html: From there he hands out civilisation in instalments. Laws. Punishments. Lifespans. Illness. Good and evil. Medicine. Three hundred and sixty matters in all. Somebody counted.
blocks.ko: 거기서 그는 훗날 문명이라 불릴 것을 할부로 나눠 준다. 법. 형벌. 수명. 병. 선과 악. 의술. 모두 삼백육십 가지. 누군가 세어 두었다.

blocks.html: There is a short way to tell the rest, the way it is carved on stones. The long way begins, as long ways do, with a bear who wanted something so badly that she outlasted a tiger for it.
blocks.ko: 나머지를 짧게 전하는 방식이 있다. 돌에 새기는 방식이다. 길게 전하는 방식은, 긴 이야기가 늘 그렇듯, 무언가를 너무나 간절히 원한 나머지 호랑이보다 오래 견딘 곰 한 마리에서 시작된다.

blocks.html: A bear and a tiger come to him and ask to be made human. He gives them a bundle of mugwort, twenty cloves of garlic, and one instruction: stay out of the sun for a hundred days.
blocks.ko: 곰과 범이 그를 찾아와 사람이 되게 해 달라 청한다. 그는 쑥 한 줌과 마늘 스무 쪽을 주고 한 가지를 이른다. 백 일 동안 햇빛을 보지 마라.

blocks.label: The Sacred Birch
blocks.ko: 신단수

blocks.html: The bear stays. She comes out a woman on the twenty-first morning, garlic still on her breath, and finds the mountain already staffed — wind, rain, cloud, and not one of them a husband. So she stands under the sacred tree. Not once. Every day, on the path he has to take if he means to reach the hall.
blocks.ko: 곰은 남는다. 스무하루째 아침, 입가에 마늘 냄새가 남은 채로 여자가 되어 나오니, 산은 이미 사람이 가득하다 — 바람, 비, 구름, 그리고 남편이 될 이는 하나도 없다. 그래서 신단수 아래에 선다. 한 번이 아니다. 그가 전각으로 가려면 반드시 지나야 하는 길에, 날마다.
blocks.art: Open on the cave mouth: the tiger’s tracks leading away into the snow, then her first step into daylight.

blocks.caption: Ungnyeo. Twenty-one days in a cave, and the tiger left first. A husband should be easy.
blocks.ko: 웅녀. 동굴에서 스무하루, 먼저 나간 건 호랑이였다. 지아비 하나쯤이야.

blocks.html: He means to reach the hall. On the third evening he gets as far as the birch, and the seal in his hand becomes a thing he is holding for no reason he can name.
blocks.ko: 그는 전각에 닿을 작정이다. 사흘째 저녁, 자작나무까지는 온다. 손의 인장은, 왜 들고 있는지 스스로도 말할 수 없는 물건이 된다.

en: You're going to walk past again.
…Not today.
Yesterday you did.
And the day before. I was standing right here.
I saw you.
The garlic reached this far.
Twenty-one days of that, and this is what came out.
…I was going to say don't come closer.

lines: 가지 마. 아니— 가지 마시오. 손이—
en: Too late.
Stay. I mean— don't go. Your hand—
You already have the hand.
…Scared of the rest?
I am.
Because you're looking at me.

lines: 나무는 보고 있을 테니까. 나는… 더.
en: Then come down.
The tree can watch. I want… more.

blocks.html: The kiss is clumsy. Beard, a new mouth, birch bark at her back. She makes a small furious sound and tries again, and the second one lands.
blocks.ko: 입맞춤은 서투르다. 수염, 처음 쓰는 입, 등에 닿는 자작나무 껍질. 그녀가 짧게 성난 소리를 내고 다시 하고, 두 번째는 닿는다.

blocks.html: White silk goes down among the roots. The fur at her throat opens under his mouth. She laughs once, startled at the sound, and pulls him down by the hair.
blocks.ko: 흰 비단이 뿌리 사이에 내려앉는다. 목덜미의 털깃이 그의 입 밑에서 풀린다. 그녀는 한 번 웃는다. 그 소리에 스스로 놀라서. 그리고 머리카락을 잡아 그를 끌어내린다.

blocks.html: By the time the moon clears the snow on the peak, the rust-red sash is somewhere in the moss, and neither of them has gone back up the path.
blocks.ko: 달빛이 봉우리의 눈에 닿을 때쯤, 붉은 띠는 이끼 어딘가에 있고, 둘 다 그 길로 돌아 올라가지 않았다.

en: …You're going already?
I can't.
I don't know where I put the seal.
Under my head.
I took it. …Don't go.
…Thief.
Marry me in the morning.
Right now I'm here.

blocks.label: Asadal
blocks.ko: 아사달

blocks.html: Their son is Dangun. The name on the stone is Wanggeom: a king who governs, not one who inherits a bone rank. He founds Asadal where the mountain meets the plain. He rules for fifteen hundred years, and then he becomes the mountain.
blocks.ko: 그 아들이 단군이다. 돌에 새긴 이름은 왕검. 골품을 물려받은 임금이 아니라 다스리는 임금이다. 그는 산과 들이 만나는 곳에 아사달을 세운다. 천오백 년을 다스리고, 산이 된다.

blocks.caption: Dangun. Half heaven, half bear, and all the paperwork of a first king.
blocks.ko: 단군. 반은 하늘, 반은 곰, 그리고 첫 임금의 서류는 전부 그의 몫.

blocks.hanja: 乃授天符印三箇 雄率徒三千 降於太伯山頂神壇樹下 是謂神市 熊女與婚 生子 號曰壇君王儉
blocks.ko: 이에 천부인 셋을 주어 다스리게 하니, 환웅이 무리 삼천을 이끌고 태백산 꼭대기 신단수 아래로 내려와 이를 신시라 하였다. 웅녀와 혼인하여 아들을 낳으니, 이름하여 단군왕검이라 하였다.
blocks.html: He granted three heavenly seals and sent him to govern. Hwanung led a following of three thousand and descended under the sacred altar-tree on the summit of Mount Taebaek; this was called the Divine City. He married the bear-woman, and she bore a son named Dangun Wanggeom.
blocks.source: Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) bk. 1, Wonder 1 — Old Joseon (Dangun); Ha & Mintz tr., pp. 32–33

blocks.html: Where the mountain meets the plain, and the first crown met both.
blocks.ko: 산이 들을 만나는 곳. 첫 왕관이 둘 다를 만난 곳.

blocks.html: Every later crown in these kingdoms argues, one way or another, back to the woman who used to be a bear. Her son’s city keeps his name long after he has become a mountain.
blocks.ko: 이후 이 왕국들의 왕관은, 어떤 식으로든, 한때 곰이었던 여자에게로 거슬러 올라간다. 아들의 도성은 그가 산이 된 뒤에도 오래 그의 이름을 지닌다.

blocks.label: The Fall of Joseon
blocks.ko: 조선의 멸망

blocks.html: Joseon outlives its founder by a long way. Two thousand years on it is still there, run by other kings now, from a walled city on the Taedong that has kept his name: Wanggeom. In the autumn of 109 BC, Han comes to the gate.
blocks.ko: 조선은 시조보다 훨씬 오래 산다. 이천 년이 지나도 여전히 거기 있다. 이제는 다른 임금들이, 그의 이름 왕검을 그대로 지닌 대동강가의 성에서 다스린다. 기원전 109년 가을, 한나라가 그 성문 앞에 온다.

blocks.html: It takes the empire of the West a year to take one fortress, and they do not take it. Wanggeom holds through a siege that begins in the autumn and is still going the following autumn.
blocks.ko: 서토의 제국이 성 하나를 얻는 데 한 해가 걸리고, 결국 얻지 못한다. 왕검성은 가을에 시작해 이듬해 가을까지 이어지는 포위를 견딘다.

blocks.html: So they stop attacking the walls and start talking to the men behind them, which is cheaper and has never once failed.
blocks.ko: 그래서 그들은 성벽을 치는 일을 그만두고, 성벽 뒤의 사람들과 이야기하기 시작한다. 더 싸고, 단 한 번도 실패한 적 없는 방법이다.

blocks.label: The King's Wall
blocks.ko: 왕의 성벽

blocks.html: King Ugeo has stopped sleeping in the palace. He sleeps on the wall, where he can hear the Han camp coughing, and his son, the prince, has started sleeping somewhere else.
blocks.ko: 우거왕은 궁에서 자지 않은 지 오래다. 한나라 진영의 기침 소리가 들리는 성벽 위에서 잔다. 태자는 언제부턴가 다른 데서 잔다.

lines: 성문만 열면 성 안 사람은 아무도 건드리지 않겠답니다.
en: Father. They’ve sent terms again.
Open the gate, they say, and nobody inside gets hurt.
They said that last autumn.
Who brought it to you?
…Does it matter who?
It matters.
Get off my wall.

blocks.html: One of the ministers who have been doing the talking goes over the wall that week and dies on the road before he reaches the Han tents. Another does not bother with the road. One night at the start of summer he sends men up the wall-stair instead.
blocks.ko: 말을 주고받던 대신 하나가 그 주에 성벽을 넘어가다, 한나라 장막에 닿기도 전에 길에서 죽는다. 또 한 대신은 길로 나서지 않는다. 초여름 어느 밤, 그는 성벽 계단으로 사람들을 올려 보낸다.
blocks.art: Torchlight on the wall-stair, knives, the king turning from the parapet too late.

en: Majesty—!
blocks.speaker: Seong Gi

lines: 사람들 데리고 나가. 살아서… 어디서든, 새로 나라를 세워라.
en: …Seong Gi?
Don’t hold the city. Not for me.
Get the people out. Live… and make a new country. Anywhere.

blocks.html: Seong Gi closes the king’s eyes, goes back up to the parapet, and holds the city anyway.
blocks.ko: 성기는 임금의 눈을 감기고, 다시 성가퀴로 올라가, 그래도 성을 지킨다.

blocks.html: He holds it until the dead minister’s son and the prince go down into the lanes, where people have been eating bark since the spring.
blocks.ko: 죽은 대신의 아들과 태자가 골목으로 내려갈 때까지는 지킨다. 골목 사람들은 봄부터 나무껍질을 먹고 있었다.

lines: 그럼 이제 누구 때문에 굶는 거요? 저 사람?
en: The king is dead.
So who are you starving for now? Him?
blocks.art: Choi pointing up at Seong Gi on the wall.

blocks.html: Before morning Seong Gi is dead too.
blocks.ko: 아침이 오기 전에 성기도 죽는다.

blocks.html: Someone lifts the bar.
blocks.ko: 누군가 빗장을 든다.
blocks.art: Wordless. The gate of Wanggeom swings open from the inside; Han banners wait in the grey light.

en: The wall did not come down.
A door was opened from the inside.

blocks.html: Han takes Wanggeom. Some of the people the king told to live go south over the mountains. They settle in six villages around Surabol. Two generations later, they'll go looking for a king. The rest stay, and the empire cuts them into four pieces. The last piece is still collecting taxes four hundred years later.
blocks.ko: 한나라가 왕검성을 차지한다. 임금이 살라고 한 사람들 가운데 일부는 산을 넘어 남쪽으로 간다. 서라벌 둘레 골짜기에 여섯 마을을 이룬다. 두 세대 뒤, 그들은 임금을 찾아 나설 것이다. 나머지는 남아, 제국의 손에 넷으로 쪼개진다. 그 마지막 하나는 사백 년 뒤에도 세금을 걷고 있다.

blocks.html: That is the story Munmu gets, in his mother’s version, with extra garlic. He came for the bear. He keeps thinking about the door.
blocks.ko: 문무가 들은 이야기는 그것이다. 어머니 판본이라, 마늘이 좀 더 들어갔다. 그는 곰 이야기를 들으러 왔다. 그런데 자꾸 문 생각이 난다.

blocks.html: Eight hundred years later, the empire comes back to the same river to do the same thing. This time, Goguryeo has a prince left…!
blocks.ko: 팔백 년 뒤, 제국이 같은 강으로 돌아와 같은 짓을 한다. 이번에는 고구려에 왕족 하나가 남아 있다…!

logline.en: Geom Mojam raises Goguryeo’s flag and finds a royal to stand under it. They disagree about dying, and only one of them sees the morning.
logline.ko: 검모잠이 고구려의 깃발을 세우고 그 아래 세울 왕족을 찾는다. 둘은 죽는 일을 두고 갈라서고, 아침을 맞는 건 하나뿐이다.

images.alt: The Tang Andong Protectorate built over a Goguryeo city — real streets, walls, and a Tang yamen
images.prompt: Cinematic historical still, 16:9, high view of a REAL 7th-century city on former Goguryeo land: packed-earth walls, a Tang administrative yamen and grid of streets laid over older Korean streets. Gold Tang banners, a few remaining red Goguryeo roofs. Xue Rengui a small white-armored figure at the east gate. Painterly cinema. Flat sky, no clouds. No text, no watermark.

images.alt: The old Goguryeo white-tiger standard raised again on the Taedong
images.prompt: Cinematic historical illustration of white tiger banner, Three Kingdoms of Samhan / Tang era (670), scene: Goguryeo Revival Society, painterly digital art, dramatic natural light, rich period costume, no modern elements, no text, no watermark, --ar 3:2 --stylize 250

images.alt: A single torch burning with Goguryeo red flame in darkness - resistance lives on
images.prompt: Resistance drama: A single torch burning with Goguryeo red flame (#C30000) against pitch black negative space

images.alt: Fleet as triangular sails against horizon with golden accent - minimal iconic symbol of Tang naval power
Palace silhouette against golden sky at sunset - minimal iconic symbol of Tang architectural grandeur with vast negative space
Single Tang banner flag in wind with gold accent - minimal iconic symbol of Tang imperial authority and pageantry

blocks.label: The Protectorate
blocks.ko: 안동도호부

blocks.html: Every revival needs two things: a flag and a royal. Geom Mojam has the flag.
blocks.ko: 부흥에는 두 가지가 필요하다. 깃발 하나와 왕족 하나. 검모잠에게는 깃발이 있다.

blocks.html: The empire has done it again on the Taedong. Pyongyang is a Protectorate now, run by Tang clerks who seem surprised that anyone minds. Mojam minds. He kills the clerks, raises Goguryeo’s colours, and goes looking for someone royal to stand under them.
blocks.ko: 제국이 대동강에서 또 같은 짓을 했다. 평양은 이제 도호부다. 누가 싫어하는 걸 보고 놀라는 당의 서기들이 다스린다. 모잠은 싫다. 서기들을 죽이고, 고구려의 깃발을 올리고, 그 아래 세울 왕족을 찾아 나선다.

blocks.html: He finds one on an island in the western sea, mending a net. His name is Anseung. His father is Yeon Jungto, the uncle who took twelve cities over to Silla. His mother was a king’s daughter. Mojam only needs the second half.
blocks.ko: 그는 서해의 한 섬에서 그물을 깁고 있는 사내를 찾아낸다. 이름은 안승. 아버지는 열두 성을 들고 신라로 넘어간 숙부, 연정토다. 어머니는 왕의 딸이었다. 모잠에게 필요한 건 뒤의 절반뿐이다.

blocks.html: Mojam, a daehyeong of Goguryeo from Surim Fortress, gathered the surviving people, marched from Gungmo Fortress to south of the Pae River, and killed the Tang officials and the monk Beop'an. Heading for Silla, he reached Saya Island in the western sea, found Anseung, son of the Goguryeo minister Yeon Jungto, brought him into the River Palace, and set him up as lord.
blocks.ko: 고구려 수림성 사람 대형 모잠이 남은 백성을 거두어 모아, 궁모성에서 패강 남쪽에 이르러 당의 관인과 승려 법안 등을 죽였다. 신라로 향해 가다가 서해 사야도에 이르러, 고구려 대신 연정토의 아들 안승을 만나 한성 안으로 맞아들이고 임금으로 받들었다.
blocks.hanja: 高句麗水臨城人牟岑大兄，收合殘民，自窮牟城，至浿江南，殺唐官人及僧法安等。向新羅行，至西海史冶島，見高句麗大臣淵淨土之子安勝，迎致漢城中，奉以爲君。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 6, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 10 (670), sixth month

blocks.label: The River Camp
blocks.ko: 강가 진영

blocks.html: By the next spring the revival has a court, a royal, and four thousand households camped along the river. It also has a Tang army coming down the north road. The two men argue about it in front of everyone, because a revival has no rooms with doors.
blocks.ko: 이듬해 봄, 부흥군에게는 조정이 있고, 왕족이 있고, 강을 따라 진을 친 사천 호가 있다. 북쪽 길로 내려오는 당군도 있다. 두 사내는 모두가 보는 앞에서 그 일로 다툰다. 부흥군에게는 문 달린 방이 없으니까.

blocks.speaker: Geom Mojam
en: We hold the river. We hold Pyongyang.
If they want it back, they can climb over us.
lines: 도로 가져가려면 우리 시체를 넘어오라 하시오.

blocks.speaker: Anseung
en: They climbed over Pyongyang two years ago. With better walls than ours in the way.
lines: 두 해 전에 저들은 평양도 넘었소. 우리 것보다 나은 성벽을 두고도.

blocks.speaker: Geom Mojam
lines: 평양 땅에는 사백 년 묵은 임금들이 묻혀 계시오. 그분들을 두고 신라 사랑채로 가겠다는 거요?
en: Pyongyang has kings in its soil four hundred years deep. You want to leave them for a Silla guest room?

blocks.speaker: Anseung
lines: 땅속의 임금들은 기다려 주실 거요. 그 위의 사천 호는 못 기다리오.
en: The kings in the soil will keep. The four thousand households above it won’t.

blocks.speaker: Geom Mojam
en: Then go. Take your households.
I’ll hold it with whoever stays.
lines: 그럼 가시오. 그 사천 호 데리고.

blocks.html: He says it loud, to the fires. Around the fires, men stop eating. Anseung looks at them. Nobody stands up. Nobody sits down either. He understands what that means before Mojam does. In the morning they will follow whoever is still alive.
blocks.ko: 그는 그 말을 크게, 모닥불들 쪽으로 한다. 불가의 사내들이 먹던 손을 멈춘다. 안승이 그들을 본다. 일어서는 자도 없고, 다시 앉는 자도 없다. 그게 무슨 뜻인지 그는 모잠보다 먼저 안다. 아침이 되면, 저들은 살아 있는 쪽을 따를 것이다.

blocks.speaker: Anseung
en: …You’re right, General.
Let’s sleep on it.

blocks.html: That night Anseung has him killed in his tent. It is the first Goguryeo blood the revival spills, and it is spilled by Goguryeo.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 안승은 그를 장막 안에서 죽인다. 부흥군이 흘린 첫 고구려 피이고, 그것을 흘린 것도 고구려다.

blocks.html: In the morning the men by the fires do not ask where the general is. They pack.
blocks.ko: 아침에 불가의 사내들은 장군이 어디 있느냐고 묻지 않는다. 짐을 싼다.

blocks.html: Then he takes four thousand households south, to Silla.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 사천 호를 이끌고 남쪽 신라로 간다.

blocks.label: Silla's Guest
blocks.ko: 신라의 손님

blocks.html: Munmu gives him a title, a district, and a name for the thing: Goguryeo, still standing, inside Silla. It is a useful fiction and both sides know exactly how useful.
blocks.ko: 문무왕은 그에게 관작과 고을과 이름 하나를 준다. 신라 안에 여전히 서 있는 고구려. 쓸모 있는 허구이고, 양쪽 다 그것이 얼마나 쓸모 있는지 정확히 안다.

blocks.html: Silla settles him in a town that was somebody else's kingdom ten years ago. Within the year he is called King of Goguryeo. In time he gets a bride, and a seat at Munmu's feasts. Well below the king's.
blocks.ko: 신라는 그를 열 해 전까지 남의 나라 땅이던 고을에 앉힌다. 그해가 가기 전에 그는 고구려왕이라 불린다. 때가 되자 신부도 얻고, 문무의 잔치에 자리도 얻는다. 왕의 자리보다 한참 아래다.

lines: 신라 안에 고구려 왕이라. 황제가 질색하겠군.
en: A king of Goguryeo in Silla. The emperor will hate it.
Good. Give him a seal. A big one.
And end the patent the way the emperor ends his. “Be reverent.”
Twice. He’ll hate that most of all.
lines: 책서 끝은 황제가 쓰는 대로 맺어라. ‘삼가고 삼갈지어다.’
두 번. 그게 제일 싫을 거다.

blocks.html: Anseung bows when the seal comes, very low: a king of Goguryeo in a Silla hall. Far north, on the Taedong, a tent is still standing with nobody in it.
blocks.ko: 인장이 오자 안승은 아주 깊이 절한다. 신라의 전각 안에 선 고구려의 왕. 저 북쪽 대동강가에는, 아무도 없는 장막 하나가 아직 서 있다.

blocks.html: The emperor hears there is a king of Goguryeo in Silla. His general reaches for a brush instead of a sword…!
blocks.ko: 황제가 신라 안에 고구려 왕이 있다는 말을 듣는다. 그의 장수는 칼 대신 붓을 집어 든다…!

logline.en: Xue Rengui would like to win this war by post. The king does not go to bed.
logline.ko: 설인귀는 이 전쟁을 편지로 이기고 싶어 한다. 왕은 잠자리에 들지 않는다.

images.at: Alas! While the two kingdoms stood
images.alt: Munmu stands at the black window of his writing room, dictating through the night while the scribe writes.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Interior, deep night, the king's writing room in Surabol. Low WORM'S-EYE from beside the scribe's desk. ONE device: one tall lattice window, black, with a sliver of moon. King Munmu, FACE ONLY from the attached portrait, in his crimson robe, STANDING, one fist pressed against the window frame, turned half back toward the room, jaw set, mouth open dictating — tired and furious, his father's charm gone hard. In the foreground the scribe's bent back and brush hand over a long paper scroll, out of focus, the writing a soft blur, nothing readable. An ink-stone and spent candle stubs on the desk. Munmu's shadow climbs the receding plaster wall. Key: the desk lamp from below, crimson #C41E3A specular on his silk; the rest umber black. CANON — KING MUNMU — FACE and garments from attached /ch_munmu.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Square jaw, goatee and moustache, confident grin; arms folded when he is pleased with himself. Dress: As king: crimson robe with gold dragon embroidery, blue shoulder pieces, gold Silla crown. Earlier: prince/hwarang stage portraits. Crown: Silla gold crown, as the attached crown: a gold band with three tree-shaped uprights stepped like the character 出 and two antler uprights at the back, hung with round gold spangles and curved green jade gogok, long gold pendants at the temples. ref_muyeol shows it worn with the king's red robe and gold-scroll collar (ignore its painted backdrop). Demeanor: Cocky, warm, practical; his father's charm with his uncle's spine. #C41E3A as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: katana; Tang dragon robe in place of Silla court dress. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Silla: attached /ref_hanbok_silla.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline.
