blocks.label: THE LAKE REMEMBERS
blocks.ko: 호수는 기억한다

blocks.html: Old now, between campaigns that are mostly paperwork, Yushin still finds the cavern. The steam is thinner. The three are not. They look the same age they always looked — which is either mercy or mockery, and he has never asked which.
blocks.ko: 이제 늙어, 대부분 문서인 원정 사이에서도 유신은 동굴을 찾는다. 김은 옅어졌다. 셋은 아니다. 늘 그 나이로 보인다 — 자비인지 조롱인지, 그는 끝내 묻지 않았다.

blocks.html: Hyullé’s hand finds the water beside the ledge where he always sits, and stays there. Fifty years of the same ledge.
blocks.ko: 혈레의 손이 그가 늘 앉던 턱 곁의 물을 찾아, 그대로 머문다. 같은 턱을 오십 년.

en: You still undress like a soldier checking for wounds.
Sit. The counsel is shorter these days. So is the war. Slower. Let me look at you.
lines: 앉아요. 요즘은 충고도 짧고, 전쟁도. 천천히 해요. 얼굴 좀 보게요.

en: He’s going to say it.
Watch — three, two —
But Her Majesty is gone.
…I still hear myself saying it.
Ugh… even in the Western Flower Field she gets the title.
What did that mortal have that we don’t?
…Don’t answer. Stay until the steam drops. Before the hill keeps you.
lines: 으엑… 서천꽃밭에서도 그 인간은 직함을 가져.
그 인간한테 우리한테 없는 게 뭐였는데?
…답하지 마. 김이 식을 때까지 있어. 언덕이 널 두기 전에.

en: I didn’t — bring —
…It’s just warmer there.
You always liked it. Come sit. Please.

blocks.html: The steam thins. For a breath his father’s mouth is in the water — not the counsel, only the name — and then it is steam again.
blocks.ko: 김이 옅어진다. 한 숨 동안 아버지 입이 물에 있다 — 조언이 아니라 이름만 — 그리고 다시 김이다.

blocks.html: He sits. For once he does not rush the border. Narim talks about a tree that outlived three kings. Golhwa falls asleep against the stone mid-complaint. Hyullé says nothing, and that is the visit he will remember when the biographies start lying.
blocks.ko: 앉는다. 이번만큼은 국경을 재촉하지 않는다. 나림은 임금 셋을 살아낸 나무 이야기를 하고, 골화는 투덜이다 돌에 기대 잠든다. 혈레는 말이 없고 — 열전이 거짓을 쓰기 시작할 때 그가 기억할 방문이 바로 그것이다.

blocks.label: The Deathbed
blocks.ko: 임종

blocks.html: Seventh month, 673. He is seventy-nine. He has fought for sixty of those years and outlived nearly everyone worth outliving.
blocks.ko: 673년 칠월. 그는 일흔아홉이다. 그중 예순 해를 싸웠고, 오래 살 만한 가치가 있는 사람들 거의 전부보다 오래 살았다.

blocks.html: The King comes to the house himself, which kings do not do. Munmu does it anyway — he has known this man his entire life, and for most of it has not been sure whether to call him Marshal or uncle.
blocks.ko: 왕이 몸소 그 집을 찾는다. 왕이라면 하지 않는 일이다. 문무는 그래도 그렇게 한다 — 평생을 알아 온 사람이고, 그 세월 대부분을 이 사람을 대장군이라 불러야 할지 외숙이라 불러야 할지 확신하지 못한 채 지냈다.

blocks.html: The old man's eyes are already somewhere younger.
blocks.ko: 노인의 눈은 이미 더 젊은 날에 가 있다.

en: Yushin…

blocks.html: Nobody has called him by his bare name in forty-one years. The last one was a queen, on her coronation morning.
blocks.ko: 마흔한 해 동안 아무도 그를 이름만으로 부르지 않았다. 마지막으로 그렇게 부른 이는 즉위하던 아침의 여왕이었다.

en: Princess…
…The boy. Is he eating?
He’s farming. Badly. Shall I send for him?
…No.
Good. That he’s eating.

blocks.hanja: 伏願殿下 知成功之不易 念守成之亦難 疏遠小人 親近君子
blocks.ko: 엎드려 원하옵건대 전하께서는 공을 이루기가 쉽지 않고 이룬 것을 지키기도 또한 어려움을 생각하시어, 소인을 멀리하고 군자를 가까이 하소서.
blocks.html: I humbly pray Your Highness know that to succeed is not easy, and to keep what has been won is also hard. Keep petty men far and good men near.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 43, Biographies — Kim Yushin (final counsel); Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 2, p. 404

blocks.html: Kangrim reads his name three times at the bedside — Yushin. Yushin. Yushin. — before the marshal's last answer.
blocks.ko: 강림은 침상 옆에서 그의 이름을 세 번 부른다 — 유신. 유신. 유신. — 대장군의 마지막 대답을 듣기 전에.

en: Marshal.
One hundred and eight draws, one win that ended a friend, sixty years of being useful.
Question: were you becoming Silla — or proving you never needed their blood to outserve them?
lines: 백여덟 무승부, 친구를 끝낸 한 승, 육십 년의 쓸모.
질문: 신라가 되려 한 겁니까 — 아니면 그들 피 없이도 더 섬길 수 있음을 증명한 겁니까?

en: …I wanted in.
Wanting in is not shameful. Pretending I did not is.
lines: 들어가고 싶은 건 부끄러운 게 아니야. 아니라고 꾸미는 게 부끄러운 거지.

en: Clean answer.
His Majesty’s kingdom has room for men who told the truth late.
lines: 폐하의 나라엔 늦게 진실을 말한 사내를 둘 자리가 있네.

blocks.html: When the escort walks out through the courtyard, Munhee is standing by the well. She is sixty-seven. She sees her brother walking beside the stranger. Nobody else in the yard does. Above the roof the eastern star is up, the one that sits among the stars without being one of them.
blocks.ko: 저승 길잡이가 마당을 지나 나갈 때, 문희는 우물가에 서 있다. 예순일곱이다. 낯선 사내 곁에서 걸어가는 오라비를 그녀는 본다. 마당의 다른 누구도 보지 못한다. 지붕 위로 동쪽 별이 떠 있다. 별들 사이에 있으면서 별은 아닌, 그 별.

en: Brother. Are you a Silla man now?
…I don’t know. Ask them for me.

blocks.html: She lets him go without asking twice. There is nobody left now who calls her little sister.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 두 번 묻지 않고 그를 보낸다. 이제 그녀를 동생이라 불러 줄 사람은 아무도 없다.

blocks.html: He is buried at Geumsan with the honours of a king and the rank of a subject. Somebody will close that gap. It takes a hundred and sixty years.
blocks.ko: 그는 금산에 왕의 예로, 신하의 품계로 묻힌다. 누군가는 그 틈을 메울 것이다. 백육십 년이 걸린다.

blocks.html: — Kim Yushin —
blocks.ko: — 김유신 —
blocks.art: Full-page end card. The name and the five italic paragraphs after it (through “…made him a king.”) share one page.

blocks.html: His grandfather bought the family a rank with a kingdom. Everyone honoured the deal, and everyone remembered it. So he made himself the one thing they could not do without, and he was very, very good at it. He loved a queen for forty years and never once said so where it could be heard. They would not let him all the way in while he lived. Once he was safely dead, they made him a king.
blocks.ko: 그의 할아버지는 나라 하나로 집안의 신분을 샀다. 모두가 그 거래를 지켰고, 모두가 그것을 기억했다. 그래서 그는 그들이 없이는 안 되는 단 하나가 되었고, 그것을 아주, 아주 잘해 냈다. 사십 년을 한 여왕을 사랑했으나, 들릴 만한 자리에서는 한 번도 그렇다고 말하지 않았다. 살아 있는 동안에는 끝내 다 들여보내 주지 않았다. 안전하게 죽고 나자, 그들은 그를 왕으로 만들었다.
blocks.art: Full-page end card, continued.

blocks.label: Lady Jiso
blocks.ko: 지소부인

blocks.html: After the funeral Wonsul comes down from the hills at last and asks at the gate for his mother. The lamp is out. Lady Jiso has already cut her hair for the nunnery.
blocks.ko: 장례가 끝나고 원술은 마침내 산에서 내려와 대문에서 어머니를 청한다. 등불은 꺼져 있다. 지소부인은 이미 비구니가 되려고 머리를 잘랐다.

blocks.speaker: Lady Jiso
lines: 여자는 셋을 따른다 했다. 아비, 지아비, 아들.
네 아버지가 너를 아들이라 부르지 않았는데, 내가 어찌 네 어미가 되겠느냐.
en: A woman has three to follow. Her father, her husband, her son.
My husband would not call you son. How am I to be your mother?

blocks.html: She does not come to the gate. The answer is carried out by a servant who cannot look at him. Wonsul stands in the road until dark and then goes back up into the hills. The record says only that he left weeping, and that he never stopped trying to give the afternoon back.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 대문까지 나오지 않는다. 대답은 그를 똑바로 보지 못하는 종이 들고 나온다. 원술은 어두워질 때까지 길에 서 있다가 다시 산으로 올라간다. 기록은 그가 울며 떠났다는 것, 그리고 그 한나절을 되돌리려는 일을 끝내 멈추지 않았다는 것만 적는다.

blocks.html: The king has buried his uncle. He still has one letter to answer, and a path nobody ever showed him…!
blocks.ko: 왕은 외숙을 묻었다. 아직 답할 편지가 하나 남았고, 아무도 보여 주지 않은 길이 하나 남았다…!

logline.en: The day after the funeral, Munmu signs a traitor’s death warrant, then finds his uncle’s spring. Something older than any kingdom is waiting on the water.
logline.ko: 장례 이튿날, 문무는 배신자의 사형 명령에 서명하고 외숙의 샘을 찾아간다. 물 위에서 어느 나라보다 오래된 누군가가 기다린다.

blocks.label: The Second Letter
blocks.ko: 두 번째 편지

blocks.html: The day after the funeral, a letter falls out of a sleeve.
blocks.ko: 장례 이튿날, 소매에서 편지 한 통이 떨어진다.

blocks.html: It is short. It is addressed to the Tang garrison at Bear Ford, and it promises them a door in the wall of Surabol, the way a man at Daeya once promised Baekje a granary. The hand is very steady. The king knows that hand. It copied his letter to Xue Rengui.
blocks.ko: 짧은 편지다. 받는 곳은 웅진의 당군 진영이고, 서라벌 성벽의 문 하나를 약속한다. 언젠가 대야성의 한 사내가 백제에 곳간을 약속했듯이. 글씨가 아주 차분하다. 왕은 그 글씨를 안다. 설인귀에게 보낸 그의 답서를 정서한 손이다.

en: Majesty. A softer word here and there—
lines: 전하. 여기저기 말 한두 마디만 누그러뜨리면—

en: You said that in the writing room.
You copied my letter very well, Daeto. Copy this one.
lines: 내 편지를 아주 잘 옮겨 적었소, 대토. 이것도 옮겨 적으시오.

blocks.html: It is his own death warrant. Daeto copies it out fair, and his hand is still very steady. His wife and children are made slaves. Nobody mentions it at court.
blocks.ko: 그것은 그 자신의 사형 명령이다. 대토는 그것을 정서한다. 손은 여전히 아주 차분하다. 처자는 노비가 된다. 조정에서 그 이야기를 꺼내는 사람은 아무도 없다.

blocks.label: The Steam Cavern
blocks.ko: 김 서린 동굴

blocks.html: That evening Munmu rides alone into the hills east of Surabol. His uncle never showed him the path. He finds it anyway, the way sons find what uncles hid on purpose.
blocks.ko: 그날 저녁 문무는 홀로 서라벌 동쪽 언덕으로 말을 달린다. 외숙은 그 길을 가르쳐 준 적이 없다. 그래도 그는 찾아낸다. 아들들이 외숙이 일부러 숨긴 것을 찾아내듯이.

blocks.html: He strips at the rock lip as if obeying an order nobody ever gave him in writing, and steps into water so black it reflects nothing.
blocks.ko: 그는 종이로 받지 못한 명령을 따르듯 바위 끝에서 옷을 벗고, 아무것도 비추지 않는 검은 물로 들어간다.
blocks.art: The house rule is the same: naked, clean-shaven, and only Kims.

blocks.html: Crimson leaves his shoulders the way a soldier sheds a campaign coat. Steam takes the rest. He does not look up until the water has him.
blocks.ko: 진홍이 어깨에서 내린다. 병사가 군복을 벗듯. 나머진 김이 가져간다. 물이 그를 잡을 때까지 올려다보지 않는다.

blocks.html: For a long time he only stands in the water. He is forty-seven, and a king, and there is nobody left alive who taught him to ride. He lets the steam have his face, so that nobody has to see it. Not even the rock.
blocks.ko: 한참 동안 그는 물속에 서 있기만 한다. 마흔일곱, 왕이다. 말 타는 법을 가르쳐 준 사람은 이제 아무도 살아 있지 않다. 그는 김에 얼굴을 맡긴다. 아무도 보지 않도록. 바위조차.

blocks.html: They smell him before they see him. Uncle’s heat, father’s road-dust, both houses in one walk. He still thinks he is alone. Golhwa’s mouth opens and does not close. Hyullé cannot get a word out. Narim bites her lip and fails at being eldest.
blocks.ko: 보기 전에 냄새로 안다. 외숙의 열, 아버지의 길먼지, 한 걸음 안에 집 둘. 그는 아직 혼자인 줄 안다. 골화의 입이 열리고 다물어지지 않는다. 혈레는 말이 안 나온다. 나림은 입술을 깨물고 언니 노릇에 실패한다.

blocks.html: They know him. The best of both: they said it first when he was twenty-one and came in with a jar, and they say it again now that the uncle is ash. Gaya in the shoulders. Surabol in the mouth. Fire comes off Golhwa’s skin. Water streams from Hyullé’s chin. A leaf turns in the steam around Narim and will not fall.
blocks.ko: 그들은 그를 안다. 양쪽의 최선. 스물하나, 항아리를 들고 왔을 때 처음 그렇게 말했고, 외숙이 재가 된 지금 다시 말한다. 어깨는 가야. 입은 서라벌. 골화의 살에서 불이 난다. 혈레의 턱에서 물이 흐른다. 나림 주위 김 속에서 잎 하나가 돌고, 떨어지지 않는다.

en: …You’re still here.
I brought a jar last time. I didn’t bring anything tonight.
lines: 지난번엔 항아리를 들고 왔었소. 오늘 밤엔 아무것도 안 가져왔소.

en: You brought him. On your shoulders. We can smell it.
Sit. Before you fall—

blocks.html: He looks at her like she is kind. Narim cannot finish the sentence. She is out of breath, and pretends the steam did that. Uncle’s shoulders. Father’s mouth. She is not supposed to want both, tonight of all nights.
blocks.ko: 그가 친절한 사람을 보듯 그녀를 본다. 나림은 문장을 끝내지 못한다. 숨이 가쁘다. 김 탓인 척한다. 외숙의 어깨. 아버지의 입. 둘 다 원하면 안 된다. 하필 오늘 같은 밤에.

en: He’s the one crying and I’m the one who can’t sit.
…Sorry. Ignore me. Stay till the steam drops.
lines: 우는 건 쟤인데 못 앉는 건 나야.
…미안. 나 무시해. 김 식을 때까지 있어.

en: Hello. I’ll be quiet.

blocks.html: That is all Hyullé gets out. She stands near him in the water and looks like she will break. He keeps the black water as a wall. He does not climb out.
blocks.ko: 혈레가 꺼낼 수 있는 말은 그게 전부다. 물속에서 그의 곁에 서서, 금방이라도 부서질 것처럼 보인다. 그는 검은 물을 벽으로 쓴다. 올라오지 않는다.

en: Sit down before you fall in again.
We are the mouths the hill uses. Wisdom, if you stand in the water and ask once. The uncle is gone. The hill is not.
lines: 언덕이 쓰는 입이에요. 지혜요, 물에 서서 한 번만 물으면. 외숙은 갔어요. 언덕은 안 가요.

en: I came because he died.
…Will the west stay taken.

blocks.html: Something goes out of the cave. When they speak again the eyes are solid: green, cyan, ember.
blocks.ko: 동굴에서 무언가가 빠져나간다. 다시 말할 때 그들의 눈은 통째로 빛난다. 초록, 청록, 불씨.

en: The west will take your name and call it peace.
Keep a sea in the other hand.
lines: 서쪽이 당신 이름을 가져가고 평화라 부를 거예요.

en: That was the hill. This is me.
Come back anyway. With nothing in your hands, like tonight. We like you better that way.
lines: 그래도 또 와. 오늘처럼 빈손으로. 그게 더 좋아.

blocks.label: The Man on the Water
blocks.ko: 물 위의 사내

blocks.html: Then the steam goes thin enough to see through, and a man stands on the water as if the lake were a court floor — old robes, sandalwood-coloured light, a face that has outlived every kingdom on the map. The three go still on the rock. This visitor is not theirs.
blocks.ko: 그러다 김이 얇아 투명해지고, 한 사내가 물 위에 서 있다 — 마치 호수가 조정 바닥인 것처럼. 낡은 옷, 자작나무 빛의 얼굴, 지도 위 모든 나라보다 오래 살아 남은 얼굴. 셋이 바위에서 멈춘다. 이 손님은 그들의 것이 아니다.

en: You wanted a king for all when you were six.
The title you are looking for is older than your father’s reforms.
Wanggeom — not Sacred Bone, not True Bone. The first who stayed when heaven descended.
lines: 여섯 살 때 모두를 위한 임금을 원했다.
네가 찾는 칭호는 아버지의 개혁보다 오래되었다.
왕검 — 성골도, 진골도 아닌. 하늘이 내려왔을 때 머문 첫 임금.

en: Who are you.
Which court sent you.
Asadal is dust.
The mandate is not.
Finish what your uncle could not name aloud.
lines: 외숙이 입 밖에 내지 못한 것을 끝내라.

blocks.html: Munmu tells no one. The court records note only a day’s ride and a night’s silence. But he has heard the bear’s son’s name before, in his mother’s version, with extra garlic, and he keeps it.
blocks.ko: 문무는 아무에게도 말하지 않는다. 조정 기록에는 하루의 기승과 하룻밤의 침묵만 남는다. 그러나 그는 곰의 아들 이름을 전에도 들은 적이 있다. 어머니 판본으로, 마늘이 좀 더 들어간. 그는 그 이름을 간직한다.

blocks.html: Kim Punghun said he could wait for a ship. The ship is here…!
blocks.ko: 김풍훈은 배를 기다릴 수 있다고 했다. 그 배가 왔다…!

logline.en: Xue Rengui comes back by sea. His guide is a Silla boy whose father the king killed.
logline.ko: 설인귀가 바다로 돌아온다. 길잡이는 왕이 아버지를 죽인 신라 소년이다.

images.at: When the last horse is off, Munhun stands up.
images.alt: Bernini’s David on the dune: Munhun twists up out of the grass, sword drawn, the Tang horses standing in the surf behind
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. POSE: Bernini’s David. Low worm’s-eye from the dune grass at dusk on the Cheonseong beach: the Silla general Munhun twists up out of the grass mid-coil, torso wound, jaw set, his ring-pommel sword drawn back over his shoulder ready to swing, grey steel lamellar with blue cloth at the collar, tall cone helm. Behind and below him, small, the empty Tang ships in the shallows and a line of unloaded horses standing in the surf. One last red sun break behind the boats rims his blade with a long glistening streak; the dune and sky are black-violet. Encased in darkness: at least 80% of the frame is near-black umber void, the figures pulled out of it by one hard raking key. Old-master tenebrist canvas (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour oil brushwork, glazed umber-black darks, impasto on the brightest highlight, canvas grain; silk brushed in loaded strokes; only faces and hands keep clean webtoon ink line. The steel glistens: the key runs down every blade as one long white-hot streak with a tiny star-glint on the edge. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — Kingdom banners: copy field colour and emblem from the attached flag_*.png ref onto period silk war-banners — tall poles behind each side, long streamers, small pennants on spear-tips and saddle-backs. Painted silk, wind-whipped, torn and smoke-stained in battle; never a flat modern flag graphic. Each side's banner colour is the clearest colour on its half of the frame, so the kingdom reads at a glance. Silla banners: blue silk with a white crescent moon. Attached flag /flag_silla.png. Tang banners: vermilion silk with a yellow sun disc and a dark brush glyph inside it — painted as an illegible brush mark, never readable text. Attached flag /flag_tang.png. SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.alt: King Munmu standing in a black void on a low crimson tide-bar, almost lost in shadow
images.prompt: Minimal iconic 9:16 poster. King Munmu, king for all, dragon of the strait. ONE geometric device: a CRIMSON TIDE as a low horizontal BAR of #C41E3A silk-water occupying only the bottom fifth. He stands in it, poster-scale, almost lost; a sea-dragon ring-pommel catching one red glint. Face matches the attached portrait. Face mostly in shadow; thin crimson rim-light. Striking silky court-military hanbok. Eighty percent black void. Form defined by rim light, not a floating bust. No army. No palace clutter. No text. No watermark. Graphic color-blocking, anime-painterly, monumental.

blocks.label: The Landing
blocks.ko: 상륙

blocks.html: Xue Rengui comes back by sea in the ninth month. His pilot is Kim Punghun. Munmu killed his father. Now the son is showing the enemy fleet the way into his own coast.
blocks.ko: 설인귀가 아홉째 달에 바다로 돌아온다. 길잡이는 김풍훈이다. 문무가 그의 아버지를 죽였다. 이제 그 아들이 적의 함대에게 제 나라 해안으로 드는 길을 일러 준다.

blocks.caption: Horses by sea, horses by land. Silla has decided this war is about horses.
blocks.ko: 바다로 오는 말, 땅으로 오는 말. 신라는 이 전쟁이 말에 달렸다고 정했다.

blocks.html: He is older now. The white coat is a reputation he can no longer take off. Tang’s eastern command sits on his shoulders the way a yoke sits on an ox that still believes in the field. In a poor field at home, his ancestors are still waiting for their graves.
blocks.ko: 그는 이제 늙었다. 흰옷은 벗을 수 없는 이름이다. 당의 동방 총지휘는, 아직도 밭을 믿는 소의 어깨에 얹힌 멍에처럼 그의 어깨에 있다. 고향의 척박한 밭에서는 조상들이 아직도 무덤을 기다리고 있다.

blocks.html: Punghun stands at the bow beside him. He left Silla a boy, a hostage in the emperor’s guard. He is coming back as a guide.
blocks.ko: 풍훈이 뱃머리에 그와 나란히 선다. 소년으로 신라를 떠나 황제의 숙위에 볼모로 갔던 그가, 이제 길잡이로 돌아온다.

en: You know this coast, Master Kim.

blocks.speaker: Kim Punghun
en: I know my father’s coast.
The king made it mine to sell.
lines: 왕이 그걸 제가 팔 물건으로 만들어 주었지요.

en: I am not buying anything.
I only ask where the sand is firm. For the horses.
lines: 말을 내릴 모래가 단단한 곳을 여쭐 뿐입니다.

blocks.html: Punghun looks at the beach below Cheon Fortress for a long time.
blocks.ko: 풍훈은 천성 아래 바닷가를 오래 바라본다.

blocks.speaker: Kim Punghun
en: …There. Firm enough.

lines: 신라… 예전에 우리와 같이 싸웠던 나라.
이제 그 나라가, 나의 마지막 상대인가.
en: Silla… the country that once fought beside us.
And now that country is to be my last opponent.
zh: 新羅……曾與我并肩作戰之國。
而今，那國竟成我最後之對手。
zhLatn: Xīnluó… céng yǔ wǒ bìngjiān zuòzhàn zhī guó.
Ér jīn, nà guó jìng chéng wǒ zuìhòu zhī duìshǒu.

blocks.html: He does not curse them. He checks the ji’s bindings, the same way he once checked plough-rope, and goes ashore.
blocks.ko: 그들을 욕하지 않는다. 언젠가 쟁기 줄을 확인하던 손으로 극의 묶음을 확인하고, 상륙한다.

blocks.html: Above the beach at Cheon Fortress, a Silla general named Munhun lies flat in the dune grass and watches the boats come in. He has been told to stop the landing. He has decided to let it happen first.
blocks.ko: 천성 바닷가 위, 신라 장수 문훈이 모래언덕 풀숲에 엎드려 배들이 들어오는 것을 지켜본다. 상륙을 막으라는 명을 받았다. 그는 먼저 상륙하게 두기로 했다.

blocks.html: Beside him lies a ship captain named Sideuk, who has commanded boats for twelve years and never once won anything.
blocks.ko: 그 곁에는 시득이라는 선장이 엎드려 있다. 열두 해 배를 몰았고, 한 번도 이겨 본 적이 없다.

en: General, they’re unloading the horses. Horses first.
blocks.speaker: Sideuk

en: Good. Let them.
blocks.speaker: Munhun

en: We were told to stop the landing.
blocks.speaker: Sideuk

lines: 젖은 모래에 선 말은 못 돈다. 배가 빌 때까지 기다려.
en: We will.
A horse on wet sand can’t turn. Wait till the boats are empty.
blocks.speaker: Munhun
Sideuk
en: …Wet sand. I’ll remember that.

blocks.html: When the last horse is off, Munhun stands up.
blocks.ko: 마지막 말이 내리자, 문훈이 일어선다.
blocks.art: Silla spearmen pouring over the dune crest; horses rearing in the surf; Tang boats backing oars.

en: To the boats.
zhLatn: Huí chuán.

blocks.html: By evening Munhun has fourteen hundred heads, forty Tang ships, and a thousand horses standing in the surf with nobody to ride them. The sea road is closed again.
blocks.ko: 저녁이 되자 문훈의 손에는 목 천사백과 당나라 배 마흔 척, 그리고 탈 사람 없이 파도 속에 선 말 천 필이 남는다. 바닷길이 다시 닫힌다.

blocks.html: Nobody ever learns whether Punghun knew about the sand. Xue does not ask him. He sends him back to Chang’an on the next empty transport, and neither country writes his name down again.
blocks.ko: 풍훈이 그 모래를 알았는지는 아무도 모른다. 설인귀는 묻지 않는다. 다음 빈 수송선에 그를 실어 장안으로 돌려보내고, 두 나라 어느 쪽도 다시는 그의 이름을 적지 않는다.

blocks.label: Maeso Fortress
blocks.ko: 매소성

blocks.html: So the war moves inland, to a fortress on the Imjin where the road to Surabol begins.
blocks.ko: 그리하여 전쟁은 내륙으로, 임진강가의 한 성으로 옮겨 간다. 서라벌로 가는 길이 시작되는 곳이다.

blocks.html: Good walls. Terrible stables.
blocks.ko: 성벽은 좋다. 마구간이 형편없다.

blocks.title: Maeso Fortress, twenty-ninth day of the ninth month, 675

units.label: Li Jinxing · Mohe and Tang
units.sub: a Mohe chief’s son in Tang service — the Samguk Sagi says 200,000

blocks.note: 30,380 horses were taken, and weapons to match. Historians read the 200,000 as Silla counting generously; nobody argues about the horses.

blocks.html: The army at Maeso is mostly Mohe, and the Mohe are mostly horse. Thirty thousand of them graze the flats east of the walls. The grass is outside. No fortress on that river was built to stable a herd.
blocks.ko: 매소성의 군대는 대부분 말갈이고, 말갈은 대부분 말이다. 삼만 필이 성벽 동쪽 들판에서 풀을 뜯는다. 풀은 성 밖에 있다. 그 강가의 어떤 성도 그만한 무리를 들이도록 지어지지 않았다.

en: Forget the walls.
Cut the picket lines. Bring me the horses.
blocks.speaker: Silla commander

blocks.html: The worst stretch of the line is under the walls, where the archers can see. A man nobody in the capital has seen for three years asks for it.
blocks.ko: 가장 험한 자리는 성벽 바로 아래, 궁수들 눈에 보이는 곳이다. 세 해 동안 도성에서 아무도 보지 못한 사내 하나가 그 자리를 청한다.

blocks.speaker: Silla commander
en: Name?

blocks.speaker: Wonsul
en: Lieutenant. Of Seokmun.

blocks.html: Before dawn the herd moves all at once, and not toward the fortress.
blocks.ko: 동트기 전, 말 떼가 한꺼번에 움직인다. 성 쪽이 아니다.
blocks.art: Wordless. Knives at the picket ropes in the dark; then the whole herd streaming across the flats toward the Silla lines.

en: The horses! The horses are going!
blocks.speaker: Mohe rider
blocks.art: Mohe riders running after the herd on foot.

blocks.html: Horses are the thing. An army that has lost thirty thousand horses on the Imjin is not riding to Surabol next spring, or the spring after. Li Jinxing knows it by noon. He takes what is left north across the Hantan.
blocks.ko: 중요한 건 말이다. 임진강에서 말 삼만을 잃은 군대는 다음 봄에도, 그다음 봄에도 서라벌로 달려오지 못한다. 이근행은 한낮이 되기 전에 그걸 안다. 남은 것을 이끌고 북쪽으로 한탄강을 건넌다.

blocks.speaker: Silla commander
en: Let them go.
Count the horses first. Then the spears.

blocks.html: Afterwards the king sends for the lieutenant to give him rank. Wonsul comes in still smelling of horses.
blocks.ko: 뒤에 왕이 벼슬을 주려고 그 비장을 부른다. 원술은 아직 말 냄새를 풍기며 들어온다.

en: Your father would have—

blocks.speaker: Wonsul
en: My father would have said I owe one afternoon, Majesty. I haven’t paid it yet.
lines: 아버지라면 제가 한나절을 빚졌다 하셨을 겁니다, 전하. 아직 다 못 갚았습니다.

blocks.label: The Fleet
blocks.ko: 함대

blocks.html: Out at sea off Cheon Fortress, Xue hears it from a courier: the army at Maeso has lost its horses.
blocks.ko: 천성 앞바다에서 설인귀는 파발에게서 그 소식을 듣는다. 매소성의 군대가 말을 잃었다.

lines: 농부에게 말을 잃는 일은… 밭을 잃는 일과 같소.
en: …So the horses are gone.
For a farmer, losing horses… is like losing the field.
zh: 對農夫而言，失馬……如失田。
zhLatn: …Mǎ méi le.
Duì nóngfū éryán, shī mǎ… rú shī tián.

blocks.html: He withdraws without spectacle. The chronicle will remember Silla’s thirty thousand horses; it will remember less how quietly the White Tiger II accepted that the east was no longer his to harvest.
blocks.ko: 그는 떠들썩하지 않게 물러난다. 연대기는 신라가 얻은 말 삼만을 기억할 것이고 — 백호 2세가 동쪽을 더 이상 제 수확으로 삼지 않기로 한 그 조용함은, 덜 기억할 것이다.

blocks.label: Surabol
blocks.ko: 서라벌

blocks.html: In Surabol the number arrives a day ahead of the generals.
blocks.ko: 서라벌에는 장수들보다 숫자가 하루 먼저 닿는다.

en: Thirty thousand, three hundred and eighty, Majesty.
blocks.speaker: Messenger

en: …Heads?
Horses, Majesty.
blocks.speaker: Messenger

blocks.html: After they have lost the horses. Munmu is nearly fifty and still, occasionally, checking his father’s work against the day.
blocks.ko: 말을 다 잃은 뒤에. 문무는 쉰을 앞두고 있고, 여전히 이따금 아버지의 셈을 그날그날에 견주어 본다.

blocks.html: The Tang history says Maeso was three Tang victories, after which Silla begged pardon. It does not mention the horses.
blocks.ko: 당의 역사서는 매소성이 당의 세 번 승리였고, 그 뒤 신라가 용서를 빌었다고 적는다. 말 이야기는 없다.

en: Then get me ships.
It’s the sea now.

blocks.html: One last river mouth. One captain who has never won a fight. Three tries to end a war…!
blocks.ko: 마지막 강어귀. 한 번도 이겨 본 적 없는 선장 하나. 전쟁을 끝낼 기회는 세 번…!

logline.en: At the river mouth where the Tang landed sixteen years ago, a captain who has never won anything loses twice on purpose. Xue Rengui watches his fleet sit down in the mud.
logline.ko: 열여섯 해 전 당군이 상륙했던 강어귀에서, 한 번도 이겨 본 적 없는 선장이 일부러 두 번 진다. 설인귀는 제 함대가 진흙에 주저앉는 것을 지켜본다.

images.at: The last of it happens at the mouth of the Geum
images.alt: Poster key art: King Munmu gallops the white heavenly horse through the surf at dawn as the last Tang sails leave the river mouth
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; crowns, antlers, wings and heads stay well inside the central band; no title, no lettering. Dawn at a river mouth opening onto the sea, mudflats and surf, a few tiny Tang sails dissolving on the horizon. Low angle at the waterline. INTERACTION: King Munmu rides the wingless white heavenly horse Chunma at full gallop through the shallow surf, leaning low over its neck, both hands in its mane, crimson robe streaming, shouting with joy; spray explodes off its hooves and curls up into cloud streamers. Horse and king are one diagonal across the frame. CHUNMA HAS NO WINGS: a wingless white heavenly horse, bare white back and shoulders, nothing feathered anywhere; it rides the air on curling cloud-and-flame streamers trailing from its legs. One low crimson sunrise (#C41E3A) behind the clouds catches the spray, his crown and the horse’s white flank; the sea and sky are ink and slate. Spray droplets as painted bokeh. STYLE: HEEWON STYLE, more painterly, with hints of Korean ink painting — Korean webtoon figures (clean ink linework, simplified expressive faces matching the attached portrait, watercolor-washed) inside a hand-painted world of watercolor and oil with traditional sumukhwa ink: splashed-ink storm clouds, bold dry calligraphic brush strokes in manes, fur, feathers, robes and grass, ink bleeding into wet wash, small ink splatters and drips near the frame edges, patches of bare rice paper where the edges dissolve; oil glazes only deepen the darks, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. Movie-poster key art: bold iconic silhouette, the two subjects large and close, one dramatic low angle, one bright break of light behind them, big dark masses, few hues plus one accent, film-poster drama but NO text, NO title, NO credits, NO logo, NO seal stamp. Not photoreal, not 3D. No glow aura, no halo, no emissive outline — the accent colour is real light. One of each named person. No watermark. CANON — KING MUNMU — FACE and garments from attached /ch_munmu.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Square jaw, goatee and moustache, confident grin; arms folded when he is pleased with himself. Dress: As king: crimson robe with gold dragon embroidery, blue shoulder pieces, gold Silla crown. Earlier: prince/hwarang stage portraits. Demeanor: Cocky, warm, practical; his father's charm with his uncle's spine. #C41E3A as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: katana; Tang dragon robe in place of Silla court dress. | CHUNMA (천마, hyukgose's heavenly horse, guardian of Silla) — attached board /obj_chunma.png: WINGLESS white heavenly horse in the Cheonmachong saddle-flap style: long arched neck, streaming white mane and tail, legs flung out in a flying gallop. It has NO WINGS — no feathers, no bird wings, nothing growing from the shoulders. It rides the sky on curling cloud-and-flame streamers trailing from its legs and chest, as on the painted birch-bark flap. Divine render: numinous through scale and atmosphere, never a glow outline. Kneels and cries beside the purple egg at Najeong, sees men approach, neighs and rises into the sky. | HORSE ANATOMY is a centrepiece: the whole horse body reads clearly and beautifully — arched neck, deep chest, sloping shoulder, round haunch, clean long legs in a correct gait, every muscle modelled by the one hard key with a bright edge along the topline and deep shadow under the belly; the horse is never cropped into a blob, never hidden behind dust, never stiff like a toy; mane and tail as flowing painted strokes; the coat colour exactly as the board. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS are a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST room (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt) painted in that same wash-and-glaze: a warm umber-to-black ground, walls, timber, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft with soft sfumato falloff — the webtoon figures are set INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: In the second month, the emperor's headquarters quietly leaves Pyongyang. Then it moves further. Then nobody mentions it. Xue still has a fleet, and a fleet doesn't need a headquarters.
blocks.ko: 이월, 황제의 도호부가 슬그머니 평양을 떠난다. 그러고는 더 멀리 간다. 그러고는 아무도 입에 올리지 않는다. 설인귀에게는 아직 함대가 있고, 함대에는 도호부가 필요 없다.

blocks.caption: The protectorate packs for Liaodong. Xue Rengui keeps one fleet and one last idea.
blocks.ko: 도호부는 요동으로 짐을 싼다. 설인귀에게는 함대 하나와 마지막 생각 하나가 남았다.

blocks.label: Final Ford
blocks.ko: 기벌포

blocks.html: The last of it happens at the mouth of the Geum, in the eleventh month. Sixteen years ago the Tang came in through this same water, onto a mile of grey mud, while Baekje watched from the high ground. Seongchung had begged a different king to hold it. Now Xue Rengui brings the last fleet in from the open sea.
blocks.ko: 마지막은 열한째 달, 금강 어귀에서 벌어진다. 열여섯 해 전 당군이 바로 이 물로 들어와 십 리 잿빛 개펄에 올랐고, 백제는 높은 땅에서 그것을 지켜보았다. 성충이 다른 임금에게 지켜 달라 애원했던 물목이다. 이제 설인귀가 마지막 함대를 끌고 먼바다에서 들어온다.

blocks.speaker: Silla helmsman
lines: 사찬님, 배 위에 망루를 올렸어요. 망루를요.
en: Sachan, they’ve built towers. On the ships. Towers.

blocks.speaker: Sideuk
en: Then they’re heavy.

blocks.html: The Silla ships belong to Sideuk, the captain who has never won anything. He takes them out on the ebb and loses.
blocks.ko: 신라의 배는 한 번도 이겨 본 적 없는 선장 시득이 맡고 있다. 그는 썰물에 배를 몰고 나가, 진다.

en: Sachan, we’re going out again?
blocks.speaker: Silla helmsman

en: When the tide turns.
blocks.speaker: Sideuk

blocks.html: He goes out again and loses again.
blocks.ko: 다시 나가, 또 진다.
blocks.art: Tang hulls high and dark over the Silla boats; the Silla line turning back.

en: …And a third time?
blocks.speaker: Silla helmsman

lines: 큰 배는 개펄에서 못 돈다. 끌고 들어와.
en: Their ships are big.
A big ship can’t turn on the mudflats. Draw them in.
Like a horse on wet sand.
blocks.speaker: Sideuk

blocks.label: The Third Sortie
blocks.ko: 세 번째 출격

blocks.html: The third time, Sideuk does not try to win. He runs.
blocks.ko: 세 번째에 시득은 이기려 하지 않는다. 달아난다.

blocks.html: He takes eight boats out toward the Tang flagship on the last of the flood, close enough to be insulting. Arrows thud into his deck. He lets them. Then he turns, badly, the way a beaten man turns, and makes for the mudflats on the north shore.
blocks.ko: 그는 밀물 끝자락을 타고 배 여덟 척을 당의 기함 쪽으로 몬다. 모욕이 될 만큼 가까이. 화살이 갑판에 박힌다. 그대로 둔다. 그러고는 진 사람이 돌듯 엉성하게 돌아서, 북쪽 기슭 개펄로 간다.

blocks.speaker: Silla helmsman
en: They’re coming! All of them— Sachan, the big ones are coming!
lines: 옵니다! 다— 사찬님, 큰 놈들이 다 따라옵니다!

blocks.speaker: Sideuk
en: Of course they are. They’ve beaten us twice.
Keep running. Look scared.

blocks.speaker: Silla helmsman
en: I’m not pretending, sir.

blocks.html: The tide turns under them. Sideuk’s boats float in a hand’s depth of water. The Tang tower-ships need a man’s height. One by one, the great hulls feel the mud take their keels, and stop, and lean.
blocks.ko: 발밑에서 물때가 바뀐다. 시득의 배는 한 뼘 물이면 뜬다. 당의 누선은 사람 키만큼의 물이 필요하다. 하나씩, 큰 배들의 용골이 진흙에 잡히고, 멈추고, 기운다.

blocks.speaker: Sideuk
en: Now. Turn. Everyone, turn!

blocks.html: What follows is twenty-two fights, large and small, in water too shallow for the ships that started them. Silla men cross the mud on planks, on oars, on their own bellies. The tower-ships cannot turn to face them. They can only lean further.
blocks.ko: 그다음은 크고 작은 스물두 번의 싸움이다. 그 싸움을 시작한 배들에게는 너무 얕은 물에서. 신라 군사들은 널빤지로, 노로, 제 배를 깔고 진흙을 건넌다. 누선은 돌아서 맞설 수가 없다. 더 기울 수 있을 뿐이다.

blocks.label: The Flagship
blocks.ko: 기함

blocks.html: On the flagship, Xue Rengui stands at the rail and watches his fleet sit down in the mud like oxen in a flooded field. He is sixty-two. He knows exactly what he is looking at. He grew up looking at it.
blocks.ko: 기함 난간에서 설인귀는 제 함대가 물 찬 논의 소처럼 진흙에 주저앉는 것을 지켜본다. 예순둘이다. 자기가 무엇을 보고 있는지 정확히 안다. 그걸 보며 자랐으니까.

blocks.speaker: Tang officer
en: Commander. We can still float the flagship on the night tide. The others—
lines: 대총관. 밤 물때에 기함은 띄울 수 있습니다. 나머지는—

en: The others are a field we planted in the wrong season.
Float what floats. Take the men off the rest. Leave no one in the mud.
lines: 나머지는 철을 잘못 맞춰 심은 밭이오.
뜨는 것만 띄우시오. 나머지 배에서는 사람만 내리시오. 진흙에 아무도 두고 가지 마시오.

blocks.html: He does not curse Silla. He never has. At midnight the flagship lifts off the mud, and he turns her west.
blocks.ko: 그는 신라를 욕하지 않는다. 한 번도 그런 적이 없다. 한밤중에 기함이 진흙에서 떠오르고, 그는 뱃머리를 서쪽으로 돌린다.

en: Ancestors.
I asked you to wait a little longer. It was longer than I said.
I am coming home without the east. I still have the ji.
lines: 조금만 기다려 달라 말씀드렸지요. 말씀드린 것보다 길어졌습니다.
동쪽은 못 가져갑니다. 극은 아직 있습니다.

blocks.html: No treaty comes after it, and no envoy. The Tang ships simply keep going west, and nobody on them looks back.
blocks.ko: 그 뒤로 조약도 오지 않고 사신도 오지 않는다. 당의 배들은 그저 계속 서쪽으로 가고, 그 위의 누구도 돌아보지 않는다.

blocks.label: Surabol
blocks.ko: 서라벌

blocks.html: In Surabol the king waits a month for a letter from the west, so that he will at least have something to refuse. None comes.
blocks.ko: 서라벌에서 왕은 서쪽에서 올 편지를 한 달 동안 기다린다. 적어도 거절할 거리라도 있도록. 아무것도 오지 않는다.

en: Have we… won…?

blocks.speaker: Court scribe
en: Nobody has told us we haven’t, Majesty.
lines: 졌다고 알려 온 사람은 아무도 없습니다, 전하.

blocks.html: He laughs, for the first time since the funeral, and goes to tell his mother.
blocks.ko: 그는 장례 뒤 처음으로 웃는다. 그리고 어머니에게 알리러 간다.

blocks.html: The boy who stole a sentence at six is about to be king of all Samhan. His mother would like him to hold still…!
blocks.ko: 여섯 살에 한 문장을 훔친 소년이 이제 삼한 모두의 왕이 된다. 어머니는 그에게 가만히 좀 있으라고 한다…!

logline.en: On the morning he becomes king of all Samhan, Munmu opens the hall to the yard. Five summers later, Kangrim asks him the question.
logline.ko: 삼한 모두의 왕이 되는 아침, 문무는 전각 문을 마당에 연다. 다섯 해 뒤, 강림이 그에게 질문을 던진다.

images.alt: Otherworld ink leaf: flat blank paper with a sparse drift of tiny painted flowers, old Queen Sunduk far off walking away through them, one vermilion sleeve
images.prompt: A Korean ink-and-colour album leaf, otherworldly and symbolic: flat blank cream paper, NO sky, NO sun, NO clouds, NO horizon line. ICONIC MINIMAL LAYOUT: ONE device: a sparse diagonal drift of tiny boneless-brush flowers (peonies, chrysanthemums, lotus) scattered across the paper from lower left to upper right like a path, soft mineral colours, lots of empty paper between them. Far along that path in the upper right third, tiny, the aged QUEEN SUNDUK (face and garments from the attached portrait, face a few strokes, back mostly turned) walks away unhurried, one vermilion #E8552B sleeve the only strong colour, her hand trailing over the blooms. At the lower-left corner one small cut peony lies on the blank paper as if dropped. Serene, emptied, final. One blank red seal square. PARODY RULES: always a hand-made PAINTING, never photoreal. Reproduce the original work’s composition, poses and signature look so it reads instantly as that exact work, with our characters swapped in. If the original is a painting, mural, print or scroll, match its medium, surface and brushwork. If the original is a photograph, film poster, album cover, anime frame or statue, PAINT it: a painterly illustration of that image with visible brushstrokes, simplified forms and anime-adjacent faces, NOT a photo, NOT photoreal skin or pores, NOT a 3D render, NOT a CGI statue. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portraits, recognizable but restyled into the medium; never the portrait’s standing clasped-hands stance. Character hex lives only as real color inside the work (pigment, cloth, light), never a glow aura, halo, emissive skin or neon outline. If a sword is visible it is the ring-pommel 환두대도 (small ring pommel at the heel of the fist, short grip, long straight blade, handle:blade 1:3), never a katana, never a tsuba. No readable text, no title, no credits, no legible inscriptions or signatures (red seal stamps only as blank red squares), no logos, no watermark.

images.at: stands where a six-year-old once stole a sentence
images.alt: Poster key art: King Munmu grins on the hilltop where he once stole his childhood sentence, the white heavenly horse shoving its nose into his shoulder
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; crowns, antlers, wings and heads stay well inside the central band; no title, no lettering. Late afternoon on a grass hill above Seorabeol, the war over, a huge clearing storm sky. Low heroic angle from the grass. INTERACTION: King Munmu, crimson robe with gold dragon embroidery, blue shoulder pieces, gold Silla crown, square jaw and goatee, stands with his arms folded and a cocky grin; the wingless white heavenly horse Chunma butts its nose hard into his shoulder, knocking him half a step, and he laughs and hooks an arm around its neck. Far below, the city roofs small in haze. CHUNMA HAS NO WINGS: a wingless white heavenly horse, bare white back and shoulders, nothing feathered anywhere; it rides the air on curling cloud-and-flame streamers trailing from its legs. One crimson-gold sun-break (#C41E3A) behind them rims the crown, his grin and the horse’s mane; the hill falls into dark green-umber. Grass strokes in the near foreground. STYLE: HEEWON STYLE, more painterly, with hints of Korean ink painting — Korean webtoon figures (clean ink linework, simplified expressive faces matching the attached portrait, watercolor-washed) inside a hand-painted world of watercolor and oil with traditional sumukhwa ink: splashed-ink storm clouds, bold dry calligraphic brush strokes in manes, fur, feathers, robes and grass, ink bleeding into wet wash, small ink splatters and drips near the frame edges, patches of bare rice paper where the edges dissolve; oil glazes only deepen the darks, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. Movie-poster key art: bold iconic silhouette, the two subjects large and close, one dramatic low angle, one bright break of light behind them, big dark masses, few hues plus one accent, film-poster drama but NO text, NO title, NO credits, NO logo, NO seal stamp. Not photoreal, not 3D. No glow aura, no halo, no emissive outline — the accent colour is real light. One of each named person. No watermark. CANON — KING MUNMU — FACE and garments from attached /ch_munmu.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Square jaw, goatee and moustache, confident grin; arms folded when he is pleased with himself. Dress: As king: crimson robe with gold dragon embroidery, blue shoulder pieces, gold Silla crown. Earlier: prince/hwarang stage portraits. Demeanor: Cocky, warm, practical; his father's charm with his uncle's spine. #C41E3A as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: katana; Tang dragon robe in place of Silla court dress. | CHUNMA (천마, hyukgose's heavenly horse, guardian of Silla) — attached board /obj_chunma.png: WINGLESS white heavenly horse in the Cheonmachong saddle-flap style: long arched neck, streaming white mane and tail, legs flung out in a flying gallop. It has NO WINGS — no feathers, no bird wings, nothing growing from the shoulders. It rides the sky on curling cloud-and-flame streamers trailing from its legs and chest, as on the painted birch-bark flap. Divine render: numinous through scale and atmosphere, never a glow outline. Kneels and cries beside the purple egg at Najeong, sees men approach, neighs and rises into the sky. | PLACE Surabol (서라벌 (경주)) — attached board /pl_eastern_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Seorabeol palace: Silla giwa halls, packed-earth yards, timber verandas. | HORSE ANATOMY is a centrepiece: the whole horse body reads clearly and beautifully — arched neck, deep chest, sloping shoulder, round haunch, clean long legs in a correct gait, every muscle modelled by the one hard key with a bright edge along the topline and deep shadow under the belly; the horse is never cropped into a blob, never hidden behind dust, never stiff like a toy; mane and tail as flowing painted strokes; the coat colour exactly as the board. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS are a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST room (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt) painted in that same wash-and-glaze: a warm umber-to-black ground, walls, timber, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft with soft sfumato falloff — the webtoon figures are set INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Bupmin, King Munmu now, stands where a six-year-old once stole a sentence. The war is won, the ally has been shown the door, and the childhood dream has had the bad manners to come true.
blocks.ko: 법민, 이제는 문무왕인 그가 여섯 살 아이가 문장을 훔치던 자리에 선다. 전쟁은 이겼고, 동맹은 문밖으로 내보내졌고, 어린 시절의 꿈은 무례하게도 이루어지고 말았다.

blocks.caption: Sixteen years, start to finish. Watch where the blue stops.
blocks.ko: 열여섯 해, 처음부터 끝까지. 파란빛이 어디서 멈추는지 보라.

blocks.label: The Collar
blocks.ko: 옷깃

blocks.html: It ends where it began: a woman in a room, getting someone else ready.
blocks.ko: 시작한 자리에서 끝난다. 방 안의 여자 하나가, 다른 사람의 채비를 돌봐 주고 있다.

blocks.html: Munhee is seventy. She is the last person alive who remembers all of it from the inside, and she is straightening her son's collar. She was twenty-six when this story started. Her sister burned a skirt on a hill so that she could be married.
blocks.ko: 문희는 일흔이다. 이 모든 일을 안에서 기억하는 마지막 사람이고, 지금은 아들의 옷깃을 여며 주고 있다. 이야기가 시작될 때 그는 스물여섯이었다. 언니가 언덕에서 치마를 태운 덕에 혼인할 수 있었다.

en: Hold still. Your collar is crooked.

lines: 어머니. 저 오늘 삼한의 왕이 됩니다.
en: Mother. Today I become king of all Samhan.
Then all the more reason to hold still.
Mother.
I kept the childhood sentence.
I know.
I packed for every country that tried to stop you.
lines: 너를 막으려던 나라마다 짐을 싸 줬으니까.

blocks.html: She has been in the room for every single one of them. The sword was never in her hand, and she is the only one still standing.
blocks.ko: 그는 그 모든 자리에 있었다. 칼을 쥔 적은 한 번도 없고, 아직 서 있는 사람은 그뿐이다.

en: Your sister rode out of this room to Daeya.
Hold still. I’m not losing another one to a door.
lines: 네 누이는 이 방에서 대야로 떠났다.
가만있어. 문 하나에 자식을 또 잃을 생각은 없다.

blocks.html: A letter has come from Chang’an. It is the first in Inmun’s hand in twenty years, and it is very short.
blocks.ko: 장안에서 편지가 왔다. 스무 해 만에 처음 보는 인문의 글씨다. 아주 짧다.

en: Brother.
The emperor made me King of Silla for a season. I got as far as the coast road before he changed his mind. I am told I abdicated. I agreed.
Word came that you said my name. I heard it.
— Inmun
lines: 황제가 한 철 동안 저를 신라 왕으로 삼았습니다. 해안 길까지 갔는데 황제가 마음을 바꾸었지요. 제가 물러났다고들 합니다. 저도 그렇다 했습니다.
형님이 제 이름을 불렀다는 말을 들었습니다. 들었습니다.

en: His handwriting hasn’t improved.

blocks.html: She folds it into his sleeve, next to his arm, where he will feel it all day.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 편지를 접어 아들의 소매 안, 팔에 닿는 자리에 넣어 준다. 하루 내내 느껴지도록.

lines: 아버지가 늘 하시던 말씀이 있었잖습니까. 천 년 가는 나라.
en: Father used to say a thing. A kingdom that lasts a thousand years.
He always did round the numbers up.

blocks.html: Silla lasts nine hundred and ninety-two years. He was, as usual, very slightly optimistic and essentially correct.
blocks.ko: 신라는 구백구십이 년을 간다. 늘 그렇듯 그는 아주 조금 낙관적이었고, 본질적으로는 옳았다.

blocks.label: The Hall
blocks.ko: 정전

blocks.html: The hall is full of bone. True Bone in the front rows, Head-rank Six behind them, and behind them the new men nobody has a rank for yet: Baekje captains who fought for Silla, Goguryeo’s guest king and his officers, a Mohe interpreter. Out in the yard stand the ones with no bone at all. They have come to see what a king for all looks like. Mostly he looks tired.
blocks.ko: 전각은 뼈로 가득하다. 앞줄에 진골, 그 뒤에 육두품, 그 뒤에 아직 관등이 없는 새 사람들. 신라를 위해 싸운 백제 장수들, 고구려의 손님 왕과 그 신하들, 말갈 통역 하나. 마당에는 뼈가 아예 없는 사람들이 서 있다. 모두의 왕이 어떻게 생겼는지 보러 왔다. 대체로 그는 피곤해 보인다.

en: Open the doors.
All of them. The yard too.

blocks.html: The doors open. The yard comes up to the threshold and stops there, the way people stop at a river.
blocks.ko: 문이 열린다. 마당 사람들이 문턱까지 와서 멈춘다. 사람들이 강가에서 멈추듯.

en: Sixteen years of war were paid for with grain borrowed from people who had none.
Every grain debt from the war years is cancelled. Today.
The men of Baekje and Goguryeo who bled under our banners will hold Silla ranks. The same ranks.
lines: 열여섯 해 전쟁은 가진 것 없는 백성에게서 꾼 곡식으로 치렀소.
전쟁 동안 진 곡식 빚은 모두 없던 것으로 하오. 오늘부로.
우리 깃발 아래 피 흘린 백제와 고구려 사람은 신라의 관등을 받소. 같은 관등을.

blocks.speaker: True Bone elder
en: Majesty. The bone ranks are older than the throne. If a Baekje captain sits where—
lines: 전하. 골품은 왕좌보다 오래되었습니다. 백제 장수 따위가 앉는 자리에—

en: When I was six I said everyone would have to listen to me. Even the bone people.
…I meant you, my lord.
lines: 여섯 살 때 내가 그랬소. 모두 내 말을 들어야 한다고. 뼈 있는 사람들도.

blocks.html: Somebody in the yard laughs. Then the whole yard does. The elder sits down. It is the first time that hall has ever heard the yard.
blocks.ko: 마당의 누군가가 웃는다. 이어 마당 전체가 웃는다. 원로가 자리에 앉는다. 그 전각이 마당 소리를 들은 건 처음이다.

en: I asked my uncle once. Every kingdom, or every person who bleeds for one. He never answered.
Both. Write that down.
lines: 외숙께 여쭌 적이 있소. 나라 전부냐, 나라를 위해 피 흘리는 사람 전부냐. 끝내 대답을 안 해 주셨지.

blocks.label: The Eastern Star
blocks.ko: 동쪽 별

blocks.html: Thirty-four winters ago, three men looked up at one star and wanted the same title. One died a guest in Chang’an, still calling himself a king. One died in his bed, and the king of the dead came to fetch him in person. One left the title in his son’s mouth.
blocks.ko: 서른네 해 전 겨울, 세 사내가 별 하나를 올려다보며 같은 칭호를 원했다. 하나는 장안에서 손님으로 죽었다. 끝까지 스스로를 왕이라 부르며. 하나는 제 침상에서 죽었고, 저승의 왕이 몸소 데리러 왔다. 하나는 그 칭호를 아들의 입에 남겼다.

blocks.html: That night the son climbs the hill above Surabol where two boys once lay on their backs, arguing about the sky.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 아들은 서라벌 위 언덕에 오른다. 한때 두 소년이 등을 대고 누워 하늘을 두고 다투던 곳이다.

en: Uncle always said it was a planet.

blocks.html: It sits among the stars without being one of them. He looks at it until the cold gets into his knees. Then he walks down to his own house, like anybody.
blocks.ko: 별들 사이에 있으면서 별은 아니다. 그는 추위가 무릎에 스밀 때까지 그것을 올려다본다. 그러고는 여느 사람처럼, 제 집으로 걸어 내려간다.

blocks.label: The Ancestral Temple
blocks.ko: 종묘

blocks.html: In the morning he reports to his father. The tablet stands in the ancestral temple, and beside it hangs the iron oath from Mount Gain, the one he swore over his uncle’s horse.
blocks.ko: 아침에 그는 아버지께 고한다. 위패는 종묘에 서 있고, 그 곁에 취리산의 쇠 맹세문이 걸려 있다. 외숙의 말 위에서 그가 맹세했던 그것이다.

en: Father. I broke it. Every line.
Baekje is ours. Its prince is in Luoyang, with a title and no country.
His sons are growing. I asked. The gods have been lenient with us both.
lines: 백제는 우리 것입니다. 그 왕자는 낙양에서 땅 없는 작위를 받았습니다.
그 아들들은 잘 자란답니다. 알아봤습니다. 신들이 우리 둘 다를 봐주신 모양입니다.

blocks.html: He leaves the oath where it hangs. The kings of Silla will have to walk past it every time they visit their fathers. He wants them to read it.
blocks.ko: 그는 맹세문을 걸린 그대로 둔다. 신라의 왕들은 선왕을 뵈러 올 때마다 그 앞을 지나가야 한다. 그는 그들이 그것을 읽기를 바란다.

blocks.label: Five Summers Later
blocks.ko: 다섯 해 뒤

blocks.html: Five summers later the king for all is dying, and he has left instructions his ministers do not like. No mound in the hills beside his fathers. Burn him, and put what is left in the sea the Wa come across.
blocks.ko: 다섯 해 뒤 여름, 모두의 임금이 죽어 가고, 그가 남긴 분부를 대신들은 달가워하지 않는다. 선왕들 곁 언덕에 봉분을 쓰지 말라 한다. 태워서, 남은 것을 왜가 건너오는 바다에 두라고.

en: The war is over. Melt the swords. Make ploughs.
Lighten the tax at the markets and the ferries.
And don’t build me a tomb. The people would only have to carry the stones.
lines: 전쟁은 끝났소. 칼을 녹이시오. 보습을 만드시오.
그리고 내 무덤은 짓지 마시오. 그 돌을 날라야 하는 건 백성이오.

blocks.html: Kangrim reads his name three times at the bedside — Bupmin. Bupmin. Bupmin. — the name the boy stole a sentence with, not the one the ledger writes.
blocks.ko: 강림은 침상 곁에서 그의 이름을 세 번 부른다 — 법민. 법민. 법민. — 장부에 적힌 이름이 아니라, 소년이 문장을 훔치던 때의 이름이다.

en: King Munmu.
Sixteen years of war, one hill, one ally shown the door, and a yard you let into the hall.
One question, then we walk. Were you a king of Silla — or a king for all?
lines: 열여섯 해의 전쟁, 언덕 하나, 문밖으로 내보낸 동맹 하나, 그리고 전각에 들인 마당 하나.
하나만 묻고 갑시다. 신라의 왕이었소 — 아니면 모두의 왕이었소?

en: …Ask the ones with no bone.
There are more of them.
The ledger has never asked them anything.
…I suppose I’ll start. Come. The sea is this way.
lines: 장부는 그들에게 무엇 하나 물어본 적이 없소.

blocks.hanja: 朕身後願爲護國大龍 崇奉佛法 守護邦家
blocks.ko: 짐이 죽은 뒤에는 호국대룡이 되어, 불법을 받들고 나라를 지키고자 한다.
blocks.html: After I am gone I wish to become a great dragon that guards the country, to uphold the Buddha’s law and protect the realm.
blocks.source: Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) bk. 2, Wonder 2 — King Munmu becomes a dragon; Ha & Mintz tr., p. 95

blocks.html: They burn him on the shore and put his bones under a rock a hundred paces out to sea, which is still there, and is the only royal tomb in the world with tides.
blocks.ko: 사람들은 바닷가에서 그를 화장하고, 뭍에서 백 걸음 나간 바위 아래에 뼈를 모신다. 그 바위는 지금도 그 자리에 있고, 세상에서 밀물과 썰물이 드나드는 유일한 왕릉이다.

blocks.label: The Tablet
blocks.ko: 위패

blocks.html: Eleven years after the tide closes over him, an envoy comes from the Empress’s court with a complaint that is thirty years late. King Muyeol’s tablet in Silla’s ancestral temple says Taejong, and Taejong is the Second Emperor’s temple name, and a vassal may not share a name with the Son of Heaven. Nobody from the Empress’s court mentions the iron oath hanging beside the tablet, broken in every line.
blocks.ko: 밀물이 그를 덮은 지 열한 해 뒤, 여제의 조정에서 사신이 온다. 삼십 년 늦은 항의를 들고. 신라 종묘의 무열왕 위패에 태종이라 적혀 있는데, 태종은 선제의 묘호이고, 번국은 천자와 이름을 나눌 수 없다는 것이다. 위패 곁에 걸린 쇠 맹세문이 한 줄도 남김없이 깨졌다는 이야기는, 여제의 조정 누구도 꺼내지 않는다.

blocks.speaker: Tang envoy
lines: 그대들의 선왕이 선제의 묘호를 빌려 쓰고 있소.
en: Your late king has borrowed a name that belongs to the Second Emperor.
Change it.
zhLatn: Ěr xiānwáng qiè yòng xiāndì miàohào.
Sù gǎi zhī.

blocks.html: Munmu’s son answers in writing.
blocks.ko: 문무의 아들이 글로 답한다.

blocks.speaker: Silla reply
lines: 선왕께서는 덕이 자못 높으셨고, 살아 계실 때 김유신이라는 어진 신하를 얻어 한마음으로 다스려 삼한을 하나로 만드셨습니다.
그만하면 이름 하나 값은 된다고 여겼습니다. 이미 임자가 있는 줄은 몰랐습니다.
en: Our late king had a great deal of virtue. While he lived he had a good minister, Kim Yushin, and the two of them were of one mind, and they made the three Han one.
We thought that was worth a name. We did not know it was already taken.

blocks.html: The court reads the name Kim Yushin, and an old archivist goes looking. He finds a note in the late emperor’s own hand, from his boyhood: a voice in the sky once told him that one of the Thirty-Three Heavens had been born in the east as a general. Nobody ever learned whose voice it was. Heaven gossips more than it lets on. The complaint is dropped. The tablet still says Taejong.
blocks.ko: 조정은 김유신이라는 이름을 읽고, 늙은 사관 하나가 서고를 뒤진다. 그는 선제가 어릴 적 손수 적어 둔 쪽지를 찾아낸다. 하늘에서 들린 목소리가, 서른세 하늘 가운데 하나가 동쪽에 장수로 태어났다고 일러 주었다는 것이다. 그 목소리가 누구였는지는 끝내 아무도 알아내지 못했다. 하늘은 보기보다 말이 많다. 항의는 거두어진다. 위패에는 지금도 태종이라 적혀 있다.

blocks.html: But we left someone in the snow. The winter Pyongyang fell, a Mohe father walked north with something in his pack…!
blocks.ko: 그런데 눈 속에 두고 온 사람이 있다. 평양이 떨어진 그 겨울, 말갈 사내 하나가 등짐에 무언가를 지고 북쪽으로 걸었다…!

toneNote: The chronicle exhales — warmth after war, and a new star in the north.
title: Epilogue

logline.en: The winter after Pyongyang falls, an old man carries a piece of a crown through the snow.
logline.ko: 평양이 무너진 그 겨울, 한 노인이 왕관 조각 하나를 품고 눈길을 걷는다.
